Paul Davis is a nice, reasonable professor. Annoyingly, his lectures were extremely easy to the extent that going was an inefficient waste of my time. This was because the tests would be textbook heavy and based on the textbook and material he didn't at all cover in lecture. Therefore it was better for me to not go to class and read the textbook.
Great guy, always willing to help out. Pay attention in lecture and you will be fine. Strongly recommend.

Avoid if you're a non-traditional student.  The class teaches you how to screw  employees, and if you have a previous working background, class is very difficult to follow because of the inherent experiences you take with you to class.  Pointless lectures.  No charisma.  Overall, a nice personality.  He'll give you "hints" in office hours.

Very easy class to get an A.  If you do the work and put in any studying for the exams you should get an A.  Professor's lectures are sometimes a little boring and repetitive, but i would definitely recommend him.

Really great professor! His tests are really fair and are mostly based off of clear points from lectures. Davis always tries to make the class entertaining and provides printed slides every class. Quizzes are open book and only two out of three assignments are required. Probably the best professor you could take for this course

Great professor. Fair exams, interesting lectures, and no busy work. Prints slides for his students. Office hours are very helpful. Really personable and cares about his students. Favorite ILR professor.
love Professor Davis. He's34 so he's very relatable and makes HR interesting and understandable for everyone. If you take intro HR take it with him for sure
Take him!! He is so great.

Although the class is generally low effort and there are few assignments, so as long as you do well on those you can get a good grade. She barely knows how to use canvas so the site was a mess. All the assignments and exams were CANVAS MULTIPLE CHOICE QUIZZES. There were calculations in the questions but no chance for partial credit

Rudest professor I've met here, made me quit my project team because she didn't support any students. Always loved hearing herself talk and brainstorm, and bored me every meeting. I don't know how she is in class, but she's an insufferable person

Pretty tough on grading and a bit hard to meet with, but I'd recommend discussing projects with her beforehand to work out any issues, since she's really experienced in her field and will easily identify holes in your projects. Pretty nice to talk with face to face. Will randomly call on students during class. Interesting but disengaging lectures.
Very critical. Not one for constructive criticism just pure criticism. You have to say and reproduce exactly what she wants to hear.
Dr. Nelson is kind of intimidating. She will shut your ideas down if she doesn't agree with them. She also will not hold back on tearing apart your work. She is very hard to please.
This class is easy and interesting! The teaching team is so caring and passionate about the subject. Overall, such a great class.
Nice professor and generally good class, content is kinda dry and one-sided for those really passionate about public health. show up, ready the book and  you'll do well
Passionate and smart professor; great class overall.

She makes lectures as interesting as possible and always makes sure to answer students' questions throughout class, thoughtfully. She grades with mildly high expectations of what students will submit (specifically final paper draft and other materials). Readings discussion posts twice a week are assigned.

Professor Slayton was amazing. She was engaging as a professor, cared about my success, and kept the lectures and readings interesting. The readings are long and are assigned for each class but are very important for success.

Professor Slayton is great! Her slides are detailed and informative. Her quizzes are very fair and she tells you exactly what she expects, and everything comes from the slides. The readings were a little challenging, but before quizzes, she reviews concepts from them that she wants you to know. Her paper assignments are graded fairly as well.

I don't really write reviews, but Prof Slayton is someone that deserves the recognition for her work and care for her students. Readings can be technical, but she really breaks them down to help you understand. Can get kind of boring, but the concepts are still interesting. Grading is very clear, and she gives A LOT of help and feedback on essays.
Super clear and enthusiastic lectures. Exams are really easy

She is extremely knowledgable in her field and does a great job of sharing her enthusiasm.  She provides excellent feedback and is always willing to help out with writing strategies, assignments, and etc.  The class was extremely enjoyable and interactive.

She pretty much knows everything there is to know about in the Baroque + Classical periods, whether be instrumental, vocal, dance, opera, etc. She will boost your love and appreciation for music to a new height.

Extremely interesting - this prof is super knowledgable and discussion sections were great too. Lots of work for a 3 credit class but definitely worth it. Would recommend to anyone interested in opera!

Way too much work for a 1000-level and 3-credit course. Not an understanding professor and seems to think her class is the only one in existence. Although there are no pre-reqs, the class is taught as if the students all have a pretty high level of understanding of music. Would not recommend.

Funny and caring, and a fantastic lecturer. Her assignments take some effort but are rewarding. Over a year after I took this course I happened to run into her; not only did she remember me but we chatted warmly for ten or fifteen minutes. Highly recommended!

Professor Schneider is wonderful; her class isn't difficult and at all and she genuinely cares about students and wants us to learn the material.  Overall just a really lovely prof and I had a good experience in the class.
Professor Schneider is very passionate and it comes through in her lectures! She is very helpful and the class is interesting.
Rebecca is invested in this subject and her students. Best class I've taken at cornell even though is was a 9:05
She only teaches you the basic mineral and expects you know a lot of stuff for the exam. Her exams are 11 pages long.

Teaches at the middle/high school level, and assumes that her students have no experience in intellectual thinking. Also, she and her TAs believe that there is only one way to interpret text, and thus only one correct essay format. And she is unresponsive to student feedback. Hands down worst professor/class at Cornell.

This class could have been so much better, but at least some of the major medical ethics topics were covered.  Essayscommentaries were graded difficultly, and too many lectures were simply students talking in groups, in a lecture hall.

Bioethics. Erin Taylor is incredible. Her lectures are very clear, the workload is not overwhelming, and the class discussions are very useful and engaging. She is very passionate and makes other students feel that way too. Also, she's really easy to talk to.

Her lectures are appropriate for middle/high school level courses. Also, she uses outdated data so nothing you learn is relevant. She is not open to students' opinions and is very unhelpful with developing ideas as well. The TA's are very subjective and the assignments are pointless as well.
Admittedly her lecture style is a tad too rudimentary but she's amazing about meeting with students and actually quite smart and lovely in person.

Ethics and Healthcare. Best lecturer I've had at Cornell. She is very clear, organized and coherent.The topics are engaging and contemporary.I recommend this to everyone, especially those who are pre-med/health.

I'm used to assignments with very objective grading and straightforward expectations, so this class threw me off. TALK TO YOUR TA before writing any essay, since each grader for this class expects something different. Readings were relatively interesting, but leave all the interpretation to your TA, or else you'll be "wrong".

Her lectures are at an 8th grade level, despite the intricate nature of the texts and assignments. And I'm pretty sure she misinterprets the texts. Without my TA, I would be lost. And I am certainly bored in class. From what I can tell, everyone else is as well. Hardly anyone comes to lecture, though almost everyone goes to section.

She is an extremely boring lecturer. She says nothing of interests and just repeats the material from the reading. There's no real reason to take her class. If you do, you just have to do the readings for the homework and essays and you'll be fine
Excellent professor - class topics were interesting and the handouts were very helpful. Always made time to talk, even outside of office hours.

Class topics were very interesting but she isn't a great lecturer. Does not keep you engaged and makes the topics less interesting. However, there are only 3 essays and weekly blackboard assignments and no attendance is taken in class or discussion. If you do your own reading you can do well in the class.

Great prof, really went out of her way to help me by providing extra tutoring since I enrolled late in her class.Her voice is a bit soft,so sit close to the front of the class to hear her clearly.Very meticulous in her notes on the blackboard and eager to discuss interesting points of the readings with students.Definitely a class I'd recommend.

I found professor Taylor very clear and helpful in her lectures. We were studying Kantian ethics for about half of the semester and for such difficult material, I though Professor Taylor did an excellent job.

It's VERY hard to hear professor Taylor in lecture and she can be EXTREMELY dry since she waits till class starts to write EVERYthing on the board.  Even the TA's slept in class. She (and the T.A's) are only looking for specific points in each paper and each look for different things, so be sure to talk with YOUR TA. I do not recommend this course!

Seemed like the perfect, easy elective class at first. She doesn't use powerpoint, just sloppy writing on the board. Nothing useful was ever added to the blackboard site. Issues are NOT contemporary, nor presented in an interesting way. Must know how to write a philosophy oriented paper.
No Comments

Erin is very kind, but her teaching style fell flat for me. Seminars were boring. She could've ended class (2 hours) early most weeks. Grading was inconsistent and not based on a rubric, so it was difficult to know how to improve. That being said, she was more than willing to meet about an assignment or discuss concerns if you had them.

Professor York-Cornwell has been one of the best professors I've had at Cornell, if not the best. She is incredibly caring and friendly as well as insightful and intelligent. If you have questions about how a test was graded she will talk with you and sometimes give back points. Also gives the opportunity for extra credit at the end of the semester

Attendance is mandatory but Professor Cornwell's lectures are very organized and useful. If you go to lectures and understand the slides well, exams are not hard at all. The comment below about the first prelim is not true - she gave a generous curve and also gave back some points where we wrote our assumptions on the side. Very caring of students.

Seems extremely unorganized and inexperienced. Her class is very dry - basically the professor just reads off the slides and knows there would be nobody in lecture if attendance wasn't mandatory. Everyone did poorly on the first exam and she refused to accept blame. Very disrespectful of our break times in regards to scheduling exams.

Very good professor teaching a fascinating subject.  If you go, pay attention, and take notes, you will do excellently.  I did not read except when she told us that there was going to be a quiz/paper on the topic and received an A+.  Doesn't care if your answers are wrong on the test if you justify them.  Quality professor who likes teaching.

One of the most interesting classes ever. Some interest in topic is required but if you like using STATA and the computer rather than a textbook its a great class. Dr. Cornwell is one is the most approachable professors at Cornell and she is really nice. I would recommed any class with her.

Whatever I type here will not be enough to accurately describe Dr Cornwell. She is One of the best professors I have had at Cornell. Excellent style of lecturing and she knows what appeals to the class. Exams and papers are hard but extremely fair and she gives you chances to make up for your mistakes. Great class overall.
She is a really nice person. You can talk to her anytime,she is there to help you. Very sweet person. Her readings are very interesting, at least fot sociology of law.
Squyres is LEGENDARY. Awesome lecturer, hilarious, AND he worked on the flippin' Mars Rovers. What's not to love????? Definitely one of my favorite professors here.
You'll not regret it. This man is LEGEND.

I enrolled in 1700 not knowing who this dude was. Holy crap thank goodness I took it on a whim! Favorite class so far. There is a crap ton of reading, but you only have to read enough so you can participate in discussion (it's not on exams). I got a C- on the midterm and cried, then I got it together and received an A-! TA Nick is very helpful
I hate this subject I love this man  Tests aren't that easy if you're taking an intro class to fulfill a requirement, but it's worth it to hear this man talk. Love him
Amazing professor. He is so passionate about astronomy and well respected in his field. This class is definitely worth taking.

Hands down one of the most interesting men I've ever met. Great lecturer (took two courses with him, history & astronomy), and it is very obvious that he has a strong passion and great enthusiasm for both his fields of study and teaching in general. Also, holding an important position on the Mars Rover Program, he gives interesting updates on them.

Only one word describes this guy: incredible. He's so passionate about everything he teaches, but especially in this class because he is an explorer. Whether or not you grew up following Squyres' Mars Rover missions, you will love this class. It's truly one of a kind, and so is he. Best professor ever.

Possibly the best class I've taken at Cornell so far.  Lectures were fascinating and readings in the second half of the course were especially fun.  Probably the only time I'll be able to read about an explorer and then have a Q&A with that explorer the next day.

Class is fairly easy. Tests are based entirely off powerpoints; not necessary to read the text. You do not necessarily need to attend lecture; but you must review the powerpoints before the test! I urge you to attend though, because Squyres is a very interesting guy. The Mars Rovers reviews are very fascinating.

This class was by far the most amazing class I have ever taken! There were a lot of guest lecturers which were interesting, but when Professor Squyres taught on the NW Passage, North & South Pole Exploration, Space Exploration, and the Mars Rovers, the lectures were incredible and un-missable. I'm so glad this class was a part of my education!!!
Lots of people fall asleep in lectures, mars updates are cool but useless for exams. the class is boring and sections you just do math worksheets or other useless information.
Riveting.  He makes the science exciting and the whole thing comprehensible.  Conveys the big picture and then brings details of his own work into class.  Challenging but boy, is it worth it.
Great course.  Graded on a few writing assignments that require research... but the essay topics are certainly interesting.  Squyres is definitely dedicated to teaching his students.
This guy is a genius. You learn a lot from him. The big BUT is that his exams are beyond difficult.

This class has been my favorite by far at Cornell. His lectures are always interesting, his Mars Rover updates are awesome, and he's just a really great guy. I'm taking ASTRO 280 in the fall with him and I cannot wait. He's the best professor at Cornell in my opinion. Take this class, you won't regret it!
He is a good professor but is not clear about what information is important for tests.
one of the best classes I have ever taken.  Squyres is amazing and i HIGHLY recommend
AMAZING class. I suggest you take it. Squyres incredible.

Incredible Professor.  Engaging, articulate, and very excited about what he's teaching.  I could've gotten the same grade in the class by not attending a single lecture - but instead didn't miss a single one.  Sadly enough it was what I looked forward to throughout the day.
Astro 104 was great because of his lectures. I looked forward to his mars updates everyday. He helps make Cornell world class by bringing his expertise to the class.

Cool Guy. Loves what he teaches and gets very excieted about Astronomy. Being a Lead Investigator on a really really big space mission such as MER is beyond awesome. Good Luck in your future endeavours Dr. Squyres.

His lectures made the class worthwhile.  I wish he hadn't been splitting the lectures with the other prof.  A bit harder than normal for an intro class, but again I think that was the other prof.  Overall brilliant guy, great at lecturing.
Excellent lecturer.

Squyres is amazing, great guy and great teacher, who loves teaching. He saved this class from the other prof, Margot. Take whatever class you can get into that Squyres teacher, as long as J-L Margot doesn't make up your tests.

Great guy.  Really knowledgable and practically experienced (he is the lead scientist for the Mars Rover Expedition).  Great lecturer - clear, makes the material intresting purely based on the science, not on lame gimmicks.
Best professor I have ever taken.  I have learned more in this class than all others.

This definitely was a hard class.  But I think if you worked hard you learned a lot.  The thing I liked best about Prof. Jordan was how helpful he was outside of the classroom.  The first reviewer seems sour and needs to go back to grammar school to learn how to spell.  I would suggest this class to anyone who is serious about the subject.

If you really want to learn finance and are not afraid to study, this professor is the guy to take.  I learned gigabytes more than my classmates who took the same class with other professors.  If you want a top job on Wall Street, take Professor Jordan's class.  It's that simple!
Ditzy, unorganized, high screechy voice.  Very unprepared for lectures.  CANNNOT teach.  HW/lectures/readings have no correlation whatsoever.  One of the worse professors I've encountered at Cornell.
Overconfident professor who thinks he knows that he's doing. Lectures are highly unorganized. Homeworks are very ambiguous, testing material not taught in class nor textbooks.

Generally interesting material covered but Prof. Wolf has a "my way or the highway" approach to the subject matter, all while claiming that debate and discussion is an important facet of the course. Grading is fair, but be prepared to say what Prof. Wolf wants to you to hear rather than your own opinions about the subject matter.

I was really excited to take this class for my major, but Wolfs style of teaching really hurt the subject matter for me. Hes very matter of fact and actively invalidates other perspectives. He rambles on and on while making the same point 5 times in 20 minutes. Lots of papers that are arbitrarily graded. Subject has potential, but hes rough

I was first scared away from taking this class because so many people told me it's a hard class. It turned out to be a fairly straight-forward, insightful class! Professor Wolf is very good at explaining overarching governance concepts and organizing the course material. There are some group projects and weekly essays, but overall not a hard class!
One of the best professors I've had at Cornell!
Amazingly clear lecturer. Presents very interesting material. Is a very critical thinker and demands that same level of thought from the class.

Great professor. Class offers lots of opportunity for discussion and is generally interesting and well organized. That being said, there is a lot of work for a 3 credit class (weekly essays and lots of readings to keep track of)
Arrogant, pompous. Walking cliche of the 'Ivy league prof'. Smart guy, but annoying at multiple levels.
I personal did not like him but the class itself was ok. He just rubbed me the wrong way, but you do learn a lot. He is the problem not the class.

thought he was great. organized and interesting lectures...responsive to any questions. class is casual and always open for discussion. responses to readings due each week, all in all, not a lot of work.  learn a lot

Thinks he is God's gift. Grades based on whether or not he likes you, not the percentage you get. When I questioned him about my grade, he wrote back basically telling me that I wasn't capable of understanding the material. Major jerk! His class completely turned me off to the subject area.

Great Lecturer. Very nice professor. My only complaint is of great personal bias which is that he used too many "2"'s in his exams and homeworks on complex analysis. The amount of confusion I got when trying to differentiate between if what I wrote down was a 2 or z. Not his fault of course, completely mine however that is my greatest gripe.

Professor Strogatz is a great guy and he knows his math, but I really struggled with the content and his style (which was not obviously structured and hard for me to follow). Plus he had beef with the other 'main' instructor of the class who was making the exams, and it felt like prelims were more in line w/ what the other prof taught/focused on.

Strogatz is a real gem. Being a timid freshman, I was intimidated by the difficult concepts of multivariable calculus, but through his lectures, I became more confident in my abilities. Although the lectures went slightly off-topic sometimes, it was all relevant information as they focused more on the application and I really enjoyed them!
Great and very smart man. It was my first cornell math course and I never took multi so I got destroyed but just be on top of thingds and youll be fine.

Beyond being a great lecturer and being passionate about what he teaches, Prof Strogatz really cares about his students. Even though our classes were online, he tried to interact with us as much as possible and would always stop to explain if a student was lost. You could really tell that his goal was not only to teach but also to inspire us.

His teaching style and delivery was dry and uninspiring for the most part. Compared to some other teachers I've had at Cornell, he didn't seem very excited about what he was teaching. His pedagogy skills weren't very noteworthy. Sometimes his decent sense of humor would come through, or he'd talk about something interesting unrelated to diff eq.
I am watching his lectures on Youtube. Professor Strogatz is great at presenting materials. Also, he's fun and inspiring. I am glad that this course is accessible for everyone.

Steve is an excellent professor. He's able to take complicated topics and explain them with great ease and clarity. This class was both interesting and well-run. Sometimes the lectures get behind the homeworks and it becomes harder to do a few questions though. Steve's also a nice grader and the class is curved pretty generously.
Steve is a living legend.

I took him for the upper level math class that was crosslisted as the graduate mechanical engineering course. He is beyond kind and really takes time to prepare his lectures and references helpful parts of the book that he wrote. He even says hi to me when I see him  in Malott. Overall, an amazing individual who is dedicated to his students.

The most engaging math class I've ever taken at Cornell. I like how Professor Strogatz uses visual representation to convey concepts. The material and grading is also not too hard. Awesome class overall.
My favorite lecturer at Cornell. He keeps class interesting and is very clear. He is also very available outside of class
Fun class, lots of games and mini-projects, grading is vague though
Steven is hands down the best Maths professor ever.
Great professor, well organized, very clear lectures and homework, reasonable tests and grading policies.

He was a really great professor and really tried to make math engaging. He worked with you at your own level and always tried to incite discussion between students. We had short reflective journal entries after each class so it really wasn't much work.
Great Professor, makes difficult topics very clear and fun. Lectures are pretty entertaining and interesting; goes at a good pace. Really helpful and a nice guy as well.
Awesome Prof

Fantastic professor. Hard, but worth it. Curves grade to a B. Definitely knows his stuff, one of the best math teachers I've had. Makes lectures interesting and funny. If you put in the work, you will definitely come out of the class with the fundamentals of calculus down.

This is the first year he taught Analysis. While it wasn't bad, it certainly wasn't good; while he makes lectures enjoyable, he ended up spending a lot of time on material that wasn't ultimately necessary (like failed historical proofs) while glossing over much more important info. Awful book, awful TA, and lectures weren't as rigorous as his HW.

Professor Strogatz is a great teacher. He has vast experience in Math and Physics which he incorporates into his lectures by explaining how certain theories and methods can be applied. Not only is he great at teaching the material, but his lectures are also entertaining and casual, which makes class much more enjoyable.
As good of a professor as you could possibly hope to have. Clear, helpful, and a great speaker.
An excellent professor.

He offers tons of interesting case also the clear and deep reasoning behind them. His course about Chaos definitely give me the new perspective about the world and the way to understand it. Love this guy!

He is one of the "star" professors at Cornell, but he sure is not a "star" instructor. He is intelligent, has insights, and so on - but he is not able to communicate his thoughts effectively & correctly. Plus, why does he make students memorize trig formulas and geometry formulas for DiffEq exams? I guess that adds "stubborn" to his teaching style.

I find him to be extremely rude.  He shows up late to office hours (the day before an exam!!), and left a few minutes early after cutting off a question because he wanted to go home.  Overrated in my opinion
He is a great lecturer and he keeps class interesting. The only bad thing I have to say about him is that he is not very approachable outside of class. He gives off a "your wasting my time" persona.
Great Professor!  One of the best I've taken so far.
Best damn teacher alive!
AAZING professor.  I think he is the best that I have had at Cornell so far.  Always makes the class laugh and is very clear.
A wonderful human being, having Strogatz for a professor is like having your friend's cool dad teach you math.
He's so great
Real funny guy, makes entertaining lectures.
Strogatz was a great professor.  He taught difficult subjects with clarity.  While his grading was fair, it was a little inconsistent throughout the semester

Strogatz is the best professor in the math department. He has a very relaxed style of teaching and knows his stuff. This class in particular had a very comfortable pace which made it easy to pick up the material. Highly recommend!
Strogatz is the best Math prof I have had at Cornell by far.  He is very good at explaining things and he tests very fairly.  He is also very funny and will not bore you in class.

Strogatz is a funny guy. He was also a great lecturer and knew how to break down concepts crystal clear while capturing the class's attentions (just sit down in one lecture and listen to his witty/hilarious remarks). Homework and prelims were fair, final exam was killer. My friends and I didn't find him too friendly during office hours though..
Excellent lecturer, but not very good at writing the exams. Homework is fair.
His explanations are perfectly clear, and apart from being a brilliant professor, he is an excellent teacher. His exams are fair. I would highly recommend Strogatz for any course here at Cornell.
LOVE strogatz. funny, fair, and makes math interesting (hard to believe, i know). my favorite professor at cornell

Could not ask for a better professor. Explanations are ridiculously clear even in the most confusing subject matter. Funny, and always makes class interesting. Rewards hard work by making tests a lot like homework and weighting homework heavily.
By far the best professor that I have had here at Cornell. I even bought his book.

If you have an opportunity to take a class taught by Prof. Strogatz, I'd highly recommend it. His lectures are clear, engaging, and helpful (a refreshing contradiction to most of my experience at Cornell). If you do the homework, which might take some time but is always doable, you will succeed. *Note: don't take the chaos class from anyone else.
Good teacher; the material is pretty dry but he is quite clear and knows somewhat how students think. We just re-used the math 293 textbook and notes that he posted online.
good
The lectures largely followed the book, but that's because... he wrote the book.  Both were very well done.

Superb at lecturing-- puts all other profs to shame.  Leading mathematician, yet manages to be crystal clear and helpful in his teaching.  Knows exactly what students have trouble with and will always address these problems during lecture.
Strogatz is a great professor, hands down. Lectures are as interesting as math can be, and he has a fun personality. One of the better professors I’ve ever had.

A bit arrogant at times and indulges in self-promotion a lot, but let's face it, the man knows what he's talking about and can teach better than just about anybody. Gives a clear picture of the material and makes sure you know how to apply it.

Professor Paling is clearly a capable web developer with a lot of field experience, but he has a lot of difficulty teaching the concepts. I was fortunate to come in with web development experience, and that allowed me to do very well in the class, but my peers who did not have experience struggled because of his teaching ability.

Very little taught. Spends 2/5 of lecture doing 'housekeeping' related to upcoming assignments, which should have been in an e-mail or on the class site(Piazza). The next 30 minutes are filled with tangents/anecdotes, without explaining the code shown. At the end of the course, 1/3 of the enrolled students showed up. We all learned more online...

I really enjoyed this class a lot! Prof. Son is very caring and approachable, and she does a nice job keeping everyone engaged. There's not too many assignments for this class- 1 short writing most weeks, a midterm, and a final project + short essay. The class is pretty discussion heavy. I feel like all the topics are super interesting though!
Absolutely unfair. Mocks students for taking class for an S/U option. Unfair and fickle grading criteria; does not know what she's talking about. Thick accent makes her lectures difficult to follow.

Prof. Son is great!!! She is caring and always very patient. Students in class had good discussions and connections, and we felt being respected. I enjoyed the class with her. Definitely one of the best professors at cornell!
can only get A- if you dont do extra credit assignments

Prof. Song is still a great professor. KOREA 1102 is a little harder than 1101 though. You have to learn a lot more grammatical structures and vocabulary words. An A is still achievable, but you will have to put more work in. Attendance policy is the same. The final project is a group skit.

Prof. Song is a kind teacher who cares about her students. Daily discussion is primarily taught by 3-4 TAs and attendance is mandatory (absence for 2+ weeks = grade drop). Lectures are taught in English 2x a week. NO PRELIMS/FINALS! Just a final project! Remote biweekly lesson quizzes. Daily homework. I went in knowing NOTHING and learned so much!

The most structured and organized class I have ever taken. You will learn Korean extremely well if you complete everything on time and show up to discussion. If you want to pick up the Korean language fast and are willing to put in the work, this is the best class ever and Song ssn is the best professor out there.
Very helpful and clear. Is "strict" about attendance and homeworks etc, but if you put in the work, you will learn the language

She is awesome! She's always willing to help out with any question, will incorporate Korean Drama clips into the syllabus to show examples of people using certain expressions. The only annoying side (as is with all language courses, is the daily WAL at Noyes, but oh well...). The homework is not bad either! Definitely recommend her! 재미

She teaches Korean for people who have absolutely no knowledge of the language. Really nice, funny teacher. Will try to be "strict" but that just means she wants you to attend section...which is part of your grade, haha. Very helpful, highly recommended!
Super interesting material, although lectures can be somewhat dry. As close to an easy A as you can get at Cornell.
Professor Sonnenstuhl is extremely knowledgable about on campus life. His lectures are applicable to every day life. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them all to succeed.

Professor Sonnenstuhl is awesome. Super knowledgeable about on-campus issues pertaining to school values, Greek life, and alcohol consumption. Class involves weekly discussion sections with TAs who are junior/senior leaders on campus. Super chill lectures with iClicker participation, and two research paper projects count for main grades. Take it
He is such an amazing professor. I highly recommend taking a class with him. Fair grader too

Excellent teacher, one of the nicest I've ever had. Will give you as much time as you need to clarify any course topics. While lectures can be dry, the interesting course material and relevance of classtime to graded papers are helpful.
Professor Sonnestuhl is a great guy.  His lectures can be dry though.  If you study, you're sure to get a great grade.  Highly recommend this professor for good grades.
Very nice and easy but incredibly boring. Wouldn't recommend it if you arent in ILR. The lectures are completely useless.

I fell asleep in every lecture. Lectures are unorganized,  class is useless, and I don't recommend it to non-ILR students. Luckily he co-taught with Sam Bachrach. However, he is one of the nicest people I have met- he genuinely cares about his students' well-being and is always more than willing to help out if you are having a rough time.
Expert on Alcohol Research
Clear organized lecture.  Unproblematic guy. Tests were very fair and representative of the material.

Dr. Lin was great. He gave clear explanations of topics during lecture, and was lowkey funny in doing so. Homework was helpful to prepare for exams. Dr. Lin highlights which lecture topics will be on exams, making it easy to know what to study. He was also extremely accommodating and easy to reach outside of lecture.

Professor Lin is an amazing professor. If you're going to take orgo, you should pray that he is the teacher. His lectures were well prepared and easy to follow. The tests were a lot easier than the practice prelims. I would often go into the exams thinking I was going to fail, and then I would come out of every test confident.

This class was the toughest I have ever taken, but that is no fault of Professor Lin's. This would have been unbearable under any other professor; he did everything he could to make a difficult class manageable for us students. Anyone who dumps on him can't differentiate a hard class from a bad professor. You're lucky if you take orgo with Lin.

His lectures are easy to follow so using the textbook isn't necessary (I found understanding the textbook to be hard). The prelims are easier than the practice prelims given and cover the material explained in the lectures.

Very good. Works well with students. Ochem is expected to be hard, but the lectures were solid and the tests were fair. He likes to meet people in person, but be aware that the class size is going to be large.

What a professor! I came into organic chemistry with a lot of fear, and Professor Lin made it much better. He is always very calm and makes sure to explain every question you have. He cares a lot about his students and their success. He is also an amazing person to talk to outside of orgo. I heard he's teaching Chem 3570. Please treat him well!!!
Came to office hours for the professor, stayed for the dog.

I was the meme where the dog is walking itself. There is only 1 OH offered a week which is not enough!! During corona, he gave us even more difficult exams, with the averages dropping by about 15 points (4 exams are 90% of grade), increased the workload from 2 psets a week to 3, while lectures became more mundane. He did not pass the vibe check.
Great AP professor. Explain things in a clear, organized way. Exams can be tough but grading is fair.

Professor Lin did a great job teaching Organic Chemistry. His lectures are super clear and organized. His exams focused more on applying the concept to new situations rather than memorizing mechanisms. His exams can be challenging sometimes, but the grading is fair.

Prof. Lin did an okay job considering it was his first time ever teaching undergraduates. However, I found this class incredibly frustrating as he would never build topics off of one another and would never emphasize anything during lecture. Lectures were mostly him talking to the blackboard. Also, he held very few office hours.

It's hard to make an extended lecture starting at 8am engaging. Dr. Huson is very kind and includes just about everything you need to know on the slides. Communication started to dwindle by the end of the semester and there wasn't a lot of preparation before the final... class ended very abruptly. The discussion sections are relatively unhelpful.

Great class with lots of real-world applications. Guest lecturers included industry professionals and she organized a QA panel and dinner to meet them as well. She was able to share a wide breadth of knowledge on the subject and keep the course work engaging.
Great experience and overall I learned a lot in the course. She has a very clear passion for her work and is more than happy to meet with students to help ensure they succeed in the class.

Overall, I liked Dr. Husons teaching style which relied pretty heavily on memorization of powerpoint slides. Projects usually fun also. She does a good job of trying to make the material practical and interesting, which I also appreciated since genetics can be pretty dry. Get ready for group projects galore

Dr. Huson has officially been my least favorite professor here at Cornell. You will either absolutely love her or strongly dislike her. Her teaching style doesn't teach at all. She literally copies everything directly from the textbook onto slides and then reads them word for word and adds "basically" before everything she says as if interpreting .
She is so understanding and caring. Thought some of the assignments were unnecessary but overall such a fun class.

Ms. K is the best! Her lectures were super interesting and the group projects were a lot of fun. We also got to host a fundraiser and go on a field trip to a food bank in this class. The projects and assignments all had super clear grading criteria. She is also a sweetheart and responds to emails fast and is accessible outside of the classroom.
Good professor, cares about her students and makes lectures very interesting.

Not that interesting of a class and she goes over a LOT of material with very little/poor explanation of it. The case study was not a well made assignment and she really does not teach well - more like a brief overview. That being said, slides are posted, there are many opportunities for easy points, and she grades VERY easily. And she's nice!

Prof. Kolakowski is one of the most caring and knowledgeable professors I have had. Her lectures (about the hospitality industry) were interesting and engaging. This class was during the Winter - it is fast-paced and project-based. Prof. Kolakowski gave in-depth feedback on all of our assignments. Would highly recommend taking a class with her!

Steve's INFO 1200 was so entertaining. However, this class has a TON of reading, and a tests that really grills you on your comprehension. If you're good at reading and understanding nuanced points, you will thrive in this class, it literally made me switch my major to info sci. But, my friends who hate reading and writing struggled- be warned!

Really interesting class. Prof. Jackson is a nice and knowledgable person. Many readings, but not bad if you're interested in tech and/or law. The policy memo makes up 25% of the grade and wasn't graded until finals week. But, aside from that, the class is really doable. I got a B- on the memo and still managed an A. Recommended!

Lectures were always pretty clear, reading was very dense in this class but the two professors eventually lightened it up a bit due to student feedback which was nice. My grade was a complete mystery to me until it came out on student center, and you're only graded by a midterm, final, a paper, and participation.

I'm happy with my decision to take this class for a distribution requirement. It wasn't super easy but it wasn't horrible either. Grade was composed of 15% kinda hard prelim, 25% 4 pg single space paper, 20% easy final, and 40% participation (including weekly "response" 200-300 word papers).

At the beginning of this class, I regretted taking it because there are many dense readings assigned for hw, but as long as you keep up and take copious notes on them + the lectures, it's definitely doable to get a good grade in this class. The first prelim (MC) didn't go too great for me, but the final (explain the term) made up for that.

Took his sp22 trial class- computational sustainability on earth- interesting guy, interesting class. The class was 3 hours but more peer-led discussions, not lectures. About 2-3 hours of reading before the weekly seminar, final group project, and leading one week of discussions with a group- not a difficult class at all!

Clear lecturer, but he has a longer time slot so it's sometimes harder to stay focused. Course content is interesting and not too difficult. Covers a lot of relevant topics that make doing work more interesting. He'll sometimes forget things, but it's a rarity.
learned more from steve than lowi or kramnick and thats saying something because those profs are amazing and I loved their classes and learned a lot. steve jackson is THE man
really helpful. i agree with the post below though, jack moran is a bit harsh.
useless assignments and bogus grading
jackson is really nice, but over-analyzes researching and writing... his class is pretty useless if you've written govt/econ/soc research papers before this

Steve Jackson is the kid who was nerdy in high school but involved enough in whatever project he was working on that he just didn't give a flip what you thought.  He's very eager to help, although his mind is supercharged enough that it's sometimes hard to keep up with him.

Steve was a nice guy. Lectures were useless, but very helpful in office hours. Cared about his students and very interested in their progress, especially when his research interests converge with yours. Great guy for advice. I'd honestly say Steve was one of the top 10 profs I've had at Cornell.
The class is dreadfully boring.  Jackson comes off as arrogant but knows his stuff.  The students just don't care about the class

The worse part of the CIW program, Govt 500. He takes what little fun and adventure there could be doing research and squashes it. It's never clear where you are going for this paper, because it's done in stages. His research advice is also unhelpful.
Poor speaker; lazy, does not prepare for class ahead of time; not really interested in students.

Clearly loves the material, however, he is very disorganized in conveying it.His thought process is almost impossible to keep up with and follow, but he cares a lot about his students and wants to see them progress.Too much front loading. I don't recommen
Jack Moran is better.

A little disorganized but very helpful and caring.
Very tedious material, a decent amount of work for a FWS.
A hard class, and prepared to work for your grade.  Good content, lectures and labs.  Just a lot of work if you want to score decent in the lab.
Class was disorganized. Assignments/Labs poorly made. One of the worst professors I have ever had. In general, don't take this class with this professor.

Horrifically disorganized course. Actual lecture material was fine, but provides no annotated slides/lecture notes. Makes it nearly impossible to study - practice problems given with no solutions. Labs were a mess and instructions were unclear and graded extremely harshly.  Actively tries to make it hard to study and understand the course material,

Must've been his 1st time teaching ECE 4750 bc this course devolved into chaos in the 2nd half of the semester. To be fair, the course started out ok but he raced through the material towards the end and the lectures suffered b/c of this. Labs are A LOT of work & amount of guidance / help provided wasn't nearly enough. Take this course with Batten.

Lectures relied on past materials, lacking elaborations on complex concepts and ample examples. Handwritten notes are illegible and not posted. Labs demand unreasonable testing and analytical rigor without enough instruction. Exams are brutal since there are no prelim practice problems, only 4 psets without solutions to check answers.

The most disorganized class I've ever taken. extremely harsh grading projects. didn't provide details on how points are deducted. didn't finish a lot of topics that were taught in previous years. For half of the class, no handouts or helpful readings are available. Handwriting was so messy. No practice problems or materials to study for the final.

Most incompetent professor to have taught comp arch over the past few years. Left plenty important materials untaught or briefly skimmed over. Homeworks are unfairly graded and we were asked to do many things that serve zero educational purpose. He doesn't publish annotated versions of lecture notes and he shows zero sympathy to student requests.
He's a really good professor and teaches you about trade-offs in architecture well. A little disorganized, but I enjoyed taking this class!
I liked the class, some better organization would be helpful, but he's a good lecturer and the material was interesting!
Awesome class.

He gives decent lectures but really lazy and sometimes even secretive. For example he would refuse to give out even homework solutions. Also he even flat out refused to answer students' questions about grading because according to him "it's not productive to wonder about your grades"

Funny guy and decent lecturer, but super lazy. He literally canceled several lectures for no reason. And he absolutely refused to give out practice prelims and homework solutions for studying. Also he (probably deliberately) left important parts of his lecture slides blank. You have to pay attention in lecture and work a lot on your own.

Great professor! I had him for ECE2400 and I learned a lot from him. Very secure and he definitely knows his stuff. If you want to learn, this is the professor you want to take; on the other hand if you want an easy A, I recommend going somewhere else because Professor Martinez is going to make you work for it.

The class was quite challenging but really interesting. Exams were really difficult but if you understand the lectures properly you should be okay. The professor is very passionate about the material and thats really inspiring. Overall, very helpful class. Learned a lot.

Funny and engaging lectures. Few caveats: lecture notes are sparse and assignments cover a fraction of material. First assignments were quite straight forward, last were quite time consuming. Exams were very difficult due to lack of material provided for prep. Overall, very rewarding class - learn all of CS 2110 and more. Take this class ECEs.

Martinez is a great teacher, he knows his stuff! Class wasn't too much work at all, there are roughly weekly quizzes, two prelims and no final. The only problem was that he had really sparse lecture notes, so you had to pay close attention in class and take good notes to do well. Overall, I would recommend taking a class with him.

Acts menacing, and is menacing. Explains concepts clearly in lecture (you MUST go to lecture), but labs can be near impossible. Tests are very tricky, and practice is not relevant: you need a good intuition to do well on the exams. Learned a lot from the class, okay professor
Exams are not fair, labs are tedious and boring, avoid this prof for 2300.

The course is not supposed to be difficult but this guy manages to make it very painful. The labs are extremely tedious, if not impossible. This guy is completely under-appreciated. Although I had him for my engineering 1050, and he showed up maybe twice and made his TA organize everything.  For 2300 (the class that mattered), he was the exact opposite, he was very clear with his lectures and tried to make sure everyone understood the material. So far 2300 has been my favorite class.
Bad prof

Not the most friendly person. Very strict when it comes to deadlines. Not given enough time to have even a slight chance of finishing prelim. intimidating to speak to, as if he looks down on his students.

Absolutely the best professor out there
Such an inspiring professor... Jose Maria always goes out of his way to help his students. In all honesty, he is the reason I became a SPAN major.
Whoever said JM has a big ego probably doesn't know him at all. He is a really caring professor and always willing to help. Never saw him making fun of a student for not having the right answer.
Awesome!
Jose Maria is wonderful. He is such a great guy and loves participation of any kind. He is super knowledgable and friendly. There is no way not to like him!
My favorite professor from all times. I have taken two courses with J.M. and they were both excellent. Yes, he is not an easy grader, but then again he is brilliant.

I had him in fall 2006 for Spanish 215. He is a great professor. Very, very understanding and helpful. Reading is manageable, but very hard at times. Have to read, because he will call on you unexpectantly. Grades essays quite hard. Very focused on grammatical errors in essays rather than content. Overall good professor, loved his accent.
Awesome prof, but tough on grading.

Jose Maria redefines A+. I have taken SPANL 316 & SPANL 215 (formerly 318) with him, and I can only say that he is the most hard-working, dedicated, and enthusiastic professor I know. His class is always an enjoyable experience.

The best SPANL class I have taken so far. Jose Maria is a brilliant professor, even if you struggle in Spanish, he will inspire you to learn. He is also very understanding and is always willing to help.
He is really good keeping 20 students awake. Gives detailed examples and knows literature incredibly well. His class is always fun.
Amazing guy. He has so much knowledge to give... best of all, he is willing to share it. You do have to read the novels for his class, though.
Can't get enough of him! I used to dread Spanish, but now I love it because of Professor Garcia. He has really helped me the improve the quality of my essays.
Good and interesting.
Prof Garcia is a really nice guy. He is from Spain so his accent is flawless. Class has a good structure and he makes it interesting. I wouldn't hesitate to take another class with him.

I took SPANL 316 with Professor Rodriguez-Garcia about a year ago. He is very intelligent and his lectures are full of life. Thanks to him, I decided to double-major in Spanish literature. If you must take SPANL 316, make sure it's with him.
Jose Maria is a great professor. He has a solid knowledge of Spanish literature. Moreover, he is a very caring professor. Definitely take him if you can.
He is the most helpful and dedicated professor I have had at Cornell. I definitely recommend taking any of his classes.
The best professor in the Romance Languages department. He loves teaching and truly cares about his students.
Best lab TA ever! He grades pretty easily and he really knows his stuff. But more importantly, he plays Lady Gaga during labs and blew up a gummy bear in our last lab session. Really nice guy.
Lab TA.  Not the most helpful or most concise TA out there, but he does grade relatively easy and will help you when you ask.

Terrible professor. Save yourself and do not take an FWS with him. He made a class that should be an easy A a horrible and dreadful experience. Not supportive to students, a stickler for citations, and rude. I never looked forward to this class. I saw my peers in other FWS's doing less work and receiving easy A's for simply doing the work.

Avoid at all costs. Perhaps the most passive aggressive professor I've ever had. Professor chastises the students for not remembering the most obscure details and refuses to repeat. The distinct lack of empathy is only accented by his condescending tone. If you are taking this class in the future, may God have mercy on your soul, for he will not.

Dates/times for assignments change without proper notice, professor nitpicks for grammar rather than content and provides resources but then penalize the student if they were misinformed. professor encourages no work over break, but then is amazed when the students do not have an entire essay draft the day we come back. in short, AVOID IF POSSIBLE!

If Abby Lee Miller was a teacher. Professor is belittling to 18 year olds who are just learning how to write at a college level. You would think he cared about the students the way he advocates for mental health but instead he shames us every class for small mistakes like not knowing obscure grammar rules. Visible fear in students when he teaches.

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM! This professor was extremely inaccessible and seemed to find joy in his students hardship. He doesn't respond to emails and office hours are limited, unhelpful, and during times when other classes are. One of the worst classes I have ever taken. Don't even bother trying because even your best work won't be enough.

This professor seemed to lack empathy for the wellbeing of any of his students. Ideas would be shut down, snarky remarks would be made, and he would consistently talk badly about students. The syllabus was always changed and due dates would switch without prior announcement. EVERYTHING is a violation of academic integrity including misspellings...

AVOID this class and instructor. The syllabus and grading scheme changed over 8 times this semester. 

Nearly everyone I know got a B- or lower. The writing standard is excessively high for an introductory course. Other FWS courses are much MUCH easier. Even humanities majors struggled, and a strong writing background doesn't guarantee even a B.

Do not take a class with this professor. He is the most passive aggressive professor I have ever had. He will constantly shame and belittle you, and will accuse you of violating academic integrity even if you guess on a test question or misspell a person's name in a paper. He is insanely strict for no reason.
Lovely professor! She is very motivating and truly cares about her students. Her lectures are meaningful and she teaches things you can use throughout your life not just in her class.

WORST INSTRUCTOR I'VE HAD IN 13 YEARS OF EDUCATION. AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS! She gave me < 50% for participation, but I talked every day in class. Those who talked off-topic or never got 100%? Prof Belogolovsky is a great professor. The best I've ever had at Cornell. Her class is very interesting. You'll learn a lot. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and always willing to help.

Great Class. Took her for compensation. The material is extremely dry but I enjoyed the class mainly for her wit and humor. Very helpful and wants to see students succeed. Her tests are meant to trick you, something I did not enjoy about the class. Lots of opportunities for extra credit to make up for poor tests. You'll learn a lot in her course.

Took her for HR and for Compensation, got an A+ minimal effort. Lots of extra credit opps. Very willing to help, give points back/curve. Compensation had 3 prelims, a group project, and 2 papers, but minimal studying and work prep needed for all of them.  Group project took 2 hours total to prep for.  No final which is SO worth it

Prof. Belogolovsky is really not a good professor. Her lectures don't relate to the tests at all and are a complete waste of time. Her prelims are poorly written and are more of a semantical game than a real test of the material.
Prof. Belogolovsky is the best prof I've ever had. The lectures were very organized and interesting. I LOVED this class. Would highly recommend.

Belogolovsky is really sweet and brings a lot of energy to class. I would agree that a smaller class size would better fit her teaching style because she likes to ask pose questions to the class, which is difficult in a lecture setting. Sometimes she gets flustered, which makes her an easy target, but she is overall a dedicated, knowledgable prof.

LOVED HER CLASS! I can't understand other poor ratings. I agree she'll be better at teaching a smaller class, but her teaching wasn't awful. She listens to students and genuinely cares about their success in class. TAs are helpful. No final, 3 prelims (all multiple choices) Get the textbook for prelims and assignments. Prelims are easy if you study

Belogolovsky is a great professor & person. Her negative reviews aren't deserved. It's understandable that HR is not everyone's favorite discipline, but she does well in teaching the material. Her lectures are clear, she lets you know what's on the exams, and the course outline is clearly defined in the syllabus. Relatively easy, would take again.
Very caring prof. Class works backwards so you do classwork and learning for hw and do the assignments in class.
Wouldn't take her course again.
She's great, its a lot of work but its not wholly difficult and its pretty useful stuff

Her quant class is very helpful. All of the assignments could be finished in class and youre given a group you can collaborate on everything with. Not a difficult class. She also the only one of my professors this semester that acknowledged Shawn Wests passing. She gives plenty of resources and she cares!
Terrible Professor. The accent is hard to understand. Seems lost in the lectures.
Never take her course again. Worst of them all.
Terrible Teacher. Comes late to the class. Was the least caring professor of all time.

I love his lecture because he try to explain why you should learn concepts, properties, and theorems in the graduate students' point of view. Especially, he tried to make connection between probability and your research area, how to adopt what you learned from this course for your research. I got A, but I heard that he had tough grading policy.

Absolutely no learning in class, lectures are same to same content from text book. Exams r hard. Tough grading policy , professor does not make clear his grading policy he will talk in terms of mean and median , normalization if yo ask for grading criteria and will make you confuse. Better not to take this class ever. Professor is in USC now.

You won't like probability at all after taking this class. You would not learn anything in lectures, lectures are dull and boring, lecture notes are from book only (same content). Exams are very hard . Professor shows no pity even though nothing of that sort is taught in class as he ask in exams. Recommend, to avoid this professor.

Probability is a very hard course and he made it harder. Does not give grades in exams and sets them too hard. His grading scheme is also too hard to get past - he expects you to get 85+ to get a B, which is very challenging given the nature of the subject. Not friendly at all.  Do not study under him. It is a disaster.

RVR is one of my favorite professors I have had at Cornell. Knowing that you're being taught OS by someone who worked at Bell Labs with the creators of Unix and C is very compelling and inspirational. He is hilarious and his office hours are immensely helpful, more so than TAs. He is also very active on Ed. His demos in class are also insightful.
Man is a legend of his field. Super smart and caring!

I loved having RVR as my professor. He can come across as disorganized at times, but it wasn't a big deal for me. I found that he was a hilarious professor that obviously knew the material he was teaching so well yet was so down to earth and super approachable. I thought all the homeworks and projects weren't difficult and the prelims were fair.
Prof. RVR's lectures are quite good, even if they move slowly.
good professor but class is often disorganized. grading and exams aren't representative of the content covered in lectures.

RVR's weekly assignments were sized appropriately and reinforced the lecture materials, reasonable workload. He was helpful after lectures in answering questions, and walked through difficult assignment questions. I wasn't a fan of his exams and this was my downfall - it required a deeper understanding of concepts than what is provided in lecture.
He's one of the most genuinely caring and personable CS professors I've had at Cornell  I feel lucky to have him as a professor tbh
he is a really caring person, and I found his lectures easy to follow
the whole course is a mess and won't teach you much stuff. The professors and TAs are unhelpful. You'd rather self-study instead of taking this class
Although he is kind, its clear he did not spend much time preparing for lecture. This resulted in a very disorganized course.

Professor Merritt was overall a great lecturer, and prioritized learning Greek over assignments and exams, which was clearly reflected in how he graded. While quizzes and midterms could be tough, and grades were not posted on canvas, he was adamant that our final grade reflected our knowledge of the language. Very passionate, I would recommend.
Very good lecturer. He teaches the first half of the course but honestly wish he taught the entire course
Grimson is a really clear lecturer. Tests are hard and it's a lot of memorization but all the information is in the lectures.  Material was really interesting though and the class is curved to a B+.
Good lecturer, presented info clearly.  Tests are hard, but it's biochem, so it's to be expected, but he's as good as you can get for a difficult, pre-req class.

Professor Grimson teaches the first half of the 2-credit biochem.  He is a great professor who explains things very clearly most of the time.  He attempts to keep things interesting and provides many real-life examples of technologies that are relevant to the material being studied. It's a lot of material, but it's very interesting. Good professor.
I took Latin with him and did not learn much. Not only was the class boring, but the reading was very dull. He's also very egotistical. He rarely responded to my e-mails.
I took Music 1101 with Professor Hicks. It was abysmal.

Music 1101 is dreadful. Do not take this course. Out of all the courses I've taken at Cornell, Music 1101 has definitely been the worst. I have not learned anything. Lectures are dull and assignments are more than tedious.

The most inspiring, knowledgeable professor I have ever met in Cornell. His study is highly interdisciplinary. The lectures are amazing. They revolutionize my way of thinking about music as a non-major.

The textbook is very useful since the homework assignments come from the textbook. Lectures are useful as well, and the professor gives a 5-minute break during lectures. The course itself is not too difficult and is really straight-forward.

Logistically a mess due to Zoom. But he's a good, very old-school lecturer. I wish I had more time to spend on this course, because it was extremely rigorous and the hardest I've worked for 3 credits. I didn't enjoy it, but I appreciated what he was trying to do. I'm not a MechE so I wish I took it with someone else with a more streamlined approach

Methodical, clear lecturer, if at times a bit fast. He encourages questions; he insists that we ask questions we are afraid to ask, because we are never alone in having them. Very accessible outside of the classroom for extra help. Takes time to address your questions. The homework and tests are hard, but they are effective.

The course curriculum set by Professor Ruina was very poor. Professor Ruina also seems to be a bit arrogant and needs to humble down. The way he runs his lab is also very poor. Wouldn't recommend his classes to anyone.

Terrible Professor. Not accommodating whatsoever. Tried asking specifically what to study for exams, his reply, everything you learnt since freshmen year is free game. Out of the 60+ homework questions and practice papers from 2000-2020, youd expect something to come from there right. Nooooooooo.

Prof. Ruina is truly amazing. Lectures are clear and well-structured and he makes the course content really engaging. The workload is quite heavy but it also helped me so much in understanding the material. He really makes an effort in making sure that students learn in his class and that's why he's my favorite professor at Cornell.

Prof. Ruina is hands-down the best professor I've had at Cornell. He's so incredibly accommodating (this is review is being written during the coronavirus pandemic, btw) and he really cares that his students LEARN. His lectures are very interesting and you can tell he genuinely enjoys the material he teaches. Cannot recommend him enough.
Decent professor. Difficult class overall. He is very knowledgeable about Dynamics, though sometimes goes into extreme detail. You will need to work extremely hard for a good grade.

Every MATLAB script I have written has benefited tremendously from lessons and examples provided in class and in our textbook. On top of his superb hands-on style, Professor Ruina is one of the most understanding, accommodative teachers Ive ever had, and he gave me invaluable help in a time of need. I cant recommend him highly enough.

I have never been more offended by a professor than with my interactions with Professor Ruina. My recommendation to him is to treat his students with more respect; people are more than their work. You can ask hard questions and challenge students without being rude.

Prof. Ruina is a great professor!  I have had 2 course with him and in both his lectures were clear, digestible and forced you to think.  He holds LOTS of office hours. You do have to work in his courses but that's engineering - doing lots of problems. If you are a delicate flower then you will be offended by him. But he cares about students.

I like Professor Ruina so much! I took three courses( Intermediate dynamics and vibraion, Dynamics of Flight and Advanced Dynamics)from him and did two projects with him. It is a pleasure and even honor to work with him. He is the reason why I am pursing my Ph.D. research in dynamic walking and robotics. To me, he is a mentor, more than just a prof

Ruina knows the subject matter in and out, really encourages asking questions,  engages active strategies to encourage understanding and class participation, and is always trying to improve. However you will work for your grade, and his attitude tends towards tough-love. If you are okay with that, you will enjoy his classes.

Worst Professor ever! He may be smart but his personality and teaching style makes many many students dislike him. I don't know why there are positive reviews unless they share his affinity for disrespecting other people.
I really like Professor Andy Ruina. Compared to other professors, Andy did a very good job in teaching. His way of grading students is really good. Everyone could get a better grade in his class.

Excellent lecturer. Lectures are very well organized, clear and concise. He even has a systematic way of erasing the blackboard during lectures. He's smart and knows the material he's teaching very well. However, his textbook is really bad. I liked him and his teaching style but frankly, I didn't really learn much from his textbook.

Ruina is the reason why I chose mechanical engineering. His teaching style is clear and concise, makes the material very approachable and interesting. I've heard in the past he wasn't so great, but it's clear he has perfected his teaching style since then. He is my favorite professor from my college experience.
Entertaining and Helpful
Very fatherly. Ruina embodies the spirit of tough love.

Although the material is difficult, I feel as though Ruina's lectures are well-organized. He drops your lowest exam and homework grades, and I feel as though he's not trying to fail us. The emphasis on MATLAB is very strong (which I personally don't like), but it seems as though this might be useful in the future.

Ruina is probably one of the smartest guys I ever met and he definitely tries to help students (ie exam problem redos, dropping lowest grades, etc.). However, despite his good intentions a few things backfire (ie exam redos result in simply a higher mean with smaller deviations). I hated how he used a textbook he wrote that just echoed his lecture.

Textbook is not useful at all.  Lectures are fast and confusing, it almost seems as if he tries to confuse you on purpose.  It was hard for me to understand, esp since the textbook was so poor.  He def tries to be helpful though, and drops the lowest homeworks and prelim probs.

People respond to Prof. Ruina in one of two ways, they either love him or hate him, which is evidenced given his middle score rating. My experience is that he lectures to the top portion of the class. That being said, the course is hard. If you have to have him as a teacher, then be prepared to do alot of work with the TAs and ask alot of questions

He is perhaps the smartest guy I met. He is a very good lecturer, especially if you are interested in understanding a subject deeply. Pay attention to everything he says in class, and try to figure it out if you do not quite understand it -- you will be rewarded.

I thought he was a decent teacher, though it's ridiculous that we had to buy his crazy expensive book...of which we only used half (the first half was statics). He seems to know his stuff...but I have trouble getting past how much he likes himself. He thinks he's really funny, and so even when his jokes are okay I don't want to laugh.
This guy is awful. problem sets are impossibly weird, TAs never know the answers, half the time there are no answers. why should we have to live with matlab&him 24/7 anyways ???
That book is terrible there is a reason why it is not published, but Ruina is a decent teacher
Kinda weird but nice. All you have to do to make this class easy is buy the solution manual to the textbook. Not that bad of a professor.. wants to make it clear to the class.

Doesn't really like preparing for class, grading, or doing much of anything except answering questions. Problem is no one really knows what to ask. I'd look for someone else.
This guy can really Ruin-a class.
Eight years later I still have bad memories of crazy Andy and his piece of crap homemade textbook.  If you have ANY opportunity to take Dynamics from someone else, take it.

I had Ruina about 5 years ago - you might not like him, but you'll never forget him.  Like it or not, you're probably gonna have him for Dynamics (which is a widely hated course no matter who teaches it).  So bite the bullet, buy the book, live in office hours, and learn the stuff.
