My only regret is that I didnt take a course with him sooner to allow me to take more courses that he teaches. Highly recommend

Tests you on ridiculously minute details, oftentimes mentioned in passing during lecture or readings. ALWAYS go to class, do the readings beforehand, study, and you will do fine. Slack off and those tests will kill you.

Captivating professor. He posts lecture slides, but I found that I could have taken better in-class notes. He includes questions directly from the textbook on the prelims and final, so read the textbook. He doesn't return prelims but lets you see them during OH, and he reuses several questions on the final. Final40% Prelims20% Paper10%

The best professor I've ever had. Interesting, intelligent and incredibly talented at explaining concepts during lecture. Go to lecture and do the readings and you'll be fine. Pre-lims are slightly difficult but fair. Lecture is always interesting. Term paper is easy but make sure to incorporate a lot of your own ideas

The lectures are fine. The problem is the material. You learn little about social psychology. Instead, you memorize experiments. Take the class if you are a psych major. Otherwise, stay far away.  He also claimed that psych majors know more about economics than econ majors, so I guess his brain just works differently than everybody else. Ironic.

Gilovich is a great professor. He is smart and his lectures are incredibly interesting. He is quite a rockstar in psych and he exudes knowledge about the subject. The tests are straightforward though they require a very thorough reading of the textbook

Terrible class. Gilovich clearly cares and knows his stuff, but the class is very poorly organized. It's a large lecture for a topic that NEEDS to be taught through discussion, so lectures end up being him rambling about random topics in psychology. Grading is unfair, super harsh, and nitpicky. Unless you're a psych. major, DON'T take this class.

Professor Gilovich is one of my favorite professors. He really knows his stuff and shares it with you in a really interesting way. I really enjoyed his lectures. That said, his tests can be hard, even when you study; there's a lot of nitpicky details from the books. Overall, definitely take the class. You learn a TON of interesting things!

Loved this class, so many interesting ideas applicable to everyday life. He is a fantastic lecturer and he also offered a review session before every test that I would recommend. This class is hard however. Make sure that you do the readings because his exams can be tricky. One of my favorite classes at Cornell.

My favorite class at Cornell, definitely take it. So interesting and applicable to daily life. Gilovich is a rock star in the psych world and he knows all the material by heart + wrote the textbook. Both prelims and the final are horribly specific. Read the textbook word for word. Attendance not required but will definitely help you on the test
Psych 2800 is a great class, the tests are a little tricky but overall everything was good. Make sure to do the readings!

Really great lecturer. Tests are a little hard and readings can make or break you on exams. He is a little scattered sometimes but overall I had a great experience with him as a lecturer! He also held review sessions before tests, which were nice.
A great professor! His lectures were fun and interesting every time, and he played cool music and videos. Very understanding and helpful.
While psych 2800 requires a little bit of work, it is worth it.  Very interesting and a must-take for psych majors and a great class for non psych majors.

I took him for Social Psych and the class was fantastic! He's a really great lecturer and the material was really interesting. His prelims were really hard though; he's REALLY into nitpicky details from the book that you could overlook. Despite the hard tests though, it's a great class!

Goes on ad nauseum about the smallest details and typically goes off on a tangent during his lectures. I am a psych major, and even I have difficulty finding interest in his lectures. At least the TA is bearable.

Professor Gilovich is a great guy, but this class was SO hard. The prelims were ridiculous and borderline unfair. He packed so much info into his lectures that it was nearly impossible to stay awake and keep good notes. I tried really hard in this class, and it still didn't pay off. Only take this class if you love psych more than anything.

I took writing section (WIM), so experience was different. But Tom is a great researcher and speaker. Lectures do trail off in liveliness towards end of 75 minutes, partly because he throws out so many experiments. I didn’t study, of course, but when he went over prelims, I was grateful I took WIM — MC are hard! I Recommend WIM, TA was very chill.

Very good lecturer. Engaging, never very dull, and very clear explanations. However, exams are very tough (means in  low 60s usually). The class is also a lot of work, as there are mandatory and often lengthy readings. It's also a little annoying that he expects you memorize multiple experiments. Overall, class is good, but definitely demanding!
Tom is a chill professor. His explanations are very clear.

Gilovich is by far one of the most captivating lecturers at Cornell. Fascinating subject and he makes it fun and interesting. His class was tough, but if you attend classes and do the reading you will be fun. Definitely take this before you leave Cornell!

I was a little surprised about how boring I found this class, especially with all the comments on this site. He was my least engaging teacher, and would throw a TON of experiments at you for each topic. The tests were graded unnecessarily harsh, too. He curves, though, so don't worry. And I recommend taking notes on the slides as you go.

Probably the best prof. I've had at Cornell. Very enthusiastic about the material. Also knows the stuff well, since he wrote the textbook and conducted a lot of experiments presented in class. Each lecture contains a lot of information, so make sure you stay focused through out. Tests are hard, but they are well designed and fair. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Incredible, incredible speaker-- never even went close to nodding off during his class. The way he presents material is incredible. (Tests are hard, not going to lie, but if you do the reading and really remember the experiments it talks about, you'll do well. Another plus-- he helped write the book, so all the lecture stuff is covered.)

He is probably the best prof I've had at cornell. He's extremely interesting and a fantastic lecturer. He uses the book he wrote for the class and the readings were almost enjoyable to do. The prelims were pretty hard but they're curved so it doesn't matter too much. Not the easiest course in the world but not a lot of work definitely worth it!
fun class
GREAT PROF.  GREAT CLASS.  tough grader

Good professor and interesting lectures, but made tests intentionally hard, and would go over prelim answers extremely quickly so you couldn't really understand why you got certain questions wrong. One of those professors who will pick out small details from textbook that are often looked over to test you on. Read CAREFULLY. Otherwise, OK class.

Interesting lectures, but incredibly unclear and tangential.  Designs tests to be intentionally difficult and low-scoring.  Irrational requisite for attention to detail.  Requires much more work than the average course in the department.  Only advised for students who have a profound interest in the subject matter.

Tests are incredibly difficult multiple choice questions, often confusing and contradictory ten times.  Tries to make class hard.  In all, it was doable if you put the extra effort in, but not sure it was worth the time. Means on exams were low, but lectures were (sometimes to rarely) interesting
Great lecturer!! good class
good lecturer and interesting material but tests were unreasonably hard for a class that most took for an elective

This class was great! material is fascinating and gilovich is a great lecturer. Regan talks waaaay too fast, but they both give outlines for each lecture which makes it easier. Pay attention to experiments and do the reading. Take this class if you can!!
He's a great professor, and a great speaker. When I'm trying to do a presentation for another class, I try to speak like Professor Gilovich, and the presentation goes well.

Not only is Gilovich brilliant, but his lectures are interesting and even humorous. Sometimes his lectures are identical to the reading, but that's because he co-wrote the textbook. Tests are tricky, but if you go to class, do the reading, and study, you will do fine.

Take this class! Gilovich and Regan give you lecture outlines, which means that instead of frantically scribbling notes for 75 minutes straight, you can listen to the (mostly entertaining) lectures. Gilovich throws in a lot of fun material, and is clearly passionate about psychology. The textbook he co-wrote is sometimes even-- gasp!-- fun to read.

Neat guy. Knows the subject intimately; he's really well-known in the social psychology world. Heck, he was one of the co-authors of the brand new (and very useful) textbook. Good sense of humor, too. But yeah, prelims are pretty hard. Take good notes (or get TakeNote) and do all of the readings carefully, especially in the textbook!
Very knowledgable and a good lecturer. Tests are very difficult though.

Probably the best professor I had at Cornell. His lectures are incredibly interesting and very practical. Difficult class but if you study the material and read the book, its not too bad. This class is definitely worth it. Gilovich rocks!

Gilovich is the greatest! He's very intelligent and extremely amusing. The subject is interesting, but Gilovich makes it intriguing. I signed up for 350 next semester cause I thought Gilovich was teaching it, but it turns out he's not, and I am really sad. Oh well. Definitely take 280!

Gilovich is the man!  He and Regan have very different styles, but I found both to be effective lecturers and I don't even think it's fair to compare.  Gilovich is "flashier", I guess - powerpoints, videos, funny stories.  The class is tough, tests especially, but well worth it.  I loved it!
Very hard class (tests are brutal). Very nice and helpful guy (I found him a bit less helpful than Regan). Lectures are very interesting and good.  Great class

A pretty good, entertaining lecturer. BTW, I strongly disagree with the person who perferred Gilovitch over Regan. They’re both good profs - Gilovitch might be more charming, but I think Regan actually has the edge on explaining things and caring about students. Good class overall if you're into it.
Loved his class.  If you think he's overrated, know it isn't so: I read his book as an undergrad, and now 10 years later I have to read it again for a law school class.
this guy is awesome! the best teacher i had at cornell!
No Comments
Gilovich is awesome.  He is very intelligent and always clear.  I wish it was just Gilovich teaching this class (rather than him and Regan).

Knows his stuff, but he speaks in a monotone, after a while it gets boring. He has no facial expression!  This guy makes psych more boring than it has to be.  His questions are tricky on exams, esp for 280.
im naming my first son after him!
Great professor, funny and helpful, but sometimes not quite clear.
really good lecturer, inserted a good amount of fun material into class. made all the topics interesting, even when describing the details of an experiment. take psych 280

Good prof, tries hard to makes class interesting. He uses good examples and makes points clear.  Have to say though, tests are short, so pressured to do well on so few questions and his questions on tests are ambiguous.
This is the most boring class I ever took at Cornell. More boring than Chem 207.
Awesome professor. Why can't more instructors be like him?
No Comments
He's like the nicest guy ever! Plus, he rides his bike to class! Awesome teacher!
Really hot, cute, i love him, i want to have his children, he is so passionate... about psychology... =D

Took both his American Econ History Courses (3310 & 3320). Classes are full of info and Lyons is a great lecturer. You ABSOLUTELY HAVE TO GO TO CLASS and TAKE GOOD NOTES, if you skip lectures you will be screwed since there are no powerpoint slides and the class is graded on two prelims+final with pretty much all the questions coming from lecture.

This guy is hands-down the best professor I've ever had. He's almost unbelievably relaxed and his classes are fascinating. Tips: 1. Go to class, do readings. 2. Nothing phases this guy. He will happily answer questions like "which readings actually matter?" in office hours. 3. The "Mechanical cotton harvester" is a trick question.

Get ready for a throwback to high school history class, just with more material to rote-memorize and regurgitate on the tests. Which by the way are graded by a grad student who doesn't even attend lecture. Tom Lyons is the archetype for checked-out, tenured professor who genuinely doesn't care. Go to every lecture, take copious notes and memorize.

He's a living textbook. I've taken his American Economic History course before, but the Chinese Economy course was a completely different beast. Just go to class, take down notes, and you'll be good to go. An advice I received is to think about what the core concepts are and study that. Sujan is also an amazing TA!

Going to class is a must in addition you must take very detailed notes. the exams will cover very obscure things but his office hours are helpful, readings not necessary at all. Overall is a tough teacher, study the handouts, and study in a group. Not flexible on grades and almost all the class gets a B+

Definitely lots of information in a 75 minute class. Use a laptop, because you're gonna be jotting for a while. Some people may consider him to be a bit boring, but he uses subtle humor about Frank Sinatra and other stuff that no one really understands b/c they're about old stuff. Really smart guy with lots to say. Lecture and reading   mandatory.

- Super clear lecturer, TONS of info given in class - Readings are not very important; much much more important to attend class - Tests are straightforward but will fully test your knowledge. Pretty much all short answer. Fair grading but will take points off without much hesitation - Moderately interesting class; NOT MUCH MATH which was great
Great Prof

Mostly lecture-based. No powerpoint slides and readings are useless so if you miss one class its a big deal. Tests were generally fair but there is a lot of information and classes are very boringearlymonotonous. Only take him if you are planning on going to every single class and taking very elaborate notes.
Great Professor with crystal clear lectures.  Helpful as long as you attend his office hours.

great professor! lectures are clear useful and full of information so notes are necessary. readings are pretty useful too. only thing is that outside of the readings and lectures there isn't much else to help you through the course. generally a good challenge of a course but not impossible. again great prof though definitely recommend him

Gives out tons of information in class. In the syllabus it says the readings are mandatory, but just skim them. Exams are straightforward but not easy. Overall, not too bad but I wouldn't go out and tell people to take this class. Take this class only if you are a morning person and/or don't mind note-taking.

He is one of the most knowledgeable and helpful professors in the entire department.  I took two of his classes before, and was totally impressed by the plethora of information this guy possesses.  He does, as some reviews suggest, become a bit monotonous from time to time, but his subtle humor nevertheless gets the class's full attention.  Bravo.
Great teacher, so long as you like tons of information.
Very clear about his information. He might be monotonous sometimes but he has an underlying wit that keeps people from falling asleep. The man is a faunt of historical information.
No Comments
Completely unreliable.  Says one thing and does another.
No Comments

His lecture style is to mostly just talk. It can be a good or bad thing depending on the person. For me, his style makes me pay attention in class. He's pretty clear too. And as long as you have good notes from class you'll do fine on exams. The assigned readings are just extra.
Tom Lyson was the best professor Cornell has ever had. He was dedicated, dynamic and brilliant.We will never see the likes of him again. He's in Professor Heaven! Look down on us kindly!

This professor is deceased after fighting a courageous battle with cancer.  He cared deeply for people and the world around him and was devoted to the creation of a sustainable food system.  His concept of "civic agriculture" will reshape the way people view the food system.  He will be remembered with love and respect by all who worked with him.
VERY easy grader.  Class was boring though - very repititive and pedantic.  Rather arrogant and not nearly as bright as he thinks he is.
Course = Social Inequality.  Best course ever, read interesting books and then discuss.

This guy is a living legend.  He has over 500 published papers, and has been the pioneer for the field of chemical ecology.  His story-telling is fantastic, and all of the stuff he talks about is just so interesting.  One of my favorite professors that I have ever had, I stand in awe of his accomplishments as a researcher and a teacher.

FANTASTIC! Incredible storyteller, beautiful speaker; brought a sense of wonder, excitement, and commitment to nature to every lecture. Also, he's hilarious! I really loved this class and encourage everyone to take it; no grades, just for its own sake. you will relax, learn a lot, and enjoy.
There's a facebook group called "Tom Eisner Fan Club" because he is teh awesome.  His lectures were entertaining and informative.  And my chem HW this week used some of his research!
An amazing array of visiting and local speakers - whether you consider youself a naturalist or not, take this class.
An amazing class. He brought in a ton of great guest lecturers, but I thought his lectures were the best. He is so cool and a great biologist, but he talks very quietly.

SO OLD AND SO GOOD. Sometimes hard to understand because he moves around a lot and speaks softly, but if you pay attention to what he says, your mind will be blown. One of the most fascinating lecturers with the best slides. Funny, too.

Every undergrad's dream biology professor. I saw someone wearing a handmade "I Want to Be Tom Eisner" t-shirt around campus. That's how cool he is. There's like five different professors who teach this course and he's definitely the highlight.
Simply Amazing Professor.  One of the Best at Cornell, a man every undergrad should meet.

I heart Tom Eisner.  Catch him while you can.  (He's really old.) I took this class the first semester it was offered and there was no work, just a guaranteed S.  It's like getting credit for watching the discovery channel or national geographic.
Eisner is the greatest! He's so hillarious and cute and engaging-- I highly recommend taking his course!
Amazing prof. funniest and most interesting lecturer I've had here at Cornell.
this guy has a lot of interesting stories to tell.  have a conversation with him if you can.
grandpa!!! hes awesome. bugs blowing stuff out their butts at other bugs!
This guy is brilliant and he's a great teacher.  Very funny during lecture
No Comments

Homeworks are kind of difficult and really really long, but they are all due by the end of the semester. There are no practice exams provided, so taking notes on the slides will be the best bet. I avoided lectures since he spends most of the time going over impractical examples. Class is not hard, but it is TONS of boring work.

DiCiccio's lecture style is to just read off of notes he posts online. This course has the reputation of being one of the hardest in the stats major and that rep is earned. DiCiccio makes it as easy as possible, with lots of helpful office hours, and a very generous curve at the end. Probably the nicest guy at Cornell.

Diciccio is super nice, open to all questions, and accomodating. Only take 3110 in the Fall if you can. Class is straightforward. Lots of HW but it is all due at the end of the semester with recommended deadlines during the semester. Exams can are a breeze if you follow the HW

Although Professor DiCiccio was very accessible outside of class and had a good sense of humor, he delivered EXTREMELY boring lectures. If you can take a different stats class, do that. Even if it is slightly harder you will at least have a better time doing it

One of the funniest and chillest professors I've seen at Cornell. That said, not huge into the whole teaching thing. If I hadn't taken stats before class would have been infinitely harder since lectures are tough pay attention to. Overall very easy class if you know what you're doing, but not a whole lot of learning for me. Fantastic guy though

Professor Diciccio is an awesome man, he explains things clearly, although in a pretty fast pace. Overall an pretty awesome course in understanding basic concepts and notions of Statistics. Worth taking!

Many students enjoy the class due to his extra credit offerings. As a student in ECON 3120, the lack of depth/rigor in his material is punishing. I indicated difficult for the class since it was excruciating to read his paragraphs on slideshows. AVOID!!! You will not learn with him. He gives no feedback and never responds to email.

Nice enough guy, but worst class I've taken, coming from someone who considers themself fairly good at math (although I've never taken stats before). Lectures were convoluted and slideshows had full essays on each slide, but it was never clear what any of them were supposed to mean. Whole bunch of words thrown at you, never any explanations

I love him so much. Very very fair. Very flexible with due dates. One hw per week w/ unlimited attempts to get a 100, one test (take home, more than 24 hours to take, covered half course material). Two extra credit opportunities. Responds to email fast, very helpful in office hours. Don't have to go to class, can watch the lectures asynchronously

Professor DiCiccio genuinely cares that his students are understanding the concepts without being overwhelmed with work. His assignments focus on key-concepts that are reviewed heavily during lecture. He was incredibly accommodating for online classes. If you work hard, an A/A+ is definitely attainable with him.

Undoubtedly the GOAT. The nicest professor at Cornell who, unlike most here, actually wants to see his students succeed! Seriously a gem, super understanding and his office hours were really helpful throughout the semester for someone like me who struggles with this sort of stuff. Couldn't recommend his class more.
Literally the kindest man I know. His classes are extremely well-taught and his sense of humor is awesome. Really cares about his students. By far my favorite professor at Cornell!

I love his lectures and he was definitely a sweet person. But the problem is that he wasn't so mathematically rigorous and the difficulty was low. So if you love high grades and easy things, go ahead and enjoy. But if you are into math, please turn to a stats professor that is no an ILR professor.

He's actually the sweetest professor I've ever encountered. Even after we moved online he constantly checked on us and was very considerate and caring. He has a good sense of humor and lecture isn't boring. The course is not easy but he grades very generously.
i loved his class! insanely easy, and he makes lecture fun with funny stories. 11/10

He is the best. Some would say he is a bit boring, but his dry humour is what makes his class the best. Not only that, he is very generous with grading, very hard to fail his class. I put off 4090 because it is a hard class, but he made it extremely survivable.
Best professor at Cornell! He is truly always there for his students and wants to see every single one succeed! His office hours are also helpful for the homework!

VERY amazing professor, hands down the best. He makes courses interesting and often interjects with an anecdote or stock advice to keep up entertained. I learned a lot from him! He is lenient on the homeworks and would definitely accommodate you if you have difficulties meeting deadlines. Also the tests are easier than the homework!

This is a straight forward statistics class. It's not a big deal if you have never taken stats because the only thing you need to prep for the exams is the lecture slides and homework. Going to class isn't that important but he gives funny stories and is very accommodating. Have to study even if the tests are open everything. Take 3110 with him.

Tom Diciccio is the best stats prof you'll find. Lectures are dense but he does his best to make dull material interesting and often pauses lecture for a "break" in which he'll tell stories about his past or explain the importance of investing in your future (get that roth IRA!). Extremely helpful in office hours, class is curved heavily also.
Terrible lectures. He clearly doesn't prepare them very well and does not care about the class.
Everything is take home. Doesn't necessarily mean everything is easy. Can be entertaining in class, but you don't necessarily have to go.
Hardest class I've taken at Cornell

His slides are very dense material-wise but the class isn't difficult at all. Never took stats before and did fine. Homework is an easy 100%, attendance at section is unnecessary. Tests are long w/ a lot of questions but open everything. Diciccio is good at explaining things if you go to class and pay attention and tries to keep things interesting.

tom isn't super into teaching in general but will be helpful if u reach out. homework can get really annoying cuz they sometimes don't really have anything to do with the lecture material but he makes the exams fit perfectly with the lecture slides which he makes available. discussion completely unncessary if u can do hw alone
Great professor very accommodating still learn lots of material but very lenient.

this man is truly an angel on earth. a heavenly being sent to bless cornell university with his presence. never will you meet a kinder, more accommodating and merciful math professor. he makes an effort to make his class the least stressful as possible. also his deprecating jokes give me life

Never went to class or discussion. HW is easy, you can submit online until you get 100%. Midterm+final are open everything -- do hw & just open up slides & Google as needed. Extremely nice in grading.
Tom is hilarious and clearly really smart. He's a real expert in statistics, so I feel like we're lucky to have him teaching a basic stats course!

Being statistics, classes can get a bit dull at times, but Diciccio tries to make it more bearable by joining around a little. He is really helpful in his office hours, and is extremely approachable. His lecture notes are really useful, and in addition to the Webassign homeworks, are more than enough preparation for the exams.

Tom was a really nice professor. He knew class material was boring, but tried hard to liven it up with interesting stories about statisticians and his past at Stanford and in Canada. Pretty easy tests, a lot of self-learning, but he is really cool during office hours and he is very flexible and understanding.

Prof. DiCiccio is a super nice guy, very approachable, really wants you to succeed. The webassign HW's are kind of a pain but a guaranteed 100. Both the mid term and the final were open notes, open book. The class avg was not good but he curves to an A- I believe. Attendance is not really mandatory. All material overlaps with AP Stat.
Best professor ever. Nice guy who genuinely cares about his students. Also tells great stories to keep lecture interesting

Although information is very dull, he interjects with funny comments. Really easy course if you want to fulfill a math requirement. Didn't feel like I learned much though. Assignments include short weekly homework assignments, a take-home midterm and a take-home final. Go to lecture and office hours and you will get an A.
Easy even for those who have never learned stats before. On-line quiz and take-home mid-term and final. Good sense of humor. Generous grader. However, not l much to learn from this class.

A great class if you're looking something to fulfill your quantitative requirement but aren't the best at math. He explains well and the textbook he uses is the best math book I've ever used. If you do the reading and don't put off the assignments, you will get an A. Though you don't always need to attend class, the guy is hilarious when you do.
Pretty clear, lots of writing

T DICICCIO is the bomb. Although lectures can be dry, their loaded with great info. prof very helpful. Take home midterm and final heehee, and really overall nice guy in general. Has a funny sense of humor (u gotta listen for his jokes haha) and his complaints about classroom technology are hilarious. Recommended to take him!

Prof. Diciccio is one of the top statisticians and one of the smartest profs I have ever had.  He knows the ins and outs of the stats industry, and he knows a range of material very well.  He has a good humor (a little awkward but it lightens up the class).  There was only take-home exam which was pretty straight forward from his teachings.

Really boring subject, but if you pay attention, you can do really well. Even if you don't, you can still get a good grade because of his ultra-generous curves. Really helpful (though not always punctual) for office hours, and good about granting HW extensions. Really funny too: has a lot of bizarre anecdotes and often mutters things about Prozac.

I hated that this was a mandatory class.  The material will be useless to most people.  Not really a hard class, but it's all theory and could give some of you problems.  DiCiccio is a good guy though.
His sense of humor keeps lectures bearable while he curves his tests so that everyone does well, even though the tests can be tough.

This guy is awesome. His tests are really easy and his deadpan humor makes the class really enjoyable. All of the homework answers are given in section too. Plus he's very helpful during his office hours. Great prof.
Very tough course, but Prof. Diciccio makes it ok.
Diciccio is a great professor.  He makes stats as fun as it can be.  His funny stories and personal remarks cut the intensity of the subject material.

This prof rocks.  He makes stats seems not only doable but also entertaining.  He is an excellent lecturer; probably one of the best that I've had.  And, he is not overly horrid with grading.  The curve and his teaching style are definitely plusses to getting through this course.  If you need to take it, take it with him.
Cuts through the normal **** most stats professors put you through and gives you the straight up dope that you'll ever need in the real world. very cool, easy to work with. Highly recommend.
Curves so that over half the class gets A's and class is open-book.  Absolutely take Diciccio!
A truly amazing professor!  He makes stats so entertaining and easy.

He is very strict with students attending lecture ON TIME WITH ICLICKER. If you show up 2min late you might as well go back to bed because you would have missed the iclicker. His lectures are extremely boring and homework are harder than what he expects in the lecture. His instructions are confusing and his jokes are lame too....

Really enjoyed Evans lectures. Study for the tests by reviewing the homeworks closely. A lot of people say that his office hours are confusing. Always clear where you stand compared to others due to his clear grading criteria with distributions for every homework and prelim. Appreciated his organization skills.

I. hated. this. class. He took an intro level course and turned to to something way too complicated. Little to no use of the textbook, and dont bother trying to study from it. Nearly the whole grade was based on two tests. Essay questions were super confusing and feedback was even worse. A lot of hard work but it didnt matter.

about 3/4 of the grade was on two tests. multiple choice is not bad. short answer was really tough (even though you study) and comments on answers were unrelated, vague, and still confusing as to why you got it wrong. we didnt use the textbook. graded it tough, no extra credit. a ton of work and assignments, but it was barely 1/4 of my grade.
go to class and do your homework and you will be fine

Ok, Tom knows how to teach an Intermediate Micro class. For a subject that I thought I wasn't very interested in, he managed to be extremely engaging and clear in every lecture. He starts each class in the morning by playing music and then tells a news story related to a concept we are learning about that day. Not an easy class, but enjoyable.

An interesting class. Applies a lot of models and learning to the real world. The professor is clear in his explanations- homework follows what is taught in class, but is surprisingly tougher. It's probably the most challenging part of the class, but if you can do the homework then the prelims are very manageable.

Probably one of the greatest professors ever. Great lectures, mad chill. Homeworks are pretty straightforward and they're pretty easy to finesse. Exams are straightforward. Tom Evans is a great lecturer, he constantly engages the class in thoughtful discussions and he's pretty funny too. Overall a great class, Tom Evans deserves a teaching award.
Evans is really thoughtful and caring. He goes out of his way to help students. Class is challenging but really satisfying when you understand. It takes hard work but totally manageable.

Lectures are excellent and engaging.  Material is delivered at a very quick pace.  Professor Evans was helpful, responsive and encouraged me not to quit, and I'm grateful for that.  Verbiage on exams doesn't match text verbiage, so understanding problems from the text isn't always helpful.  Exams are crazy hard, but he curves.  Survival mode.

Class is overall straight forward concepts and professor is kind and funny. He does his best to bring real world stats into class, but the big downside is that he is not good at slowing down to explain the mathematical process. This makes the tests real rough. People were crying after the first prelim. Good professor teaching a too-hard intro class

Took PAM 2000 in Spring 2014. I really liked him as a professor. He definitely will present his biases on things, but loved how we opened every class with discussion. He wrote fair exams and homework and genuinely care about students.  One of the best professors I have had here. I would recommend any course that he teaches.

Evans had interesting lectures and generated discussion, but never clearly told us what we needed to know. He graded HW for accuracy but when he went over answers in class after, he often concluded that even he didn't know the right answer. Overall, interesting lectures but poor structure
very passionate and it come through in his teaching

Evans is a good professor. He teaches everything in a clear manner, and incorporates useful real world examples. The only problem with him is that he drinks the free market limited government no taxes juice too much. His views are  short sighted and I don't think he thinks critically enough. Might just be a problem with economists in general though

Great Prof. Lectures were extremely interesting to attend. Not an easy prof though. Tests aim to see how well well you apply what you learned, not just knowledge vomit. Graded pretty fairly, and curved fairly too. I thought I was on the verge of B+ A- but got an A? This class is not easy but not too hard either.

This class was a struggle for me. It didn't help that this was Prof. Evans' first time teaching PAM Stats. Prelim 1 was ridiculous, Prelim 2 and the final were fair, and going to his office hours sort of helped. The curves were also fair, because without them a lot of us wouldn't have passed. Never again, though.

Exams can be unfair because there's no partial credit, and he makes mistakes in mathematics often. Also, going to office hours help, but only if you can withstand his condescending tone. Otherwise willing to help and his exam percentage policy is pretty fair. Exams can be long though, just pace yourself.

He is a great lecturer. You never need the textbook - his notes are fantastic as well as his problem sets. His exams are tough but he curves them a lot so everyone does ok in the end. If you study his notes and problem sets though you'll end up doing well (with the curve of course.)
A fine man. I would love to take another class with him. Engaging. Funny. He made you think critically about economics.

Very good prof. Understandable, friendly, interested that the class understands what's going on (both the subject and applicable current events). Can be a hassle that attendance is mandatory, but usually worth it
Tom is a great guy.  He is reasonable and very understanding.  Best professor I have had so far at Cornell!
awesome econ professor....clear, accessible, and curves tremendously

Tom is great guy. I thought he was funny and he always made the lectures interesting. Prelims were unreasonably hard, but the curve is generous. If you have to take introductory microeconomics, take it with him.
Clear, willing to help students learn, gives extra sessions for struggling students, will address current economic conditions.

Evans is so wonderful. His class is so interesting, he is so smart, an so excited to share his thoguhts with the class. He makes great class discussions and is the best teacher I've had yet at Cornell.

Evan's is a great lecturer. He's very entertaining and always teaches exactly what you need to know. I never read the textbook and I did well. The homework problem sets are difficult, but if you understand them, you'll do fine on the exam. Go to a discussion section or some form of office hours if you have problems and you'll get an A.

Great Prof. Insane prelims, though he finally curved them and also curved the grade distribution (i.e. an 85= A-) b/c people did so poorly on the prelims. He is understanding and more than willing to help out. Take advantage of his office hours, they are great. He is a true genius but doesn't understand not everyone else is

Tom Evans is an amazing teacher. He makes every lecture interesting on some level, and his graphs and powerpoints are always very helpful. He's also just a really funny guy who tells good stories and bizarre examples that you'll be talking about after class.

Class is far above "intermediate economics". Evans is clearly a genius but he's not very good at getting his points across. His lectures lack direction, are confusing, and he thinks it's funny that his students do not understand the material. I'd recommend taking PAM 200 with another professor.

Made real analysis super interesting yet built our foundation of the subject. It is his first time teaching as a professor yet he is highly organized and willing to help. Difficulty of course is due to nature of content, but he tries to show the motivation for every result. He taught many topics normally not taught, such as Lebesgue integration.

Analysis is definitely a difficult course, but Prof. Hwang was able to relate the information in an accessible manner, especially considering he was a brand new professor.  In office hours, he was always willing to help make sense out of the information and had very convenient and many hours available.
It's a class that is worth waking up early for... He also gives you tons of extra credit opportunities so getting an A is not too difficult.

I honestly don't know why people like enjoy his class - he is a complete weirdo to the extent that I am creeped out by him. His research on 'laddering' and 'prototyping' the ideal customer is useless and silly - without much support for his methods. This class was by far the best one I have taken at Cornell. Wansink is incredibly interesting, engaging, helpful and inspirational. I can't say enough good things about this man.

Professor Wansink is charismatic, however his students seemed to take a back seat to his book promotion and research.  Blackboard web site was frequently not updated, assignments were not returned in a timely fashion (if at all), and TA support was minimal.  Class would be worthwhile if these issues were addressed.
Amazing guy, very friendly and down to earth.  Incredible dedication to his students.  He works more closely with his students than any other Professor at Cornell.
I've taken all the AEM classes and he is the best of all. In fact he is the best in the world.

awesome guy who cares deeply about his students and makes sure that the class is a collaborative process between students and course staff. He is a great lecturer & provides lots of real-world case studies that go beyond the readings. Really enjoyed the class
Seems to care about teaching but thinks that grades don't matter. His grading seems very arbitrary especially for exams. I don't believe his grading was fair.
Funny guy. A walking textbook
good guy

Great professor.  He writes on the blackboard in an extremely organized fashion, only erasing the oldest thing, and keeping everything in chronological order.  The class is hard, and the frequent random quizzes are a nuisance, but his lectures are some of the best I've seen.

This class is pretty cool.  Professor Kirby's lecture is really engaging.  He was helpful in office hours the one time I went.  I could do without the quizzes in every class tho especially on fridays.  The homework is pretty hard too.

Helpful but most you can study by yourself.  He is good guy, but he missed 6 classed without any make-up.  Exams are extremely diffcult, lecture and handouts are not really helpful.  Auditting will be the best for this class.  He teaches order of 1, and expects order of 10000000000!
Professor Kirby is a good teacher.  He is funny and makes class interesting.  He is very helpful in office hours!  I also think it's cute that he talks about his puppy in class.

Funny guy.  Young, into cool music and surfing, very personable fellow.  Also very helpful if you have a question, clears it up pretty easily.  Makes a lot of jokes that unfortunately a lot of humorless engineers are incapable of understanding.  Only complaint is the incredibly slow grading
Great guy
Amazing professor - very useful course due to its relevance to real world necessities.

Wow, Brian was probably the best professor I have ever had at Cornell. He is smart, funny, caring, and basically I could go on and on. The class is not that difficult, just make sure you read the book before the two tests, other than that, enjoy yourself and the lectures! Speeches are a breeze as well. Great job Brian, we love you!
Brian saved my bacon during my years at CU. A great teacher and better advisor and excellent friend. Far too few Brian Earless in higher ed. Highly recommended!
Prof. Earle genuinely cares about his students and his class was the most useful for post-college life!  He's wonderful!
Prof. Earle is awesome. He's funny and understanding, and you'll learn a lot in this class. A must-take before entering the business world! Per his request, I have labeled him as smokin' hot. Yowza!
Brian's the man

I was unexcited about the class at first, but it actually was very useful/valuable. A must for CALS Freshmen, taught by one of the most quality people I've ever met. He was always amazingly understanding, never giving up until he helped students to the best of his ability.

I just thought that this would be a continuation of COMM 201, but it's so much better than that.  His class is about REAL-WORLD stuff that I will never forget (i.e.: interviewing skills)  Really useful class and you enjoy talking to him just try not to mention that you like the Yankees.
the best prof i've ever had.

I was very unenthusiastic about the class at first, but it actually helped me develop study skills and learn a lot about Cornell's history. Very easy A to offset first semester Bio and Chem. Highly recommended.
Prof. Earle cares about his students and he obviously wants them to be able to take the skills and knowledge he imparts on life-long journeys.  He's a darling!
One of the best in the business. Most applicable course to the real world that Cornell offers.
I graduated in 1995, and even back then, Prof. Earle was one of the best at Cornell.  Take his class, it's easy and you'll learn a lot!!!

Not only a great teacher, but also important in the department. He's a large part of the reason I was able to transfer in, and he even eventually became my advisor. When I think about great teachers at Cornell, Brian is one of the first to come to mind.
Very reasonable guy, funny too.
unhelpful oldie
Everybody should take this class... He is very easy and will give you an A no matter what you do. Easy guy to ass kiss to get a good grade

Great guy, interesting course.
Pretty easy class... funny guy

Absolutely amazing professor. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches and is extremely interesting in and outside of class. He is very good at leading engaging discussions and is not a harsh grader at all. Very entertaining. And the amount of work is fair.

He is an absolutely wonderful professor! He is helpful and his lectures are always interesting. Very open and thoughtful. The one draw back is that the exams are all over the place in what is considered important material. On a side note, I took this course for writing in the majors and it was amazing! Would definitely take a course of his again!

He is a fabulous professor; he explains material well and is extremely responsive to questions. The material is interesting and easy to understand, although there is a ton of memorization. Great speaker; he makes time in lectures fly by. He's very straightforward, organized, and responsive when it comes to answering questions.

Wonderful professor, definitely one of the best I've had at Cornell. He really wants his students to learn. Pay very close attention to the PowerPoints, not the textbook.
Amazing! Loved it.
OB is interesting but Professor Lucas was an average lecturer

This is an amazing class. I thought the content was so interesting that I didn't even mind memorizing it all for the tests, which is, in fact, all you have to do to get a good grade. Lucas won't inspire you in his delivery, but he teaches the material well. Study the lecture slides and skim the textbook.
Read the textbook to do well. Exams are 50% lecture 50% textbook things not covered in class. Lectures are worth attending and Professor Lucas is interesting.

Professor Lucas was a good professor with interesting lectures. His tests were for the most part reasonable and a fair concentration of lecture and textbook material. The only downside is he isn't approachable at all and clearly doesn't want to be approached by students despite his friendly demeanor in lecture.

Lucas is a very good teacher who has very engaging lectures. Going to lectures is helpful as the tests lean more on stuff in class than reading. The course content is extremely interesting. Lucas also allows for a lot of extra credit opportunities. One note is that the tests are more conceptual and situational questions not just straight facts
Prof. Lucas is a great professor. Clear instructions on class assessments and cares about students. He tries to relate to student experiences which is appreciated.

Content is valuable, but the structure could be a lot more student-friendly. Grading is petty and inconsistent, with hidden criteria. "Nothing a TA or professor tells you is guaranteed correct". Relies heavily on pre-recorded videos, actual class time is redundant. Weird 9 P.M. deadlines. Prof's lack of enthusiasm affects learning atmosphere.

I would reccomend taking this class with Professor Whitmore. Tarantino makes her prelims very tough and provides no review or resources for her prelims. The average was below a 70% and she blamed the class on not studying hard enough. All the assignments are graded by the TAs and the rubric is always so vague and unclear. Good luck if you have her.

Tarantino does not care about her students. The videos assigned are extremely boring and redundant which makes the mandatory aspect of the class very irritating. The grading criteria is not clear at all and trivial points are taken away. I really don't think my boss would fire me over having "too much space in a column" so why take off the points?

Not a fan of the inverse course structure HADM1740 (we learn 95% through pre-recorded videos, and in-class is just basically study hall and asking questions to TAs). Professor Tarantino barely teaches anything in person, yet attendance is mandatory. Class average for the excel midterm was lower than 60%, and instructions on prelim are unclear

Terrible prof. Doesn't teach, just has you watch her videos which are hard to listen to because she ends every sentence like it was a question. She isn't very knowledgeable in her field either. She has a hard time answering questions she doesn't expect. I could have learned more by watching somebody else's YouTube videos. Take someone else.
He presents the material very clearly and lectures are organized and interesting.

Even though Kramnick is retiring, I have to leave a review because he's just that amazing. He's the epitome of a brilliant professor in need of a hair stylist. His lectures are mind-blowing: his ability to make anything interesting made me look forward to every lecture and motivated me to really put effort into his class. Highly recommended!
An incredible professor who is world renowned.  I absolutely loved Kramnick.
Excellent class, really interesting
Amazing professor that managed to engage me with a subject I had little interest in. Clear, accessible, and not unnecessarily difficult I recommend everyone take a class with him.

Kramnick is the epitome of an old school, laid back, brilliant professor with wild gray hair. 1 assignment for our grad seminar (a paper) that doesn't have a due date. He said we could hand it in next spring if we wanted. Lots and lots of reading but he's realistic in that he realizes we have other courses and it's hard to read everything. Take him

I am currently taking a online Winter session with Kramnick and must say he is a genius. As a Senior, I have worked with many Professors and Kramnick is in my opinion, the best professor in the Government department. Cornell is lucky to have him! If you are a Gov major you must take his Intro to Political Philosophy course.

Fascinating, old-school professor who is always on his game. Lecturers are interesting and detailed. Would have liked for him to let the class participate and ask questions, but overall, good professor.

Kramnick was a fantastic professor! Got me excited about American Political thought. Lectures could get a little boring by the end, but overall, they were great. I've never felt so connected with a professor in a large lecture class.

Kramnick lived up to the reputation. He is brilliant and it shows. He may be getting old, but he hasn't lost his touch (like Lowi has). I highly recommend anyone interested in government, philosophy, or history to take American Political Thought.
He's really helpful

Kramnick is an award winning professor who really knows his stuff. If you do the reading, you should have no problem.  I didn't and still managed a B+. TA's tend to be very knowledgeable also although they teach in completely different styles and are a little tough on papers

He was very clear in his lectures, but also painfully boring. Many people (myself included) found it extremely difficult to stay awake in class. He's very knowledgeable about what he teaches, but he tends to repeat himself over and over and lectures became monotonouse and uninteresting. On top of that, there is a lot of reading. easy to get behind.

Kramnick is very interesting and enthusiastic about his teaching subject. However there is a TON of reading and TA grading is pretty hard. There is a midterm and a final as well as a term paper so there isn't a ton of work but it also makes it easy to get behind on the reading.

The lectures make the class super easy. If you pay attention, the readings will only become supplements to your essay. The TA's grade harshly, but that is how it is with all Gov TA's at Cornell. Kramnicks passionate, and it really makes the lectures better. He would save a whole lot of time by not repeating the same point over and over again though

Has an incredible love for the material and is a great lecturer. Someone you'd want to be your grandfather! Not too difficult a workload, with 2 essays and a final exam, but the lack of assessment kind of encourages you not to read...and you don't exactly need to know the readings until the final.
Amazing class, as was expected having taken 161 with Prof. K.
Entertaining lectures, highly approachable and will review your essays favorably if you feel your TA didn't quite get it.
Excellent readings, but Kramnick refuses to go into any depth with them. It's a shame, seeing that this is his specialty...

Kramnik was an excellent lecturer, but if you are not a govt major, be wary.  There are only three graded items (midterm, papre, and final), and if you can not express your ideas well and have any understanding about your topic, you will do poorly.  The TA sections are kind of a waste of time, but unfortunately, those are mandatory.

You could probably not do a single reading and get by just on the lectures (although if you are interested in taking this class, these are readings you'll enjoy).  Prof. K is the man, but the TAs vary from exceptional to mediocre at best.  Try to get a good TA then get on her good side.

Although you won't learn anything incredibly profound, this is still a solid intro class. Kramnick is a class-act guy who is  to schmooze with students and help them out. The course itself was pretty straightforward, and is not difficult at all if you go to lecture and see what he emphasizes.
I actually took Prof. Kramnick's intro and upper level political philosophy classes. I loved both classes. I never wanted to miss a class because his lectures are amazing.

Two requirements for a great professor: infectious love of the material, and gets along well with students. Kramnick excels at both (and many more). Has great interest in making Cornell a better place. "And now we come to the most INCREDIBLE SENTENCE!!!..." And yeah, he does act like Woody Allen, but in a good way.

Kramnick is the quintessential friendly grandfather figure with a side of academic know-how and rainbow sprinkles on top. Despite the large size of the lecture, he tries to get to know students personally, which I found really likable. As for the class, the real source of info is him. You can get away with skipping a few readings, and still learn.

Though he acts a little bit like Woody Allan, kramnick is my favorite teacher this semester. He is interesting, intelligent, and insightful. Sometimes the lectures can get a little boring, but I think its more the material than him. Very down to earth, try and have lunch with him and you'll see what I mean.

Amazing lecturer! His lectures always connect with the readings. There's no sections, but there is a lot of reading. Just remember one thing when you go to his class, "the race for life."  You'll know what I mean when you take the class :D. Grading for papers are subjective and varies by TAs.  Go to class b/c prelims require class notes!

Take it if you can, and you're not one of the idiots that thinks there's a war on Christmas.  It's not hard, it's straightforward, and it's better than most other classes.  Kramnick is funny and smart, and even if you disagree with him, you have to acknowledge that he's not making things up or distorting facts.

Kramnick's egotistical, but most celebrated profs are. The material is interesting, but a little boring. It kind of sucked that we never had a test all semester (only take homes) and then had a final exam that was worth 40% of our grade. Eek. I probably did fine though. Oh yeah, and we only talked about Malcolm X for 4 minutes. Learned a lot though

I took a few with him.  I am a government major, who focused on political philosophy, so I may be a bit biased. But I think Kramnick is amazing.  Engaging, intelligent, funny, very good.  I would recommend at least 161 with him.
He's a funny guy at times.. but he condescends fairly easily.. that and I see him as a bit ****.
I loved this class.  I'm not a government major, but I though the lectures were intersting, (even if he does go off topic a lot) and there was practically no work involved.  Easy and fun.
amazing teacher, smart, very clear, brings up some really interesting issues
It's kind of a silly class.  You don't really learn anything...  you just hop along tiny excerpts of texts throughout history until you get to his pet philosophers.  It's easy though.
Course coordinator for GOV 210 - good guy.
Fun and eye opening class

Kramnick is clearly a smart man.  His lectures are very clear, but up to a point where they become redundant.  He'll try to drill the same point home for an entire lecture.  Fair grading.  Reading not too taxing, some of it's optional
Good lecturer despite crazy ideas.  Hardcore liberal.  Class organization is questionable.  Grading seems arbitrary.  Overall fair class.  ***WARNING*** Possible ****.
Kramnick is the God of American History.  'Nuf said.
Great organization and ability to give spellbinding lectures.  Not so helpful, but he has TAs for that.
i agree with the other comments- smart but pompous. grading is tough as well. the course is am polit theory (161) on steroids (366)
amazing speaker and amazing person

entertaining lecturer
too into himself, lecture course not designed to be lecture

just him reading the slide! don't need to come to the lecture at all

He is very nice and fair. Lecture is optional, there's no homework, and there were 3 prelims and 2 papers. All were fairly easy. You can study just by reading the textbook or reviewing slides/flashcards and you'll do good. Interesting, easy A class!

Prof was basically reading off slides that he posted on Canvas so going to the lecture isn't necessary, however, I did think some examples and extra details he gave in class were helpful. The tests are multiple-choice and pretty easy as long as you review all of the slides (No need to read the textbook, the slides have all the info you need).

Great and very understanding professor. Lectures are dense, but he gives amazing review sheets with everything you need to know for the exams and the final wasn't cumulative. I would definitely recommend this class.

- not a bad professor. however, lectures are just him reading off the slides -- slides are straight from the textbook reading and are posted online. not much motivation to come to class
- his study guides prepare you for the content he puts on the exams. exams are very straight forward.

not very engaging class but very interesting content overall

Comically nerdy guy, but nice enough. As someone who knew nothing about CS I learned a lot. Lectures are recorded so there's no reason to attend. Everything's curved heavily. Median was a B, I think.

He seemed apathetic towards students who had a hard time learning the material. His lectures are not that well. He creates like 90 slide power points. Definitely doesn't give as much support to new leaners as a lot of the other professor in the CS department. Prelims are fine. Final is typically a bit harder.

Get ready to work! Labs, assignments, prelims and a final. U will be exposed to a lot of CS concepts thru the vehicle of Python and his lectures will not be enough to cement the concepts. Professor Van Loan is a talented professor, but the course has so much material, that he doesn't always get a chance to fully elaborate on each concept. Class was taught differently than in the past. Very math based and not the best segway into other object-oriented languages. Good if you're in CS and going into data science-y classes.

It's a tough class because the material is tough, not because van Loan makes it tough. Prelims are doable if you do the labs and mostly understand the assignments (which are easily the hardest part of the exam). Everyone benefits from a big curve, but sometimes its hard to compete with the CS majors who do really well on each assignment.
Not very clear during lectures but always available for help.

Very knowledgeable of subject matter. Sometimes is repetitive during lectures, but he just wants to be clear. The slides are posted online for viewing whenever you want. iClicker questions sometimes during class, but your answers only matter for swaying borderline grades. Makes groanworthy jokes

Took CS 1110 Sp15. Really enjoyed the class and thought he did a good job of going over and introducing fundamental concepts.  He makes the assignments fun and thought that the workload was manageable(given that is a CS 4 credit class) Would definitely recommend taking it if he is teaching.

Great professor! Knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. His sense of humor makes the lecture interesting. His courses are definitely worth considering. Don't pay attention to the whiners in intro CS classes who can neither do math nor code!

Nice enough guy. Lectures are well organized and present the majority of the needed knowledge for projects and prelims. Van Loan lectures are hopelessly boring and he makes a lot of mistakes, but if you can stay awake you will learn it. I was cautious before entering COMS322, considering all the terrible reviews. lame, lame, lame.

She's a difficult grader, but I LOVED going to class! She's hilarious!

Horrible!  Plays favorites and does not teach well!  I learnt nothing.

Horrible professor.  I didn't learn a thing; her lectures were boring and focused on elementary grammar points.  She gives EXTREMELY unclear instructions for assignments, and even more unclear justifications for grades. DO NOT RECOMMEND!

Lyrae is one of the most incredible teachers, and inspiring people I have ever met.
