PK's course was on a level all its own. Case studies, daily debates, a research project, and a crash course on political economy rolled into one class. If you put in the work, it can be one of your most rewarding experiences at Cornell. Essential for any serious IR student.

Lectures were amazing . The discussion based nature of the course was one of a kind for a lecture of that size. The length and time given to the research paper  allowed students to do in depth research on their topic. The professor was  unbiased in his lectures, but would never hesitate to challenge students on their assertions.

PK is the best professor I have ever had, and his class on American Primacy was the most beneficial and enriching academic experience I've ever taken part in. He lives and breathes for teaching and will do anything possible to help his students. Head and shoulders above other professors.
I was told that this class would be  memorable and it was for many positive reasons.

This class enlightened me in my understanding of the complicated relationship between politics and economics, both at an international and regional level. The HBS case study method was challenging, requiring consistent in-class participation, which led to thorough engagement with assignments. TAs helped tremendously with the long research paper.

This class was hands down the best course I have taken at Cornell. I recommend it to anyone who is remotely interested in international affairs - any aspect of it! We had a very diverse class in terms of academic interests and that's what made the class great. PARTICIPATION is important!!! Besides, one research paper, which is not TOO tedious.

This was one of the best classes that I've taken b/c of how much it pushed me. But, if you are not interested in stepping outside your comfort zone, do not take this class. The TAs were a huge asset helping us learn the nuts and bolts of int'l finance, case study analysis and how to structure our large 25-30 pg paper.

Professor Katzenstein is an inspirational professor. GOVT 3547 was a demanding class as far as participation, but PK is a fair grader. As long as you prepare for class you will be able to succeed. For anyone with a genuine interest in international relations and achieving a global perspective, this is a great class and fantastic professor.
Great course with a unique setup. You must come to class prepared and ready to talk. The 25-30 page paper at first was very daunting but the TA's are extremely helpful and great. Learned so much.

Great course. One of the best I've taken at Cornell. Loved the setup with the case method. The 25-30 page paper at first was very daunting but the TA's are extremely helpful and great. Learned so much.

PK is my favorite professor at Cornell so far. I took GOVT 3547 with him during the Fall 2015. For the course we wrote a 25-30 research paper, read several economics/finance books, and read and debated many Harvard Business School case studies. I gained a lot from the course and feel more prepared to apply to MBA programs after graduation.

PK is a fantastic professor! I took GOVT 3547 with him this fall, having heard so much about his lecturing style and insights into world politics. Though I think he's still working out some of the kinks with the course's unusual style (case study-based, with a heavy emphasis on class participation), I learned so much from his lectures.

I took Gov 3547 with PK this summer. Having taken his Gov 1817 class as a freshman, I had high expectations. I wasn't disappointed. The lectures were wonderful, the class discussions valuable, and the TAs incredibly helpful. I would recommend this class to anyone with even a remote interest global politics/economics.

Took Govt 3547 in Fall 2015 with PK. Easily the best class and professor that I have had at Cornell!  I loved the combination of HBS Case Discussions along with amazing lectures by PK. I learned immensely and it really stoked an interest in the field of international political economy. Take a class with PK (esp HBS case method) before you graduate!

PK is as amazing in GOVT3547 as in his other courses! One part to highlight in this course, besides its HBD case method, is the requirement to write a full-length research paper, which you choose your own topic. The weekly TA session really helps to let you make step-by-step progress finishing the paper from literature review to the conclusion!!!

PK is finally back from Harvard. Actually, he brought back HBS case study method. Although an experimental course, GOVT 3547 run extremely smoothly during the semester and student participation rate, as I noticed, reached almost 80% at last, quite abnormal at Cornell, even at Hotel School. The course is really for every major!

GOVT3547 was the second course I took with PK. Similar to GOVT1817, US Primacy Challenged was one of the most inspirational courses I took during my time at Cornell; different from lecture style courses, GOVT3547 used HBS case method to study political economy of regional powers around the world. Full length research paper was assigned but no exam!

Katzenstein is amazing. Not only is he a funny lecturer, he also clearly cares about the students. Govt 1817 was a difficult class, because of the many readings. grades depend on TA. do readings or die
Will definitely not take his class again.
Tough class. Prof is brilliant in the classroom, possibly some of the most interesting lectures at Cornell. However, grades are at the hands of the TA who are often quite unfair.

Great Class, Great Professor - There's ALOT of readings but its totally worth it in the end. Took it as a freshman and it was overwhelming but I don't regret it at all. Got an A at the end of the course because I put in so much effort. It's do-able. You just need to care enough
Brilliant professor, delights with wit and knowledge in equal measure. Busy, but still willing to help outside of class.

The class is worth taking just to be in the same room with the guy. The readings, however, are unnecessarily long, and international relations theory sometimes has painfully little to do with practical events. But Katzenstein is truly an amazing professor. OK class, brilliant mind. Expect a B / B + with an average amount of work put in.
So much reading it was difficult to keep up. The lectures were interesting, but the tests are based off of your ability to memorize over a thousand pages of reading.
Tough class, difficult readings, brilliant professor

This is a very difficult class, although amazing in terms of how much you learn. The readings can be extremely overwhelming. Katzenstein himself stated at the end of the course that it was by far one of the hardest classes an undergraduate could take at Cornell. Save this amazing course for junior/senior year.

I loved this class! Professor Katzenstein is truly an expert in the field of international relations, and he is an amazing lecturer. The TAs are also very helpful. It is a difficult, and there are a lot of readings, but it is worth all the work. Just study super hard for the final!
Amazing professor. Interesting lectures. Difficult class and lots of reading, but it is worth it. Take this class.
GOVT 1817 is an amazing class.  If you take this class and really pay attention, you will not regret it.  Katzenstein is simply one of the brightest minds in International Relations.

Professor Katzenstein is an amazing professor. He is an expert in his field, and a great lecturer.  I sincerely enjoyed going to his class.  Yes, the material is tough and there is a lot of work, but the TAs are very helpful and knowledgeable. Professor Katzenstein challenges his students immensely, but you will learn a lot.

KATZENSTEIN IS THE MAN!!! This class is very difficult, but worth it. Even if you don't do extremely well, the material is fascinating (and I am not a Govt/ILR major). Tons of dense readings, but mainly INCREDIBLE TAs that help immensely dissecting them. Go to office hours. Study hard for the brutal final. This class is WORTH IT

One of the few professors I have had who takes the teaching part of his profession seriously. He expects a lot of reading, but the work load is completely worth it. He is extremely smart, a great lecturer who has perfected teaching this subject at the introductory level. High emphasis on critical thinking.
The discussions were really interesting but the lectures were always boring by the end because he was just talking (albeit about interesting topics) for an hour and a half straight
best IR professor, his class is intensive but the TA (nicole) made it clear. this class is less difficult than labor law with gold.
Hardest class I've ever taken at Cornell with the hardest prof, but the material I learned was all worth it... even the decrease in my GPA.

A great prof.  I was lucky enough to take his Senior Govt. Major Seminar and it was a real challenge but being in such an intimate setting really helped us think on a higher level, one fit for an Ivy League school.  He was rude with his comments via e-mail, and the workload was a challenge, but i'm glad I took his class.  He is an expert.

The readings are extremely hard. Katz is very interesting, but he can be confusing. He is unavailable out of class, and a lot of what you get from his classes depends on the TAs, who will practically determine your grade/whether you understand the readings. Lecture is for your interest, not the tests - which are totally based on the readings.

Insanely difficult, but no other class will measure up.  Tons of reading, you need a study group, but Katzenstein is such a good professor that you show up for lecture 10 minutes early.  Changes your whole perspective on the world.  Get to know your TA's preferences because they grade the essays and care about different things.
Hard class, grades not very fair

Though called an 'Introductory Class' this is by no means introductory. Katzenstein said so himself in his final lecture. This is the most amount of work I have ever had to do for a single class. Expect A LOT of readings, and expect them to be very hard. Katzenstein knows his material very well, but his lectures are not straightforward. VERY HARD.

There's no question that this class is a lot of work.  Nonetheless, Katzenstein does an amazing job teaching the material, and the class is well worth taking.  It is possibly the most eye-opening class I have ever taken.  It really gives you a whole new perspective on world events.
god-like. that's all i have to say about that.

absolutely brilliant. i can't stress enough HOW interesting this class is and how much of my hero prof katzenstein has become. no doubt it's very very tough, the readings are insanely intense and large in number, but it's worth it. this guy is unbelievable. TAKE HIS CLASS.

This class is a bit of a shock. There is an unmanagable amount of readings (which I still mangaged to complete before, but now have a study group for). It is, however a very interesting and informative class. Professor Katzenstein is one of the most brilliant professors at Cornell and is highly regarded in the government field.

Interesting lecturer, going at a comfortable pace; interacts with students. Spends beginning of each lecture going over current events and emails from students. Knows his subject well; one of the best in field. Readings fairly interesting, though WAY too much for 3 credits. Concepts learnt, though, will last you well beyond this class.

One of the hardest classes i've taken, but also the most interesting. He's a brilliant teacher who really knows the material and makes an hour+ lecture very interesting. The only thing that took away from his class was the horrible section. However, a good TA would only help improve his class bc the material can be very difficult. I RECOMMEND IT

TAKE THIS CLASS! It's a difficult course (lots of reading, abstract/theoretical concepts) but Katzenstein is a brilliant, engaging lecturer, and actually not that difficult to follow. Absolutely worth the work. Best class I've taken at Cornell by far.

An incredible lecturer.  I looked forward to his lectures, he knows a lot and makes the information interesting and accessible.  That said, it is a very hard class with a lot of reading, but it is all worth it.

He is usually a funny engaging prof. Yet, the amount of reading given was extreme. I have not seen more reading in 300-level government classes here that are even in the same field. He is an expert in IR, unfortunately his brilliance does not shine through in this intro-level course. Try one of his upper-level courses if you really want to take him
Great guy, fun lectures, but often confusing. The reading were good, but there were far too many for a 100 level class.
Take this class! Very hard and lots of reading (all on the exams) but SO worth it. Katzenstein is an amazing intellectual and professor at the top of his field.  He's my hero!

Best class ever- not easy, a lot of reading... but very interesting... almost nothing on the exams are from lecture- but it's worth it to show up, to do the readings, etc. Very relevant. The prof really connects otherwise abstract material to what is going on in the world.
Take this class... it will make you think hard, a lot of reading, but gives a new perspective on the world.  Especially important for this era we're in.
He was ranked by the economist as the most influential scholar in international political economy. His lectures are great, but you have to come prepared. Not an easy class

best class at Cornell. DO the readings. you cheat yourself if you don't. there is a lot to read but unlike other gov classes, this is all great. his lectures are extremely informative. he's also a genius. this is a MUST take. clear your schedule. this class taught me how the world really works.
Interesting, but had trouble staying awake during lecture.  Also, A LOT of reading.

Without a doubt, the best class I have taken at Cornell -- and also the hardest.  Seek out the TA's for help, and be sure to do most of the readings at some point.  In all honesty, this is the type of class makes Cornell a legitimate Ivy League school.  He expects a lot, but you'll learn so much about the world and be forever grateful you took 354.

He's very smart and has a lot of knowledge. Can be arrogant, but overall a nice guy (read lyrics of Sunscreen song on last day of class). A ton of reading, much of which you have to do. Exams are comprehensive and to do well you have to prepare far in advance. Also some basic economics knowledge is helpful for this course, though not necessary.
An amazing professor.  Katzenstein is brilliant and funny.  He's the best professor I've ever had and thanks to him I'm now a government major.  Be prepared to work a lot, but it'll pay off.
Lecture notes are a bit confusing but the man is a genius.

Best class I have ever taken.  Seriously.  Also perhaps the hardest class I've ever taken, but it's well worth it.  Katzenstein is absolutely amazing and now I'm gonna have to take every class he teaches.

If you have come to Cornell to learn how to think clearly and sharpen your mind, then don't waste your time on **** easy courses.  This course is life-changing and it is rare to find such a gem.  I hate to end on a cliche, but nothing really good comes without hard work.
He is one of the most pointless convolluted teachers I've ever had, what a waste of time
almost 2000pages of readings!  readings have no correlation to the lectures, though lectures are interesting.  he is very liberal.

Its a real shame this guy's not teaching this semester. Really smart and ties themes to current events very well. Class is not easy, lots of reading, but you can manage. Sometimes puts very personal, liberal opinions into lectures.
One of the most intelligent people I've ever met. Extremely friendly and helpful. A fantastic teacher.
nice man. bad lecturer.

Professor Katzenstein's grasp on political economy is amazing.  He is intelligent, articulate, and a great lecturer.  He adds current events into the class, making comprehension of the material very simple.  It's not a cakewalk, but not too hard either.

At risk of hyperbole, I'll just say he's the best professor I've had. period. His IR seminar is four hours at a stretch, and the class just never drags. What a fascinating mind, and as available as anyone would ever need outside of class. He is a gift.
Great Prof!  But it's a hard intro class.  He is one of the most brilliant professors you'll find at Cornell.  Make sure your in a good section that will help you handle all the reading.

Interesting course.  Nice teacher who listens to students.  Not always clear how the lectures tie in with the readings.  Never-ending reading. Still, good class.  Learned a lot.  Nice teacher--really knows his stuff--almost intimidating.

Goes well with the course, he knows his stuff. He, however, continuously bashes America too much. We understand he's a citizen now, but that does not mean he should force his negative personal views of America on his students. Overall, though, not bad.

Absolutely brilliant professor. You can't miss a course with him if you have any interest in Politics. The course is hard: lotsa reading. But you'll find him quoted on your readings! He's very knowleadgable.
Accent kinda rocks, even though it makes him harder to understand
Very interesting lectures. Great class

This is def. one of the best courses I've taken. The reading load is close to crazy but they're discussed in section so I wouldn't worry about it. The exams are not difficult and the lecture is very enjoyable!
Great professor... Great Guy... Great Lecturer.. Funny...and Hot as hell   If you do the readings (there is alot), the class is easy

This was probably the best class I ever took at Cornell. He is an amazing lecturer and absolutely brilliant. There's no doubt that it's tough, but you don't have to do absolutely all of the reading (as with any government class).
Lectures and course material are really interesting, but be prepared to read more than you probably will in most 300 and 400 classes.
This was the first government class that I took at Cornell.  He's a great lecturer but the amount of reading for the course was ridiculous.  Make him do the Terminator voice
Far too much reading for a 300 level course.  Interesting topic, however overt liberal bias evident in some lectures.
I didn't actually take Professor Arias's class for 3316, but I pretty much did, considering I substituted all of Jian's lectures for Arias's lectures.

Truly some of the best lectures I've experienced at Cornell. Prof. Arias' unique PSets were really long and hard, but were some of the most insightful I've ever done. Very knowledgeable professor who can also help with all sorts of physics and math problems.

Prof. Arias is the best lecturer I have ever seen. The class was at 9 AM, but each day I woke up excited to climb the slope and watch his lecture, being sad when it ended. The homeworks can long, but extremely informative and rewarding to do (arias makes his own questions). Exams are fair. Arias is a rigorous (mathematically) source of knowledge.

Arias explains things very clearly and his class is extraordinarily organized. Although Psets were hard, taking 10-15 hours (I never went to office hours bcuz of time conflicts, which may have reduced the time ), I gained a really good foundation for quantum mechanics. Exams require you to work really fast but they're fair and easier than Psets.
Arias gives fantastic lectures. Course website is well prepared. Homework are quite a lot but generally inspirational.
Professor Arias was one of the most passionate professors I have had at Cornell. Even though I despised physics, he somehow managed to make me enjoy the class.

Arias is a nice guy, but is not very accessible to get help from. The P-Sets were incredibly difficult, covering material not taught and requiring 5-12 hours a week in office hours. The TA's often weren't sure how to do the questions (citing them as being harder than some of their grad-level P-Sets). OHs were ALWAYS packed (50-80 kids at a time).

Professor Arias is a wonderful professor that really cares about his students. The problem sets and lecture videos/pre-class exercises are a lot of work, but Professor Arias' dedication to his job makes it very enjoyable and worth it!!
Take him now - it will be a fun ride.

Good teacher, only complaint is that the tests questions were asked in very obscure and confusing ways. Many of the tests were based on randomly plugging in formulas, without the need for much physics.

Arias knows A LOT, and wants to meticulously prove things to his students. He is a GREAT lecturer, and is very open to talking to students both in and out of class. Homework was really difficult and took many hours (for me, 8-15), but I did come out of it a lot better at math.

Arias is very passionate, which makes lectures more enjoyable. Other than that the class is crap. The discussion section is not representative of the difficulty of prelims. The problem sets are WAY too hard and do not help you for the prelims. In my experience, you feel like you know your stuff and then the test rolls around and you don't.

I liked the flipped format of the class but I found the homeworks to be unnecessarily difficult. The tests were difficult but nicely curved. The lecture videos and questions were informative, organized, and easy to complete. If you put in the time to understand everything and attend lecture as the course goes on, you can do well.

Physics E&M was a lot of work and demanded a lot of time that I sadly did not always have. Prof. Arias is a really nice guy who genuinely cares about his students and is truly happy when the median grade on exams is high. Don't sweat the problem sets too much, as long as you understand the Co-Ops you'll be okay for exams.

Arias really cares about the students. He gets very happy when people in class understand the topics in lecture, and if they don't, he does his best to clear things up. This course is very fast-paced, and Arias doesn't like to waste much time. The problem sets are incredibly challenging, but if you understand the COOPs you'll be fine on the prelims
He really wanted to see us succeed and seemed genuinely happy when prelim scores were high.  Probably the most likable professor I've had so far.

He kind of reminds me of a dad. He was very approachable and encouraging during office hours. I started off struggling, but he was always willing to accommodate my learning style. Some people liked the flipped classroom method, and things really started to click once we switched to videos.

Prof. Arias is a good teacher.  I learned a lot through his 'flipped classroom' method of teaching.  I would highly recommend watching the video lectures at  a faster pace, as Arias speaks kind of slowly and pauses a lot.  You can take a 45 minute video lecture and turn it into a 12 minute lecture.  Major time saver. Definitely attend lecture.

Professor Arias is the best professor that I have had in my time at Cornell. He is kind, approachable, knowledgeable,  and an all-around great guy. When students voiced concerns, may it be with format or content, he listened and acted, at one point even starting to produce hour-long video lectures to help. He is amazing, and deserves high praise.
Clearest professor I've ever had. Empathizes with what the student knows and doesn't on a intimate level. However, you'll have to do a lot of work for his class (if you want to do well, that is).

Arias is truly dedicated to making sure his students understand the material. The exams (with the exception of the multiple choice on the first one) were very fair and very straightforward. Problem sets were challenging but very doable. He also made himself available for questions and pretty much wouldn't let you leave until you understood it!

Best professor I've had in my four semesters thus far. He's extremely helpful and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. He's also very passionate about the material and teaches is better than anyone else could. If you have a chance to take a class with him, don't pass it up.
Simply the greatest

Arias is an amazing professor. If you ever have to take 2213, make sure he is teaching. Arias is so caring about students performance, and he is genuinely a nice guy. This is a really difficult course, especially if you struggled in multivariable like I did. The problem sets are hard, but they prepare you well for the exams which are pretty fair

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. His lectures are theoretical but he make tough topics extremely clear to understand with a lot of enthusiasm. He cares a lot about his students and truly wants  them to learn the material. Tests are slightly challenging but the homeworks prepare you well for exams.
Wonderful professor; however, he curved the class to a lower grade then normal, so that contributed to lower grades. Very clear and enthusiastic.

Best professor I've had at Cornell yet. If you're the type of person who just wants to memorize equations and apply them then you will probably not like this class. However, if you  find the subject interesting and want to truly understand the fundamental concepts then Arias is a spectacular professor.

Probably one of the most brilliant people I've ever met. Lectures were indeed mathematical- but in the best way possible. Contrary to what some would say- his derivations go far beyond what's written in the book. He generates his own problem sets that are tailored to what you'd expect to see on an exam. Phenomenal instructor for a phenomenal class.
HORRIBLE! do not take a class with this professor. literally did not learn a thing. makes me fail every prelim because he does not teach us how to approach the difficult problems he presents.

If you don't enjoy the derivations involved in learning physics, then you don't enjoy physics. They're the point of it. That said, this class is amazing. Arias approaches electromagnetism intuitively, and teaches all of the fundamental concepts and theories by deriving them. If you really do like math and physics, you'll love Arias.

Does a pretty good job explaining derivations during lecture.  Pay attention to these as they are pretty close to what the problem sets and tests are like.  I do admit the class is very "mathy" although it's really not bad.  The problem sets are good at bringing up old material so that you are always practicing what you've learned
He spent all of lecture going over derivations provided in the book, and just made us do math heavy problem sets. I would recommend not taking the class with him.

Absolutely brilliant. He focuses a lot on theory and mathematical calculations during lecture and doesn't really give much application and problem-solving, but he is very organized and extremely clear in his explanations. Would definitely take another course with him.

For electromagnetism this semester, the lectures were not very helpful with regard to exams, feel free to skip them and read the textbook. The problem sets were excessively time consuming and calculus heavy. He's not that bad, but I recommend taking this course with another professor in the spring semester.

This is a review for how he taught electromagnetism for engineers. He gave extremely difficult problems sets, but the prelims were fairly easy. His lecture is very easy and simple, on the conceptual side, but that will not help with the homework which all rely heavily on vector calculus. The lectures were not all that helpful for exams either.
Hes the professor now for autotutorial physics. Take this class. He's good at explaining things and a very smart man. Course is time consuming but easy grade.

Pretty much what everyone else said.  Very good teacher, knows how to explain things in a way that's easy to understand.  The class wasn't too hard in my opinion, but I think they curve the class to a pretty low mean grade, so you need to work pretty hard if you want an A.

Prof Levine is the best professor I've had at Cornell. His lectures are lively and interesting even at 8:40am. Very engaging and passionate professor. I learned a ton!

Absolutely an awesome lecturer. He's very engaging and is clearly passionate. The class isn't that hard (the midterm was multiple choice and short answers) and he is very approachable outside of class if you have any questions.

Terrific class! Great lectures and very fair exams. Worth waking up early for!

Totally recommend this class! Professor Levine gives amazing lectures that are engaging and well-organized. Anyone interested in American politics should take this course! It is one of those classes that makes you seriously smarter and a more informed person. The class was incredibly interesting. You develop time management and writing skills and are treated as an independent learner. Professor Law is an engaging lecturer. She was my only professor all semester to keep my attention the entire clas time.

Professor Law has an extremely lively lecturing style and a great sense of humor. She is incredibly knowledgeable about Japanese Religion, drawing on both her fieldwork and from contemporary theory. She cares about her students and puts in the effort to meet students' individual needs. High but worthwhile workload for a 3000 level class.

Wonderful professor - very thoughtful and caring. She clearly loves her job and puts tremendous effort into every aspect of it. I've learned so much from a semester of her teaching. She keeps her students in rapture for the entire lecture - I don't even mind when we go a little over the time limit. The work is challenging, but not impossible.

Prof Law is the best lecturer I've had at Cornell, and solely taking this course for her paid off because it was fascinating. The course had a great religious, cultural and historical perspective on Japan. The workload is manageable with time management and the writing makes the class worthwhile. Law is there to help you at and point along the way.

Amazing lecturer and awesome person. Sitting in lecture is a pleasure because Professor Law really knows what she's talking about and makes it extremely interesting. Workload is easy - weekly page long reflections (but could be on anything) and two essays.

Great experience and start to education at Cornell. Law engaged with every student who was willing to learn, assessed individual levels, and helped us improve. When I first read the reviews before I took this class, I was very intimidated by some comments-- like final paper is 30+ pages or so. That's completely false! This Professor is the best!! She is an amazing teacher and goes out her way to help you! She cares about all her students and wants them all to succeed. It has been a pleasure taking her class and I am so happy to have taken it. Thanks to her I have improved my writing to another level! I definetly recommend someone to take a class with proffer law

Professor Law is one of the best professors I have had so far at Cornell.  Her passion for the subject is infectious, and her lectures are some of the most interesting and engaging I have ever seen.  The midterm and final papers are difficult, but not impossible.
One of the best teachers I've had at Cornell. Intelligent, passionate about the subject material, loves to engage with students.

She is a brilliant teacher and a very impressive and inspiring personality. I was lucky I got to interact with her. She is passionate and serious about the subject and inspires the students to make a good effort. Her's was one of the best classes I have taken. I wholeheartedly recommend any class taught by Prof. Law to anyone.

She has to be one of the best teachers I've had at Cornell. How many professors will open up their home to students and invite the entire class over for dinner and discussion? She genuinely cares and is invested in our learning and success. We were in a higher-level seminar so it wasn't easy, but it was worth the work. Very helpful and approachable

I have taken several classes with this professor, and she is absolutely phenomenal. I love JaneMarie Law. She is a fantastic teacher mainly because she loves and is very passionate about what she teaches. You do have to read and write a lot for her classes, but it is definitely worth it. I have taken 3 courses with her and they have been some of my favorites at Cornell.

Professor Law is easily my favorite professor at Cornell. She cares about her students and is a extremely interesting and knowledgeable professor, even outside of her field of study. You actually learn in her class and receive takeaways you can use.

Great professor and great storyteller! I really enjoyed going to her class, even though it wasn't easy. You don't always get the opportunity to go to a class that makes you see the world from an entirely different perspective. Highly recommended.

Absolutely wonderful professor! She's not an easy A type of class, but it's not that hard to just keep up with the reading. She makes all the classes super interesting and fun to attend. Absolutely ridiculous amount of work and reading. We were expected to read a 200+ page book over a weekend. There is no way that the median grade is an A. No standards for grading whatsoever. Do not take this class. The median grade report says A. It is not an A. The final was a 30 page essay. And where was this mentioned on the syllabus? It was not. A self-righteous, arrogant and condescending, feminist hypocrite. She has strict guidelines for her students while indulging herself at all times. Awesome Class, Awesome Teacher, her passion and knowledge, amazing, her stories the BEST, not a religions major, class was quite a bit of work, but well worth it, definitely recommend her class to anyone interested in Asian Religions.

Very interesting course on religion and culture. Prof is entertaining to say the least. I think she's a professional story teller so she does a lot of that in class. Great class- so glad I got into this FWS... term paper assignments are no longer stressful, as jml really focuses on paper formatting... highly recommended- you'll be set for honors/masters thesis after her class-a lot of work though, several 10 pages papers, final paper is 35 pages. Great lecturer; enought said.
Kirshner's lectures were clear and funny.  I actually looked forward to going to his class.  Def. take him.

Good class, but a huge amount of reading and the man talks SO fast. The exams were difficult and readings were fairly necessary. It would be useful to have a lot of background knowledge in the international relations area. Keep up with the material or you could easily get lost.

Prof. Kirshner is a fabulous lecturer.  Lectures are fun and humorous, and the concepts are really interesting.  The class isn't very much work -- just two exams (midterm/final) and one paper, basically a book review.  I highly recommend this course.

A FANTASTIC lecturer. Very fast-paced, but incredibly intelligent, clear and imenselly funny. His exams are relatively difficult, for an intro course. Only reason his rating should not be 5 is because he's not easy. If you can, take a course with him.

You will never look at the world the same way after this class.  The lecture format is the ideal way to digest dense theoretical texts.  Culler makes graspable the obtuse. take him before its too late

cornell's theory star, he is good at explaining things. he is very smart, but a little arrogant.

EXTREMTELY disorganized. very inconsistent grading and homework did not have any value.

This class can be as challenging as you want it to be, depending on how perfect you want to get with all of the exercises. Good class

She was exceedingly boring and the only thing drier than the lectures was her personality.  I was so interested in the topic, she's just not a very engaging instructor.  She would be better off in a library somewhere than in a classroom.

Professor Blackburn is a great teacher! I learned a lot about post-colonial studies, and as long as I kept up with the readings, the seminars were interesting and engaging. Lots of difficult reading tho.

After the awful comments on here, I was worried.  But this is the easiest class I've ever taken here.  She is nice, and while her lectures are confusing and dull more often than not, the individual projects assigned are quite interesting and enlightening for your information.
She is the most terrible teacher I've ever had for sure.

Prof. Blackburn is very intelligent and nice, although a bit boring. I found her lectures to be slightly dry but dense with information, which to me suggests that any problems are my own. As far as grading, I thought she was good and fair (which doesn't mean giving an A for every student).

Professor Berger is absolutely outstanding. She really engages with the material and inspires her students to do the same. If you're willing to work, you will get a lot out of her classes. Fantastic professor...really knows her stuff. Very friendly.
i just love this woman

Great, encouraging professor with clear, easy-to-follow lectures. Holds helpful office hours and review sessions. Projects in the class are a great balance of challenging and engaging. Learned a ton in the class and would recommend to anyone who is trying to get into CS!

Anne Bracy is one of the best professors I have at Cornell. I came into this class not knowing anything about CS, and I walked out of this class with an A. The materials were very interesting to me, and I enjoy them substantially.
I loved Professor Bracy- she is truly a great lecturer and has a very impressive professional background. She made me want to major in CS!
Good lectures, very accessible and caring about students. Difficult class with a lot of workload but Bracy does a good job at navigating the course.
Crazy analogies. Intense workload. Interesting content. Compassionate professor. Can't ask for much more.
Amazing professor! Very kind and inclusive. Lectures always very well organized and prepared. Engaging lectures.

CS 3410 is no joke. The projects are challenging and ridiculously time-consuming. I think Professor Bracy makes the course fair and is a great lecturer and professor. My only criticism is the exams in the course are much more difficult than they should be and are frankly really hard to study for.

Wonderful lecturer! CS3410 is a challenging and difficult class, but Prof. Bracy's lectures makes it bearable with her jokes and funny/good examples and comparisons. She is also super accessible outside of class, and is supportive of students with disabilities. I think anyone who says otherwise has to reflect on their (internalized) misogyny.

Professor Bracy is great at what she does, lectures are very content-heavy but always worth going to. Do NOT procrastinate projects or you will come to regret it, office hours are available all week and very helpful. She gives lots of relevant practice materials for exams and although the tests can have hard questions, they are all graded fairly.

(Note that she gave a textbook but literally no one used it) Very clear lectures, assignments are pretty straightforward, tests are fine if you study well. The class, in my opinion, is not meant to be a class to take "for fun." It's pretty time consuming, and Bracy expects a lot, but she made a significant effort to ensure students are prepared.
Pretty easy class, feel like I learned the fundamentals well. Lectures are not the most helpful, but the labs and assignments are great to learn.

This is more of a review of CS 1110 than of Prof Bracy, but I have zero prior coding experience and learned a lot and liked the course without being too stressed by assignments or exams. Class is heavily weighted and a few exams had very low unweighted averages (60%-70% range usually), so it's usually possible to recover from a bad test/assignment

Great class and great professor! The material could be challenging at times but she explained things amazingly clearly and often worked in fun examples to keep it engaging. The class does have a fair bit of work, specifically time consuming projects. Luckily projects are very interesting and there are lots of office hours.
Spring cs1110 is much easier than fall cs1110. Bracy didn't really impact me during the class, but I thought she was fine.

I don't have any experience with her in other classes, but in CS1110 she was great! Not perfect, but I certainly felt it necessary to attend lectures just because of how fluent she was in explaining the core concepts. The class itself was very difficult, but I think she certainly alleviated that a great deal.
A professor that forces financial hurdle on students by requiring physical iClicker.

I was a repeat cs1110 student this spring (took walker white last fall). Bracy and Lee are a great combo for teaching and I found the assignments more interesting than in the fall, and therefore I was more engaged and completed the course successfully. If possible I would wait until the spring to take this course. I feel more confident in cs now.

3410 is a tough class because material is new to most people and there's A LOT of work, even if it's mostly just busy work. Concepts usually build on top of one another so you do not want to fall behind. Class will seem overwhelming at first but gets better. Felt that Bracy makes the class doable contrary to what others might say. She's also funny

Fantastic lecturer! Makes CS clear to all, whether you are a first time learner or more experienced. Professor Lee writes tests and assignments, but Bracys lectures are super helpful for these. Would highly recommend taking!

Prof. Bracy was awesome, and I was pleasantly surprised by the way she taught CS. This class is definitely not easy, and requires a lot of effort, but if you put in the time and effort you will learn so much. Bracy was very nice, helpful, and accessible. The tests are hard but curved, the course is quick but help is given to people struggling.

Professor Bracy held all lectures for this class and ensured that all concepts were easily explained in class. While, many of the topics were extremely difficult to a first time programmer, it was clear that all topics were learned in a professional manner with clear examples that were performed in class.

Clear lecturer who's very passionate about the subject, and makes many references to Wegmans during the lectures. Went through numerous examples during class when covering more complex topics like caches, and reduced the difficulty of the assignments to accomodate for a hybrid class format. Had a reasonable slip day policy for project submissions.

Professor Bracy's class was so incredibly difficult for the sole purpose of being difficult. Bracy is an excellent lecturer and really cares about her students. That doesn't mean the assignments and prelims aren't insanely hard...
Terrible person. I was hospitalized for a week and she forced me to use all of my slip days instead of just granting an extension like a human with empathy.

Bracy is a great teacher and clearly knows her subject. Her lectures are well-designed with clear language and she drops hilarious lines from time to time. This class covered a lot of highly technical details and sub-regions of CS, and not attending the lectures would make it hard to understand the slides. That said, the textbook is comprehensive.
Really I wish I could give her 0 star. Just dropped the course, and do not understand where those good comments come from.
Not intelligent in teaching at all. Confusing lectures, baffled homework... I hope someone could let her know how awful her lectures are. By the way, she is rather mean and arrogant in the same time.

I love Bracy! She's a great professor and her lectures are done in a way that is easy to understand and accessible. Assignments are always geared towards what we have already learned; if you can do the assignments, the tests should not be too difficult. There are clicker questions to log attendance, but they're only 5% of your grade.
One of the worst classes I have taken.
Unintelligible class.

Bracy is a god among men. Never have I seen such a professor so passionate about both the material and her students. She gets so excited teaching and talking with students that it makes lectures my favorite time of the week. Yes, the class is difficult and condensed, but if you pay attention in lecture, the class is very manageable. SHE IS AMAZING!

Professor Bracy is a talented and funny lecturer. Her lectures explain material extremely well while also being fairly concise. CS 3410's projects were hard (10-20 hours per project) and its exams harder, with means around a 55/90. I would highly recommend taking her classes she teaches.

Bracy is an amazing lecturer and made this class (which could have been terrible) pretty enjoyable and interesting. I really loved her classes and thought the assignments were pretty standard for a CS core class. Also, she's awesome to talk to outside of class and genuinely cares about her students. 10/10 would recommend!

Bracy is so great that I'm taking CS 2110 with her next semester. I loved her teaching style because I am a very visual learner (she's won teaching awards). She inspires great questions from her students in lecture, and the lecture material clearly laid out what was expected on exams. Beware of the tricky assignments and make use of office hours.

Her lectures were usually pretty good, but sometimes slightly disorganized. She's super nice though and has plenty of office hours! Apparently her assignments were a lot harder than the fall CS 1110 professor's, but they were doable.

Bracy is by far the best professor I've had at Cornell! She is passionate about CS and her lectures are clear and enormously helpful. The assignments were quite difficult at times but prepared you greatly for the prelims and final. I came in with zero coding experience and learned so much in a semester. Challenging but immensely rewarding class!

She is a great professor. Her lecture style was clear, and I the examples made tough concepts easy to learn. Her expectations were clear and it was easy to gage how I was doing in the class. Not an overbearing amount of work, and makes CS really fun to learn. Also, she is just an awesome human.
I really loved cs3410 with her :) I maybe only scraped past tests, but it was worth it for the interesting lecture and great content.

Best undergrad professor I've had. She turned systems from a hated subject of mine into my graduate focus. Negative comments below are reactions to unconventional teaching. Lectures focus on concepts, exams are difficult but test your grasp of concepts in terms of big picture. Not a cookie-cutter professor/lecturer - what makes her great.

Great Professor. The lectures are very clear. Attend the classes since It takes more time to figure out the lecture note than just attending the class. Not sure why are there so many very negatives comments. I took 4410 in the Fall semester. The lectures are a bit slow and repetitive and the projects are pretty difficult. But t's fine overall.
Super difficult class, but the best proffessor I've had at cornell
Awesome teaching with low scores. Think thoroughly before you enroll!!

Fun lectures that fly over topics at the speed of light. Be sure to read up before lecture begins (there's HW before every lecture to help with that) and take notes like a good student. Tests are difficult and annoying as they often test a concept that you know well but contorted so that no one knows how to answer. Still, great, fun person.

Lectures and projects have little overlap, and tests are hard to predict. Bracy is good at teaching in lecture, but little of what she teaches is actually useful for the tests and projects.

Overall, I wish there was more thought put into the course. Projects were not well planned, had too much time to complete, but little support. Having weekly problem sets would have helped students know what to focus on. Many difficult topics on the exams were covered in the book, but glossed on in lecture. Had to self-study to do well on exams.

Little to no TAs use the piazza, and some of the answers are rather rude. Tests have means in the 50s and are unrelated to anything learned. Lectures have minimal overlap with projects, and the projects are very hazily laid out. For one project, we were told to simply google any questions. It's a shame this course is mandatory.

Very tough test, so many assignments that do not match it's credits. unclear lecture notes, skip the class? you will not clear about what leature notes talking about. besides operating system, the course also contains computer network and security. if you have choices, never choose it! it does not worth in any way!

Despite Prof. Agarwal's messing up of the entire class, she was actually a good lecturer and you can tell from piazza and office hours that she actually cares and wants students to learn and succeed. She was organized and clear. 10/10 would recommend

I really like Anne as a lecturer but this class was just awful. 3410 was good but 4410 was by far the worst class I've taken at Cornell. One of the best professor at cornell! Homeworks can be a little disorganized but her lectures are always interesting, informative, and entertaining.

Professor Bracy is one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. I took a class with her, and also was a TA for another class that she taught. She knows her stuff, and can answer any question you throw at her. This class will be near impossible, but Bracy and the TA army will help you out.

Wow, Bracy yourself for 3410 cause it's the bomb dot com. While the projects/ homework aren't too hard, they are time consuming. The 3410 TA army and Bracy is there for you though, so you are in good hands.

ASTRO 3334 is a great chance to get hands-on experience with Python techniques in Astronomy. Lloyd is helpful in class, although difficult to reach outside of it. The class consisted of 8 projects that ranged from the very easy (apply to research programs online) to finding exoplanets and other difficult tasks. You need Python experience.

If you have any interest in astronomy, this class is an easy way to satisfy distribution requirements.  Lloyd is a good teacher and he cares about teaching astronomy but a lot of the students don't show any interest in the class and just want an easy A, so some of the students complain about it, but all you need to do is just do the work.
Lloyd's lectures are mostly good.  He does lots of demos that are really entertaining.  The class is pretty easy, but there are homeworks and you need to study for the exams.

Lloyd has his ups and downs. Some of the lectures - especially those with demos - are pretty interesting. Others are fairly dull. He also isn't very good at answering questions and will often brush off a student's inquiry as ignorant. It's easier if you're interested in astronomy. Pretty easy to do well if you study before the exams.

I love Professor Maralani. She is intelligent, cool, and a great lecturer. She clearly cares so much about her students and wants to get to know them individually, even in a large class. She's transparent about her process as a professor and genuinely wants feedback to improve, even with a lot of teaching experience under her belt. Great class!

Brilliant sociologist and excellent at breaking down statistical concepts in applied ways. Highly recommend this prof for taking stats. Definitely grades tough, but curves overall. You will have to work a lot - weekly assignments are time bloats, but are good learning tools.

Professor Maralani is a very intelligent stats professor and she can teach you a lot. That being said, sometimes she is a little toooo smart and will confuse the whole class, but if you talk to her one on one she'd clear it up. The tests are pretty hard, and sometimes feel like they are unrelated to class content. But, the curve is generous.
Ridiculously hard content with very little explanation. Inhuman amount of homework and tough grading.

Professor Silberstein, while good intentioned, comes to class wildly unprepared for lecture. Would often do problems and realize (after students called her out) that she had done them completely wrong. I got through this class solely by reading the textbook and learning on my own. Not approachable, kind of mean.
She is so mean and rude and just an awful teacher. I would give her a negative rating.
My only complaint is that her handwriting is really bad and can sometimes make it hard to follow her notes. Otherwise, she is great and I enjoyed the class

I had Professor Silberstein in Spring of 2016. Right from the get-go I knew that the class (statics) would be horrible, and by the end my initial impressions were confirmed. The grading policy was horrendous and is essential set up so that students are not successful. I wish ratemyprofessor had a rating lower than 1. I do not recommend her.
Uncurved class.. mean on the final was a 62. Makes it incredibly hard to do well. Prof Silberstein succeeds in making an intuitive and interesting class for engineers into a complete nightmare.
Least favorite professor I've had at Cornell. The class isn't that hard but she's not a good teacher and is especially unhelpful when you ask questions.
Handwriting is messy and the lectures are disjointed. Lectures consisted mostly of her going through example problems without explaining how she was solving them.

Silberstein is alright. The expectations for the course are pretty straightforward, and all the info you need to know for the homework and exams is in lecture. She doesn't curve the class, but the prelims weren't that bad and the averages were 83 or 84. The iClicker quizzes are the worst though, they're 20% of your grade which is insane.
Please take this class with Sachse. Nothing else to say.

So far my least favorite professor I've had my three years here. Lectures were frustrating because her handwriting was messy and her hand always blocked her notes. She was extremely condescending at office hours and didn't even know how to solve the problems. Not helpful at all and only laughed/scoffed at me when I would ask her for help.
She aight

It's her first time teaching, and yes, you can tell. But I think that her lectures were all right, and the discussion classes were very helpful as well. I learned enough in lecture and discussion to be able to do the homework without much problem. I'd say she's doing all right for her first time teaching.
worst professor i have had in my undergraduate career thus far. too bad i have to pass this class.

First time she's ever taught a class. You can tell. She really doesn't seem to have any interest in helping her students do well and sometimes I feel like she actually wants to fail half the class. Her I-clicker questions and quizzes are useless.
Silberstein is an alright Prof. she teaches the material that's on her tests, and her tests aren't that hard. Annoying laugh though.

Agreed. If this is not a requirement course for you, DO NOT TAKE IT. I've had my fair share of good/bad professors but she is definitely the worst I've had. Lectures are one of the most boring and unorganized I've ever seen (very few pp slides, almost all handwritten notes)

Just run. She might be the single most condescending professor I have ever encountered. She thinks we're all stupid and she just laughs at everything. Her lecture is an enormous waste of time, unfortunately she takes I-clicker attendance. Her handwriting is both illegible and tiny. Effectively curves the class to a C which is just grand.

I had no idea what to expect when signing up for this class, but I can honestly say that it completely changed my outlook on the idea of parenting. She's brilliant, and yet still seems happy to be teaching us. The 4 quizzes shouldn't be a problem if you go to class and take notes. Take this class, it will change your views on everything.

Small is an excellent teacher. She goes over the material slowly, and honestly seems to enjoy talking with us. However if you don't come to class or don't speak during discussions she tends to get exasperated.

Small gets great enjoyment out of having the power in the student-professor relationship and is convinced that she is always right. The information in the course is interesting, but her attitude ruins everything. She also grades harshly. Do not take this class.

Anthro of parenting was the best class I've ever taken. Meredith is HYSTERICAL, and the whole class consists of drawing from your own lives & her stories. You read a ton but it's fascinating and she ties it all together. Write down her every word during lectures; she makes it clear what's important. The final paper is actually a blast.

Anthropology of Parenting was one of my favorite classes at Cornell. Very interesting and low stress. Seems like a lot of reading, but as long as you skim and can discuss, you'll be fine. Only 5 quizzes and a final ethnography project. Prof. Small is amazing!

Anthropology of Parenting is a wonderful class- the readings are fun and not too stressful, and your grade is based on 5 quizzes and a term paper.  Prof. Small structures the class this way because she wants you to do well and learn something; she's not out to kill anyone's GPA, unlike many profs at this school.  Highly recommended.

Had her for both intro to human evolution and anthro of parenting and she was awesome! I wish I was more interested in biological anthropology because I would love to take more of her classes. Tests/quizzes are easy, straight forward, and there's not BS. Great book, interesting lectures, great classes!

I took Human Evolution (Anthro 101), and it's one of the most interesting classes. She just lectures and shows slides, but the material is really interesting. If you go to lecture every day, you'll get an A. No prelims/finals/papers. Only 5 quizzes - 10 min each! (Quiz every 2 weeks) Very low stress. :)

i took anthro of human mating - INTERESTING CLASS!! She's a really good lecturer (just talks and writes on chalkboard), but her tests can be nitty-gritty at times. the books to read were incredibly interesting. i will most likely be taking anthro of parenting because i love her so much - but p/f because she's hard

One of the best at Cornell. Excellent teaching skills, friendly and dedicated to her students. Passionate in her views...and I think this is a great thing! Rocked my socks...and I would take 10 more classes from her if I could Get into a class taught by this Prof...not to be missed.

Small had a large chip on her shoulder.  I remember a statement she made on the first day of class regarding pre-med students (I was not one): " I will NEVER change your grades!"  Professor Small, It's really about learning and understanding of the information.  Right?
The answers she looks for on tests don't have much to do with the questions she asks and in her lectures she contradicts the books we read. Kinda hard to get a good grade, but I learned a lot.

Small is an excellent teacher.  She does a great job of tying an understanding of humanity into how we can go about living our lives in such a screwed up world.  There is nothing hard about this class but it is very interesting and informative.

She's not a great teacher. I don't know how someone so average as her is so established in her field. Anthro is an interesting class but the grading of her tests is VERY subjective on the essay parts.
Very thorough. Friendly. Exams are not terribly difficult or detailed, which is nice.

Uses her professorship as a podium for left-wing pontifications.
Would take a class with her again

Very engaging and clear lecturer.
