If you genuinely care about the course, you will learn and grow so much as a writer with her as your professor. Cares for her students' well-being better than anyone else.

Prof McCray is very caring for her students, and she makes sure we know it. She promotes self-care and is willing to grant extensions on assignments. She is a refreshing change from the rest of the professors. Her grading is pretty lenient, too, and is mostly participation-based.
She's nice, but lectures are boring and messy, and I got nothing after taking the class.
She can be pretentious and does favor the students who only sit directly in front on her during lecture. Shows lots of movies.

Gonzales is pretty boring. BUT GO TO LECTURE. She gives A LOT of extra credit. My course had 7% extra credit received through writing assignments and iclicker points. Go to section as section is about 50% of your grade (writing intensive). I failed the first prelim, did above the mean on the 2nd and did ok on the final and got an A in the course.

Hands down the worst professor I've had. She cancels class at least once a week and has us watch 1.5 hour movies instead with a question sheet to fill out. All assignments are due on Saturday and Sunday nights which completely ruin the weekend. She even made the final paper due the Sunday after slope day. Boring lectures. Do the extra credit.
Its not a hard class, but the prelim/final are difficult. She offers a lot of extra credit though, buy the textbook you use it heavily!
I liked this class!! Preli and final were hard though. like wtf. basically, know the textbook REALLY well. but everything was interesting and the movies were cool. Great class!
Lots of reading but a great course and a great instructor. I got an A+ and I did terrible on my prelim and final, there are a lot of extra credits to boost your grade

Lectures terrible.Incoherent. Nobody actually took notes. Exams unrelated to lectures. They are all based on readings. There are tons to read for this class. She gives lots of extra credits, but they are to make up for hard exams that she gives..but  it's not hard to get an A if you read what was assigned.

The tests were useless and random, and I got the hardest TA who gave everyone check minuses and low participation grades, we all complained about her.  This class is completely useless and not curved.  A lot harder than in the past.

Agree with the poster below me. Her test is a bunch of random stuff from the textbook (which, btw, is the most boring and badly written textbook ever; chapters are 500000 pages long). Lots of reading and you have to do them if you want to do well. Response papers were easy to BS if you get an easy TA.
Loves busy work, tests are composed of random facts from the text book
This class was so easy. I got an A in it and did terrible on the final. My TA was awesome but she's no longer here. Just go to lecture read stuff and you'll do fine.

boring lecture, mostly just watched movies where you had to fill out question sheets while watching...not super easy like its supposed to be in the fall, attendance mandatory, lots of annoying papers, extra credit opportunity

her lectures are useless, everything is verbatim from the book. but you have to go to get attendance points. the movies are really good. TAs are on the whole fair graders but not helpful if you have problems. the assignments seem like busywork, but are easy. just show up and do the work - staff is frustrating, but the class is still really easy.

If she took her own class she would have lost all the points for attendance in lecture. She hardly showed up and when she did put a movie on instead of lecturing. However, the class is cake so it doesn't really matter
i swear to god i showed up to this class more than she did

The professor was overly redundant and not easily approachable. It seems as though she was always out of town or late to catch a plane somewhere. She would rather have students talk to the TA than to her and she gets flustered when we email her. The clicker was a complete waste of money. We rarely used it.

The most diva you can get with a professor.  DSOC 101 is NOT an easy A with her.  I do NOT recommend taking any class with her.  TA's are of little help and are like a wall when asking for help.  Also if you email Gonzales she will give you a ****y response hence the Diva-ness.
No Comments
really good, clear lectures. very helpful outside of class. alot of reading for course, but tests aren't based on readings, just comprehension of ideas.

I felt that he made very complicated material extremely simple.  I left both classes (230 & 314) feeling like I knew everything those classes covered absolutely.  He was so good at explaining in lecture that the pace even felt slow even though a lot was covered.  So far, my favorite courses in ECE.

Knows the material well, but reuses slides and lectures can be a bore. The course is not run very well - homeworks/labs are never returned in anything close to a timely matter and the grading procedure is a mess. This class isn't terrible but is often extremely frustrating.

This course was a fantastic introduction to logic design. The professor explained the basics clearly, and labs were VERY illustrative and interesting. Some of them were more open-ended, but they were challenging and I learned a lot.

Long is a joke.  Doesn't know his own slides, gets confused by his own slides, contradicts the textbook on the day of a prelim and then later admits he's wrong, posts homework late, changes homeworks a few days before they're due, has stupid procedures for homeworks, can't answer homework questions correctly in class.  Is extremely boring.  Awful.

doesn't know his slides. gets confused in the middle of lecture.  doesn't necessarily know the topics at hand very well, though he may have at one point. makes stupid analogies. answers questions in the most round-about way.  the homework he assigns can get tedious.

Doug Kriner is by far one of the best Government professors at Cornell. It's clear he is passionate what he teaches and is always happen to listen what students have to say. Discussion sections matter! Make sure to do readings as they are vital for prelims and writing assignments. Overall, this was a fantastic course!
For GOVT3161: It's a fine class, but all of the writing assignments are heavily stats based (analysis and all that), so please be aware of that before signing up.

An amazing lecturer, so if you don't like the class, it probably means you don't want to study government. Participation in discussions are mandatory but graded somewhat arbitrarily. It can be tough to figure out what TAs want from writing assignments. Exams aren't bad.

Lectures weren't engaging. I just got by with my general knowledge of American politics and didn't do most of the reading. The data analyses he assigns should be super easy but take a lot longer because he wants you to use Microsoft Excel. It wasn't a bad class content-wise, but it was so complicated that I wouldn't put myself through it again

Although the content itself was interesting, it felt as though he was ranting during lecture, and not all the material that he talks about is on the slides, so if you miss a day, you will more than likely fall behind (as he doesn't even post them). Also, so much reading. There are only a few assignments, and if you don't do one, watch out!

I loved intro to American politics with Kriner. He is passionate about the subject matter and does a great job of incorporating data to make the themes have a poignant impact for the present day. He does focus heavily on the lecture slides, but he is a really good lecturer. 

The supplemental readings are SUPER important to do well in the course.

Professor Kriner was really knowledgeable about American Government, and I learned a lot in his class. What I disliked about this class were the TAs. Mine graded extremely harshly without giving good feedback and barely covered the readings during discussion.

Great class! Prof. Kriner really shines when talking about his speciality of the American Presidency. Throughout the course he provided insight and fostered interesting discussion about the American Presidency. Grading was generous and the final project (a survey) was both interesting and relatively straightforward. Highly recommend!

Skip this class if u can, I took it for fun and it made me change my whole major. I originally came in as a govt major and immediately changed it after this class. TAs graded unfairly (some didnt read any of the papers while others never gave above a B) his lectures are BORING, it was the longest 75 min of my life and I had to do it twice a week

Kriner is one of the best lecturers at Cornell. Other intro classes barely scrape half the class to show up to lectures, while most students showed up to Kriners lectures, despite them mostly repeating the textbook readings. Kriner was an engaging lecturer and I genuinely enjoyed showing up to class, but TA discretion largely determined grades...

I have Kriner now and he does not read from a script anymore. I can tell he is passionate about what he is lecturing on, and that he cares about the students. He is charismatic and funny and I would take another class of his.
Professor Kriner's lectures sure are scripted; however, the detailed descriptions of each topic are super useful.

Although you can tell hes reading from a script, I appreciated his effort to organize lectures in a way that helped students study for exams. I loved staying after lecture to listen to him answer students questions; I could tell that Kriner loved what he was teaching and was happy to see students engage.

Readings are dense sometimes, but are always analyzed in the discussion section so you can get the main ideas. In his lectures, it was clear that he puts a lot of time and effort into considering what to talk about - he does a lot of case studies/data analysis, and he is so accessible in office hours and invites student participation always!

His lectures were incredibly boring. I swear he was reading off a script during class. His lecture slides were disorganized and all over the place. However, we had really good discussions during class. We also only had four assignments due throughout the semester, and they were super light.
Loved prof Kriner! He puts so much effort into his lectures, and the workload is totally manageable, all while learning a tremendous amount.

Alright what.. This class has an hour and 15 minute lectures along with a 50 minute snooze discussion section that requires participation or you get points deducted from your grade. There are pre-recorded 30 minute long lectures & as someone else pointed out he reads off a script, NOT ENGAGING. Theres also sm readings, 4 essays midterm and a final.

Kriner seems like a nice guy, but in lectures all he does in ramble on. You can literally see him reading off of his screen during live lectures AND pre-recorded lectures, so it's hard to engage with the material he's reciting. He also makes you read overly-long material before class. (BEWARE if you have no background in US gov / history)

Lectures are fascinating and always involve real-world applications/examples. Trump's impeachment inquiry began a month after class started, and Kriner adjusted on the fly and dedicated a bunch of class time to the impeachment proceedings. Somewhat easy A if you engage with the material.

Prof. Kriner gives lively lectures with opportunities for student input; theres a clear rationale throughout. Course went through insightful analysis on history of and contemporary debates on American government.
Very tough

Professor Douglas is the most encouraging and guiding artist I've studied with. He is a "yes, and..." professor, building on your ideas with his wealth of knowledge and acute perception. I've made some of my most boundary-pushing work under Douglas. It's also really easy to get along with him and he has great style.

Douglas is one of my absolute favorite professors at Cornell! He gives amazing feedback and is very open to new ideas! Always accessible outside of class! Would 11/10 recommend to anyone who is able to take his classes!

Douglas is a world class professor. Hes an absolute genius in the way he aids people with their artwork and learning process. Lots of studio lab hours so you can get a lot of quality work done. And he is extremely helpful and insightful. Too good for Cornell. More a MIT media labs guy. Asked for a lot and we learned a lot

Frequently seems to care more about how well you can explain your work than the quality of the work itself. At least for 2601 - Get ready to pay for materials (in AAP, this is most classes, but more so for Photo).

One of the rare professors who has the ability to encourage students to challenge themselves beyond the academic assignment and outside the studio setting. Knowledgable, resourceful, unconventional, insightful, relentless in helping students. Most impactful studio course I have taken yet.
Whatever he teaches, take it. Whatever he tells you to read, read it. His classes are an artwork unto themselves.
One of the worst professors I've ever had.  Seemed to be very immature and teaching didn't come natural.

Dedicated, brilliant, honest, great listener/observer, thoughtful with comments/feedback, won't do anything unintentionally, a lively man who is passionate about teaching and not for tenure or concerned about making friends/enemies. Extremely focused.
This guy pays just too much attention on coding style and will deduct your marks unwarned because of that. I got a C... Though good teaching anyway.
A beautiful mind
This guy is a beast

He is soooo helpful that although he does not usually hold office hours (they got cancelled easily), he even tend to help us when he can, for instance, teaching us automata during a trip to Orlando, telling us about number theory even down in the deep water there with a scuba He is certainly able to explain problems well when he wanna do so.
Wouldn't say more... He is a solid man
Great Professor, super accommodating about deadlines and always availabe to answer questions. Very interesting class material too.
He is extremely boring and everyone is asleep. He talks forever in a monotone voice.

Super easy fws about a really interesting topic. Professor Jordan likes people to participate but if you do the readings its easy enough. Nice grader who truly wants to see improvement, will give a good grade if you show curiosity

Very nice, sensitive professor with humor, you are graded by 3 papers and participation alone. Class topic was interesting and we had numerous guest lectures that added to what we were discussing nicely.

Excellent lecturer; really brings material to life as he's lecturing, loves to make funny self-deprecating jokes. Grade for class is almost entirely 2 essays and 2 tests so no room for error, and for the tests you really need to study because the class covers SO MUCH material. Grading standards are high, but he curves at the end of the term

Professor Jordan's lectures were easy to follow and thoughtful and this made the material understandable for someone like me who had literally zero knowledge of archaeology/anthropology. He is caring and kind and easy to approach: he wants to help! Pro tip for class: take notes on the readings as you go along--will make the papers so much easier.

He is genuinely a nice guy and very passionate about the class. Lectures were clear, although his PowerPoints were too wordy and the class would get boring sometimes. He would occasionally crack a few jokes which I appreciate. The exams were fair, although his additional assigned readings could make the in class essays easier.
Kurt is passionate and knowledgeable. I'd recommend ANYONE take his Indigenous Ingenuities class if he's still teaching that with Jolene Rickard. Very interdisciplinary, creative, and fascinating.

Good lecturer and a great guy. He really cares about archaeology and Native American culture. Extremely approachable and will work with you to help you do well in the class. Readings aren't totally necessary (no discussion) but they benefit you a lot on the exams and papers. Tests are pretty hard and very specific. Highly recommend.
Good writing seminar in my opinion. He expects a lot from the essays, but grades fairly and has a lot of interest in the subject, which makes the class more enjoyable. Would recommend.
An extremely dedicated professor who really wants to help his students. You WILL improve your writing if you take this class. Be prepared to put in the work, but it's definitely worth it.

I can easily say one of the best professors at Cornell. Very clear, comprehensible, very fair grader, if you put the time into the essays he will give you an A or A-. Very dedicated and approachable and always willing to help. His lectures are never boring. I would very highly recommend this writing seminar. Absolutely amazing guy.

He's a great guy, extremely helpful and knowledgeable, and takes his classes seriously.  He'll do anything for you if you show interest and dedication.  He expects what college professors should of their students.  I would recommend him to anyone

What a nice guy. He may be a tad bit shy/nervous and not the best public speaker but he's knowledgeable about the subject and passionate about it, and if you go to him for help he is always there and very understanding and kind. Only negative is that he expects REALLY good papers and really detailed, hard grader. Good class overall, learned a lot.
This class was not very difficult, and tests were very fair. The readings outside of class were often boring and tedious, but the lectures were pretty good.

If you do your work, the class isn't that hard.  It's just that people think this is an easy A class where you get an A just for showing up.  I didn't do really well, but I definitely got what I put into the course.  Lectures are sometimes boring, but you NEED to go to know what's going on (unless you buy takenote).
Class readings are pretty good, a few dense books though, lecture is interesting, tests are VERY straightforward, you'll know exactly what to study for.
He is very boring to listen too. Of all his lectures I don't think I stayed awake for any of them. He has a monotone voice what tends to put people to sleep.

Found it very hard to stay engaged with his bland, text heavy, lectures. Tests were based off of the many readings & were very specific to policy. I felt that even though I read and studied, I was unable to do well. Very disappointed by this class and professor. Not always the most interesting lectures but he's nice cool & accomplished, very cool dude
Professor Matsudaira is one of the best I've had thus far. He was passionate, helpful, and very intelligent. Really cared and wanted to engage the class. He was also funny!

An excellent class. He uses very interesting material for teaching so it is easy to stay engaged and learn a lot. The group empirical assignments and presentations were not easy, but they were always interesting and I learned a lot from them.

Only about half of what he teaches us is about actual film music. The rest of his class is about discussing the problematic history of hollywood where he goes on tirades about marxism, male gaze, and the evils of whiteness. You're gonna learn a few things about film music, but don't be fooled, he strays away from the actual subject a lot!
Amazing professor and made learning German fun and easy!

Although I would not necessarily call the class easy, I absolutely loved it.  Professor Hull is one of a kind, and the class is one I will never forget.  She has an incredible knowledge of German History, and the class (Post-War German History) is a great one.  If you have the opportunity, take her class!  You will not regret it.

Had I.V. Hull in '81-'83.  Demanding professor who cares about quality.  Best professor I had at Cornell.  Glad to see she is still true to form.  She made me understand that history is a product of interacting groups in society, not just the actions of one leader; not just the program of one ruling party or government.

Hull is probably the best professor at Cornell. She will actually take time and proof your essays before you turn them in (she actually encourages it). She is clear, intelligent, and caring. Idiots beware, she will call you out. Come to class prepared, or get chewed out. If you are prepared to work, definitely take a class with Hull.
Course is a lot of work. Come prepared to sections, go to lecture. Tough grader but not unreasonable; she does have a serious attitude problem, however.

great lecturer- clear concise and a great discussion leader, but her personality leaves something to be desired. If you don't like profanities and hostility directed towards you for no good reason - don't take her.
One of the best profs at Cornell. Take whatever class she is offering--it will be worth it.

Awesome! She is incredible. If you want to become a more critical reader and writer, take her course. Her class is a lot of work but definately worth all the effort. She is the best professor I have ever had!
Really sharp and great discussion leader. Hard grader but completely worthwhile.

This professor graded very harshly and it seemed impossible to do well on an assignment. The class environment made me nervous to participate because I have seen her single students out passive-aggressively. If possible avoid taking a class with this professor as you will put a lot of time and hard work into your assignments for mediocre grades.

SPAN 2095: I always feel comfortable in Spanish classes but this was the first time in my life that a Spanish class made me feel so uncomfortable. She's very passive-aggressive. If you are a native speaker she would grade you harsher. She will literally take off 2 pts in the hw if you forget an accent mark. The material is good, she's not.

she is nice, no busywork which is nice, accessible outside of class, my only issues were the 10 minute quizzes which gave you like 2 minutes to answer each question and how strict grading short response answers was in the class.

Most compassionate professor I've ever had! Assignments have a purpose behind them as the content builds off each other, so there isn't any busy work. Make sure you thoroughly read the readings and pay attention in lectures because there are in-class quizzes. The lectures were pretty engaging, and she really wants you to learn!
amazing professor!
Robin is awesome. His class is interesting and inspiring! Strongly recommend!!!!

Loved the class. 6 quizzes, participation, and one final translation project make up the whole grade. The quizzes are all covered in class. If you studied those well and attended classes regularly, it is an easy A+. Professor McNeal is very understanding and flexible to accommodate students' scenarios. He genuinely cares about the students.

Robin is the best! His lectures are engaging, interesting, and informative. The assignments are well balanced and fun. This guy truly cares about his students and he knows his stuff! I can't recommend this class enough.
Just randomly assign grades to students. Students who work hard and participate actively in class ended up getting lower grades

Doesn't allow for your own interpretation of the theories and readings. It's his way or the highway. Class has a separate clique of people who defend everything he says and therefore succeed in his class.

Had good impression at first, but then realized he gives preferential treatment to a select few and grades are completely based on his opinion. Even if your paper is well-written, if he doesn't agree with you said, expect to get a much lower grade than what you deserve. If you manage to get on his good side, then all is well. Would not take again.

McNeal is my fav prof at Cornell. He's incredibly passionate about his field and is very flexible and considerate. He makes the material interesting and so long as you attend lectures, read most readings, take your time on the essays, and study your notes you'll get a good grade. It was 100% worth getting up early to attend his lectures every week.

Really enthusiastic and knowledgeable of his subject. That being said, he goes off on tangents really easily. Fun to listen to still. As long as you go to lecture, quizzes and papers are really easy. Don't think he gave below an 86 on first paper. Subject material mostly analysis of myth, and only ancient ancient Chinese myth.

He doesn't have a particular format to the quizzes, and grading takes him far longer than it should. He is not that funny, though he tries to be, and some days he doesn't even say anything important to lecture because he goes off on tangents. This course is more literary theory than actual myth but if you want an easy course than this is it.
Lectures are very interesting. Quizes are relatively easy/fair as long as you attend most of the lectures and do some of the readings. I have to say, he is a funny man
He is really great! He is tending and understand the urgent situations. Grading is good too. Really love his course!!!!!
He's a really good teacher and you can tell he loves his subject. He comes in to teach every section for a day. Very easy class, and Wikipedia will be your best friend.
Great guy- funny, realistic expectations. Brought a whole new perspective on China to light. TA's are easy graders; class is really easy to get a good grade in.
Professor McNeal makes learning about Chinese mythology fun and accessible. Awesome teacher, easy class!

take his class ! the best prof in asian dept. very interesting topic and GREAT lectures. like original ideas and discussion. asks questions that make you think. great connection with students! remembers everyone's name and willing to talk to spend time to talk to students. grading is easy too.
Very nice professor and patient. His materials are not too difficult as long as paying attention in class and prepare for quizzes a bit. He explains things well and you know he knows his stuff.
Very good Professor who makes everything he teaches interesting.  Sometimes he oversimplifies more complicated material, but this is an intro class...

This prof has known me for a while. I liked his course a lot. It was an easy course and being Chinese myself I actually learned things. The sections were not that helpful. The essays and quizzes are graded easily, and the homework is almost guaranteed full credit if you just put the effort into them.

An excellent intro to the culture and history of China.  Fun and easy to stomach.  The tests and quizzes aren't hard, and I don't remember reading a lot of the assigned reading (though the reading he assigned was interesting).  The TA can make the class work, like any class here, though, so get in good w/ him/her.
so so easy. SO EASY. he is a good professor. the class is even better if you have a awesome TA like i did.

McNeal is by far the most interesting and helpful teacher out there.  His brilliance is only reiterated by the fact that some of the documents used were translated by him.  He's also incredibly helpful and caring; he will meet with you if you're busy during his office hours.
The prof is HOT, fun, and funny...what else do you want from a class that you're taking to fulfill distribution requirements? Remember gals: eye candy.
Thought 2nd grade multiplication tables were easy? You haven't seen nothing yet. This class will blow your mind. If you don't get an A, you probably should be going to Ithaca College.

Incredibly passionate about ancient Chinese military texts, and can make even a dull reading come to life. Funny, liberal, and an easy grader. That said, not one of the most brilliant minds in the department, and at times you will wonder if the class is worth your time. Great prof if you need distribution requirements; for substance, go elsewhere.
His "Art of War" class is just pure AMAZING...he is a very energetic professor and makes you love the material as much as he does. I absolutely recommend taking the class!!!
I agree that he spends too time on the bronze age.  So he has to rush at the end.   This may because of the reasons why the later part of the course is boring compared to the first half.
Great class, my favorite professor in all my time at Cornell, geniunely interested in the subject, and speaks fluent Mandarin!

Pretty easy class... prof is clear but as he is specialist on bronze age, i think he dwells too much on that period then rushes through the class and then makes the final based on the rushed through portion. That being said, his lectures are clear and he is a nice guy.
Great professor, and very nice guy. Very knowledgable in his field. If you live in Dickson, get to know him, he's your FIR!

Terrible guy. Went to him for help on suggesting academic programs but was replied that my grades suck and thus it would be impossible for me pursue any further study. Is this really what a professor should say? Can't believe such  a man could secure a place at Cornell!!

THE worst lecturer I have ever encountered, which is bad because he tests on them. Slides are unorganized and almost incomprehensible. Uses words and terms unknown to mortal men. TAs even acknowledge that lectures are horrible. Do the reading and go to section and you can get a B. He tests on terms used in lecture, which again, no one understands.

The lectures make almost no sense - even the TAs recognize that. That said, the material is very interesting, and you should be fine if you just do the readings and contribute in sections. You don't really need to understand the lectures that well to do well in the course (although you definitely should try to make sense of them before exams).

Worst teacher I've ever had.I'm not angry about my grade, b/c I did relatively well, but I'm pissed about the class in general--too much reading for a 100 level class, and his lectures are impossible to follow because they are boring and because he has a tendency to ramble and use words and terms that no one understands. DONT TAKE THIS COURSE.
His lectures are incredibly boring, very confusing, and he is completely oblivious to this fact.
Love him! I thought he was a great lecturer and seems to know a lot.

DON'T TAKE unless you have to. awful lectures. He is almost impossible to follow, doesn't know how to use lecture slides. His slides and lectures don't flow at all. He is unorganized, all over the place, and the worst lecturer I've ever had. Readings are interesting though, the subject is interesting, his delivery leaves something to be desired.
Unclear and inserts political bias into every lecture.

DON'T TAKE! Worst prof I've ever had. He tries to act like he's brilliant by making up words. TA's don't speak English. He won't let you choose your TA or switch TA's if you can't understand. He also forces his political views on his students, no opposing ideas or debate. He has no interest in anything that doesn't come from his mouth. PRETENTIOUS
Uses the lecture stage to impose his own beliefs on his students. Books contain no opposing viewpoints.
The dude looks like Santa claus and throws out big words when lecturing- 'nuff said

Don't take don't take. Besides being really pedantic and loving to hear himself talk, Herring doesn't make clear what he's looking for in the exams or on the essay. I went to every lecture, studied, and read and still have no idea what he talked about all semester. Take other intro govt classes instead.
I LOVE THIS MAN!!!!!!!!

Prof. Herring is a pretty chill guy. He likes to use a pretty expansive vocabulary when lecturing and they can sometimes be a bit dry, but if you have any interest in politics and government, you should take this class.Its a lot of reading but thats about it besides one big paper and a midterm&final
Very complex topics but Ron truly wants to see everyone succeed. He always makes an effort to get to know students on a more personal level.

Drugs & the Brain is the hardest and best neuro class I've taken (and I've taken a lot). Between the structure of the course, incredible lectures, and challenging assignments, I learned so so much about neuroscience in this course - more than I have in all my other upper level neuro classes. great lecturer and genuinely cares about his students!
Very engaging lectures and Ron is a super nice guy. Genuinely wants to see all his students succeed and shows everyone tons of respect.

Harder and more involved than bionb 2220 but an excellent introduction to neuropharmacology! The material on the exams comes straight from lecture although they do require a bit of studying. The assignments and final paper are great and provide a deeper understanding of the material. One of the best classes at Cornell, but not nearly the hardest.

The class is fantastic and Dr. Harris-Warrick is an incredible professor. He is extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter, well-organized in his lectures, and always willing to help. Would recommend this class to anyone willing to put in the work.

intelligible and amiable prof.  Very approachable and willing to help his students. Heavily tests out of lecture AND text.  READ, KNOW, UNDERSTAND both.  I had to work hard in this class, but I really enjoyed the neuroscience behind it.  You'll work hard to do well, but it was a fulfilling class!  Go to his office hours before the exams.
Awesome professor.  The best professor I will ever have been taught by and the best class that I will probably ever take.  Everything was so well organized, so clear. He's also a genius.

The material was really interesting. Its a team-taught course, so each prof. teaches what interests him. H-W's drugs lectures were fascinating and very organized, which made it easier to study. Exams were still trickyyy. Tested in great detail, considering the large amount of material. Booker was my favorite lecturer. He is the best.
fun course/professor(s) but very bad grading system. would not recommend.

Very bad class to take for those premeds maintaining good GPAs. Course is structured around a few professors who lecture on different topics. Considering this is an Intro Neurobio course, there is just waay too much information presented. The exams are not only tough (a,b,c,a+b,b+c,all of the above) but curved to a B-!!! interesting but not worthit
Talks fast, gives a lot of information in lecture and yes, you need to know every detail, but very interesting. Partly took the class because he was one of my favorites from BioNB222.
The tests are difficult, especially if you don't have a biochem background, but the subject matter is interesting and he's a good lecturer (better than Nowak, who teaches half the course).
Harris-Warrick is amazing as anything! One of the BEST professors at Cornell!!!
No Comments
whoa...celebrity?
Professor Harris-Warrick is really funny, especially in the drugs lecture. His lecture notes are amazingly useful. Very clear and organized. And he definately knows a loooot!
Ronald is a great teacher. Despite the fact the class is pass/fail, he gives students a lot of attention and wants them to both pass and understand the content. He also gives great life advice.
Excellent professor that gives fun and engaging lectures on C++. Very funny, tells great stories, and gives a level of attention to students that is uncommon in an S/U class. "Never say never!"

Fine professor, but I disagree with the way he taught C++ this year. He attempted to teach the 2003 version of the language first, which caused many issues with modern windows computers. His lectures aren't engaging, but the slides are accessible online and helpful for homework. Weekly assignments were unegaging and sometimes frustrating.

I forget I took this class sometimes. He's a nice dude but I think he was filling in for the previous prof who apparently made the class super fun. Dinapoli kind of just read through the slides and I kind of just had to figure out how to do the assignments on my own bc lectures felt pointless to me. Better ways to learn UNIX but nothing against him

He expects you to read his mind on assignments: doesn't give specific instructions and penalizes students heavily for not following implied instructions. He clearly cares more about his other job than he cares about teaching.
Fantastic class. Concisely hits the key features of C++. Gives just enough technical context to appreciate how the language works, without getting inundated by superfluous detail.
Very practical class.  Teaches C++ in a clear, concise fashion. Generally helpful, and a bit eccentric.
An extremely knowledgeable and respected professor

a really incredible person. the tests are very fair and he is always willing to meet with any student. a truly good person to meet at cornell and a person guided by values and compassion for his students. take this class.

Amazing professor who really understands and knows the field. He is very passionate about the subject. Only graded by two exams and a analytical group research paper (usually combining economics and statistics). Read his book-its very helpful and the past exams are usually what he asks on the test.

Professor Ehrenberg was the best professor I have had at Cornell. I am so thankful that I took his class and wish I could take it again before I graduate! He is generally an amazing professor and I recommend that all students have the opportunity to take his class before graduating. He genuinely cares about his students. You're the best RGE!

RGE is a professor you won't appreciate until the very last day of classes. But he truly is an inspiration, a renown economist, and you will learn a ton from his class. He's also very fair - take his paper seriously, use the practice midterm/finals to study from, read Tuition Rising, pay attention in lecture and you'll be fine. He's genuinely nice.
Extremely caring and helpful. Really makes you think about controversial issues and encourages you to form your own opinion. Ehrenberg is the best!
willing to work with students who care

Wonderful professor. Clearly not trying to overburden students with work or destroy any GPAs, just wants us to understand the complexity of university decision making. Attend lecture, pay attention, read Tuition Rising, practice with last years' tests, and go see him in office hours.
Very interesting professor and class. I disagree with commenter who said he is full of himself; while he does boast it is very tongue in cheek.

Ehrenberg is awesome. You have to go well out of your way, more so than with other profs, to get him to notice you... but if you do it's well worth it. He's opinionated, and it's awesome, especially since ILR seems to only hire bleak, boring people who have nothing worth saying anymore. Ehrenberg is the best thing to happen to ILR
Good Class!
I dont know too much about the content, and that stuff... but two words...Stud Muffin.  Every day in this class was like a vacation of my senses.
Good class.

He's a great professor and lectures are very interesting. This class is perfect for economics students who want to listen to fun stories and write essays instead of solving math problems. Attendance is not mandatory, but you won't be bored if you go. Make sure you understand the practice prelim and you'll be fine for the real exam!

Great class. Great professor. He's so funny and amusing. Subject matter is definitely interesting, too. For the economics major, it is definitely a class to be taken if you want a break from all the math and tough grading.
Very interesting guy, good at telling stories, funny and nice but kind of full of himself (in an endearing way though...).  Good class.
No Comments

i had a great time and learned a lot. a very lighthearted but in-depth approach. was nervous about taking a course based on the prof's own book (those can be bad, when the prof just basically reads verbatim -- why go to class!??), but this was well worth it. had a good time with my end-of-term project too.
Very nice and helpful. Exams are a joke and he's very very easygoing. take 240 with him for an easy time

Ehrenberg cares SO MUCH about his students.  He is a very personable, endearing professor who has a passion for what he teaches.  His Econ of the University class is very interesting, great class, and good if you don't want too much work.
No Comments
really interesting, great and easy class (good excuse for a 300-level econ).
coolest prof at cornell... without a doubt
I have never met a man this intelligent or this skilled in his teaching abilities.  A few more like him and this university would be top five.

Not enough space here to describe how horribly unorganized this professor is. Its like they poured researched gathered online and put it on random powerpoint presentations that were full of errors and messy. No clarity or explanations on assignments, very dry course teaching, no interactive experience on such an importance study of a course. Awful

I took a course with Prof. Mize at Oregon State University and the course organization was a disaster from day one, he gave almost no instructions on how to participate in the class discussion board, and then graded rather harshly. A majority of the class had their grades fall in week 3.  Doesn't answer emails on time or at all, do not recommend.

He really knows what he is talking about. Though he is very distractable and goes off on tangents sometimes, he is always entertaining, and will get the class laughing at/with him at least once per class. The reading is heavy, and necessar. You can choose to make this a hard or easy course depending on how much real thought you put into it.

The best teacher I've had at CU. He made lectures interesting and engaging. I couldn't ask for a better lecturer. It's a bit reading intensive (~150pgs/wk) but worth it!!! Take his classes. He's even got a fanclub on facebook!

The class is so easy its embarassing. The prof, though, really shouldn't be at Cornell. I have little problem with a liberal bias but he has no basis for half of his conjectures it's really a disgrace. The textbook is so jaded it's indescribable. And he has no insights at all, just jabs at anything conservative. Class's easier than h. school though

He used statistics, history, & a few specific case studies to describe the communities, but never went deeper than that. No analysis, no insights, almost nothing about culture. Just when I thought it was going somewhere, he would move on to a different ethnic group. Bland, superficial, uninteresting. Not bad, just not good.
Excellent Professor! Great teaching style and definitely knows how to make the material interesting. LOVE HIM!
Very interesting professor.  Topics of discussion were extremely interesting.  He's a fair grader and more than willing to assist any student when in need.  Take his courses.

Covered a broad range of topics concerning an incredibly broad range of racial and ethnic groups. He assigns a lot of readings but it's all really interesting. He really challenges you to introduce new thoughts. Extremely fair grader. AMAZING professor. Take any one of his classes.
Tough grader but not impossible. Attend lectures, go to discussion, you'll be fine. Essays aren't that bad, do the readings

Prof. Kline is very engaged with his material. Although the material itself is not always very exciting, he presents clear arguments about everything he is teaching, and thus makes the content more interesting and applicable.

Prof Kline keeps the potentially boring subject of technological history interesting by focusing upon the use/human-driven perspective of history rather than the much overused technologically driven view of history.  A short writing assignment is due every friday and the majority of your grade consists of 3 papers.
Great

I love prof. Kline- he's a cute old man, esp when his hair is messy. He makes the history very interesting- showing all perspectives, including politics with no bias at all. Very, very interesting readings, and papers were actually sort of enjoyable to write. Grades fairly for sure- do a good job, get your facts straight and you'll get a good grade

Made the subject matter very interesting, surprisingly enough. Is obviously expert in his field and is eager to help anyone who shows interest. Very professional and a real gentleman. This is a great history course for anyone, engineer or not.
Excellent prof, cares very much about his students.  Go to office hours, take advantage of all Prof. Kline has to offer.  You will take a lot away from his class - well worth your efforts.
A genuinely good guy.
Interesting lectures.  Consisted of 3 essays and a final paper.
_Very_ well organized, you know exactly what he's going to be talking about throughout the course of the lecture.  Made an effort to make issues in the History of Technology not boring.

pretty fair grader, people got through the class with B+/A- without doing the readings. really nice man.  tries to crack jokes.  very accessable. says the words "essentially" "striking" and "emphasize" a lot.  a really great teacher
Easily the worst professor I've had at Cornell.
Boring. Hard to listen to.

I don't recommend him or any of his classes. His lectures are very disorganized and unclear. He himself is also very disorganized and unhelpful. He barely knows his material and spends most of the time trying to crack jokes and seem cool. He can be very offending to students at times. Long story short, try your best to avoid this guy!

Professor Booker's teaching style is more annoying than helpful...his tactics to make students pay attention in class ultimately led to distraction. He knows what he's talking about, just doesn't convey it well. The material is pretty straightforward, but the test questions are not very well written.
He stresses what he thinks are important. He words questions so poorly on exams. He shouldn't teach. Pretty much the worst professor I ever had in my life.
He claims that he's a biologist but he doesn't know his material at all. How is he a professor? Students know more about biology than he does. It's a shame that Cornell has a professor like him.
He doesn't even seem to know his material. He's so focused on trying to keep students awake and making jokes that it's distracting. One of the most annoying professors.

Booker made learning fun and entertaining. He was helpful during office hours, and the students who went to OH regularly did better in his class. Just make sure to understand the concepts and review until you do. Ask about stuff you find confusing and you’ll remember it better. Questions will ask indirectly about the material.

He is a great professor who really cares about his students and tries hard to let you LEARN and think. I went to his office hours every week and he makes sure you don't leave his office confused. You do have to put in the effort too, however. He curves the class nicely, and wants people to do well. Tests are fair: work in=work out.

STAY AWAY FROM THIS MAN. Everyone who went to office hours for help left crying. He would attack kids for no reason and was extremely unapproachable and not helpful. He likes to say that he and his daughter worked so much harder than all of us in college. he curved the class to a B-

Cannot keep his focus. He values showing off more than actual teaching. Never gives you a straight answer to without arrogant, useless, and irrelevant sophistry. Took another of his class too, it was the same thing. Arrogance coupled with the inability to keep his mind on a topic consistently for 5 minutes. A peasized brain not suited for the job.

Booker's inability to give a lecture without trying to be "cool" is as irritating as his inability to draft comprehensible exam questions. Prelims are not about understanding material, but about trying to ascertain what he's attempting to ask in his misguided and poorly-worded questions. In office hours he is condescending without needing to be.

Knows his material and is obviously knowledgable, but he seems moronic sometimes (he makes mistakes during lectures and gets confused, gets angry at students who simply do not understand, and makes multiple grading errors). But he DOES care about students, and is very helpful about course advice and the like. Not bad.
Worst professor ever. ruins your gpa. never take his classes.

His subject material is a lot tougher than Seely's for this class but he seems to do a reasonable job of presenting it.  He comes across as a little brusque sometimes but I think it's all in fun.  He's pretty funny sometimes.

Uses a textbook that is designed for upperclassmen and grad students, which is extremely dense. His lectures seem okay, but you have to read the textbook in order to actually understand the material at the depth he wants and do well on his exams. Extremely difficult class that is way more work than an introductory class should be.

He cares more about finishing his lecture than presenting it in an understandable manner. So the material becomes confusing and he's not very approachable for help. Almost as if he doesn't care about the students.
As a lecturer, he's sort of confusing and has SO MANY typos in his powerpoints. He's funny and all, but I had to read the textbook to get clarification. He doesn't really respond to e-mails either.
Not always present, doesn't give useful information always, really only knows his developmental stuff. Doesn't respond to emails.
No Comments

Considering I had Professor Chen for his first time lecturing CHEM 2090, I think he did reasonably well. His lectures got better over the course, and often were relevant for exams so I don't recommend skipping them. Note that because the chem department reuses exams, he doesn't release the answer keys for prelims. Make sure you go to office hours!

This class was alright for the most part. The only reason this class doesn't deserve a 5 is that the professor did not provide any practice material. The content covered on the prelim and final were rather reasonable and can be studied for with just materials you find online.

The exams often go further than what was covered in lecture. There was also a lack of practice exams, meaning that we were completely in the dark as to the format of the questions. The notes were also not posted on canvas.

Honestly not as bad as many people say he is - the lectures are fascinating, and he's very by the book in terms of teaching the content - often following it closely. Unlike previous semesters, he interweaves his research focus, but in a way that is interesting and not heavily focused on(test-wise). Review sessions are a must attend

Lectures seemed pretty irrelevant, Dr. Chen didn't give a lot of information about actual labs. Quizzes were okay but pretty random; office hours were also unhelpful. The lab reports were TA graded, and very lenient. Labs themselves were pretty difficult, but manageable if you prepared for them. The class overall required a LOT of work!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Two thumbs down. Lecture irrelevant to current lab work (content covered in class after lab is complete). Quizzes unrepresentative of learning goals, more like random trivia. Gave it my all, but missed a lab due to an injury which resulted in a HUGE hit on my grade (lost half a letter grade b/c I only told my TA instead of him). Regretting chem.
Horrible class, good professor. I REALLY learnt what that x-axis means.
He didnt make us buy textbooks. He cares about the students but not about the class. He could try to make 3020 better but he doesnt.
tests go way above the chem 2090 syllabus
Lectures are easy to follow but do NOT reflect the exams. Repeats test questions so does not give practice prelims or study guides.
Extremely hard to understand in class and read what little information he puts on the board. Definitely should not be teaching an intro class for freshmen.
The test does not reflect homework. He teaches beyond what he's supposed to teach and puts them on the test. Lectures fast and hard to read handwriting or understand his pronounciation

Terrible handwriting + doesn't know how to erase the chalkboard. He has trouble pronouncing things. Goes into his own research and escapes the bounds of General Chemistry like he's supposed to be teaching.

Good lecturer, but topics are presented out of order (in a way that I found non-intuitive). The course (especially the labs) might be very difficult if you've never been exposed to chemistry. Exams are more or less fair, but there are one or two curveballs on each one. Study the lecture notes carefully and read the book to do well.
No Comments
Best chem professor ever. Nuff said
hard to understand but he's a very good professor. doesn't go over the whole book though so you must read it to do well

One of the worst courses I've taken in Cornell partly because of the lecturers and partly because the tediousness of lab. Chen conducts the class with professionalism and with an iron fist. She is very strict but don't be afraid because she's like that with everyone. As a lecturer, she was monotonous. Wished she  made the course more interesting.
Two faced. Classes were close to useless. It was all up to the students to cover the work. She ditched lectures very often and handed us to the oblivious TA's. Very moody as well.

Learned a lot in lab and became more confident in my research skills, but she is too strict, especially on those research papers. Good lecturer but course is too time consuming, especially for a measly two credits!
Great class, everything was very clear and well organized. Dr. Chen is really nice and more than willing to help you out.

Professor Chen is extremely dedicated to teaching. Her lectures are well prepared and she will spend a lot of time during office hours helping you out if you need it. She is a very tough grader, but there are 400 students in the whole course, so she needs to be fairly strict. Overall, she is a very intelligent and dedicated asset at Cornell.
She's pretty helpful, especially during office hours. Although quizzes/tests/papers were fair, she could be a tough grader at times. She really wants to help you learn, and it shows in her teaching.

At first glance, Professor Chen seems like an awkward and strict guy. But once you get him talking, he is super friendly, accomodating, and funny. I can tell he puts a lot of thought into his lectures and is very prepared for any questions you could possibly throw at him.

Professor Chen has great lectures. He was very accommodating as well: when I fainted in class, he personally called Cornell Health for me. However, his prelims and pop quizzes were very difficult. He also cold calls in class, so do the readings. Professor Chen was very inspiring though. I've dedicated the rest of my life to optimizing concrete.

Tests are fair. He does not give the most interesting lectures (partly because of his accent), but if you pay enough attention you will learn a lot. Office hour can be super helpful since he only guides you through the problems and makes you do them by yourself. He is also very caring and offers extra office hours before exams.

He's not the best lecturer, but he's a nice guy. I usually zone out during lecture because the material isn't very engaging, but it's easy enough that you can learn it by yourself. He's really nice with homework etc, I think we had 9 assignments for the whole semester, and they were all pretty easy. He makes sure you don't have hw over breaks!

Her lectures are extremely boring and often run past when the class ends. However, there is really no reason to go to lectures since attendance isn't mandatory and the entirety of the course is graded based on 3 papers, which you can all write on the same thing.

I cannot emphasize how much I regret taking her class. Easily one of ILR's worst professors. Gives little to no instruction for papers, then grades them insanely harshly. Averages on her papers were normally in the C range, even perfectly good papers. Lectures were boring and she always goes overtime. Very few kids got into the A- or A range. AVOID
Very little direction on papers. Lectures were extremely boring. There is a ridiculous amount of reading. If you can, choose someone else.

Professor Chen is extraordinarily familiar with the material she teaches and lectures were packed with interesting detail, if sometimes a bit disorganized. She gets a bad rap because it's impossible to do well without at least skimming the readings, but if you keep up and come to lecture you'll do well. Best first-year ILR prof if you put in work.

I did not enjoy my time with Chen by any means; she was a new prof and you could tell. Her rubrics lacked consistency, and though she promised a curve at the end the semester, there wasn't one. You can do without reading what's assigned - using just the slides will do. So long as you write about what she personally agrees with, you'll be fine.

Do not take Labor History with Chen. She and the TA both graded so harshly yet assignments had minimal and unclear instruction. Lectures went overtime every day. So much reading each week. Content was interesting but this class could've been taught way better.

Avoid this class with Professor Chen!! Both the Professor and TA are extremely harsh graders and the entire grade in the class is made up of 3 essays. The essay prompts are vague and the criteria they use to grade the essays is very specific, and impossible to meet. With only 3 assignments it's very hard to improve your grade.

Very hyped professor who mostly lives up to it. His grading scheme is designed for everyone in the class to get an A. DSP sort of bounces around between image processing (not that interested) and cooler stuff like multirate filters. Projects make no sense but are essentially graded on completion. Overall, an easy if slightly disappointing class.

I only went to class a few times, but the times that I did were always great. Oftentimes he would write something silly on the board, or if you were lucky he would make fun of a student for asking a bad question. It's also always a fun challenge to try to understand what he's saying. If you actually want to learn, however, you have to read.

He is not a bad professor, but this class can easily be passed just by doing homework and reading the textbook. I would say go to lectures if that is an easier way for you to comprehend the material. Lots of stuff on prelims and finals can be found in a textbook. Homeworks are not graded but weekly quizzes are solely based on homework.

It is a pretty tough class and the TA's are pretty bad. The professor is good at teaching, but he is very archaic. Homework is optional but you need to do it to pass this class. Textbook is your friend. This class is more learning it on your own.

The class is tough tbh. Got A in 1920, B+ in 2930. Lectures are chalk & blackboard and quite organized. Funny to me, not to everyone. 2 concerns: 1) He doesn't do examples in class, you'll only see them on HW. He only teaches theory (at least for most topics) AND 2) He will often, especially early in the semester, run overtime by ~3 minutes
Textbook is helpful, interesting lectures, friendly
He's definitely not for everyone as his teaching style is pretty archaic but if you get used to it you'd see he's actually a very good teacher.

stopped going to lectures after the first month and fully completed the class by learning from TAs and the textbook, incomprehensible and confusing lectures.

He also put his office hours right after the weekly quizzes, likely so that no one comes to him for help.
avoid
Escape if you can.
Lectures have a lot of info that aren't relevant for exams. Often, he would rush at the end and go over the class's time slot. Tells jokes sometimes. The textbook was much more helpful.
Lectures were interesting but largely unhelpful, you're better off teaching yourself via the textbook.
Fine professor

Lectures were pretty unhelpful and confusing, mostly just proofs and didn't really teach how to do the problems. The textbook was definitely really important. All of the test problems (Prof. Berest wrote every test though there were two other profs) are really similar to textbook problems so do the homework and you'll be fine.

Lectures are all over the place and not even relevant to what we do for homework, quizzes, and exams. Ended up learning from the textbook and doing the homeworks, and his exams didn't even have to do with those and what we did in class. I attended a few lecturers for the other professors and the difference was huge. Do not recommend at all.

If you want to learn calc 2, youre better off watching khan videos. He is all over the place in lecture and seems to add more than needed in the small amount of class time. Even though he says a lot, you practically get nothing out of it.
Not a good teaching method
Clumsy during lecture. Unclear objectives. Makes condescending jokes. Mean and loud. Exams were graded unfairly. Test questions were about as well put together as his lectures.
Good lectures, assigns an appropriate amount of homework to teach the material. Often falls behind the lecture schedule however.

Professor is very good at explaining course material and answers any questions in-lecture. Doesn't, however, cover anything that is not in the textbook, in principle. Sometimes decides to make some jokes, which are usually pretty funny. Overall, a fine professor.
He's good. The lectures are clear and  well structured.

Professor Berest followed the textbook very closely, and if you paid attention in class, was very helpful. A lot of students don't like his lectures, but they were useful as long as you didn't slack off yourself. The exams were challenging but doable if you keep up with the homework, and this class was much better than MATH 1920.

Really didn't seem interested in teaching the course. Lectures were very dull and at times could be condescending, office hours weren't very helpful either. Tests very proof based for an engineering math class and watch out for the truefalse questions. Material seemed to repeat itself after the first prelim. Most didn't go to class mid semester

I can assure you, there's a huge chance that after the first few weeks, you stop attending this man's class. He is basically useless, and you learn everything from the textbook. He also has really mean negative grading true and false questions that mess a lot of people up. If you have a choice, take it with another professor.

Class was always packed but it was rather dull. He tried very hard to make it interesting but, we were often bored. All in all, he's a nice and enthusiastic professor but the book and other resources were essential to learning in this course because his teaching style was difficult to follow.
Nice professor. Comes late in lectures tho.. and finishes late.. kinda funny.. overall a decent professor

I dropped this course last year because I couldn't keep up, but Yuri's excellent lectures kept me going through the interminable homeworks. That being said, he usually arrives 5 minutes late for lectures and finishes 10 minutes over time (punctuality is not one of his virtues...)
I can't understand people here complain about him.. His explanation is crystal clear and very helpful.
No need to attend lecture. Just go to discussions and learn from the textbook yourself.

His lectures are very clear and sequential. Example questions are very similar to prelim problems. Homework is not difficult just tedious. TA is helpful. He tends to keep us late, which has become really annoying.
Yuri is awesome.  Learned a ton in his class.  Probably my favorite math teacher while I was at Cornell.

Funny guy.  Standard Theorem-Proof lectures.  HW was long, about 70% proofs.  Exams were fair.  Usually late to class, always in a rush, and usually kept us 10 minutes over.  Didn't like people coming to office hours without specific questions, but willing to help.

Separate graduate student as grader. He is easily sidetracked. Can sometimes be unclear (likes to give "non-examples"), but generally the material can be figured out with help from the book. Problem sets due once a week, reasonable. Entertaining person, but boring topic. Bring something else to do to class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.  HEAVY accent, tests too difficult, unwilling to help because it will give away answers.  Sloppy on board.  TA's unhelpful.  AVOID AT ALL COSTS.  Take a different course, this one is basically useless.

I hated his class, I hated the way he taught, I hated everything about Math 213. But then I went to Office Hours during Study Week and even though I failed three out of the four tests (including the Final), I still pulled off a C. So I can't give him a really bad rating.
Nice guy, but not the most effective teacher.  He seems to confuse a somewhat easily understood topic.

Berest is a very clear lecturer, and he uses the board very well. His accent can get in the way, but overall he relays the information well. And he tries to make jokes, which work about 30% of the time. At least he tries. But an enjoyable class overall.

Berest was not a solid lecturer.  He was clumsy on the board, and not clear.  Typical of professors I've found thus far in the math department: extremely smart, and very dedicated to his work, but lacking in lecturing skills.  Math 336 itself is a joke...I taught myself and got a good grade.
I don't like her. gives discussion posts too late. like two days before they're due.

Awesome professor who is deserving of a rating. She was very accommodating and understanding (especially during covid 19 pandemic). Each assignment has very clear grading criteria, so it is easy to do well. Lots of guest lecturers, and the course covers a lot of content that gives you a very comprehensive understanding of public health nutrition.

She is a great professor. Very knowledgeable. It is a fun class, you learn a lot of relevant things and a new perspective on examining scientific work. The midterm was graded very fairly and if you completed the study guide it was easy to do very well. The papers are more difficult. Weekly reflections are a major grade boost. I enjoyed the class.

Discussions are great- always compelling and interesting. The assignments are relevant to the class but also very useful- they are worth the time and effort and never just busy work. Grading is fair. Very helpful and willing professor. Lectures are on the dry side, but if you hang in there till discussion, all can be forgiven. She wants to help you

Vogel is a great professor when it comes to class discussions and giving relevant assignments. She is also very helpful and eager to help, just ask questions and go to her office hours-- she really does want to help and cares if you understand the material or not. Her lecture style, however, is boring. It knocks out a kid in our class every time.
smart, pleasant, hot

She was a clear speaker, although her verbal crutches (i.e. "for example") sometimes detracted from what she was trying to say. The reading consisted of articles, and the work was mostly reading responses. I did well in the class, so I'm satisfied!

A lot of reading and writing. For premeds, this class is VERY valuable. The issues and material you learn are very helpful. Professor Vogel is a really nice lady that truly cares about her students and their feedback. She really tries to help her students throughout the course. Just go to office hours.  She's really helpful.

The subject matter is really great- relevant, interesting & current. But Vogel's lecture style just doesn't match the material! She's a very monotone speaker without much passion in her expressions. This could be a phenomenal class if only she could be more lively. Sections are great if you get a good TA!
I loved Vogel. I thought she was pretty interesting if you sat up front and stayed engaged...pretty easy class as long as you go to the review sessions.
Amazingly boring...defied the laws of nature in terms of how boring she could make a lecture.  I often left lectures without the desire to learn anything ever again.
Most of the material in lecture is interesting, although she is not the most dynamic lecturer. The TAs grade the papers, but Vogel has been accomodating with midterm grades and such.
No Comments

Vogel is a waste of space.  I have never seen a more lazy, less dedicated professor.  This lady has no interest in her students whatsoever and makes completely unreasonable decisions regarding grading.  The miderm is not too bad, but papers are graded harshly.  The discussion section is extremely stimulating, lecture however is painful

All she says in um over and over.  I counted one class for 17 mins, and she said um 225 times.  She can't convey a point, she grades very hard for a class that should be medium/easy and lecture is the worst thing ever

Prof. Long is overall an awesome person and very passionate about what she teaches. While being an easy grader, she gives great constructive feedback on writing assignments. She also gives you some free rein on writing topics and usually supports whatever you are enthusiastic about.

She's very nice - won't bother you in class - if you don't want to talk or don't want to volunteer, she won't make you. She gives great advice on papers and a short meeting with her will leave you with an awesome thesis. She grades pretty easily and knows what she's teaching. Also, she invited us over to her house and made us a delicious brunch :)
She's an awesome professor, very easy to talk to, incredibly smart, and I absolutely loved her class. I wish she were teaching this semester!
Fairly easy but very kind and intelligent.

She's a pretty interesting prof. and seems enthusiastic about the subject.  However she constantly assigned readings after saying "I know I've already assigned too much reading, but..." and held class after saying "I know we're getting out late, but...".  Otherwise though she's a good prof.
Amazing...so smart! A very powerful woman! Great class and a good hold on reality!
I love prof. Long, she's very friendly and helpful and very excited about what she teaches.
Professor Arnink was great! Wines and Vines is a great class, and Arnink really cares about her students and teaching them about wine.
Dr. Arnink is really sweet! Her lectures can get a bit boring since it's not entirely necessary to pay attention but you get to drink wine every day so I'm not complaining.

She's a very kind woman, but often seemed confused by what she was teaching. Her lectures consisted of her reading off the slides verbatim and then repeating the exact same thing in a slightly different way. The class often felt discombobulated. She's nice and understanding, but not a particularly helpful instructor.

Barbara was one of my favorite professors at Cornell. Her experience with wetlands before becoming a professor is one of her biggest assets when it comes to her teaching style. She is also very willing to provide extra credit on an individual basis, if you approach her. Barbara has continued to be a mentor of mine since my graduation in 2013.

Barbara is an extremely friendly and understanding person. She really cares about wetlands and the environment, and so her philosophy is based more on teaching rather than testing. The class is fairly easy to do well in, especially since she gives so many opportunities to do better. The (outdoor) lab is highly recommended.

The real deal. Extremely passionate about the subject, and one of the few at Cornell who combines outstanding science with practical experience in the 'real world' (which she assures us is out there). Take her class!
She was fabulous and I learned a ton.  She was very accessible and encouraging and continued to be a great mentor even after I graduated.
Barbara is a wonderful professor and her class was one of my favorite at Cornell.  The lab section comes highly recommended.  She is very helpful and very knowledgeable and passionate about her work.

She's an incredibly smart and opinionated person in the best way possible. She challenges you to look at neurobio in a new way, and I loved her papers, assignments, and lectures. If you can take a class with her, do it!

great class, Prof Finlay is incredibly knowledgeable and will really stimulate your interest in cognitive neuroscience.  the material is challenging, but if you go to class and do the readings you will be fine.  she's very approachable and willing to help students.

also Psych 425. This class was my favorite Neurobio class. It made you question everything you thought you knew about consciousness, motor control, memory, thought, everything. Learn about interesting studies, read dense but interesting articles. Workload isn't bad but papers are challenging. Encourages group collaboration and leaves time for it. She is brilliant. Highly recommend!!
useless readings, papers assignments excessively difficult...she is a just impossible to deal with
ambiguous assignments.  never understand what she's asking for.  she thinks nearly everyone else is wrong so consulting other sources is irrelevant.
REally, really smart.  She is one crazy person. She would lecture to an empty lecture room and not notice that everyone was missing.

Her lectures are really disorganized, and she frequently forgets to bring her own notes and then tells the whole class about it. Her tests are tedious and some of the questions are impossible to answer correctly unless you memorize all of the textbook. Overall not such a great class.
I love this class. I decided to switch to an HD major because of it.
Shes so unclear! Always contradicts herself and gets her own iClicker questions wrong! If this class isnt a requirement for you dont take it!!

really nice lady. love the layout of the class - one day discussion, one day lecture. really interesting material, but be prepared to dissect research articles. no tests, 3 summaries and a big paper. really laid back and a nice change from tons of prelims. great lady, also, really wants you to learn and help you
nice woman but lectures were boring and unclear, tests were really specific and unfair....definitely do the poster grading option because it is an easy A and will bring up your grade

some professors know how to lecture, prof C knows how to teach. She will uplift you and inspire you to work harder, do better, and not care what others think. She has such zany ideas about these classic texts, shell really surprise you! Shell expose you to several of the trickier dialects of academese along the way.

Take this prof if you enjoy rich theory-informed interpretations of challenging poetical works. This is not your grandmother's Shakespeare professor. She expects bold, theory-rich readings, and daring, cutting-edge theses. The sky is the limit in Prof C's class. How much you'll learn only depends on how far you're willing to go.

Lenient grading and light amounts of reading. Overall a kind and very easy prof. She is so encouraging and sweet, and her classes are highly enjoyable. It'd b hard to find a better course than Renaissance Poetry w ProfC, in which students recite sonnets to each other and engage in lively conversations about lyric form, poetic devices, & e-m culture

Lenient grading and light amounts of reading. Overall a kind and very easy prof. She is so understanding and sweet, and her classes are highly enjoyable. It'd hard to find a better course Renaissance Poetry w/ Prof C, in which students recite sonnets to each other and engage in lively conversations about lyric form, poetic devices, & e-m culture

She had unreasonably high standards for grading and was unwilling to give constructive feedback, even to the point of refusing to meet with students. Will take points off if you suggest anything she does not agree with. Speculates wildly in class but docks students for speculating, even if it's the same speculation she made. Overall, horrible.

Really enjoyed this class. Great availability for office hours and opportunities for extra credit. Light work load and interesting discussions. However, I would not recommend it unless you are already a fairly skilled writer. Get ready to be wrong often but learn from your mistakes.

Eccentric character. Assignments are manageable - ripped apart my first essay but then I started getting better grades, felt as though my writing improved over the semester. Every Friday was discussion. Will start to dislike you if you skip class, especially those Fridays. Will tell you straight up if she agrees with you or not.
She was terrible. We started with a full class but almost everyone dropped. She was rude and condescending to everyone in the room.

Rude to students in class. Forces her interpretation of the text. Takes any disagreement and lack of 150% attentiveness in the class (any missed classes or late to any appointment) very personally. I desperately wanted to love this class but the professor made it hard to.
Very focused on the academic point of view ONLY. Helpful outside of class, but very schematic within it.
Professor Correll has a great sense of humor and is obviously passionate about her subject. What she knows about the Renaissance poets could fill a library.
Knows what she's talking about. Really hard grader but somehow I managed to do well. Offers chances for extra credit. Interesting course.
very funny and down to earth
Very knowledgeable about the subject and an enthusiastic teacher. Not the easiest grader in the world, but most end up doing fine in the end (or so I'm told).
One of the best, most practical classes I've taken, taught by one of the best professors at Cornell.

This is probably the best course available at Cornell.  This 3 credit course is two weeks in Washington D.C. over winter break but counts towards the spring. You get to go out and interview people.  AMAZING!  Prof. Knuth will open your eyes to the real policy process and teach you more than you could learn in four years in the government major.
Amazing professor. I strongly recommend this class. It's mostly based on understanding experiments and studies. There is a lot of discussion.

I love Prof. Lust. She has helped me refine my interests over the past year and always answers my questions, no matter how numerous they are. She is much better in smaller group settings, so take a seminar with her if you can, but she's wonderful in any class. I've taken five of her classes and plan to take many more.
Great professor- so helpful and so willing to work with you. If you go and talk to her, she works with you. This is the professor all Cornell professors should be like!

Although I was able to make up for this fact, her lectures and notes were entirely disorganized and her tests were poorly worded. It was easy to see why my classmates had difficulty drawing larger themes out of what she presented in class. Her research has lagged of late, making her frustrated and difficult to work with. Avoid joining her lab.

She is an insult to the field.  She simplifies science down to an elementary and extremely understandable level, but in the process murders the validity of the material.  That being said, the class is easy.

I'm not gonna be shy about it - professor Koslowski was one of my favorite professor at Cornell. From the academic side - yea her work was fascinating and important. But outside of the classroom, she was one of the easiest professors to connect with, and one of the most helpful. One of the other reviewers had it right when they wrote 'role model'.

While she really is a nice woman, her tests hardly corresponded with the lectures (which were often not very organized). Her TAs graded the tests and were too specific for what the lectures provided.
