Professor Kelly's negative reviews are understandable, but do not easily write her off as the worst professor at Cornell. If you put in your best, she recognizes and rewards dedication and hard work. This class TREMENDOUSLY helped improve my writing skills but this course will not be for everyone. Professor Kelly set me up for success at Cornell.
A-lot of work!
Would not take her class again, please be aware of her ridiculous workload.

She wasn't THAT bad lol. You do A LOT of reading for classes and for papers she makes everyone write multiple drafts. I never had troubles with her grading so the class for me was just an FWS with a lot of work, but a lot of my classmates understandably hated the class. If you're not really into US history, there are easier fWS's and chiller profs
Terrible professor. NEVER take her class. Grading is unreasonable and work load is ridiculous. Had a horrible time in her class. I should have dropped while I had the chance.

Terribly boring lectures and strange discussion based class. Weekly writing assignments amounted to well above 5,000 words per week. Several longer essays were 15+ pages. Tough grader and has unrealistic expectations in terms of the time assignments should take. Definitely do not take if you're a stem major. Even it you're not, wouldn't recommend.

This course is not difficult conceptually. But it becomes the worst class I have ever taken at Cornell because of her. She is such a tough grader and never says things clear about her criteria. She also demands a lot from her students without doing much on her own.

I dont know why this class would exist. There are so much extra works, and they are not helpful at all. I don't think my writing qualities improved through her class. Instead, I was so stressed, and I wished I could drop this class earlier. I think my college life would be much better without this class.

She is the worst professor Ive ever met at Cornell. Her assignments are heavy and tedious. Even the essay rubrics do not make any sense. There are so many extra weekly individual meetings - so intense and time-consuming. As a student who suffered in her class, I suggest you guys not take her class. Good luck!

The worst professor ever. NEVER EVER WANNA TAKE HER CLASS AGAIN!!! Her assignments do not make sense at all and are so fk time consuming. I did not learn anything from this class. Just don't take her class then you will have a wonderful college experience!

King-O'Brien was an incredible professor, you will learn SO much with her. Yes, this course was insanely difficult, so only take it if you're up for the challenge, but she will give you the grade you deserve based on the work you put in. She's also such a fun teacher when you have a good group of students. Be ready to participate!

Every class has a quiz regarding the reading previously assigned. Each reading is between 60-150 pages between a 2 day period. Multiple papers are due throughout the semester including one up to 15 pages. She is not easily accessible outside of class and difficult to reach by email. She'll make you work to pass and does not let you miss class.

Taking this class was the worst decision I made last semester. Very vague with the feedback, not likable, and all around a tough grader. Every paper will be at least five pages ( one was over ten) and the take home essay required us to write eight pages in 24 hours in response to a prompt she posts online. Way too hard for an FWS. Do not take!

Easily the best professor I've had at Cornell.  You definitely have to work hard to get anything out of her class but it is so worth it in the long run.  She is incredibly helpful in one-on-one meetings.
I was excited to take this class. But this prof. is horrible. Major chip on her shoulder - i always felt like she was mad at me when I asked her anything.

She is probably one of the worst teacher's I've had at Cornell. While her assignments make no sense, she grades harshly and would rather fail you than help. You can tell that she doesn't care about students; she treats every student as if they've wronged her in some way. I highly recommend against a class with her.

If you love literature DO NOT take this class. This teacher really knows how to dampen interest and enthusiasm. Loves to be authoritarian. This teacher will treat you like a middle schooler, so if you want to be treated like an adult her class is not for you. She is intentionally intimidating. Does NOT create a comfortable atmosphere in her class

Super cool professor! I had her FWS on poetry (specifically loving and hating it) and as someone who doesnt love poetry, i still loved this class. Discussion is super tuned into to real life and not just old white british men. Fair grader and really just wants to help you be a better writer. One of the few online classes that i genuinely enjoyed

Amazing lecturer, really cares about students, and is very accessible. Entertains all questions without making anyone feel silly. Final kicked my butt but course was otherwise pretty fair if you read the textbook outside of class
go to lecture and do readings ahead of time if you dont want to grind before exams. do every homework problem at least once
Multi was very cool to understand. Delp does an excellent job in really providing a conceptual and intuitive mastery of the material. Challenging but very fruitful. Would take again.

The textbook is the saving grace of a Delp course; relying on lectures would leave you desperate, stranded and alone. You will have no choice but to take 1920 with her, but only having the previous reviews to set expectations is a sin- you will be sorely disappointed. Honestly, I am not positive that I had the same professor as other reviewers.

Loved Professor Delp she has skeleton notes for all of her lectures making them so easy to follow and fill in, and she will answer any question you have in office hours. Clearly loves math and wants us to love it too
Amazing professor who is really passionate about what she's teaching. Made a huge difference in the class despite its difficulty.

I didn't show up to 1920 lecture much, but whenever I did she was an amazing lecturer. Expectations for quizzes and tests are clear and if you do the homework and study it well you will do well. Deadlines are a little flexible. If you have the chance to get her, take her and you won't regret it.

Professor Delp is a cool dude. You'll probably get discouraged while doing the homework since some of the problems are straight-up impossible, but the questions on the quizzes and prelims always seem to be fair. She goes pretty fast in her lectures, so stay focused and don't get distracted by things such as the majesticity of her hair

Professor Delp really cares about her students, and is such an inspiring, fair, and passionate person. I thoroughly enjoyed taking multivariable calculus with her, and learned a lot from the course. I came in with no experience in the subject, and now feel confident with all the material. Quizzes and Exams(except maybe the final) are all very fair.
Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures were extremely well planned and organized, and the homework questions were chosen. If you can get Delp, get Delp.

Heard multi can be very bad. However, I was very lucky to have Delp as my professor. I actually ended up liking multivariable. Homework is helpful and prelims/exams very fair. Discussions are helpful.

The only good thing about this class is that hw is worth 30% of grade. She adjusts grade cutoffs very fairly, but that doesn't take away from the material being hard and boring. She is a nice person in general, but her lectures are terrible. She is scatterbrained and gets distracted easily, making it difficult to follow the math problems.

The material itself is hard but going to lectures with Professor Delp and participating makes all the difference. Professor Delp is so excited about math and cares so much about her students, her lectures are great. Wish I could take another class with her.
I don't go to lectures that often since it's 9 am, but when I do go, I never regretted it. She's great at explaining difficult concepts with simpler ones. Also, the lecture note is amazing.

Professor Delp is fantastic! She is really passionate about what she teaches and brings good energy to her lectures. Her exams are really fair and are based on understanding of how everything works rather than just giving really hard questions that are meant to stump students. She is kind and understanding, as well.

Great professor! Truly cares about students, makes an effort to engage the class and keep them awake during the early morning lectures. Very passionate about the subject which comes across in her teaching. Pretty fair weight of homework/assignments, great grading scheme, very accessible especially over EdStem for doubts all semester long.
I have never met a professor as passionate about their course material as Professor Delp. Her lectures are fantastic and engaging. Truly an excellent teacher.

I dropped the class last sem because of another professor, Connelly. I was on track to get a C+ or at most a B- in the course, as Connelly's lectures didn't work for me. Delp's course organization is phenomenal. Love the "skeleton notes" Now on track to get an A/A+, and I have a solid grasp of multi now. Great lectures, textbook is a supplement.
Prof Delp is by far the most engaging and thorough math professor I've had. Multivariable calculus is a difficult, boring subject that she makes enjoyable.

I actually really enjoyed math 1920 because of professor Delp. She gives very clear and engaging lectures which make the course material much simpler and more comprehensible. The homework is reasonably difficult and prepares you well for the exams.

Professor Kelly Delp is a real gem. She has a passion for teaching. Her homework questions really make you question your major. I am lucky to be in her Math 1920 class. I respect Professor Kelly Delp a lot. Sometimes she can speak in Calculus 9 during her lectures so you should know the material well

Dr. Delp is a great teacher and her passion for math really shows in lecture. She's good at explaining difficult topics and very open to questions. Makes very fair tests and wants everyone to do well.

Delp is an amazing person and professor. Extremely kind, passionate, and helpful to all her students. Though the lectures were just what the textbook says, her breaking down the topic in lecture was helpful for me. The lectures were enough for me, no crazy amount of textbook readings, but reading a bit before lecture was always solid.

Lectures didn't really help me in terms of understanding material so I just stopped attending. I basically learned everything from the textbook and did fine. Professor is really kind, caring, and makes lecture fun though. Exams were not too bad; very manageable if you did the homework in my opinion.

Professor Delp taught this class in an extraordinarily approachable manner. The lecture was fun; she may seem a bit disorganized but she is extremely knowledgeable about the material, is passionate about the content, and successfully manages to inspire students with an eager sense to learn. The textbook is a must. Restored my joy in mathematics.

She is literally the best. She is so caring for her students and really tries to make sure you understand the material. Office hours are super useful and thats where she gets to know her students. Even on zoom she played music and made it a really fun environment. She was also really good at answering questions in the middle of lecture.
Kelly Delp is an amazing lecturer! I was intimidated by multivariable calculus but she made it quite easy to understand. It is the best class i have taken so far.
Professor Delp's office hours were extremely helpful. Don't be afraid to schedule an appointment with her as wellshe'll go above and beyond to make sure you understand a difficult topic.

Great Professor. Unlike many professors here she cared about us learning the material and having fun along the way. Dynamic lecturer, and she really goes deep into the visualization of the nitty gritty concepts, which was a lifesaver for a visual learner like myself.

Dr. Delp is a passionate, energetic, and dynamic lecturer who made me love multivariable calculus. If you have to take 1920, take it with her--the class and her exams are FAR more fair than other professors who teach the class. Lectures are essential for understanding conceptual parts of the course, which she loves to test on her prelims and final.
Gives sample past exams but doesnt give solutions. What's wrong with her brain?
Delp is a really cool person who is obviously very passionate about math. Lectures are sometimes tangential and the tests are way too hard (especially prelim 1)

She ditzes out - a lot. And her voice is annoying. And goes on tangents about graphs, and the "+, -, 0" game. For Example - she didn't know the name of the fingers. and then spent a couple minutes telling us about it.

Kelly's lectures are energetic and she's enthusiastic about sharing her love for math. She also tries her best to provide visuals for a better understanding of the material. However, it is multivariable calc, and won't be easy.

Multi is notoriously a hard class; however, Professor Delp has great energy so far this spring. She's a great lecturer and seems like she really enjoys teaching multi. She has her lectures prepared before hand and does not get side tracked. I really like her so far.
Her lectures don't make any sense and don't help with homework or section. Alot of notes aren't given and the group work is stupid.
She is very energetic during lectures and is open to answering questions. Uses a lot of visual representations, which helps with understanding the 3D structures in multi.

She's really sweet and nice but the problem is she can be a little scatter-brained and she makes a lot of mistakes. She's very good about catching and correcting them but by that point you're already confused. Multi is hard enough even with good lectures.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Shefter is horribly boring and has no personality; moreover, he systemically goes on unintelligible tangents which only detract from this course's non existent value. He's a poor teacher, has no identifiable grading structure and its over-dependent on his TA's and the textbooks. The TA was neurotic, formalistic and semantic.
Most boring man on the face of the earth whose lectures are useless. Get to know the TA -- your grade depends heavily on doing so.
horrible class and person. don't know cornell has so many poor profs

super super boring & the only good thing to take his class is that you get guaranteed A besides, you learn nothing.He relies on his TA for everything and rarely interact with students despite the small class(everyone except who wants to get good grades avoid the class)totally unreasonable. what could a good grade count when i got misled and lost!!!

avoid this class by all means. shefter is a bad lecturer and is very biased with his grades. some of his racial comments in reference to 19th century labor history were borderline, if not actually discriminatory which offended me and other non-white students. just my opinion, but this class should really be avoided.

The class is easy to get an A in, as you can see from my grade (A+). This is because of the bonus paper that bumps your grade up, in addition to some sort of grade correction that the TA's do. The lectures are extremely disappointing - very boring. Additionally, I feel that he repeats points too often, and speaks way too slowly. I slept during clas
His lectures are terrible. I was really interested in the material, but I found myself skipping class often and dropped it in late September. It felt like a chore.
His lecture was terrible; belabored points and had a poor style of teaching.  Left mid-lecture and dropped it.

I actually enjoyed this class-- but for the readings, not the lectures. Shefter's lectures are slow-paced to say the least and rather disorganized as he at times gets lost in his notes. The selected readings are interesting and helpful. It's an easy A, as the tests are extremely predictable.

Really, anyone interested in serious scholarship should just avoid.  Unorganized, unclear, and not good at provoking class discussion.  This seminar turned into a lecture every time, and it really wasn't worth my time.

He's nice, but what he teaches is not going to blow your mind. I found myself falling asleep as he basically read bullet points during his lecture. Also speaks waaay too slowly. On top of that, the in-class exams are rushed and the amount of reading is intimidating. Not worth it when there are so many other great gov profs at Cornell.

I'd heard that this class was super easy...but it def was not a breaze last semester...I asked around and everyone I talked to felt the same way...maybe we were all wrong, but don't take it if you are looking for an wasy A.  The TA's run the class basically.  The class is, however, very interesting.
No Comments
Great professor: it is the case that this class is interesting (if you like the material) and easy.

Shefter's 318 (US Congress) class is really easy.  The grade is based upon 1 midterm, 1 final, and an optional paper that can significantly boost your final grade.  His lectures are sleep inducing though...

it IS the case that shefter gives decent lectures despite his quirks.  it IS NOT the case that the class is very difficult.  is IS the case that the in-class exams are rushed.  is IS NOT the case that you'll have to study like an engineer to pass. (etc)
No Comments

Boyer is a great guy and he keeps lectures interesting. Highly recommend taking this class! Material is interesting if you like history. Graded by 2 exams and optional paper only. Exams are straightforward if you prepare well. Review sessions before each exam and comprehensive slides posted. You don't really have to read or attend class.

One of the best professors ILR has to offer. Could not recommend more highly for the advanced econ requirement, especially if math is not your forte, since grade is based on two tests which are entirely written and a paper. Very nice guy who really cares about his students.

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. Lectures and slides contain all the info needed for prelim. Offers helpful study session before exam. Super chill and tells bad jokes to keep lectures interesting. Definitely take his class if you get the opportunity!
lot of reading, lectures are dense with information, his opinions on course material have an edge on them but he makes jokes and is humorous
Posts notes but you also have to read and study, grading criteria is tough, wants specific details on tests, know your stuff

He's a nice guy who'll be helpful if he trusts you're making an effort. He presents the material in a helpful, organized manner without making you work extra to learn it. I think he doesn't always understand the ability of his students, though; you may have to prove your interest or ability to him if he pegs you as less of an achiever than you are.

George Boyer is by far the most engaging professor I've taken at Cornell. Only 2 exams and an optional paper. If you attend lecture and take good notes, you should do fine. He is really funny, too. I always look forward to attending his lectures.
I Love this Guy

The homie Boyer was really funny and got the main idea across in each of his lectures. Super entertaining and a genuinely nice guy. It was easy to get excited about the topic and then the test was straight forward. What else do ya want?

Boyer was by far the best of all the Work, Labor Capital professors. Clear with his material, and a very funny and likable guy. His test is very straight-forward, asks you questions about overall themes and patterns. If you have him for this course, you'll be pleased I'm sure

This class is kinda interesting. Boyer is hilarious! Dont need to do the reading, just take really, really good notes. Tests are fair. The study guide is helpful. I'd recommend this class to anyone needing an advance ILR elective. Only 2 tests and an optional paper.

Great lecturer, relatively easy prelim which had a median of about a B+. If you go to his office hours he lets you know almost exactly what trends/info you will need to study to do well on the exam. Tells terrible jokes in class, but they keep you awake and in focus

Good lecturer but used so many handouts and graphs that showed up on the test that it was really difficult to remember all the countries and trends which was useless and unfair. Either take really good notes or read the book for this class, don't need both. Median is a B for his prelims. Damn near everyone got a B...Givan's paper boosted the avg.

GREAT lecturer, and even his bad jokes keep things interesting.  He makes a habit of explaining why this or that MATTERS, which prevents the material from feeling obscure.  Only complaint:  way too much reading assigned, a lot of which is COMPLETELY unnecessary.

He is simply a fantastic professor! He makes history logical and narrates it in a natural and very entertaining manner. He answers any kind of question with full interest. I have had no formal background in history whatsoever, but I found it no problem to follow his class. Helpful, extremely entertaining and a GREAT professor overall!

Great professor. Lectures are entertaining. Do either all the readings or attend all the lectures. Both are not required. As far as economics classes go, this is one of the best. It's a more historical account, but very interesting. Boyer is not out to get you, he wants you to learn. Take the class!
One of the best I've had at Cornell. Very funny and interesting lecturer - 75 minute lectures fly by.
Lectures are a lot of fun with Boyer.  You definately need to devote some time to studying, but the grading is relatively-fair.
Class is about average for hardness.  There are a lot of readings but if you go to section and partcipate you should be fine.  He makes lectures fun.

Required for ILR, material isn't too interesting.  However, Boyer makes lecture interesting; nice guy who's really funny and good to talk to.  Tests are a bit tricky, and you have to know a lot, but study and it's not bad.  Boyer rocks!
Boyer is awesome!  The tests are a bit hard, but he is an amazing lecturer, and definitely keeps you awake with his humor.
simply the best lecturer I will probably ever have. tests are easy but the grading is harsh. he delivers with such enthusiasm; it's almost like every class is a performance.

The class is extremely fun to go to. I always look forward to attending his class. Professor Boyer is never boring. He's always making these random comments that are soo funny, you can't stop thinking about it even after class.

I've had Professor Boyer for two classes, the introductory ILR140 and "Social Policies in Britain and America". He's extremely easy to get along with and his tests are straight-forward. Sometimes you feel like he's in the classroom to practice c
Though he seems very nice, he doesn't answer questions asked in office hours. He likes to have his ego stroked and loves it when you just agree with him. Interesting material, not the best class.
George Boyer, if your reading this, I LOVE U! :)

It's too bad that all the joy of Labor Econ is frontloaded in Boyer's class. By the time one reaches the absolute hell of 340, the will to live having been sucked out of their soul by Larry Kahn, the genuine genius that is George is a forgotten dream. '03

His lectures are clear and straight-forward- the reading is a lot but he lets you know what to know and explains it all thoroughly. Plus, he is hilarious and one of the most intelligent teachers at Cornell.

An extremely brilliant man who really wants his students to do well in his course.  He is not out to fail students like most teachers are.  He is very funny and tries to make his lectures as non-boring and possible.  Very enjoyable class to take.
No Comments
The class would be more interesting if he only spoke about baseball.
Rather entertaining lectures for the subject he teaches and he wears sweater vests, now that is stylin!
he is an awesome professor, plus you have to take his class if you are in ILR
amazing and funny
An absolutely amazing professor.  Extremely funny and very interesting.
Really clear lectures. Very funny!
the man
This guy is hilarious! Its like learning economics from a stand-up comedian!
He makes the historical events of 145 years ago come alive and uses them to illustrate his ecomonic point.
No Comments
No Comments
One of the best Professor at Cornell!

Canina is perhaps one of the best professors at Cornell! She cares deeply for your understanding of the principles and will take time to go over the material before pre-lims. Speak with her early, let her get to know you and she will help you along. Also very involved in the entrepreneurship community at Cornell. AMAZING PROF!
Professor Canina is great! She cares a lot about her students learning the material. She also wants students to get comfortable speaking up in class.
Tough but direct and cares enormously about her students. I learned more in this class than any other last semster.

Horrible professor. Her class is completely unorganized. You feel like the class content just get thrown at you from no where. There is no slides available, everything is just talked about and written down. Even the readings, she just says to read them once in class, and then would cold call random student and expect you have done everything.

Linda Canina was one of my most memorable professors at Cornell. Her unique sense of humor and lecture style kept me engaged throughout the hour-plus lecture, and I felt I learned a lot from her class. She LOVES to call on students- it kept everyone on their toes and definitely made class more interesting. Would highly recommend this course.

Attendance not mandatory, but GO TO CLASS. Book is not as important as her lecture slides. All the concepts on the test are on the slides. Take notes of her explanations in class. Copy everything she writes in class. Redo the problems. Understand the concepts behind each step. Problems on prelims and final  problems from lecture. I learned a lot.

Pr. Canina's lectures are interesting, and should be treated as a supplement to the book. Tests are usually drawn from the book, but by going to the lecture it is possible to determine on what they are going to focus. She obviously cares about the class and students, sometimes to the point of making  disinterested students care about the class.

Fantastic teacher. Smart, funny, and extremely helpful. Class was challenging, but not impossibly hard. Grading is fair, lectures are interesting, and I've learnt a tremendous amount more about Finance. Would definitely take another class with her. One of my favorite classes this semester.
Very Harsh grader. The lectures were very tedious and not overly helpful. Even the most studious will find success in this class to be challenging. I would avoid.

Really great class. One of my favorites if not most favorite one. Material is interesting and teacher is engaging. Class is mainly comprised of case studies and quizzes, none were easy but she explains the material very well so it's easy to follow. Very open for questions/concerns after class ends. Not an easy A class but highly recommend it.
Although this class is not easy, I definitely learned a lot.  Prof was clear and prepared for every class.  She keeps you alert and thinking about the material by calling on everyone!

This is an advanced level class, and consequently is not easy. However, she is very organized and presents the material in a very logic and comprehensive way, which makes it easy to understand. Case studies used are interesting and supplement her lectures very well. Exams are fairly difficult but manageable. Overall, awesome class & great Professor

If you're looking to take an easy class this is not the class for you. However, if you want to learn finance through a challenging yet rewarding course this may be the class you're looking for. Professor Canina is a wonderful person who cares about her students and will go the extra mile in trying to make you succeed. I highly recommend this course
Assumes prior subject knowledge and doesn't prepare students for exams

This is a great class.  If you have any math experience whatsoever, you shouldn't have a problem doing well in this class... although doing the practice homework problems is pretty essential.  Prof. Canina is funny, helpful, and amazingly kind and will work with you to make sure you understand the material well.

She is a great career advisor and an okay teacher, but this class does have a lot of work. With at least 1-2 things to every other day, there is a lot of time and effort needed to pass. You can get ahead and complete assignments in advance if you can. Lectures are boring, but this class provides a lot of time for personal reflection which was nice

For a 2-credit course, there is an absurd amount of work involved. Written work is uncomfortable, as prof requires you give her an extraordinary amount of personal details. Directions are vague and grading is quite harsh. Many tasks seem juvenial, menial and irrelevant. Coloring is a chore you will become all too familiar with. Huge waste of time.
I couldn't believe the amount of useless work in this class. I left with no understanding of why we did most of the assignments we did. Many assignments were time consuming and involved coloring
Really regret wasting my time with this class. Would have dropped if it wasn't just 7 weeks
Poor excuse for a class. Something that should be enjoyable (exploring careers) was made into a frustrating chore
Her phone rings and disrupts class. Plus we use crayons way too much for a college class

Class has a lot of potential since most people don't know what career they want to pursue. But that doesn't make up for multiple time-consuming assignments due each class and incredibly harsh and vague grading. Gasser truly cares for her students but runs her class very poorly. She's nice one-on-one but the lectures are beyond confusing

Comical how she expects "professionalism" from all of our assignments but then writes instructions that are very unclear and contain typos. Very confusing to actually figure out what she wants--you only figure it out when you get assignments back and she wants you to re-do them which happens for about half the class
Many assignments and very vague instructions. Unfortunate cause the class could have a lot of potential

She gets points for being nice, but that's not enough to make up for the incredibly poor level of instruction. Her cell phone rings several times per class and she loses her train of though in an already pointless lecture. I would have dropped this class if it wasn't only 7 weeks. Would not recommend, take a class that gives graded credit
Not a difficult class, just pointless. Doesn't help me with careers in the slightest. Really should have taken a real graded class
Very poor instruction with disorganized lectures. Too many assignments, none difficult, just pointless and time consuming

Professor Gasser is a very nice lady, but this class is an unreasonable amount of work for two credits pass/fail. The assignments are completely unnecessary and quite frustrating. I cannot understand how she thinks these completely useless assignments would help. You would have to be completely desperate for credits to take this class

Required textbook, at least one assignment due per class, 3 long papers, cannot miss class. Overall, this class had a ridiculous amount of work for a 7 week 2 credit pass/fail. Would not recommend if you already have a heavy course load It took up way too much time that could have been used for my graded classes.

Career Development: Theory & Practice.  Class is best for freshmen & soph. who don't know what they want to do. Not good for students who want to learn the methods of career dev. to help others.  ALOT of assignments, most unnecessary, lectures were all over the place, needs to be taught in a full semester if you're going pack in that much info

She is actually the coolest person on the planet. I want to be Dr. Rayor when I grow up. Beyond that, she's an AMAZING professor. She doesn't assign busy work; everything she expects you to do will help you grow as a student. She expects a high quality of work because she believes her students are capable of it. Cannot recommend enough.

If you're interested in spiders, inverts or entomology take 3150 for the full experience. If you're not too sure, but want to try something new/fill a requirement or have an extra spot and love bio take 2150! Dr. Rayor is brilliant, amazing, hilarious, kind, and the coolest prof ever. My only issue is that I wish she taught more classes at Cornell!

Obviously loves the topic, and was excited about teaching. She wasn't very prepared sometimes, and actually wrote part of the final as we were taking it. Very tough grader and a little intimidating, but in a way that makes you want to perform better to meet her expectations. Expect to be called on in class to answer questions.

Really fun class! You don't need to do any of the readings and she gives you a lecture packet that you can use as a guide for what's on the test. Very low maintenance except for the exams (just a crap-ton of memorization). The point of the class is just to convince you that arachnids are awesome, so the lecture topics are really interesting.

Do NOT get the wrong idea from the #s!  This is an awesome course, but if if youre not an entomologist (I wasnt and Im still not) it'll take some getting used to (I did really well on a prelim and got a job in her lab). Dr. Rayor deeply interested in her work and wants you to get interested too.  If you need help, never be afraid to ask, its there.

Great teachers inspire their students. I have been inspired. The course couldn't be more interesting, comprehensive, and unique. She enjoys the topic matter and makes each of her students enjoy it just as much. I will now continue to study Entomology throughout my Cornell Career. Thank you Dr. Rayor.

The class is very interesting. She is very enthusiastic about spiders, and this comes across in her lectures. She has the tendency to be a bit unkind sometimes though. I wholly recommend entom 215. I loved it.
She is pretty easy. She is a nice person but your grade is partially dependent whether she likes you or not.

Dr. Rayor is one of the top people in her field in the nation, and the class is excellent if you're into spiders. Even if you're not, it's still quite fascinating stuff. You learn a lot with her, though there is a lot of memorization here. The TA's are also very helpful.

Good class, interesting subject matter, enthusiastic TAs. Rayor may be up there in her field, but she's not the best teacher. Not to say that her lectures were boring -- quite the opposite. I just thought she was full-of-it. I found myself rolling my eyes when she angrily corrected me on her title: "Doctor," not "Professor."

Dr. Rayor went out of her way to interact with students and give feedback, but definitely wasn't as organized or as knowledgable as she should've been (or as she was for Spider Bio). Rayor was wonderful, very enthusiastic about teaching

I LOVE BRETT HE'S THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER <3

Professor Baptist is very knowledgeable and kind to his students. Would definitely recommend, however be prepared for tough grading.
