Amazing professor, very clear, informative, and engaging. Every lecture is well presented. I wouldn't pass up an opportunity to take a class with him. I've learned so much.

Very into his own research work, but is also too pompous in that regard. The grading is too harsh and he does not really understand East Asian labor at all. He thinks he's rather superior to his students and the people he studies

Chinese labor.  Very informed guy that has done research in China about workers and speaks the language too.  Need to do readings and had 3 quizzes with a final research paper. Class attendance is required (signin sheet) and participate and ask THOUGHTFUL question.  I think he has a good BS meter, and it might hurt you.  Very knowledgeable!

One of my favorite professor! He is so helpful with my class, and I was so impressed by his way of solving problems. Other students and I always ask him problems right after the class, and he always stays 20 minutes or 30 minutes later to answer our problems. His homework is tough, but his tests is not hard at all.

Wonderful professor. Occasionally lectures seem off topic, but if you go the extra mile to understand them you get the chance to see something really beautiful. Not so good at arithmetic (what kind of self-respecting mathematician is?), but gives fantastic geometric views of the material. He's also quite friendly! Best of  luck at IC Dr. Marshall!

The class is super hard, and requires a lot of work, but Prof. Marshall's lectures are very clear. He's also pretty funny. I just wish they hadn't been 8am lectures, because if you miss class, the course will get much harder than it needs to be and work will most definitely pile up.

Marshall clearly cares and as such prepares pretty good lectures, especially for a Math professor. Lecturers for the same class didn't feel as adequate at explaining ideas. Marshall is willing to help and is very approachable.

I was really grateful for this class and am glad I found out about Roger. I was so busy this last sem and his class allowed me to get so much done! There really are no expectations. Just take it and get your A. The benefit for you is extra breathing room in your schedule to focus on actual subjects and a free Gpa boost. Works for me!
This class saved me. Roger is a blessing. I would've never graduated without his class. It allowed me to accomplish so much.
Roger is the perfect professor. He is selfless and only wants to educate you. He is so so helpful!!

Roger is my favorite professor because of the way he engages me in the classroom and the way he facilitates a safe space for discussion. He makes me feel like I'm doing well and improving. His feedback on my essays is generous and helpful. The poetry he assigns is fantastic and rich. I only wish he assigned a little more reading.

Amazing! I loved his style of teaching. He allows students to really develop their ideas about the content through open discussion. 

We even met his dog! and discussed our book outside on the grass. What I loved most was the chosen material. I found myself laughing and weirded out sometimes but it was difficult to put the material down.

Professor Gilbert is clear with instructions and deadlines. The assignments required a good amount of reading, but he does not ask for too much from students and gives thorough and helpful feedback. The reading assignments were pretty interesting but could have been a bit more varied regarding themes. Easy to reach and quick to respond.

Very boring and probably not the best value. The prof added little the conversation, and most of the students weren't taking it seriously. It reminded me of my high school study hall. E-Z way to get credit if you're just looking to zone out, get other hw done, or hide in the bathroom.

He's very similar to Tom Hill. You won't learn anything at all, and you can count on getting an A without doing any reading, ever participating, or even attending class. Intellectually, his class is terrible. If you're just looking for credit, however, it's fine. He's too anxious to talk back to or correct students. He mostly just keeps quiet

Professor Gilbert is great. You can tell how much he loves what he studies and he gets so excited teaching it. He assigns a lot of readings but I thought they were all interesting at least. Definitely graded the papers harder than I expected but gave enough feedback to be constructive.
Not the most animated, but still clear and fair. I have much more appreciation for poetry now that I have the patience to understand it. I've even tried writing my own...
Overall a good teacher, especially considering all the trouble I made him put up with last semester, being the wild/rowdy freshmen of the bunch.
I love his sweaters.  And what can I say--he is hot, hot, HOT.
belittles poets by finding them "cute"or "funny"; seems unprepared for class and claims not to understand john berryman as if that is berryman's fault
Easy to get into contact with. Such an interesting and intellectual guy. You know you're in the presence of a great person and scholar.
He's incredibly talented.

He's very non-elitist (I'm not classically-trained) and prioritizes accessibility, is very empathetic and cares for individuals, and is knowledgeable enough to make accessible obscure schemas and 18th-century music terms. he's also interesting, buoyant, and injects life into what is otherwise distant. Solid human being great lecturer

This gentle man is a master of British humor, a fan of Mozart, and just a good pianist. His vocabulary is astounding. Very approachable and respects your input. Never condescending at all. He makes learning about classical schemas much less painful. Oh, and he teaches well too. I honestly can't ask for more.
GREAT PROFESSOR! He was really helpful - all you need to do is hit him up with an email and he's there to help you.
Awesome British accent! He makes class really fun and engaging and always very approachable and nice to students. Definitely one of the best Cornell professors.

Awesome professor, witty and engaging. He is one of those extremely intellectual people that sometimes use words no one uses in conversation, but he comes across as friendly, not egotistical. Material for this class can be boring at times, but his always makes it seem interesting and relevant.  Take a class with this guy if at all possible.

Professor Loring was a really good lecturer and the material he went over in class matched up nicely with the topics on exams. The workload was manageable, and although the material was hard, he taught well. He was really helpful during office hours and I enjoyed this class.

Best organized professor I've ever had. He explained things clearly and excelled especially at teaching one-on-one in office hours with a socratic method. The content can sometimes be dry. Take good notes during class, try hard on the problem sets (go to office hours if you need!), and you'll ace the tests. Very reasonable course.

A really amazing course. Loring was very organized and receptive. He was one of the best professors I have ever had. Quantum mechanics is difficult and mind-blowing (the perfect combination, truly!). Take advantage of all of the extra help available.

He makes the class extremely difficult. While his lectures are interesting and he is clearly a very smart guy, his homework questions come out of nowhere and it is impossible to do the homework without spending countless hours in office hours. The TAs are willing to help, but it takes forever to even get help because there are so many people in OH.
One of the best classes I've ever taken, and it wasn't even very useful for my major

Class is really hard, but he prepares you well. Homeworks often take upwards of 5 hours bare minimum. Speaking from experience, prelims are sort of similar year to year so you can get some insight from previous prelims, but the best way is definitely to do a lot of practice problems.

Loring goes through the material so clearly and knows his stuff. Material is insanely hard that you will get lost but the homework tries to reinforce the key points though it will take you hours (or days). Tests are challenging but fair and tests concept, almost zero memorization.
Very organized and clear. Kept the focus on the important stuff and elucidated it using excellent HW questions. Cannot ask more from an instructor.

Professor Loring is an incredible communicator. Lectures were the best I've had so far. Even though the class was very difficult and tests very hard, there was rarely anything unreasonable or pointless memorization.    It was a true blessing that he taught the course. I'd love to  have Loring for every Chem class

He knows his material like the back of his hand, AND he knows how to teach with a clarity and precision that not many professors can achieve. He's very easy to get along with and extremely helpful during office hours. He's definitely someone you should get to know if you're a ChemE or Chem major.
Professor Loring is awesome. He knows how to make even the most complicated topics at least palatable and interesting. He's one of the smartest professors I've had. You're lucky if you have him.
clear but boring

He's boring in lecture. Once I asked him a question after class, but he'd rather us ask these to our recitation T.A. Do HW problems by yourself (without copying someone else's). Tests were somewhat hard. Read book. Practice as many HW problems as you can.
great professor.  really nice, really good at what he does.

Professor Loring is such a short and adorable old man. I LOVED his lectures. I mean, I didn't even like chemistry that much, but his lectures were too intriguing. His tests were fair too. I also enjoyed how he made side chemistry jokes.. and no one laughed (except my chuckle of course, that no one heard), but those were funny.
Gives very fluid lectures that are well-organized and relatively clear.  Tests are certainly challenging, but they're not unfairly difficult.

His half of the semester was infinitely easier than Crane's , and he was a clear and informative lecturer. But if you ever went to office hours, you would want to punch the guy because he is one of those people who flaunts how much smarter he is than you. Also he never really answers your questions because then he might be "giving away the answer."
Clear Lecturer, nothing unexpected.  go to class and know everything he writes on the board.  Far less difficult than other premed classes
Very clear and organized in his lectures. Exams are fair and accurately reflect the problem sets and old exams. Much better than Crane

Presents the material clearly & methodically (unlike Crane), though i could just read it in the textbook. like someone else said, if you can do the p.sets on your own, you're golden for the exams. Nothing he does makes/breaks you in the class.

CHEM 207 is really not as difficult as most people/pre-meds make it out to be.  Loring is a very good professor and very clear on what you need to know.  People have said he's mean to them when they ask questions, yet I'd be mean too if someone handed me a problem set without any writing on it for help.  If you make an effort, he'll help you a lot.
He's very clear, he tells you what to expect for the prelims

Good teacher.  Wrote and spoke clearly, unlike Crane.  The exams aren't ridiculous, so if you do the problem sets and readings you'll be fine.  Not a bad class, but I'm just not too fond of chem in general.
Not a horrible class but not one that I would want to take again.
Although very informative, his lectures were boring. He didn't seem to cover the material well enough to just learn from them. Do the readings ahead of time!
No Comments

I learned so much from Dr. B this past semester and would recommend this class to anyone interested in the US Health Care System.  TA's wrote Takenote, as well as the quizes, midterm and final, and graded all assignments.  Invest in Takenote, forget the book (unless you want more depth), and you should do just fine.  Overall, great class!

Class was easy to pass, but hard to attend.  Prof. Battistella lectures with no apparent plan or coherent thought.  Quizzes are easy if you do the supplemental reading, but the textbook is incredibly boring.

Professor Batistella knows so much about the US health care structure today.  It's amazing that any one person can be so up to date with the material.  He's so friendly.  But his lectures are a little all over the place.  Questions about exams and gradings should go to the TAs since they wrote and graded all the exams.
No Comments

Material is interesting. Prof is a bit flaky. His lecture notes are all over the place. TakeNote saved me. TAs grade everything. Prof is always willing to help if you approach him or just sit and have a discussion. Cool guy.

Roger is one of the best teachers I've had. A real visionary in the field & completely on top of all emerging trends. No one knows the healthcare industry better than Dr. Batistella. Insofar as his class, if you like the McNeil Report then you'll do fine in his class.

Prof. B really knows his stuff. His material is always up to date so you learn all the relevant things about today's health care system. If you pay attention in class, the quizzes/exams are a breeze. The subject matter is always interesting and he MAKES it interesting.
awesome prof! :D

Super nice and caring prof, put in the work and show that you care and the prof will be super nice and helpful. Accessible outside of class & loves meeting with students to talk out ideas. A LOT of work and reading, the content is interesting but the workload is extreme for a 3cred course (many indicated this in eval's so workload may be decreased)

Took this class for a distribution requirement for Arts & Sciences. Would never recommend this professor to anyone. My participation grade was completely inaccurate and we were told final grades were "non-negotiable." Instructor made me feel extremely uncomfortable when discussing grades or anything regarding this class.

Ashley is the best professor I’ve had at Cornell. She’s very relaxed and class is a nice atmosphere and the time passes quickly. She also encouraged me and made me feel confident in my writing for the first time whereas teachers in high school would only criticize.

Ashley is the best teacher Ive had at Cornell. Ill never look at reading the same way after taking her class. She starts from ground zero on how to analyze stories and then shows you how to use the various narrative elements as a springboard to write your own story. The only class this semester I actually enjoyed attending.

Its early on in the semester but every class has been awesome. Im excited for the rest of the course. She breaks down the readings in a way that will sort of blow your mind. Shes also super hot and funny so that doesnt hurt either.

I absolutely loved coming to this class. Ashley is so caring and so funny. She makes you look at reading in a whole new way. She also teaches you actual strategies to get better at writing. The course isnt demanding per se but she makes you want to work hard and give her your best. I wish I could take it again!

Ive learned so much from this class. Ive liked reading and writing at a young age but at high school, English classes have been taught in a way that discourages that. Hand is caring and passionate about writing. Her class is a breath of fresh air. You will learn to become a much better writer in this class.

Ashley is one of the most caring profs at Cornell. Her prompts are broad, so you're really able to run with the assignments and do what you want with them to make it your best work. You'll get out of this class as much as you put into it. Ashley made me view literature in an entirely new and exciting way, and I'll forever have this class to thank.

Hands down the best teacher I've had at Cornell. You're lucky if you get into her section -- the class is pretty easy, but it's memorable and makes you look at the world differently. Assignments are pretty open-ended. Lots of freedom to do what you want!

She is so unbelievably kind, you can tell she actually cares about you as a person. I do find myself spending a lot of time on the assignments. The instructions can be sort of complex but she's a forgiving grader as long as you put in effort. It does take a while to get your papers back, but she gives great comments and is really encouraging.
She's charismatic and kind and keeps class interesting. Favorite prof so far.

This definitely should have been a four-credit class. Professor Rich assigned so much reading and work for a class about sociology. I did really enjoy a lot of the content but the workload was insane. Tests were also really difficult to study for.

Good professor! Very passionate, knowledgable, and the structure of the content was very good and flowed smoothly. Assignments were easy, and the exams were fair in my opinion. The grade structure was VERY forgiving in my opinion. You still need to study and put in some effort, but otherwise easy class!

Social Problems in the US with Prof Rich was definitely a lot harder than in years past, but he's a very fair and straightforward guy. I also think the weightage of homework and attendance vs prelims+finals is very lenient, so as long as you show up and pay attention you should be in a decent spot. Certain exam questions are very tricky - watch out

Though Professor Rich is a nice person, the class is extremely arbitrary. basically, he presents us with arguments from things he's read and we have to memorize like every detail of each reading and then he expects us to be able to formulate arguments and such on the exam without ever doing an instance of practice.

Professor Rich is one of the most caring professors I have ever interfaced with! As long as you make an effort to pay attention in lectures, the problem sets are pretty straightforward. Even if you don't, he's always willing to go over things in office hours and will work with you to make sure you fully understand each concept you ask him about.

Easy class as long as you put the work in. Really nice guy. Explains everything in great detail and is always ready to take questions. Exams are also online, easy, and open resource. Homework redo's on incorrect questions are allowed for partial credit redemption.

I took 2 of his courses. You do not need to attend the actual classes, but for stat stay on top of homework very easy to fall behind. For soc problems review powerpoints and class notes. some stuff on tests comes from little things said in class. there are no A+ but easy A for sure. for essay get extensions if you need they will help.
Covers lots of interesting topics and is very engaging in lectures. Not hard if you do the readings and pay attention. However, there are alot of readings! Overall nice professor though.

Solid professor. Lectures are generally engaging, though sometimes they overlap too much with the assigned reading. Encourages class participation by giving you things to talk about with the person next to you. Very knowledgeable about what he's teaching. A fair amount of readings, but not too bad.

Prof Rich is very fair and caring. I missed the announcement for when a postponed prelim would be moved to so I basically showed up to class, not knowing it was prelim day. Didn't have my cheat sheet or calculator and showed up late but prof let me print my sheet out and use my phone as a calculator and made sure I was okay and gave me extra time.

Professor Rich is seriously the best Professor I have had at Cornell! His Social Problems in the US course is vital for any student at Cornell. He is a very lenient and understanding professor who encourages collaboration and holds reasonable standards for his students. He actually cares about the struggles his students face outside of class.
Somehow made an intro to sociology class insanely difficult. This was harder than my physics course. Tons of work to do.
Lots of homework and readings. Tests are nothing like the homeworks. Be ready to study hard or you won't do well
If you do the readings and show up to class, you will get an A. I did not study for any of the tests, and I did not spend more than an hour on any of the papers, and I got an A+

So unorganized. I had him for PAM statistics and him and his head TA seemed to not know the material. Lectures were ineffective, homeworks were graded extremely inconsistently, and study materials for the test were full of errors and missing answers. I've heard good things about him in other classes, but PAM statistics was terribly run.

There was a lot of reading required each class that he gives questions on every day. That being said, hes very lenient in grading projects, and the tests are very easy if youve paid even the slightest bit of attention in lecture. I learned a lot of really interesting content, and it was my favorite class of the semester.

I loved Professor Rich! The course definitely felt more like a 4 credit rather than 3 credit class due to the amount of reading and work we did, but it was definitely all manageable. He chose a few books for us to read that were genuinely interesting and engaging. There are tons of opportunities for extra credit, and the prelims aren't bad at all

Professor Rich was an amazing lecturer. The books that he assigned were interesting to read and thoroughly discussed in class. I learned more in this class than I have learned in any other class at Cornell. Also, he provides so many opportunities for extra credit making it easy to do well. HIGHLY recommend taking a class with him.
Extremely clear explanation, Willing to help students
Vale is crystal clear, funny and makes analysis as good as it can be.
Extremely helpful, work hard
Was very helpful in and out of class. Great professor!

The perfect straight man for any of your jokes, try it out with him.  If your comment is stupid enough though, he'll just ignore you.  If you are a class clown, be sure to act up in his class.  Oh yeah, good professor, knows his math.
No Comments

Lectures are engaging and funny. 3 reading reflections (1 every 4-5 weeks), two exams. Discussions were chill. There is a lot of reading (most is skippable if you skim before discussion). its important to go to lecture and take good notes because the slides are outlines. explanation/essay based exams. focus on understanding concepts over details.

Stedman is a great professor. His fun demeanor and obvious passion for environmental studies and social sciences makes you want to learn and retain what you learn in class. He messed up the midterm a bit, but admitted his mistake, curved it, and gave us a different (easier) test type for the final. That kind of self-reflection makes a good teacher.

This class was a good intro to the more theoretical side to E&S. Lectures were engaging except for guests who came in and seemed to detract from the other aspects of the class. Discussion sections were really fun and made some great friends in them. First prelim was silly but changed the format to an in-class essay for the final which was good.

Stedman is a great teacher, his class is very easy with 3 quizzes that are so easy. Then a final paper that is 1500 words taking about a future problem, so you make it all up. He is very chill and really cares about what he teaches. He doesn't want to fail students and just wants you to enjoy the class and hopefully learn something from him.
I really enjoyed learning everything in this class and really felt like professor Stedman genuinely cared that we were doing ok. Especially with coronavirus!

Loved Professor Stedman! The topics in the class are very relevant and important as human population grows and evolves. Took the class during corona, and this was one of my most accommodating courses. Overall positive experience!

Incredibly dull lectures. Goes off on tangents, no clear point or outline for the discussion. Weekly reading of about 150+ pages and weekly 1 page papers, due at 9am Saturday. In-class discussion was also very dull, he would respond to one student for 10+ minutes without allowing for engagement. Very long research paper, graded harshly 50% of grade

prof is really old and lectures are really slow (he will remark on every comment someone makes for ten minutes each.) my class was full of kids who sucked up to him, which I found really annoying personally. the class itself is fine but def one of my least favorite gov classes that I've taken at Cornell.

Amazing professor who teaches without bias, cares about students, and rewards effort. Discussion-based seminar which he guides without being overbearing, and encourages you to think about the material critically. 100pg assigned a week, which is v. reasonable for the class level. Grade: 50% weekly 1pg reading reactions and 50% 20pg paper. Median: A

Really loved this class. Homework was just reading around 30-40 pages of a novel and then writing a few sentences on what parts of it we'd include in our ideal world. No intermediary papers. Final paper is 15 pages describing your perfect society. Graded very generously, mostly on effort. Highly recommend it.  Median was an A- for the course.

Bensel is great.  It took me almost the entire FWS session to figure our where his political affiliation was because he's so good at arguing all sides... something I haven't seen in enough professors.  Take one of his classes, he's amazing.

I took my FWS with Bensel, and it was a lot of fun. The course discussed many interesting topics about the formation of a society, and he facilitated great conversations. If you have a chance, I recommend taking Utopia as your FWS.

Bensel is great! I took Conservative thought with him and it was so interesting. He is the sort of professor who tries to elevate the level of discourse and asks students to really question themselves and those around them. I highly recommend this course! Also--he grades really fairly. If you do the work he'll give you a good grade.

Professor Bensel is so so amazing! I learned so much in his senior seminar American Conservative Thought. It just makes you a smarter person. He is really helpful and easy in that if he thinks the course is going well as a whole he will give everyone a good grade. He just wants everyone to learn and be thoughtful. TAKE A COURSE WITH HIM!
a gem of a prof

Easily the best, nicest, and most helpful Professor I have had at Cornell.  Will literally sit down with students for hours to discuss anything from exams to future life plans.  Lectures are good, though he is soft-spoken and occasionally difficult to hear.  Wouldn't have missed his class for the world.  Take him before he retires!

Great Professor! Court, Crime, & Constitution was my favorite History course hands down & Prof. Polenberg was an amazing instructor he's very knowable in the law field & knows the facts of almost every Supreme Court case. The course is discussion based and only required 2 papers so besides reading the course isn't too demanding. Polenberg=Awesome
I didn't do too well in his class but I still think he is an excellent professor who cares about his students learning.
He's AMAZING! Extremely interesting, easy to understand, helpful, and flexible. He even invited our whole class to have dinner at his house! love him!!

wow arguably one of the best professors at cornell, he is dedicated to ensuring that his students both understand the material and succeed in general. he is remarkably knowledgable and can just get up and talk about subject material with no notes. one of the kindest, sweetest professors at cornell, and truly a mentor to me.

Great professor! He'll be retiring soon so take something from him before he goes! Be careful w/ essays (since he's a grammar freak)... Also, try to be on his good side or else you might see his bad side...

Polenberg is a very nice person, relatively easygoing, helpful, and interested in students doing well.  He encourages participation, reads many drafts of papers, and brings cookies and cider to class.  If you can, take a relaxing course with him before he retires.
Great lecturer, nice guy, very interesting course.  Definetly presents a left-wing bias though.  Acceptably balanced by readings.
Absolutely the man.  Take any of his classes - he is fair, funny, and knows everything.  You'll be happy you took a class with him.
So cute and sweet!  This was one of the most interesting classes because he lived through it at Cornell - very earnest and always has interesting anecdotes.
I had him for both a writing seminar and Constitutional history. He's a really nice guy, a pretty easy grader and very laid back. His lectures are decent, but skippable.
Excellent lectures.  Get him before he retires.
awesome guy. likes going on and on but his stories are interesting. very very knowledgeable and very laid back. good seminar professor
Great professor, knowledgeable, interesting, noticeably intelligent and kind guy. Very fair class.

A really nice guy, he puts time into class and you can tell he likes to the subject material.  However, he didn't expect much of the students, leaving lots of "discussions" silent when no one had read the material, and for a writing seminar, there was little focus on the process of writing.

I may have the course # wrong, but the course title was Recent U.S. History. He is entitled to his opinions, but much of the lecture sounded to me like anti-US propaganda. I got an A by skipping the lectures and going to discussion section.
Relied too much on TAs and then would tell students he thought they were incompetent.  You buy a lot of books that don't matter at all.
really good, smooth lecturer; sometimes pushes his own opinions a bit too much, but overall a really good prof and course

Everything already mentioned and more. He'll stop class for an anecdote about his mother if it's related to the class and still make it interesting and very much worthwhile. Take anything with him while you still have the chance!
a kind professor who has wonderful lectures. tells stories well and is one of the few professors who asks for questions from students in class.
The best professor I have ever had.  Brilliant, compassionate, great educator, great man.
No Comments
Great storyteller and teaches an exciting course. Dont share essays; hell find you and his bad side is ugly. Great course though.
one of the kindest faculty members I've known, & a great storyteller

Prof. Pollenberg is committed to educating undergrads; he takes a personal interest in his students. Although he enjoyes educating and enlightening his students, he is also willing to step back and let student discussion take its course.
No Comments
He is a nice guy, but the material is incomprehensible, and he assumes you have a ton of background knowledge that isn't explicitly required by the prerequisite classes.

He knows what he's talking about, but he has no idea how to talk about it. Lectures were monotonous repetitions of the textbook which, though generally legible, at times became indecypherable. One definition was a paragraph-long sentence which I gave up trying to interpret. Cool and easy material, acceptable book, nice guy, poor teacher.
He's probably the best guy in his field. I learned so much from his class.
No Comments
A bit unclear at times though in general he is great
I took Qualitative Methods with Richard last semester. He is a brilliant professor. Definitely take his classes, you will learn!

Loved it! Lectures were always super clear and the tests and problem sets correlated strongly. Psets got tougher as the semester went on, but group work is a great solution. If you read the textbook and take good notes on the lectures, you will do very well in this class. Very straightforward, knowledgeable, and responsive professor!

Astro 2212 with Nicholson convinced me I wanted to major in Astronomy. The guy's really been around the block in the field of Astronomy and often brought in guest lecturers who are experts on the topic, and his lectures were great. Grade consisted of 5 psets, the midterm, the final and a presentation on a subject of your choice in the Solar System.

Nice guy. Optional textbook and no reading. Five problem sets made up most of the grade: not hard but takes time to think about the problems, mostly high-school level math with some calc 1. One midterm and canceled the final; a 5-10 paged paper at the end of the course. Cool class; might be too much work if you don't think astronomy is interesting.

This was by far one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. My only critique is that the tests were HARD. If you have a photographic memory you will do amazing on them because you need to memorize all the slides word for word. Homeworks were very easy but tests were very difficult.

Must-take class for anyone interested in healthcare!!! Very informative class and has a nice curve which helps since tests can be tricky. It's also not very much work if you don't do the readings (only one or two true or false questions per test about them).

Professor Nicholson is a pretty decent prof but lacks some empathy for students' situations. The exams are harshly graded, but you can submit regards. Overall, pretty decent class if you show up to lecture and do the readings, but small details matter.

Amazing professor, tests could be hard but understanding the lecture material and demonstrating that knowledge gets you a good grade. Was super close to getting an A but final messed me up. Anyways though prof is really caring and always willing to meet outside class! Highly recommend

Prof. Nicholson is extremely knowledgable and I found it easy to get questions answered in office hours, assuming there weren't too many other students there. Tests are graded very harshly, however, and even if you have a suitable answer, you may not get credit because you don't use the correct stats or you may not have the correct wording.
Amazing lecturer and a great class overall. Prelims are quite tough though.

TAKE THIS COURSE! I don't know how he does it, but Dr. Nicholson somehow condenses the material in a way that makes this Byzantine system understandable. If you go to class, pay attention, and think critically, you'll come out with more than a good grade; you'll come out with lessons you'll take with you for years to come. Best professor ever.
Really nice and engaging lecturer, but the prelims are pretty tough. Otherwise, the homework assignments were relatively easy and you can tell Sean really cares about his students!

Incredible lecturer, easily one of my favorite classes I've taken at Cornell. Class is very lecture heavy, you basically cannot miss one or else you will miss a lot of important info. You have to WORK for tests but they're fairly graded. Rewarding class.

Solid professor. Well-versed in his field, & keeps contact even after semester is over. Curves final grade, not individual prelims. Generous on point-back system, and always wants to get to know his students more. Would definitely take him again.

Dr. Nicholson is a great guy and all, the content of the class is super interesting, but hes just a really bad lecturer. All he does it just ramble on and on during class. Prelims are really strictly graded, you have to hit the keywords in the answer key and literally pull straight from the lecture slides to get full credit.

One of the BEST lecturers I have ever met at Cornell. The content is super interesting and understandable. Tests are open-book and mainly based on lecture slides. Sean is great at explaining things so don't worry if you are confused about anything anytime. Course design is related to current events and very inspirational. 100% recommend!

One of the best classes I've taken at Cornell. Professor Nicholson is not only an excellent, engaging lecturer, but he's also just an amazing person. He was extremely accommodating during Covid/online learning, and made sure we all had the resources the succeed in the class. Assignments were easy and prelims were primarily memorization-based.

One of the best classes Ive taken so far. Exams are memorization heavy, but online it was open note which made them very easy and straightforward. Homework assignments were easy and took little time. Prof Nicholson is super caring and answered many questions despite a huge class. Also got us cinnamon rolls and brought his dogs to office hours!
He is the best prof I have ever met at Cornell. He is chill and gives really good lectures. He really understands his students. You will learn a lot from him seriously. He knows what he's doing.

Such a good professor. Made us cinnamon rolls, includes funny clips during lecture that reinforce points but also are a break up the lectures really well, very understanding with deadlines and timing, willing to adapt the course to covid circumstances, so many good things to say

Prof. Nicholson is a really great guy, very knowledgable, and a fantastic lecturer. The content he teaches is interesting for anyone interested in healthcare. I hear a lot of people say this is an easy class. Don't be fooled, exams can be tricky and the class is curved because of it. You will need to put in some work to do well.

Professor Nicholson is a great lecturer. Everything you need to know is on the slides if you miss anything that he says, because he does go through the material pretty quickly. He includes funny videos from time to time in class that make the class more interesting. He truly wishes to connect with students, which I really like.

Hands down, an amazing professor. His tests can be a little overly specific at times, but they are easy to study for - nothing out of left field - and his teaching style is engaging. He is a professor that is truly excited about what he teaches and you can feel that when he speaks.

Biggest lecture I've ever taken at Cornell, yet Nicholson still made every class engaging, relevant, and interesting. Powerpoints posted online contain all the necessary information, but I went to class anyway because he was that good of a lecturer. Stay on top of lectures and memorize everything for the tests (including graphs) and you'll get an A

Absolutely amazing class. Favorite class of my entire life's academic career. He knows his stuff (he's the director of the MHA program!) and this class actually made me want a career in health admin/policy. It's fun, invigorating, and inspiring. He also takes students to Banfi because he's just a cool, normal dude like that!

Very respected and very good lecturer. Disperses fun yet very relevant videos in his lectures that keep them interesting. But he also basically reads off his slides, and he posts them online, so no need to go. Tests are fairly hard, but the class is curved crazily nicely, so not difficult at all. The 3 assignments are easy 100s as well.

Prof. Nicholson is a great lecturer. He can get side-tracked sometimes, but everything he says always ends up relating back to the material. The exams are almost entirely based off the slides, which is good because the slides are well-organized. He knows what he's talking about and takes time to answer individual questions despite the huge class.

Most people would say this class was "easy," but, for me, I didn't do so well on the exams. You learn A LOT about the U.S. healthcare system overall and little things no one ever knows. Prof. Nicholson shows HILARIOUS videos in class and he is a good lecturer. Would I recommend this class: UM, YES!

Nicholson is the best professor I have ever had. He truly cares about the students and is a brilliant economist. The class is fairly easy, with only three fairly straightforward assignments and three prelims that are very fair in grading. I looked forward to going to class--he makes the dry material very interesting.

Very interesting lectures, unbiased analyses of current events. Easy homework assignments and tests, however TA grading of these can fall short sometimes but Professor Nicholson is very reasonable if you take the time to talk to him.

Everything you need to know are on the slides. The key to doing well in this class is 1) study objectives that he lists in every PPT 2) remember trends 3) memorize ratios. I think his prelims are getting trickier. I took another class of his, and they were straightforward. Questions more thought-provoking now. Write down what he wants to see.

Nicholson is one of the best professors at Cornell. SO precise and clear. Definitely go to lectures. You don't need the books, you don't need to read any of the articles at all. You have 3 Assignments all year, not too bad. And the prelims are very similar to past ones! He's great in office hours too.

Took in the Fall of 2013. He is absolutely fantastic, delivers lecture material in a very clear manner and really wants to get to know students!  The prelims could be a little tricky but overall not too hard of a class. Definitely recommend because this class was one of my favorite classes at Cornell!

Overall the class is very arbitrary, especially when 60% of your grade is based on what decides to give you on prelims and your "class participation" . Overall he is a very tough grader with the average in our class being a B. You come in thinking he's a nice guy but there are easier classes to take for your concentration with a higher mean

Made a very challenging subject, usually taught at graduate level, very digestable to this undergrad. He supports interaction during lecture to clarify key concepts and gives an incredible amount of helpful feedback to every student on weekly assignments and exams. One of the most professional, gracious, and capable professors at this school.

One of the most interesting classes Ive taken at Cornell. It is essential that you thoroughly do all reading homework because she cold calls students in class. This can be stressful at first but is honestly not a huge deal. I honestly never felt bored, and as long as you show up to every class (attendance is huge) and take good notes you'll do well

Really an amazing class!! Prof. Hans is an accredited expert on Juries and brings a lot of her interesting research into class. However, the assignments were graded a bit tough by the TAs. Also, they did law school style cold calls, so be prepared!

Professor Bambha taught my favorite class of my freshman fall semester! Her FWS was fun and engaging by having the actual interests of the students being the main focus of the essays. The class in total was only 4 essays with a final project. Topics included reviewing popular media articles on play and reviewing toys!

Valerie's FWS class was by far my favorite class of my fall semester of freshman year! You can tell that she's very passionate about how children learn through play, and she makes the lessons super engaging and fun! The papers assigned were so fun to write about, that it didn't even feel like mandatory assignments. Totally recommend this FWS!

She assigns 3+ journal papers with associated pre-recorded lectures that can be 1-2 hours long each every week. The in-person class is boring and isn't helpful for the exams. Your course grade is 100% exams. The content and exam questions are difficult. There is nothing to help you prepare for them. The class average was a B+. Would not recommend.

This professor does not really teach. She assigns you pre-recorded lecture videos to watch outside of class, and a fair amount of scientific articles to read as well. During the scheduled class time, you just discuss the readings with your classmates. Testing unfair because a curve is necessary, but she allows people to take it at home unmonitored.

A truly great English Prof. at Cornell. Super approachable and with absolutely no ego or intellectual snobbery, which is rare with older white male English profs. Taking Decadence from his is truly a privilege considering it's what he specializes in. I'd recommend this course to all Cornellians perhaps as the most ingenious English class here.

Prof. Hanson's is the one class you must take on the Victorian period. He lets out all the gas and shows you why the 19th century is not only stuffy 'n boring but sometimes cool, even spicy. Prof. Hanson will teach you why the Victorian period still matters. He will show you that the 19th century can be for you even if you thought it wasn't before.
Prof. Hanson taught me why Dorian Gray matters, and he taught me how to understand Oscar Wilde. He is such a talented teacher!

The literature assigned in decadence did not disappoint me. Prof. Hanson is very suave, has great insights and is very approachable.  He facilitates a safe space for discussion of taboo subjects and assigns some raunchy and exciting texts.  If you like Edgar Allan Poe and that kind of Gothic aesthetic, you can't miss out on this class.

Hanson nefariously picks apart essays with hypercritical comments. His interpretation of the material trumps all, and he will let you know you are reading something slightly wrong. He has shown nude material in class in an immature way multiple times, including when we played spot the phallic element in Beardsleys' drawings. Made me uncomfortable

Professor Hanson is fantastic. If you're looking for a two-credit course to take that is easy, Oscar Wilde is the one. Very flexible on deadlines, easy to do well without completing the readings, or watching the asynchronous lectures. Definitely a must take!

Fundamentally careless, redundant, and painfully desperate to be Foucauldian. He doesn't seem to know or care at all about what the difference between Decadence and Aestheticism is. He seems to have never grown out of the bad habit of trying to assimilate the authors one admires. Be yourself! And stop playing long videos in class!

He has an ego but his teaching is mediocre at best. He may be a first-rate intellectual, but his contemptuous indolence is tiresome. I'm not sure if it's arrogance or just a general sense of ennui, but there's something irritating about him. That he holds ONE office hour/week and neglects to put his email on the syllabus tells u all u need to know
His lectures are the most poetic ones I've taken at Cornell. He is nice and caring and very responsive with questions and emails.

The best lectures I've ever had. ellis absolutely knows his field and can always articulate the matters very fluently and elegantly in the lecture. He gives very detailed feedback and might be a bit picky on the papers, which you probably won't get from other professors, but that is extremely helpful. also VERY willing to help.

Ellis is a talented and engaging speaker. Material was always a joy to read and I looked forward to his discussions. As for grading, he makes you work for it. He can be intimidating at times, but he's mostly friendly, witty, and helpful. Did I mention he is hot as hell??????

Hanson's lectures are the most poetic and fluid I have witnessed so far. Don't take this class if you aren't comfortable with various interpretations of art-- they may seem off, but Ellis always has his reasons. I always looked forward to going to lecture in the evenings and reading the material was enjoyable.

If you are interested in Oscar Wilde or Baudelaire then Decadence is the course for you. Hanson is a man who embodies the words he speaks. Sometimes class is more  performance than lecture. He rambles sometimes and he will grade your paper harder than most. But we watched bdsm in class and for sheer entertainment factor he can't be be beat.

Probably the most fun lectures I have ever had at Cornell. Prof. Hanson uses video clips and images extensively, and the lectures seem to go by quickly as a result. I learned a lot, and the grading was not difficult. A really good elective if you have some interest in studying sexuality.

this class is what you make of it - ellis is a really friendly, intelligent professor, but he also has a bit of an ego. if you really listen to what he has to say and take it seriously, you can learn a TON from this class. however, it is easy to coast through and do decently. TAs were outstanding. i had kaelin alexander and he RULED!

He's a strong lecturer--he knows how to perform for a class and how to keep students engaged. However, the quality of the lectures varied--some lectures were brilliant, while other lectures were filled with fluff. The class wasn't difficult: he gives you topics for the 2 essays, and the 3 quizzes are easy as long as you pay attention in class.
WORST TEACHER EVER!!!!
horrible prof! this guy may be smart but he is the worst prof ever. fire him cornell!!!
bad bad bad bad bad

Lecture is always interesting and I enjoyed the reading and discussion sections a lot. Relatively helpful during office hours, although it's probably better to go to TAs since they do most of the grading. Easy to ace the quizzes. LOVED the Ellis holidays.

Best class I've taken at Cornell. I thought this was an english class at it's best. If you go to lecture and study at all you can ace the tests and paper grading was fair. I would go to lecture just out of interest even if I weren't taking the class. There is a lot of shock value, but the literary analysis was genuinely incisive also.

Ellis' Desire class is worse than oral sex with teeth. Classes are just flamboyant ego displays. Lectures are remarkably unhelpful and curiously labeled as part of a Cornell "English class." The TAs are mostly brown-nosing, self-involved "PhD candidates." 98% of people taking the class are looking for titilation, not English scholarship/literature.

Provocative and highly entertaining lecturer - holds attention effortlessly for the entire hour and is delightful to listen to. Quizzes are not difficult if you pay any attention in class & the papers are fine if you put in the effort. Section was unwarranted. Sometimes seems to say things for pure shock value and seems wholly uninterested in interacting with students outside of class, but definitely worth it nonetheless.

i took both 355 and 276. this man is amazing. the class is fun and he's beautiful. i had to miss a few lectures and was more upset about missing the opportunity to hear him speak than missing material for the quizzes.  great class. amazing professor.

POOR lecturer! style is stream of consciousness, unorganized, and redundant.  class is more FLASH than substance.  Hanson was inaccessable, thankfully i had a wonderful TA: peter bailey.  Most people seemed interested in this class for the SHOCK value, not for intellectual development.  several misogynist comments during lecture as well.

His lectures are brilliant and the material is amazing, but he's an aloof intellectual. He's hard to reach: you must sign up for appointments to talk to him and I had to use the directory to get his email. He considers sticking to his own policy more important than helping students out in hard times. Take the class, but beware of him.

One hell of a course. He is a fantastic lecturer and the readings are excellent. He's the english teacher you've been waiting for--off the wall, with absolutely no fear of offending. I couldnt take notes fast enough in his lectures.

I can't gush enough about this guy. From his invented class holidays (which involve lots of latex and hilarity) to the amazing lectures which had me racing to get his words on paper regardless of whether or not they would be "on the test..." Some people are just born for teaching. Take his class.

OMG! Best class ever! I went to the first lecture just for fun, and enrolled the next day-- one of the best professors on campus, fun, and passionate about what he does. And hilarious, I want to be an English major just to be in the same building as him!!!!!!
never met anyone with such intensity and charisma! Brilliant class, great readings very stuctured and organised. did i mention he is hot as hell??
take this class!  eye opening and engaging!

3 words...best class ever! He's a crazy man, in a good way. Lecture is very fun and his quizzes are awesome. Just go to class and you'll be fine. He's amazingly brilliant and fun. An absolute MUST take before graduating...like wines :o)

Ellis is the MAN.  He speaks so smoothly, it's awesome.  If you take this class, don't waste your energy taking notes, you'd be ruining a great opportunity to listen to a very fine speaker.  Everyone deserves one thoroughly entertaining class like this each semester.
No Comments
No Comments
ellis is hot and so is this class

Though this was not the course number when I took it, Hanson's course on The Sexual Child is a tour de force and must not be missed.  It combines all of his strengths--edginess, wit, and intellect--with fabulous material.
Ellis is amazing (and so hot). his lectures are always interesting. decadence is an amazing class, so off from the typical CU class.
No Comments
Excellent and absolutely marvelous!!!
this was the most fun i have had in class at cornell thus far.
No Comments
While his class topics can be interesting, he often goes off on tangents, without actually analyzing the subject of desire itself.  He has more potential, as does his class.
For his first lecture, he came to class in a tuxedo and drank champagn. He pushes the buttons, and the topic of this class desire is extremely interesting and fun - unusual for Cornell classes.

The class content was overall interesting but the lecture and readings were very dense and covered a lot. Some of the grading seemed more subjective as it was graded more on analysis as opposed to knowledge of content. Overall a sweet person though - pretty approachable if you did need help. Attendance optional for some lecture days!
Had her for an FWS. nice and fun teacher. seems like a big nerd (in the good way). not the best at facilitating a useful discussion though. Overall pretty easy grader.

Professor Roby is not a helpful professor at all. Overall, her Ancient Medicine course was extremely disorganized. She expects you to do three assignments every weekend (including breaks) and is very unreasonable when communicating with her about issues you may have with the class. Lectures are monotone and poorly delivered. Would not recommend.

Extremely clear, yet tedious professor.  Has a sweet disposition and definitely knows her material.  The class itself is boring, however, and I would never attend lectures if she did not randomly ask us to submit our thoughts on powerpoint slides to be a part of the participation grade.  Readings are really cool and discussion section is so so.
Good class. Great professor. Very kind and understanding.

She is an awesome teacher. Her class is super fun and easy. There are two discussion posts every week and 5 essays to write. I spend on average 30 minutes a week doing work for her class (not including watching the movies). She really cares about her students and is very approachable. The workload is very doable and I 100% recommend this class.

Marysia is an absolutely fantastic professor! Her course, Histories of the Apocalypse, was interesting and filled with multimedia presentations of the course information. Moreover, her use of a forum, like the Apocalypse Now forum kept the course interesting and relevant. I highly recommend taking a course with professor Jonsson!

The lectures are really fascinating and it's obvious Professor Jonsson really knows the material and is passionate about it. However, the class has an INSANE amount of work. The class would typically give 100 pages of reading PER NIGHT on top of having assignments and papers left and right.

Clayton is really just a grad student, but he shows no interest in furthering your knowledge. Unprepared for class discussions, awkward, extremely unhelpful even w/ simple questions, gives B's to everyone b/c he doesn't know how to grade, and hands back papers over 5 weeks later. I would not recommend if you actually want to improve your writing.
Decent lecturer and a nice guy, but unfortunately isn't the most helpful and understanding on an individual level.

Great professor. Tries his best to introduce fun moments in his lectures. Class is graded a bit harshly, but material on tests felt fair. I barely read the textbook (but I think it's required to access online homework). Recommend grinding problems and going to tutoring for help (1007 class too). Attended every lecture but he records most of them.

Great professor, exams were fair. Lectures were a little too in depth but did give a good comprehensive view to understand the content. However, estimated curves for each prelim were not indicative of final grade.
Wilson does a lot of deriving during lectures, but otherwise, he explains things very well and is very accessible outside of class.

Professor Wilson is highly recommended for giving constructive feedback, delivering amazing lectures that simplify complex concepts, and keeping classes engaging and hilarious. His valuable feedback aids student improvement, and his teaching style makes learning enjoyable.

Subtly funny. Lectures move quickly, but are interesting and done well. Often goes into a lot of depth on topics(ie derivations),which is interesting but not needed for the exams. Exams aren't that hard,but theres no time on them(final was fair). IMO, if I took regular chem, I'd have gotten an A,but Im glad I took this class (reg chem is boring)

The prelims were extremely hard. But dont worry, the curve is fair. Overall his class was fun but he could cover things too fast sometimes. Challenge Problem sets were optional. Except you really want an A+, you dont have to do them or read the textbook actually.

Teaches the material very well. Often times goes through the material too quickly to get through all of it. He cares about how well you do and explains everything well in office hours, but the exams are definitely difficult. Not too much work, but you have to keep up with readings and studying to do well.

Chem 2150 with Wilson was amazing.  From day one, he had the class like O Mg (Oxygen and Magnesium).  He often speeds up near the end of lecture, but is still easy to follow and explains everything.  Labs can sometimes be long, but the in class demos made up for everything.  Must take for pyrotechnics #thermite #oxygen&hydrogen #burningdollas

2150 was definitely my favorite class this semester! Prof. Wilson knows what he's talking about - lectures can be fast, but office hours helped a ton. The labs didn't get super good until halfway through the semester, but cool demos in lecture, like what was probably one of the awesomest things ever in Baker 200, the THERMITE REACTION *mic drop*

I absolutely loved this class and Prof. Wilson. He tended to go very quickly in lectures but was always available in office hours or outside of class to clarify and answer questions. Be sure to do the OWL homework and challenge psets as they will prepare you best for the final. Lab reports are ridiculously long and annoying though. Take this class!

Knew what he was teaching, but was very boring. I mean VERY boring. The pace of the class was very quick too since he covered a lot of material that was not really needed or understandable for introductory chemistry.
A good guy, he really wants you to understand the material, and while he may go too slowly or too quickly in lecture on occasion just be sure to raise your hand and ask questions if you need to.

Super chill, but not a very good teacher. He is very derivation-heavy, and introduces some irrelevant concepts in the process of these derivations. His CengageBrain homeworks, however, are good preparation for the prelims and final. The class itself was very interesting, but don't kill yourself over copying everything he writes on the board.
He's ok. Tests are pretty hard but fortunately there's a pretty big curve. Lots of reading required and all the hw is online.

His lectures can be interesting, but they also can put you to sleep. The reason I rated him so high is because when you do listen, he explains the material very well. He's also very straightforward in his lectures and adds a little humor, which is refreshing.

Overall, lectures are intellectually stimulating and mostly conversational rather than a traditional teach-topic-test-topic type course. All in all, I enjoyed the course but definitely had to work for a good grade. Both the take home assignments, final paper, and exams were at least moderately challenging and would take a lot of time to complete.
one of the best history professors at cornell
Phenomenal. His lectures make you think doing history is sexy. Prepare to read a lot for his exams. Fun fact: he doesn't have a smart phone but he's proud of it.
pls take a class with him if you can, amazing

I love Prof Tagliacozzo. He's a really nice, distinguished, funny, and chill guy. I skipped half of the assigned readings and pulled more than one last-minute all-nighter to write my papers and I still loved to engage in his very interesting discussions and I ended up doing well, so if you're gonna put more effort than me, then you're golden.

He is probably the only professor that makes me want to come to class. Discussions are engaging and very informative. He also gives really good feedback. Has to be the best class I've taken here at Cornell so far

He gives a lot of readings, but his class is pretty easy as long as you do the work. Gives really good feedback on essays. He is pretty down to earth, and he held one on one office hours for 15 to 20 minutes, which was helpful.

literally so amazing and awesome! please take global islam if you can. has opened up a whole new perspective to me in terms of how i think about islam! very understanding towards freshman who have never taken a college writing course

Tagliacozzo is the man. If you're a freshman, definitely take a FWS with him. He is so passionate about SE Asia and I would definitely jump at the chance to take a class with him again. If you do the work, put in the effort, show up to class, you're gold baby.

He's a great lecturer, keeps things interesting. Honestly, I didn't think I would find SE Asia this interesting. Professor Tagliacozzo definitely played a big part in it making things interesting. Papers are graded pretty hard, and there is a lot of reading every week. Going to the lectures will save you a lot of work later on.

Office hours are a good opportunity to see how passionate he is about SE Asia. He is always more than willing to dive into the material with you and clarify information. He also happens to be very chill and will chat with you on just about everything. He even encouraged me not to worry about my 5 page paper and go out on a Friday night haha

Amazing class & prof. Fantastic lecturer, interesting guy, wants you to do well. You will become interested in SE Asian history even if you weren't before. Papers are graded pretty tough. Exams cover a lot of different topics, split up the readings. Attendance isn't "mandatory" but it's by far the easiest and most interesting way to learn it

Nicest professor at Cornell.  Genuinely cares about his students understanding of the material and also their general well-being.  He really knows his stuff and he's a lenient grader when it comes to essays.

Excellent Professor. Initiated my interest in the Indian Ocean World. Extremely helpful and approachable. His love for the subject is contagious. Got a great sense of humor, which makes classes so much fun. If you want to learn more about the the Indian Ocean World, you must definitely take a class with Professor Tagliacozzo.

Tagliacozzo is the man.  He is fabulously brilliant and yet so genuinely kind.  He will leave you with a bad case of wanderlust by the time he is done regaling you with tales of his adventures throughout Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean.  Easy grader, too, but I still learned tons from him.  Try to meet his kids, they're adorable.

Tagliacozzo is an incredible professor. He knows multiple languages and can make connections on just about anything. He's a brilliant lecturer and a huge soccer fan. I was skittish on this class at first, but it turned out to be one of the best classes I've taken at Cornell - and that's saying something, since I'm an English major lol

Wonderful professor who makes the material come alive with his enthusiasm, trips to the museum, show-and-tell presentations and great sense of humor. You are missing out if you don't take a class with him!
Professor Tagaliacozzo is an amazing teacher! He is so humorous and entertaining. His lectures were very interesting and engaging. He's really brilliant, but, not gonna lie, he's also really cute!

I took his History of Things class and it was boring. We talked about things such as salt, sugar, spices, etc. We had to write 5 papers and he was very obscure on how we should write each of them but the ironic thing was when he graded them he was tough. He focused more on the number of sources we used instead of the quality of sources we used.
Amazing lecturer. Makes every class enjoyable and has a great sense of humour. He is always readily available to help his students.

Professor Tagliacozzo is an excellent professor, and anyone who takes his courses are sure to enjoy it. He is so kind, helpful, clear, and approachable. He co-taught with Prof. Sherman Cochran, who is equally an excellent professor and very kind and helpful man. Overall, a great class. I highly recommend it.

I took his South-East Asian History class a few years ago and Prof. Tagliacozzo was amazing. He was by far, the best professor I have had at Cornell. He is extremely smart, multi-lingual, very approachable, and so nice. He genuinely cares about his students and answers any questions that they have. Fantastic experience with him as my Professor!

He is simply one of the best professors at Cornell. Extremely well-organized and eloquent, he presents his lectures in such interesting and coherent way. He is extremely knowledgeable about SEA and in lectures you can visibly see his passion for it. He does provide a lot of info in one lecture but he makes it so fascinating and fun. Plus, so nice!

An excellent professor!  Prof. Tagliacozzo is a total expert in his field...it's just amazing all the stuff he knows about SE Asia.  He's a fair grader who offers great feedback. Class is challenging with endless readings, but as long as you stay on task you'll be fine.  I hear he's up for tenure this year..he deserves it...great sense of humor too
Great Prof!

Fantastic seminar leader, and one of those professors who genuinely cares about his students. Also, the only Cornell prof who spends time on docks in SE Asia smoking clove cigarettes with smugglers for research.

Probably one of the best professors I ever had.  LOTS of information in his lectures  but very interesting(you can tell he knows so much about SE Asia), extremely nice and helpful.  Easy grader (but you have to study for it!)and did i mention how hot he is?

Terrific professor, crams a lot of information into class so learn shorthand. A lot of reading but the papers are easy and the tests too if you study briefly. Definitely worth the effort to take, and he has many great stories about his research experiences. Also cute as a button and genuinely nice.

very good prof because he's obsesssssed with SE Asia and knows everything about it.  has tons of random anecdotes from his travels there.  classes are interesting and engaging.  lots of reading, but overall the class is not too hard, as long as you make an effort to participate.
History of Modern Southeast Asia. He is a really nice guy who has travelled to the places he's talking about. Clear and effective lectures. Class was 4 papers... which is wonderful.

Excellent lecturer. Its hard to beat his outlines, and effective presentation. Yet, he manages to do so with his enthusiasm for both the subject and teaching. One of the up and coming stars of Cornell's history department.
Extremely well-organized, clear & coherent. The MAN!
No Comments

Cornell should hire more professors who, like Professor Rebillard, actually know things and can evaluate and train professionals in the field. One of the few scholars in Cornell Humanities left who hasn't given up on facts for trendy theories and nonsense.

Idk why we were graded so harshly on exams, and no transparency on grading. If you want an A u need stellar knowledge of Roman history and corresponding dates. Even with that, its hard to get better than a B on exams. Attendance was also absolutely mandatory and he will get upset if you leave the class mid lecture even for a legitimate reason.

1205 had weekly quizzes and they started out rough for me. 

A nice person, but he has very high standards for your latin knowledge and does not like to repeat himself once he has gone over something already. You have to know the translation well before class. Accessible during office hours. He wants you to do well, but you have to put in the work

The class mainly students who take Latin for the language requirement and he knows it. The text itself is dry and theres not much that can make it more interesting. His weekly quizzes are easy if you review the passages thoroughly and hes pretty patient answering questions in class. Hes helpful in explaining syntax too.

I took Professor Rebillard's graduate course called "Change in Late Antiquity." His sheer intelligence and knowledge seemed daunting at first, but I grew to appreciate his extremely careful criticism. He's also a kind person. Cornell is fortunate to have such an expert in the field.
He was really caring professor and I really enjoyed class. His tone is sometimes monotonous. You have to do the assigned readings to follow the class. His lecture is done on the basis of readings.

Very dry and plodding: he just does the same thing every day. Make sure you prepare the translations for class. He gets annoyed when people ask questions that he has already answered. If you show up, can explain your translations, and follow his specific rules for translation, easy A.
a tad dry at times but a basically good professor. Study hard and pay attention and you're golden. Pretty mild-mannered guy (not sure what other reviews are talking about)
Okay class, decent teacher, easy tests.
Quite possibly the best professor at Cornell. The French accent is great.

oh. my. god. what an awful professor. how this man managed to suck all of the interesting material out of one of the most interesting subjects EVER (roman history) i'll never know. perhaps it is because his class is designed for people who already know a good deal about the subject. way to inspire learning.

worst teacher i've ever had in my life. oh and just a heads up to the person who disagreed with unfair grading, take a look at what class the person was referring to. it was a latin class, not whatever class you took. so less bitterness, more paying attention.
No Comments

He is the WORST teacher I've had in my entire educational career. Not only could I not understand him but he was a total jerk to our class.
