if you like lecture-based classes and take good notes this class is perfect. if you like cramming right before the exam, not paying attention during lectures, and teaching yourself the material (me) this class is extremely difficult. grading is really varied too which is frustrating. just not for me
Good professor and a great person. He truly cares about his students. The prelims are short-answer based and there are a few writing/design assignments.

i did the extra credit without realizing that it didn't contribute to getting A+ but that's fine. He's very nice and holds lots of office hours which were very useful to the prelims. His presentation notes aren't very good so you pretty much have to show up for class

Great class. Would definitely recommend! Prof.Evans is very friendly, and his lectures are engaging. However, make sure you download the lecture outlines and organize your notes accordingly, because he does not always mention explicitly which section he is in so you could get lost. Grading is very fair. Go to office hours and you can surely get A!

Professor Evans is such a great professor. The material in this class is super interesting no matter what your major is. The work is very manageable. It's clear that Professor Evans loves teaching, and he is very kind person and wants his students to succeed.
Fantastic professor. Very interesting and relevant material. Always willing to help out students!
Elite... that's all.
I was genuinely interested in the topics that he covered. As long as you fill out the practice questions for the prelim ahead of time you should do well in this class.

Very interesting class. Dr. Evans is accessible and truly cares about his students. Grading is very fair, but not an "easy A" class. You have to work on things thoroughly and ahead of time to make sure you get all the points. Some people don't do this and underestimate the workload. Then they get points off and think the grading is harsh.
Professor Evans is a fantastic lecturer and you can tell he really cares about his students. Highly recommend!

I can't rave about Gary enough. He is extremely caring and accommodating to students. He has no problems with giving extensions. The class itself is pretty easy. If you went to lecture and took good notes, exams should be a breeze, but still pretty time-consuming. Assigned readings aren't necessary to get an A. The class material is also very cool.

I really enjoyed the lectures, but the exams were extremely intense and graded toughly (despite questions being released ahead of time). The TAs are tough graders too when it comes to the projects. This would have been one of my favorite classes if the exams were not as excessive/detailed. The professor is really insightful.

Very straightforward and easy class. Lots of opportunity for extra credit (with SONA), and the rubric is very clear. Going to lecture is pretty important as his slides/slide summaries aren't very informative on their own. He's a very engaging and good lecturer though, and it's very clear he knows what he's talking about.

Absolutely a great class. Makes you think beyond simple principles and forces you to apply your understanding to real world, environmental examples. Prof. gives ten essay questions before the test, and the tests consists of four of the ten, randomly given. Very very fair, and the class makes sure that you understand the material. Tons of extracredt

Gary Evans is a wonderful professor. He really loves teaching and is very willing to talk to outside of class. The tests, however, are a series of incredibly specific questions that are given out a few weeks before the test. Prof. Evans does hours of prelim review, which is essential for doing well because in grading he looks for specific answers.

Evans is such a nice guy. Go to lecture, pay attention, and you will breeze by with an A. Distributes ample exam questions well before tests - answer them thoroughly, because he picks 4-5 of them of the 8-10 given to place on the exam. Don't buy readings, just take notes in class. Tests feel long, but if you answered the ?s beforehand it's easy.

I took an economics class with the allegedly distinguished professor Evans. When I had received a puzzling low mark on an assignment, I had asked him for Office Hours, where he repeatedly made clear he only takes students alone. When I had arrived, he seemed very distracted and was constantly jingling change in his pocket. Unprofessional boomer

Gary is an amazing professor and his teaching style has really contributed to making my life simpler. You have to go to lecture or make sure you know someone who takes good notes because his slides are hard to understand if he doesn't explain them. His grading system is fair and office hours are a very beneficial. Also make sure to ask questions.

Professor Evans is a great lecturer - I took this for a distribution requirement and loved it. Just make sure you go to lecture and take good notes, he encourages to use group effort to prepare for all exams and all answers to 10 essay questions are covered in lecture. No need for any readings, so don't buy them! Just go to class, and listen:)

Took this class not knowing anything prior about the subject to for credit requirement. Lectures were really interesting. Pay attention during them because slides won't really help much and office hours before prelims are packed. love his prelim system, and the extra credit helps a lot. Dont be afraid to approach him before class!! fun guy

DO NOT buy the required textbook material. Don't need to do readings to get an A go to lecture and write down examples for exam. You get possible 10 questions on exam and 4 are actually on it. If you go to office hours he literally goes through them and gives you answers & you can do psych studies for 20 points of extra credit.

Professor Evans is amazing! His slides are easy to understand and he makes them so applicable to our lives! The class is interdisciplinary and very interesting, and his method of preparing students for exams is really effective and shows that he cares. Definitely recommend!

Don't expect to be able to ask your TAs about making anything clearer before tests or projects; they aren't responsible for grading, and some (if not all) of them don't even go to class. Gary Evans is a fine lecturer (if he would just put some words in his slideshows instead of just pictures every now and again), but the class is disorganized.

LOVED this class and Professor Evans. Such interesting material that changed the way I think about the world around me. The readings aren't necessary, but they're interesting. Taking thorough notes in lecture will give you everything you need to do well on tests and projects.

Professor Evans is very helpful and clear in lectures. His lectures are engaging and usually interesting. His tests are not too bad but sometimes his TAs grade a bit harshly. Professor Evans is very helpful in his office hours and very fair. He has done a lot of famous research and written several books but he is very humble in class.

This is an interesting, low-stress course that gives you a language to think about the environment in. Gary is helpful, exams are fair, and projects are relaxed. The one frustration was that many studies seemed vague or even outdated. We needed to think about fewer studies in more depth rather than brush over sketchy data.

This class is great for anyone interested in design, human behavior, or a little self-reflection. TAs grade prelims kind of harshly, but you can easily make up for it with the projects and attendance grade. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT; it will help a lot. Overall, good lecturer, VERY interesting class.

The only redeeming aspect of this course is that attendance is not required.  Gary Evans is a nice human being, but shockingly stupid.  Class is rampant with overgeneralizations, confusion of correlation and causation, and old, weak data.  If you wish to become a more critically thinking person, do not take this course.

Class is very interesting for anyone. Assignments aren't hard. Tests are doable, but sometimes the TAs grade too harshly. After one exam, I got a pretty low grade and asked the TAs why I lost certain points. They couldn't explain some to me, so I went to Evans and he offered to meet with me for 2 hours going over each little point. Recommended.

Talks about things that really make sense and can be applied to everyday life but are still unique and insightful. Great for anyone interested in design, and for anyone just interested in how people of different cultures and in different settings interact with their environments.

Gary is a great lecturer, very insightful and fun to just sit back and listen to. You can do pretty well without doing the reading, but the readings are actually pretty interesting and you end up getting a LOT more out of his lectures if you've done the readings beforehand. Also he's very approachable and great to talk to.

Tests are very lengthy and may be only 4 short essay questions, but each question has an 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d, 1e, 1f, etc, so really it's like answering 30 q's. Wish I were kidding. you really have to prepare, & even then it doesn't guarantee you'll do well. Take the WIM section. it reduces the test grades to only 25% of your grade. Much easier that way

Professor Evans is a clear lecturer, is interesting, and is very helpful in his office hours (especially in that he has many many office hours near prelim times).  The tests are short essays, but you are given a bank of essay questions (4/10 questions chosen) before hand, which is nice :).

He is literally the nicest person I've ever met. Super reasonable when it comes to work and he doesn't try and trick you on tests or anything. Understands that kids are busy and is willing to work with you. Listens to students' suggestions.

Class is no longer an easy A like it seemed to be in previous years. Going to lecture is not mandatory and I don't think I opened any of the textbooks all year. Unfortunate that no one really watched all of the movies either. Prof. Miya. is really quiet and hard to understand. His lectures are rambly and tend to make no sense.
boring guy. Not an easy A+ class anymore tho he is really nice in gradings. Friends who never went to lectures managed to pull an A+, while I couldn't.
VERY nice guy. I felt bad for him as no one came to lecture. His reading and movie selection is no longer from light easy anime. But easy grader.
The easiest A+ class ever. Never attended a single lesson. Never learned anything.
No Comments

Okay... so the guy's a little boring, but he chooses great readings and links them together really well.  His essay topics tend to be a bit ambiguous but he is very willing to answer questions and help you out.  Overall, not the best prof, but was good enough that I am looking forward to a second class with him.

Okay, the subject matter was interesting but as the semester progressed I found myself losing more and more interest due to super long readings, ambiguous essay topics, and uninspiring lectures.  A very nice guy though. I guess I learned from this course.

Content was interesting to analyze but made the material way harder than needed. Half the time, I couldn't understand what she was saying. Class involves discussions and busy work, which are easy but repetitive. Isn't very accommodating towards absences (only get two absences before your grade goes down, including illness and death in the family).
He's awesome! Really nice guy and truly a brilliant scholar.

I took an FWS with Professor Weiss in the fall. He is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about linguistics. I am only hoping that my next FWS is going to be as good as his. He gives you good feedback on your papers, and I, as someone who doesn't like to write much, thought his prompts were very compelling. An awesome professor all around.

Historical linguistics (an FWS) with Michael Weiss is an absolutely fascinating course. Not only is he a great professor whose lectures remind me of reading National Geographic but the course was an easy A. You have to put in effort, but I had by far the best FWS experience among all my friends. If you need an FWS and this is open, TAKE IT!

Not much reading, but all of them are quite informative. He motivated us to read some classic paper in linguistics. However, if you happened to read a bit about linguistics, you should know many of the anecdotes he will share.  Most lectures are self-contained units about a certain ancient language/unrecorded history of existing languages.

Just fantastic. His lectures are a flood of knowledge from his massive mental store; this was the only class I actually enjoyed taking notes for. He's laid back, pleasant, and a bit goofy. You'll get both a wealth of general knowledge regarding the historical method, and a great deal of fascinating tidbits from taking his introduction course.
Laid-back, funny, and engaging. Good guy.

Have taken a couple of classes with this prof, (historical ling and Intro to ProtoIndoEuropean) incredibly knowledgeable on Indo-European and Historical Linguistics.  For people interested in linguistics, definitely take his classes.  His classes are not really for those looking to fulfill requirements though.  Awesome prof and awesome classes.
very, very knowledgeable and helpful. very organized and responsive.  however, this course is not very interesting unless you;re a true linguistics fanatic, don't take it.

It was a very "interesting" class; we learned lots of neat tidbits. But for anyone majoring in linguistics it's not deep enough. We did the phonology for almost the entire semester, and the one thing I was interested in (syntactic change) was hardly mentioned. He also missed a few classes without telling us beforehand or explaining after.

From a distance he looks like your average guy in a T-shirt and cargo pants. He's not. He knows an heck of a lot, and keeps the class really fascinating. This course can feel a bit fractured (a lot of mini-units), but by the end it doesn't matter. And it DOES help to take notes, even if he says you don't have to; little details show up on  prelims.
Great Class. Great professor. Very knowledgable
I found his class to be a touch boring, but an interesting subject nonetheless. Do you know anyone else who can write in Tocharrian A?? I sure don't...overall, pretty good
such a nice and competent prof. and an easy A class. he got me interested in Indo-European languages (his specialty).

There were VERY few instances where he did not know an answer to a student's question, not matter how in depth, off the top of his head. He has an EXTREMELY good knowledge of the subject matter. He was always willing to find the few answers he did not know. I give him the highest ratings.
very easy but interesting class! he's so knowledgeable about his field. also, he's a great lecturer.
No Comments
just amazing.
Absolute sweet heart. Didn't learn a thing.

Clearly passionate about the work that he does and the material that he teaches, but lectures are extremely disorganized and thus difficult to follow. Grade is based on a project (which you can get a good grade on if you put in the work) and take-home exam (three 4-5 page essays). Surprised by grade received b/c I didn't read at all.

fantastic professor! never met one more caring about his students. doesn't use TAs for this class so it just enhances the learning and experience. the few assessments he assigns are substantial but very reasonable and manageable over the course of the semester. TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HIM!!!

Weiss is a fantastic guy, super knowledgeable about WWII, the world, and humanitarianism. His lectures are extremely disorganized to the point of not being very useful (for completing the assignments). You don't really have to go to class. Many readings and weekly discussions, but you can bs the discussions if you understand what the book is about

Weiss is hilarious and if you show up and read our stuff, he will notice and help you out a lot. I wrote a paper that was presented in Washington DC and it was the best experience I've ever had at Cornell.
Passionate about the material. Engaging professor
Lectures were disorganized but discussions were great and Weiss always goes above and beyond to engage you in the course material as much as possible. Very likeable and friendly guy

Prof. Weiss may not be the most laser focused professor Ive ever had, but he certainly is the nicest professor Ive had at Cornell. He goes above and beyond for his students and really knows his stuff. You wont do poorly in his class if you do the work but you will learn something and meet a great guy, you have nothing to lose if interested in ww2

Weiss is unconventional for a CU prof.–class is free-flowing and discussion-based, which is nice but leads to organizational challenges. He is exceptionally kind, reasonable and goes out of his way to help students. Unbelievably smart, willing to tap every resource from textbooks to his connections– he lined up great, big-name guest speakers.

I absolutely recommend any class with Professor Weiss. He is one of the nicest and most supportive Professors you will find at Cornell. He has his own style of teaching, but if you take the time to get involved in discussions you will find you learn an incredible amount.

The mid term for the WWII history course was barely comprehensible.  Not that it mattered because it didn't count if it hurt your grade.  This class is a great filler class for busy semesters-- you don't have to attend lecture or section and will probably get an A anyway so long as you skim the readings on your own and aren't an idiot.

The professor was very poor in lectures, but he is a great guy that is very passionate about the material. The class itself education wise was not the best, but it did open me up to a new world. Professor is not bad overall. No better, no worse.

If you don't appreciate/like Professor Weiss then you're an idiot.  Yea some things in his classes aren't conventional.  Hey guess what, if you go to class and read the material then you will learn a LOT.  That's what he cares about and that's what really matters.  Take his classes!

Great, fun, relaxed class.  Weiss is a WWII historian so you learn about Iran as the course moves along.  He has ambitious goals for the semester, don't worry if you don't reach them.  Also no pre-lim, no quizzes, basically a guaranteed A with an amazing professor.

I step into class wondering how he has slipped through the cracks. While the readings and subject matter are fascinating, his lectures consist of him rambling about unrelated topics totally unrelated to WW2, and generally disregarding the curriculum which he set forth. His lack of structure in the class room is really a shame.

Lectures were completely pointless, and none of the notes were ever needed. Weiss did provide an extremely interesting reading list and was very enthusiastic about is subject. I never went to class, got an easy A, and learned a lot about the subject from the readings. Would absolutely recommend this class.
Lectures were pretty useless, otherwise tried hard to get people to be proactive.
JW is fab, fab, fab; the best teacher at cornell. take his class before he retires - which i hope is never; an asset to all undergradt

World War II - Prof Weiss is a very nice guy. The class might be difficult for someone who does not have a good background in the material - it's very unstructured - but for those who enjoy WWII history this clas is right up your alley.

Provides many different perspectives on all sorts of topics relating to WWII in Europe.  Some might say it is disjointed, but I don't think they get his style at all.  Weiss is very nice and approachable.  Great discusion sections, good lectures. It is true that the lectures aren't a chronological account of WWII- but that is what readings are for!
not a great lecturer, but a really interesting and enthusiastic guy.

His lectures are awful. He has no focus. His ideas are actually pretty archaic, although that's de rigeur for the history department. On the plus side, he does send out loads of irrelevant emails to people in his classes, so that's an ego boost.
great professor with a ton of interesting perspectives on how to learn about world war 2. his discussion sections are some of the best classes at cornell. i can't recommend his courses enough.

A hisory buff who knows everything about French history & WWI/II.  He's a great guy to talk to, and a good professor, though he is best in small, discussion oriented environments.  His lectures tend to ramble as he's trying to convey too much material!
The worst teacher I have seen at Cornell.

I took a few courses with Professor Cohn when I was at Cornell. She's an exceptionally gifted instructor and a real advocate for her students, always providing help and encouragement where it's needed. Couldn't recommend more highly.

So awesome. One of the clearest lecturers I've ever had, and very funny and friendly on top of that. Lots of material, but she makes it straightforward. Splits larger projects into very reasonable pieces. Extremely supportive; will always make times for anyone. I took two courses from her and still miss both of them more than two years later.
No Comments

Abby is awesome! One of the most friendly, down-to-earth professors I've met at Cornell. In addition, she's a fantastic teacher, she's incredibly passionate about Linguistics, and she's great to chat with about just about anything. Highly recommended.
Super kind, super understanding, very kind! Her syllabus is very well spaced in terms of course work, and she gives excellent 1 on 1 feedback for papers. Nice class overall!
If you take the time to complete all the lectures and assignments, the class is extremely easy

If this class isn't required, I strongly recommend not taking it. It's mostly mindless memorization with 2-3 hours of online lectures before class. The class is poorly structured, time-consuming, and boring, with lectures filled with quiz questions worth 30% of your grade. Prelims were easy but included trick questions meant to lower your score.

Boring class. Wouldn't recommend it unless it's required for your major. Had to memorize the Tree of Life, which required a lot of work while also seeming completely useless. Exams were fair as long as you study.
I knew I should have avoided this professor. Avoid her at all costs!

Attendance is 100% mandatory because of clicker questions during each lecture and 5 question quizzes to start to see if you did the homework. Yes, it is annoying, but if you do the work (which there's a lot of), you'll be fine. Material isn't necessarily difficult, just a lot of memorization. If you put time and effort in, you will get an A or A+.

This was an incredibly boring class. Took it as a non-stem kid for my bio credit, and it was torturous. The kids in your group make a huge difference, and the effort was low all around. Constant tedious work so it's easy to fall behind. Had a bad interaction with a TA who refused to let me make up an assignment.

The amount of grunt work this class gives (for no reason) is absolutely appalling. The only thing the flipped classroom structure does is waste your time outside of class. Not happy at all with how the course is taught. The professors claim that research on flipped classrooms is more beneficial but research findings change all the time...

Flipped classroom style - lots of repetitive busy work and in-class sessions were mostly sitting around. Frustrating miscommunications (TA told me exam was open note, announcement days before exam that it wasn't). BUT they changed stuff after mid-semester evals, so she does care about students. Not a hard class, but requires time and memorization

A hybrid class where you watch hours videos each week, spending class doing quizzes. A class Discord, no Ed, where you must post with your real name if you want help. A course email where you will be ignored. A lack of TAs leading to rushed discussions. A condescending professor. All this plus more make for the worst class I have ever taken here.
One of the worst professors I've had the privilege of taking a class with. Listening to her feels like bad chalk on a blackboard. I don't encourage anyone to take a class with her.

Disclaimer: I took 1781 asynchronously, which isn't an option here so I picked 1780, which has the same content but diff structure.
Excellent lectures that force you to learn, as well as helpful assignments. Very time-consuming course. Tests are open book. Prof is not very responsive to questions.
I recommend this course only if you have time.

Took BIOEE4940 Biostats w her over summer. Inconsistent in responding to questions emailed in abt material (she'll answer some questions in an email but not others??), tested on material that was never taught (as in "oops-here's the R code for that"), sent out an exam for material that hadn't been covered yet (granted, this was quickly fixed).

1780 is heavy on memorization but offers lots of room to succeed (total exams make up 1/3 of grade, the rest is essentially participation). Compared to bioee 1610, 1780 requires more studying and outside work but has a higher median in the end fwiw. Abby clearly cares about her students' learning and is enthusiastic about he material.

My main complaint about Abby's teaching is that recorded lectures were long and repetitive (2x speed is a must). In-person "lectures" were annoying and not very helpful review sessions. She can come across as a bit condescending, but she's at least enthusiastic about the material. I don't think anyone needs to dread her class.
Lectures were meh, lots of work and lectures, wasn't a huge fan of flipped classroom model, but at least the course was easy.

Class is easy but 100% memorization based. You have to learn the entire tree of life, which is rly hard. My semester was online, which made it slightly easier. The profs and TAs are very accessible. Grading is split up into a lot of small things, which means you have to try hard on everything to do well, which is annoying but overall good class.

Passive aggressive for no reason, as someone else mentioned in their rating. We understood the assignment without writing down anything (it was not required, we just had to get the answers), and she tells us as a group “if you guys are guessing I wonder how you’ll guess through the exam”. We weren’t guessing. Be cautious. Simple class.

Professor Drake is unnecessarily passive aggressive. We were completing a team assignment in lecture (we did it very quickly without actually doing the assignment), and she came up to us and talked to us for 5 minutes about how we didn't do the assignment (even though we got all the questions right). Beware. Otherwise, the class is really easy.

She's kind of crazy but in a good way. This class uses flipped classroom/active learning, which worked really well for me as a more independent learner -- it's just a heavy workload. They do a great job of teaching the material, rotating lecturers. Abby is very caring and a good communicator. Also interesting material!

This class is essentially entirely online. There are weekly pre-lecture modules containing video lectures and quizzes. Unfortunately, that doesn't mean you can skip the in-person lectures as there are iClicker questions. The content is simple and the prelims were straightforward. Study the learning objectives and memorize the TOL and you're set.

As others said, 1780 has many in-class quizzes. If you do take it, take good notes on the pre-lecture videos, as that's what the exams will actually cover. The material is interesting, and Professor Drake is very nice, but the teaching style didn't work for me. Take BIOEE 1610 if you just want to fulfill the A&S biology distribution requirement.

I'm pretty sure if I took this class in-person it would be a nightmare. She may take things slow during lectures, but the material was fascinating. You can tell that she loves teaching the class. The class was straightforward enough to allow for a strong understanding of material. It did help that I was online and exams were open-note, otherwise...

Dr. Drake seems to have good intentions and did want us to learn. Otherwise, I disliked her as a professor. The class was nothing but painful memorization. The tests were written very unclearly, and the lectures were pointless. I learned more about evolution in the short time we spent on it in my AP bio class in HS.

I don't usually review literally anything, but I loved this course, so I had to. It's an active learning class, with heavy emphasis on class participation through small group activities and iClicker questions. A lot of people don't like this, but I have ADHD and it was beyond perfect. Dr. Drake is great, attentive, and helpful.

Professor Drake is the real mastermind behind 1780. She is nice and well meaning, but her voice can be annoying as it constantly sounds on the edge of a nervous breakdown. She is a huge fan of "Active Learning", which basically means tons of in class clicker quizzes. Lectures are pointless otherwise - all the actual teaching is done via videos.
Awful course. She's the worst lecturer and she runs the course. Prepare to drown in iclicker questions, section assignments, and readings that are really nothing but busywork.

As mentioned previously, not the biggest fan of the structure of the class (way too participation-heavy, interactive, and elementary), but the material itself was very interesting and at times relevant. Exams are easy. Take good notes on/study from vodcasts, show up to lecture and section, and keep up with the material and you'll do fine.

This class is very memorization heavy and the "flipped classroom" can be highly frustrating. A lot of the learning is done through homework, while the actual lecture is a lot of quizzing. However, Abby is very caring and seems to really want her students to do well. Your grade in this class is based on more than just a couple of tests.
dull class, lots of pointless memorization.

Makes many mistakes. Not organized at all. Class is all over the place. The interactive classroom thing is not effective. Class is essentially useless if you're not going into evolutionary science. All memorization. Wish I never took it.
Dr. Drake is on the teaching team for an intro bio course (1780) that is heavy on memorization of taxa and phylogenies. If you can memorize you will be fine.

Took 1780 class can really drag and is a lot of brute memorization of phylogeny and taxa no one would ever need to know unless a researcher in the field nor will remember after the test. Also not the biggest fan of flipped classroom, very little actual material presented about half of class is spent solely on testing

Dr. Abby Drake was one of the professors in the teaching team when I took 1780. She was definitely into the subject she was teaching, but in all honesty, memorization of phylogenetic trees is dull at best. I didn't like her "flipped classroom" method, but that being said, she is a really caring professor who wants to help her students succeed
nice prof but a terribly useless class

If PHYS 1110 is with Prof. Crites, take it. While yes, the class was disorganized throughout the whole semester, Prof. Crites always put on the front that it was all going to plan. Even if 10 kids showed up for the 8am, she was always psyched to be there. Overall, very nice, lenient, caring, and will always be there to help.

Professor Crites is always incredibly bubbly and positive, even when only 15 out of the 200 students show up to class. The labs barely have any instructions, so you just make up random experiments or sit there and do nothing. This class was a mess, but it was so entertaining watching people complain on the ED Discussion. 10/10 would recommend.
Professor Cohn was wonderful, very easy to contact and was super flexible with deadlines. I loved her class so much. Highly reccommend.

Elisha is hands down the best prof I've had the pleasure of learning from at Cornell-- I even asked her to be my major advisor, and nominated her for a teaching award (literally wrote 3 full pages about how wonderful she is). She genuinely cares about her students and wants everyone's input. She values student readings as much as her own!

Pros: Super approachable and knowledgeable professor who makes an effort to keep class interesting and gives specific feedback, not difficult to get a good grade if you put even a little effort into essays and talking in class Cons: A LOT of reading, class participation is important to your grade  Overall, a good class that did improve my writing!
Pros: Lectures were amazing and I was always engaged. Teacher is very nice and enthusiastic about her work. Essays are easy as long as you come to class and take notes on her ideas.

Very clear, engaging and nice. Class was lively: somehow everyone used to contribute(unlike my other FWS where like 2 people ever talk). My writing improved a lot! She points out mistakes exactly so you can work on it. Don't take the class if you aren't at least mildly interested in British Lit, though(but that goes without saying,duh).

I took this class freshman year as FWS, and I immediately dropped it. The time I was in it we spent in a circle just noting random facts about the book at hand and didn't get anywhere at all, plus it was ridiculously boring with no variance in activities whatsoever. Felt like I was back in 9th grade lit. Like the topic; don't like the professor.
Class if extremely interesting and Elisha is very engaging in class. Not that hard of a grader, engaging lecturer.

Poe was a pretty good Professor. It is possible to do well in the class if you do the homework and go to office hours. Poe is also very friendly and truly cares about his students. I recommend this class if you are interested in econ.

Loved him, corny sense of humor but a dorky professor who I got along with. If you actually do your homework, go to office hours, and go to his TAs for extra help, there is no reason not to do well. lectures are a bit annoying but he's way more helpful outside of class.

I wasn't interested in this class tbh, but he's a nice guy and professor and does a lot for his students. I strongly suggest going to his OH and class because that's how you'll do well. He's a good professor and really does care for his students.
I never understood anything in class. All of my teaching came from the TA's because I never understood what he was talking about in class.
unless you must take it, never even think about taking this class. takes up so much of your time and useless

I was extremely interested in the topics in this class. His classes were for the most part interesting and I enjoyed going. The course is not hard as long as you can pick up the basic ideas of economics and relate them. Go to office hours if you need help, he is extremely helpful during them.

Class is quite easy overall. Tests were easy to do well on as long as you know how to do the homeworks and did the practice exams. He is not the best teacher in the world but good enough for me. I just hate how the HWs have to be turned in at 9AM the day of class (and not even in class, you have to walk to warren to turn it in)

Poe is a nice guy, but that didn't make him a better teacher.  His powerpoints are not very helpful and it's very easy to fall asleep in his class.  He tries to make it interesting in the beginning by using real money to exchange things in class, but it doesn't work and his jokes are cheesy. I did relatively well in the class, but I didn't like it.

Poe is probably one of the worst professors I've had at cornell. The class is not hard, and he's not a bad guy, but he should not be teaching. The material is very easy, but the way he explains it makes it very complicated. Always talks about what a good guy he is. He thinks he's really cool..

Poe has trouble relaying calculations/mathmatical information to his students.  He is a very fair grader and tries to help you out.  However, he's also very passive aggressive and prideful.  Not an enjoyable class.  Stay on top of the work from the beginning or it will catch you off guard at the end. Not as easy as it first seems.
