Not an enjoyable class.  Stay on top of the work from the beginning or it will catch you off guard at the end. Not as easy as it first seems.
Cheers.

GLP is a cool guy, and very helpful when you go to his office hours. In lecture he talks a lot and i frequently find myself not paying attention, which doesn't matter cuz the tests are really easy if you study enough for them.my advice is to go to his office hours, he WILL remeber you and help a lot

Logevall is by far the best professor I have taken a class with at Cornell.  Unfortunately, he will not be teaching next semester because he is being appointed the head of the IR minor.  He is a real softy at heart. Questions are on readings and films, probably doesn't give below a B, and gives extra credit through optional sections.

Fantastic, in depth, knowledgeable lecturer. Really knows a lot about foreign policy esp Vietnam (his book won the Pulitzer). Optional discussion section for extra points. Lots of paperback reading that isn't really required until the prelim/final, where it plays a heavy part. Takes lots of questions in class. Highly recommended, interesting prof
He is a wonderful professor. Very engaging in lecture and always takes questions if something was unclear. The tests are tough but fair. The only caveat is that the TAs are extremely unhelpful.

I've taken a lot of history classes and Logevall is the best lecturer I've ever had. Tests aren't easy, but very manageable. Not a ton of reading either and some of the books he assigned were really interesting. Take this professor.

by far the best lecturer i've had in my three years at cornell. i had no interest in the subject, but his lectures are engaging as he's not simply giving information, but rather telling a great story. only one paper and 2 exams which was nice, but there was quite a bit of reading. i definitely recommend any history majors this professor!

History of early American foreign policy. He's pretty good at lecturing (though his sentences always start out loudly and quickly trail off) and has a funny, quirky personality. But not very inspiring, often runs out of time, and only rarely discusses the readings in class (no sections). Not very good readings at that. Pretty easy. Overall- 2.5/5
Really good professor, always willing to help, leads very interesting and thought-provoking discussions for the history honors seminar.

Great guy, very nice. Really enjoys history a lot, you can tell. Always runs out of time but is so passionate. Get him as your section leader. Nice dude, exams pretty easy. A lot of reading but it's worth it.

Logevall is a nice guy.  Good discussion leader. Class wasn't very heavy in requirements.  My only gripe with him is that he gets through so little information in lecture, making the class end up fairly limited in depth of material covered.
He is very clear and concise...lectures are interesting and well-organized.  He is always willing to meet with students.  Definitely one of the best profs I've had at Cornell!!
Great teacher.  He is clear, concise, and articulate.  He keeps the class interesting (be sure you get him for section).  The reading gets dense at times but is generally manageable.
shelley is very funny as a TA and knows a lot about sociology. Very passionate about the topic and fair grader for essays.

Shelley is one of the best TA I have encountered at Cornell. She helped the professor deliverer some technical contents and is very available and helpful for research and writing projects. The grading was fair and the professor also did a great job clarifying grading criterion.
Xuewen is an amazing TA who knows a lot about the subject and would make herself accessible to students. She also organized interesting class activities for us. Very useful class and would recommend.
the worst TA i have ever had, nice and fair and all but CANNOT teach. an absolute waste of time, resources and effort for everyone involved.

This was such a good FWS to take my first semester of Cornell. Dr. Green cares very much about both the content of the course and his students. He also takes feedback and makes changes to the course based on that. Grading was very clear and based on effort and improvement over the course. He also offered extra assignments for extra credit. 10/10

Dr. Green was such a nice and encouraging professor. Course demanded a decent amount of work, but grades are labor-based and not quality-based. Aka your grade is an actual reflection of how much effort you put in. Chose interesting books and he tried really hard to make the material interesting. Participation matters. Would recommend!

really nice and easygoing, contract grading system so you decide what grade you want and do the amount of work for the grade you want. no technology in class or slides only writes on the whiteboard so hard to focus on what is said a lot of the time

Dr. Bulthuis is an exceptional professor & explains complicated content in a clear, palatable way. He makes you want to learn the material. This course was on the Philosophy of Aquinas--heavy duty stuff--& Dr. B he made it enjoyable and exciting. I was blown away at this course from beginning to end. He wants you to get it & is very approachable.

Bulthuis explains course concepts very clearly and in an engaging way. Even when readings initially seemed incomprehensible, Bulthuis managed to make the material seem simple. I was always excited to go to class (even though it was in the morning!). I am hoping to major in philosophy because I loved his class so much. He is my favorite professor.

Professor Bulthuis was very good at explaining the different topics we covered especially since the assigned readings were sometimes long and difficult to fully grasp. Lectures were interesting and he was usually very accessible during office hours to go over things.

I went to office hours to catch up on classes I missed, and Professor Bulthuis helped me to understand things about philosophy I didn't even know I didn't know. He is the reason I want to be a Philosophy major, after taking his INTRO class. His lectures are phenomenal and engaging. His grading is tough but undeniably fair.

Bulthuis did a good job of explaining the concepts in each unit. There was a decent amount of reading (some weeks easier than others, watch out for Hume) and our TA gave us the option of in-class quizzes or responses (500 words) based on the reading. Exams were fine if you did the reading and studied well. Papers were tedious but fairly easy.

Way more reading than expected.  TA grading often seemed subjective.  I took the course when Prof. Bulthuis just introduced prelims, making it significantly harder to obtain an A or an A-.  A B or B+ is attainable without much effort, but if you want anything higher you will really have to work.

2200 was one of my favorite classes I have taken at Cornell. Not saying it's an easy A by any means, I put a lot of work into this class. The exams are very specific and you have to pay attention in class to get everything out of it. The two papers are graded pretty leniently though, so it is definitely doable. I would definitely recommend!

In my personal experience, I found myself working extremely hard without improving over the semester. I did not find it clear what we were expected to learn for the test despite going over the lectures and the textbook rigorously. The lectures are incredibly dense and boring and the amount of information that we are expected to know is unrealistic.

If you don't have a solid background in the brain, this class will be more on the difficult side because it is a lot to know and it is not always clear what we should know. The tests can be hard and the lectures boring, but they grade the two term papers fairly and somewhat leniently. Going to lecture is very helpful but not completely necessary.

I definitely recommend. He is very intelligent and shares some great information. The 75 minute classes can get boring and he tends to mumble, but hes a really cool guy and knows his stuff! Very approachable too. Exams are fair and he curves if need be.

Very intelligent and approachable. Takes his lab seriously, but always wanted to make sure the RAs were happy.  Research is very interesting. Definitely talk to him if you're interested in his research.

Amanda is a great instructor and is very patient with all her students. Cannot remember a class I looked forward to more than hers. Make sure you are prepared when possible and try not too miss too many miscellaneous points and you should be good!
I feel bad for you if you get stuck with her

So, she doesn't teach at Cornell, she teaches at Seattle U now. Anyway, she was an awesome teacher and I highly recommend her if you can get her at whatever school she goes to next year. she's awesome and is a boundless spring of information in the best way possible.
Best English teacher that I ever had!  Really goes above and beyond and changes your writing for the better!

There was 8 papers, each had a rough draft, peer review, and final. Gives you the questions to the papers ahead of time so you can begin writing as you please. The final is an in class essay that he gives you the questions for. He knows his stuff and can be interesting.

Do the reading and you will do well. Tests can be difficult, but the class is curved in the end. Kyle is very intelligent, helpful, and down to earth. If you have to take Macro, I would take it with him.

Professor Kyle might be the best professor on the Cornell Campus. Lots of impressing experience combined with humor and academical honesty. He´s lectures are 100% easy to follow if you just listen to what he says. Tests are pretty easy and he follows the textbook chapter to chapter so its easy to look stuff up after class. Recommended course!

Kyle is smart and funny. He knows a lot about Econ. However, his lectures have a loose structure, and often ends up glazing over things that aren't in the textbook but are important. EVERYthing is fair game for final, even abstract and trivial things. If you love Econ, go for it, if not, it may be worth waiting someone else.
He's a great teacher and quite funny too. He always answers questions and makes the material seem not too difficult.

Kyle is a great professor. His lectures are always engaging (he makes fun corny jokes too), and he is always willing to take questions. The tests are a bit challenging-but just go to lecture and do the readings and you should be fine.

Teaching a class with nearly 300 people can be difficult, but not for Kyle. He has a booming voice & personality and sort of reminds me of Santa Claus. He makes a lot of stupid economist jokes in lecture to keep people awake. Some are funny. This class is very easy if you just do the readings, which are not long. Section & lecture are optional.

Kyle is a great professor. He is a genuine guy, he is funny in his own self-deprecating way, and he makes it all seem interesting. The test aren't too bad but some of the questions are a little misleading. Overall, take it!

Kyle hands out an agenda at the beginning of every class but rarely sticks with it. Lecture is solely him talking, no Powerpoint, and he can go off topic. In the end he winds up covering the most important things. Keep up with the textbook, do old exams online, and you'll be fine in the class.
Really nice and funny guy. His class isn't easy but he curves. You need to read the textbook to do well, and he requires you to read about 1 chapter for every class.

Prof Kyle is a pretty good lecturer and is clearly enthusiastic about the material. He's willing to help you if you talk to him after class.  He could sometimes be unclear and hard to understand, and he got off-topic a little too much.  He's really into real-world applications of concepts, which makes the class somewhat challenging.

I really couldn't ask for a better professor. He doesn't use notes or powerpoints when lecturing - doesn't need 'em. Regularly makes jokes, most of which aren't funny, but they keep you awake which is more important. He interacts with the class, not doing any Socratic method BS, but just asking easy questions to keep you active. Just awesome!
Tries to keep you engaged during lectures. My TA was probably the best one available and that helped a LOT. Do the past prelims and finals, they prep you quite well. The grading is fairly easy.

Prof Kyle does an excellent job of incorporating current events and issues into his lectures and exams. It makes the class both more interesting and relevant. I would recommend him to anyone. If you study and do the problem sets, you'll be fine.
Fairly funny and does a good job appealing to a lot of people. The lectures can drag a bit but the tests are very easy.
THe lectures are very clear and interesting. The problem sets have nothing to do with the prelims. He does not give out A+s unless u get 100%. Pretty mad at him ~

Professor Kyle is a professor who is very interested in his subject and this is conveyed in his teaching.  I had never taken economics before but was surprised at how clear and relevant professor Kyle's lecture were.  The average is a B or B+, which is easy to obtain if you pay attention in lecture and go to section.  Section answer hw questions.

easy class... just make sure you read the textbook. you can get away with not going to lectures but make sure you go to sections-- the TA's actually cover useful material that will be on the exams. one final paper that is pretty easy
ECON 102: This class is listed as 3 credits, but don't kid yourself; if you do all of the reading and all of the BUSYWORK problem sets on Aplia, it should be worth much more than 3.

Very interesting class, especially if you know nothing about ECON coming in to it.  Lectures not too structured, but prof very knowledgeable about material and always excited about teaching it.  Sections review material and do actual computation.  Great course no matter what major.
COTA wasn't as bad as others say.  Take it if you can, no final, but a paper, which was very easy.  Tests not too hard.

His lectures are not quite as structured as Wissink.  I wished the information was presented in a more definitive nature. The tests were okay. Not easy; but not hard.   Your TA helps you to understand the information alot, so choose a good section.
Take 102 from him. His lectures are okay, and you will learn from him. He is a very nice guy and really helpful. So long as you pay attention and do the readings, this class is very easy.

I am less inclined to think highly of Prof. Kyle, simply because his head TA cannnot get her act together. He should have been more thoughtful in his selection, she brings the whole cidate.ourse down, is unclear, and can't get anything right in her first email. Kyle should have used his Harvard education to pick a more suitable cand
TAKE THIS COURSE!!!!

Take 102 from him if he's teaching it.  Very clear lecturer and usually has funny jokes.  Problem sets may not correspond that well to the book or lectures but they're still fairly easy to figure out.
Very good at lecturing.  Very clear, uses diagrams well.  Not great in office hours.  Exams are medium, but final paper takes a while.  Good class overall.
Willing to help at any second, professor Kyle is perhaps one of the best econ prof's in the dept. I'd strongly recommend his 102 over any other.

Much more interesting lectures than I got in Econ 102.  Lectures explain the readings, so go to class (it'll help your grade a lot).  Fair tests, but not exceptionally easy. TA's vary, so section can be very helpful or awful
Kyle is pretty much what you would expect from a Harvard Ph.D. economist-- mustache, gray hair, really knows what he's doing; great lecturer.
easy tests, easy (weekly) problem sets, but they don't really correspond with what's being taught in class.  seems like a nice guy who tries hard to be funny, and sometimes can be.  knows his stuff
Very straightforward lectures. Find a good TA and go to their sections. Problem sets don't really correspond to the material. Fair, predictable tests.
A very distinguished-looking prof.  Much better than Wissink- good lectures, easy problem sets, and fair prelims
love that mustache

This class is rough, BUT, if you really put in the work and grind office hours, you can get by pretty well without attending lectures. This was 100% the most time consuming class I took this semester, but if you just attend labs and OH (can't stress how important this is) you can end up with an A+.
not a fan of him, unfortunately he teaches nearly every single info sci class at cornell

I have had a horrible experience with Kyle Harms. He has been my professor for 2 semesters, for info 1300 (got an A) & info 2300 right now. He is abrasive, condescending, unapproachable, and overall I cannot stress enough how horrific it has been. There are truly not enough words in the English language to express how terrible my experience was.

Had him for 1300 last semester, now taking 2300. There is a lot of project work for both classes but if you go to class, pay attention, and try, its an easy A. Courses are designed so well for beginner programmers. I do not understand all the hate!!
This professor is terrible. I will definitely not take his course again.

Generally reasonable and tries his best for students to understand how to code. Sometimes felt like I was being spoon-fed information. Lots of tedious homework. Energetic, which may be hard to endure for an 8:40am class.

Having the class at 8:40 am every Monday and Wednesday is torture. Not to mention his course style of taking attendance at this point in the day. Assignments were fine and doable but very tedious. The design journeys I get the point but it gets a little too much when done multiple times.

If you take a "Web Design Course" taught by Kyle Harms, just know that you are in for a rough semester. Harms is super un-approachable and rude when you go ask him for help.  He is snarky and pretentious. I do not recommend!

If you take a "Web Design Course" taught by Kyle Harms, you will not be learning "Web Design". Rather, you will be learning "Kyle Harms Web Design". Prof Harms is super un-approachable, and designs his rubrics to grade deflate. If you ask for help, he is snarky and pretentious. He is not accommodating at all; yet he makes mistakes constantly.

Kyle Harms is a fine lecturer, but he is genuinely abrasive and needlessly rude one-on-one. Harms scolded me during his office hours for "wasting [his] time" and that I "was not a priority." No professor of mine has ever come close to his level of unpleasantness. Yes, the class was informative, but the assignments were needlessly tedious.

his classes are project based, so how much effort you put into the projects sort of determines how much time you'll be spending on top of basic website functionality reqs. required participation helps you not fall behind in class, and his teaching style really emphasizes learning objectives and good practices which is pretty valuable imo

Great professor that knows the material he is teaching very well. He wants to make sure we develop good practices, even if the work seems a bit tedious. Listens to student feedback and adjusts accordingly, providing lots of leniency. What he expects is pretty straightforward, you just have to read/watch lectures and project write-up well.
Would recommend, really clear grading criteria

Man was bad, but man has CHANGED.Was struggling in INFO1300 but this time 2300 he has obviously improved so much. He genuinely cared about the students and adjusted the courses based on the feedback. The final project was heavy but he was very understanding. Keep it up KYLE!!

Took his class two years ago and this semester again. I genuinely admire how much he has improved and how willing he is to take in feedback. Never thought I would say this but he truly cares about his students and anyone who doesn't see this should give it time. 10/10 KYLE.

This was one of the classes in that I spent most of my time working on the projects: it was challenging and time-consuming, but after all, I learned a lot and had qualified content for my portfolio. I could see that the professor was trying a lot to figure out how to communicate with the students and organize the class content.

He's one of those people you can tell is not only a terrible instructor but also a person you wouldn't want to ever be friends with. Stuck up, condescending, rude, overly critical.

The class concept is simple but he drags things out so painfully, teaches them in weird roundabout ways and just makes everything harder than it needs to be.
man was bad in the past, but MAN IS IMPROVING. This 5 is a recognition for being more accommodating this semester, kyle i know you have been trying and i appreciate it!

If there's a class that significantly decreased my will to keep on going, it'd be INFO 1300. The amount of repetitive work that Harms expects of you, which simply doesn't facilitate learning, no matter what Harms might repeat. An absolute waste of time and a horrendous introduction into the information science major.
professor is quite condescending and doesn't listen to anyone but himself

Both professors seem genuinely enthusiastic for this class, but they talk to students as if they are children, and assign an insane amount of busywork graded only for completion. Mandatory 9 am lectures make this class even worse.

A 3-credit course with a 12-credit workload. A project milestone once a week which takes at least 12 hours to complete and mandatory attendance at 9 am with WATERMARKED attendance sheet. Coding was not hard, but it only consisted 35% of the class. The rest was basically bullshting the design. It was the biggest source of pain for me that semester.

At surface, Kyle Harms seems like a nice approachable guy based off the way he teaches his lectures. However, when you go to ask a question after lectures, he gives you bitter looks and answers. He also does not care for his students. He is not willing to accommodate regardless of your situation; he only wants to do whats convenient for himself.

Grading is literally ridiculous. They are unclear w/ expectations and untimely w/ grading, and take off so many points for the smallest things. And the workload is astronomical as someone mentioned; all my friends know how this class consumed my life this semester. Do not take unless your life depended on it

Truly the worst professor I've ever had, I can't fit everything in this word limit. 

Workload: Unbelievably tedious, repetitive, useless

Harms: SO inflexible, annoying, does not care for students. I asked for an extension bc I had to literally fly home for my grandma's funeral, but he just made me use half my slip days. 

DO NOT take this class

Do not take INFO 1300 unless you are required to. Lectures are very engaging and slow paced, I can actually pay attention at the crack of dawn. However workload is astronomical. Grading is disorganized and "gotchas" that cause students to lose points are NOT made clear. Students are not told how they are graded and don't receive timely feedback

Course material itself is incredibly easy but the professor has made this the most painfully tedious course. I would rather listen to nails on a chalkboard. Professor is also very condescending and teaches as if you were in primary school. If you want to design websites, self-learn the material in several weeks and avoid the mind-numbing busy work

You can learn the semester-long material in the span of 2-3 weeks using the Odin Project. He literally makes you write bullshit and then grades you for not having written good bullshit.

This is a coding class for web design but the actual web design part is like 10% of time invested. The rest is following his stupid curriculum made for 1st graders

This was the hardest class I've ever taken at Cornell. The workload during the first two assignments was somewhat manageable -- 20 hours/week, but the workload during the last assignment was around 40 hours/week. The class feels like it should be at least 6-7 credits, and is insane for 3 credits. 

NEVER TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

The main issue: it's a 3 credit class that should be an 8 - from weekly lab homeworks, prelecture assignments, lecture assignments, weekly project deadlines and weekly lab attendance grades. It's a lot. I would recommend not taking this to learn sql/web dev when you could just learn it on your own. He's extremely strict on grading for no reason.
too much work, not considerate at all
Honestly just an all-around bad professor. The assignments in the class are extremely boring and require a lot of repetitive work. I would never take another class with him.

I'm actually surprised by the negative reviews. The writeups could be tedious, but they did help me learn to justify my designs and plan my projects. Professor Harms was a great lecturer and his project instructions were always detailed and clear. Wouldn't recommend if you already know web dev and you're not interested in learning about design.

Kyle seems to get more flack than he deserves. Having been in 3 of his classes, it's clear that he wants the best for his students. He puts time/care into planning lectures, answering questions (only getting "mean" when repeatedly asked the same thing), and giving feedback. As long as you're attentive and follow instructions, you'll do just fine.

Would be very tough if you have no prior experience. Harsh grader and takes away lots of points for very small and minor details. I liked the way his lectures were set up but he was very hard to communicate with and every conversation seemed like he felt I was wasting his time. The topic was exciting but he took the fun out of the subject

I'm a non-major, and took this class thinking it would be a fun introduction to web design. I was wrong. The majority of projects are spent on write-ups, and they feel like a waste of time. Professor Harms is extremely passive aggressive and condescending, and hides "gotchas" in projects to make you lose points. Do not take if you don't need to.

This class is unbelievably easy, I think you would have to try to get a grade lower than an A. However, Kyle absolutely ruins this class, he has a terrible condescending attitude, and this class one of the worst at Cornell. I genuinely think he is one of the worst professors at Cornell, and i would NEVER even consider taking one of his classes.

I had Professor Harms for INFO 1300, 2300, and I'll have him next semester for 4340. He's a really nice guy, and he genuinely cares for his students- it was obvious, even over Zoom. There was a lot of tedious work in his web design courses, but all the complaints about that probably come from coders who've never had to justify their designs.
Redundant easy work. I hate the way he talks to students, sounds like dripping in passive aggression.

The majority of my friend group dropped this class, and I should have followed suit. The write-ups for the projects are genuinely unbearable and seem infinite. The course is listed as a web design course, but it feels like an essay-based class. Good luck getting help on Ed, where Prof. Harms response with the vaguest answers on earth. Do not take.

Kyle Harms' class has been my worst experience at Cornell by far. This introductory level course is unreasonable hard, with multiple extremely difficult deadlines each week. The amount of stress that this class causes is unbearable. Because of this class, I have started to attend mental health counseling and therapy sessions almost every day.

There are 4-5 deadlines each week with an insane amount of writing and he's unreasonable and inflexible with grading and deadlines. It's my second year pursuing the InfoSci major but I'm convinced to drop my major because of this man.

Without a doubt, this is by far the worst class and professor I've ever had at Cornell. He treats his students like children (not in a caring way but a patronizing one) and acts like a toddler whenever you try to talk to him. He may appear nice and act as if he cares but he's inflexible and will forsake your wellbeing for his own. Be warned.

This class is abysmal, honestly one of the worst classes I have taken at Cornell. While it may seem like a web dev class at first, the class is much more focused on unnecessary, busy-work writing than actual coding. For the first project in this class, I coded around 1-200 lines, but had to write over 3000 words to describe my "design process."

I was excited to learn about web dev at an esteemed institution such as Cornell. Kyle deserves no esteem, nor is his class a worthwhile use of time, unless you like doing arts and crafts, since all projects incorporate endless design drawing portions, which kill both trees and students' sanity. I also wrote more in this class than I did for my FWS.
Only responds to questions with "Yes" on Ed. For example, "Do I use this method or this other method" "Yes".

Honestly, one of the best professors at Cornell. He takes our mental health and well-being very seriously and has been one of the only professors this semester to be accommodating during this pandemic. Also, the lectures, labs, and projects are pretty straightforward and easy to implement if you pay attention.

should be a garbage easy class, and it is, but harms adds all this extra junk with the design journeys and user testing. content is easy but every single task is wrapped around a convoluted menial thing like interviewing users among other garbage that makes this class and its assignments unbearable
ONE MORE THE MOST CHEERING PROFESSORS I HAVE EVER MET! REALLY SAVE ME THROUGH THE CLASSES UNDER COVID TIME!
Fun projects! Kyle does care about students' success and offers a loooot of help if you request for them in class. He tried to make his class a warm community.
One of the best lecturers at Cornell. Lectures were straight forward and I enjoyed the projects as well.

I've taken INFO 1300, 2300, and 4340 with Kyle. He is extremely knowledgable, and is very dedicated to making sure his students learn the material. This dedication informs all of his course policies and teaching methods  but as a consequence he is strict with the rules. Follow his rules to the letter and you will do well and learn a lot.
Kyle is an easy professor grading-wise, which is great. Despite this, the class holds your hand way too much. Design journeys are brutal. Easy A though.

Kyle cares profoundly about making sure his students understand the material fully. He is always very energetic considering it was a morning lecture and you have 4 unexcused absences to use throughout the semester to miss lecture. The grading criteria was very clear, thus making it easy to do well in his class.

Honestly, I really enjoy Professor Harms' lectures and try to attend as often as possible, even though it's an early class. He uses a lot of graphics/models when describing certain concepts, which really helps me as a visual learner. It is very clear that he is an expert in his field and he does a really good job breaking down the material.

INFO 2300 is a very easy class, but the thing is that Harms is just really not understanding of any extraneous situation and is really inflexible. I do not recommend this class if you have some kind of coding experience and it's not required because the web design contents covered in INFO 2300 can easily be learned over just one or two days.

Kyle is a very motivated and focused professor, it's clear that he cares a lot about his students learning the skills behind the material that he teaches. However, as a result, there ends up being a large amount of work with strict grading guidelines with minimal leeway. But if you stay on top of everything you will gain practical skills.

He is a stickler about attendance (takes it every lecture) which sucks for an early morning class, but you can tell he wants us to actually learn the material he teaches. The projects are straightforward and you really get a good grasp of the material. Plus he was super understanding of a personal situation of mine and that meant a lot to me.

Professor Kyle Harms did really well for his first semester at Cornell. He really spends time explaining concepts to students and does not skip over steps. He did a lot of live demos at class. He also had the class do engaging activities. Maybe use clickers next semester for attendance.

Easy easy class. Projects can be frustratingly tedious but not difficult. Final exam tested basics and nothing more. Attendance is taken at both lecture and section but you're given a good amount of slip days. Harms is good at explaining things and very willing to help. Class meant for beginners so it can feel a bit slow if you have cs experience.
He has the strictest attendance policy, but you shouldn't miss class. Great at explaining things further. Loves people who ask questions and are generally interested in the topic.

Congratulations! If you're reading this, it's because you won Kyle for your instructor. Kyle is great at answering all questions, as in-depth as you want, and super clear and easy. Kyle could write his own textbook "Chemistry for People Who Aren't Good at Chemistry". He is super clear and cheerful. Prepare to work SUPER hard, though! He expects it!

This class covers incredibly difficult content but there are a lot of resources available. OH not mandatory but I don't think I would've passed the class without attending every week. Lectures move incredibly quickly so be ready - I don't recommend ever skipping lecture as not a lot of materials are posted online, it would be hard to catch up

Although his lectures were great and explained the matter in a clear way, he can be dismissive of questions in office hours. There were however a lot of TAs that could also be used, so you just have to find one you like. The labs were slow and annoying.

He's very knowledgeable and funny at times. However, grading is tough and those PSETs are brutal. While lectures and office hours are technically not mandatory, they are almost pseudo-mandatory because he doesn't really post everything he teaches and PSETs are borderline impossible without them.

He was very understanding of the struggle of this year for students and curved the class to a B+ instead of a B for us. Tried to make zoom as fun as he could and dressed up with his TA every so often. Material is pretty standard chem matieral but was a lot of material bc gen chem. Taught the material pretty well too.
You have to work for a good grade
Enthusiastic about material, but he teaches really fast and his test questions are lengthy and require quick critical thinking... definitely recommend taking 1070 if it is available.

Kyle is a funny man, but gives off an aura commanding respect. Clearly very intelligent, and likes to throw in memes and references to lectures. Course is very structured and rigid, in both grading and material. You *can* skip class if need be, but material makes much more sense in lecture than in book. Labs suck, but not terrible. Beware prelims!!

Good professor who really tries to keep students engaged in class but moves very quickly in lecture and it's hard to keep up/learn the material from lecture alone. Class/tests are graded fairly. Class takes a lot of time and has a lot of work.

You can tell he loves teaching chemistry to students and tries to make lecture as entertaining as possible. He always tries to joke around during lecture and actually wants you to learn the material, rather than memorize it. His office hours are great too and he really takes the time to teach you a concept you're really confused about.

Professor Lancaster is not only an engaging lecturer, but he is also incredibly knowledgeable and is truly concerned with helping students find an interest in chemistry. His jokes are genuinely funny and lighten up the lectures on days when the topic feels like its over your head. I would definitely recommend this class for a rewarding challenge.
He's the best. He loves to blow things up and is the best and most entertaining teacher! His explosive personality really makes the class interesting and bearable. 15/10 would recommend.
Tried to be funny/entertaining
funny guy, but hard to keep up with his lectures. If you have some chemistry background you should be fine for the first half of the course. no practice prelims :(
Dr. Lancaster is absolutely incredible. Great lecturer. Easy to learn from. Reasonable prelims and labs. Class was moderately difficult, easy A if you put in the work and time.

Dr. Lancaster is, hands down, one of the best professors you'll ever have in any Chemistry class at Cornell. He is always clear and explains complicated concepts in a simple way while managing to entertain the class at the same time. Always willing to help students in office hours and was a DJ at one point in time.

Brilliant professor who plans his classes amazingly. Everything in his lecture is important and the textbook is only helpful for practice problems. The best way to study is to do the book's practice problems right before the exam and review notes. Amazing guy.

Kyle's brilliant, and has the ability to make difficult concepts seem clearer; the times he had a sub because he was off giving lectures elsewhere, everyone just wanted him back. His test questions aren't that difficult, but sometimes, there's just too many. The curve will then either save or ruin you. Definitely recommend 1007 along with this.

Although I did not enjoy Dr. Lancaster's course due to my dislike for chemistry, his enthusiasm for his field and his ability to explain concepts made the class bearable. He's a great professor, and although his class may be tough, if you work you can learn.

Lancaster is truly amazed by chemistry and wants each of his students to feel that same passion. He's a clear lecturer and hilarious. His test are fair but challenging, and make for good opportunity to score above the mean. Take CHEM1070 & you won't regret it (will definitely help your grade). Would definitely take another class taught by him.

Dr. Lancaster truly cares about his students and wants them to care about chemistry. Tests are difficult but fair. In lecture, he is clear in his explanations and writes important notes on the board. I recommend going to office hours to get help (not just before tests). He is inspirational and can make complex concepts of chemistry fun. Great guy.

Such a funny, passionate, and overall great professor! He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed and enjoy chemistry. If you've taken chemistry before, this class shouldn't be that bad for you, but you will definitely have to put in the work.

Dr. Lancaster is an amazing professor who makes fair tests and really makes a subject I thought was boring much, much more interesting. I didn't take AP Chemistry but would recommend taking CHEM1070 in addition to this class to help keep up with the material.

Kyle is an INCREDIBLE professor-- hilarious, dynamic, and brilliant all around. I went into the class with really weak foundations in chemistry, but Kyle is such a clear explainer and has such an effective teaching style (writing all essential notes on the blackboard) that it's manageable to keep up and do well if you put in the time.

Lancaster was a great lecturer! His tests were completely fair, and if you took AP chemistry in high school and understood it, then you'll do pretty well in his class. Can't speak for those who didn't.

Great professor: teaches well, knows what he's talking about, personable guy. Go to office hours at least once to get to know him (and perhaps more than once because it's not an easy class!). You should go to class because he teaches the material well and it's hard to get it from the book. Speaking of the book, no need to buy anything but Sapling.
Great teacher. Talks so fast and super easy to get behind.

Even though attendance isn't mandatory, you really won't be able to get the material anywhere else. He's pretty young (33?) so he still has enthusiasm for the subject and he's able to convey that enthusiasm in lectures. While some of the material is hard (prelim 2 average was 89/150), he knows it's hard and curves the class accordingly.

Lancaster is an all around great guy, in and out of the classroom. You can definitely tell that he genuinely wants his students to be interested in chemistry. However, just because he wants everyone to love chemistry as much as he does, does not mean that the class is easy. The average grade on prelim 2 was around a 55% so don't expect an easy A.
Exams are difficult but plenty of help is available if you are willing to take it. Lancaster keeps lectures interesting for the most part and brings humor to what can be a more dull subject.

Prof Lancaster definitely expects a lot, but gives a lot too. Chemistry has never been my strongest subject but he made me love it and was always available for extra help. His lectures are hilarious and he knows how to relate to students. Definitely a gem.
Probably one of the best professors that you will ever have at Cornell. He makes difficult topics so easy to understand!
Lecture was actually enjoyable with Lancaster. Made chemistry accessible. Also in Forbes Top 30 under 30, so cool guy.
Really great teacher. You can tell he actually cares about and enjoys teaching. Exams are tough but fair.

Professor Lancaster is simply brilliant. He is one of those professors that truly and absolutely has a passion for his subject and has a blast teaching it. Students look forward to his lectures and truly cares about them, always accessible to ask questions. I would recommend anyone reading this to take a course taught by him. You won't regret it

Super knowledgable guy, very engaging lectures. Homework assignments are long and challenging but very well-written and overall enjoyable. Available both during stated office hours and at other times, and by email.
take his fws!! great teacher, very fair grader and very approachable. Always willing to help and gives great feedback

Kyle Shen, while an accomplished researcher, can show immaturity when students ask him for help in his class. He has told students they should drop the physics major because they asked a question he didn't like. His lectures are clear and you will learn a lot, but he could be a lot more accommodating in helping students in his course.

Extremely insightful and entertaining lectures and problem sets. Material can be challenging but the class is structured and graded in a way that doesn't punish students for taking the harder option. I'd recommend sticking around for an extra 10 minutes after lecture to listen in on Prof. Shen's Q&A which cover many subtleties of the subject

Professor Shen's class was probably the most engaging online class I took. His explanations were clear and understandable. Expect to spend considerable time trying the psets and going to office hours for help on them. He is also considerate if you have any issues with the course and is willing to help you achieve a good grade in the class.

Shen is a great and engaging professor perhaps the best I've had yet. The content is HARD (coming from a literal physics major) but put in the work and you will get a lot out of it. The workload is on the heavier end for time but it does really enrich the understanding of the material. Clear he cares about students too.

Shen was quite a figure on the tongue of people in the class. Many things and many stories you will hear of him and people will fantasize about him.... The class is hard and might be a shock to many of the students (including me) coming into a physics degree. But you get out of the class with a lot of new skills that is necessary for any physicist.

Extremely hard class, but Professor Shen definitely made it bearable. He offered a lot of options for you to get help when needed. Lectures were very clear and precise, and he clearly had the best grasp of how to do a zoom lecture out of all my professors. If you're a phys major, def take the class. If not, probably want to stay away.
A rude awakening to the life of the physics major. Work very hard and go to every office hours and you might be able to pull an A-. He's so cool and one of the best teachers I've ever had
He is a very understanding professor and very accessible, is willing to help you and accommodate as much as he can. Very good lecturer. Clearly cares about his students.

The best lecturer I've ever had. I already enjoyed physics but I've never been challenged to understand it more than in Shen's lectures and in the homework he gave. You really shouldn't miss lectures, the notes get posted but you miss LOTS of detail. Plus he makes them fun to be in.

Probably the best teacher I have ever had, although I am only a freshman. Not only does he know what he's talking about, he also is able to convey it in a clear way. If you're taking 1116, do it in the fall so you can have Shen.
His class is really hard, but he is a great teacher. Very enthusiastic. He is much more interesting if you talk to him outside of class, he gets kind of nervous in lectures. He is soo attractive.

Great professor, really makes lectures lucid. The homeworks are leagues more difficult than the lectures however, which can be frustrating. Also, lectures are carried out in a group fashion; students are assigned to random groups of 3-4 and take in-lecture quizzes together.

Very good professor. For 2213, he does a great job in dealing with huge lectures and a huge amount of material. He makes lectures interesting. The only thing is the lecture material is hard to relate to the hw and discussion stuff. Get the textbook even if it is not required. It's hard to know what goes with what between the lec, dis, and hw.
He records video lectures before class, and uses learning catalytic in lecture and sections. Videos are very clear and helpful. He's very enthusiastic about physics .
great class

Prof. Shen is a great professor. First physics class I have ever taken, and he sparked my interest in it. The class was not even close to easy if you have never taken AP physics, but he makes it worth it. So glad I took his course.
Excellent professor.
Professor Shen is a boss.

Amazing prof. He is extremely helpful, clear, and possesses a frightening amount of knowledge about physics. If you take his class be prepared to work your ass off. The problem sets are very tough: they require exceptional ingenuity and conceptual skills. This class makes you earn every point of your grade. Every point earned, however, will feel amazing. If you dare take this honors level course at an ivy league noted for its tough curriculum, by all means go for this one. Just be prepared.

This professor is AMAZING. He is extremely clear, has a brilliant sense of humor, and is very caring. He makes the course very very intellectually rigorous however.. but you learn so much about physics that the hard work pays off. One of the best professors at Cornell, without a doubt!!
BEST physics teacher ever! He really makes you think, and also makes you love physics! Awesome guy.
I love professor shen!!!

Awesome teacher.. very very helpful and great lecturer.. but this class is VERY hard. the class goes into very advanced math covered in sophomore level classes. ONLY take if youre an AEP or Physics major.
Best. Physics. Prof. Ever.

AWESOME teacher and amazing person as well. Very interesting, and goes out of the way to help students (ie - posts Pset solutions / lecture notes online). Very tough course though. Prepare to work hard.
absolutely amazing - very very clear and organized. very very cool / awesome guy as well. class is VERY tough - be prepared to work hard.
great prof, really shows that he cares.  Does a great job making the class organized
GREAT professor. Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable, very willing to help.

Quizzes, homework and exams will really make you think. Hard. This course is not an easy one, but Kyle Shen attempts to make it as enjoyable as humanly possible. A man with great teaching skills and an even greater character.

Awesome professor. Really helpful. Goes out of his way to make sure you understand the material. Always answers e-mails quickly, knows everyone's names, has field trips, gives out candy. Class is very difficult. Exams are awful and the problem sets will take over your life. take this class if you dare

Amazing professor, one of the best here at Cornell. Works hard, cares about students, and always does more than anyone would demand from a professor. Lectures were amazing, entertaining and never really dull.

An absolutely wonderful professor and a great introduction to college level physics. If, like me, you have never had a serious physics course, Shen will make you work. But he is a great teacher and truly cares about his students. He is definitely one of the greatest professors at Cornell.

Kyle Shen is a great professor!  His lectures are clear and prepared.  He cares alot about the class and will go the extra mile to make sure everyone is happy.  Only downside is his prelims and final are VERY hard.  I enjoyed this class very much

Kyle Shen was an awesome professor. He was a very enthusiastic teacher and eager to help. His quizzes were sometimes hard and tricky, but they helped us learn the material for the prelims. He really went beyond the call of duty in making extra handouts and example problems. Plus, Kyle is a genius and a rock star too!

Kyle Shen is an amazing professor!!  He puts so much of himself into helping his students because he really cares and wants us to learn.  He explains things very clearly, thereby helping us actually make sense of physics in the real world.  Highly recommended.  :)
You had to study a lot and had daily homework but the course was very easy if you praticed a lot.

Underrated. She is a very nice person, and her lectures are overall structured and organized. The proofs in the lectures may be a bit overwhelming at times, but they are good knowledge for you. Her exams are very reasonable with 1 easy 1 medium 1 hard question and the hard question has easy subparts. I'd say it's worth it to take her course.

This Professor is teaching Stochastic Calculus for Financial Engineering I and II back and forth since the last 10 years, but when she teaches it looks like a Kindergarten kid has been given to teach the course. Very unprofessional Professor, does weird things in the class, as a result only 6 students took Stochastic II , ruining students career

Minca is weird. She is super inconsistent/irrational in her behavior, is ok research wise. She sits on your head (metaphorically speaking). I wont recommend her for Phd. You wont learn that much or go anywhere.

I have never worked so hard to still get a grade that wasn't great. All the work has to be done by yourself, and you essentially read an entire textbook. He also talks incredibly slowly, so I always had his videos on at least 1.5 speed to make it feel normal.

Insanely tough. This class broke me, and I definitely bled a little... Exams waaay harder than practice prelims, and curve is competitive (if there is a curve). Each exam is a puzzel with all sorts of unexpected twists, memorizing provides tools to solve them. Be good at taking exams. If you can think beyond the objectives, you will go far kid.

Professor Blankenship is a great teacher. Biochem is difficult, but there are tons of office hours staffed by multiple TAs. Make sure you thoroughly answer the objectives for each unit by reading the textbook, watching the review videos, and talking over the objectives with a TA. If you do this, you are bound to get a decent grade.

Jim is a nice guy, but his actual tests were 5x harder than the practice tests(actual tests from previous years). It could also be that this course was completely online this semester due to COVID. During the semesters where this class is offered in-person, the class is usually fine. Stay clear of this class until in-person instruction resumes.

This course is great, and the material is very interesting and applicable. The auto-tutorial format is well suited because biochem in general is memorization heavy. Jim is available to answer questions, and he has a great teaching team to help out. His review sessions are great too, and he's a sweet person who loves teaching!
He is very dedicated to all students. Exercises tough love.

Auto tutorial classes substitute genuine educators for student laborers, bulk memorization, and arbitrary weekly assessments. Any student that says that they enjoy this kind of pseudo-learning must, in fact, detest learning and instead be enjoying the mindless parroting of uncontextualized information. BIOMG 3300 is definetly not worth your time
Really enjoyed 3300; one of my favorite courses at Cornell

Makes mud as clear as water. Excellent professor! His review sessions are short and sweet. Material can seem a little heavy, but is actually not that bad, especially with all the tons of help he and his assistants offer. Always wandering the study center asking if students need help with material, and asks for feedback on quizzes and tests.
Awesome class! Jim is really cool.
BEST CLASS I loved biochemistry, and I loved his teaching method. He knows what he's talking about, and wants you to learn!

Doing well on the weekly quizzes will take up hours each week.  However, studying for quizzes makes studying for prelims relatively  easy and the material you learn in this class come back again and again in many other science classes and especially the MCAT.  I've learned more in this class than any other at Cornell, but be prepared to work for it

Autotutorial biochem was very difficult in terms of material that you must learn.  However, there are always TAs on staff to help you out during the day.  Prof. Blankenship gives optional lectures, which can be helpful.  He was one of my favorite lecturers, which really says something, since this was an autotutorial course.

took this molecular cell bio. class during the summer during the 6 week session. if you can, take it! covering something as deep as cell bio in 6 weeks means at least 25+ hours of work per week for each of the 6 weeks, but if you keep up, you will be rewarded with a wealth of knowledge. Also, there were only 4 people in the class- amazing.

This is a hard course heavy on information. Yet, Jim made it one of the most fair, interesting, and rewarding classes I have taken at Cornell. I did not enjoy "hard" science until I took this class. Key to success is simple: study the objectives (exactly what is on prelims.)It's unfortunate Jim doesn't teach a lecture class, he would be brilliant.

Autotutorial biochemistry is no cakewalk, but Jim outlines exactly what he wants you to know in the course packet.  If you study those objectives and know them by heart, you'll do well.  Unlike orgo, you can actually get a good grade if you put in lots of effort.
The autotutorial class is so absurdly hard I bled a little. I still enjoyed the material and learned a lot. The prof constructed a really solid challenging class.

You will remember this class for your entire life. Excellent auto-tutorial course. The optional "review" sessions led by Jim are good refreshers for exams or before Unit tests. Workload=life consuming. Talk to TAs in the center and clear questions up ASAP. Jim is always in the center helping TAs with unit test, grading, tutoring.

Best autotutorial class at Cornell. Possibly best Biology class. Jim is clear and organized and WANTS YOU TO DO WELL. Class is organized around this basic motive, so oral tests are not graded, written tests are fair, and prelims are very fair too! No complaints. The material was really interesting too. Workload not too bad.

Like with most auto classes, what you get out is directly correlated to how much time and effort you put into it - you can get a lot of out this class by learning the material thoroughly. Didn't  have a lot of contact with the prof, but his review sessions were great and he seemed accessible and helpful. Actually one of my favorite classes here.
This class has a huuuuuuuuuuuuuuuge workload, but in the end you learn alot and it's pretty interesting.  The prof was helpful and nice.

In BioBm330, I didnt have too much contact with Jim. The class itself was very intense and rigorous. You dont have to wake up for lecture and you can skip material you already know, but reading text book alone can be depressing sometimes. You dont have to read the text book, just *memorize* the objectives, good way to develop study habits.

He's an ok guy, personally though, I thought he was sorta condescending to certain students at times- so for that I think the guy is a bit of an ass.  I'm guessing all these great reviews he's getting are from his "favorite" students.  Review sessions were helpful though, the test were hard but if you studied you would do fine.
He should be a professor teaching a Real class.

Hard class (seriously, whatever amount of time you expect it to take multiply by two and add a few hours).  Great professor, one of the best I've had.  Go to the review sessions!  They are tedious but very helpful.  Don't do what I did and take orgo at the same time.

Jim Rocks!  He is hands down one of the best professors at Cornell if not THE best!  I finished this class hoping he would teach another class.  If you have any interest in biochemistry whatsoever, this class is a must!!! You won't regret it!
Awesome guy.  Genuinely wants you to learn and understand the material.  Very approachable and always willing to listen.

This class takes a lot of time, but is worthwhile in the end.  Between the study guide, the TA's, review sessions and the prof, lectures are not needed and although i was very opposed to autotutorial classes before taking this one, i would recommend it over the lecture class.

This class isn't just about memorizing, esp. the last unit about metabolism.  Memorizing is essential but will only get you so far; you have to integrate your knowledge.  That said, Jim is a great teacher and very helpful.  I would recommend this course to anyone.
Great professor. Too bad he is teaching an auto-tutorial course.
Jim is a great teacher and is fair to all of the students. (Some other person thought he only helped pre-meds). He is a wealth of knowledge and will help anyone who seeks him out.
the class is autotutorial. And yet it has some of the best lectures I've attended at Cornell. Odd don't you think?

A really nice guy, even though the course is hard, he doesn't mind helping you out, although he will refer you to the undergrad TA's for help first. I think he prefers dealing with the administrative end. his help sessions are VERY thorough re: the tests.

Definitely don't be narrowminded.  It's not hard material, but it's definitely a lot of work and a lot of memorization.  The review sessions headed by Blankenship are extremely helpful as long as you don't get distracted by his personality.
Jim is an awesome guy and a great teacher. He makes the material easy to understand..it's a shame that such a good teacher is heading an auto-tutorial course
Jim is the Best!!!
No Comments
this class tests one thing - ability to memorize.  any form of reasoning is highly discouraged.  i did learn a lot though.
No Comments

Jim was only helpful to pre-meds.  He made it very difficult for me to get extra help with him, and reserved his hours for his favorite students.  This is BY FAR the worst class I have ever taken at Cornell. Even Genetics is a cake-walk compared to this.
No Comments
No Comments
This guy's not only very knowledgable, but extremely nice in person. A word of general advice, though: don't be narrow-minded.
auto-tutorial biochem is a lot of work...stay on track and ask the ta's for help
My favorite professor at Cornell! Professor Dai really cares about students and gives amazing lectures.
Professor Dai really cares about students and his lectures are extremely clear. The assignments are sometimes difficult but all the TAs are super helpful.
Prof. Dai is one of the best professors during my college life.

The worst professor I have ever experienced in my life. The class was very disorganized and communication with Professor Dai and the course staff was difficult. This made it very confusing to know what I was expected to do. Also, he was pretty difficult to understand and rarely took questions in class. Avoid taking any class with him at all costs.

Impossible to understand what he's saying at first but it gets better over time. Cares about students even if it doesn't seem like it during lecture. Prof Dai really wants everyone to understand the material and will do his best during lecture to clear up any misconceptions if you ask questions.
Cannot understand anything he is trying to explain ever. Not great learning experience
His lectures builds on course materials extermely well. Don't miss out his lectures so that you get to know all the examples and his wisdom about life.

Professor Tantillo is a great lecturer who covers interesting topics and subjects. He always has a ton of energy, which brightens our mornings. He is also very hilarious and gracious. Definitely recommend taking his class!

he's a charismatic lecturer & knows his stuff, but this class is odee for a 2000-level humanities class. hard to keep up w/ numerous readings. midterm/final involve multiple in-class essays that could be on an obscure topic (worth 33% of grade each). he never posts lecture slides online, so you better be in lecture, or else you might get screwed.

Professor Tantillo is such an awesome dude, really cares about his students. His class is very heavy on reading with up to 100 pages/week sometimes. But it isn't really mandatory, but HIGHLY recommended. He has a midterm and final which are on the topics of the course and you really can answer the questions however you feel necessary. Great teacher

I started this class pretty nervous because of Professor Tantillo's reputation of giving a lot of readings and grading so few assignments. All of that is true, but like others say, you can get away with skimming a lot of it. The lectures are pretty interesting and I left the class having learned a lot. I would recommend him

Worst professor I have ever had the misfortune of having at Cornell. His "lectures" (I use that term very loosely) are very disorganized and consist of him basically rambling random quotes. Course reading is HEAVY, easily over 100 pgs/wk for most of the semester. Take-home midterm (avg 25-30pgs), term paper, nightmare in-class final. Stay away!
don't take this class. this guy is the worst.

Tantillo was one of the worst professors I have ever had at Cornell. In lecture, he does NOT use powerpoints and simply just talks at the class, goes on random rants and reads quotes from books. Outside reading is VERY heavy. Despite telling you to "skim," he expects you to know tiny details on the essay final exam and take-home midterm. AVOID!!!
Enjoyable, great depth of knowledge

Dr Tantillo is knowledgable in his field and a good lecturer. Ntres 3320 is heavy in philosophy and lighter in environmentalism, however there is both. His lectures are really just him talking but he emphasizes important things that are reiterated in readings and discussion. Not the easiest class, but I didn't read much and still got a B+

Tantillo is absolutely my all time favorite professor at cornell.  he is completely brilliant and knowledgeable.  be warned, however, that he expects his students to participate and know the material.
The most hysterical man. Had him for summer college and we still act like best friends.

Very smart and humble. He is extremely well-read and knows what he is talking about. He is an excellent speaker, and he won't tell you this, but he is often invited to speak at colleges/events about aesthetics/hunting. A very hard class, but manageable if you are a fast reader. I read a lot of books that every college student should read.

Unquestionably, Tantillo is a great speaker and an interesting person. Sadly, his teaching skills are extremely lacking, and his expectations greatly outweigh the quality of his lectures and efforts (his TA grades everything!). The readings he assigns are difficult to keep up with, assigning a 400 page book for two weeks. I would not this class!!

One of the hardest classes I've taken. The reading is rather impossible, by his own admission. First reading assignment is on how to skim. Books run from "sublime" (Cronon!) to idiotic. Lectures poorly attended. Has own agenda, have of which you'll agree with. Final exam is graded easily but truly a nightmarish encompassing of all reading.

He is a very smart guy.  His speech is so eloquent that he is fascinating to listen to.  I really enjoyed the class before the midterm because we were reading one book at a rate of about 40 pgs. per week.  The book was by Kagan and was interesting.  After the midterm, he started to assign a new book to read every week- almost impossible to keep up.

He is a charismatic lecturer, but irresponsible.  BEWARE! The readings are so numerous and tilted towards his own viewpoint that it becomes difficult to recognize his agenda.  He attacks certain environmental movements and writers without ever examining them.  He's easy to like, but actually listen to what he says and attack him on it.
the class seemed interesting at first, but the amount of reading and the lack of discussion about what we read made it impossible to enjoy

Wow, this guy has to be one of best lecturers. He knows his material and is eloquent. The drawback...too much reading! Be prepared to stay on track or forever be behind for the semester. Best advice, take his class s/u... Definitely worth going to class and not much effort required
Very appreciative of creative thought.No boundaries teaching.Bring something of your own to the table:he'll slice it,dice it,put it on a platter,and mark it with a "B".

Wow, can this guy talk. He's a very good lecturer and will keep your attention. Very demanding course though. Lots of reading. Exams are tough to study for because of so much information that is valid for each exam. Just hope you are lucky...
Jim is extremely knowledgable. He's down to earth and fun. I learned alot from this class.
I enjoyed Tantillo's class immensely.  Although it was a lot of reading, it was very much worth it, and he made you want to come to lecture.
Jim is an awesome person and teacher. he was extremely helpful and his class was interesting, but a bit of work. i recommend taking a class with him, and getting to know him as a person.
He is extremely well-read and I like the course

Love Jim!!! I took his Beginner's Dance Comp class freshman year and now I can't wait to take Intermediate Dance Composition with him next semester!! Such an awesome guy! The class is tons of fun and really opened my eyes to all types of dance!
Professor Self is an amazing teacher, easy grader, and awesome guy! I definitely recommend his class to anyone even remotely interested in dance! You will have SO MUCH FUN!
Great but sometimes weird..
dance extrordinary and great personality.  you will love his classes!
Jim was very kind, given that I haven't danced since I was 6.  He got everyone excited about modern dance, and this was by far the best gym semester one could have.
No Comments

Incredibly enthusiastic and inspirational. Does this guy ever have a bad day? Really interesting experience in the real estate world and genuine willingness to help students. Makes an effort to get to know all of the students. Dynamic presentations with a variety of media. Assigns interesting case studies. Cornell needs more professors like him.

Dustin has a great personality and brings it all to make for engaging and interesting lectures. He is high energy, and his variety of teaching styles (media use, presentations, discussions) keeps the momentum of the course up. Always there to talk to and just a kind person overall, you can get a lot out of taking his course.
Man, this woman kills your gpa. DO NOT take the online course. she's the harshest grader I've ever gotten at Cornell. Don't get fooled.

She was funny and intelligent... well informed and simultaneously cordial. Although it was an online (distance learning) course, I felt like she was conveying the material and assignments clearly and personally. I would definitely take this class again - it was fun!
TA for Intro to Global Health Class
great, attentive professor. explains concepts well. very organized. a lot of homework, but not overwhelming. material is tough, but he teaches it well.
A solid professor- taught the material clearly and the homeworks were all do-able.

Go to his office hour, especially before exams - it helps A LOT ( he holds many office hours before tests). He's really nice and helpful and the way he explains the concepts makes them easer to understand than the textbook. Tests can be tricky but if you do put effort to go through all the recitation and workshop materials you should be fine.

Wilkens is by far one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. He's a very captivating speaker, great at answering questions, charismatic, and funny. fun lecturer and engaging material

Insanely good lectures. It's like he can telepathically understand everyone's train of thought while explaining something. However, I think all these 5-star reviews have boosted his ego a little too much, since he can sometimes come off as a little boastful.

I walked in with a 1 on AP CSA (and a 5 on AP CSP but that's fake though) and waked out with an -A and feeling confident enough to not get weeded out of CS instantly.  Walker White is simply the goat. SAY HIS NAME. LET HIM COOK. I will say though, the exams/projects have a weird emphasis on math, which make the exams harder then they should be imo.

Clear, fun, engaging, enthusiastic. He makes CS enjoyable.
No doubt he is the best
Fav prof at Cornell.

Professor White is hands down the best professor I've ever had so far. This professor is SUPER rude. I won't go into details but I got a good grade in this course and thought he was a good lecturer, but super rude person
Prof. White is the best professor I've had here. Always clear and to the point but also very engaging. Highly recommend.

Walker White is genuinely an amazing Professor, his assignments were very representative and preparing for his exams. Walker White is probably a great professor - like what others have mentioned. But I found myself... not really paying attention to his lectures. Genuinely amazing. Honestly, the model professor for anyone. Not only is he incredibly organized and provides all the resources you need to succeed, he WANTS his students to do well. One of the best professors I've had. Great class to take regardless of whether you had previous coding experience.

White is an insanely competent/inspirational teacher. Not only is he good at lecturing but he seems to truly be passionate about what he does. This class is really well suited for students who have little to knowledge of the subject. I would definitely take one of his classes again in the future.
One of the best lecturers at Cornell. Highly recommend taking cs1110 with him

Great class!
