She was also really helpful outside of class in explaining anything you needed.
Not a bad professor.  Little practicality, though.  Her lectures are disorganized, but her exams are just like the problem sets and class problems.  The final was VERY difficult.

This teacher is a little cooky. She tries to scare you going into prelims by presenting tons of formulas, but the prelims are straight forward and much easier than problem sets. Section, textbook not necessary. She's very proud of her Israeli heritage and references it during lectures. She can't spell at all, but her English is comprehensible.
Horrible Teacher.

I respectfully disagree with the people who recommend her class.  I recently graduated from Cornell with a 3.9 and have been an A student throughout my college life.  I found her to be the most unorganized teacher at our university (both in lectures and course layout).  I recommend the other teacher teaching the same class.
Nice woman, terrible teacher - you have to learn how to do problem sets by yourself often.  Tests are long and too complicated at times. Sections would have been very helpful.
Bar's tests are very straightforward. Just do the problem sets and know them by heart, then you will be fine. If you need to take Econ 313, Bar is a good choice for the easiness of her class.
Professor Bar is helpful, clear, and an expert on the material. She's also nice and understanding. I highly recommend taking 313 with Bar.

Professor Bar is a great professor. I don't know what everyone else is talking about. She is clear and very helpful. The course isn't easy, but it shouldn't be. Take econ313 from her if you get the chance.
She's really nice and her lectures are decent.  Prelims are a bit difficult (always do the practice exam); the final exam is easier.  Not the most generous when it comes to final grades.

Professor Bar is one of the best teachers I've had at Cornell.  She was a very clear lecturer and was also fun because she told silly and mostly irrelevant stories every once in a while to lighten things up.  I found the prelims and exam to be extremely related to what we had studied and the problems on the homework sets.
she is a good and caring person but a terrible teacher...Her exams have nothing to do with what she teaches in lecture or the problem sets... :(
Prelims are hard but she's a great professor and you can tell she really cares about her students
Great Professor

Anyone giving Professor Bar negative comments is likely because he/she did poorly in a challenging course.  Her prelims are difficult but an A was not that hard to come by with a little effort on the problem sets and some studying.  She is a great teacher

She is one of the best professor teaching 313. She emphasizes intuition in understanding economics rather then just solving math questions like other profs. BUT, her exams are extremly ARBITARY and HARD, no relevance with P.S and lecture. Great TA!!!

Her lectures are very boring and her prelims don't have anything to do with her lectures. She seems to aim at preparing the prelims with questions that students have never ever seen, so that they will get even more perplexed!
very hard prelims, lectures are dull and uneccessary and are not aimed at material on prelims
ehhhh...lectures are...boring. almost no relevance to the problem sets, thank goodness the TA gives out handouts...otherwise i'd be completely lost, nice lady tho
very very unhelpful teacher... Prof. Bar spends hours talking about the easiest things over and over again and never gets to explain the most difficult parts
Perhaps the worst teacher I've had at Cornell. EXTREMELY difficult to understand. Thank God I had a good TA!
Lectures aren't wonderful, but she wants you to do well in her course, fair grading
very pleasant class and professor - moderately challenging content, learned a lot. 10/10 recommend

It is pretty clear that Mike doesn't care at all about this class.  Assignments are thrown together without much clarity and are not very engaging.  The upside to this is that the class is incredibly easy.  There were six assignments total and a weekly discussion post-- the way he grades is very lenient.  Easy A

easy A+ class, 2 page paper every week that summarizes what you learned and liked/disliked about the lecture material. Final paper is a bit longer (5-8 pages) and is a case study with a copyright client problem, also not hard if you just go through the slides. Professor is super nice and accommodating

This is the class you should take for both your A&S science requirements. It is basically like a very easy history class. There are a lot of little quizzes that you can take as many times as you like, an easy online midterm and final, and a research paper. Lecture is not mandatory but I liked to go because the professor is passionate. great class

His class is really well organized, and I like how the assignments vary in style (not just all exams like other classes). We even visited the museum (on our own time) for this class. We covered a large breadth of topics, but he made it less overwhelming. Super accessible outside of class, and always looking to help students out. 10/10.
Incredibly easy class, we primarily watch documentary clips. There was a fun self-research project, and the prelims and final were easy.

HE 1150: The Afterlife of Fashion. Learned about sustainable fashion, the history of fashion, and the concept of fast fashion. Quite an eye-opening class. In total, had to write around 4 papers, and weekly annotations, were completely doable. Overall, do not regret taking this class and would take another class with Professor Roberts.

Professor Rogers' first duty is to her filmmaking. She started the semester with a good impression on her students, but the course did not proceed as it was stated on the syllabus. Professor Khatchadourian is a fantastic archeologist and even better instructor. Her own research is fascinating and worth exploring regardless of whether you are taking one of her classes. Dr. Leonard has wonderful lectures that are thought provoking. She is very engaging and encourages her students to speak their mind. There are no tests, just 4 essays total. Amazing Professor.

Great professors are professors who can still be viewed as respected teaching hard subjects. Godwin is a great professor and is constantly looking out for us. This is gonna be a tough class just because of the subject. That being said, I can't imagine taking the class with a better professor. He is a great professor and any rating outside of a 5 is wrong

Honestly one of my favorite professors within Dyson. Weekly homework and quizzes, but work load is manageable. Super responsive and understanding with any issues/confusion. One answered one of my emails past 10pm. Recommend going to class to get best understanding of concepts.

One of my favorite professors I've had so far. Teaches with a passion. Weekly homework activity and take-home quiz. If you go to lecture and pay attention, you will succeed. Professor Smith's lectures were very informative and followed the assigned readings very closely. The few projects in the class were fun and really helped understand the importance of the material!

Almost impossible to pay attention in class and lectures are the audio equivalent of reading a dry textbook. The amount of reading required is massive with reading quizzes every class. The way the material is presented might be interesting to those very interested in the topics, but otherwise you'll find yourself falling asleep.

Professor Smith is super engaging and very knowledgable in his field of work. The lectures were all very interesting and heavily based on the readings assigned. The readings along the lectures worked really well together in getting you to understand the concepts. Heavy on discussion but a really good overall experience.

Instructor Smith is an extremely thoughtful lecturer, generous with his time with students and very approachable. His lectures are well organized and takes students' input and surveys very seriously. His class examples and tests are challenging yet stimulating and has excellent comand of the subject.
Mr. Smith was an excellent lecturer, he made fairly complicated concepts easy to understand. You could tell he was really putting time and effort into the course.

Man, Prof. Smith is so poor at communicating the message across that it makes the class way harder than it really is. Having taken AP stats in high school, I know most of the topics are exactly the same and yet I learned more from my high school

FWS: Word and Image. The readings each week were a bit much upfront. She's a slow grader but gives lots of comments . The grading system for the papers and course are really transparent. She is so knowledgable and PUBPOL 3110 is an extremely interesting class and lectures were engaging even if not mandatory. There is a decent amount of homework for the drug project but it is graded very leniently and the tests are pretty fair. Also there are no readings so everything you need to know is on the slides.

PUBPOL 3110 is very similar to PUBPOL 2350 but a lot easier. The prelim and final make up half your grade and are super easy. The remaining half of your grade is a project (group or solo) that takes the entire semester and is also super duper easy. Overall, a great professor and a very passable class.

I LOVED Professor Michener. Her personality is so enchanting. Her teaching is very comprehensive. She is understanding and gives each assignment a 72-hour extension. 3 fair pop quizzes on the readings, 2 papers, a midterm, and a final project. It was a lot of reading and the TAs could improve but overall a lovely class with interesting topics!

Great class. Michener is very knowledgeable and kind. Easy material to understand if you know anything about government, and 3 pop quizzes on readings but relatively straightforward. 2 essays that were short and easy. 1 midterm that was open note writing. Final project you can work in teams. Calls on students who never have anything relevant to say

Would absolutely take a class from Prof Michener again! Would NOT take a class from my TA (who makes up the majority of your grade) again! Lectures were wonderful- would have rated this higher if not for TAs, whose grading is both very particular and unclear-taking off points for personal preferences/ opinions about how things should be written
I dropped this class. Michener was great, but the TAs provided no clear guidelines and penalized people for missing obvious answers. Avoid this class for your own benefit.

An excellent lecturer and clearly cares about her students. I'm sure the course was a little different because of Zoom University, but she adapted well and I'm sure that she's even more engaging IRL. Taken Fall 2020.

This class was one of my favorites this sem and it was definitely because of Prof Michener! Her lectures were always really engaging and I appreciated her candidness about her political beliefs when topics came up (which was a lot since the class is about politics of policy). Assignments were challenging but rewarding! Definitely would recommend.

She is an amazing lecturer! She gives great, engaging examples of the topics we cover, and is real about their implications. There is a lot of reading, but they're interesting an generally pretty easy to read.

wouldn't recommend this course. While this class is extremely informative& teaches you about a crucial topic, simply not worth it. Prof. M doesn't really lecture - it's more like she preaches. lectures are hardly informative-she says whatever comes to mind

Michener is easily one of the most engaging lecturers I've had at Cornell. The best professor I've ever had at Cornell. Amazing lecturer and understanding so long as you COMMUNICATE openly and honestly with her. I've taken more than 2 classes with her because of how much I enjoy her. FYI: Try to look up the books online before buying as they can be a bit expensive and you can usually find them.

This class is a lot of work but well worth it. You get about 20-50 pages of reading a night. The assignments aren't super difficult, just time-consuming. If you don't do the readings, prepare to suffer. The final is heavily built on the readings. Super engaging in lecture and she is very reachable outside of class

All in all the class material is extremely interesting and very eye opening at times. She was a good lecturer and was clearly very invested in the material and made it very understandable. In terms of material she chooses great readings that are very memorable even outside of class. She gives a TON of reading. My TA was a tough grader

Professor Michener is a wonderful lecturer! She encourages participation,  is very approachable, and is a fair grader. The class is well structured, and although there are many long readings, they are fairly interesting.  Overall, an eye-opening and applicable class--I learned a lot!

Michener is really interested in what she teaches, and one of the nicest professors I've had at Cornell. Very approachable and laid-back. Funny. She's not an easy grader - normal for a Cornell prof. Her class was well-organized and we followed the syllabus. Lots of reading. Essays only. Very eye-opening class. Good for the beginning of a gov major.
He is obsessed wiht shadow puppets and exotic spices. He is my only love for ever any always.
A little awkward, not very interesting. Not too hard of a grader though...
All around nice guy. takes a while to get used to the way he teaches the class. very subdued

Prof Simons is definitely very passionate about what he teaches. He's a nice guy, but can come off as a little intimidating sometimes. Teaches organizational behavior, but is so unorganized it hurts. He has no rubrics. The only way to get a good grade is to cater to his beliefs about life.

Horrible. He is so disorganized for teaching literal ORGANIZATIONAL behavior. His TA's know more about the class than he does. Prof Simons is definitely a nice guy, but he often fails to provide the necessary attention and/or information to be a good teacher. He delegates a lot of the explaining of assignments to TAs, and the assignments on canvas have very little instruction. Though I must say, his in-class lectures are somewhat enjoyable.

One of the most caring professors I have had at Cornell. Professor Simons truly cares about his students and can be flexible with deadlines if you speak to him. I enjoyed going to this class every week. Professor Simons is open and honest and teaches the material well.

VERY unorganized, especially when it comes to assignments and due dates. Is a nice enough guy and will work with you if you need help. If you do what he wants how he wants it, you'll be fine. As a class, OB is just making up fancy terms for common sense concepts. He posts his slides & everything is in book so you don't really need to go to class.
A bit scattered, but a knowledgeable and genuinely nice guy.
very rude and unorganized. Lots of meaningless work.

The worst professor at Cornell. He is definitely a tough grader, and there is no rubric. Nobody knows what is he looking for. very unorganized. don't tell the class about the due date. I hope you never, ever teach this course again.

Professor Simons teaches organization but is super unorganized himself. He gives assignments but does not specify due dates. There is no set rubric for how he grades his papers. Most of the class is concept based so if you dont interpret something the same as him you will get a bad grade.

Prof. Simons is an odd guy, but a great teacher. He really cares about his students and teaches information that seems unimportant initially but as soon as you get into the world you realize how important/interesting/applicable it is. Show up to lectureyou'll learn a lot and usually have a bit of fun. Would definitely recommend Prof. Simons for OB

In the beginning of the year, he came off as a great and caring professor; however, as time went on, he showed himself to be very closed minded and disorganized. he wants all of his students to think like him, which is nearly impossible. he gives very little instruction on assignments; make sure you go to see him about every big paper otherwisefail

A B in OB is a joke. Should not have been grading as hard as he did. It is actually a joke. He is a hypocrite. Talks about managing people but he can barely manage to keep a clean office. Avoid taking him. I made the mistake of not trying to get a different teacher and now I have a B in OB. Switch professors if you can.

Real two faced teacher. Acts nice and grades hard. Not clear at all about what he wants in assignments, and doesn't give you any helpful feedback to improve your paper grades over time. Not a surprise that most people wish they had other OB teachers

Best course of my semester. He is very flexible but does not like it if it being taken advantage of, just talk to him. I would say that it is the best balanced course I have had so far in terms of deliverables, difficulty, readings etc.

Simons is kind of a mess, but I think he's one of the most fun professors I've had here.  You do a ton of cool in class demonstrations and watch a lot of videos.  Mostly straightforward work, and the book is almost optional.  Not the best professor, but a great guy and a fun class.

One of the most disorganized teachers in the Hotel School. His office defines "chaos" and your papers will not be returned on time because they've gone fishing in his office... somewhere. If you're a minority student, run away.

What a waste of my tuition money. Lectures were torture because S Pinet cannot build strong classroom discussions other than her letting her minions say really banal things. Will fulfill my requirements with other professors who can at least make lectures insightful.

Literally my favorite Spanish teacher and my favorite Spanish class that I have ever taken. She is so passionate. The homework is super light, and we have weekly reflection papers. That is it! I loved the class with my whole heart and plan on taking her senior seminar last year.

I love how even the supposedly positive comments here have a crap ton of dislikes because NO ONE believes this professor is remotely capable of teaching a decent class where ever single one of us felt the tiniest bit comfortable

It was a mediocre class. The lectures were very discussion-focused, so make sure to read the assignments before then in order to not be embarrassed by Simone. Also, avoid office hours at all costs. You'll regret it if you dont.
The reading material was sometimes boring, sometimes interesting. But Simone herself did not create an inclusive learning environment. I recommend taking the class with a TA
Simone is a pretty okay teacher. The class was fine and she's knowledgeable, but working with her on getting clarify for assignments was torturous.
Simone was great, I was timid in my speaking skills and had difficulty understanding so she checked in with me through office hours often and helped me understand the course curriculum.

One of the best professors I had. She is easy to approach and class with her is very enjoyable!

Simone is not only one of the smartest people I've ever met, but she is engaging, funny, and open to the ideas of her students. I'm shocked by all these bad reviews; she's inspiring and down to earth despite her impressive qualifications.

If you want to learn something, take this class with Maria Antonia or another professor. Even if Simone spent 100 years on a remedial teaching journey, her hatred for students would prevent her from actually evolving into a somewhat decent instructor. She knows it too, hence all the self comments she is writing due to low enrollment in her courses.

Without a doubt one of the most memorable professors that I have had here at Cornell. In terms of the class, she gives a lot of creative freedom as well.

Simone is literally a bully in every sense of the word. She preys on young students.  Her relentless efforts to write positive reviews herself won't change every day reality. She lacks the respect of both students and faculty.
Simone is literally the best. She is a professor you will look back on 30 years from now and remember what she taught you.
Simone, aside from having written five books in different languages, is a passionate and caring professor. I love her and her classes!
Almost poked my eyes out! Simone's insecurity is only matched by her infinite hostility for her own students. Her lack of scholarly publications compared to other professors speaks for itself.

One of the best classes and professors at the university! Professor Pinet was always willing to help me improve my writing or just discuss class content. She made me think of certain ideas in such mind-blowing and new ways. Overall I really enjoyed this class.

Lectures aren't interactive as Simone only wants her favorites to talk in class even when they say things that lack basic analysis. Essays are fine and quite short in general. Simone does take attendance in every class, though.

She's an amazing teacher who is beyond nice and laid back. Of course, you need to try to some degree and a clear comprehension of Spanish is required. However, she makes the course enjoyable regardless of your skill level.

Simone is willing to help as long as you care and are passionate about the subject.  She is fair in her criteria and gives you the chance to succeed as long as you put in the effort.  As long as you participate the class should be fine!  One of my favorites so far at Cornell.
Simone may be hostile at times. Papers are simple and quite short. Just participate and you are guaranteed a decent grade.

Unsure as to what would be more painful... another twice-a-week class with Simone or or being eaten alive by a bull shark. Lectures are endless and she mocks you if you don't say exactly what she thinks is right. Write down everything she incoherently speaks and give it back on every essay. Forget other options if you want to pass.
Just awful. The worst professor I have had in my entire life. Mean, unclear and a total nightmare. Any interest I had in pursuing a minor was crushed by this class and this woman.

I loved Simone's perspectives class.  She taught a ton, and, as we were all interested in Spain as a country, it was fascinating.  We were always asking questions and getting amazing, thoughtful answers.  She set the tone for my time abroad, and I'm glad that I took her class.

Simone is the worst professor I have ever had. The only opinion that seems to matter to Simone is her own. If you do not agree with her, she will tear you apart. Although she is smart, this is clearly the wrong career for her.  Once you get on her bad side, it is impossible to get a good grade.

This is a required survey course for majors and not many professors teach it. I have fixed feelings about Simone. As a rule, it is best not to ever contradict her and to stay on her good side. Grades are entirely subjective but if you keep that in mind and don't argue with her, it's easy to get great marks.
No organization. No coherent style. No feedback. Simple assignments. Not many options for Spanish majors.

Simone takes Spanish Golden Age literature and introduces new and unexpected ways to view and interpret the texts. She understands the fact that this is only a survey course and doesn't expect gratuitous analysis of literary minutiae. Instead, she sets the groundwork for a working knowledge and appreciation of the texts covered in class.

The Spanish Golden Age is one of the most fascinating periods in literature. Simone, however, manages to bring to life the worst aspects of this period, as you feel that you are experiencing Cervantes' struggle--being kidnapped and hoping desperately that someone rescues you. In the end, it is not Simone's fault that she isn't professor material.

Simone took a class on a period of literature that has the potential to be really boring and makes it interesting and relatable. We even did trips to the Johnson museum and Rare Books library to look at manuscripts from the time period we were studying and art from that period. Very fair grading and overall a very good class.

this professor cursed me out in her office, saying that I was stupid, yelled at me, and told me to get out of her office (because I yawned). she is outright nasty, insecure, and got the job because of her husband, who once said in class, "as far as human ignorance is concerned", perhaps I will include myself". Painful elective. Simone imbues the worst of everyone in the class; however, if you write down everything she says and reproduce it on the essays, one can pull of an A or A- easily.

Crazy woman. Loves to say: "I'm very, very good at what I do." Unfortunately, if that were true, everyone would know it and she wouldn't have to say it all the time. Her class is not that hard if you are on her good side.
Professor was out of control. She assumed we knew tons about Medieval Spanish Literature even before the class. Stay away at all costs.

Just finished her "Theater of Early Modern Spain" elective. Simone fails as a professor because she is teaching something she lacks passion for. Add to that her creepy personality and it's the longest 75-min lecture in which the best thing to do is to bring a bodyguard and pray for night fall.
I dropped this class after attending the third session yesterday. Can't imagine having someone so moody and dictatorial for a full semester.

Threw everyone out of class once because according to her no one read that day. Translation: if you get assigned over 100 pages a night, make sure you are able to recall every tiny detail. Otherwise, prepare to be thrown out of class after hearing a huge lecture on how you are not taking education seriously.

Don't try to learn anything. Bottom line, if you want to do well and not get harassed, tell her exactly what she wants to hear. Not too difficult if you pretend to agree with everything she spills outs.
this professor is terrible. she should get a different job.

Professor Pinet is too abrasive. SPANL 217 with her is similar to being on the Wizard of Oz and hearing "I'll get you, me pretty, and your little dog, too!" Like the previous poster mentioned, the books were plain gross, e.g. imagine reading about thieves who****innocent women and then cut their throats.

Simone's class is for anyone who enjoys reading books about pirates who make their victims eat fecal matter. Yes, really. The name of that book is "Naufragios" and it happens to be Simone's favourite. Appalling.

By its nature, Spanish literature is subjective! Come on. Leaving aside the previous poster's error--"to much," medieval Spanish lit with Simone is not demanding b/c she says the important things about each book. yes, it's true she only talked about Mexico a few times. Her major flaw was being too cocky and not having enough office hrs. OK overall.
To summarize the experience: "Give me another professor or give me death!"
No Comments
Pay attention to do well. AVOID creativity on essays. For the final exam, review notes. And, try to show interest in Mexican culture. That's all it takes. Eeeeaaaassssyyyy A.
Run away or pray for another person to teach this class
Never met such an insecure human being. The semester was wasted on bogus books... Probably the most boring stuff I have read. Ahhhhhhhhhhh!!!!!!

Expected grad level work even though it was SPANL 319. The less you ask, the better off you are. Anyone who comes across as intelligent is penalized. It is unacceptable for Cornell to hire such unprofessional staff.

One word: CHAOS. Simone made what was supposed to be an interesting course feel like you were burning within four walls. If you do not have a strong Spanish grammar background, forget about doing well, this prof didn't really have many office hours.
This woman is obnoxious. Don't ever contradict her. Avoid at all costs.
A moderately intelligent prof who seems to dislike most students

Funny how the previous student hit the nail right on its head. SPANL 319 had a distinct emphasis on Mexican works/culture. Not sure I would say Simone is "evil." In my experience other profs from the span lit dept have been nicer. Of course this doesnt mean she is terrible.

Had this professor for medieval spanish literature. Simone does not listen to a word you say. She was determined to prove her intelligence to the class, nothing else. good luck to her future students.

The class provides a biased point of view--Simone's; no other is tolerated. Most of us never understood why she became a college professor at Cornell when she kept talking about Harvard all semester long. The title for SPANL 319 should have been "From Bad to Worse to Hell."

Like most students, I experienced a terrible semester with Simone last spring. The only reason I ended up with an A- in the class was due to the endless hours I spent working on each essay. Hard classes do not scare me, but Simone is probably the rudest and most unpleasant professor I have had at Cornell. DO NOT enroll in any of her courses!

On average all 400-level courses at Cornell are pretty difficult, but Simone made the course a living hell that only got worse throughout the semester. She offered no help with the papers, and constantly reminded us that this was an advanced course and it was our responsibility. I pity anyone who takes a class with her, including myself.
Takes attendance on a daily basis, you cannot afford to miss class. Prof. Pinet talks way too fast sometimes. It's almost impossible to get a decent grade.
dont know anyone who likes her. class was a waste of my time. avoid

Grrr... surviving this class was a concern I had. Unfortunately, for SPANL 319 there aren't many options. Lectures seemed endless. The material itself was challenging, well maybe for me-- Spanish is not my native language. I did not ask Simone for help many times, but when I did, she was not very nice about it.
Ok class. Some of the novels were very interesting. Simone may not be the nicest professor in the department, but at least she has some original, capturing ideas from time to time. I have had worse.

Lots of banal books to read, none worth one's time. Simone is not very good following a complex idea, so she often attempts to mock her own students as the result of her lack of understanding. I'm happy that the class is over.

Granted, 16th and 17th-century spanish lit is hard to understand, but this class was just too much. Simone expects you to read at least 70 pages a night and be able to recall the most insignificant details from the novels. She knows her stuff, yet her animosity toward her own students creates an uncomfortable learning environment for everyone.

Well, I loved magical realism until I took this class. The instructor expects you to agree with all her ideas and if you don't, she will attempt to ridicule you. This class had no room for one's personal interpretation and theory. To make matters worse the class ended with a dull final paper assignment.

Glad to hear I'm not the only one who did not enjoy this class. As others mentioned, it's not the fact that papers are graded harshly as much as unfairly. Class itself was painful, and I actually like spanish lit.
Painful class & instructor
This class was a true nightmare, mostly due to the professor.

I haven't taken that many Spanish literature classes at Cornell, but I sure did not enjoy this one. The class lacks structure. The professor was never nice to us. The entire class had a very negative feeling. After 3 absences, your grade in the class will suffer.
Simone never offers any help to her students. Her essays are graded harshly. I should have taken this class with someone else.

In my three years at Cornell, this was the worst class and professor I have encountered. The readings were never interesting, class time was brutal. I wish I would have taken this class with another professor.
Worst professor ever. She is never available during office hours and one can never approach her. Avoid at all costs.
In one word, awful. She is highly disorganized and does not offer much help during office hours. Stay away from her SPANL 319 course.

Prof. Simon is, in a word, amazing. This was one of the most interesting classes I've taken in a while, and she really knows a lot about the material (health policy). She was extremely helpful, very responsive to email, and would always do whatever it took to help you understand the material. Tests are fair, and the research project is appropriate.

Prof Saccamano's class was my favorite this semester. Very knowledgeable in his field and knows how to articulate it to his students. VERY discussion-based class sessions that he uses next to none slides to stimulate, but he stimulates nonetheless. Books are interesting and cohesive, for the most part. I would strongly suggest taking this course.
Indubitably the very best the Cornell English dept has to offer. He is flawless in every way and checks every box with flying colors. A truly top-shelf, first-rate academic.

Prof. S is an expert on the novel who is exceptionally well versed in philosophy, political and critical theory. He is an easy grader, and he's cool with doing most of the talking in class, even if it's a seminar. He has a friendly demeanor, and he's very laidback and easygoing, but is also serious about teaching. Def connect with him if you can.

I took my FWS with Prof. Saccamano this summer, and it was really well-organized. The books we've read were mostly very interesting and connected with each other. Prof. Saccamano also gives detailed feedback on how to revise and improve our essays. Overall, I think it was one of the most interesting and worthwhile courses I've taken at Cornell.

Professor Saccamano is a pleasure to listen to in lectures. While the material can sometimes get quite dry, he makes up for this by his unique in depth analysis of the plays we read; we viewed them through religious, political, sexual, and various other fascinating lenses. Really makes you think about the impact of identification with theatrics.
Very approachable, a fair grader, and also very helpful during office hours.
I got the idea that this guy was a phony.  I did fine in the course, but he seemed more interested in showing off than anything else.

I graduated with honors in English in 2001 -- this was the one class I couldn't stand even though I did well in it. The prof's not actually that bad, but the readings were endless and he gave quizzes to see that we'd read all 1,000,000 pages of Tom Jones and Clarissa. I wanted to kill myself.
This professor genuinely cares about the students, and he is passionate about the literature he covers. He's one of those instructors you never forget; he was my professor in 1988-89!
Incisive, fair, to the point
This class was awesome. He really digs into the texts and the lectures are fabulous. He is also genuinely interested in hearing what students have to say.

The lectures were entertaining and provided fascinating background.  The professor is totally great-- he chooses interesting material and presents it well and doesn't take crap from stupid kids.  Woo-Hoo.
No Comments

Dr. Mattson is an exceptional educator. He understands his content, knows when not to take himself too seriously, and has curated an exceptional pedagogical experience in controlled-environment horticulture. If CEA/hyrdoponics interest you or you just love plants, I cannot recommend this course highly enough.

Most of the grading occurs at the end of the semester, so it is difficult to gauge your performance in the class. There are interesting concepts taught in this course and it is heavily discussion based, so participation matters. The professor believes his opinion is fact most of the time, so be careful with disputing.
Best Professor I had at Cornell!

Neil was the best professor I had at Cornell. His expertise really shined in everything he said. It's refreshing to have a professor with heavy real-world entrepreneurial experience and didn't just "learn it" in a classroom. He always makes himself available and goes out of his way to help students with class and even starting their own company.

This class is a lot of work due to weekly presentations and team meetings but you learn a lot about entrepreneurship. It is also a class that you can mention in interviews since it is so unique. Even with the workload, the grades turn out fine and there are opportunities for extra credit at the end of the semester.
Employ the Business Model Canvas approach to developing a business concept.
Great Professor!  Really wants his students to learn.

Neil is a great guy who will always take the time to speak with and assist his students.  Entrepreneurism is not a straightforward "If this, then that" type of subject, but Neil ties in a number of real-world scenarious combined with his personal experiences to help students understand the holistic approach to launching a successful venture.
Tarallo was great. Really cares about students and always available in his office. Be prepared to be inspired.

Interesting class. Group project that meets throughout the semester and gives a good understanding of product development from start to finish. Could use clearer grading criteria - grades are arbitrary based on how much she likes your work. Lewis also is clearly not interested in students; she was pretty rude to me when I approached her after class
simply the goat ...
Mark Lewis is like Brock Lesnar. He looks good on the outside, but he sucks actually.

Took this class with dual-professor, Lewis and Dai. Compared to Dai, Lewis is a joke. He lectures about his daughter and answers cell phones in class. His tests cover everything, but involve redundant crazy computations. Also, the extra credit questions ask about her daughter's gymnastic score. I mean, WTF.

As a person, Lewis is a great guy. Funny, interesting to talk to and willing to help. But he is a terrible lecturer and orator. Spent most of the time talking about random stuff and his life. However, tests were easy and I learned most of the class from the textbook and discussion.

Prof Lewis is a love or hate type of guy. I personally really enjoyed coming to class. He loves to tell funny stories and keep the class engaged. Many complain that he is a bad lecturer, but I think that the material is understandable and not that hard if one pays attention and reads the book outside of class. He is one of my favorite profs so far.
Spent more time talking about personal life than lecturing on material.  Also, terrible at explaining material.  The class was easy enough though,
Worst ORIE professor I've had thus far. Everything I learned in this class is a result of me teaching myself. Lewis cannot teach for his life.

Incredibly arrogant - spends more time talking about himself than the material.  Lectures were incomprehensible as he simply copied equations onto mistake-filled slides and skipped around without bothering to explain anything.  Has very poor command of the course material and was often thrown off by questions in lecture and office hours.

Seems like a nice guy on the surface but is an abysmal lecturer. He waters down the material so much in class to the point that it's incoherent. Not rigorous in his presentation of the material at all.
Really great! Enjoyable lectures (which is rate in engineering.)

ML seems very interested in making sure his students understand the material. He frequently emails with follow up examples and is very approachable. He breaks up his lecture with really amusing stories so his class is entertaining and you stay awake.
Lectures not helpful.

Great teacher.  Had him for into to physics.  He has a great way of making a copmlicated subject seem straight forward.  Would take any of his courses in a heart beat.  He sincerely wants you to do well.

Zach is an awesome TA.  He makes everything so easy to understand and he is always so enthusiastic about the subjects we learn.  He knows how to get students to learn and does it well.  If you have the opportunity, have him as your section TA (or hopefully professor in the future!)

Hes honestly not that bad! All lecture slides posted online which is super helpful and the content is very interesting. He may not be the most lively professor but its clear he loves communication and cares about students doing well. I would recommend him.

His class is the problem, not him. Introverted, caring guy who tries his best, but the subject matter is horrifically awful. If you hate abstract theory and are turned off by group discussions during lecture, steer clear. Norman himself is fine though. Fair, accessible and reasonable.

Norman speaks in a monotone voice and seems genuinely bored by teaching. However, the material was extremely interesting and his projects and papers are surprisingly interesting to complete. I actually looked forward to the class even though he very clearly does not want to be there teaching it. And if you study, you'll do well on the test.

Very boring teacher. Lectures and slides are very helpful in understanding the material. Lectures could be more clear and quizzes can be a tad specific. Overall, if you do the work, read the book and show up to class, you shouldn't have a hard time doing well

Extremely boring and monotonous. Manages to turn exciting material into confusing, unimaginative, sleepy lectures. Asks self-defeating questions, loves platitudes and crams his course with meaningless group activities that are neither enjoyable nor rewarding.
One of the worst professors at Cornell. Doesn't know how to lecture so class was focused around group discussions.

Lectures can be long/boring but he's a nice guy that is there for you/will help you if need be. Sections are way too long in my opinion, and somewhat unnecessary. Papers aren't too hard but require a lot of thought. Put in some effort and you will be fine.
The professor is really boring and doesn't know what he's talking about half the time.

Brutally boring. Readings are long and put you to sleep and professor is very soft spoken and monotone, so falling asleep in lecture is definitely common too. I want to go into Advertising so Visual Comm sounds like something enjoyable but his curriculum makes it dreadful, in my opinion. But essay topics are well thought out and make you think.
Prof. Goldberg must be one of the most patient professors at Cornell. His grasp of technical concepts is so strong that he can answer any question that you may and will ever have!

Teaching Style - Lectures were problems or proofs that would highlight key theories that were prevalent within that chapter. 

Very fair, intuitive approach to statistics. 

I would hunt down this profs courses.

I love this guy, but I don't love the way he teaches. Super cool guy, but his lectures are unclear and he includes material that is neither in the textbook nor lectures in his prelim. I thought BIOG 1440 was easy, but he was by far the hardest out of the four professors. Still love him though.

He's interesting and engaging, but his slides are mostly pics so you need to pay good attention. A lot of times he talks about unrelated things. The class is moderately difficult. There's videos, readings, and mandatory quizzes twice a week, 4 prelims, optional final, and attendance is not mandatory. Prelims are tricky. Don't take if not required.
One of my favorite lecturers from this class.

Lecture notes are unclear and difficult to understand. Supplemental material don't pertain to lecture. Lecture topics random and disorganized. Lectures are repetitive and boring. Tests are on hyper-specific topics sometimes missing from lectures entirely. no curve

His lectures are a bit boring and each of his slides are just crammed with info. Pretty friendly guy tho. He makes an effort to teach but sometimes he explains concepts in a way that is more confusing than it should be. I also feel like the content on the exams are deeper than what he discusses in lecture.

He didn't get everyone falling asleep in class, but that DOESN'T MEAN he was a good professor. Lecture content was VERY different from test material, and the class WAS NOT curved. The average was supposed to be a C, but he widened the bins so everyone got a B-. Then the very last day of grading, he changed half the grades due to math error. RUN.

Dr Gilbert is by far the funniest and coolest lecturer of 1780. He teaches Animal evolutionary history and is hilarious and one of the few professors for the class that is actually engaging. Very down to earth, very meme worthy. Favorite professor of the semester by far, if only for the pure sass and sarcasm emanating from this man.
The insect collection is tough, but that's mandatory for the course and good planning will make it work. Cole is hilarious and caring.

This professor is boring and disorganized. I have not gotten lower than an "A" until this 1440 Biology class. If you think looking at slides all course and cracking silly jokes is fun great. Exams had no continuity with lectures! Should have gotten out of his course. Then half the final grades posted were wrong and the final grades reposted - WOW!

Cole is a great lecturer and cracks a lot of dumb jokes. Definitely a steep learning curve in the lab and obviously geared towards people with some background knowledge already. Be prepared to spend a lot of time on the insect collection.

The fun does not balance out the work. The first half of the semester is unreasonably hard. Lecture is interesting even though it is early in the morning. Lab and the practicals are harder than class.
Terrible Class. Will never take again. Must have entire bug collection in addition to lab tests AND prelims in class. Tons of work. No reward.

He is definitely a nice guy, but I don't see how the lab and lecture correlate. In lab, you get thrown right in without any explanation. Lectures, he talks about basic, cool things, but you have to know a lot of details which he doesn't make you aware of. This should be an intro course, but I feel like I should have had a lot of prior knowledge.
Cole is an amazing lecturer and incredibly funny. He's super helpful and really does his best to make the class as informative and fun as possible.
So much better than Booker! And he's funny. He's very clear and keeps students engaged. Great professor!

Prof. Gilbert was great! He tried to be as interesting as you can with this material. His lectures were clear and simple, and he showed genuine interest in our understanding the subject and being prepared for the exams. Oh, and sometimes he'd randomly run around to make a point. Cool guy!

Cole is one of the best professors at Cornell that I've encountered. His lectures are interesting, and doesn't just lecture the reading; he goes above and beyond the reading. He is an incredibly nice guy, and extremely knowledgeable about entomology. I loved this course with him. A+

Hilarious.  The powerpoint slides he makes are very entertaining.  His material in 1780 can be hard because it's all memorization but he gives lots of interesting examples.  Possibly my favorite of the five 1780 lecturers.

Cole Gilbert is awesome.  Coming from an engineering and pre-med background, its really refreshing to have a teacher that is enthralled with what he teaches and can talk to students in a relaxed atmosphere.  As for the class, study his lectures and ask questions during lab and you'll do fine.  I just wish he'd teach more classes!
It was clear that he wanted us to do well, but he was not effective at teaching and I found the tests to be unfair compared to the material taught.

Fun class, Professor Gilbert made what would have been rather dry and straight from the text much more interesting with his anecdotes and examples but did not get sidetracked by them - lecture focused on major concepts not detail.
Great, interesting professor.
No Comments
Okay class, not a great teacher. Make sure you stay on schedule with the readings.

Dr. Gilbert is really, REALLY good. One of the best lecturers I could wish for. I wish all teachers could be so amiable yet knowledgeable. There are some profs you can't hear bc they mumble- Dr. Gilbert will never subject you to that. Crystal clear! Makes Bio accessible!!!
nice guy, sort of interesting sometimes, class needs a lot of reading and lectures can get pretty boring

Dr. Gilbert is an amazing teacher. Unlike other profs, he genuinely wants you to succeed and isn't out to get you. Tests are fair, but be prepared to put in a lot of effort. Goes through ppts and lectures very quickly, but they're all online afterwards. He also has pre lecture questions to help with the reading. Overall, an amazing teacher.

Fun lecturer.  Goes through slides a little too fast, but posts powerpoints and audio recording of lectures online, so you can catch up later and study easily.  Tests aren't easy, but they won't contain that many inordinately difficult questions.
Kool dude. Go through the powerpoint and lecture audio before the exam and ur golden.

Dr. Gilbert is not a good professor...he flies through his powerpoints without taking a breath...it's impossible to catch hardly any of what he is saying...his tests are unbearably difficult b/c of the large amount of material he inadequately covers..if you want to pass his class, be prepared to put in lot of extra work teaching yourself everything

Cole Gilbert is one of the most helpful professors at Cornell just go to his office hours. Though he zips through lecture and it can be difficult to keep up at first, as long as you actually put some effort its managable. He has a sence of humor too and truly tries to make class entertaining. Great professor to have.
Though he zipps through his lecture he tries to keep it interesting and is extremely accessable and helpfull during his office hours
No Comments

His lectures were informative but boring, he chose some really random and irrelevant things to go in depth with. Otherwise really helpful though. Good use of powerpoints and the clicker questions were actually helpful. For prelims though, your best bet is to just memorize the book. It's a challenging class, but not impossible.

His teaching style doesn't make or break the class - he's just aite. Ideally, you could look at the ppt slides (& listen to audio if you want to) & skip class & do just fine, but you gotta go for the clicker q's. Study really hard, you know the rep of intro bio...
He's very enthusiatic and willing to help anybody
I liked how he taught the class with funny jokes and whatnot

Dynamic and exciting lectures. He sometimes goes into certain topics too deep, but that's fine. Prelims can be harder than you think so be prepared. I personally didn't like his prelims because some questions seemed irrelevant. Yet, overall, Prof.Gilbert is a great guy.
I like his lectures. The diagrams are great !!

Gilbert is AMAZING!!!  I absolutely love this class.  He's a really dynamic lecturer, and he knows his stuff.  I'm pretty sad that he won't be teaching 2nd semester intro bio.  The best way I've found to study for this class is to take my textbook and highlight/take notes in it as he lectures...he tends to follow it pretty closely.  He's great!

As an intro level bio class for majors, the class is meant to be difficult and lives up to its reputation. However Cole does a great job in teaching the class. By going to lecutres, keeping up on the readings, and studying difficult material extra the class in manageable. Cole does excellent lectures, has great powerpoints, and is so knowledgeable.
No Comments

Ent 212 was the best class I have ever taken!  Dr Gilbert teaches in a fun, involved manner; he takes a deep interest in each student's progress.  Classes are interesting, field trips are fun, and the lab-work actually holds purpose!!!!!!

VERY rude, sneaky, back-stabbing Prof. WATCH OUT for this lady. She'll give you attitude if you cross her, and she won't hesitate to put your grade on her guillotine. She cares WAY too much about participation, and even if you're shy and do your best to speak up here and there it's not good enough for her. If you're a native speaker she'll like you

Prof. Waldron is very energetic about the subject and wants her students to do well. She was available outside of class whenever I needed help with papers. The class focused on French movies and was very interesting overall.

She's super charming and oftentimes class ended up being one long discussion between all the students and her.  It's not hard to get an A.  Participation is important, but she does a good job of getting even the quietest people to speak up and share.   It's obvious she wants you to succeed.  She's also just really funny to talk/listen too.

Easy class, easy tests. Prof. Waldron is absolutely amazing! She's funny and she genuinely cares about you. She'll go out of her way to make sure you succeed in the class. One of the best professors I've had at Cornell! She also brought in food for the class as well. Feedback is helpful. Participation/attendance mandatory.

Mme. Waldron was a good professor. She led my class "French Through Film" when I was at Cornell. Between her, the late Mme. Daly (who was my professor in 2 other courses), and some great classmates, I had a wonderful French language experience at Cornell.
She is absolutely a great professor. She was always giving in her best to help the students. In short, she is awesome!

Colette is a WONDERFUL person with a  big heart... But her class was a miserable experience.  Get ready for confusion, MANY tests, unclear syllabi, EXCESSIVE amounts of busy work, and endless headaches.
Great professor! A bit disorganized, but clearly is enthusiastic about the subject material and wants her students to do well.  Workload is reasonable and Colette is very helpful!
very good professor, chose really interesting/thought provoking films. be sure to participate as that is mostly what she grades on. I improved a lot during her course

Participate! That's the key. A very nice woman who loves to teach, and loves to see students improve. It's true that if you're on her good side she grades you a little better, but it's easy to get there. Highly recommended.

It's not that the class is difficult at all, but rather, that the grading is very unfair. If she likes you, then you can write the worst essay and still get an A. On the contrary, if you are on her bad side, it won't matter how much effort you put.

Madame, je vous adore! Mme. Waldron loves discussion, and if you take her class you'll speak and listen well to others in French A LOT. If you keep up with the book, which isn't hard at all, you'll find the class pretty easy. (Contrôles can be slightly tricky, but nothing too much.)  Beware silly grammar mistakes, they can be met with sarcasm!

Adorable and geuinely nice person, a little disorganized, obssessed with participation so do it right away, if she knows you are working hard she will take care of you, ask for help if you need it, be energetic

extremely disorganized and not always dependable. there aren't many choices for profs in the fr dept so i guess as far as the dept goes she is pretty good. the class is laid back.  just make sure she knows your name and that you participate.

A little disorganized (you may turn things in and then never see them again) and is known for unpredicatably assigning things that aren't on the syballus...but I adore her. She is very helpful and obviously cares about all her students and wants everyone to do well, which is a somewhat refreshing quality to find in a professor.

Phenomenal teacher and great class.  She is truly a gem!  So sweet and caring and willing to help.  She really does want you to do as well as you possibly can.  Her class was very very enjoyable, thanks to her and her style.  Don't slack off; work hard and you will do well.  Oh and smile and talk a lot, as she does!!  Go Mme. Waldron
She's a great teacher, I liked her a lot.
Always helpful, good sense of humor
Such a funny lady!
Nice lady, very helpful and sympathetic but her grading is unpredictable.  Still, made class interesting and fun and was very approachable.
She's so nice and helpful and her grading policy is definitely on the easy side as long as you participate in the class, which is interesting anyway.
Love her! Always willing to give help. Grading is not by a set rubric, and she definately pays attention to efforts and hard work. Very funny.
Overall, a great professor but I think that she doesn't grade anything. She'll just give you the grade she thinks you deserve. Luckily, most people get A's or B's.
Inspirational professor, but her grading is a bit suspect.
she might seem mean at first, but she's really a nice person and an okay teacher. her class is super fun and she grades pretty easily.
excessive busy work. subjective grading. average teaching although energetic.
Really nice prof who will go out of her way to help you...busy work at times, and assignments do take a considerable amount of time, esp essays...tests are fair and aren't bad if you study well...
Good Professor.  Always energetic.  Fair tests and essay assignments.  Will improve your French (especially speaking).  Some busy work that could be eliminated

LOVED Waldron. Though her grading system is unclear and you'll never see your assignments again (or much later at least), she's fun, entertaining, energetic, not afraid to correct you, and she'll make you confident.
One of the best professors I've had. Clear explanation. Well-prepared, structured lectures. Easy to follow. Too bad he's retiring from Cornell.

Man knows his stuff and his lectures are alright, albeit boring. However, he gives very few things that determine grade (10% HW, 35% Midterm, 55% Final) so your grade may suffer. Also rarely shows up to office hours, so it's very hard to get help from him. Even making appointments doesn't help - he just forgets.

If you haven't taken the equivalent of Calc III or more, do not take this class. I mean it, just don't. Calc III material is "introduced" with one or two examples in a lecture, with the rest of the lecture relying upon that prerequisite knowledge. Also class only has a midterm and a final, so your grade is up in the air for the entire semester.

Make sure you go to class. Lectures are extremely boring and make you want to go to sleep, but they're definitely important. Memorize the lecture notes if you want to do well. Do NOT only practice the HW problems because you will fail the midterm like half the class did (including me). Grading is left to the TAs, so can be rather harsh,

With the new changes to the department, He decided to make the class ridiculously hard. Handed out really easy psets and practice midterms only to give the class an extremely hard midterm (average was a C-). If you want to take this course, (1) you have to love theoretical math. If you don't, don't take the class. (2) memorize his lecture notes.

Definitely one of the top few professors in the Economics department! Although his accent is a bit heavy, you get used to it after a few classes if you're willing to listen. He's extremely clear with his explanations and writes very easy exams. However, he leaves too much in the hands of his TAs so grading turned out a bit harsh despite easy exams.

He's a nice guy and try hard to explain all the concepts, but his accent made me extremely sleepy... I went to every lecture but I have never stayed awake entire time ... The exams were not very hard, but sometimes I found the problem set pretty tough. I barely studied for this class except before hw due and before exams, but grade turned out well.
