Heidi is really so so sweet and is so understanding but she does not understand how a cornell student functions. She does not give A+ when they matter so so much here and she is heavy on group work to the point where our final project was a group project. She is so kind but a LOT of work
I loved the course structure and knowing the professor's expectations. The depth on the discussion boards was fantastic.
Attention to detail. The professor took the time to read the students weekly assignment and write a comment. The course was very informative. I also liked the weekly video the professor posted.

Well-designed course. Good-balance of reading + lectures. Discussion Board emphasis: great, but cumbersome -many in class do not post until late in the week or on the day the assignment is due; recommend 2 substantial DB posts per week instead of 3 . Gives timely thoughtful feedback. Is Inspiring, challenging, brilliant. Best Prof at Cornell.

Reid Friedson's classes are challenging and inspirational. I have taken two of his classes and walked away, not only with solid base in the subject matter, but also with a desire to learn more. There are expectations, certainly, but that's required if we are to grow. Take a class with Reid Friedson. You'll be glad that you did.
A real pleasure! Looking forward to having him again in a future course.

Taught Quantum Mechanics II. Very unintuitive course material, but this professor makes the course as intuitive as possible and has great explanations. Clearly knows what he's doing and makes this course tolerable.

Frank Wise is an incredible professor and lecturer. He cares deeply about the subject and the students, and really wants everyone to learn. He continually adapts the curriculum to fit the students needs and is always very understanding. One of the best professors I have ever had.
Prof. Wise is one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. He understands the material extremely well and is great at explaining it/answering questions.

Prof. Wise is a cool guy.  He knows a lot about nanotechnology and can explain it on a lower level so it is easy to comprehend by people who have no prior knowledge of the subject.  Very interesting course material.

Since the course does not have a textbook, all studying must be done from your in-class lecture notes and other resources Professor Wise provides. The lectures and labs are interesting, though often covers unfamiliar material. Overall, a decent class to take as your ENGRI, though somewhat difficult.

Prof Wise is certainly a remarkable instructor. His clarity and quality is apparent in his lecture notes and homeworks. And he does a great job relating the theory to real-world applications and technologies. Take any course he teaches and you will be more than happy.
His lectures are well planned and but he can also adapt to answer group specific questions.  He is also willing to help and is anxious to use questions as a teaching tool

My favorite professor/class first semester of freshman year.  The class material can get quite difficult at times, but if you go to lecture and the occasional office hours, Frank will clear things right up. Also, he manages to make even the stupidest question an opportunity to teach something cool.

Prof Wise knows his stuff more than almost all professors at Cornell, but the class can get frustrating, especially during the problem sets. Tests are a challenge, but fair. Office hours are quite useful. Don't try to do the homework by yourself, talk to other people.

Professor Wise is one of the best professors at Cornell. His lectures are well organized and clearly presented.  His tests are difficult but fair.  He very much wants his students to understand the material and becomes concerned when they have difficulties.
Great Lecturer, CS4220 is a HARD class with a lot of linear algebra

Really knows his stuff and explains things clearly (but in that way where you're listening in lecture and you're like "ahh yeah makes sense" but then you have to synthesize it outside of class and you're like "????"). Really wants to help. Homeworks were very difficult and time-consuming; the class groupchat was necessary.
Great lecturer, committed to teaching the material and open for questions. Enthusiastic about the subject, really enjoyed his class.

The best teacher I've had my entire life. Understands how to explain concepts thoroughly and precisely, leaving little room for ambiguity. Homework took me a VERY long time (more than most), but the class was still well worth it.
A really good professor. Really smart and welcome. Can be considered as the best professor I ever met at Cornell.
Good lecturer. Homeworks were quite difficult.

Would not recommend taking this class with him. I took it when COVID first started but think about it to this day. He's nice and it's an easy A, but I learned the literal bare minimum of linear algebra. I occasionally am embarrassed that I don't know linear algebra concepts I need in my STEM classes now. If I could go back I would take ENGI linalg.

Professor Nerode is a fine mathematician, and a very interesting person to listen to, but I unfortunately learned next to nothing in his class. He gave us an overview of the subject matter more than an explanation of it. The main ideas seemed to be there, but we never got any real practice in order to assimilate them.

While his lectures were often confusing, he was always open to meet outside of class. He is clearly extremely well read. He doesn't care about grades, but is interested in students getting the most they can out of the class and their investment. If you can show that you are interested and care about the material, the grades should follow.
Don't take his class if you want to learn the material. Literally didn't learn anything. Got an A in the class. What he teaches and what's on the tests are completely different.

He is a legend in the Math world, but he is old and lacks clarity during his lectures. However, discussion sections are helpful, and as long as you hand in all of your homework assignments, you should do well. Also, there were two in-class exams and no prelims nor finals. Get to know him though; he is a very interesting man.

Prof Nerode is an excellent person, and always ready to help. His lectures can be slightly unclear at times but if you study the material, its almost fine and the Prof is always there to spend time with you to help you understand. Willing to help out beyond his class. Homeworks are sometimes long and hard, but fairly graded and exams are quite easy

Nerode is a really nice guy. His lectures are pretty pointless since he mostly reads from his notes that are online anyway. However, those notes (which he wrote) are pretty good. Tests are pretty easy. Homeworks are a bit harder and kind of long but not terrible.

Prof. Nerode is kind, approachable, understanding, and overall just a great man! The fact that he's still teaching at the age of 81 explains why his lectures can at times be a bit difficult to follow. But he was very understanding when it came to prelim conflicts so he has my utmost respect. Would definitely take any other class with him!

Took linear algebra with Prof. Nerode in Spring 2013. Professor Nerode is a very kindhearted and caring man. He's a great person, but unfortunately not mumbles to himself in lecture, but that's totally understandable since he is 81. Problem sets were mostly all proof-based (great for math majors) while prelims only had computation-based questions.

Nerode is an amazing mathematician but it's just very hard to understand him because he lectures on such a high level.  He is getting older and he can be very impatient and incompetent at times.  The class was hell, the assignments were very tedious and people at the support center even said he is odd, to say the least.

He has decided to no longer use a textbook so he has his long printed lectures that he just reads in class so there is no point in going to lecture.  Homework is difficult and for me, going to TAs office hours were a must- his were useless.  He is a nice grader though.  I got a 33% on the first exam and I still got an A in the course.
No textbook for course. No need to attend lectures. Homework is hard but workable. Extremely easy exams.
He's nice in grading and test. Useless lectures.
Greatest professor ever! His tests are just like the sample tests. The first quintile on a prelim was 118...out of 120. Take any of his classes.

I think he's better at teaching history of mathematics/logic than analysis. Classes are usually unclear and it doesn't seem to make much of a difference if you go or not since reading the book by yourself gives pretty much the same result. Plus you won't have to decipher his handwriting if you just read the book.
I know this guy is brilliant, but he can't teach for his life.  Very unclear, rambles and cannot answer questions.  The class isn't so hard, though.
Lectures were absolutely useless the entire semester.  Learned jack.  Doesn't seem to work his own problems for exams so doesn't know exactly how doable (or not) his own exam is.

Prof. Nerode is a really nice guy.  Unfortunately, he doesn't even understand his notes.  All he does is read them off and get himself confused. Class is 100% useless and the homework is really hard to do with no teacher. ALWAYS go to SECTION. Tests are so easy.
The class was pretty easy but I still felt like I learned something.

The class is ridiculously easy in that you hardly have to do anything to do well on the tests. Even so, his lectures are useless and I could not understand a single thing he tried to explain. It doesn't help that it is also impossible to read his handwriting on the board.

I took a "math in perspective" class with him and one other student.  I didn't get a whole lot out of the class content wise, but he told fascinating and funny stories and anecdotes about the history of math and his associations with other famous mathematicians.

The most kind and compassionate professor on this campus!  You will all do well in his class because he doesnt care about grades as much as he cares about teaching you how to logic, reason, and think.

He's a brilliant man, I wish I could understand all he tried to teach us. I think that was the biggest problem - teaching on a level that most undergraduate students could understand. Fascinating and intelligent.

Lectures consisted of him reading to us off overheads (which usually had errors).  Never looked up during lectures and mumbled a lot.  Nice person, but lectures were useless.  Only 25% of the class came to the lectures.
Easy assignments, useless lectures

I took Professor Netravalli's class as a non-FSAD major and personally found the material a bit difficult to digest. However, Netravalli was very understanding and was available and enthusiastic to help during office hours. He even held a review session for the final exam. Overall very fair testing and wonderful professor!!

The Fibers, Fabrics and Finishes class was an interesting introductory course. Professor Netravali worked hard to make sure his students understood the material, which for the most part, was very basic. Be prepared to do a lot of memorizing though! Tests were extremely fair and straight-forward.

Amazing class. I learnt an amazing amount in this class. I expected it to suck, but he made it not only fun, but interesting. The tests were very understandable and easy and he is a great professor overall who loves to talk about fiber science. He's AWESOME.
Has a cool accent! Shows us random videos, and comments on work a lot.
Hard to follow his comments a lot of time, but he's entertaining enough... Class is pretty casual which is nice, and he's always available for help

I took this course with her and Sachse teaching. Originally in Sachse's section, I found him too fast and difficult to understand. I found Van der Meulen great. She explains quickly, but she gets to the point and is great, especially in office hours. She's actually quite understanding and just plain awesome, imo anyways.

The grading scheme was absolutely skewed as it set most students up to receive grades in the C range. Homework was crushing in its length and she talked too fast during lecture for anyone to adequately understand.
This class sucks ass!
Too much work for a 2 credit class. Projects and assignments were boring. Guest lecturers were unbearable. Highly unrecommended!

This class was on absolute disaster. The professor obviously did not want to be there. Grading was completely unfair.  No grading scheme was ever communicated to the students, homeworks were not returned, and no feedback was given to the students. The homework was pretty straight forward, but for some reason the average was about 75%.

great professor; very clear and passionate about her courses and research; very understanding and personable; very willing to help you out if you have specific questions or concerns; demanding in a good way; makes you think and teaches you a lot
No Comments
Very good professor.  I also don't know what that kid was thinking - she's also very attractive.

lacks ability to keep class interest and organize the course... lucky enough the class is merely 2 credit pass/fail so attendance is rarely nescessary... terribly unhelpful and bitter... perhaps because shes a female version of matt miller, even he may look better in a dress
No Comments

The class is straight-forward but the professor dislikes dissenting opinions. If you agree with everything he says, he'll give you an A/A- on assignments; if you try disagree or present a different theory, he will penalize you with a B/B-. If you're okay with compromising your personal opinions, you'll do well in this class.

friendly but awkward to talk to. seems to be nervous when you to talk to him, so i was never sure if he didn't want to answer my question or was just awkward. grading is easy. essay and finals are about taking notes of what he says and repeat them in your essay and final. dont even have to read, goes over same stuff in class.

THE WORST PROF AT THIS SCHOOL. killed all my interest in korea. extremely boring lectures, consists of whining about how everyone wronged korea and led to its problems. entire course is about han (resentment in korean mind) and does not allow you to talk abt anything besides this. 50% of grade based on final, which is brutal memorization. unfriendl

Great professor. Can be a little dry at times, but is extremely informed and a clear lecturer. Cares deeply about his students and it shows. Was my advisor and was always available to me. I always found his lectures to be interesting as well. Can be a little hard w/ the grading.

his teaching style is not too bad but he discourages independent thought. the material is interesting if you are willing to be interested. the only huge minus is the TA - she does not speak much english and is not very friendly.

no doubt about his knowledge and accomplishment in his area of study. great resource but unclear. takes on korean-style of teaching (i.e. don't question the material, just memorize.) would have been a better class with more dicussion and debate. TA was not helpful as her english was limited but hopefully there will be a new TA for future classes.

he's extremely knowledgeable about historical facts, but he completely discourages independent thought and new ideas. every time i introduced an original idea in my paper, he gave me a B+. every time i repeated exactly what he said, he gave me an A-. as a historian he's great. as a professor, he's the pinup of a very close minded individual.
though he may be a communist, he is relatively interesting (takes thing very seriously though), lectures pretty clearly and definately grades fairly.

Prof Shin is one of the only resources Korean students have on this "great" campus.  He serves his community in a great way, and with his expansive knowledge and relaxed personality, he can be a great person to learn from.

Great Class!  He seems a little awkward when lecturing, but will cancel class every so often.  I wish I took more from the class (I was having a horrible semester, so I slacked in this class ... and got away with it!).  Definitely engaged with his work.
Interesting lecture but the equations that you need for homework were never mentioned in lecture, don't take this if you really need the 1 credit.
The most disorganized class structure I've ever seen.
Solid introduction to PV and thermal solar technology
Nice guy. Confusing in lectures at times, but still good overall.
Very smart professor and great one-on-one or in small groups. Lectures can be a bit confusing - oftentimes, there are just recaps and future outlooks and no material actually discussed.

He is knowledgeable of the content, but doesn't seem to care much about the class itself. Many times, his lecture slides are incomplete in class. Course material is covered in lecture once, and never again. Prelims are incredibly in-depth and he provides no additional material for studying. Pop-quizzes are on very specific details from the readings

Prof. Mallett is very knowledgeable and I enjoyed the content, but I found the grading structure to be difficult to deal with, and ultimately dropped the class. Expect unreasonably hard pop quizzes occasionally. If you don't ace every test + the final paper, it's hard to get above a B+ as there is no curve and questions are weighted heavily.

Very knowledgeable professor of urban planning. Lacks personable skills to relate to students and takes topics too seriously. Harsh grader and brutal critic. Limited grades throughout the semester, many readings required, with potential to do poorly on pop quizzes due to exact fact memorization required. Learning potential is high, work hard.

Genuinely my favorite class at Cornell. He's funny and its really clear that he is passionate about the topics he teaches. His classes are fun and interesting and he actually care for his students. He always asks for feedback on what to teach and essay feedback is also really clear (if you do what he tells you, you'll get a good grade).
Do not take this class. Highly unclear grading criteria, and the lectures were dull and felt unbearably long. The contents he chose to speak about were absurd and mindless.

This class was basically just Prof. Manne getting 3 hours a week to talk about whatever issues he wanted to yap about, which made it SO GOOD because the best lectures are the ones that the lecturer is passionate about / has a lot to say about. He's a really opinionated guy but doesn't shy away from opposing takes. I think he is very based and cool.

Great professor. The class did not have any formal, powerpoint lectures and it was mainly discussion-based. The topics we covered in class were very thought-provoking and opposing ideas were valued. Professor Manne was a fair grader and seemed to genuinely care about his students. Overall, I would've loved to take another course with him!

Professor Manne is a great professor and his class is not too difficult at all. As long as you do the readings and pay attention in class you should be good for the papers/the final. Very light workload and he is very flexible with deadlines. Pretty easy and interesting class overall. Would recommend!
Professor Manne is awesome!!! His class was always a chill environment and he's flexible with deadlines. He genuinely cares about his students and I'd recommend taking his class to anyone!
Probably the best class I've had at Cornell

Professor Manne is a fantastic professor, he makes a boring subject extremely fun and interesting. Easy quizzes every week and papers are graded easily. Wish he taught more undergrad classes - best prof I have had
Never ever take this course. Not-caring personally to students. Boring lectures. Unclear grading criteria.

This class was taught with Julia Markovits as well, who was a really good teacher. Prof. Manne however was not the most clear speaker. This class felt quite quite long. Attendance is mandatory, and counts for like 20% which is great if you attend. Every class requires a blog post too on the readings.

I absolutely love Professor Manne. She is extremely respectful & caring of her students and is careful in covering the complex ethical issues explored in this course. I have truly never encountered a professor who seems to care as much about her students as she does. In addition, she is a brilliant, brilliant academic whose class is engaging & fun.
One of the kindest and most thoughtful professors I've had at Cornell! She explains the material super well and is very responsive to emails. Really accommodating as well.
Amazing prof and a great class. I'd highly recommend it!
Extremely smart, articulate, and kind.

Overall I think Kate was a great professor. One tip I would have for 3410 is to learn to take notes on discussion-based/interactive lectures. Also do the readings, but don't get held up on specifics; try to get the main idea. Her lecture style is interactive and might take getting used to. She is very responsive to emails etc. and very kind/helpful

The textbook is used heavily, and tests are hard, but neither is her fault. She helps you as much as you need it, and facilitates the class well. She will give you breaks in the form of good grades on projects if your grades are lacking in other areas.  Overall, a good, caring prof. Would recommend.
Very caring and very willing to help. The texts can be difficult at times. Still, I recommend her class.
Liked this class a lot.
In intro to iberian lit, she tries to make the material interesting.
Very interested in helping students! Not moody, but honest and approachable.
Very unexperienced and moody at times
If you do all the work and go to every class, you'll be fine. Just don't expect As on writing assignments unless your grammar is perfect.

She is well known in the community and places students well and knows her stuff. But she is kinda bitter to talk to. She isn't the most pleasant easy going person who is happy with her life. She can be acerbic and rude.

The assignments were hard at times but not unreasonably so. The textbook was written by Tardos (and others) specifically for this course, and the explanations are outstanding. The exams are manageable since the questions are similar to homework questions.

Professor Tardos is not a very clear speaker due to her heavy Hungarian accent. However, she is very willing to reexplain anything she says during lecture. Sometimes, she will gloss over material that she thinks you know, but, again, she will clarify anything needed. The homeworks are pretty easy; however, they can be poorly written and confusing.

pretty decent prof. A little confusing at times, but very approachable and willing to help. However, her Homeworks are frustrating, as many problems are vague/poorly worded. Overall decent/pretty easy class.

Worst professor at Cornell, can barely understand what she is saying and the problem sets were so terribly written and difficult to understand. I felt like it was an easy class that I just could not understand at the same time. I was much more confused after listening to lecture than before it. Terrible class, worst I have ever taken. Hate it.
Overall decent teacher. Somewhat unclear at times in lecture, but very friendly/approachable/nice person.
I really like her. She knows her material very well and she is extremely helpful during her office hours. She also seem to be very concern about students' well being as well.

Seems like she might know the material, but is very bad at teaching it. Isn't clear in lecture, and is bad at being precise a lot of the time on both homework questions and on examples, which is bad for a course that is in large part a logic course. Sounds like she's better in the higher courses.
A good teacher once you get used to her accent and handwriting.  Very willing to help students during her office hours.

Professor Royer lectures very well and is very considerate of students and student requests. I would definitely recommend going to his office hours. He is very clear on his expectations, but might occasionally miss one or two topics that you should read in the textbook or go ask about in office hours or after class.

Royer is an incredible professor. The class and material were pretty difficult as expected, but I have never seen such an adaptable lecturer. His lectures evolved over the course of the semester, becoming very helpful as he adapted and updated his lecturing style. He is very approachable and funny, and he brings that personality into his lectures.

I was surprised when this really young professor that mainly focuses on research was so effective at teaching. Thankfully, he works closely to align his course with Dr. Ritz (who has long organized this course and the exams) and the quality is about the same. Dr. Royer just takes it to the next level with his enthusiasm, care, and French accent.
Cool dude, fun stuff
needs more organization. we only used a few pages of each books we had to buy
Barry is the man. Really great guy especially if you get to know him outside of class. Fair grader. Take this class if you want to expand your mind and get a solid grade along the way

Extraordinarily interesting and mind expanding class.  He's one of the best profs I've had at Cornell and he really enjoys his job.  And he's definitely hot in one of those free thinker revolutionary kind of ways.

Recalling Neruda's assertion regarding those who fail to read Cortazar, those who do not take a course with Barry suffer from "a serious invisible disease which in time can have terrible consequences. Something similar to a man who has never tasted peaches. He would quietly become sadder...and, probably, little by little, he would lose his hair."
I adore Barry. He gives me hope for the world.
Very engaging and interested in the material he teaches; more of an alternative teacher who nonethless suceeds at causing his students to think creatively

He is an amazing guy and has a great teaching approach. Very much discussion based, but he really makes you think and become very interested in the subject. Be prepared to talk in class, but most likely you'll want to. I'm taking another class with him next semester. Only two papers required. no tests.

Interesting man, kind of a paradox. Very committed to his students, but never returns ANYTHING. Alternative teaching style, discussion-based but highly disorganized and often frustrating. You pretty much either love him or hate him. I hated him but I realized his merit and I learned a lot from his class. Not sure if I would take it again, though.

Policing and Prisons is an interesting class, but Maxwell ruins it with his lack of structure, organization, and overall knowledge of the subject. Although he is very passionate about the subject, he does not have a clue how to teach. You don't need to do any of the readings, or even show up to lecture.
Great teacher- chose great material, chose a great subject, lectured and led discussions passionately, intelligently, and thus engagingly.
think twice. show up to class, be interested, read the material. otherwise, sleep in.
best professor i've had by far
great

A very smart, well-read, insightful guy.  That said, his courses are poorly organized, his lectures contribute little to understanding the course material, and he is often hard to follow.  Good for 1-on-1 conversations, but not as a lecturer/instructor.

A tough, demanding teacher that will expand your mind and make you think like a good drug. Great 1-on-1 and at leading a class. committed to undergrads, treats you like an equal though he is very intelligent + accomplished. Highly recommended.

Strauss is legendary. Seriously, look him up. One of the best lecturers I've had at Cornell. Wish we had more like him as they are a dying breed. Sections are optional (still get 4 credits). If you take good notes in lecture, you don't need the readings. You'll do well if you can write well.

Professor Strauss is awesome. His lectures are very interesting and the amazing graphics to go with them are the icing on the cake. Kinda a lot of reading but manageable. Tests are doable but not a free A. This class was wonderful online, and if it was in person it would have been even better.

Excellent professor! Knows his stuff, helped cement the foundation of my knowledge of Classical history. His lectures are amazing and his class is exactly what a Humanities course should be. You learn a lot without an extraordinary amount of stress. His tests and essays target essential knowledge without bordering on unreasonable. Can be arrogant.

Quite possibly the best lecturer I have had at Cornell. Very clear and very engaging. You need to go to class and do the reading but, if you do, the exams and papers are very fair and are not graded harshly. I would also recommend doing the optional section. Just being forced to do the reading and having others to talk it over with helps a lot.

Love this professor. His lectures are incredible, his way of conveying information is engaging, and the content of his class is very interesting. Knows a lot about the subject, yet very supportive and always answers any questions in class. You really don't want to skip the lectures, because this is where 90% of exam material is covered. The best.

One of the most uptight and self-interested professors I have ever had. Refuses to respond to student emails and is extremely disinterested in student feedback, questions, and comments outside of class. Which is a shame, because the class subject matter itself is extremely interesting. Lectures are engaging if not a little disorganized.

Hands-down the best professor Ive had at Cornell. As previously mentioned, exams are based solely off of lecture material, so although attendance isnt taken, you really shouldnt be skipping class. Prof. Strauss really makes an effort to get to know all his students and genuinely enjoys teaching.

Requires extremely good skill in note taking. Strauss does entire lectures orally. The slides are only pictures to support his orally delivered material, as interesting as they may be. It is difficult to remember everything he said when the exam comes. There is no place to find past lecture material if you miss a class so don't skip class ever.
I had him as a freshman many years ago. He taught me how to write. Perhaps the most useful class, at any level, that I ever had.
Great professor. Lectures are very interesting. Very knowledgeable in his area. Strongly recommend.
Not too good, not too bad.

He's good, but not "amazing". He is not the best lecturer I have ever had and his lectures definitely do not feel like "story time." I would recommend him if you have an interest or background in the ancient world, but not if you're just looking for an elective.

He's ok..but an entire class on Greek History and you don't get to Aristotle? He spent time on the technicalities of naval battles in Ancient Greece instead of delving into Aristotle and Plato? He's a good lecturer, helpful, class isn't too bad if you take good notes. But unless you like military history, you'll be bored at times.
Lectures feel more like story-time to me, than class.  Beware though - Midterm/Final was all about identifying sometimes obscure people and terms - and attaching dates with everything.

I heart Professor Strauss!  Most profs who are as prominent in their fields as he is usually come across as pompous and arrogant, but Strauss is so down-to-earth and adorable.  Wonderful lecturer and very approachable in office hours.  You must take a class with him before graduating--he will truly go down as one of Cornell's best!

Barry is amazing.  He is the most professor-y professor I have ever met.  I love the class, and he just makes me smile.  He is funny, sweet, and enjoys long walks on Mediterranean beaches.  In summary: everyone at Cornell should take a Barry Strauss class.
Great lecturer, gives interesting points and his humurous. The class gives engaging material, and exams are not all that hard. One of the best history classes here (and I've taken a lot).
One of the best lecturers in the history department, engaging, interesting, and very fair class.

Dude, ask him to be your advisor anyway. (I did!  Yay!) Just because he's going on leave doesn't mean you won't be able to reach him when you need advice--it just means he's not teaching classes or holding office hours per-se.  His 256 class is awesome.
Great professor, very interesting material.
My favorite class this semester.  This guy's a wonderful lecturer, and the readings are amusing.  Try to get into the section that he leads.  You will love this class.
I would recommend any course by this professor. He is a wonderful lecturer
His honors seminar is a breeze and he is so chill.
Course is challenging but lectures are clear and if you complete the reading you will love the class.
This class was my favorite.  He is a great lecturer and a very knowledgeable historian. I can't wait to take his next class in the spring.
Amazing teacher.  2 papers, each of which can be rewritten, 2 prelims and a final which are very easy if you do the (fairly light) reading.  Really organized, great class.
The only class where I have not missed a single lecture. Take anything he is teaching.
Amazing teacher--wish he wasn't going on leave!  *wants and advisor*
coolest person ever
Excellent. whish he did not go on sabbatical
Loved his class....examination difficult
best ever...i love barry strauss

Professor Mao is a nice lady but is super hard to understand during her lectures. She reads directly off of the slides so class gets slightly repetitive. There was no attendance taken but she does do WSJ discussions at the beginning of class. There were 3 prelims in class and a final so lots of tests.

Lectures are dry and she cold calls every single class. She doesn't explain well so it's difficult to participate as often as she wants. But, she is really caring and wants you to do well. LOTS of office hours. Tests are exactly like homework, and she gives so much partial credit you could get every problem wrong and still get a good grade.

Professor Li is newer, so there are definitely some small organizational kinks to the course. However, the course as a whole is very interesting, and the professor is clearly very passionate about the subject. He does a good job of letting students know what content is emphasized on each prelim, and cares a lot about the success of the course.
Really helpful and caring guy - he reached out to me individually when I wasn't doing well and it meant a lot.

Professor Buckley is an amazing teacher, I went to his office hours every week because I didn't understand a lot of the lectures. He really took the time to help me learn and understand. With this class though you can not just memorize. You really have to apply the concepts. I think I could have gotten an B or A if I really tried. Lec is boring.
Great lecturer that cares a lot about his students and will do anything to help you out!

Absolutely amazing! Best professor I've ever had. Takes all the bio concepts and info and relates it back to everyday life. Lectures are extremely interesting and go at the perfect pace. Definitely take this class!

One of the greatest professors! He made me a lot more interested in biology. He respects the students a lot and as well as every silly question a student might ask, whenever in class or office hours or emails. Additionally he always smiles at you!!! If he is going to teach another higher level class, I would definitely take whatever the subject is.
One of the best biology professors! Very inspiring.
In  my opinion he gives the best lectures in all of Cornell! Absolute gem! He teaches with a style that just gets to you and makes you want to learn more about microbiology.

Professor Pereboom made what I thought would be a really dull class engaging and thought-provoking - he really cares about all the students and class discussing, which makes you actually want to go to lectures. Great class!

pereboom is amazing. i was scared at the content at first cuz it seemed like a different language especially cuz philosophy is not my major, but he's so good at explaining things. he leads great discussions!! he knows so much about Kant and determinism/free will he's brilliant 10/10

Spectacular professor, and the class is a great introduction to people unfamiliar with Philosophy. If you're interested in dipping your feet in the field- a must take; Professor Pereboom makes even the more boring history of Philosophy parts interesting to listen to in lecture. Discussion section mandatory, lecture optional.

This man is one of the greatest professors at this university. He is such a smart individual but isn't arrogant or hard to approach. He runs the course very smoothly and fairly: two essays and two exams, but he gives you study questions for the exams and holds reviews for the exams. The only negative would be getting a bad TA to grade your essay.

Among the best that Cornell has to offer. 1) well-respected contributor to his field, 2) very nice person, very entertaining sense of humor in lectures, 3) generously fields questions in & outside of class, w/ great feedback 4) teaches lectures  so interesting they're almost effortless

I cannot recommend Pereboom enough. He is a great teacher, a friendly person, and a passionate philosopher. Though I had little to contribute to his seminars I enjoyed simply listening to the back and forth between him and us students. He grants generous extensions, gives clear advice on improving your work, and grades kindly. Take his courses.

He knows the material very well and does a great job of keeping lectures interesting. He's less involved in the papers (unless you go to get help from him, in which case he'll be extremely helpful), but he gives you a list of test questions before each test, so there's no reason to do poorly. Definitely recommend.
Undoubtedly one of the best professors at Cornell. Extremely smart and really friendly as well. I'd recommend him to anyone.
Great guy, incredibly boring lecture. More like a history of philosophy, which is very dry.

Derk is an awesome guy, and modern philosophy is relatively easy (I believe the median grade is around A-). The readings can be a little difficult (esp Kant). Also the final/midterm is awesome because he gives out the questions beforehand. TAs can be hit or miss (watch out for birch). Main complaint is lecture is unnecessary.
Prof. Pereboom is great! He has a great insight in the topics, which he teaches with great clarity and precision. If you want to learn about Modern Philosophy, this is the class to take.

(Modern Philosophy)Derk was great. He is very approachable and friendly, and I had no reservations about asking questions. The class was really easy too, and to get the most out of it one has to be self motivated to do the readings. His lectures often lacked discernible structure, but class was still very stimulating and a pleasure to attend.

Dr. Pereboom is my favorite professor so far. I highly encourage taking his course! The material is very difficult, but don't let that scare you. He is extremely helpful. Just put in some work and you're guaranteed a good grade :)

Derk encourages discussion but is also a great lecturer. He knows everything about metaphysics but is also really knowledgeable about related scientific theories. The more work you put into the class, the more you get out of it. Readings seem optional because Derk covers everything but DO IT ANYWAY.

The GOAT of ORIE himself. Very engaging lecturer. Participation is based on how much you answer or ask in lecture, and he tries to remember everyone's names. Clear and concise lectures, will explain until students understand. Weekly graded HW and python lab sessions. Overall, not the easiest ENGRI but definitely learnt a lot.
So bad! He makes up your participation grade and gives extremely long HW every week. Combined with the fact that he can't teach and is super disrispectful in office hours.
The homework assignments are so complicated and poorly explained that you almost have to go to office hours to be able to complete them.
doesnt explain concepts in depth during lectures, outside of class readings are hard to understand on your own

Doesn't answer questions very well, doesn't explain material well or will be a bit snide if you have questions about something that has already been covered. Very harsh grader for homework and no collaboration allowed for homework which somewhat defeats the purpose of learning new material

David Shmoys is the best lecturer/professor I have had so far. He is very generous and understanding with grading, and truly cares about each student(knows everyones names, very accommodating). He is very passionate about ORIE, and every lecture I experienced with him clearly shows this passion.

Very smart, caring, and respectful. His homework assignments were pretty hard. Office hours would always be full of students seeking help on the hw. His lectures were interesting, but sometimes he explained things too fast and moved on quickly. I wish he had worked through more problems with the class to teach us how to apply the concepts better.

I actually love this guy. Amazing teacher on every level. Gave great insight into the ORE field, and was super passionate about the material. I was originally on the fence about majoring in this, but I have decided to after taking his class.

Epic professor, wants to make the class curious about the topics rather than have them memorize anything. Organized lectures and fair exams. Homework requires a lot of work, but its not that hard if you start early. Probably the best prof you can get for this class. A very good class to take with him if you're unsure about ORIE/ like math-cs stuff.
Awesome professor. Explains everything well and makes it interesting.
Very good prof.  This intro to OR class gave me a great idea as to what the field was like. The tests were very fair, and his office hours are extremely helpful.
Yo this cat was balling, son. And the p-sets and prelims were actually pretty fun in this class, much better than 320.
no comment.
A great teacher
never thought i would actually think a cs professor was good
No Comments
No Comments
Good professor.  enthusiastic.  So what if he's short?  Short people make good professors too.  And he's a great example.
The difficulty is progressive. The final outcome is impressive. ANSYS and MATLAB in the pocket.
Really good professor. One of the only classes that will remind you that you are at Cornell University!!! It's a lot of work but its really worth it. Every single engineer should take this class!
great
One of the hardest classes I took at Cornell. That said, by far the most useful, and applicable to my life as an engineer. FEA is really worth understanding.
Intense course. Homework is not easy but extremely helpful. Lectures are really good.

Difficult course but you can succeed;attend lecture, study the lecture notes, and attend office hours. The professor was a good lecturer who wrote clear, thorough notes. This course is a great resume enhancer because of its applicability to industry. It also gives solid theoretical understanding and the professor is very willing to be a reference.

Lecture was disorganized, usually unclear, and he taught only the hardest parts of the material in class, requiring studying through the lecture slides to learn the rest. Group homeworks were exceptionally hard, and frequently not helpful. First exam was brutal, second was OK. Final project was a lot of work, though leniently graded.
A professor who's only interest is productivity. Α successful teacher, but a failed educator and leader. Students are not slaves, but critical spirits..

During a recent interview, I was asked questions related to FEM/FEA and I was able to draw my answers directly from this course. The interviewers literally started taking me much more seriously after I explained some of these things in detail. I've never been as challenged as I was in this course, but it has paid off greatly.

The course gives an all-around perception of the finite element method. The methods are basic in FEM but they are of great importance in the further study. The Professor gives excellent presentations by introducing the most core things in limited time. It's the most impressive course I've taken. Though I didn't master everything, I learned a lot!

One of the hardest classes for an undergraduate. His comments are all caustic & sarcastic which over an extent makes you feel sick & dizzy! He is good at teaching but sitting in class can be painful because of his comments. His TA's just cannot speak English - it sucks!

This class was the most valuable class I've taken for my Master's degree. The material was complex, but explained well. Zabaras had thorough slides and the material was hard at times but possible to understand. I really don't think my education would be complete without this class. It's so valuable!!!
Useful class for Graduate students.
If you don't like somebody, send him to this class. Terrible!
Studying FEM was an experience. It was not easy for sure, but I believe it is going to repay big time later. I like the way the entire program is structured...its fundamental!!

Interesting material. Professor Zabaras is one of the smartest and funniest professors I have had at Cornell. Lectures are enjoyable. Do NOT take this class if you do not plan to work very hard, but if you are looking to actually learn the material, this is THE class to take.
definitely one of my hardest classes at cornell. many hours spent and near-allnighters pulled. useful class though. the subject is really good.
This was the hardest course I have taken at Cornell.  Zabaras expects hard work and genuine quality work. He has high expectations, but he is fair.

The course was fun, lots of sleepless nights, tough mathematical slides but you get a hang of them in the end. Assignments got us all crazy & exams were not so bad! He is extremely intelligent & expects his class to perform & apply common sense!

Extremely difficult class, but if you put enough effort and time into it, it can be very rewarding. The lectures can be both impossibly confusing and extremely interesting, and I've been on both ends of the spectrum in this class. Pay attention, go to office hours, and put a lot of effort in, and it will be worth your while.

Very difficult class.  Was his first time teaching it this year but lectures were clear and slides/notes pretty complete.  You can learn a lot but you need to put in a lot of time for the homework and to understand the material.  Exams were very difficult, apparently the whole class did poorly.  Requires good understanding of previous material in h
it is a rewarding class

Dr. Zabaras is great professor. He explains complicated material in a clear manner and with real world examples and humor. In office hours he is very helpful. I recommend going to his office hours if you need something explained. To some students he come off as stand-off-ish or aloof, but he is a nice a guy.
Great class - challenging, but he's extremely helpful. Really wish more classes were structured the same.
Just...don't take his class...unless you have no choice

Zabaras's course is definitely more difficult than the other thermo lecture. However, the material is much more interesting and he really knows how to engage you with it and teach you it. You need to attend all of his lectures and make sure you spend plenty of time on all the homework, but if you do all of this the course is definitely doable.

Thermo with Prof Zabaras has been the most intellectually engaging and rewarding class I've taken. My understanding of calculus was enhanced by taking his class because the math is so tightly integrated into the thermo concepts. The professor himself has a sense of humor worth attending every lecture for. Meticulous work, but rewarding class.

Whoever said Thermo is horrible has never had Professor Zabaras, or is a real slacker ! Yes the course is challenging, but if you work you can do really well in it !  And Professor Zabaras makes lectures FUN !!! (not to mention : interesting ! ) This class was the highlight of my semester !
His section is MUCH harder than the other ones.

Great professor. He really cares that his students understand the material and is very willing to help you out if you show you are trying. You can really learn a lot from him if you pay attention.  Office hours are a must.

Zabaras understands thermo at its depths, and about once every lecture you get to have that feeling of understanding. He really shows how the math reveals the underlying concepts of the subject. Probably the first time you'll see actual chemistry (with calculus).  The course requires a good amount of work. Great professor, take this to learn.
class as described. A++++++ professor. would take again :)
Cold and unhelpful.  Not a great professor, and he doesn't seem like he cares about his students.
Helpful but gets angry
asdf

his class is "tough" but Zabaras won't let you down in the end as long as you work hard.  Also, he has an extraordinary memory.. so you better not skip his classes. Even though he doesn't know your name, he might remember your face. take this class!!!
go to section

This guy is nuts!  Be prepared to work hard and learn even more.  Don't even think of skipping lecture.  Zabaras explains things very quickly and efficiently.  In the end your grade is dependent on him knowing that you know the material - go to office hours!

His class is definitely harder, but if you go to his office hours, he is more than willing to help you out.  (I prefer his O.H.'s rather than the TA's O.H.'s)  He wants you to learn.   Also, the homeworks are hard, but they are relevant to what he tests you on.  Finally, don't let him catch you sleeping in class!

Professor Zabaras is the man. He made a potentially boring class very interesting by showing how thermodynamics was used in real life situations. His humor and honesty in class also makes his teaching very attractive. One of the best professors I've ever had. I don't know why some people didn't do well on some exams, they were just hw problems.

BEST Prof. Crazy, Sarcastic, Zany, Hilarious.  This guy single-handedly made Thermo fun.  Best memory:  He pulled out a transparency one time full of this long-winded derivation on some enthalphy property or something and just as we get done copying, he pulls it away and said in the goofiest voice- Just kidding folks u werent supposed to copy that.

Amazing teacher.  He really cares about his students and doesn't let you slack off.  He will help you (and like you a lot more) if you show that you are trying and go to office hours.  Exams are hard, but not impossible if you do the homeworks and learn the material.  Hilarious in class.  Makes an otherwise dry/challenging class interesting.
Incredible teacher, best professor i have had, but most difficult class I have taken also... Good luck, give it a shot... hes crazy
Class is tuff, but Zabaras is the man.  He's goofy and hilarious in lectures. Don't fall asleep though or he'll pick on you.  Great guy.  Take his course if your not afraid of a challenge.

He's CRAZY!  That being said, good class.  It was a LOT of work, go to office hrs for HW (makes up more of the grade than he lets on). If you understand the HW and examples in the book, should do decently in the class (that means a B+ or better).  He actually is very nice and helpful is he knows you're trying. Actually learned a lot. Good Luck!

may come out as tough prof, but if u show that u care for the subject and put work into it, he'll help u. do NOT fall asleep in his lecture if u don't wanna get picked on. exams aren't that bad if u do ur hw and do practice prelims. office hrs r "must" to understand hw tho... good luck :)

First of all crazy, but once you get past that he's alright.  Very demanding when it comes to effort put in, but he promises that we will be happy at the end of the semester.  Doesn't worry about whether you like him or not.  Responds very well to those who go to office hours seeking extra help.
Moved way too fast and way beyond what the other 221 course was teaching.  Altered the way the prelims were given and made it a lot better.

Spends a long time on derivations.  He's rushed the class so we're now covering material my TA has never seen. He's threatening to ignore the lowest 20% of the class in determing the mean and grading the class. Gets mad if you don't go to lecture.
He is on an ego-trip with his class and is leaving students behind.  We are far ahead of the other lecture section, yet we understand very little (evidenced by our last prelim score distribution).
No Comments
Hard and extremely demanding.  Comes across as kind of a jerk in class, but if you show up in his office and demonstrate you're putting effort into the class he'll respond well to you.

BTRY 3090 not 5954- I'm not sure how to add another course. I took this class as a statistics major elective and I was close to dropping it before the first prelim but I'm SO glad I didn't. This class was possibly the most useful and applicable class I've taken so far, and Professor Das was so caring and invested in us. It was hard but so worth it!
strict criteria and non-sensical grading expectations. The workload is not reasonable and the instruction is vague for all the assignments. AVOID this professor
too many useless group projects. heavy workload. do not take this class if possible!!!!

She is just sharing her working experience when she was working at a consulting company, which may not be suitable for everyone. Also, she likes to make everything as a group assignment, even if a 1-2 page assignment, which is extremely meaningless. So much homework. Not sure why Cornell hires her and gives this course. Nitpicky and troublemaking.
Took this course in fall 2022. New added core course, no idea why it exists and why she is here to teach. Totally useless.

I took BTRY 3090 with her and I really enjoyed it. The class content is not easy, but she's an excellent lecturer, and she really cares about her students, although it did not seem that way the first month of class. It took a little while to warm up but I would definitely take another class with her again. The prelims are hard but manageable.

I gave one point because RMF couldn't receive a negative score. She is an exceptionally unkind instructor with a strong sense of self-righteousness. too intense. RUN don't take please

Great professor, very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about inequality, poverty, race, and families. Classes are mostly discussion based, so participation based on readings (which is pretty heavy, but very fascinating) is crucial. This was easily one of my favorite classes at Cornell, and one in which I learned a ton.

The class is seminar based so you need to do the readings. Maureen is really passionate about the material and wants you to engage with the readings which aren't hard to grasp. Speak up in class, relate the material to qualitative methods & soc. theory, and you're good!
Great!

Definitely not "nice" as some people said below. Has an attitude. Definitely take another policy class in PAM, this one may be a little easier but there are other PAM courses that are just as easy and much better.
Nice easy PAM class. You don't really need to go to class just do the textbook readings. She's really nice too
Professor Waller's research work on poverty and families was especially interesting.
Pretty interesting class, a little basic and repetitive in the beginning, but it gets better. Some cool projects and tests are pretty fair. Nice woman doing interesting research in the field.
Class material can be repetitive, but very nice woman who is doing a lot of the research you learn about in class. Tests are pretty easy and there are some interesting projects.
Boring, but easy A.

makes this class way more difficult than it needs to be.  extremely boring and i don't recommend her at all.  try taking the same class with a different prof, or skip it altogether if possible.  sometimes people would laugh at her, not with her.
Unbelievable professor. Easily the best lecturer at Cornell. She is a humble genius who steers the conversation in such a way as to be unimposing but also critical

Really great history class that pushes you to think of the big picture rather than just regurgitating events. Readings were all extremely interesting. A bit of a tough grader on the essays but she values improvements and gives a grade based off performance not numbers. Great class overall

Gives complete control of grades to TA probably with instructions to grade tough because you usually do not have the right to question. Material is interesting, but you are encouraged to follow her view on the subject matters even though her class is mentioned as open to debate. Would not recommend taking it unless absolutely necessary.

TA grades the papers, very unfairly. Prof Ghosh is good but readings are boring and hard to digest. She gives the control to TA completely. Discouraged to challenge your grade in class. Grossly unfair
One of the best lecturers I've had. As an engineering student I usually don't enjoy humanities courses but Ghosh was different. I can't imagine what someone who actually likes humanities would think!

Probably my best professor at cornell.  Her lectures were very organized and helped to explain the readings.  She is very helpful and open to questions (no matter how basic).  She grades very fairly and gives good comments.  I highly recommend Hist275 (it also fulfills a LOT of the A&S requirements).
Really good professor. Engaging lectures, extremely helpful and nice. Fair grading and good workload. Lots of academic readings. Recommended

Class consisted of 2 5-page essays, a midterm examination, and a final examination. Both examinations were in-class and a choice of essay topics. Reading assignments were moderate and interesting. The class is excellently organized and Prof. Ghosh is very articulate and interesting.

She is brilliant and articulate.  She's friendly, although she can seem a little brusque and not that personable.  I'm learning a LOT in her class, although there is a lot of very difficult reading.  She cares about teaching and wants her students to be engaged.

Shes not for everybody, as you can see by the sharp divide on reviews. Shes very strict with deadlines and making sure you are in class and engaged, which rubs many people the wrong way. But she truly does care about the students and will go out of her way to make sure you are doing well.

Likes student questions but will ask them to shelve the discussion til after class if time's an issue. Requires airtight logicexplanation on HW. "Harsh" bc she doesn't allow laziness, rudeness, or excuses from the students - expects people to read posted announcements, doesn't accept the "I forgot" and "I'm really busy" excuses for late work, etc

You will do matching markets of basically everything you could ever think of. She was unclear most of the time; don't expect much of an explanation on concepts beyond what's already on the slides. You also don't have much in the way of other sources to consult for help on HWs since 1) there's no textbook and 2) the subject matter is hard to Google.

She is awful. Subjective grading, not based on any real evidence. Condescending. Will not listen. Try not to argue with her. Material gets old really quickly as she spends 8 weeks covering matching algorithms. Boring after a while and it gets hard to pay attention in class. Do not take just because you liked Networks I (which is an amazing class).

Nicest professor I've had at Cornell by a long shot. People who complained about her "arrogance" and "harshness" are simply those who went into her class with the intention of getting an easy A but ultimately failed. She's extremely fair to her students and she is constantly trying to improve her lecture style by asking for feedback.

amazingly unclear. half of students get what shes talking about and she tells the anyone who's confused to learn it on their own, do extra reading, or see her outside of class which happens 5-10 times per class.  i'll also echo the arrogance statement - seems she feels insecure and tries to make up for it by being condescending to students

She is very clear in lectures and consistently goes over material several times to make sure that students have a firm grasp on it. However, her grading can be a bit arbitrary and you could end losing many points for one mistake (i.e. very little partial credit).
Extremely unfriendly and arrogant during her office hours. Do not try to argue with her or you're doomed. Overall the worst professor in CS/IS department.

This was Prof. Ghosh's first ever course and I thought she did a very good job. Unfortunately, the students came from very diverse backgrounds so some found it easy and others found it more difficult. In all I enjoyed the class alot
Prof. Ghosh was the worst professor I've had at Cornell. Not very helpful, subtly arrogant, and does not present/lecture well. A class with her is most likely not worth your time.

Not the best lecturer. Can harshly grade. We spent 8 whole weeks on matching markets, which got old way too quickly. If you were interested by Networks I, do not take this class. It's not as interesting, nor is the class as good. Avoid if possible.

One of my favorite teachers/professors ever! It felt less like a formal student-teacher relationship, and more like a relationship of mutual respect. She's happy to meet with you for office hours, which you might need, since she's picky about thesis. She is very eccentric, but it creates an incredibly lively and entertaining in-class environment.

I will agree that she is very scatterbrained, but she keeps class very entertaining and is passionate about what she teaches. Does say some very odd comments but she was not racist in MY class (I have seen some comments saying she was in theirs, which I don't doubt). Lots and lots of work, but easy grading. Brought homemade bread on last day!
No African American would ever claim another African person's lived experience with racial microagressions to be untruthful. This is all I will say about the comment below.

She is chaotic but her energy is infectious and if you put in effort she responds really well in her grading. 

I had no problem as an African American student. I obviously am concerned by the comments on this site but I asked other former students about their feelings and they were all super positive.

Avoid at all costs. Extremely disorganized and if you are a student color, prepare to be intimidated.

I agree with past comments that she's all over the place. Her class is literally a chaotic mess. Also, shes had a few "problematic" comments to say about peope of color. I dont recommend taking any class with her.

Like some of the other comments mentioned, she is a bit eccentric and her instructions are often unclear. However, the class was a genuinely enriching experience and fostered an intimate, introspective environment. She can be intimidating and does call on people at random, but sincerely cares about students. My Spanish noticeably improved.

Genuinely cares about students and takes time to meet with them outside of class. Passionate about her subject. Somewhat disorganized and gives instructions that are often confusing. Can be hard to figure out what she expects from students on the assignments.

Great professor! She is kooky in a good way. Her class is structured like an AP English class but with Spanish literature and of course only using Spanish! There's a lot of reading and a lot of writing. But that's about it---no tests! She's very easy to plan a meeting with and will give you feedback. She also gives a lot of extra credit opportunit

She's nice and flexible about deadlines, and her grading isn't bad. The papers themselves are short and easy, but there is a lot of reading for a "writing workshop." Her instructions are often confusing/unclear, and it feels like she imposes her own perspective of the readings onto us, so any conclusions we make about them are heavily guided.
She's really wacky and amazing. I love her. She does grade a lot of papers like you'll get homework every day but it's super easy to follow and she offers lots of extra credit.

This lady is bomb. Many people can't handle the class and thats understandable but if you are ready to be challenged and learn Cecelia is the ideal prof. She makes you work for your grade but the classes she teachers are wildly different from the rest at Cornell and it's a very fun break from the norm

I am seeing a lot of negative comments below, but Cecilia Lawless is one of the best professors at Cornell. She definitely pushed me beyond what I thought my limit was and this class perfected my Spanish writing. Yes, perhaps she would forget some deadlines, but as long as you check your email, all of her instructions are there. She is the best.

She's amazing teacher. I was quite competent and spanish and still needed a tutor for her essays from time to time. I ended up with an A in the class (i was actually aiming for an A+ since i went to soooo many extra credits) so I am happy. She is incredibly sweet, interesting, and fascinating!!!! I was forced to take the class b/c of the rquirement

My Spanish really improved in Cecilia's class.  For introductory level courses, I'd imagine she's a bit overwhelming, but if you're a Spanish Major/Minor, you already have a passion for the language and would enjoy her class.
The class can be a little unorganized and homework-heavy, but she's very approachable and definitely cares about you if you show you're trying. A

Cecilia cares most about the quality of effort you put into the class. The essays are not too long, and she makes sure your writing and speaking improves over the semester. The reading material, discussions, and assignments are interesting and relevant. If you participate, don't miss class, and care, you will do well. Fair grader. Highly respected.

Absolutely incredible. She definitely makes you work for the class, but she often allows late work, gives extra credit, and gives meaningful feedback. Plus, she's always enthusiastic about class discussion, she'll genuinely care about you (if you put effort in), and her assignments are very open and thought-provoking. I wish she taught above 2180!!

I absolutely loved having Cecilia as a professor.  She is quite scatterbrained but she is so passionate about what she is teaching and she really does care about students.  My writing improved incredibly this semester, not just in Spanish but in English too.  I'm hoping to take a class of hers next semester, too.
Prof. Lawless changed my life; I will never forget her.

No, she doesn't know what time it is and yes, she is eccentric, but Cecilia is a passionate, articulate professor and I will be forever grateful I signed up for a class with her. She cares personally about students and is incredibly encouraging if you put in the work. Take the time to go to her office hours, even if it's just to chat!

she's an amazingly passionate teacher who really knows her stuff. sure she's disorganized but the assignments are super open ended so you can literally write about anything. she's a pretty interesting lady who will genuinely care about you and how much you learn. EASY EASY EASY GRADER. if you show genuine interest you'll get at least an A

She takes a bit of getting used to. She is a bit disorganized and never knows what time it is, and her assignment directions can be a bit confusing. However, she is very goodhearted and genuinely tries to help students if they tell her they are having trouble. She is passionate about Spanish and indigenous peoples. Class helped my Spanish so much!!

She is a little bit "loca."  Often arrives to class in a fluster and is somewhat disorganized.  Sometimes her assignment directions make no sense.  However, she is a thoughtful professor who is willing to extend deadlines if needed.  She also cares deeply about her students and is always willing to help.  She's worth putting up with.

Cecilia is a professor for people who really care about spanish. She knows who's serious and who's just filling a requirement. I've taken several of her classes. She's a bit confusing in terms of assignments and her style is a bit peculiar, but if you want to have legitimate skill and experience w/ the Spanish language, and you work hard, shes 4 u

Horribly disorganized & unable to properly communicate. Gets angry with class when we can't figure out what's supposed to be happening. Assignments are somewhat bogus & a lot a of work.
