I would not take another class with her even if I had to switch to French.

My Spanish improved by leaps and bounds in this class; my writing is now more or less automatic, and my speaking is more fluid.  Of the 2 professors teaching this course, Sra. Lawless the more laid-back one.  All assignments and exams are written, and the focus is more on analyzing Spanish lit. and films than filling out grammar worksheets.

I really liked Spanish before I took this class, and she's not horrible or anything, but I just didn't feel I learned very much.  She seems disorganized and though she starts out with a syllabus, it quickly becomes modified-again and again. We didn't use text books so much--more in class discussion.  Homework regularly
Pretty bad, avoid at all costs.
Ridiculous essays. A bunch of psychobable and pseudo-philosophy. Horrid accent.

At first she may seem a little bit distant or above her students. But if you do the readings and truly participate she absolutely has a lot to offer, though her arguments can be complex sometimes, especially if you have not done the readings!

A really enthusiastic educator....watch out for her distinctive smell, you'll start to notice that all your Spanish notebooks smell like her. She's not good with technology or emails so make sure that you get on her class list serve.
You have to try in her class, as long as you do, you will be ok. A's are rare in her class, but it's pretty easy to get B's. Just go to class and participate every now and then.

Though not an easy class, Cecilia tries very hard to get you interested. Some students may say that she is tough, but how else are you going to learn Spanish? Overall, I really like her teaching style.
No Comments

I REALLY liked Cecilia. After my first spanish instructor left on pregnancy leave with only 4 weeks left in class, Cecilia came in and blew us all away. Thought extremely eccentric, she is a great teacher. She really pushes you to speak spanish which only helps you. She obviously cares about making you learn and not just get though the class.
An excellent teacher who instills analytical strategies into her students while challenging them to develop their own unique voice to nurture.
Horrible teacher!  Unorganized and even ****.  I would not advise anyone to take her EVER!  It's a shame she is still teaching.
HORRIBLE, HORRIBLE, HORRIBLE!
Very unorganized(ie never came to class with a watch, never even brought pens!). During office hours she does not help at all, and only seems to want to leave.
Very kind professor.  Extremely helpful if you approach her.

John Bunge knows so much about the statistics field and isn't afraid to spend entire lectures discussing an interesting hot topic, such as the replication crisis. He followed the textbook pretty closely, and exams and HW were reasonable. You should definitely go to lecture because he was so funny and gave great advice to stats majors.

JB is an amazing and passionate professor. He cares more that you truly understand the material more than anything else. Even though his class was at 8:40 in the morning, it was still one of my favourite classes and I tried not to miss a single lecture. Highly recommend taking this class if youre interested in stats.

One of the more interesting stats advanced electives. He makes the material interesting and has a generous grading policy with hw being worth 50%. However, he's a bit lazy as he posts the past prelims before the midterm but he doesn't post solutions which makes it hard to study. Also need to go to class because there's no textbook nor online notes.

An amazing professor who truly cares about his students and takes the time to respond to emails about homework. Most of your grade is homework, which is straight forward if you attend lecture, while most other classes at Cornell place much larger emphasis on exams (65-85%). He gives you every opportunity to do well in his class.

Best statistics professor and best statistics course I have had at Cornell.  Professor Bunge is hilarious, and he actually knows how to teach statistics.  He goes back to the basics at the beginning of the class, but it was much appreciated; it was the first time I had actually been taught ANOVA properly!  Could not give a higher recommendation!
Best statistics professor at Cornell. Take his courses if you are taking any stats courses at Cornell
He is the best statistics professor I have ever had! Take him before you leave Cornell.

Prof. Bunge was definately one of my favorate profs at Cornell. He was an extremely knowledgable guy in both statistics as theory and the current state of statistics.  I actually learned useful information in his class, and although I did not have to really take any notes, I looked forward to his lectures.

Get there early. He starts writing notes before lecture that you need. He makes mistakes-just writes the wrong stuff, and has gotten corrected on concepts by students. He starts 3-4 sentences at once and finishes 1. He does everything he can to avoid answering questions. Hes very smart, but get ready to teach the class to yourself. Tas r chill

Jumps back and froth between topics during lecture. Legible handwriting. Long problem sets. Was missing for some crucial lectures that the grad TA ended up giving which resulted in an average of 50 on the final.

Prof Stroock is a great professor. Not only does he engage the students in class in via posing questions, but cares to get to know them on a personal level too. He's great 1-1 if you're having difficulty with the course, but just raising your hand and asking the question during lecture doesn't bother him in the least (unlike some other professors).

His lectures were always pretty clear. He was precise with how he worded things, and I was rarely ever confused by how he taught. Not an exciting lecturer, but he certainly gets the job done well. Pretty nice guy.
Pretty good professor - has clear lecturing style and engages class by posing questions frequently.

Elizabeth Meyer clearly cares about printmaking - but her feedback is semi-helpful at best and downright demeaning at worst. I frequently was given better direction by the TA and technician. At least for introduction to Print, the workload was intense.
Loved this Intro to Printmaking! At the end of my semester I got to take my work to the Print Fair in NYC. Hard work - but worth it.

Passionate professor who is proactive with keeping the print media department contemporary. Expects you to engage fully in the class and you learn alot! She is critical with feedback/advise and pushes you to do well.

I don't think I have ever had a worse experience in my life. She constantly interrupts her co-teacher and other students while they talk, and she would talk non-stop for three hours about unrelated matter. She makes insensitive, rude and offensive comments, and she pries into your personal life. She expects you accommodate her mood and schedule.

Elisabeth is definitely a very passionate, worldly, and insightful professor. I think the conflict with students and her is her occasional mood-swings and judgmental spurts. She definitely chooses favorites. Her class is demanding, you learn a lot, she's tough, but students need that sometimes, especially students in Art School.
Personally One of the worst teachers I've ever had...
She's rude and insensitive.
She is bad at teaching.  She is inpatient.

I would never, ever, ever take a course with her again -- I recommend to all my friends the same.  Her comments are very misleading and often conflicting. She is moody and overly intense -- she refused to speak about one students work in crit bc they didn't look up the artist she suggested.
Don't expect her to be your best friend, but she will help your artmaking process so much. Yeah, she is tough, but students need that sometimes. She really does care about helping you.
Really Crazy.  Makes decisions based on her mood.  She gossips about students and teachers to students.

Likes students with good work ethic (try to work outside of class when she's there so she can see what a dedicated student you are).  Difficult teacher when things don't go her way in class.  Working through her assignments and class critiques were invaluable... take the class no matter how much you suffer.

By far the WORST professor I had in the department. Reminded me of Martha Stewart w/her cold compulsive demeanor. Favors men to an embarassing degree, and cares more about placing an ink can 30cm to the right than explaining why youre using it in the first place. A miserable perfectionist and miserable class, its like she tried to make you unhappy.
plain and simple, this woman is crazy.  like wacko crazy!
She is an intelligent woman who really cares about her students. As long as you can connect with her, you will love her. She is the consciousness of the art department.
No Comments

Course is essentially an extended research project. Fairly self-guided, invest a lot of time in learning about and finding a good research topic. A lot of opportunities for feedback on your writing and you learn a ton about how to conduct and present research. End up with a nice writing sample useful for internships or senior thesis apps.
So nice

He's a distinguished professor, but should really not be teaching undergraduates. He basically leaves the students on their own to do research with very little guidance. This class is only good for students that already have a good deal of macroeconomic knowledge or field experience.

Pretty clear in his lectures, only 2 prelims & 1 final so exams are 85% of your grade but he gives 2 options. Class avg is a B+ I think, he gives practice final pdfs, & lots of office hours. Lowest 3 hws are dropped, pollev for participation each class. Exams are fair but can be tricky so study the slides. At the end, he offers extra credit

bro is kinda the goat, go to office hours if you're struggling since the class does move fast. offers extra credit questions on every test that're easy if you go to lecture as well as a 5% ish curve, class median was a B+ I think

I've loved Orlov as a professor.
I've taken his micro & macro intro classes, and I loved the way he structured the course. He always gave a review class day and a class off before a prelim, which I appreciated. Tbh his lectures were not super helpful for me, especially at 9am, but the HW helped reinforce the topics I'd need for the prelims.

By far, the most difficult economics course I have taken this far. The content itself is not terribly difficult, but he moves through it at a rapid pace. He does have an accent which makes certain things difficult to understand.

Okay so Professor Orlov is a really nice guy who is clearly trying his best to provide a good experience for his students. Despite this effort, he teaches introductory macroeconomics like it's a 6000 level graduate course. Difficult subject matter that goes beyond basic Econ, tests are ridiculous, homework is overwhelming, and the list goes on.

The prelims are horrendous; 20 questions valued at 5 points each. You miss two and that is a whole letter grade down. He is a nice person but terrible professor. He goes through 10 slides in a matter of seconds. Worst professor I have had, not even Stephanie Thomas was this bad. His class will make you wish you never enrolled.

Professor Orlov is a great human being, and he is one of the kindest Professors I have ever had. With that being said, the prelims were ridiculous. The median is far below other macro professors, and the lectures can be quite hard to follow. I never left class understanding what I was doing. Best of luck.

Orlov is a great lecturer. While many say otherwise, the way he treats lectures is more of a supplement to the textbook. Light workload and a lot of practice tests. Orlov even cares about keeping the same grade distribution from previous years. Man is trying his best.

Unstructured and not engaging. extremely low median exam score for prelims (which make up most of your grade in the class). I did better on the exams when I read the textbook on my own and stopped caring for the lecture. Discouraging class to take, but it's an intro class and requirement for so many people so you just have to bear with it.
If you want to take a class where you are given absolutely no guidance and have to teach all of the material to yourself, Orlov is the professor for you to take.

While the class doesn't have a ridiculous workload, he's a terrible professor and his lectures are painful to sit through. Theres weekly hw with large textbook readings, and I'd be ok with this if I felt it prepared me for the prelims, yet the class average on our first prelim was a 71, a ridiculous grade for an introduction class with 400 people.

Smart guy who was super nice. If you struggle in Econ I suggest you take this class because he is always willing to help. Also gives out chips and snacks during the late night class. Graded on attendance so super easy A

I'd definitely recommend taking Prof. Orlov's class. Be aware that ECON 1120 is lecture heavy and there will be mandatory attendance as well as hefty homeworks 1x week. 

That being said, it's pretty obvious he wants his students to succeed. He makes himself extremely available and will go over material in class to ensure a thorough understanding.

Genetics is one of the hardest classes you'll take as a bio major because you can't rely strictly on memorization - you have to consistently practice and engage with the material. Dr. Barbash is an excellent lecturer and made the concepts really clear and understandable! Prelims were difficult but nothing unexpected.

Genetics is a really hard course but the material is very interesting and I found Barbash's lectures to be pretty engaging. However, he doesnt go through how to solve many of the problems (that'll be on the exams) and you'll have to go to OH or do those yourself

The lectures are long, slow, and have almost nothing to do with the tests that make up 97% of your grade. Yes, 97%. Barbash is not a good lecturer, but this almost doesn't matter since the only way to do well on the exams (and what even is "well" when the median is a 50%?) is to go through problems with a TA. The TAs are teaching this course alone.

If the class median on a test is failing, then the solution is not simply to "curve it up" to a B, the solution is to FIX HOW YOU TEACH. If most of the class is failing, then you are failing as a professor. Grade inflation won't fix that. I'd rather earn a fair grade and actually learn something.
This is a very hard course, but Barbash is willing to answer any questions during office hours and is always kind and patient.

Grades are based almost entirely on prelims and the final despite there being weekly quizzes and assignments. Also there is simply too much material covered in this course, needs a discussion section and to be 4 credits rather than 3. Honestly, enough content for a full year rather than a semester.
Very hard problem sets

Barbash is a good lecturer.  It's a really hard course no matter who you take it with but Barbash is really nice and is happy to answer questions.   Prelims were tough (means were in the 50's for all 3 of them) and the class is curved to a B.
Prof Barbash walks through really helpful examples during classtime. He is really nice and engaging.

Gave good lectures but the class was very disorganized. The labs were taught by the TA's and didn't always relate back to the lectures. Homework and labs were often very confusing and required a lot of time at office hours for clarification. Tests were much too difficult for an ENGRI class. Would not recommend this class.

A great lecturer, but may go off on (very interesting) tangents and not get through all he planned, but it will still be on the test. That or it all gets repeated in the next lecture, you never know. Very accessible outside of class and I'd recommend going to every lecture and office hours to learn and because of how funnily quotable he is.
Great overall class. Tests destroy self confidence but material is very interesting. The homeworks and labs are graded generously, and there is a curve at the end.
Really helpful, clear and even humorous.
Knows his stuff and is really great at clarifying things when you ask for help. Homework was not hard and the labs were fantastic. His tests are very hard though.
class is great

Prof Xu's intro to engineering course is one of the most difficult in that category. Prelim 1 had a mean of 41%. That being said, material is interesting, labs are fun and Office Hours with him are quite useful.

Prof. Xu is very smart, but not the greatest teacher. His class was very interesting and you learn a lot from him. Tests are surprisingly hard for an intro to engineering class (on our midterm, the mean was something like 40/95). Homework doesn't take up much time. Labs are fun.

Overall excellent professor. Funny but focused. Lectures were well organized and clear. A difficult first year class (at the level of Purcell/Morin and Griffiths) but at the end I have definitely learned a lot. Grading was generous; Prof. Xu is more interested in what you learn.

He is a very good teacher. He explained the content well, and has a good sense of humor. He is willing to help if you ask for it. The tests were very hard. The problem sets were difficult,  but there is not too much homework. Overall, a good teacher and difficult content.

Chris failed to explain the subject matter in a clear way. He gave no suggestions for other helpful books, which I had to find myself with trial and error. Motivation for the topics was rare, giving the lectures the feel of a boring textbook.

Toughest class I have taken at Cornell, hands down.  Some of the material was dry, but he presented it in a clear way.  Extremely tough problem sets and exams.  They really make you think in ways outside the box.
he's SO boring and the class is SO early. the two just don't mix.
Chris' teaching is a beauty to behold, clear and crisp.  He will challenge you in ways that really highlight the subtleties, complexities, and beauty of E&M.  Extremely recommended.

My experience with professor Xu was average. His lectures had the most quantitative material, but were all very basic and easy to understand. He likes plants, numbers, and graphs about plants, so you'll like him if that's your thing.

1610 was an average intro ecology course, taught by Dr. Xu and Dr. St Juliana with a TA-led section. Dr. Xu was a decent lecturer, and the content was not particularly difficult. There is a textbook, but I rarely read it. However, the tests could be unnecessarily tricky (even TAs had trouble), and the section work was often unhelpful or pointless.

Xiangtao was a fairly engaging and entertaining lecturer, I rarely found myself bored to tears during lectures. Other than that, BIOEE 1610 was a fairly average biology/ecology course, which was worthwhile enough for me and not terribly hard. The tests were needlessly tricky in my opinion, but the content itself is not very hard and is interesting.
He was a super nice guy, but the tests were a little trickier than they should have been and sometimes he struggled to explain material very clearly.
Prof not too bad, but the exam sucks. Too "flexible" to relate to what you've learned

Overall Dr. Xu is an engaging lecturer who knows a lot about the subject and makes it interesting.He sometimes goes off topic and gives extra information that is not going to be tested which leads him to run out of time at the end of lectures. Class is very participation driven so go to lecture/section.
He scheduled a prelim on the day before Thanksgiving break... enough said

this is my first rating on this website but I had to give a shoutout to professor sampson. he made a very difficult class (cs 4110) that was FAR out of my comfort zone palatable and enjoyable. he truly cares about his students' learning and the class topics, 10/10 professor.

I didn't have the time to enjoy CS 4110 with Adrian (I had to drop it because of the courseload of other classes), but he was by far the most intelligent and amusing lecturer I've had as an undergrad. Consider yourself lucky to have him as a lecturer for any course.

One of the best professors I've ever had because his lectures are so well put together and he is amazing at teaching the content and answering questions. Even though the tests and psets are difficult, they feel fair because of how well the course is delivered. 10/10 recommend.

Easily one of the best professors I've had throughout my college career, if not the best. Professor Sampson is very patient and approachable, and explains concepts in a very clear, insightful way. He also allocates time during class for short practice problems so that students can practice and test their understanding of the material.
He is a great professor, very helpful and approachable. He seems to know his stuff very well.

He is a fantastic professor. He gives great lectures and is always available for help (he answers Piazza posts in seconds and will always give one on one help). The material in the course is difficult, but he grades fairly and gives a good curve. One of my favorite professors at Cornell I've had.
Prof. Lewis is super intelligent but the material is a little dry. Lectures can be really hard to follow.

He's super nice during lectures so don't be scared to get clarifications. Lectures are mostly proofs, which can get helpful sometimes, while the textbook provides really good review. Tests are hard, but they're curved pretty well.
Great professor and lectures. Goes through proofs slowly and deliberately, going through examples afterwards

Spring 2019, Median: B. His lectures were theoretical; exam questions were mixed theoretical and applied (light proofs), like his homework. Some students stopped going to lecture because the textbook was closer to the exams. lectures were mostly boring but occasionally cool. I learned a lot but its an easy course, so I cant fully credit him.

Adrian is an amazing lecturer. i can't believe he made a topic as dry as opts so fascinating to a non-OR major. It's cute how passionate he gets about the material and I really did learn a lot. The tests are pretty tough though, so make sure you actually go to lecture if you want to stand a chance.
One of the best lecturers I've ever had. He explains everything really clearly and answers questions well in class. Exams are easy if you do the practice ones he gives out.

Lewis was very clear, wrote everything on the board, and went at a good pace through difficult mathematical proofs. Willing to answer questions after class and at review sessions (and very well), but office hours were few and at student unfriendly times. Recommend taking this class with him.

Has really clear lecture notes and is overall a good lecturer. Again, if you're confused in class, ask! He goes at a good pace and is willing to reiterate. He's a bit random with his test style though. Sometimes it's computation-heavy, sometimes it's more conceptual. The answer he's looking for is never too hard, so don't think so hard!
Awful professor

Not exactly my favorite class, but Lewis is an alright guy and a pretty good professor. I did extremely well on the exams, but bombed all the hws, and only ended up with a B+ (hws worth a lot), but it's all good. Make sure to raise your hand in class when he asks questions, see if you can get him to smile (a rare occurrence indeed)

Amazing lecture...actually possible to follow. If he gets too into the theory he knows it and will ALWAYS follow up with examples. However, his teaching partner Shmoys is a "dingus." Lewis is by far the better of the two..also a decent guy.
Awesome course and prof. the lectures are very clearly organized and he writes everything neatly on the board. exams are a little too easy in my opinion
Great lecturer, very formal.  HW's and exams aren't too hard if you go to class and keep up with the material.

Nice professor that discusses pieces of text in class. There are presentations from a student group each week. The weekly readings could sometimes be a bit much. Total of 5 pieces of writing for whole semester. Only negative is the no technology during class policy which will lose you lots of points if you don't follow.

Took this class as an easy distribution and it did its job. Prof. is nice and very clearly cares about what he's teaching, though the lectures were painful to sit through. Almost felt bad that people weren't taking notes/paying attention. Essays were easy, skimmed readings, and final was exactly like the review sheet he gives.

Prof. Fiskesjo is a great person, very genuine, and always willing to assist students with questions. However, his lectures could be improved. Just do the reading, discussion posts, and papers then you'll be fine. Class content is very thought-provoking and is great exposure to cultural anthropology.
Professor Fiskesjo is a nice, genuine guy who lectures well. He clearly cares about anthropology and what he talks about. He has a lot of readings, but he goes over them in class.
Professor Fiskesjo is a nice, genuine guy who lectures well. Clearly cares about anthropology and what he talks about. A lot of readings but he goes over it in class.

Chill guy. Beware of weird ppl trying to drive you out of the course. Stranger came in 1st day and called him a psy-op bc of his Uyghur advocacy. Often went on unrelated tangents that could disengage you. 2 short essays + online final. Slow feedback but lenient grading. Was willing to hear student opinions even if they didn't align with his.

Approachable and easy going. Clear on assignments and grading. However every once in a while would go off tangent from course material to share views that were unrelated (somewhat controversial & ungrounded) to the material.
In terms of content, the course was decent. Nothing to complain about. However, he would often go on long, somewhat racist tangents. Ruined the course

This is for his Study Abroad in Cambodia course for 2 and a half weeks. I can't understand the negative reviews. How could anyone not love Magnus? He is funny and LOVES what he does. I really hope he keeps doing Study Abroad in the future. It's not just that the trip was great on its own, but he made it sooo much better!

Magnus is great! His lectures were generally very interesting and he is super passionate about what he teaches. He really encouraged discussion as well. He's also just a very likeable, if quirky guy. My only criticism is that the class was graded on just a few things: a midterm, a fairly long paper, and participation.

Magnus lectures are often very interesting despite his dry tone. The class is fairly easy for the most part (very short essays), though some of that depends on the TAs. Having attended both his Zoom and in-person lectures, I can say that he is MUCH better in person than over Zoom.

Avoid at any costs. I found his assignments are ridiculous amount of reading, and yet has nothing to do with exam Id rather take other class and read what interests me. Im not attending a trading club.

The prof seemed passionate about his subject, but the class was poorly organized. The grading system was unclear to students, even though the assignments were easy. Problems occurred with zoom and canvas (i.e. not recording sessions, not publishing info on canvas, etc.). The lectures and readings were interesting though, and my TA was great.

This might be harsh, but this was the worst class I've taken. His teaching was not conducive to Zoom. The lectures were boring. I was really disappointed by the way he discussed topics I had hoped would be interesting. The grading scheme was unclear and unfair. Easy, but I would have taken a harder and more interesting class over this one.

Class was light work. But lecture's super boring. I feel bad because no one participated but he didn't really create a great atmosphere for it. He's probably better in person, but not good at zoom. We spent the whole class talking about how things aren't really objective and then the final was defining terms objectively. Nice guy tho, wish the best

Lectures are boring and he just repeats the information from the readings. Grading criteria is unclear and he is very disorganized. He told us about our midterm 2 weeks before it was going to happen and we didn't know how it was going to graded or what the format was. He didn't tell us the format of the final then people got C's on it.
super kind and caring professor. very passionate about his field. material is very interesting. workload pretty low.

Very interesting guy, engages students in the lecture asking questions and feedback, not afraid to consider and discuss other points of view. He brings a breadth of examples and approaches to a variety of topics each week, it's impressive. Always includes the most timely debates. Assigns a lot of reading, essays were short and not hard to write.

Don't be fooled by the comment below, Magnus is a great guy who really cares about his students. It's important to keep in mind he is from Sweden and so sometimes what he says can be misconstrued. More than willing to be corrected and amend his own opinions if confronted, always up for an open conversation. In no way denies his son's identity.

Magnus is such a nice professor, he obviously means well. His TAs do a lot of the work but his lectures do explain the assigned readings. Exams are not hard, just do the readings. Essays are two pages and are not too bad. I got an A and enjoyed the class. He is very friendly and approachable!!

his lectures can get really boring. section helped out a lot because i had a great TA. there are weekly essays assigned but they are very easy if you understand the readings.  that being said, the readings can be very long and if you get bored of anthro it is easy to fall behind. easy A if you do the readings and incorporate them into essays
Everything about the guy screams smug and lazy. How he manages to live with that huge ego is a mystery.

Despite the fact, his tone is really sleep inducing. But overall, he's really helpful, always there for you. It's so easy to lose attention in his class, which makes it boring then. But overall, he's so friendly that you wouldn't want to skip his class.

Magnus is really cute in a very goofy foreign way. I feel bad for him when he asks questions in class and everyone is silent. He's super nice and goofy. His lectures are a snoozefest and you NEVER need to go to class literally ever. You have way too many essays but its all about your TA.

He isn't a very clear speaker, the lectures are usually hit-or-miss with some of them being horrible and others being really insightful. Although he isn't a great lecturer, but he really cares for his students and is interesting to speak with one on one. This isn't a bad intro class although the readings are way too long! Only take if u like anthro
SO LAZY!  Just talks about himself and his own research and clearly does not care about his students. Not nearly as smart as he wants us to think.

Very confusing and into his own research. His T.A.s did all the work and the lectures were terrible. The readings themselves were interesting yet sometimes too lengthy. Sections were laid back though, and interesting. As a person though, he is a great guy who is excited about his field-- He could use some work in teaching.

Don't let the awesome course description fool you. This class was really boring. Boring lectures are mandatory. Manages to make fascinating topics dry. Monotone voice. TA's grade everything and lead the only interesting part of the class-discussions. You'll be able to pass this class with a good grade, but you'll probably be wasting your time.
Like the others said, this guy loves his work but absolutely fails at passing any of it on.  Some of the worst lectures I have ever sat through.

He definitely loves his work!  Assigns way too much reading, and its hard to know what to cover, bc he doesn't cover all of it.  His own work is really interesting, though.  I'd recommend taking this class only for fun.

Fiskesjo is one of those teachers who loves what he does SO MUCH that he's in his own little world when he lectures and tends to float off subject. He assigns a lot of reading and doesn't really highlight key points so you'll need office hours for that. Also, he will put you to sleep faster than a roofie. Nevertheless, the material is interesting!

He is not an engaging speaker and lectures are incredibly dry. He reads off of his slides most of the time and teaches by reading 3 or 4 discussion questions to the crowd without providing answers to them. I think his style of teaching can work much better in a smaller discussion-based class. Tests are easy if you do all the readings

Class was pretty alright - he seems like he's a super smart dude but lecture was generally eh. Idc much about that though, but this class had so much work to be done. 4 1200 word reading responses + a 15 page final paper in addition to the 40+ page reading to be done for every class. It was insane and much harder than other advanced writing classes

Great professor. Readings were insightful and informative. He expertly covers a plethora of interesting topics, including workplace cultures and discrimination. Papers are really easy (just have to reflect on the readings), and tests were graded fairly. I enjoyed the lectures, but if you aren't interested in the topics they may be boring. Gives EC.

The entire class is based off of readings, most of which I found interesting, but long. The class has no clear theme and is very disjointed. Lectures are useless, but mandatory. The actual grading is entirely done by your TA and it matters which one. I like the content and idea of the class but it was poorly executed.

Class itself was not that difficult just incredibly boring and required you to do an obnoxious amount of reading which was NEVER talked about in class so you had to infer meanings on the tests. Tests are mostly short answers and discussions were useless. He seemed like he did not want to teach the class and word-for-word read off the slides.

God, he is the absolute worst. He literally just chats, like no content comes out of his mouth, he just says words. I personally think his class is the biggest waste of time, but attendance is mandatory!!!

For a 1.5 credit class, the amount of readings and work given seemed unnecessary. Professor Ivory used an index card system that made lecture attendance mandatory. They improved after the first prelim, but the lectures were generally pretty useless and did little to help me understand the incredibly dense and long readings for the week.

unnecessarily strict with his attendance/deadline policies and is unsympathetic to needing flexibility. he basically reads off of his slides, so going to lecture feels pointless, and rather than discussing the incredibly dense readings, he just puts "discussion questions" up on the board and reads them to the class. he doesn't even answer them.
Seems like a nice guy, but I couldn't hear a single thing. Talks into his neck. Tests were dumb. Like high school. Did not enjoy. Some readings were interesting though. Lectures were just not good.

Class is based on readings which are never discussed meaningfully in class, useless lectures, attendance is mandatory with mini flashcard assignments about readings, he doesn't seem like he wants to be there, must study hard, some TAs make class much easier than others, overall would not recommend class unless you have to take it as an ILRie
Very boring and useless lectures. He just reads off from the slides every day. And attendance is mandatory. Extremely heavy readings with few explanations in class lectures. Would not take it again.
Benissimo

This was easily my favorite class at Cornell. Dr. Zacher is super sweet and will always help you, as long as you're proactive about asking for it. Super fun person to be around too, she's funny and even brings her dog into class sometimes! Highly recommend.

Professor Zacher is absolutely wonderful! She brings enthusiasm to the class and makes the material engaging. She makes sure that we won't feel stressed but also stay motivated enough to keep on track. I took the course for requirements but ended up really enjoying Old English. This is one of the best classes I've taken at Cornell!

It is true that she ignores student emails, but also true that she is a good teacher when you are lucky enough to see her in class. It's a privilege to even see her and students should appreciate the privilege. Zacher is amazing, and just to see her in class is a delight. Don't expect more than you need

ENGL3280 Prof. Zacher makes high-level material accessible. You can be in any class year and take one of her 3000-level classes and succeed if you put in the work. Her class involves long readings and in-depth lectures, but doing the readings is enough to score high. She has a warm spirit that always brightens the day and makes even old texts fresh

She was so nice! I was dreading taking this FWS because it was a requirement but she was a pleasure. The work was not bad at all and she is very understanding. I would definitely recommend participating in class.

Zacher is an incredible professor and such a kind and caring person. Her classes are always interesting and informative. She is a fair grader but pushes you to be the best writer that you can be. Do not miss out on taking a class with her at Cornell.
Samantha is incredibly nice & fabulous! She's so energetic & passionate & enthusiastic, making obscure topics really interesting. Will definitely take her class again!

This class one so well thought out. There was a flow between topics that really made sense and the texts we read were fun! (Especially the section on John Mandeville). Would highly recommend taking a course from Professor Zacher!

Interesting, challenging, fun, understanding, but most of all relevant!
