Such an understanding and engaging prof, workload is minimal and fun. Take this class :)

So knowledgeable in the subject area, and clearly cares about her work. Class time is split evenly btwn lecture and in-person workshops, and there are weekly readings and Canvas posts. Two "big" Projects but you are given ample time and support to complete. Very tech saavy, smart, witty, and understanding. Will definitely take her again!

Super laid-back. Classes with him are really relaxed. He points out great writing advice and tips I never knew about. He's just not too into fantasy writing and head's up: not good with remembering names. I've taken two classes with him.

Ernesto was my professor for True Stories (FWS). He is a great and will really work with students. He assigns few papers and gives good feedback. The class is about radical political movements in the US, and we sometimes watched movies and did light readings (less than 5 pgs). Would 10/10 recommend this class to anyone!!

The fact that this is my first time giving a review here is testament to Ernesto's teaching ability. He's sharp, open-minded, funny, experimental, inspirational, and doesn't BS. He won't sugar-coat, but he will make you a better, more aware writer. And if he pulls you aside to encourage you to send your work out... you know you've made it :)
If you put in the work, you will do very well.
Friendly, but provides no useful feedback and no help improving work. Doesn't pay much attention. Easy grader but you learn nothing.

Didn't think creative writing was going to be this interesting.  Ernesto, and he never wants to be called professor, would play a film clip and then have us read a short story and lead us to see the same narrative techniques being used in fiction. Amazing!!!  He is very cute but he wears the same black shirt a lot.  Easy grader.
Interesting guy, extremely laid-back and passionate about the material he teaches. Dynamic, creative professor. Very easy grader.

Professor Bassi is an expert in trade history and globalization. I studied with him when he taught in Spain. If you are interested in these areas, I recommend his class. He loves "flipping the classroom".

Professor Bassi was one of the best professors I had at Cornell. His assignments were straightforward and if you did what he asked then you got a good grade. His office hours were very helpful and he proofread my essays before I turned them in. I would definitely take another class with him
Professor Bassi is one of the most engaging lecturers I've come across. His assignments were also thoughtful--overall, felt like I learned a great deal about colonial Latin America.
He is hard to understand and passes almost all of his work to his one TA. He grades pretty hard and does not allow you to argue your grade. No prelims or final however, just papers.

Great professor and great class. Professor Nelson is a genuinely kind man that enjoys his students and what he teaches. Meets with each student 1-on-1 at least once a semester. This is the easiest 4 credit class Cornell offers, and I would recommend to anyone. You will also probably enjoy it and do well if you manage to make the night lectures.

Sam Nelson is a delight. Though his class seems unorthodox, he really cares about debate and loves to see his students engaged and excited. Taking this class improved my public speaking skills and it was a very easy, low pressure 4 credit class. The essays seem like a lot but they really aren't, and always lets you out early.

Day 1, there was a scenario about if he brought in beagle babies and started stomping on their heads, what would you do? He makes you think. Sometimes in crazy ways but the class makes you think about where your values lie through a lot of topics. I learned a lot about debate and getting my opinions across. Go to lecture and you'll do great.
One of the goofiest professors Ive had at this university. Would absolutely recommend him

So so easy. The class can be interesting but sometimes drags on. People do very poorly on the first exam in general, and often not great on the first paper (which he lets you resubmit), but the median is still an A. Cares about students and meets with all of them during the semester.
One of the nicest and most genuine professors at Cornell. He cares about his students and tries to make sure each and every student is set up for success.
Easiest class ever. Only like 2 projects and paper and Sam is a super easy grader. Lets us leave lecture after like an hour.

Sam is a great professor. Just like advocacy and debate, rhetoric is also a very easy class. The class is 2.5 hours once a week but often finishes over an hour early. The few assignments he gives are easy and the grading is light. Definitely take this class for a free 4 credits.

For each 2.5 hour lecture, there is maybe 15-20 minutes of actual content, and the rest of it is just Sam chatting with the students in a pseudo-forum. You *have* to read the textbook (or study the quizlets made by past students) for exams. The canvas is never updated and paper expectations are only explained in lecture. It's fun though- would rec.

Sam is a great professor. He is very nice, accommodating, and makes a somewhat boring topic enjoyable. Class is only once a week and there isn't much work except for a few papers. The class is easy even if you have no prior knowledge, he will cut you slack if you simply ask, and the average grade was an A. Take this class.
His debate class is easy and he is just such an amazing human being. I would definitely recommend anyone to take the class!

Sam is a great person and is easy to talk to but I didn't actually enjoy this class like I expected to. I don't feel that I learned much or that my debate skills improved. Lectures were full of tangents and stories, so some classes will be more important than others. Tests were definitely curved.

Nelson is a weird professor and you will need to adapt to his interesting style. You HAVE to read the textbook. A lot of students made the mistake of glossing over it and not performing well. Also, make sure you go over EVERYTHING from the lectures. He asked for quotes on the final without warning. Everything is fair game.
He is an entertaining lecturer, and highly recommend taking the debate class if it satisfies requirements. This class will also make you a better public speaker.

Sam is a really funny and caring guy; favorite professor I've had so far. Made lectures really interesting and worth going to, despite it being a night class. Tests are 50% lecture, 50% book details, so lectures are definitely necessary, as is the book. Discussion is kinda boring; don't take early in the morning. Overall, great class. 9.8/10.

Sam is an amazing professor. His teaching style is very nontraditional but I still learned a lot from his class. Discussion sections were really interesting because that is where you actually debate and they were on interesting topics. Super easy A and you become a better public speaker after this class. HIGHLY RECOMMEND HIM IF YOU WANT AN A.

Easy A from a mediocre professor. If you are even the slightest bit interested in rhetorical criticism, prepare to be disappointed. Sam is so lazy, he manages not to give a single lecture. NOT ONE. Your FELLOW CLASSMATES will be teaching each class. Hopefully they read the textbook. You will learn nothing. You will get an A.

Very easy A, "alternative" teaching style. Engaging lecturer for a night class, always has interesting stories. Gives exact test questions in class, but if you have a friend give you the notes, you'll be fine. Still worth going to lecture for the stories though.

Sam is great. But I wish he was more clear about what would be covered on the exams! The only thing I had to go on was that he could ask us anything about anything from all of his lectures and the assigned text (that he NEVER went over). I failed the first test because of this, but aced the second exam because I knew what to expect that time!

What an inspiration!  I wish more professors mimicked his style.  He is very down to earth and has the best lectures I've ever attended!  The first test is all about definitions (they'll tell you this) that can be found in the text.  Much of the grade is based on debate participation.

Sam is, by far, the best teacher I've ever had. I had him for my ILRLR 3300 3-week summer program and it was undoubtedly the highlight of my summer. He's super funny, super friendly, and super knowledgeable. He gives lots of lectures but they're always fantastic.  I visited him a lot during my course and even met with him at CTB. He's a true gem.
BEST TEACHER I EVER HAD

Hands down one of the most influential classes in my Cornell experience. You'll learn to articulate your opinions and argue effectively. Sam's great in lecture. He always presents great hypothetical scenarios when trying to illustrate a point. The lectures are 3 hours long, which sucks, but there is a break halfway through.

Awesome Professor. I cant even sit through a 3 hour movie, let alone a lecture. But he made it fly by and it was so interesting, I actually LOOKED FORWARD to his class!! Definitely Should take this class while youre at Cornell.
Very easy and entertaining class. You'll become a better debater and public speaker just by virtue of attending lecture.
You must take Argumentation & Debate with Sam Nelson.  He is hilarious and genuinely wants his students to learn.  As long as you show that you're trying, you'll get an A.

half the time no one, as in him or the TA, knows what's going on. 2 tests, 1 final, which was all true or false this year, papers, and 3 debates.  he's extremely funny and it's an entertaining class, and you do learn some stuff but mainly the questions for the test are stuff you read in the book.
The class can be kind of dysfunctional at times, but Sam is hilarious (if he wasn't a debate professor, he could have a successful career as a stand-up comedian) and it is an easy A.

GREAT PROFESSOR!!!! Lectures were extremely interesting! His laugh and his jokes kept me laughing the entire class time! You must take this class, it is not too hard if you put the effort. Read the book, you MUST go to lecture to do well on his tests, and do the assignments given...

Sam is mad funny, by far one of the better professors at Cornell. He is always cracking jokes and loves to hold class discussions on interesting debate topics. I was always awake when Sam taught Great course. Great Professor. Easy A

Sam is mad funny, by far one of the better professors at Cornell. He is always cracking jokes and loves to hold class discussions on interesting debate topics. I was always awake when Sam taught until his asst came to teach. Great course. Great Professor. Easy A
Definitely the funniest professor I have ever had. As stated before he makes the 3 hr class fly by. It was the best 3 hours of my week hands down.
GREAT Professor!! Although I can't stay awake in a 45 minute course, Sam can keep my attention in a 3 hour course. Take his class! It's an easy A.
agreed with above. awesome professor.

Quite possibly one of the ONLY professors that can keep my interest in a three hour lecture. His lectures consist of a joke every five or so minutes at the very least, and the material he teaches you is interesting. Tests are easy if you skim the book, and as long sa you have an interest, it's an easy A/A-. A+ is somewhat hard to get, though.

Stay away for your sanity. The only positive thing about him is he cares about Linguistics and puts a lot of work into his lectures. He shouldn't be a professor at Cornell he has no empathy for students who added the class late making their participation and homework grades lower. He will fully ignore and not respond to emails. He has a huge ego.

Professor Tilsen's lecture are pretty technical and sometimes confusing, but he is a chill guy. He obviously shows a passion for the subject, but the course isn't always taught to reflect that I feel. Homeworks are not too hard, prelims too. Although the homeworks aren't hard, I do feel that they don't really give you sufficient practice
he might be a good person but his lectures are kind of confusing. pop quizes are scary

One of the best professors at Cornell! Incredibly sweet and funny, and a very engaging lecturer. There are some annoying things (attendance required, pop quizzes from textbook readings) but exams are straightforward. I wasn't very interested in p-side linguistics before this class (I only took it as a major requirement) but Sam made it worthwhile.

He is clearly very knowledgeable about linguistics and a great lecturer. However, he never stuck around after Zoom lectures to answer questions. It felt like he was doing the bare minimum to teach us. The homework assignments were challenging but reasonable.
Not a very good teacher. Kind of technical. Cocky in a way that makes it seem like he's overcompensating for his lack of ability to teach. Lacks basic human empathy. Stay away from this guy.

Doesn't know how to teach. He has trouble explaining things that the book explains simply. A lot of times, I had trouble understanding what he was talking about, but when I read the book it was clear. He kind of expects you to read his mind.
Gives very hard tests and hard assignments as well. TA Hitomi is not helpful at all. Not considerate at all when students are facing difficulties with the pandemic. Stay away from Tilsen!

Took the class S/U. Lectures are engaging, but sometimes too technical. Weekly homework. Didn't even bother buying the textbook. Good as a very broad basic intro to the various subfields of linguistics.
I think he is new to teaching. I had a frustrating experience with him and I love phonetics. Very cocky.
He doesn't go easy on you, but you're sure to learn a lot.

Prof. Tilsen is a very solid teacher.  He teaches pretty difficult material and is a relatively harsh grader, but he is funny and usually pretty clear when teaching.  If you have a question, he is very good at finding a way to explain things a second time in a different way.

Aye was the most amazing and inspirational professor I ever had. Her material is very hard - I struggled immensely with her material, but at the end of it all, I felt rewarded with a wealth of knowledge that has forever impacted the way I understand chemistry and biology. I felt that I had learned, rather than studied, organic chemistry.

Prof Aye is definitely one of the most intelligent professors that I have ever had, but she has a hard time slowing down and breaking the material down into helpful and informational pieces. She either teaches a concept in a way that is too simple or too complicated and then she tests on multiple concepts combined.

Professor Aye is really challenging, but her lectures weren't entirely bad. There's a bit of a language barrier and she tends to focus on drugs/biological applications. SHE WILL TEST YOU ON THEM. She only gives answers to in-class practice problems during lecture, so make sure you show up ready to write really fast. Tests are rough but interesting

When I searched in google for one of the concepts, I realized that it was an unproven mechanisms published on NCBI that she wanted us to know. I feel like if I master all the mechanisms she wants me to know I will be able to synthesize a new cancer curing drug or something by myself.

Dr. Aye is the worst avoid at all costs, try to take Dr. Ruttledge his class is not easy by any means. But, Dr. Aye is not engaging, her test involve unnecessary reading that further complicates orgo. Her test are horrible, at least in Ruttledge's class you are clear on instructions even though the problem may be really hard.

Professor Aye is definitely a bright individual who should be teaching Organic Chemistry, but teaches this Intro to Organic Chemistry class as though we have already taken her section of the class twice. The class overall is test heavy and those are what determine your grade. Professor Aye makes Dr. Ruttledge's tests look like middle school quiz

Professor van de Walle is a well organized and thoughtful lecturer who wants to make sure that his class is interesting for everyone. As of Spring 2023 he does not teach this course any more, but if you are interested in African Politics/Studies, then I would recommend you take some of his courses. He is very easy going, and a great professor!

A funny guy. Lectures were somewhat scripted, but made sense and were easy to follow. The one thing I didn't like was that we were graded on very few things (paper, midterm, final) and didn't know our final grades until the very end of the semester. Your TA largely determines your grade. Attendance is also factored into your final grade as well.

Good professor, but not a great one. Class is graded on three things: a paper (don't receive feedback until the end of the year), a midterm exam (graded swifty and fairly tbh) and then a final exam. Lectures are somewhat boring but manageable for someone interested in this topic. Love this topic, but wish I could have been more engaged by VDW.

I did NOT enjoy GOVT 1313: Intro to Comparative Politics with Professor van de Walle. He word vomits a lot during lectures and it's really hard to follow; a lot of people stopped showing up towards the end of the semester. Also, we only had three assignments including the midterm and the final, so we had barely any chances to bring our grade up.

Great professor who really knows his stuff and gives super interesting lectures. I learned a ton about African Politics in his class. Be sure you do the readings because he gives pop quizzes on them. In this class, a lot of your work will be about a country you are assigned at the beginning of the year.

Professor van de Walle is such a kind professor and he is so clearly intelligent it was a pleasure to learn from him. This course was extremely interesting though at times I was very discouraged by the discussion sections because they got too abstract and didn't really match the level of the lectures.

Although he is a nice guy, Van de Walle's lectures are terribly boring. He manages to take very interesting subject matter and put it in the least interesting terms possible. Additionally, grading really depends on your TA, and my section received much lower grades than other sections, indicating a lack of communication between TA and professor.
He knows so much about DRC. Each lecture is a TED talk!

He is an ok lecturer but exhibits a total lack of professionalism. This course was doomed by his inability and unwillingness to communicate with and control the class' TA. The professor never asked for the grades for the midterm, class paper or final from the TA so when the TA went AWOL after the final the class did not receive its grades.
Prof. Van de Walle is very knowledgable about comparative politics but his lectures were very boring. Hard to stay awake despite the interesting topic. Kind and funny but not very engaging.

Great professor who really cares about his students. Lectures are fun and interesting. He shows up everyday with a smile on his face, you can tell he enjoys teaching. I learned a lot and it's definitely a class worth taking for anybody.

Professor van de Walle is overall a solid professor. Some students find his lectures boring but he tends to simply embody the classic Ivy lecturer. If you pay attention, his lectures are fairly engaging. Definitely raise your hand and ask questions, he remembers. Pay close attention to readings, that's where test concepts come from.

great professor who lectures kind of slowly but very clearly. prelims and final are clear and straightforward. he also provides lots of helpful study resources such as key terms lists and lecture notes. skipping lectures won't much of a problem and supplementary readings that aren't textbook are completely unnecessary

Lectures can be kind of boring, but the content is always very relevant. His examples are always super interesting due to his knowledge of African political systems. Super nice and adorable, willing to engage students, and admit his shortcomings. I learned so much in his class, and would recommend, but feel free to skip a lecture every so often.

Very nice and sweet guy. Approachable after class.  Very interesting lectures that dove into nonconventional discussions and raised some very important questions.  Good for an intro to comparative politics and very knowledgable.

Dear Lord, the lectures can be a struggle to get through. The material is interesting enough and not particularly complicated, but he tends to ramble quite a bit. He has his moments though; very passionate, can be kind of sweet/dopey, and encourages questions and discussion. Pretty easy to BS, I skipped a lot of lectures, and only read sometimes.
Professor van de Walle is a really amazing professor. Yes his lectures a little boring but I learned SO MUCH from this class. Would definitely take again.

Professor is very intelligent and engaging. Lectures were well-prepared and organized, yet flexible to our class's discussion. Kind, helpful, and articulate, he is a great professor who truly cares about student's academic growth and will spark an interest in African politics you didn't know you had. One of my favorite classes at Cornell.

I think this class really depends on your TA. Mine was amazing, so I liked it. The lectures are really boring, but the prof. is adorable! He's super dopey and loves answering questions. The readings are completely unnecessary. He goes over the important parts during lecture and usually just disagrees with the rest. I didn't do a single one.
I love the professor. he's so sweet and passionate about the topic. the ta I had was a really hard grader, so this class wasn't worth taking.

The man has good intentions. He clearly cares about comparative politics (don't get him started on African politics), however, his lectures are boring as f.... they are not as intriguing as one might hope. If you are considering being a Government major, please don't take his class. if you have insomnia, please do, for he will put you to sleep. zzz

All in all the professor is a nice guy and would discuss subject matter in depth with any student. However, lectures are extremely dry, and the excessive reading is completely unnecessary. I did none of the reading and still did fine. He uploads lecture powerpoints and study guides so there is no need to attend lectures.

His lectures were pretty well organized and mostly interesting depending on the topic at hand. He's pretty serious but can be pretty funny/sarcastic. He encourages and takes questions asked during lecture seriously.
lectures were extremely unhelpful and confusing. reading was ridiculous and unhelpful

I had the pleasure of being in Professor Buchon's class this semester, and I must say it was an absolutely enriching experience. I highly recommend their class for anyone interested in physiology, especially if you plan on taking the MCAT
I really liked his style of teaching. He mixes clear explanations, with physiological problem sets and I really got a sense I learned a lot. A must have for premeds

Taking Professor Buchon's physiology class was super cool! He made it easy for us to get what he wwas talking about. He really cared about us doing well and was always there to help out, whether it's explaining stuff after class or using fun ways to teach. I'd totally recommend his class to anyone who wants to learn about how their body works!

Great professor who cracks a lot of jokes. he deals with the most complicated lectures in class but make them very accessible. Follow in class. This helps a lot! Accessible professor outside of class.
Very good professor that made complicated concepts pretty clear. Very accessible outside of class, supportive and quite funny.
really nice professor

Really funny professor, wrote the easiest out of the four prelims. I thought his lectures were the most entertaining and very clear. Very heavy french accent but still not hard to understand. His prelim was not too detailed oriented. Loml

Dr. Buchon is, in my opinion, the best 1440 instructor! His slides are very clear. His lecture was thorough and his explanations was extremely clear. He takes hard physiology concepts and explains it in a way that's really easy to understand. He's very accessible outside of class and holds extra office hours before exams so we get the help we need.

His videos were helpful, but it is a little hard to understand his French accent. His lectures were pretty engaging and thorough. The class is moderately difficult. There's lecture videos, readings, and mandatory quizzes twice a week, 4 prelims, optional final, and attendance is not mandatory. Prelims are tricky. Don't take if not required.

best 1440 lecturer, with very clear presentations, slides, and grading criteria. organizes and explains things very well and grades super fairly. the only problem I've ever heard from people about him is his accent, but I never had any issue (it's french, if anyone is wondering) wish he taught the entire semester!

From the three instructors in BioG1440, Pr. Buchon was the most interesting and clear.
Easy to talk to and mentions in class what the test will be on.
Lectures are content heavy, but complex concepts are well explained.

Prof Buchon's slides and lectures were by far the most clear and easy to understand. I felt like the topics he taught were some of the more difficult ones, but his explanations and heavy use of in-class practice questions helped a lot. He also pushed back a prelim when he knew the students were stressed about other emergency matters.

The ability to watch the recorded lectures is what carries this class. All the information you need for the exams are in the recorded lectures, and the three professors that teach this class have plenty of office hour times to help with understanding the lectures. The discussion sections are great fun, with great experiments. JOIN BIOG1044! GL

An interesting class where you will learn a lot about physiology. Contrary to what is said in the syllabus, it is heavy in human physiology and not so much focused on other organisms. Pr. Buchon really explained well complicated concepts.
Intelligent and thoughtful professor with interactive lectures. Explains topics well. The way the class is curved is annoying.

I really loved the lectures of Pr. Buchon, they were very structured and the problems were well explained. I took AP biology so have seen some of that content before, but this was way more structured.
I loved the lecture of Professor Buchon on how microbes influence physiology. Coolest lecture ever. It made me think a lot.

I actually loved BioG1440 and especially the section taught by Buchon. The exams were very fair, you really just have to listen to what he says in class. The other instructors were a bit less clear, but overall a good class. Exams come one day apart from chem, this was tough.

Took BIOG1440 with Buchon, Shapleigh, and Selveraj in FA 2020. Class had both synchronous and asynchronous lecture components. Buchon's slides and lectures were by far the most comprehensive and he emphasized topics that were likely to be tested. Compared to the other two professors Buchon was by far the best.
The course itself is difficult but Buchon explains things in a very clear and understandable way. He does have an accent that can be heavy at times, but his way of teaching is great
There were 3 instructors for this class and they were really uneven. The body physiology is really the coolest part. Advice: go to office hours!
I am very thankful for this professor's time. He hold something like 10 extra office hours sessions before prelim and these really help.

Professor Buchon had very good powerpoints, but his thick French accent sometimes made it difficult to understand him. BIOG 1440 itself is difficult and very memorization heavy, but I think he explained concepts well.
Fantastic professor. He made some complicated subjects feel quite simple!

Dr Buchon was very helpful during the semester. I started with a bad score during my first prelim, but thanks to TAs and Professors' office hours, I kept increasing my score. Dr Buchon advices were really helpful
Dr Buchon explained everything we needed to know very clearly and plainly. I was glad to get to study from him

Dr. Buchon is a great professor and really cares about his students and the subject material. Very easy to understand and available for extra help during office hours. I went every week. He is passionate about physiology and you will learn a lot from him. I wish I could take more courses with him!
Great teacher. Loved it!

Great introduction to physiology. Has been recommended to me by my academic mentor as a premed. This course is very time-consuming course but also very rewarding and practical to understand human physiology.

The material is difficult but presented very clearly. Exams are fair; but you better go to review sessions. This professor is very accessible, he will spend time with you until you understand things. There is a lot of information so better study from the start. Thankfully the final is not cumulative.

This professor really helped me organize to study for my exams. In addition, he took ample time to explain the material even after exams, or to explain what I was missing in my exam. This class is my last requirement and this helped a lot!

He's amazing! If you put your all into his classes you will be rewarded. Yes it will be the hardest class of your life but you will not regret a single moment- be sure to take advantage of office hours and ask questions!
The lectures are amazing. I consider changing major and taking more biology because of this class.
He was sooo helpful during review sessions!!!
Fantastic professor. He makes everything clear !
I loved that class. But it was clearly the toughest since I started at Cornell !
I took that class as an external student. The content was very interesting, and challenging. I really appreciated the feedback from the Professor, who answered all my questions quickly.
Great class. But the curving really makes it difficult to get an A.
This class is quite interesting but tough on non bio majors. The course goes quite in depth which requires a lot of memorization. Overall a very interesting class for premeds.
A very solid class for physiology
This class was terrible- so disorganized, the material was not presented in a clear way and it was very unclear what we were meant to learn. Class objectives were not meant

EVERYONE shows up to class. Is this because its an honor's course with people who truly wish to learn? to some degree probably. However, his lectures are wildly helpful and informative - Brilliant guy who clearly knows his stuff, the enthusiasm will transfer on to you if you're open to it

really passionate professor that is very interested in the subject! the class is very proof based so attending TA office hours was super helpful- recommend taking the engineering one (easier). it is a difficult class but you do get a deep conceptual understanding of linear algebra. psets are moderately difficult but the grad TAs are so so helpful

Not a great lecturer - often spends too much time on examples and sometimes explains things weirdly. Written homework and exams are sometimes not fully reflective of the most recent topics learned. But the class is easy enough that concepts don't require extended analysis.
Tough Grader
Good, ready to help, not great.
Not a good lecturer. Went to office hours and he came across as extremely rude. Difficult to understand. Would not take again.

Obviously a professor who is very passionate about the subject material. That being said, his lectures are often unmotivating and poorly communicated/hard to follow. Doesn't finish his sentences a lot of the time or takes minutes to think of a response. I ended up learning a lot of the material primarily by myself as a result.

He is a great teacher! His lectures are engaging, and you can tell he is really passionate about the subject. The exams are fair, and the exams are based solely on lectures! The class isn't curved, but there are a couple extra credit opportunities. I would def take a class with him again. If you work hard and study, you'll get the grade u want.

The  class itself isn't incredibly easy when it comes to tests/assignments. But the lectures were pretty redundant if you took 2350, and he can be really clueless/kind of funny in that way. But overall he's a great teacher and i recommend the class! Just study his powerpoints and hopefully you get an A. Go to class--there are frequent pop-quizzes.

Took him Spring 2015. He's a chill guy. Tests are reasonable and easy. Lenient grading. He tells you what will be on it. 1/3 of his lectures cover the US healthcare system which you learned from Nicholson's PAM 2350. Resourceful--helped me with a question for another class. Nerdy cute. Keeps track of attendance.

He is very hard to reach out. Did not respond to any of my emails and doesn't really take the class seriously. Always give yourself an A in the portfolio as he never bumps up the grade for getting it "right". Funny guy and gives decent feedback but it seems he does not care alot about the class. Ironically, not great at communicating.

This class manages to be stressful without being fulfilling or intellectually challenging. The class was dominated by TAs. It takes forever to get graded assignments back. Prof. Lennox is pretty hard to reach over email. The book we read is tested on for the first prelim but you get the sense that he forgets it exists after the 3rd week.
Good class to take. Learn a lot of important skills regarding communication. You will enjoy this class and the professor.
Funny guy, but very slow with returning work.
Amazing
She was very unhelpful and not nice when seeking advice from her as a student.

Her lectures are really good, but she goes through the material really fast. A lot of the class is also based around your discussion group, so she feels a bit distant from the students. The only test we took was a final, which asked about very small details covered over the whole semester, so it was surprisingly hard.
Professor Shaw is, to put it mildly, inspiring. Her lectures in the course are fantastic. She is very approachable outside of class. One of the most sincere professors I've had at Cornell.

In the middle of the class, she taught us a lot of very basic evolutionary theories that we had already gone over with previous professors in the class.  If you had taken Bio1780, the vast majority of her material was totally review.  She seems not to realize that most of us already understand basic evolutionary ideas.
Prof. Shaw seemed very unresponsive to emails, as were her tas, while many of the lecturers for this class were very good, she was not, her lectures were boring and were not captivating.
Grades harshly, but still is the GOAT
Hodes is iconically bad. Lectures are horrible. He's condescending whenever a question is asked. Huge mismatch between lectures and homework. Would only recommend it for the memes.

I don't know how he is for philosophy but don't take any of his math classes, he nitpicks a ton when grading proofs and won't give any credit unless everything is done his way (even if the logic is spot on). He's also quite arrogant and condescending (you'd think someone who can barely operate zoom would be a bit more humble.)

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. I have taken two classes with him so far. Brilliant and extremely clear. A logician indeed. Not to mention he is the most chilled professor I've had when it comes to deadlines. I don't know why most ratings are negative about him. Maybe if they took one of his smaller classes, they'd appreciate him more.
He came to class late without a sense of apology. Very disorganized, ill-prepared and irresponsible. Trite and glib. Doesn't seem to enjoy teaching or enthusiastic about the subject.

Prof. Hodes is one of the worst and most disorganized professors I've had. Lectures jump all over the place, handwriting is terrible, grading criteria is vague, grading is overly harsh, and gives assignments (like papers) on the fly with no advance notice or proper timing. Totally advise against taking a class with him.
no

Lectures were a little on the dull side, but you can tell Hodes loves logic. The proofs were interesting and homework was very simple. Exams were reasonable and based entirely on proofs done in class.

Don't take previous comments too seriously. Hodes is good at the subject and he is suuuuuper cute!!! You won't see many old nice guys around the campus. The course is hard though and worth taking only if you like to analyze boring sentences. Homeworks are hard compared with prelims and finals.

Hodes is a brilliant man, but is tragically condescending. He'll openly bash you in class for having faulty reasoning or poor grasp of the English language. The subject material is focused more on fundamentals, so it's a bit different from normal logic classes. He's usually one to stammer because the material is dense at times.

A real sweetheart, but at times confusing, and not a very kind grader. Not to be recommended if you don't have a keen interest in the subject material. The stuff we covered in class was difficult, but accessible with persistence. All that said, he's a hilarious dude with a moustache that will make you crack up. Go see him during office hours.
Hodes is (a) awesome, and (b) too cute for words. What a mensch!!!

An excellent Professor for students who accept, even though they are "Ivy League", that they are often wrong and unaware that they are wrong.  Many people like him even though they are not doing well grade-wise.  Often these are people who don't do the homework.  This material isn't difficult if you do the homework.  Do it!  Hodes rules.

As interesting a teacher as you are in the material. Those that found him boring found the material boring, while I thought both were pretty interesting. No question he wants you to do well, makes himself available outside of class, and gave us last year's tests to study by. I'd take his advanced calss next year. The text book he chose was great.

Professor Hodes is a nice guy who wants to help his students.  However, unless you are exceptionally good at things like math and logic, it is impossible to get an A.  I am very hardworking and have never had a grade below A, but in this class, despite working 10-20 hours/week, the best grade I got was a B.  He moves at his own pace, not students.

Prof Hodes is the funniest entity in the world. His bushy moustache just makes me wanna scratch it. That being said, he is an utter horror of a professor. He goes at his own speed, not the student's. And he is far too cruel to ask questions. He WILL humilliate you. Expect to see 'rewrite' next to 90% of your papers. That being said, he's too funny.
Most people dislike the class, not him. He is an excellent teacher who happens to enjoy a very difficult field. He loves what he does and makes for an interesting, if not useful course.

I really like him personally. He does try hard to be available to give outside help. But I had done well in logic with other professors and in this class I was utterly lost. I didn't understand his questions and he didn't understand my assignments, and it was all just a very unhappy experience.
He's not as bad as everyone says.  Still, he is a bit dull.

He's really not that bad. Absent-minded and yes he did assign impossible problems on the prelim and final. But his presentation in class is decent and the textbook is excellent. Exams are fair, he doesn't ask things you haven't learned. Make sure you check your prelim grades though -- he messed up mine 2 times. Do all the homework, best way 2 learn

On both one prelim and our final, he gave literally impossible questions. He announced that he messed up the prelim after the test, and realized his mistake in the last 10 mins of the final. Despite this, he didn't offer any type of compensation for the time people wasted trying to solve his impossible questions. Overall, a very unreasonable guy.
this guy makes the class harder than it is. he never helps you out on the smallestof issues & makes you feel dumb for asking something on the topic your LEARNING!!!

Prelim 1: Spent 30 min on one problem that was actually unsolvable because Hodes made a mistake writing it.  And, for my efforts in noting that on my test, I got an extra "+" next to my grade.  Meaning I got a "D-+", i.e. a D- with a gold star next to it.  Really makes me feel much better about having to drop this and take 20 credits next semester.
Cool class, terrible professor. Good Prof--but grades unfairly.

He definitely puts a lot of time and effort into his job.  He'll usually try hard to answer your questions.  Just keep a positive attitude and don't be intimidated.  And he's a bit hard of hearing, so speak up!

A GPA BUSTER! Yes he is definitly clear on what he wants you to do, that is, unless you ask a question-for if you do beware of an unprecedented tongue-lashing! Take this class with a different professor, and you may actually learn something, and may potentially make above the HODES-stipulated mean:C
completely unapproachable.  makes you feel like an idiot for asking a question.  grading seems very subjective.  avoid him.  other profs teach this class

Actually a very interesting course, but Hodes is the absolute worst.  He has a bad rep with other profs too.  His grading is not understandable (he doesn't give A's unless "you know the material as well as [he] does." AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE.

It's like you're calling him out whenever you ask a question... and he knows what you're getting at, you can see it in hi eyes, but he'll pick apart the grammar of your sentence... like a needle under your cuticle

Professor Hodes is amazing. He's one of my favorite professors so far. If you're interested in the material and you are willing to put in the time, he'll be there for you. He is one of the professors that I am asking to write a recommendation for me.
Underrated as a funny professor, not because he makes jokes, but because I just cant stop laughing when I'm around him.
HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!! HODES!!!!
Oh man, this was the worst class in the world.  Hodes! is now a rallying cry of frustration amongst many people I know.
Absolutely Intolerable. Avoid. Avoid. Avoid.
Not a fun class
This man is a nightmare.  He is not only incompetent, but he is an intolerable person as well.  He will make a seemingly interesting course into torture.  Do not take any course taught by this man.

He is an awesome teacher and lecturer, not to mention an awesome person. It's kind of sad because students (myself included) feel awkward answering questions cause everyone's so spread out, but he still makes it an extremely interesting class. Nerd out with him after class; he will act as if he doesn't know 1,000 times more than you do, but he does

Prof. Craighead is a genius.  He knows a lot, check out his wikipedia page.  He is able to clearly explain things.  His class is thoroughly enjoyable.  When he had to miss lecture for a research conference, he would schedule an expert in the field to lecture on their expertise.  Exams are fair, study your notes from lecture and you'll be fine.

Prof. Craighead is honestly one of the nicest guys I've ever met. Studying for his exams can be a little annoying because it's a little hard to figure out what you'll be tested on, but the exams themselves are more than fair. On the whole, it's a class I wholeheartedly recommend mostly due to Craighead showing he really cares about his students.

He knows so much about nanoscience it's ridiculous.  His lectures can be a bit rambly and it is hard to tell what you will be tested on.  Sometimes he appears to feel not confident about his teaching skills, but you wil learn a lot in this class.  If you are unclear on a topic, he will definitely help you out.  Assignments are not difficult either.
He's awesome. Get to know him.

Such a nice guy, I learned a lot and he made me excited to go to lab. He really makes an effort to connect with his students and appreciates when his students show an interest in the subject. I will definitely take another of his courses in the future if possible.
He's such a good professor who emphasizes learning over grades. Kind, compassionate, and enthusiastic. Flexible and works with students to make sure they can get the work done.

Best professor I've had at Cornell! Professor Mazourek is THE most understanding, caring, and down-to-earth professor you'll ever meet; his lectures are engaging and refreshing, and he always values his students' input. The class can be challenging at times, but he is always holding review sessions to clarify any questions. Definitely recommend!!!

Probability theory is not an easy topic and Raj does an excellent job teaching an introductory class while gauging interest in upper level proofs. Everything is proved in class but the test are mostly based on applied cases. Vert few professors can make you better at mathematics and that's why Raj was excellent because he made al of us better!

Raj is a great professor! He does an excellent job of breaking down difficult concepts into smaller pieces, and does his best to make time for his students. He tries to squeeze in interesting storiestrivia during class to keep students awake. Tests are NOT regurgitation of HW problems, however if you understand the concepts well tests aren't hard.

Tests, like any math course at Cornell, are ridiculously difficult. A lot of the homework from the book is more theory based (small proofs), but the tests are I think all applied problems. Textbook and solutions can be found online. The curve must have been very nice because I did poorly all semester but managed to get a B
Good course! Lectures could be less dense though
Good professor-- easy to do well if you go to class and occasionally office hours, but she was pretty rude and had a big ego. The TA's were cool though

Best professor I've taken during my time in ILR. People who claim to have problems with her don't pay attention and probably don't go to office hours. She makes her classes really easy to understand. I loved how she gave us hypotheticals for the exam and focused a lot on unions/worker rights. Best class and best professor...highly recommend!

I highly recommend taking labor law with Lieberwitz! I learned so much from her class and confirmed my desire to go to law school. Use all resources provided to do well in class - e.g., office hours, TAs, extra credit assignments, slides. Exams are open book but still require a lot of preparation. Unclear grading criteria is a bit frustrating.

Lieberwitz is a good professor - tough, but fair.  The open book exams are difficult and lengthy.  Brief all assigned cases and do all practice hypotheticals before exams! Her grading criteria is nonexistent, which can be annoying. Start early on legal memo and go to TA office hours!! Hard class, but very interesting and my favorite this semester.

No clear grading criteria for this class. The professor and the TAs communicate nothing about assignment and final grades for the class. She just claims that she will grade in our favor, but no specific scale is given. Avoid this class if you want even an ounce of clarity about your performance.

I highly recommend taking Professor Lieberwitz because she genuinely cares about her students. If you go to her office hours, you should have no problems at all. Pay attention in class because if you don't, you will get lost since her PowerPoints are not very detailed. Sweet lady - I learned a lot

Do not take Professor Lieberwitz for this class. There is little to no structure in the class, and you pretty much just rely on her arbitrary grading when it comes to exams. She assigns an insane amount of reading for every class as well which doesn't help.
If you want to have any sort of control over your grade, take it with Griffith. Grades received in this class do not at all reflect performance.
generally unclear grading criteria will leave you confused and disappointed

Awesome prof who really cares. Sample exams show you exactly what you need to do. Classes are really helpful in highlighting the legal principles and rules that you need. Make sure you do your briefs, should be 20 minutes per lecture and will be very helpful for the exam. Generally application based class with a few specifics to know.

You will do well with a lot of effort, but will also do okay with very little effort. Never did any reading and still ended up with a B. Lieberwitz's ideology is very left-leaning, and only likes to give one side of every issue, but is overall a nice and passionate professor. Show up to class so you don't have to teach yourself the material.
Prof. Lieberwitz is amazing! She is so willing to help. She will defer a lot to the TA, but she is still very involved. Definitely try to get her!!

She is a nice professor who is pretty thorough and clear with the material she presents. Reading consists of case law that you have to "brief" and her tests are hypothetical situations in which you have to apply cases you've learned about. Not looking for you to do too much, which makes the exams better to navigate through. All in all, very fair
Great Teacher. Must be able to think critically and creatively to do well. Enjoy my time in her class even though I didn't get an A.
Spunky and thoughtful. A great and fun professor and an interesting class. Not heavy on details and specifics but provides an excellent intro to legal reasoning and the general field of labor law

Labor & Employment Law: great teacher, leader in her field, get the Nutshell Book (Labor Law) and you'll have no trouble following the cases, takes some work, but it's an ILR required class so you might as well take it from a good professor. Always avail. for office ours & good TAs.

Disorganized and frequently impossible to follow, she ran a 78-person class like a 12-person seminar. She happens to be really, really good at the latter format, but the into class format was borderline intolerable. Despite my justified qualms about teaching style, I learned so much, though I'm not sure what that had to do with her teaching.

One of the easiest classes I've taken.  The class sits in a circle and discusses the cases.  I'm pretty sure the median grade is an A.  You don't really learn much though (I think we only covered like 10 cases all semester).  An easy A but don't have high expectations for what you're going to take away from the class.
No Comments

Very interesting, very knowledgable, and willing to challenge you and what you say in front of the rest of class. A must if you want to go to law school. Her papers are exactly what you will write in law school. Take her instead of Gold in a second- learn just as much with 1/4 the work.

Attendance policy was completely wack, no drops and will count against you unless you tell them way in advance (even if you become sick). The course was very difficult but worth it. Professor was sweet but also biased in her content. I enjoyed the content and the flow! Discussions were boring though

This is a difficult class, but you get a lot out of it. Tests are pretty hard and require alot of studying, but they do get significant curves. Professor is nice and is very knowledgable.  TAs are also really great and gave a lot of help on assignments and test prep. But if you don't pay attention and work hard, you're definitely going to struggle

Caring professor and gives engaging lectures. Exams are tough but rewarding. She's a lenient grader but sets her grade brackets pretty high. Felt like I did A quality work but because she does't round a 93.6% remains an A-. Definitely deflating and makes me reconsider taking a class with her again because in any other class that would be an A.

The most caring Professor I've had at Cornell! Concepts covered in class are foundational for any PAM Major, and the projects are a decent amount of work but prepare you very well for future PAM classes. Lots of resources to help you succeed (she posts 2 years of past exams, sample papers/presentations and is super accessible outside of class).

Professor Avery is amazing! This class is one where you get out of it what you put into it. It's definitely time consuming, but extremely relevant and interesting. Grading isn't very harsh, but you need to do the work in order to pass. Definitely recommend.

Professor is really organized and is a good lecturer, learned a lot about different federal policies. People say the class is a lot of work, but you're given a lot of time to actually do the assignments. Grading was very fair - if you put in the work you will get an A.

This was not an easy class, but at the end, the median was an A or A-. It was a great way to start my freshman year, I feel like I learned a ton and also learned how to study in college. The TAs are really attentive and helpful (and chill since they're undergrads). Had to study a lot for the prelims, but they got curved up by 15%.

Nice person, but I hated this class. Took it last semester and it made me drop the PAM major. She expects you to memorize random facts + statistics from lecture slides that are just almost impossible to memorize.
