I found this prof to be unapproachable and smug.  Can't recommend.
Lovenheim is the man! His class was interesting and yet challenging and he is always willing to help.

The best professor I have had in the department. His lectures are interesting, fun and challenging. Although he sometimes talks in circles, he is still great to listen to for 90 minutes. His tests are hard, but he is really fair and always available for help. Highly recommended, I learned a lot!

Great guy, all around. The nicest, most helpful professors I've had at Cornell. The class sucked but it's not his fault; econometrics is hard and required. However, he made it as enjoyable as possible (albeit that is still not very enjoyable). I highly recommend taking a (different) class with him.  He'll bend over backward to help any student!

One of the hardest PAM classes. If not the hardest.  what makes this class rough is 1) PSETS: very, very long, from 10-25 hours, and 2) STATA (which you need for psets), 3) ridiculous exams that are way too crammed for the alotted time. Be prepared for those 3 things ruining this class.
Do not recommend.

A interesting, engaging, and nice guy who is always happy to help out. However, he often lacks clarity in explaining lecture concepts in that he makes things seem more complicated than they are. Seek additional help if you have trouble understanding lecture material.

Exams are graded harshly with no partial credit. Very strict grader and very condescending in Ed discussions. Always has to tell the class to be quiet and pay attention due to not being able to get the class active.

Lectures were fast-paced and hard to understand due to messy handwriting, plus unnecessary as the online notes were 10x better, and he'd tell us to read those whenever he failed to finish all the content for the day anyway. Serially failed to engage the class and blamed everyone but himself for it. Gave 0 partial credit on very difficult tests.
The professor makes a boring topic very interesting and engages everyone. Class isn't mandatory, but all of the tests are based off what he says in class.

The ratings here are really really odd, because everyone in my class loved it. The content and the tests are not hard if you pay attention and study. The papers are also pretty interesting, and if you just put some thought into it, you do well. And the tenure comment is really irrelevant and makes me wonder if they even payed attention in class.
This professor actually expects you to earn your grade but he is fair and you end up learning a lot in this class.  You'll learn a lot more here than if you take the class with Tracey.

He's not the greatest professor around, but he deserves more credit than he gets.  He seems to be interested in the material he presents and the journal assignments teach a lot but are not difficult.  Final is very tough.

Sucked.  Take this class with Tracey.  This dude only cares about getting tenured and hates hotelies.  I learned nothing in his class and sitting through it was painful.  I want a refund of my money for taking this class.
The class was so boring--i kept falling asleep--nice guy though--too bad he forgets everyones names

He is a nice guy but will kill your GPA if you don't give him exactly what he wants. He will give you feedback on your paper and then give you a low grade because he will find other mistakes that he didn't find before. Avoid taking his class. If you don't have EXACTLY what he wants, expect a C or lower on your assignments.
He is an extremely tough grader but once you understand what he's looking for youre fine.
Terrible teacher. He makes no sense. Shouldn't be teaching.
He is a nice and interesting professor. He is also a hard grader but the class is easy if you do your work.

He has no consistent way in grading and just grades on his whim. He definitely plays favorites and is a terrible teacher. As a ManComm teacher who teaches communication skills, you would think he would be better at communicating his own ideas. It's literally "my way or the highway" in his class.

Dr. Lau is knowledgeable in AA history. The textbook is free. The course is straightforward with one a quiz a week (only 5 questions). Final is you interviewing an Asian American over the age of 50 about a topic of your choice. Comes across too professional, not very warm or relatable. Weird class with good content. TONS of reading.

Lectures are definitely worth attending as the material is engaging,  and will definitely be tested on. Professor Lau is a sweet person and a very good lecturer and a fair grader. You will learn a lot from her Asian American History class.

Good professor. Pop quizzes were a little harsh (each question was 1% of the grade), but gave a LOT of extra credit opportunities, each worth a whole 1% toward your grade. Be sure to speak up in class, get your participation grade up, and you will be fine with the class.

Don't take her. Not worth the trouble. The readings were pretty bland, she's knowledgable & really into the class though. Came off as really rude at the end. Extra credit was 1 hour 1/2 really boring events for 1 pt. If you missed a pop quiz your grade went to hell. People were crying about getting B's on their papers because they were so happy..

Prof. Lau initially came off as a little bit cold and scary, but she is one of the best teachers I've ever had at Cornell (and this year was only her 1st!). She's passionate, knowledgeable, and is sure to cater her class to her students. She moved our whole syllabus around after our mid-semester class survey. Not many prof. would do so, but she did

I liked writing before going to class and I grew a lot as a writer because of it. Excellent, honest feedback that was not harsh. She encouraged all kinds of writers, including students who lacked creativity. Assignments were fairly light and fair, and the class had a good pace.

Idk about her fws, but as a creative writing instructor, she is THE BEST. She is an excellent critic. She is nice but structures everything well. She teaches her intro class in a way that even prolific writers appreciate. And she is ALWAYS available to help and willing to put in all of the time you need for her workshops. Take her class! It's fun!

He is extremely passionate and it shines through with the effort he puts into his classes. He gives very detailed & rigorous notes for his lectures; with 4060 this was incredibly helpful since it is a complex topic, however it was definitely a lot harder. Only professor I've ever had that reminded/validated us how mechE is hard & we're doing great

Great professor - definitely loves the math side of dynamics but also very knowledgeable about the material and fielding questions. Makes you work for the class but at the end of the day is forgiving about grading.

Went incredibly fast through lectures at the beginning of the class, calmed down after a few weeks. Homeworks varied, some were easy but others were really long and tough. The material covered at the end was unnecessarily difficult for the course. Was sometimes condescending in lecture but usually helpful at office hours. Open note exams.

He speeds breathlessly through lectures so it's hard enough to write anything let alone understand what he's talking about. Even worse he makes a lot of mistakes in lecture which makes you feel even more lost. Treats dynamics as if we've all been studying it for the past ten years. The textbook is just as bad. Plenty of office hrs to help though.
super fast iclicker
I agree with the previous reviewer. In my last semester at UC Merced that was my experience. I will be talking with Dean about this professor.
He is so automated you have to plug him into the wall.  Sometimes I have "trouble delineating his voice, graphically and pictorially".

Selvaraj is very kind professor and always helpful in office hours. His lecture videos are extremely long and dense - it is very easy to get lost in them and I would have to set aside a good 2 to 3 hour time block just to get through. His exam questions are VERY similar to the in-class questions, HIGHLY recommend going to lecture for neurobio.
Such a difficult class but clearly knowledge prof and  he's so approachable outside of lecture, I just wish he put more text on the slides sometimes but ig it forces me to pay more attention :)
lecture slides are very unclear...although he is very passionate
Prob one of the most difficult classes I've taken. Prof seemed super smart and I liked his diagrams. You will def have to pour your heart and soul into the class if u want an A, though.

Excellent professor - does a very effective job of communicating a lot of important concepts in a very short period of time. Attending lecture wasn't required, but necessary if you wanted to pass the course. Wasn't the most engaging speaker (from a public speaking perspective), but genuinely wants to see you succeed.

Very bland and boring lecturer; fell asleep in his class a few times. It can be difficult to understand the lecture from the slides, but that is what class notes are for. He can be muffled, so record his lectures at the front of the room. He also asks niche questions on weekly quizzes that can make the difference between a letter grade.

He's an insanely smart guy he definitely knows his stuff. He and Dr. Allen make a great tag team, Selvaraj is the more reserved harsh grader and Dr. Allen is the energetic professor who tries to help you. Sit near the front cause he NEEDS TO SPEAK UP.

Very respectable professor, but completely unrelatable and he gives off the vibe that he is so smart that he cannot connect with students. I have heard he's a terrible advisor as well. Domestic animal bio is saved by Dr. Allen. Selvaraj is not a bad person, just not friendly.
Difficult class, mostly fair lectures and prelims

Very knowledgable and seemed highly interested in his topics (primarily neurons) in the online lectures. Tests are tough, but not impossible. I found the slide diagrams rly helpful when studying for the exams. In-person lectures (discussion-style) were just recaps of the online lectures.

I think selvaraj was fine in 1440 this semester. The class was flipped so we watched his lectures online. I didnt really like how the slides were picture heavy (vs. text), but this teaching style wasnt really a problem because we could pause/rewind/slow down the video if needed. Really nice guy also if you meet w him outside of class.
Lectures and exams overwhelm the students with information that is irrelevant or unimportant rather than testing on the main concepts.

This is a weed-out course. It's a fast-paced, jam-packed class, but it is NOT an unfair one. If this class is too difficult, then it's done its job. Vet school will be no different. Take good notes during class. Selvaraj's slides aren't something you can review five minutes before an exam. Material was always interesting.

This is a weed-out course, and Selvaraj teaches it as such. His lectures are incredibly fascinating and his interest in the material is engaging. The class content is dense, but not unreasonably so. His questions can be nichethe multifaceted nature of the subject matter allows for it. You have to work for the A, but it is perfectly obtainable.

It' obvious that Dr. Selvaraj is very knowledgeable in his field, however, he's not great at explaining concepts for an intro-level course. Lecture slides barely had text on them so attending and recording lectures is a must to get all of the information needed. Quizzes would be helpful if they tested overall knowledge instead of trivial fun facts.

I think Selvaraj would rather be elsewhere when he is teaching. Comes off as distant and uninterested (except for the ligamentum nuchae lol) Slides lack any writing so heavy note-taking required. However, he is definitely knowledgeable. Quiet voice and accent make him difficult to understand, so sit close to the front. His quizzes aim to trick you.

Dr. Selvaraj's class is difficultespecially if it's your first formal introduction to anatomy and physiologybut don't mistake the rigor of his course for poor teaching. He could be a little louder during lectures and make his slides more accessible for studying, but I do believe that he is fair and stimulating. Material is dense, not impossible.
Knowledgeable and invested.

Im not going to lie, I didn't understand a single lecture from this professor. It seems like he cares, but I was complexity lost when trying to study from my notes and his sparse slides. Would not recommend, sorry ! (take the online version 1441 if you can, it will save your life!)

He is rather hard to understand at the beginning due to his accent. His slides are not very elaborate and typically only consist of a single image or phrase. He speaks very quickly and does not usually stop for questions. He is not very easy to access outside of class and I had to rely heavily on other resources.

DON'T EVER TAKE HIS CLASSES!!! always gave us recorded lectures for an hour straight (some of them were even 1hr20min long) but he still couldn't explain things clearly. Lectures were real boring and made me fall asleep. The concepts of the class were not bad tho, just the profs.
Lecture slides unclear - not enough text, just some pictures. Glosses over some phrases that are key to understanding difficult concepts.

Professor Selvaraj really tried to explain neurons. His powerpoints unfortunately were a bit sparse and the concepts themselves were extremely difficult. As BIOG 1440 is a memorization heavy class, it was difficult, but he made very useful study sheets and was clear about what he expected from students.

I think this was the first time Prof Selvaraj was teaching 1440. His slides contained almost no information, and he overcomplicated his lectures by adding material outside the scope. He also mumbled and talked very softly while lecturing which made him hard to understand.

This is the classic Cornell weed-out course for pre-vets. Take advantage of outside resources like your textbook when you don't understand something. Labs are helpful for review/ understanding material, ask your TA's lots of questions, they are full of advice. Attend lecture, you will fail otherwise and sit and study for hours to pass prelims.

His accent is difficult to get used to and his lectures are extremely fast paced, but they are helpful and extremely informative. The in-class quizzes are a helpful tool for learning. The tests are stupid hard but the curve is fairly generous. If you want a A you really have to work for it, if you want it, you still need to put in generous work.
Very information heavy lecture. You are expected to memorize a lot of concepts so make sure you plan your time accordingly. The prelims are really information specific and full of dense material.

Very intelligent professor. A ton of studying involved. Memorization is key. One of the hardest classes I've taken, but everyone will get through it. Definitely don't take this class if it isn't a requirement.
Clear lecturer that really knows his stuff and will help you understand it. The lectures are dense, and there will be a lot of that material on tests. Labs are a ton of fun too

Dr. Selvaraj was not an enjoyable professor. He is difficult to understand during lecture and takes points off of exams if you spell things incorrectly. This class was way too much work and very stressful. Lots of quizzes.
Extremely interesting class, and Selvaraj is an amazing lecturer. Definitely the hardest course I've taken at Cornell, though
Amazing professor and one of the most brilliant people I have ever met. He teaches a tough class but it is worth every moment. If you put in your effort he will make this class the best you take

Dr. Selvaraj is a great professor and extremely interested in helping his students succeed. Older reviews reference a class which has since been improved in the areas that students found difficult during the first couple of years. It is still a difficult course but is by no means unreasonable - it takes work, but so will vet school!

Dr. Selvaraj is a wonderful professor who truly cares about his students.  This is not an easy class by any means, but if you put in the necessary work (attend all lectures, go to office hours, do the readings), you will be fine.  1100 serves as a great intro to the field of animal science and will really show you if it is the right major for you.
Tests are very hard and you have to be able to spit the book back out for each questions and know everything in great detail. I only took the class because it is required.
Great class with a great professor.  Quizzes and tests rely heavily on the textbook and diagrams, but if you take the class seriously, you learn a lot and will do fine.

This class is the perfect way to test whether or not you really want to go to vet school. This class gives you a foundation for all of your future animal classes, making life much easier as you move to other higher level courses. It's not an easy class but completely worth working through and is very rewarding. Lectures are important in doing well.

Dr. Selvaraj is a fantastic professor.  He asks a lot of his students, but not only is it to push them to be better, but also to give them a taste of what vet school will be like. The class was not easy at all, but if you have a strong interest in the subject, I highly recommend it. He is willing to help you whenever you need it. Overall great guy.

Professor is super nice and is willing to help you. The problem with this course is that it is all over the place. You are literally tested on a bunch of facts.I found the pre-lims nearly impossible to study for. If you do not have to take this class DO NOT.

Dr. Selvaraj is very kind and is very clear what is important for exams in his lectures. Although the class is not easy, it is a necessary foundation and gives you a great head start on the rest of your animal science courses. If you worked hard on this course and followed all of the resources he gives you, there will be no problem and do well.

Prof. Selverage runs a very challenging course but for many Animal Science majors the class is a taste of what vet school will be like. He is VERY kind man if you get to know him and will work as hard as you do if you just go to him. No doubt that the amount of information is a lot at times but if you are thinking/planning on vet school, take it.

Let's give this guy a break! He's a good person and a fantastic teacher, he just gave difficult exams. Most people failed to note that the exams CAME STRAIGHT FROM HIS POWERPOINTS!! And, when people didn't do well, he set up extra class times to help people out. This class was still a ton of work, but it was worth it and hes not a bad guy.

New teacher, seems interested in what he is talking about, but he's a VET. Not a teacher. He assumes massive prior knowledge of the subject matte. You are required to memorize a 500 page textbook word-for-word to pass weekly quizzes.  I do not recommend this class unless you know a LOT about animal science / intense in depth Biology already.

Expectations for the class are ridiculously high for and an introductory level. Expected to memorize an extensive amount of material, much of which you aren't even tested on. Moves quickly through concepts and either does not know or does not care that the class is not keeping up.
Not at all helpful, hard to understand the points he is trying to make. Assumes the class knows what he knows. Moves super fast and without alot of clarity. Avoid his classes if you can!
Extremely difficult.  Moves extremely quickly through topics. Focuses so much on details that the big picture is hard to understand. Expects students to already know the everything he is discussing.
Extremely hard class, expects students to know everything

Moves extremely quickly through difficult topics. Requires a lot of textbook reading. If you are taking this class (as an Animal Science major) limit your schedule. If you're not required to take this class with this professor, don't.

She was a great lecturer, she was very nice to her students and took into account when people made suggestions of things that might make it easier for us (i.e. posting slides before class). She posted all the lecture notes and opened a discussion section on Canvas for everyone to ask questions. She was awesome, wish I had her in more classes.

Professor Lawlor is the best professor I've had. She is passionate, enthusiastic and has a great sense of humor. Despite longer readings, as expected in history, her discussions in seminar are thought provoking and she's not afraid to follow the interests of students in what they read. I want to be an academic and she is no small reason why.

By far, Prof. Lawlor was my favorite professor while at Cornell. She is truly an inspiration for those who aspire to remain in academia as a career, as Prof. Lawlor is the kind of scholar one hopes to emulate. Her classes are very reading-heavy, but Prof Lawlor is very empathetic and does her best to ensure her students' success.

Her Gender & Sexuality seminar was one of the best courses I've taken at Cornell. Readings and discussions were varied, relevant, and interesting. She's extremely knowledgable, caring, and a fair grader. However, readings are long and if you're confused about a concept she may ramble. Papers are tailored to personal interests. Highly recommend.

Professor is so passionate, it radiates into the lectures and discussions. Grading scale is unique (85 is an A-) and it's writing-based but overall a solid course. She is just overall a very nice person who's accessible to students and has tons of knowledge. Lecture heavy but participation is encouraged. Final project/paper worth 40%.
Professor Chekitan was absolutely great in bringing the class attention and engage the students with group projects and case studies.

Professor Dev is undeniably an expert in the field of Branding and his enthusiasm for the field is infectious. His lectures, assignments, and guest lecturers are immediately relevant to your career and the concepts are laid out in a well organized manor. Professor Dev is upbeat, prepared, and encourages the class to engage in dialog which is great!

Professor Dev presented a framework for marketing at the beginning of the course, and used it as map to link all course sections. This provides students with a clear map of the whole marketing knowledge structure. 

In addition, various cases are used in the class to demonstrate each point. This facilitates students' understanding.

I was really excited to take Professor Chekitan Dev's class, as I actually work as a Marketer in the Hospitality Industry for 8 years in China, i still can tell the fresh and well-structured principles from the cases shared in class. and I was also inspired and get a fresh review on my existing consulting customer  like Shanghai Disney Resort etc.

The class is well organized and professor is always open to discuss and share.
Enjoy the learning process, interesting and easy to learn.
Quizs questions are all covered in class, need to be participate and engage in class.
Great marketing class with Professor Dev.

Very insightful and informative. Lots of experience directly from the service-industry. cases are carefully selected and sessions are delivered in a very engaging way. Especially for students with experiences in hospitality already, this course helps to connect a lot of dots!
So useful for the real life

Professor Dev brings his vast indepth knowledge along with valuable practical insights from the industry which really add a lot of gravitas to the topics whilst making them easier to comprehend and relate to.  He brings great clarity to marketing concepts and equally is quiet focussed on guest experience and creating great brand equity.

What I liked the most of Professor Dev's class was understanding that, apart from the creative part of cenceptualizing and building a strong hospitality brand, there is a fundamental part of the job related to the very thorough analysis of all qualitative and quantitative data within our reach in order to inform and help us take crucial decissions.

A fabulous professor who conceptualized brand value in tangible terms, well before the industry was ready for it. A true inspiration who introduced us to forward thinking concepts that would become the cornerstone of Hospitality and retail brands. 
He has been a tutor and mentor, always celebrating my successes. Its been a privileges Cheki!

Nia T

Professor Dev is very passionate and knowledgeable! He made our course interesting and fun! The environment he cultivated during the course was friendly and enthusiastic. He engaged all curiosities from all levels of professional titles, COO, owners, directors, PR's, etc. of award winning hospitality establishments from all over the world. Bravo!

His course was incredibly insightful and provided me with a wealth of new knowledge that I cannot wait to apply in my work. It has been a true eye-opener and I feel better-equipped than ever. Frankly speaking, this world-class course has been an absolute game-changer for me, and I am grateful for the opportunity to have learned from such a master!

Professor Chekitan Dev offers an outstanding marketing course that covers a wide range of topics with a systematic approach. Although each section is relatively short, the complete path to understanding marketing is impressive and leaves a lasting impression. 
The only downside is the daily exams, but they are straightforward and manageable.

def a great lecturer and will take his courses again.
He left strict instruction that no talking and any other distractions during the lecture. 
His content included a tons of mkt commercials and clips of talk shows, which will be the questions in the quizzes, so be careful of the videos.
but all in all, prof Chekitan has a solid clear structure.

Prof Dev was approachable and easy to communicate with. He took the time to understand each of our backgrounds, and seamlessly integrated our individual experiences into the course. This personalized approach allowed us to better understand the material and was deeply appreciated by all. His passion and expertise are truly inspiring.
i think that Prof. Chekitan is a responsible and respectable teacher.

Professor Dev is a legend at Cornell. His course will prepare you to think analytically through global marketing issues. I would highly recommend it. He has an interest in his students and will provide continuous feedback and offer career guidance long after the course is complete.

To be completely honest, I was a bit intimidated by the class at first, but the way Prof. Dev presented the material and allowed us to work with the owners of La Tourelle, it ended up being one of my favorite classes. I still have my "Ithaca is Gorges" frisbee that my team all signed after winning one of the week's presentations.

Dev is the best marketing mind on campus and the most compelling lecturer I had for my MBA.  Throughout my 25-year career, his lessons on evaluating the strategic landscapes of industries and customer acquisition, retention, and delight were enormously useful.  He relied on high profile case studies involving hospitality giants.
He is condescending and has an ego bigger than the room. He is also just rude, even when he is in the wrong.

This is a really useful course. Since taking the class, I was approached by a colleague asking me if I could complete a market research job for them, and I drew from lots of concepts Prof. Dev taught us in order to organize and complete that project. I originally took this course for my business minor, but it turned into a professional lifesaver!
A must-take for any aspiring marketers. Professor Dev is as respected as you can get in the Marketing industry. Full of knowledge and resources.

Professor Dev knows marketing like the back of his hand. Intro Marketing, great class. No homework: only mid-term and final. Be on time and dont talk in class or youll get exposed. Take good notes about concepts/case studies and youre set. Absolute Chad
This class was extremely fun to take with Professor Dev! He's extremely knowledgeable and engaging which makes participating even more fun. Would recommend it to all!

This is the only review Ive ever made and Im a junior. Professor Dev was THAT good, I had to make a review. He was caring, charismatic, and reasonable. The class is pretty interesting and so enjoyably easy. If only I could find more classes like this!!!!!

Professor Dev is a great professor. This is the second time I have taken a class with him. I am always so inspired by his lectures. Not only are they informative, but they are very useful outside of the classroom as well.

Awesome Professor who is well respected within the industry. Class is very organized throughout the semester so you know what to expect. Class concepts are applied within case studies/presentations to ensure thorough learning & understanding. This class prepares you for the real working world and should be required for all students!

He's an amazing person! He definitely expects you to be prepared for every class but does his part in making every class extremely interesting. Always answers any questions and is very approachable. Take his classes!

Professor Dev is very clear & compelling. He explains concepts & relates them to real-world examples so you can really understand them. He's engaging & keeps class interesting through case studies about companies students know & love. There are 2 exams that make up your grade so attendance may not be taken, but you should definitely go to class.
Great class / great professor

Prof. Dev is fantastic. I studied Architecture, but was lucky enough to take one of his classes (Marketing for Hospitality). I recently reached out and said the following, Every day I get to see the impact good service and meaningful interactions make in someones day. I studied architecture but decided to pursue hospitality as a career.
Professor Dev, I wanted to let you know that your marketing class made a positive impact on the trajectory of my time at Cornell and my potential career in the future.
Wonderful professor who is very skilled at keeping students engaged in class. Informational and gripping lecture style. He is also a Hospitality Marketing legend!

Professor Dev does a fantastic job in grasping the attention of students and retaining it through interesting case studies and visual-heavy presentations. He also provides various acronyms to make it easier to remember specific information. He's the best professor I've had at the Hotel School so far!

Professor Dev's lectures are always real highlights of my day. The class cases are interesting and memorable, and he wants you to do well in his class. For a marketing class, the principles we learn are practical and applicable even in an internship. Any employee is a marketing employee. Taking his class will undoubtedly help you.

From the informative lectures, applicable deliverables, and distinguished guest lectures, his class stimulated me and challenged my creative thinking which inspired me to pursue a career in brand management. Throughout the semester Professor Dev was extremely approachable, encouraging us to stop by his office to discuss the unique cases.

Devs detailed and visual slides were memorable. What you take away from the class is transferable knowledge about marketing, not just memorization of terms. The case studies & ecornell videos were incredible; take notes. Attending class & engaging w/ the material is a must! In order to ACE the class, use the textbook to preview & clarify topics.

Professor Dev is awesome and his Brand Management class is one of my favorites at Cornell. As a non-HA student, his class was applicable to me in my work and life. Note: You are what you put into the class! The most successful students are those who participate in class and read the case studies ahead of the class ahead of discussions.

Professor Dev is one of the best Professors at Cornell. He is an expert in his field and it really shows in his lectures. He has amazing case studies built into each lecture that teach the material in an engaging and exciting way. His tests are extremely fair. You have to put in the work to learn the material. I learned so much. 10/10 recommend!

Prof Dev's marketing class was one of the funnest classes I've taken in my time at Cornell University. It is 50% Midterm and 50% Final, which ultimately led me to change my grading system in SP2020 to S/U (COVID-19 Exception). However, if you put your time to this class and go to lectures, you won't be bored and will learn a lot! Highly respected.

I had Professor Dev in Fall 2019. I really enjoyed his class and was inspired to pursue a concentration in marketing and an internship in marketing for this summer. The class even helped me in my interview process for my upcoming internship.

I graduated in May 2019 and I had Dev in 2018 Fall. I still look back and think about his class. I genuinely learned a lot in his class and it was never not entertaining. You watch case study videos almost every class - case studies that I remember to this day. For grades, it was not hard to study for AS LONG AS you are good at memorization.

Professor Dev's lectures were both interesting and engaging. I loved working on the case studies, as they were both challenging and relevant. I gained practical knowledge that I know I will use in the real world. I highly recommend this course to anyone interested in marketing and branding.

Prof. Dev simplified complex concepts & provided frameworks to approach & solve problems. He kept the course context very real world. The best part- for many case studies he brought ppl from the case to the classroom! I'm certain if not for him, I would not have become a marketer. I highly recommend him if you want to be a champion marketer!

Professor Dev shared important insights on marketing during lectures, filled with case studies (important for prelims and exams!) and analyses. I really enjoyed his guest lectures, which gave us an opportunity to see the different ways marketing is explored among different industries.

Prof. Dev is genuinely interested in the professional and personal development of the students. He has a great network and is always happy to make introductions with alumni. And yes, very prompt with his emails. Would go back to school any day for him.

The most memorable course I've taken at Cornell! I was so inspired that I based my entire intern presentation on the case study format- with MUCH success! Would HIGHLY recommend Professor Dev to any student interested in marketing themselves or any product/service out there. I cant imagine taking an introductory marketing course with anyone else!

Prof. Dev is an engaging and involved lecturer. He teaches by using video "case studies" to demonstrate marketing concepts. Attendance is optional, but you can only see the videos in-class. There's no homework or required reading, but your grade is 50% the midterm (100 MC questions) and 50% the final (100 MC questions). Overall, would recommend!

I realy enjoyed his class. He really sparked my interest for marketing. His lecturees are interactive and he features a variety of different cases using commericials to keep you engaged for the entire lecture. Everything in the class is relevant to what is going on in the marketing world. Definitely do not miss a class, every case matters!

Professor Dev is the reason I'm in my job today. I took his class my final semester, and it inspired me to post for a marketing job at a luxury hotel. It was great to see that I could apply my love for writing/marketing to a hospitality role. I'm currently in my third year with the hotel, and will continue to stay with this career long-term.
Very engaging and exciting lectures Memorable and relevant case studies

Professor Dev is a great professor whose passion for marketing is infectious. Lectures were enjoyable and interesting. Guest lecturers were also great and provided real-world examples of concepts. I would take Marketing again in a heartbeat.

By far the best professor I have had at Cornell. A rich knowledge of the industry is evident by his many authored case studies and consulting projects which he weaves into the class discussion. An incredibly useful class.

Professor Dev is one of my favorite Professors. His lecturers are very engaging and he made me interested in marketing, which before I had no interest in. He uses case studies to provide examples of the topic being discussed and to bring everything together. I highly recommend taking marketing with him. Make sure to go to class and take good notes!

Professor Dev was an insightful, dedicated teacher. All lessons were grounded in real-world examples. Taking his course enabled me to consider new career paths and strategies for achieving them. I wish I could take the class again.

Professor Dev is super engaging and supportive. His Brand Management course is discussion-based, and he has incredible industry experience, which really brings the concepts to life. He takes the time to get to know students and help us in job recruiting, which is very nice. Two tips to succeed: participate and get to class on time!

Professor Dev leads an incredible class. You will definitely learn a lot - make sure you are doing the readings and putting the time in. It is very fair and exams are straightforward. Top tier professor

I was inspired by Professor Dev's Brand Management class. The class is unique in going beyond just academic learning - Professor Dev dives in to case studies, in detail, from brands he has actually consulted for. He gives you a real understanding of what brand consultants do and equips you skills with skills to take forward. Highly recommend!

I enjoyed his marketing course a lot! He made me realize my passion for brand strategy by creating interactive lectures that captured everyone's attention on a regular basis. Highly recommend taking his course HADM 2410

Professor Dev inspired me to go into marketing. He's the best professor in the marketing field. His classes never try to trick or harm your grade, he genuinely cares about you learning. Marketing Principles is all about the basics of marketing and the information is easy to learn. I retained so much. I recommend taking all of his courses!

Professor Dev is an award-winning marketing genius who brings his real-world experience inside the classroom. In his lectures, Dev presents important marketing terminology and fascinating case studies. In 2009, the Hospitality Sales and Marketing Association International named him one of the top 25 most extraordinary minds in sales and marketing.

The lecture is well-organized thanks to the help from the TAs. He is authoritative and respects hierarchy. Do not go to him with a question unless you exercised every other option. Very open-ended exams without a simplified outline of material. Basically read the entire textbook,  go to every lecture, and remember everything.

Dev made the material interesting & clearly cared about what he was teaching. However, I feel like your understanding of the material is not reflected on your grades. Only two 50% exams. He also grades down -(85% is a B-)I would suggest taking this course in AEM because of fair grading and more of a chance to show your understanding of the marketin

Professor brings great enthusiasm and interesting content to the class. However, I agree that the grading is heavily skewed. The tests are also slightly difficult given that you are tested on very minute details which are hard to study for and your entire grade is based off of two exams.  AEM marketing gives more of a fair chance grade-wise.

Grade consists only of midterm and final, and grading is skewed extremely upward (to the point where 85 is a B-) EVEN THOUGH the mean on the midterm was only an 85.  The tests only focus on tiny details from case studies that dont test content knowledge, or broad textbook concepts barely gone over.  Take AEM marketing for business minor, not Dev.

Prof. Dev is a really nice guy and very clearly cares about everything he teaches. It is adorable to see him get excited about marketing, and his enthusiasm makes lectures fun. He encourages participation and is always supportive. He is a VERY good teacher; one of the best I've had. He's organized, clear, and always ready to answer questions.

The class is comprised of a midterm and a final which are unnecessarily difficult for the subject matter. Similar to the review below, it's all extremely small details from the lectures. The video case studies are important. He's an interesting speaker but is waaay too strict with talking/phones and calls people out, making him look really bad.

I feel robbed. All test questions came from lecture and slides. Some questions did not pertain to overall marketing concepts but, rather, how much you paid attention to details like reptilian brain-marketing analogies. Interesting lectures. Engaging guest speakers. Relevant, updated material. TA review sessions are helpful. Learned a decent amount.

The structure of 2410 has changed. Its not straight memorization; lectures are almost essential (attendance isnt  taken though) since  half of the questions on prelims come straight from class and are not available in the textbook . Dev is great professor; thoroughly enjoyed this class as part of the business minor...a lot of cool stuff in it.

Professor Dev's class is not mandatory, however if you are interested in marketing, it is very valuable to attend. He is always willing answer questions and likes to keep the class engaged. 3 prelims, 1 final, 20% each prelim, 40% for final, straight up memorization, due to this structure, only those who want to learn show up.

Dev is a very nice guy and a good professor. With that being said, it was a very odd and useless class. Attendance not taken, nothing at all from lecture on tests. The tests are fill in the blank questions about marketing vocab that he gives before each prelim, so all you do is memorize. Because of this, grading scale is A+ 100+, A 97-100, A- 92-97

DeVault is one of my favorite professors at ILR. Super knowledgeable, engaging and interesting lectures, very helpful during office hours, fair grader. If you do the readings you'll do well in the class and leave knowing so much about labor history. She also answers to emails quite well and writes good comments on essays so you can improve

She assigns 100-250 pages of reading per week with weekly quizzes in discussion. Slides are pictures with a title and she just speaks about it. Attendance not mandatory but she tracks engagement and office hour attendance, and slides not helpful. Harsh grader on essays and final. OH not rlly helpful she laughs at questions (me and others)
Professor Devault is very passionate about labor history and it shows. She assigns a TON of reading, but you should just skim.

DeVault  gives us pop quizzes every week on the reading which is usually over 200 pages. I had pneumonia for two weeks and she wouldn't give me her notes from lecture. If you miss class you cannot make it up because she slides she post just include images and no information. Final exam where we wrote two essays in a hour.

Professor Devault assigns a ton of reading and you don't need to do all of it (though she does have weekly quizzes that typically test one aspect of the reading, so at least skimming is a good idea to not lose points there). Somewhat tough essay grader.

Highly recommend taking this seminar if you have an interest in history and need to knock out the ILR advanced writing requirement. Genuinely a caring professor, and super great to chat with during OH. Reads your journal entries in full, and writes thoughtful comments in the entries.

A very caring and passionate professor. A lot of readings but the work is manageable. Clear grading based on a mix of attendance and participation, journal entries, and essays. She is very understanding so would recommend going to office hours and communicating if you have any questions with the material.

Shes super kind and caring, you can tell shes very passionate about her work. Homework is mostly reading assignments up to 150+ pages a week and general quizzes during discussion. 2 papers and a take-home final that makes the majority of your grade.
DeVault clearly cares about the subject and the class. Go to office hours for help on the essays and you will do well.

Professor DeVault is clearly passionate about her subject matter. However, her class had excess work as well as a final exam that other labor history classes did not have. She graded harshly and the clear expectations were not laid out prior to paper assignments.

Grade based on: Critical book report, Primary source project, Research paper proposal, Final exam, and participation. Some assignment due dates vary by topic, allowing you to pick what weeks you want to work for the class. Thursday classes are all discussion so make sure to read what is assigned for the week (200-ish pages).
Weekly "quiz" on readings in discussion. Read lots of short books over the semester
Professor Devault is very kind! Although there is a large amount of reading every week, it helps acclimate you with the college course load
Lot of reading as it is a history class. Paper heavy. But she is a great professor and she is a very nice person very understanding great professor to get you into college

Professor Devault is a great professor. Labor History can be a dry topic but she is very good at trying to make it as easy as possible. 3 papers one of which is the final paper, and weekly quizzes in discussion which are not that bad. Take her if you can

Interesting professor who presents interesting material, but lectures had the tendency to be very dry. I appreciated that she made an effort to learn students' names and was accessible for questions. There were about 2 extra credit opportunities. A lot of reading, but skimming is ok. Weekly reading quizzes during discussion section, not so bad.

DeVault is one of the nicest people I have ever met. She genuinely cares about her students. I had a class during her office hours, so she regularly scheduled other times to meet. I struggled a lot with the first essay assignment, but DeVault helped me and taught me what I did wrong. Her lectures can be dry, but the information is interesting.

Awesome professor, super passionate and nice.  Lots of weekly reading with reading quizzes in discussion, but you can definitely "skim" main concepts and do extremely well. Two papers, go to TA office hours and you will do well on them. Extremely fair final. Some find the subject boring overall but DeVault makes it as painless as possible.
Excellent professor! Clear and learned a lot, definitely not an easy grader but she is very helpful and sweet and a fair grader. Love her!
Nice and helpful.

Not a bad course..very dry though. make sure you suck up in section to your TA and dont worry about the weekly quizzes too much. most imporant thing about this class would be to meet with both the TA and DeVault before both of the papers to talk about your thesis and make sure youre on the right track... they will tell you what to write basically

Unfree Labor: Slaves, Servants, Wives.  Great Teacher, learned alot, ALOT of reading, one book per week, sometimes half a book, seminar style, classes tend to be very large.  Attendance is not required but necessary for class participation points.  She really knows her stuff and goes a long way to ensure your understanding.

Comparative History of Women at Work.  Best seminar class I've ever been in, attendance is not mandatory, but necessary to get class participation points.  Reading is tough, one book per week+short paper, but well worth the effort, learned alot, seminar style allowed for greater understanding of others opinions on women's issues

Intro to Labor History, lots of reading, but if you keep  up your set, class participation counts for alot, you'll definitely learn something.  I liked her so much, I've taken 2 more of her classes. (IC636 and CB388)

DeVault is very passionate about labor history and is a good lecturer; she gave us weekly ‘reading quizzes’ which were annoying but I guess it made us read the many books we were assigned...  A pretty interesting class if you’re into the subject. 2 papers, final exam was 2 essay questions; DeVault is a tough grader but a good teacher overall.

Wonderful teacher.  She is very interested in the subject and conveys it.  She is also very helpful, friendly, and pleasant to talk to if you see her in office hours.  Probably my favorite teacher this semester.

Excellent professor. I have heard that other CB100 profs are more dynamic lecturers, but I never had a problem staying engaged or awake in her class. She's definitely a professional, and I respect her tremendously. She has very high standards for your work, but that definitely motivates you to do well.
Boring and dry, but very clear and organized.  Go to lecture and get the gist of the readings, and you'll be fine.  Was also very understanding and accommodating when I had a conflict.

I have taken three classes with her,and I would take more if they were offered! Show up to class and you're set. Being interested in history helps a lot, but overall she is extremely nice and cares about how you do.

Good lectures, make the material as interesting as it can be. Ton of reading, nobody expects you to do it all though. For papers, make sure you hav a good thesis and you will do fine. She is very interested in women's issues, clearly. Overall, great prof.

An excellent professor and lecturer.  She made a very dry topic into something interesting. She assigns a lot of reading, however she doesn't intend for you to do it all, but rather gather general concepts.  Overall it was a pretty easy course if you went to lectures.
Incredibly boring.  Her many random examples are irrelevant and a waste of time.  She also refuses to change a grade no matter how unfair it may be.

One of the best professors you will have.  Lectures were clear, easy to follow and interesting.  Take good notes in lecture and you're guarenteed good grades.  Papers are a decent amount of work but very fairly graded.  The best prof. for the class by far.

Great professor- very clear and helpful. There is a lot of reading which is useful when it comes to doing papers. Papers can be tough...it helps to run your ideas by her first. Very nice and approachable and her lectures are very clear. No complaints here!
very clear and informative lectures, requires work (esp for the reading) but you'll learn a lot about US labor history

My favorite prof so far. I wasn't expecting labor history to be fun, but it's the only class I'm never inclined to skip. She's a really nice lady, very knowledgable, makes the class interesting w/o compromising depth or clarity of material. Papers aren't bad; reading can be a bit much, but doable.
Ileen is a goddess
Excellent professor; Papers require work, but if you try you can do well; Very clear lectures

This is a very interesting course on immigration. Devault does a great job at putting the history of immigration into context with work related stuff.  She is a very nice person who is very honest and fair.
very nice and helpful if you ask.  papers aren't that bad.  very good lectures and decent amount of reading for a cb class.
Tons of respect for this professor. DeVault is organized, clear, and strives to be as accessible to her students as time allows. No complaints!
very knowledgeable, great lectures. Papers requre some work though.
No Comments

Her lecture covers a wide range of topics regarding diversity. You're graded in participation (attendance is mandatory), 3 open note take-home quizzes, and 2 projects. If you're even slightly interested in Human Resources, she's an amazing professor.

Proudfoot is very clear about her expectations. If you do the work you will probably get an A. My one recommendation would be to read the textbook carefully. The exams get progressively more difficult. Overall, it was an interesting class and gave me a new perspective on the functions of HR.

Interesting lectures, but the textbook is very dense. She pulls 50/50 from both for the 3 exams. There are 4 assignments, but only 3 are required. These are very subjective to which TA grades yours. Attendance and participation in section is mandatory

As close to an easy A as you can get at Cornell, but no A+ are given, even if you get over 100% overall, which is not that hard to do. Super interesting subject matter. Tests and essays are cake if you put in even the slightest effort.
Enjoyed guest speakers in class too

Gives the trickiest multiple choice tests! Make sure you read the textbook thoroughly because she asks more than just the bolded words in the textbook. Attending lecture will also help significantly boost your grade up, especially if you participate!
Best history professor at nyush, he basically knows everything
Best history class I've ever had

Well, he told us he used to be harsh but now he's old and all he wants is a group of students listening to him talking about history and his life. He's teaching style is like ask-me-anything-in-class-because-I-literally-know-anything-about-history. Great professor, strongly recommended.

I would definitely recommend his class, but it's a lot of reading. His lectures are helpful and interesting, especially when he includes relevant personal experiences.  However, he doesn't discuss most of the material covered in the readings, so you can't rely on only his lectures.

I really enjoy his lectures, although he goes off topic sometimes. He is truly intelligent and knows a lot in his field. A lot of reading, but as long as you listen to his lectures you're fine. Reading quizes are not hard.

Thought his lectures were very interesting! He's a great teacher and I enjoyed his class very much. The in class quizzes and tests weren't that hard. You don't really have to do the reading if you pay attention in class.

Lectures are long and ambiguous. Prof. Chen goes on random tangents for a good portion of the class before he even mentions something that relates to the reading. You learn more from the reading than from his lecture. Lecture are intended to guide you but his lectures lag far behind the reading and rarely say anything of substance about the history

Prof. Chen is extremely knowledgeable. I only fully read the two books he wrote, and I suffered a bit on the final take-home essay. Overall, he assigned relevant reading and was an engaging lecturers. Even if he repeats himself - it's interesting and helps you remember.

you probably don't have to go to class, because he assigns an astronomical amount of reading. if you do the readings (especially the 2 he wrote- he repeats himself SOOO MUCH in them) you can pass the class. reading quizzes are REALLY general and broad- you dont have to memorize any dates. gives 5 extra credit opportunities. good class.

Professor Chen is the man. Intense lecturer, lots and lots of reading, and not particularly easy. But he's a great guy, interesting to listen to, and very, very bright. I knew nothing about China and didn't even care that much and he made it a rewarding experience. I had to work my butt off to do well, but it was worth it. Great professor.

I think this is a guy who will become a "must take" prof at Cornell.  However, only take him once.  He repeats himself every semester.  Also, express (even if feigned) interest in China.  If you know anything about China, or just ask him questions about China, he will give you a way better grade.

Waaaaaay too China centered for a class on East Asia (which includes Japan)... well, in all fairness the first half of the century according to Chen can be summed up as "China Good, Japan Bad". Lectures are intense (to say the least) and he does assign way too much reading. Not an easy class but quite enjoyable.

Chen is very knowledgeable about the subject, a true expert.  He assigns far too much reading, but other than that the requirements are not too bad.  His presentation of the material can be confusing at times as his lectures get a bit disorganized.
Ok so everyone says its an easy class, but it does require a lot of work, so be really prepared for that. Treat it like another class not an easy one.
Mike Chen is a wonderful professor. He works really hard to get to know each student and is a very helpful resource. He really provides that boost of serotonin that I need to get through the day.
Absolutely amazing professor. Things learned in the lectures are actually quite helpful.
Amazing person, as well a great professor.

Dr. Chen is simply amazing! I took him at Nazareth and he is SO caring and kind. I love it when he asks how you're doing before a class, and before exams, he reminds you that you shouldn't stress. He answers emails well and I could listen to him teach all day. He for sure knows his stuff and how to explain it.
Mike is amazing and made my summer fun. He always checks up with his students before class and encourages all of us to pursue our goals and finish our school work. I am blessed to have had him!

I took this class in order to add two easy credits to my semester and it did exactly that. As long as you show up to class on a regular basis and complete the 5 minutes of homework you have every week, you will get an A. In addition to this, the material is extremely useful and applicable however most lectures end up being very repetitive.
Such a nice guy

Mike is a great guy. He genuinely cares about all of his students and helps them organize their schedules. Each week in class he makes the point of asking each student how his/her week is going in regards to exams/papers/stress levels. Class isn't difficult and as long as you do what is expected of you, you will be fine. Wish I could take again!

Tells fun and relevant stories in class. She is a good lecturer and teaches interestingcool lab topics, but oh my god don't get on her bad side. She will dislike students for really petty things sometimes, which sucks. Just try to come to all classeslabs and do things the way she wants them and she will be really nice and helpful

Dr. Solomon genuinely wants you to do well.  She gives you a variety of ways to learn.  At times, her lectures are scattered. Study the book, not her lectures notes.  Use Quizlet as a reference for sample questions.  Take the time to go to her office hours and get to know her or talk to her outside of class. Again, she wants you to do well!

Riley is the best professor I have ever had. I loved his teaching style and he always went through the homework and quizzes before we had to take them. He explains things in a way that is so easy to understand and will always answer questions. He is quite funny as well and knows how to make the class atmosphere light. I'd take any class of his.

The best professor in Dyson. Caring, funny, kind, intelligent. He makes sure students are doing in the class and no one gets below a C+, he literally makes it impossible. Almost everyone I know gets an A, but EVERYONE leaves understanding accounting.

*Winter Session* Prof Riley was very understanding of students' very busy schedules over break. Reachable and willing to meet outside of office hours. Grading for this class is objective and clear and he was willing to review exams with students. I'm very grateful for my experience in his class. Wonderful professor and easily one of my favorites.

He covers the material well, and gives lots of resources in advance for you to use (lecture slides, practice problems, practice prelims). If you attend the lectures, he gives you all the information that you need to know. The prelims and final are really straightforward too.
Lots of homework, the test can be hard, 1 bad test can lower the grade, no curve. I heard it used to be better, especially with his online class.

Riley is great. He makes accounting much easier to understand. He understands students and is willing to work with them. The class was graded on three, noncumulative prelims, weekly HW, and quizzes which they review before you have to turn them in and participation. 100% recommend

Great professor and great intro to accounting. Makes everything so easy to understand. Super willing to meet outside of class to make sure you get the content. Must purchase digital book >100. No class after prelims and super down to earth. Actually gets how hard being a student is and is sympathetic.
Best professor ever! Great teacher. Makes financial accounting sexy. Ask him about Chipotle...

Professor Riley is one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. Very clear and concise lectures, weekly homework assignments, and three comprehensive exams (two prelims and one non-cumulative final). Would definitely recommend this professor to those who seek to gain an introductory background in financial accounting.

Professor Riley offers a lot of resources/OH to help struggling students. I ended up going to his OH for help a lot and he was really able to hone in on what I was struggling with and explain things over & over until I understood them. It's a tough class but if you put in the work, read the textbook, and ask questions in OH, you will be successful!

Professor Riley is clear, concise, and approachable. He makes accounting seem like a piece of cake, and his lectures are super easy to follow. He also posts a lot of resources ahead of time, which I really appreciate. I really hope he continues to teach at Cornell!

Professor Riley is one of the best I've ever had. He made accounting really clear and went out of his way to help anyone struggling with concepts. His homework, quizzes, and tests were extremely straightforward and not too intensive, and his lectures were very easy to follow. He was funny, engaging, and has real-world knowledge. Great professor.

NS 4600 is awful. Pelletier spends most of the lectures speaking about random things; the homework is unclear; literally no one has any idea what is going on at any point; no feedback is provided; he makes up arbitrary rules , etc. For a class designed around planning, the lack of a plan in this class is truly terrifying.
He was decent

Don't not take this course! It is very ambiguous and the tests demonstrate nothing from the lectures. he is a stickler on grades and makes his own grading scale that is different from the overall NS department scale. AVOID this course if you can
awesome, fun, interesting course.

Prof Rooks was one of the worst professors I've had. She made it pretty clear that she did not care about the class and rarely showed up. If she did come, she was hardly ever prepared. Some of the grading was really frustrating and we had pop quizzes that asked really specific questions that were just to see if we read, not if we understood it.
Excellent class, encourages students to explore some difficult works. Read and participate actively.
Not only is Professor Ajunwa a great lecturer, she also cares about her students and is easy to connect with beyond class.

Went from live to online. Taken for ILR soph writing requirement. Prof is nice and pretty knowledgable about her topics. She struggles to communicate how to do assignments and when they are due but doesn't grade harshly. You may have to ask her multiple times. Not too much work and it isn't too difficult or tedious. I think participation matters.

Prof. Ajunwa has been my favorite professor at ILR to date. Shes a knowledge powerhouse and was terrific at teaching labor law in a way that would benefit non-lawyers. During the pandemic she was also very flexible with students, which is a true gem regardless. Dont miss a class with her if you can help it!

Professor Ajunwa is very smart and a great teacher. She knows a lot about law and technology, and many of the class readings were her own papers. She grades pretty lightly, and class discussions can be pretty interesting. Her one flaw is that she sometimes struggles to communicate assignment expectations and deadlines.
Standout professor at Cornell. Challenges students in a thought-provoking and respectful way, and does not take sides -- instead kindly pushes all ideas. Unique teaching message. Strongly recommend.

This was an excellent class. I truly enjoyed the class and found the material to be current. The prof. is extremely knowledgable in the subject matter. The couses leades to and to ann understanding ofthe changing nature of work as influenced both by technological advancements and changing attitudes about the role of work and work/life balance.

She is nice and willing to help students during and after the class. In the class, she will prompt you to think and discuss the real-life decision-making scenarios in a variety of ways. The reading materials, though heavy loading every week, also help a lot before in-class discussions. I am glad to have those articles and books finished.

She does a great job in leading really thought-provoking discussions and challenging our assumptions. I especially liked her efforts to help us apply business and legal concepts to real-world cases and her flexibility in adapting to the class's needs. She's a fair grader and gives clear feedback. Anyone who takes a class with her will learn a lot.

I took Fish Physiology course and I felt the course really useful and fulfilling. Besides lectures and guest lectures, we have group project "build a fish" and one presentation to enhance our learning in an interesting way. Dr. Won's powerpoint is well-organized, but you should take notes. The average grade in the course is pretty high (A-).

Dexter was a class act. Despite his incompetencies and lack of class structure. His accusations of students' behavior were egregious. He constantly harassed me and almost ruined my entire semester. He was inaccessible outside of class and used lectures as a way to verbalize his personal frustrations. Moreover, he is biased toward women and Gen Z.

Fall 2020. Algo is a brutal class and Kozen can't really change that. His lectures were alright but I didn't feel the need to go. When I reached out to him for bc I was struggling on the 2nd hw he was very understanding and basically just told me to stay the course, but it was with his reassurance that I was able to push through. Learned a lot!

Dexter was an excellent professor for Algo. His lectures were clear and organized. I took it during an all-online COVID semester, but he still used written notes that were neat and posted after each lecture. The exams were hard but fair. The homeworks are definitely pretty hard, but if you start early and use copious amounts of OH, you'll be good!
Clear lecturer who cares about students' understanding of the material. Will answer many Piazza posts personally, and made reasonable adjustments to the course due to its virtual format.

Extremely concise lectures; very well delivered. Took 2112 as a freshmen- it was not an easy ride, but I definitely learned a lot thanks to Kozen. Very rewarding class. The assignments require a lot of energy and time, but Kozen is always there to help his students.

"It's not about the points" - Kozen Definitely one of the better professors. His lectures are clear, concise, and easy to follow, and the projects he assigned were meaningful, interesting, and some of the most fun I've ever had at school. At times, the grading felt a bit arbitrary, but the massive curve at the end rendered it all irrelevant.

Amazing professor who actually cares about you!! Good lecturer. 2112 was ridiculously hard and definitely caused me way too much stress and hair loss. But I would take it again for sure because you learn so much. Exams are not bad at all, just memorize lecture and recitation notes. Labs are really useless, people stopped showing up.

CS2112 was the hardest class I've ever taken. The material is hard, but the real killer is the sheer volume of work. You will devote a huge amount of time and energy to this class, and then still feel like that is not enough. This class probably broke me. I learned a lot, but it was not worth the stress and anguish. DO NOT TAKE as a freshman!!!!
Very good lecturer, although the class was extremely difficult. Class was worthwhile.
Fun lecturer but also good for snooze if necessary

Kozen is unbelievable. As the other testimonials say, he personally answers questions on Piazza, and has the most amazingly clear lecture style, unlike a lot of other professors. I was amazed at how he managed to cover an entire 400 page textbook that he wrote, cover-to-cover, without making it seem like the 41 lectures worth of material was crazy.
hasn't changed lectures in 30 years
I've had 2 classes with him. My favorite professor at Cornell.
Amazing professor. Had him for algorithms. Very nice guy and very helpful. Prelims and homeworks are fair, and the homework load is very manageable. Was easier in 2013 than before.

I love Kozen. I had him for algorithms. Normally this course is done by Kleinberg. His lectures were on videonote, but in my opinion Kozen's were twice as good. I think Kozen is clear, interesting, and one of the most helpful professors I ever had. You never feel lost by him, or confused. My favorite CS professor by a long shot. Fair tests and HW.

Teaches well, and makes lecture interesting. Personally answers a lot of questions on Piazza. The assignments are not trivial, but you have more than enough time and resources (the course staff) to finish them. Tests are very fair, and grading is pretty generous. I regret buying the textbook though -- I never used it.

Dexter is a great professor.  His lectures are clear and he puts all of his powerpoints online.  Most importantly though, he assigns good projects.  It is clear that he put some thought into making things interesting.  NOTE: DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK

Kozen was awesome. Assignments were pretty long but he gave so much help. He was constantly answering questions (in detail) both in person and on Piazza, the online Q+A site for the course. The prelims were unbelievably fair, especially compared to previous ones on the website. He made the course relatively painless, and was also interesting.
Good guy. Extremely intelligent and knows what he's talking about. Helps you out when necessary. Assignments are incredibly tough and long but definitely enjoyable and educational.
Excellent teacher and a great guy. He makes the class interesting and he loves to go above and beyond teaching just what will be on the test.
Good guy. Made exams, assignments, and classes interesting. Would definitely reccomend.

Kozen is a good guy. He really cares about helping his students, from what I can tell. I've been to his office hours a few times and he's really friendly, and he knows how to teach. The class is really easy too, as it's not graded on a curve. I got a good grade and I learned a lot. I highly recommend cs 211 with Kozen.
pretty easy class, dont like the written tests

Kozen, unlike many professors, knows how to teach.  Presentation is clear and explains concepts very well.  Prelims are quite hard but most of your grade comes from the assignments, which are straightforward.  Friendly and understanding, likes to give extensions.

This class is a lot of work, but Kozen is a pretty good teacher.  Most of your grade comes from the projects rather than tests (I failed a prelim and did pretty well in the end).  The projects are interesting which makes them easier to do, but you still must figure out a lot on your own.
pretty easy class grade-wise. i got a 57 on a test (med. 67) and still got an A. It is a good amount of work tho. also, kozen dims the lights in lecture so its real easy to fall asleep.

The band name is "The Burning Sensations" and that's just the kind of guy Dexter is. Really smart, really fun, and the kind of person you'd like to have tea with afterwards. Good luck with the subject matter, though. Hard as hell.
