Really smart. Whenever he gives me writing advice it's on point and helps me develop. Take this prof.

Professor Galloway is an absolute delight, he is genuinely enthusiastic about everything he teaches. Reading is heavy, but the content is worthwhile. His classes are English classes though so you should expect that.

Dr. Galloway was truly inspirational. His enthusiasm about the course material was evident and infectious. He was incredibly understanding and cared about every student in the class. Attendance is not mandatory in the sense that he checks who comes to class and who doesn't (there was also a Zoom option), but you would be incredibly foolish to skip.

I took his Chaucer course. He is a truly brilliant teacher: he taught us how to interpret moments in literature as well as the meanings of whole texts . He radically changed how I analyze and interpret literature. I'll always remember his class, and I wish I could take him again. He's very stimulating in office hours too.
Very good man

Andy is a great professor; he's very engaging and certainly knows his stuff. At first glance, the course seems easy because you only have lectures and a light discussion each week, but Andy is a really tough grader. You'll have to analyze and write like a pro to get a good grade on your papers. Overall, worth it, but difficult.

I've taken a few courses with Professor Galloway during my time at Cornell, and in my view he is the best professor here. He knows more than anyone (literally) about his subject and he is the nicest, most enthusiastic, most helpful professor I've ever had. You cannot help but engage with his courses, no matter what your prior interest level.

Professor Galloway is an excited, rambunctious, and detailed lecturer whose lose for his subject comes out in his teaching.  You'll come to love not only the literature he teaches but also its historical context - he really loves history, I mean, really loves history.  This is not bad, trust me.  Also, check out his great voices!!!

loves the material and you will too. super helpful at office hours - you must go before handing in essays! this will make your essay grade better and you will also have a better understanding of the material. one of the smartest people i have encountered at cornell.
Fantastic teacher. He really cares about his students and their work, and he puts great effort and knowledge into every lecture. I recommend any class he teaches.
Great prof - would take any class he offers - very nice and helpful.
i love galloway! he is a great prof!

Knows a lot about what he teaches and related material.  Tends to go off on tangents a bit because of this, but it seems to generally be interesting stuff.  Lenient grader; seems to be more interested in whether or not you're putting in the effort.

Definitely the best course and the best professor I had last semester.  I never wanted to miss a class.  It was a lot of reading and writing every week; however, I felt it was worth it, for he gave such an animated lecture, revealing his true love of it.

Fantastic teacher and scholar. Very approachable and intensely excited about his subject matter. I took these courses expecting to hate them for the potentially dry subjects. Pleasantly surprised and still fondly recall these courses a decade later.
great class - very easy grading; a lot of reading and writing but not bad at all if you are interested in the literature; he is really into his work, its nice to see
Don't playa hate.  Galloway is da bomb!!!!!
Though he is very nice, there is something about the class that induces sleep.

Obviously very into his work, but not a very good teacher. Tends to talk to himself for the entire class period, without realizing that 3/4 of the class is asleep. Very random, often incoherent, and likes to ramble. He picks good pieces, though...
Long incoherent lectures.  Really excited about English but doesn't necessarily get his point across.  Good class if you do it for the literature.
PHIL 181: Philosophy and the Science of Human Nature  I am watching these videos online and reading the material.  She makes it fun and easy to understand.
Gendler might be enthusiastic, but she is very squeaky and she expects you to write exactly what she said in lecture for the exams. So much for your own opinions...and exams aren't clear at all.
Very enthusiastic about teaching; really care if her students understand the material.

Pretty good professor. She says things like "come visit me in office hours, I'd love to meet all of you", but then she doesn't ever seem particularly friendly or interested. Overall though it's a fun class, the textbook is good, and prof Kushnir is solid.

Very understanding of the stress that comes with a global pandemic, and TA's are very lenient. I took this as a science requirement and loved it (I usually hate science). There are weekly quizzes but they are easy if you watch all lectures and skim the textbook. There is a large final project but it is broken up so it's not overwhelming.

Prelims are factual and very doable, lecture slides provide most of the information you need, and the baby videos are absolutely adorable!! Prof. Kushnir cracks a joke from time to time, so make sure to laugh.
This class is really fun with tons of videos of babies. The grading policy is really nice- lowest of 4 test grades is dropped. Easy and interesting class.
Great and caring professor with lots of extra credit opportunities. If you are a good test-taker, you will succeed in this class, as it is all memorization.

She is very nice and funny. Clear lectures and lots of extra credits. Tests are okay - not too hard but include couple short answer questions. Tests materials are mostly from lecture. Would definitely take her class again if possible

Professor Kushnir's lectures are clear and she does a good job keeping the material interesting by including debates and podcasts. There is plenty of room for extra credit, which is very helpful, because although the tests aren't hard, you really need to know the material well to do well.

The class itself is doable. Just read the textbook alongside attending class and the extra credit can boost your grade. The professor seems really nice in class, but outside of class, she can be very dismissive. I decided it wasn't worth going to office hours after she kept asking why I didn't check w/a friend. Wouldn't recommend unless necessary.

She's really nice and encourages questions. There are four tests, and the lowest grade gets dropped. Tests are all multiple-choice, and take more from the lectures than the textbook. A good amount of reading is assigned, but it's really fine to just look at the vocabulary and charts. Each extra credit usually asks for a paragraph or two.

Professor Kushnir is a great person! She is very friendly and approachable. BUT the way she taught this class made it so difficult for me to actually enjoy the subject. If you are an HD major (Human Development), you're required to take a discussion class which focuses mostly on research methods.
Really nice person, loved this class

By far my favorite class so far at Cornell, and I'm not even an HD major. The material was super easy to understand to begin with, but Kushnir made me enjoy it that much more. Some tricky questions on tests, but the extra credit can pull you up a whole letter grade if you do it. Would definitely recommend as a fun elective!

Sweet professor. Always looking for the class to answer questions & talk, but no one does. Class is based on 3 prelims, lowest grade dropped. and 6 points of extra credit are provided that go right on your raw average. Several helpful TAs. Really interesting & easy class if you like psych or babies! Highly recommend. She loves talking to students

Professor Kushnir is the best.  She is super enthusiastic and cares about her students more than any other professor I've had at Cornell.  Go talk to her during her office hours and she will talk with you about anything, even if it has nothing to do with the course.  She might also be the smartest professor in HD.

Dr. Kushnir is fantastic! Very smart, knowledgeable, fun, and passionate about her field. She likes to challenge, and be challenged by students, but does so in a way that is inspirational and constructive. She really believes in her students and wants them to succeed.

Professor Kushnir is the best science professor I've ever had.  She is wicked smart, funny, and a bit of a goof.  Behind it all is one of the most amazing minds I've ever seen at Cornell.  She is like a science robot with the soul of an angel.
Interesting class, easy enough

Awful! Took her class as an intro level Human Development to fill a social science requirement and saw that all we do in class is watch youtube videos. Tests were written by TAs. Not a good prof at all.

Took this after Goldstein's psych 2090 - what a mistake! Kushnir teaches outdated studies and refuses to debate "controversial" topics (isn't that the point of critical thinking?). Grading is easy: agree with her simplistic take on HD. Got an A- by gritting my teeth and writing papers supporting material I knew was questionable or proven false.

Professor Kushnir is one of the best teachers I ever had at Cornell.  I graduated last year, and have spent a lot of time thinking about who really made a difference to me -- and Kushnir is one of the few.  She's a truly great prof!

I've taken HD2300 and HD 4490 with Prof Kushnir.  I like the way she teaches.  In 2300 she showed up to almost all of the discussion sections, but let the TA's do their thing, and for 4490 she does a good job of letting people talk about what they're interested in while staying roughly on topic.

Professor Kushnir is young, enthusiastic, and knowledgeable. She's very approachable if you ever need help. I learned so much about critical thinking and taking different approaches to examining the social sciences in her course. I highly recommend taking any of her classes!

Great lectures! Young and relates well with her students. Her courses are interesting, and difficult, but necessary if you came to Cornell to actually learn something. These other comments MUST have been posted by students who received a bad grade due to poor work. Prof Kushnir is fair, and passionate about what she teaches.
Tamar is frank and friendly. Her ideas are inspiring. Recommanded if you have lots of ideas and what to organize or theorize them.
I took "Children's Learning in Social Context" (HD 4990) with this professor. She is so cocky and is full of herself. I think she would keep talking if there was no one in the room.

Good lecturer. Class content is super interesting, only time I've ever been disappointed when a class gets cancelled. Exam and final paper are easy. Discussions were on some level a waste of time, but I will admit it was really cool how the results figured into lectures. Rare class that is both an easy A and academically valuable.
Awesome awesome awesome! Best professor at Cornell!
Really funny, clear and good at teaching. Take his class!

He's very precise and willingly takes questions in class. Starts off lecture with something funny and interesting. Practice as many HW problems as you can, but focus on items like math theory in recitation (they ARE tested). Otherwise, class was a breeze.
Really clear and helpful, and actually makes class fun enough to want to go. Best professor I've had so far at Cornell.
Awesome. Enough said.
Best professor I have had at cornell. Fantastic lecturer, and extremely willing to help. Tests and grading are very fair.
Good Prof - good teacher

The best teacher I have ever had at Cornell. Not only is he a great teacher but he's also funny. He is very considerate of students and understands their workloads and even has cut back on homework. Go to lecture and you are golden.  He explains the material perfectly. Definitely take class with him!
Awesome guy, and really young so you gotta know he's a genius

Nice guy, seems to care a lot about his students success. His lectures are about 90% arithmetic though. He will set up an example and then spend the rest of class working through it. All the diff eq stuff is contained in the setup, so my mind tended to wander during the 40 min he would spend solving all the integrals and whatnot.

He is a really engaging lecturer who uses great examples to explain the material. He explains things really clearly, and thoroughly. You'll understand all the material decently if you pay attention half the time, but if you pay attention all the time, you will get an A.

Professor Recktenwald is the most entertaining lecturer I have had.  He is great at explaining the material, and uses crazy examples to make the material fun.  Attend his lectures and you don't even really need to read the book to do well.

Recktenwald is the man.  I loved his class--he's good at explaining things to the class, and he is very friendly and fun to have as a teacher.  Calculus was more fun with Recktenwald.  Very approachable, the class kind of felt like a highschool class.  loved it--I'd recommend him to anyone.

Recktenwald is very clear and does his best to teach everyone. He will help you as much as he can in office hours and is very receptive to questions in lecture. Tests are very hard (first ones mean was 58) and depend more on your mathematical intuition than your knowledge of the material, but he doesn't write them so it isn't his fault.
Best Math Professor I've ever had!
I loved this class.  Explained things very well with good examples.  Engaging lecture.  Compared to other lecturers for 294, he was the best by far.
He provided many good examples on the board.
Awesome professor.  He's really interested in what he's doing and is extremely patient when it comes to helping students of all levels learn and excel.
Very good professor.  Lecturee are very well organized.  Also a very nice guy, gave me much encouragement and good advice.

Professor Reck is AWESOME! He is in touch with the students (that is, he knows what question you're asking if you are confused). He really clarifies concepts and makes himself available for students! Take his course if you can!!

class is generally just prof waite talking for an hour straight with some interjections for questions. the class is ridiculously easy for an fws, and homework is entirely self directed based on what you want to write. as long as you write something, you will get a good grade and good feedback.

Extremely boring lectures, but did 0 work the entire semester, did not attend class, and 100% of the grade is the final project, worked with a friend and got an A+, and spent just a couple hours on it. His lectures can be torturous, especially the student discussion parts, but he's kind and understanding.

Professor Waite is an amazing teacher! He is so caring and you can tell that he is really passionate about the subject. Did not give homework or exams, and participation was encouraged but not required. Only grade was a final creative project that was an open prompt, so you could do whatever you wanted. Would definitely recommend his classes!

(Marx, Freud, and Nietzsche) The class itself has no structure, 0 homework/tests. Waite doesn't really believe in grades but there's a final project (with literally no criteria) in which as long as you put in some effort you'll get an A. The material itself can get pretty interesting. Waite is chill, he just talks all class, doesn't use a mic tho

This class can be whatever you make of it. If you're really into it and have the time to dedicate to do all the readings and participating in the class, that's great! If not, I think you'll still get something out of it and get to watch some interesting films. I went to half the lectures and only read one assigned book, but he liked my final paper.

I'm a freshman and have read some philosophies in my high school. But there's something I wanted to figure out when I got into college at first. Geoff's class would let you change. If you want to understand what's going on in this hell world, just follow his guide to read some books, think about what to ask, and prepare to become a true communist.

Seems like a nice guy but the class is a total disaster. Each class is a completely unstructured discussion which is totally dominated by two or three students in the 100 person class. Entire grade relies on one paper with completely ambiguous grading criteria. Very little work but you will likely not get very much out of the class.

He is very chill and doesn't put any pressure on the students. He cares about the ideas that you write more than he cares about the actual style of writing, which is amazing if you struggle with writing.

Geoff Waite is one of the kindest and coolest professors I have had. He will treat an undergrad with no experience reading marx with the same level of respect for his/her ideas as he would a philosophy grad student. Always wiling to answer questions after class and very understanding about deadlines if stuff comes up. 10/10

Prof. Waite is the best professor I've had at Cornell. His lectures are amazing, he is knowledgable about pretty much everything. So interesting to talk to... Am taking another one of his classes in the Fall.

brilliant, soft-spoken, unbelievably chill. I took a grad-level Marxisms seminar with him and there were these two guys who had literally never read any Marx and were obviously clueless - Geoff was always super nice and encouraging with them. yeah he uses a lot of jargon but he's approachable, patient and always willing to explain
Everything about this course was weird.
brilliant professor. Work is very difficult

Really interesting dude with an obvious passion for his subject and comprehensive knowledge of the material. Tended to ramble a lot in lectures with a slightly awkward yet endearing voice that made students unlikely to participate in conversation. He's also an anarchist so you don't have to worry too much about grading pressure.

Took Prof. Waite for a Spinoza class.  The good parts: brilliant, open-minded, willing to engage all sorts of ideas.  On the other hand: yes he's a bit pretentious, and maybe insecure.  I disagreed with a lot of what he said but didn't want to speak up.  Still one of the best profs I've had at Cornell.  Also grading is easy - write on what you like

Class on Spinoza.  Fantastic professor, easily one of the few I'll really remember out of four years at Cornell.  I found him quite friendly and approachable; a little weird, yes, awkward, yes, but he's undoubtedly interested in students, and very interesting to listen to and learn from.  Thumbs up from a science major!

You want to learn what learning is? Take a class with Geoff. The man is brilliant.  Anything and everything I ever publish will give him some acknowledgment. Sometimes in life, you meet people who you know from the minute they speak you will never forget. Geoff is one of those people. He's the greatest man I've ever met second only to my Father.
Great class, there's really little to no work required, but the subject matter is always interesting. But the man does whisper.
Best class and best prof. at cornell.  You will come out of the course with so many amazing ideas.

Great class! Laid back style of teaching makes this class very easy to follow, yet extremely interesting on all levels. It's one of those classes where you're not really asked to do too much work, but you find yourselves doing the readings out of interest.
great to talk to (talks forever!) very approachable and ok maybe he's over 50 but i love love this man
Totally inspiring. Love the class.
Such a great guy.  Lots of reading but no tests, pick and choose what's interesting to you.  Seems nervous teaching in front of class but very intelligent and kind.
Best teacher ever
Great

he was really only coherent for the first 10 minutes of the first class. after that, it was all head-rubbing and nonsense-spouting. but he's nice and sometimes funny. i like that he quotes the clash in class. just sort of a wierd teacher.
Political Theory and cinema is one the most poorly run classes at cornell. unless your knowledge of political terminology is equivalent to his, it is usually useless to understand him.
I took his class "Political Theory and The Cinema."  One of the best classes I took at Cornell, hands down.

Great class with a professor who really knows his stuff - supposedly the only card carrying communist at Cornell? - that's the rumor.  Anyway very knowledgeable about subject matter, not pretensious at all.  Works w. students on indiv. level.

geoff is one of the least pretentious professor's here. he is clear, he is always willing to explain things, always willing to meet with professors outside of class. and why does "very easy" = "best", i thought we were supposed to be l
Pretentious and lousy at teaching

No office hour, had to schedule appointment. The appointment was unhappy: the meeting was supposed to be 3pm but he had a previous meeting that didn't finished. I waited for 1 HOUR and then was allowed to come in. Professor Fisher told the student next to me: I will finish this meeting within 10min. I didn't see him respect me as a student.
Nice professor but boring lecture. Difficult to reach out after class. OH is not very happy experience.
Sometimes his explanations for things are long or ambiguous. Emphasis on sometimes; other times, answers to questions or feedback are straightforward and helpful.
Lectures were deadly, your grade is basically made up entirely by the final project and the course was structured horribly.

This guy is awesome. He is one of the better lecturers I've had at Cornell. He's a no BS kind of professor and says it as it is. He expects you to do a lot of the learning on your own but his lectures are a great supplement. He's a funny guy and super enthusiastic about the content. Definitely would recommend. (1300 is a bit of work though).

Surprisingly well spoken teacher. I really enjoyed the class and it wasn't too tough. I usually give teachers low marks on this site, but I truly give danco a 5/5. He's so personable - it's almost as if he was a student here as opposed to a teacher. Highly recommend this class / teacher

Had a few years ago, and it felt like being trolled; have not commented b/c it seemed like just a bad personal fit. But looking back, realized something: he's clueless about differences of learning styles and situations in his students. With a huge amount of work, don't expect flexibility: an unconventional class, and miserable if you don't fit it.

DanCo was very enthusiastic about HCI.  He was interesting to listen to.  The class was a lot of work for 3 credits, and often times during the projects (it was a project based course) I got the impression that the TAs had no direction as to where the projects should be going.  If you did the work though as best as you could, you will do fine.

Dan is awesome. He's a nice guy and will always put in extra time to help you out if you are feeling like you need extra guidance. Also, he keeps classes lively and fun, mostly by throwing electronics against walls just for kicks. :)

Dan is a good prof, I learned a lot.  Beware tho, he will make you do lots of stupid things so that his friends can exploit you for their research.  Ex: make you send all group emails to an address he can monitor so that he can see what everyone is saying "for research" and he'll make you fill out stupid personality eval forms for all group members
WORST CLASS EVER.
Very good professor.  His explanations are clear and he teaches at a good pace.
He's a really great guy.  He really really wants to help
this guy's accent is  incomprehensible. he hardly knows what he's teaching, and it seems like he's teaching it to himself as he's going along.

Prof. Weatherspoon is a brilliant scientist and a kind professor. He is, however, not very good at explaining concepts. So confusing and keeps talking in circles. I stopped attending lectures after the first week because I learned more from reading the slides on my own. There is a lot of content covered in this course but exams are straightforward.

I would give a 5 to the professor as a person, but a 2 or 3 to the course. UNREAL amount of workload compared to the other 4 credits CS classes, they should give this course 6 credits. However, Prof Weatherspoon is a caring and respectful person, he will listen to your concerns and advice. Really feel no pressure to stay with as in person.
Delusional workload that would easily be 10 credits if properly reflective of the amount of time necessary to succeed in this class.
Never get well-prepared for lectures. Always want to end early
Awful and unclear lectures, can only learn from textbook.

Hakim is one of the most fair and honest professors in Cornell. He wants everyone to do well and goes beyond what the majority of the rest of the faculty  would do to achieve this goal. Some people complain that his lectures are unclear, but he releases them a day early so you can skim them before class to make up for it. +1 to him.
Most boring lecturer ever. Worst prof Ive ever had here.
Course is very poorly managed. Details/busy work interfere with the course content.

Hakim is a smart guy who is very approachable. However, the class itself disinterests me, and I dont think this has anything to do with him. As a result, I didn't spend as much time on this class as it demands, therefore, I am not blaming anyone.
Textbook is your best friend in the class. Otherwise, you are all alone.

He is very knowledgeable and it seems his goal is to help his students do well.  Class might be difficult at first, but bare with him and do all the assignments and you will do well.  He also has a great personality and is very approachable.
He has no idea what he is doing!

He consistently delivered lectures as though he were seeing the slides for the first time. He was notoriously bad last semester, and this was evidenced by the consistently low scores (around 50's) of the tests. He has an excellent personality, but lectures and sections were never worth going to.
Great teacher, affable.
Amazing Arabic teacher

Arabic is a hard language, especially for non-heritage speakers, so expect this to be a tough class. Still, Makda tries her best to explain everything clearly. She is very caring and funny -- she also wrote the textbook for the class so she knows her stuff. In my experience this was an amazing class, made better by a great professor.

I loved her!! Prof. Weatherspoon made the class so lively and engaging, even though it was online. She was really understanding and flexible with deadlines too. Even though participation mattered a lot, I wasn't afraid to talk or make mistakes because she made the environment welcoming and friendly. The coursework isn't designed to be hard either.

THE BEST professor I've had in my life. Took Elementary I & II and Intermediate I with her. Makes the material super accessible, ensures that all students understand the material, super personable, and hilarious. She is a major force in the Arabic department and significantly contributes to its prestige. I was extremely lucky to study under her.
One of the best professors I have ever had! Genuinely caring and motivational. Makes a tough subject fun and I feel very lucky to have had her as a professor.

Makda is the sweetest person I have ever met. I've taken both Intro Arabic I and Intermed. Arabic I with her - her classes are always fuller than any of her colleagues'. She is an easy grader, very conversational, and wants you to succeed. Make sure you participate, because you won't learn very much otherwise. Textbook is the daily workbook.
GREAT
Cute. Very good English for a native speaker. Has a funny sense of humor that is a little foreign and quirky
Great Professor!

Kadhim is an incredible instructor. As other reviewers have mentioned, he genuinely cares about his students and works hard to create a friendly classroom environment. His Arabic class was the best hour of my day, because he strongly encourages students to work together outside class. Also, he has a great sense of humor.

Kadhim is a really nice teacher and made every day pretty fun with his personality. Also, he encouraged a sense of friendship within the classroom which made it easier to study outside of class. He tries to warn for quizzes ahead of time too, which is helpful.
He is a superb teacher. I can't wait to take his next class. He is genuinely committed to helping his students both in and outside the class.

He is so nice to his students. Arabic is not easy though, and it is very easy to fall behind. You need to keep up on the daily-missing one or two days in a week will leave you struggling for the quizzes/exams. If you work hard, an A is achievable, but expect a B if you can't put in an hour/two a night. Highly recommend.
Great guy. He takes each of his students' success personally and shows up to class with a great attitude. If you're interested in Arabic Kadhim makes it accessible and fun.

Great guy who really wants to see all his students participate and do well. Professor Owayez fosters a supportive learning environment, which creates a tight-knit and capable class. Overall he's a genuine, caring, and awesome Arabic teacher.
A great professor.  She really knows what she's talking about and makes it interesting.  Got behind in lectures, but she took stuff off the final to make up for it.
Oh My God... One of the worst professors I have met... I think she is still teaching, and if you take this class, this class would be one of the worst experiences for you in your whole life. Damn...

Jeff is a great professor, who makes the class exciting. He utilizes acting games and vocal exercises to improve beginner actors. Take his class if you want to have fun, have minimal homework/tests, and play improv games. Don't take this class, if you have a lot of experience and expect to become a stronger actor; this class is for beginners.

Jeff is so incredible! This was perhaps the most amazing course I took at Cornell and he is the reason why. He is really great at making everyone feel comfortable and improving your acting, public speaking, etc. I would HIGHLY recommend taking any course he is offering! He is also a very easy grader but you must come to class.
Best professor ever. I couldn't imagine taking this course with anyone else. His physicality and love for theatre really shows. Highly recommend this course!

Jeff is definitely one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. The class was a ton of fun and just looked forward to going to it every time. Went into it not knowing what expect but ended up being probably my favorite class I've taken at Cornell.

Jeff is one of, if not THE, best professor I have had at Cornell.  He manages to focus on the important aspects of acting while managing to keep it amazingly fun.  Much better than the other professors teaching this course.
No Comments

This is my second class with Prof. Bronfenbrenner and I have to say that I'm ride or die now. She was increadibly patient and caring with me and other students. She knows what she's talking about more than nearly every other faculty member at ILR. Highly recommend.

Professor Bronfenbrenner is very well respected in her field and she makes that very clear within her class. She's very knowledgeable but isn't the best at conveying that knowledge. She can be intimidating at first, but once you warm up to her she can be very helpful and makes it clear that she wants you to succeed.
She is tough but amazing. Her expertise is unparalleled. She really is one of the best at ILR.

Dr. Bronfenbrenner is knowledgeable and experienced. However, she does not communicate that knowledge well at all. Her grading is ambiguous, she changes her mind without telling you, she only speaks in mumbles or yelling. The class could have been great, but she shouldn't be teaching anymore.
Kate B is one of the best professors at ILR. She's tough but if you take her class you'll learn a lot and be well prepared to go into the labor movement.

Without a doubt the most important labor-focused professor in the ILR School. Sometimes confusing, sometimes off-topic, but highly regarded, extremely knowledgeable, and has real-world experience beyond academia. Take her classes before she retires because the ILR School won't have anyone like her for a while

Professor Bronfenbrenner is a wonderful and kind professor who is extremely knowledgeable and well respected in her field. She may get off topic and sometimes provide unclear instructions but she is the best professor and mentor I have ever had and will give a good grade for those who put in the work. Go to her office hours and talk to her.

Very knowledgable, but not a great teacher. Assumes a lot of prior knowledge. Unclear on expectations. Will go on tangents that have nothing to do with the class (although her stories are usually interesting). Lots of reading - you have to do it to learn how to do the assignments, because her lectures are not very helpful. She is very nice, though.

Rarely were the lectures useful.  Most of my learning came from independent research. Kate provides adequate reading materials and is approachable, but expect to be challenged in her office hours as well. Very knowledgeable, not great at teaching, but great for research projects. Fair grader. Lots of reading and don't expect  to get it all done.

Kate is truly an inspirational professor who teaches extremely relevant courses for those who aspire to go into the labor movement/labor relations. If you put in the work, do the readings, and demonstrate that you paid attention in class throughout the assignments. If you don't understand something, go to office hours and actually talk to her.

She's not a very clear speaker.  If you ask questions, you probably won't be satisfied with the answers.  She assumes a lot of prior knowledge, to an unreasonable extent.  She isn't very kind, and seems to expect near-perfection.  However, the classes she teaches are extraordinarily useful.  Take if passionate about material; otherwise DON'T.

Kate may not have explicit lessons plans but she is obviously a clever, passionate professor. I have a research background in fields very different from the Labor Movement, but I can still admire the zealousness, courage and fervor it must take to examine issues related to such a marginalized field of study.

I have never had such a disorganized, unreasonable professor in my life. Course goals and expectations are so poorly defined that many students are uncomfortable during class. I highly recommend that students avoid this professor.
Extremely Helpful Professor who teaches challenging classes. Attend class, ask questions, show interest, and you will do well.
You people don't get it. She's just as tough to those of us on the labor side. If you want to learn no one teaches it better but don't expect an easy A.

She is insane, unclear, and lacks compasison for anyone not fully (200%) supporting her far left union views. If you think you want to work for a union do not take her class, she will turn you against them. The worst professor ILR has.For what you actually learn it is not worth it to decode her lectures and assignments to try and get a good grade.

Her teaching styles give way to rampant tangents that do not progress the topic at hand. Furthermore, she does not retain the professionalism required of a professor or any educator. Her biases towards unions cloud her judgment when trying to create an academic discourse.
No Comments
Very insightful "professor," she should be offered a full time teaching position for the work she does.  Also a fantastic researcher and very accomplished.

Professor Kate is amazing! She takes the time to engage with each student and is very accommodating. I have tremendously improved my writing skills because of her and would highly recommend to take her class.

I took FWS 1380 (the only course code choice was 1420, so I had to choose that) with Professor Navickas, and it was really amazing. The discussions were always super interesting, with not a lot of reading and a very doable workload. It was my favorite class of the semester.
Take care of yourself and don't take this class, or any of her classes.
pretty straightforward class and professor. do readings, understand readings, tested on readings. grading was a little vague but whatever
Definitely the best labor law professor. You won't regret taking labor law with Griffith!

Griffith was an amazing professor (definitely the best for labor law). The class is not easy but an A not impossible. You have to be on top of your work. Exams are based on class discussions; pay attention to your classmates not just Griffith.
Such an amazing lecturer. She explains everything so well and clearly. Definitely recommend her for labor law!

Professor Griffith grades based on a prelim, legal writing assignment, and a final. She is very clear in class on how to approach the prelim and the TA is very helpful for questions about cases. Make your life easy and start the legal writing assignment when she tells you to. You don't need to read every case, but be sure you have each brief.
All you need to know is... that she does her job well.

Prof Griffith is a spectacular teacher. She clarified all of the course material and clearly explained the expectations for the course. 2 tests and 1 legal research assignment. You need to be in every class because EVERYTHING is fair game for tests. Tests are pretty difficult, but she does give the course a curve and that worked to my benefit.

Prof Griffith is amazing - always makes sure her students are clear and understand the material. 2 exams one paper. Make sure you take really good notes in class, study, and you'll do great. But, if you miss something or are unclear, make sure you ask questions!! Would recommend wish I could take anther class with her!

She is overrated on here because the other professors teaching labor law are unbearable. Her class is significantly more work than other labor law professors due to the in class tests. She is a fair and reasonable person and doesn't have the elitist superiority many other professors do. There are pros and cons to her course, weigh them and decide.

really boring before the 1st midterm but it gets better.  She takes specific notes about your exam so you really know what to improve/understand your grade.  very friendly and helpful and brings in amazing guest speakers. def reccommend for labor law

Great professor. I didn't have any interest in labor law but this class was one of best classes I've taken. It was also the toughest class but you'll be fine if you pay attention in class, take good notes and work for it. Go to office hours if you have questions and show your efforts to the professor and TA. Recommend taking any of her class.

A really awesome professor who knows her stuff, and knows how to get students to learn. Made the class clear and rewarding even though i previously had no interest in law.  The research paper is pretty straight forward, and shouldn't give you trouble unless you wait until the end. And the tests are really clear, she doesn't give trick questions.

Best ILR law professor. There's a ton to study and some of the stuff you think wont be on the exams will be on there. The 1st exam is tougher and the paper is tough, but i think her final curve is strong. she's a great teacher and really sweet. do yourself a favor and take her.
What a great gal, she will answer any and every question you have during class and will slow down and review certain cases if the class seems to have trouble with it.

Excellent. Highly recommend any of her courses. Not the easiest grader, but expectations are made clear and if you put in the work, you'll have no trouble getting a good grade. She does not try to trick or cheat you out of points; everything is straightforward and if you know your information you'll be set.

Best Teacher I have had in the ILR school,  Hands Down. She is very fair and interesting. Great job engaging the class. Tests are extremely fair. Awesome. Definitely take this class with this professor.

I've taken a number of Professor Griffith's classes.  She is always fair and engaging.  She is very willing to help anyone who goes to her office hours.  Definitely the best professor I have had in ILR; probably the best I have had at Cornell.

Professor Griffith was a great teacher. She was very helpful during office hours and always asked students if they had questions during class. She was always willing to further explain cases discussed in class or details went over about specific cases. I definitely reccommend her course!

Clear, accessible, and fair. Anyone who takes the time to see her in OHs knows that she genuinely cares for her students. Presents all sides of policy debates. IMO, the best labor law prof.  Griffith strikes the perfect balance between Gold and Lieberwitz--her classes are not overbearing, but still rewarding and educational.
She's very clear and precise. make sure you pay attention in class. The cases are pretty interesting, and I thought I would hate the class but I actually enjoyed it.

she does a great job at introducing students to law and learning how to apply it. she gives exams for which you can cram but you must have gone to class and have done the reading. you will leave her class with the ability to read and pull out legal principles from cases, but with gold you will know much more but suffer more.

She is so helpful if you go to office hours. You have to do the reading to even think about passing her class. The exam questions are fair. The paper you have to write was a bit unclear but it was graded fairly. You really learn a lot in class...better than Gold (his students leave class depressed and tired).

The class isn't easy and you will have A LOT of reading and the final paper if done properly will be A LOT of work.  However, the exams are fair and Griffith is extremely helpful, especially for those who take the time to see her in office hours.  And in the end it is still less work than Gold, but you learn just as much.

The final paper and midterm/final are fair. She is helpful in office hours. Class can be difficult if you don't do the reading. She teaches the class in the Socratic method so there's a lot of class discussion. I wouldn't buy the text book. She gives you a lot of handouts and you can either borrow a book or photocopy from the library when needed.

Fair grader, nice lady. She and the TA were willing to help if you needed it.  My only real complaint is that she relied heavily on the class to produce the answers to our own questions, and it was sometimes hard to tell which answers were so-so, which were spot-on, etc. Not to mention that a quarter of the time you couldn't even hear the student.

Griffith knows what she is talking about. You learn a lot in the class. It is very straight forward. The tests and paper are very fair. Required reading every class (if you don't do it, the class is can difficult). She encourages everyone to speak.  Recommended.
Ugh

She does structure class lectures around readings. She lets the class discussions go off on tangents before discussing main points of the readings first. Does not give study guides or clearly explains the format of the midterm. Just very unorganized. The students relied heavily on the TA for proper instruction and clearification
Worse class ever!
A pseudo-intellectual

Professor McCullough is amazing. Her class made me want to pursue a minor in FGSS. In all, there is a lot of (fascinating) reading but only a few assignments. If you put the time in, you'll be fine! She tries to make it accessible to all majors and tries to engage everyone. Everyone should take an FGSS class, especially if it is w Prof. McCullough.

McCullough is great. Super sweet and actually cares a lot about her students and what she's teaching. I definitely recommend if you're willing to work really hard (especially on essays), do lot's of reading, and participate in class. You will learn if you show up!
Professor McCullough was amazing. She's a tough grader, but I would definitely take another class with her. She is honestly one of the best professors I have had so far!

I had the flu and she postponed my due-date more than a week and met with me to discuss my topic. I also asked for more reading material on a subject and she combed through her piles of books to find something relevant. She's amazing, kind, and unbelievably smart. She gives you the grades you deserve.

Professor McCullough is great! The class is very discussion oriented so try and speak up. Additionally, she is a very fair grader with opportunities for a little bit of extra credit (she does assign a good amount of work though and there isn't really grade inflation). I would definitely take another class with her!

I love Kate and you will too. She is a fair grader, but she does assign an awful lot of reading. Most of them were interesting and it helps if you speak up in class. She is very approachable, funny, sweet and cares about her students!

Professor McCullough is awesome! She can be a tough grader, but if you go to her during office hours she'll work with you on your writing. Her class *is* work (it's not super easy,) but if you come to class and go to her office hours you should be able to get a good grade.
I've take McCoullough for FGSS 201 and several other courses - I'd take anything she taught.
best teacher ive had at cornell. no question about it.
One of the best.  She deserves more credit than she's getting.
Interesting discussions but awful selection of material.
too many papers and revisions, hard grader, boring books

I generally wouldn't recommend this class because the professor seems indifferent to their students and unnecessarily complicates the material. Strategy is typically a straightforward subject, but it was made more challenging by the unreasonable exams and unclear grading system. The professor enjoys ridiculing student's final presentations.

He's an amazing lecturer. Easily approachable outside class to continue class discussions. Gives good feedback on class work and genuinely cares about his students. A very understanding lecturer. Emphasizes on learning more than grades.
Great lectures

Hands down one of the best professors at Cornell. His passion for the subject matter is immediately clear from the first day. Equally important is his passion for teaching. He loves for students to come to his office hours. Also a really funny guy.

I took a freshman writing seminar with Mertha. If you want a FWS that is writing intensive, not for you. The seminar was mostly consisted of readings and then open discussions on it. The readings and discussions covered wide range of topics and were very interesting(at least for me). Also, Mertha's China stories are always nice to hear.

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. Engaging, knowledgeable, funny, really cares about teaching, goes above and beyond for students who work hard and commit to the course. Can be long winded but just buckle up. One of the premier China authorities n the US; personal anecdotes should be taken seriously as he has a lot of wild field experiences
Mertha is the reason I have become a government major.  His comparative politics and china under revolution and reform classes will be part of my lasting memories of cornell.

I took both Intro to comparative politics and China Under Revolution and Reform with Mertha. His comparative politics class was relatively easy compared to most government courses at Cornell. His China's course was much more harshly graded.Regardless of the grading, Mertha is a dedicated educator and you will learn a lot from his classes.

Mertha is a great professor. His lectures are crystal clear and he always has interesting stories from his travels in China. He also makes genuinely funny jokes. If you need an intro for government, definitely do intro to comparative with him. Fairly graded class in which you just need to read the textbook before tests to do well.

Mertha seems like a nice guy. Perhaps it was because it was his first time teaching the course, the course was extremely disorganized. Lectures were pretty unclear and useless. To prepare for the exams, just read the chapters in the book. Overall though, I found the class to be a major disappointment albeit not difficult at all if you actually read

Take 1313 with Mertha if possible. He makes things easy and interesting, and is always willing to help. Prior to the class I had no background in political science but thanks to Mertha, now I am a government major.

This man is one of the greatest cultivators of undergraduate education I have witnessed. He keeps you interested, is an expert in the subject, is not unnecessarily difficult, and probably should even try stand-up. This man will broaden your horizons, and you will remember him 20 years after you leave this place.
Great for seminar, incredibly fun/smart/noraml.  Goes on interesting tangents, which is good in seminars b/c you can just learn and not take notes.
Interesting character with some funny stories. Passionate about subject and likes to brag about his connections in China. Great class if you want an intro to modern Chinese history/politics.

Wanders a lot in lectures, but is an expert on the material.  Very entertaining, extremely helpful outside of class.  Be prepared to keep yourself on track, though...because he won't!  Overall, great professor, but not a taskmaster.

Excellent professor, great interest in the subject, has literally lived it. Humorous anecdotes intertwined with well organized material make lecture fun and very useful. Recommend any course he teaches.
No Comments
Clear grading, prelim questions directly from assignments and lecture slides.

Great class if you simply do the work. 2 exams, 1 final paper. Studied two days prior for both exams and just followed the straight forward rubric for the exams. Posts zooms of every lecture and gives extra credit opportunities. Dr. Berry is a funny guy if you have a sense of humor. Easy class if you pay attention.

Memorization heavy class. Says you just need to know the big picture on exams but you NEED to memorize lots of details to get a good grade. (not an easy A; you need to put in the work) Very interesting material. Tries to be funny but his sense of humor got annoying after a while..

Don't know why Dr. Berry's score is so low. Prof was so funny and laid back, making class worth showing up to (attendance wasn't required). It seems all he wanted was to encourage us all to engage and participate in class, if you do that you're all set to do well and have a great time! This class exposed me to so much new and interesting material

Professor Berry really tries his best. This was his second year teaching the course, and he made adjustments because of the difficulty students had last year. His lectures are organized and his slides are clear, and he tried to engage us as much as possible during lectures! His exam was fair, and he genuinely wanted us to do well! A sweetheart!

Dr. Berry is an awesome professor. His exams really don't require specific details and you get full credit for things that can be answered with one/two words. You only need the key words/phrases!! An A is attainable. All materials are lecture-based and he's always more than happy to help students. He's very approachable, kind, and pretty funny.

He really isn't that tough a grader seriously. In all honesty, yes there is some stuff that are detailed and lecture heavy content. It's all on the lectures and the exam is SUPER do-able to finish!!! He doesn't expect super detailed responses (that would be impossible) literally I put bullets on my exam and was able to get a fair grade.

He would walk around all over the lecture hall while recording a Panopto video which was impossible to listen to since the mic was only at the front. He elaborates on a lot of things and never concludes his statement. His lecture was all over the place and his exam was 60 short answers in 75 minutes that had to be detailed responses.

Professor does not speak clearly and gives the most ridiculous exams. He assigned a 60q short answer exam (in 75 minutes) and deducted points on answers that he claimed did not need to go too in depth in class. The material itself is easy to learn but you have a lot of memorizing to do, he covers a lot of extraneous detail. Did not enjoy his class
does not speak clearly, comes to lecture unprepared, tends to confuse students with his unnecessary research

Started out boring (I mean it is econometrics), but then he got into the  application of the statistics and was an amazing professor. You can pass without going to the lectures, but I highly recommend going to them because they help a lot and he makes the subject a lot more interesting!

Professor Berry is great in the classroom. His lectures are clear and fun. Some lecture topics I could do without but that was just a matter of personal preference. The class wasn't overly quantitative but gives you a good grounding in how to interpret econometric papers, randomized control trials, and major issues in the developing world.

Boring lectures; I learned mostly by doing the psets with friends. Econometrics is hard in general, but the math is pretty straightforward if you put in the work. Definitely recommend having a group to work on psets with, otherwise it's kind of hard to figure out all the concepts.

While a very brilliant man (he mentions maybe 20 times during the year that he went to MIT), his lectures are confusing and often don't present the material in the best way to learn it for the first time. Makes the class a lot harder than its needs to be, and arbitrarily curves your final grade without clear idea of how that process occurs.

Berry is a good teacher, econometrics is just a really tough class. Make sure you do well on the HWs from the beginning, as there are only 6 and they're worth 25%. Definitely do them with a group. Tests are generally pretty fairpredictable but challenging. Lecture is dry but just because of the heavy notation. He is nice and approachable.

Professor Berry has good firsthand experience in development econ (e.g. MIT). He lectures clearly, is relatively enthusiastic, and the class isn't terribly difficult. Problem sets and exams focused on simple economic models for development concepts and stylized facts from empirical studies.

The class is fine, if unexciting.  I like that he tries to teach people basic empirical methods.  My advice to Prof Berry:  Come to class on time.  When you consistently arrive to class 5+ minutes late, it signals to students that you're not interested in teaching and that's a turn off.  Overall, a decent, if unexciting class. Note the long psets.
Lectures are a bit scattered, but the overheads are good, his understanding and knowledge are good, and the material is interesting. He's also a nice guy :D
good

Prof Debbie is a very caring professor and is very organized in her material and assignments. The exams weren't bad if you stayed on top of readings & lectures, and were mainly synthesis questions so you had to really understand the material. This semester she allowed exams to be open note which was incredibly helpful. Readings took alot of time.

The professor seemed easy-going and nice at first, but she was not very understanding of a difficult situation I had during the semester. Also a soft-spoken lecturer, so sit in the front if you want to take good notes.
Have to go to lecture and write down the answers to homework questions that she says. Not do on your own. Good class overall. Strongly recommend. Minimal work.

Meh...course paled to what expectations I had going in. Teacher is friendly and available for help anytime. Material is not as advanced as you'd expect= brief overview. If you took immuno or microbio class will be easy. Not too hard of a class to get an easy grade. Pretty tough to get an A+ or A despite simple content. take extra credit, easy pts
One of the best course that I took at Cornell. Great way to learn how to design and build technology for underserved communities in different parts of the world. Strongly recommended.
Great professor with reading heavy coursework. Be ready to explore outside of the American ecosystem and learn more about global development in all his classes.

Professor Vashistha is nice and really cares about the content of this class. There's a lot of reading but nothing that's too much to handle. The only hard part of this class is the final project where you have to start super early and show that you put a lot of thought and work into it to do well. Other than the final project, super manageable.
Professor Manthri is an exceptional teacher, truly one of a kind. I highly recommend this course: life-altering meowing experience guaranteed.
He was the greatest professor I ever had at Cornell. I can meow fluently and have been using my skills to speak to the neighborhood cats. long live Professor Manthri!!!
LEARN TO MIAO
Meow!
MEOW

Alisa is one of my favorite Spanish teacher. Her enthusiasm for the language is infectious, and her teaching style is helpful to get better at the language. Rather than getting hung up on the details, she wants students to get the language. Great sense of humor. Grades very fairly (and quickly!) and work assigned is reasonable for a language class.

All Spanish classes will have mandatory class and homework every day, but Alisa is a very fair grader compared to other Spanish teachers. For written and oral assignments she looks more at if you understand overall concepts rather than just minute details. Also, one of the fastest graders I have ever had.
Cool dude

Val is a very passionate man. He loves what he does and wants to extend that world to you as a student.

He is a bit difficult to understand, as he speaks softly and quickly, and uses a lot of architectural jargon, but overall he is a very caring and intelligent man.

Be ready to read and be in class, you don't want to fall behind.
As long as you are able to follow his line of thought, he is very very insightful. He just goes on a tangent and eventually makes his point.

Dawson REALLY CARES and goes out of his way to make the material more UNDERSTANDABLE if you show INTEREST. An EXTREMELY DRY lecturer, but posts all USEFUL notes online. 4140 will mostly teach data analysis & solid mech theory used in ACTUAL EXPSIM. REALLY COOL projects, but VERY time consuming. Often gives extensions. No exams in this class.

A difficult, miserable, and immensely time consuming course and professor that can single-handedly ruin a semester.  He is impossibly boring and monotonous to listen too, but the worst is his evil curving: He makes even numbers of A?s, B?s and C?s.  Approx: A?s: 90%+, B?s 72-89, C?s: 40-71.  Expect to work 40 hours every two weeks to earn a B.

The projects are very fairly easy if you show up to class and pay attention. Remember to include some key principals  in class in your report and include as much possible in your report.  Most of the time the TA miss stuff on your report and you can get about 1 to 2 points back out of the 15 points if you talk to them.

Very monotonic and disengaging but cares about his students are is willing to help.  Often times, hes the only person who really understands the materials as the TAs can sometimes be idiots.  The material is quite boring, which compounds Dawsons boring nature.  Information required for the projects if often times tacit and hard to obtain.

I am sitting in his class right now on my friends touch. I am so bored that I want to kill myself. Dawson is so boring that I can't even sleep. He is droning on and on about some Greek stuff. Do not tale this class if you don't have to it is miserable . The projects take forever too. Good luck if 325 is required for you.
THE MOST BORING PERSON EVER not to say he's not a nice guy. The class is all projects. If you do the work, you can definitely pull off an A.

Pretty boring, monotone lecturer. Knows his stuff though, and if you get to know him he's a really nice guy whose willing to help, its just unfortunate that he can be so disengaging during lecture. Project only class --- Projects are very time consuming, but i found them to be moderately interesting...some are hard, but more sotime consumingthanhar

I think Dawson gets too much of a bad rap as a person. Seems like Miller and him drew straws on who teaches 212 vs 325, and Dawson got stuck with the crap end of things. I don't think that anyone could teach that material in an interesting manner. Go to office hourse, have Hadas explain the projects, work your butt off, get AS's. Easy.

Without a doubt, the worst professor in all of cornell. To make matters worse, he had a TA that never gave consistent grades and it seemed she would randomly assign letter grades. Assignments take forever, and you will do poorly. Enjoy
possibly worst professor at cornell.  projects will take you about 40 hours each and then you will still fail them.
My god, this guy is the most uncaring professor I've ever seen. I literally learned nothing, except a hatred for the material he tried to cover.

The projects are enormous pain in the butt. You're assumed to have known some obscure eqn/concept that is definitely not stated in the assignment sheet. Therefore, you have to harrass the TA if you want a "guaranteed A" in the course. You have to go to section so that you might get some info to do the project. Just survive this one out.

Dawson really cares about his students, and if you ask him questions, he'll be sure to go out of his way to help you understand the concepts.  The assignments and the grading are straightforward.  An optional one week extension of any one deadline makes the class more manageable during crunch times.

If you have ever fallen asleep in classes, you will in this class. I think this is a class that is a prime example of you reap what you sow. Ask questions, make an effort to be interested, and I promise you, you wont fall asleep. Dawson is a true teacher, he wants to help his students learn. Capitalize on this.

HORRENDOUS.  absolutely miserable guy...you need to goto sections just to get hints on projects, other than that its a good time to goto upson lounge and get a quick nap.  this guy is just a big waste of life as far as teaching is concerned.

This guy doesn't know how to talk like he's a normal person.  It's like an audio textbook with bad handwriting (and he makes up greek letters i've never heard of - or they're arabic or something).  Some girl actually yelled out in pain during class one time.  avoid him if you can.

his lectures are complete and utter jiberish.  he uses thousands of subscripts and superscripts and random greek letters that look like scribbles.  which brings me to his handwriting which is completely illegible.  Do the projects, the lectures are worthless.

OH MY !!!!  Prepare to be tortured. I graduated summa****laude from MAE 2 years ago, and STILL had to take the class over, along with 18 other of my peers, for failing it. Very painful and slow lectures. Out of 120 students taking the class only about 18 showed up regularly (those who failed the previous year).

Dawson is an unusual creature: having put the effort into creating a new type of course in 325, one would expect him to act like he cares a bit more. This is not the case. The man's a walking sleeping draught, and the work is so tedious it makes me break down in tears.

Don't bother going to class, you can sit in the front row and still not read his handwritting.  Lecture material does not cover anything related to course work and the material that is covered in lecture is done at a superfical level.  Net result: you do busy work and learn nothing for a semester.
No Comments
Offensively bad professor.

Terrible lecturing, lessons are "background" to projects (read: "totally unrelated and useless")... projects are hard and its damn hard to do those A projects... tried talking with him, he just made me more frustrated.  btw Srinivas sucks too.
WORST HANDWRITING IN THE WORLD!!!!!!!!!!!!

Horrible lecturer that doesn't keep a single person awake.  Hard HWs and tests that seem so easy after the fact but are hard to study for and cause a lot of stress when they're coming up.  Oh, and computer assignments during finals was horrible too.

Very hard class. First paper had a median of around a 25%. If you want to do well on the two papers, you basically have to spend two straight weeks in the library before you submit them. If you don't want to do that, and you care a lot about your grades, try to avoid this class. Curve saves you; upper 80s turns into A+.

I had Professor Gold for Labor Law many years ago and, because the class was so exceptional, I then selected him to be my advisor for my ILR honors thesis. Professor Gold was excellent as a thesis advisor and helped me develop much better writing and analytical skills. I have always been grateful for his wisdom and patience. He will make you think!

Gold is a class act and a wonderful professor. I was definitely apprehensive coming into this class, considering all of the folklore surrounding both him and the course, but he is a brilliant teacher who really pushes for you to actually learn. I would genuinely take any class he taught.
This dude is terrible do not take this professor he will make you want to go to Cornells bridge

Gold randomly assigns you two partners to always work with for exercises. Pray you have some good partners who do the reading. I got a 27% on the 1st writing assignment that I worked my butt off on. I dedicated an entire week to the final essay and got a 92%. I averaged 56% throughout the semester and got a 69% total after the final.

Great class to get exposure to law school, but I learned nothing in this class. However, Gold is a great professor nonetheless who will call you out on your bs in class and in papers. also is just a nice and respectable dude overall. I was way below the medians on all the papers (50% weight) and still got a b+.

The pop quizzes are graded right minus wrong answers. Annoying, especially when it is later in the semester and you feel pressured to earn more points to improve your grade. The final paper is incredibly hard, so start early. You can do ok in this class. Participate and you will learn a lot. More than labor law, you are taught critical thinking.

okay so basically class grade is based off homeworks/pop quizzes abt homework and TWO big papers (+ a rewrite of the paper for final essay.) You can do well in this class but you have to go to office hours with prof and start papers weeks in advance (to have enough time to change it). not very accessible + super unclear criteria for essays.

Gold's instructions for assignment seem clear at first. Ultimately, you realize you did not and he pulls a "gotcha" and you fail the exam. Ex: I spent 20+ hours first assignment, I got a 50%. I spent another 20+ on another assignment and worked with 5 other people, I got the highest grade and it was still below average. Avoid him.

Very knowledgeable, but extremely tough course. If you are going into law, take this class. If not, you will learn a lot but put in an insane amount of time and effort. If I had the option to take a different professor, I would've because I don't want to go into law, but still glad I had this experience.
Easy to relate with and very understanding

Yeah, Gold is the hardest professor in ILR for the most difficult course; however, he is one of the most knowledgable professors in the school. This class will not be easy, and will require a lot of work. If you take this class, I promise you will leave it a better student. Gold is unique!
Gold is a gem. You will truly learn and get your money's worth. Everyone exaggerates over how hard this class is. If you put in the work, you will succeed.

Hardest class I have taken so much at ILR. The material was very dry and the pop quizzes are really difficult. Don't plan on sleeping because there are often 3+ readings due every class plus homework. Papers are graded very harshly. Gold starts every class off with a joke, but someone needs to tell him that he isn't funny.

Most difficult class I've ever taken in the ILR School. Labor Law took up at least 70% of my time this semester, with my other classes crammed into the other 30%. Because most of the cases are antiquated, they're a pain to read and understand. He distances himself from students and I felt intimidated to talk to him most of the semester.
If you value sleep, I wouldn't recommend this prof, but if you have any interest in law you have to take it with him.  Unbelievable amount of hard work, but it pays off in the end.

Professor Gold's class was not easy. But it was my favorite class at Cornell. You learn  a TON. He is inspiring and really dedicated to his students; I was assigned a group and we got along super well so it took some of the pressure off. He wrote my recommendation for law school and now I'm a labor and employment lawyer, if that tells you anything.

worst professor in ILR. Least clear assignments, but has very specific expectations. He doesn't realize that students have other classes besides his, and you will leave each class with no idea of what to do/how to apply the information from class.  Very smart man but awful instructor. Avoid his class at all costs.

if you want to go to law school this is life affirming. otherwise, get a different professor for labor law.  I spent all my time on this class and got an 80% which curved  to an A. Lots of group work but you can't choose your group which sucks sometimes. The Law school TA is SUPER HELPFUL, you'll learn a ton about labor law/your writing. MeanB+

Prof. Gold is great. His class had  a reputation for being hard as hell, but it really isn't all that bad. There is a lot of required reading and pop quizzes just about every class. Most of the homework is group work. Don't worry about his tough grading;  I had a 45% raw score at the end of the semester that got curved to a B. Learned a TON.

For Ethics at Work (sophomore writing seminar), he values more quality than quantity. You don't write that much, but you need to summarize complicated philosophical concepts and theories in 2 pages. Take notes; they help a little. Reading helps a little. Office hours help more.

If you take this class, make sure your footnotes are on the correct side of the period at the end of the sentence--I had 1% taken of my final paper for each incorrectly placed footnote (about 34 in all). If thats the kind of class you like, then go for it. If its not, then you will regret taking it and you probably wont get above a B-.

Professor Gold is the professor who lets you challenge him and doesn't dismiss your ideas when they're different.  My class with Professor Gold is the highlight of my semester. His comments on your papers are longer than the papers themselves; I learn so much about my writing style, my strengths, and my weaknesses. It's  such a pleasure.

His Labor Law course is by far my favorite class. While the work is extensive it is all extremely relevant to the lectures. He starts off each class with a joke or a funny story. He also asks if there are any questions from the previous lecture. In the end, the curve will help you a ton so don't freak about the low grades throughout the semester.

Gold is incredibly intense and intimidating & labor law is undeniably demanding. But he is a fascinating lecturer, a fair teacher, and incredibly knowledgeable. The workload is very heavy but classmates bond over essays & seemingly impossible assignments. The difficulty is worth it; I learned so much in this class. Attendance- basically mandatory.

Probably the most demanding professor at Cornell and the teacher of ILR's most demanding class. He's incredibly smart and experienced.  You will learn TONS about labor law (and time management). Workload is insane, but his lectures and your knowledge at the end of the course make up for it. 2010 is great for bonding with others over lack of sleep.

Professor Gold's course has been by far the best course I have ever taken at Cornell University.  He is a very fair professor which views students as equals, no matter their backgrounds, and challenges every student in the same manner.  I highly recommend this course.
he is a great guy and amazing teacher. don't be scared to take his class. there's work, but it's definitely worth it in the end.
The material is not easy for sure. Luckily, Professor Gold makes it interesting and he is fair.

Probably the best class I've taken at Cornell.  I dreaded the course and Professor Gold before taking his class, and ended up loving them both.  Plan your other classes around this one though -- incredible amount of nightly work.  Gold stimulates creative thinking unlike any professor I've had, and in the end, I view the world differently.

So I figured I would kick off 2009 by reiterating that Professor Gold still is, in fact, moderately deranged. With that said, he is a brilliant professor and a leader in his field. I would not discourage any ILRee from taking his class. His work is tough and time consuming, but I can not criticize Gold for demanding a lot from his students.
Amazing teacher. If you get a chance, chat with him outside of class about something besides class, you'll be suprised.

As a current law school student and former labor relations specialist, I can fully appreciate Gold's teaching style.  I'm sure that I learned more in his class than the other CB201 professors taught their students.  Do not shy away from this class if you really want to learn labor law.

Not to belabor the point, but Prof. Gold definitely is intelligent, knows labor law well, and teaches the topic well. However, unless you have a major interest in (labor) law, it is truly senseless to work exponentially harder in this class than in the other labor law classes. The grading is fair, it's just that the amount of work is excessive.

While he might be a good professor, there is way too much work compared to the other labor law class, and the grades end up being the same.  If you want to learn and dont care about grades, then take him, if however care about your gpa and or time, think twice before signing up

What can you say about Gold? Yes, it's a very demanding & grueling class & you will learn a lot. And yes, nothing that you could ever read or say will prepare you for the amount of work required for this class. He can be insensitive & a harsh grader, but you will walk away w/more knowledge than you ever thought possible. Take him & enjoy the ride.
If you want to go to Law School...take GOLD! He is one of ILR's most knowledgable professors and you are truly missing out if you choose not to take him at least once.

This class is worth at least 6 credits and not the 3 they claim, you WILL be doing hmwk for this class EVERY night and it WILL keep you up to the early hours in the morning for research papers and homework alike- Gold isn't a bad guy, but he doesn't seem to understand that students are taking more than just his class- that or he doesn't care
Gold is pretty interesting in lecture, but this class has waaaaaaaaaay to much work invovled for a mere 3 credits.... avoid if possible

Take Intro Labor Law with Gold if you actually want an introduction to labor law. Yeah this class is hard but if you put in effort you do well, and thats how a class should be taught. You'll learn more here than in any other class I've taken at the ILR school. If you can afford to, do it.
Great Professor, but this class is not for the faint of heart...

most of the positive comments that i've seen and heard about him have been about his wardrobe; i think that should say enough, shouldnt it? this class is very very very hard. there is  online homework every day, and he gives pop quizzes in class. avoid gold if you can.
No Comments

A dapper gentleman indeed, finer cloths could not be weaved by angels.  A symphony of colors await the eyes as he bedazzles the room with his latest vest's of splendor.  Oh what a sight it is to glare upon Michael Evan Gold in all of his splendor, yes a class worth taking if only for the aesthetics

Prof. Gold is one of the most handsomely dressed men at Cornell.  A throwback to a gone era when professors never wore jeans and and always wore a tie.  He classes it up with an array of argiles, sweater vests, and bow ties.  He also has the academic prowess of no one i've had at Cornell

Surviving this class is quite an accomplishment.  A typical week consisted on 3-4 homework assignments and 2-3 quizzes. He requires a lot of work, if you stay on top of it you should be fine.  No final or midterm, but you will take 50-60 online quizes throughout the semester.  He also requires a three part final paper, talk to someone who took the class before to find out how to do well on the paper.

Not that bad of a class.  A lot of work, but when it's over and you don't have to take a final it feels worth it.  You learn a lot, but work hard to learn it.  Prof Gold is intimidating at first, but if you ask him for help he's very receptive and willing.

Somewhat helpful in OH; extreeeeemley hard class, take it only if you really want to go to law school of like the law.  Sometimes can be a real jerk, but sometimes can be nice.  Not a very interesting person
Tons of work. But overall, well worth it. You will get the most out of his classes than you would anywhere else. If you are considering law school, you must take him.
He is one of the smartest profs in cornell, but the class requires a lot of work. He'll "force" you to learn stuff
The mean on a paper was a 30%, enough said. So difficult, you feel so stupid in the class.
tons of work. very difficult. stay away.
Lots of work, but if you do it and do it well, you will be fine
Impossible assignments, but great class. He is a genius and is good at providing help to those who seek it. A must for anyone considering law school, ILR or otherwise.
Tough, but if you stick with Gold's classes you will learn a ton.  He's a great guy if you prove to him that you want to succeed.  Not a professor to take if you are lazy.
You will learn more about the law than you would ever imagine.  He's extremely smart.  He talks down to you.  The assignments are impossible.  Amazing class!

You Learn So Much...He will help you if you ask!
Had this guy as professor-- get ready to work hard and fail!
Avoid!
impossible
Demanding, but a great guy if you know him
The worst--degrading to students.

Class certainly took me a bit to get used to but the lectures are very interesting and extremely engaging. Prelims and final are difficult, but not hard to do well on if you study. Be careful of the extra assignments and weekly quizzes.

He goes at lightning speed, has a LOT of information on the exams, TAs grade super hard and don't release grades for a while.
