The best lecturer I have ever had. He knows EVERYTHING to do with developmental psych. You don't necessarily need to do the readings, but get ready to type as fast as you can for the whole class. His slides are very minimal and almost all the information you need to know just comes out of his mouth. Highly recommend.

His lectures are very fast paced and most lectures have minimal slides, so get prepared to write or type fast because exams are pretty in-depth. Usually don't need to read the papers. Prof. Goldstein sometimes felt impatient when answering questions. Lectures felt pretty long, and he sometimes wasn't clear on what a concept meant.

Prof Goldstein is a charismatic and talented speaker! His class was a bit disorganized, but had interesting content. There was quite a lot of reading, and his tests required a lot of memorization of specific case studies, and the class only covers the development of infants/babies, no older kids. Still, interesting stuff.

AMAZING lecturer. truly talented in teaching.  He basically made his own curriculum (no textbook) and it is very well thought out.  He clearly has a vision for what he wants this class to be and he executes very well. Go to class, some readings were helpful but we skipped over a lot.  Use the study guides.

Best professor I've had thus far. Incredibly knowledgeable and enthusiastic- he knows his stuff. Make sure you GO TO CLASS. He covers a lot of information in detail, a lot of which is not on the lecture slides or in the readings. The study guides are essential for passing prelims; attend the review sessions. Prelims are very thorough.
Go to class, don't  need to do the readings. Do the study guides to study for the exams. For projects, definitely do them with a friend (you are allowed partners), makes work much more manageable.

Professor Goldstein was not my favorite. His sense of humor was sort of childish and annoying, and his lectures felt really long. His grading on tests was pretty tough. He was definitely willing to help if you needed it, though, and sometimes we got to watch baby videos in class which was always a nice break in the middle of his long lectures.

Guys... he is amazing. take his class. If you don't have an intellectual crush on him by the end of the course, then I "literally can't even". He's so awesome he'll make you think like a new person, the tests are average and there are group papers. TAKE IT!
I love Professor Goldstein! My favorite professor so far. He made lectures fun and interesting.

The sweetest professor I have ever had. He will go OUT OF HIS WAY to help you. He is very clear in lecture, and is quite funny in his lovable, nerdy way. Class is very do-able, but the TA's are very mean, curt, harsh, and rude. But you will learn a lot, and as long as you study his outlines/go to his review sessions for tests you'll do fine

Goldstein is great!! Amazing lecturer! Very interested in his field and makes material interesting. His lectures are casual and enjoyable. Exams are essays, and are not to bad, but TA grading is ridiculous. Other than TAs, class is great! Highly recommended.
Excellent lecturer. Really passionate about material that is otherwise pretty dull.  Just  a great guy overall. And plus, he talks about babies, how can you possibly go wrong.

First time taking a psych class as an engineer for liberal arts credit. Pretty easy class. I've decided it doesn't really suit my interest but Professor Goldstein is a good lecturer who really cares about the material and making sure you learn it right

great lecturer and interesting materials! Prof Goldstein knows his stuff, and his lecture can be really spontaneous. I wouldn't say it is an easy course, but if you are willing to learn and study really hard for it, you should do just fine. Pay close attention to every thing he delivers in class and use the outline to review.

Interesting material. This course is really just about going to all class and taking intensive notes. Write down 65-75% of what he says (TAs grade picky), use outlines to study for tests, rehearse material, spit back his language, and you’re on your way to an A. Only read parts of textbook on the outline. Good, engaging lecturer, but not terrific.

GREAT lecturer! Absolutely hilarious! His tests can be scary (all short answers + essays), but they're fair. He gives you an outline of exactly what will be on the tests and has really helpful review sessions. If you put in the time, you'll do fine. This class was a ton of fun! You'll learn a ton!

A very good lecturer. His tests were not easy, but he provided us with an outline of everything we needed to know. I agree with the person who posted below that the final can be a major grade booster if you study hard for it.

Best lecturer I've had at Cornell. He's really passionate about his field, and helpful for anyone pursuing psychology as a career. Tests are really fair and easy if you attend lecture and use the test outlines. ONLY read the parts of the textbook on the outline; I got an A and didn't read it at all. Attend all lectures, though.

He is definitely one of the most entertaining professors I've had and he knows his stuff, as demonstrated by his ability to cite experiments or researchers appropriate for just about anything related to babies.Tests can be difficult, but he's very clear about what material you should study.  Occassional homework assignments are easy grade boosters.
Great lecturer, makes class interesting and keeps things light. Environment very open to questions and class participation. Grading is fair, tests aren't difficult as long as you know the outline.
Great Professor, very energetic and knowledgeable. Learnt a lot in class! Tests are hard, so you must study and  prepare... Takenote is useful for this class.  It's a great class overall!

You really have to study for his tests, but he always gives out a "what-to-study" outline beforehand - know everything on it (be able to write a few sentences about each bullet) and you're golden. I feel like I actually LEARNED something (not just memorized). Also, the final is a great chance to bring your grade up (I went from a C to an A).
Would not take this class. Tests are very difficult (all essay). You will need to put alot of work in. His mean test grades are around a 73 and he doesn't curve.
The class is pretty difficult, you have to know your stuff for the tests because they are all essays. If you do the work you can get a decent grade but it is definalty not a slackers class.

Mike is a great professor and makes the class really enjoyable. He's very laid-back, but energetic during lectures and loves what he does. It's not an easy class, but your grade will be fair. Ask him something after class, he's a wealth of knowledge. Highly recommended class, especially for PSYCH/HD majors.

Incredibly interesting lecturer who is very active in the field. If you're at all interested in development this class is a must-take. Beware the tests: the class covers a lot of material and you really have to know a lot about (tests are more or less exclusively essays)

The tests for this class are TOUGH (almost no multiple choice).  Make sure you do all the reading (there's a ton) because you'll be expected to know a lot of specific studies on the tests.  With all that said it's still a great class to take--really interesting material and fantastic teacher
I found developmental very challenging...I worked hard for my B+. Goldstein is awesome and one of the best profs i've had at cornell. He's a great lecturer and is extremely knowledgeable
interesting class and funny professor

Goldstein is the nicest guy around, and a great prof. He's a good professor who tries to make the material interesting and loves what he does. Yet, his lecture material is often unorganized and difficult to follow. Tests are moderate; memorize it all and you'll do well.

He's decent. His fetish with rat pups is quite obvious and he talks about it any chance he gets. He isn't too organized. A standard lecture might be: "this is systemogenesis... oh by the way, rats pups are cool, but we'll talk about it next week. where was i?"
Very interesting. Goldstein is really friendly and makes the  material fun. Its not easy,his tests are demanding but ive managed to do well with enough studying.

Developmental Psych is a great class! While it's not an easy A (mean is a B-), you will learn a great deal.  Professor Goldstein is personable, easy to understand, and his lectures informative and engaging.

I'm a bit surprised that all the other reviews are so negative. She maybe wasn't the best professor I've ever had, but definitely not terrible. She seems to know a lot about the content, she just comes off a bit monotomous and unenthusiastic. The tests are really pretty easy, everything is from the slides. I actually kinda enjoyed the class

Never take a class with Professor Golan. She does not even know her slides. She just reads the slides. It was a waste of time taking NS 3600 with her. The only thing she is so serious about is the attendance.

Awful professor. Not understanding at all. Reads off of slides and does not know what she is doing or talking about. Super strict with attendance but does not even come to lecture prepared. Ive taken 2 of her classes and would not recommend ever taking her class (NS 3600 - NS 3060)

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR. They did not come to lecture prepared. Slides were always just graphs and oftentimes the professor seemed to have a lot of trouble interpreting the graphs. It is like they just showed up to class without having reviewed the lecture beforehand. STAY AWAY!!!

Yeah this professor is straight up awful. Please do not take this class for the sake of your mental health + gpa. They were not a great lecturer just read off of slides. Poor communication when providing guidelines for projects or exams. Grades very hard especially on group projects. This was their first time teaching, but I would not recommend taking it.

The worst class I have taken at Cornell. Her lectures were a series of reading off slides. She managed to make such an interesting and relevant course so unattractive. Compared to other language courses, this is definitely one of the best options. I really enjoyed this class! ADEMOYO IS A GREAT PROFESSOR! He aims to have his students learn the material but does not overwhelm them. The class is totally manageable and the professor is extremely helpful. Best language class I've EVER taken :)
Insane teacher!! Really animated and funny. Subtly disguises heavy philosophy in jokes. A good class to have in Freshman year.

Very nice professor. Likes to encourage students. Informs us on ongoing political and cultural issues. He's very animated and enthusiastic about teaching. Not the most exciting lecturer, but still clear and has a sense of humor (he's often funny because he seems so serious, yet he does/says funny things). I love how he ends many lectures with an unceremonious "kay.. that's it."

Daniel is the man. Super chill, great sense of humor and informal style of teaching. Doesn't make you feel too pressured when you're talking, which is good because talking in class is definitely emphasized. Have to study on your own a lot for the tests but he makes class as fun as it could be.
Unbelievably awesome.

I love him! The man is awesome, definitely one of the best teachers of Spanish I've ever had. His speaking is clear and understandable. You'll be lucky to have him!

Daniel was an amazing professor for my intro spanish class. Going to class was extremely fun and he made it very enjoyable for everyone - even those who weren't the strongest in the language. His grading was fair and he is an incredible asset in learning the language and doing well on tests
Prof. Duque is very nice and helpful. He grades essays harshly but is nevertheless fair. I enjoyed his class.
Such a great prof. Would take another class with him in a second.
Awesome prof. Genuine, clear, charismatic and smart. Very sympathetic and kind, too. Probably one of the best at Cornell.
What a beautiful man. He has such a radiant smile and a goatee to die for.
Best prof around. Take his class, but make sure he's teaching it. The other sections aren't that good.
Such a great professor. Smart and charasmatic but not intimidating. Would love to take another course with him.

Awesome lecturer. His lectures are very interesting and funny. One thing I love about his class was that it was lecture based as opposed to reading bunch of stuff not even remotely covered in class. Stay far far far away from this class if you want to have anywhere near a reasonable GPA. It seems like no matter how much you study for tests it is hard to get close to the mean.
Take this class over psych 101!
This guy is hilarious!! His lectures are long but interesting and he throws in funny pictures in the slides :) I loved the class!

He is an awesome professor!  Great at explaining things and keeping interest in lectures.  However, he posts his slides, so his lectures are not necessary if you have to miss.  Also, I never did the readings and I did very well in the class.  The tests were easy if you knew the material on the slides.  Overall great class!

Delightfully down to earth and runs a laid back class. Gives a good broad overview of the subject. High emphasis on lecture rather than readings. Tries hard to make lectures interesting and clear without dumbing them down. Runs a great course for beginning psych students or students looking for an elective on an interesting subject.
Great class.  Very clear powerpoint presentation of material.  Professor is helpful and funny at times.  The material is interesting.  Study the powerpoint slides for tests and you'll be fine.

My favorite class last semester. Lectures were clear and entertaining, and the posted pdfs/powerpoints replaced taken notes almost completely. Loved this professor!! Very clear lectures, and he manages to make statistics interesting. I was never a "math person" before, but this class was great and I ended up doing really well! Would love to take him again!
Awesome teacher, super nice and very clear. Would take him again in a heartbeat. I loved his in class experiments/demonstrations.

Class didn't quite go in the direction I was hoping - too much philosophy and linguistics.  Makes statistics even more boring than it already is.  Apart from that, nice guy.  Easy class.  Never had to read.

Easiest class ive ever taken at cornell. The lectures can be a little long and sometimes boring, but a lot of times it also captured my interest. His lecture outlines are great so you dont have to take notes :) Dont read anything for the class you dont need to

the class isn't really as boring as those below me said - the problem is that it would be much better in a 50 minute format rather than 75.  a lot of the material is interesting, tests aren't bad, and he's pretty engaging.  the readings are unnecessary and boring - don't bother.
sleepy time class, good lecture outlines and will listen well in office hours
Going to his lecture is like getting to pay the school for a very uncomfortable place to nap. I've done homework for other classes just to keep me awake.

Excellent prof. Knows his stuff, can present it VERY clearly, and has great notes online (go to class as it's not everything). Light reading for the class (surprising for a class in this field) with fairly easy tests. Good demos in class to keep you interested. Take this class.
He's a fairly good lecturer, and he posts really good notes online so you don't need to take your own at all.

Oceanography is a good class. You learn a lot from it, and the content isn't that difficult if you study, like everyone at Cornell will tell you since this class is famous around campus. I really enjoyed this course with professor Bitar and it made me interested in pursuing the American Studies minor. The class had a decent amount of readings that were all very accessible and posted on Canvas in a reasonable time frame. Additionally, the TA Patrick was also great and he was very educated and knowledgeable about the course. Easy A!

This class is literally "food studies." There is absolutely no reason why this class (essentially an elective course) should have mandatory attendance 3 days/week and a 13-17 page final paper. This class is not important enough to be taking up that much time and commitment out of any student's week and semester. Not sure what Bitar was thinking.

This class is AMST 1110. 
The instruction of assignments is too vague and even flawed. Many of the feedbacks on my work gave me the feeling of "what? She is looking for that?"
Overall, be sure to have your assignment checked by your TA before submitted it. I ran out of space. But the blog post was a big mess at the start of the semester as well.

Very enjoyable course. Grade consists of participation, biweekly blog posts, a few small papers, and a final paper. Papers can be graded harshly but the rest of the assignments pull your grade up in the end.

Bitar is the best professor I've had at Cornell. Extremely passionate about her topic, gives interesting readings (although long), and engages with her students. You're given a lot of freedom to study what you want for the final paper. Too many group tasks for my liking, but overall, the lectures were really incredible.

She assigns a lot of readings and writing assignments, but they're mostly short and also very interesting. She tries to make the class fun, and you can tell she is extremely passionate about the material and making a difference. She is very invested in her students and cares more about what you learn than about how well you write.

Dr. Bitar is really a great professor. She cares about her students and isn't a stickler over little things. In addition, you can get a lot out her classes. I'm not the most "school-person' by any means, but she can you to learn something. Overall, great experience

She's a great professor! The grading for homework assignments and exams is very fair. Most of the assignments were done in groups; lecture attendence is vital. The textbook is needed for the assignments, but not so much for learning the content.

By far the best professor Ive had at Cornell. Besides being an amazing lecturer, she really cares about her students and their well-being. This was clearly evident through the rocky semester we had this fall. Shes extremely fair with her homework assignments and tests. Would definitely take a class with her again.

Hands down best professor I've had at Cornell. Didn't know what a meaningful lecture was until I had her as a lecturer. I only used the textbook as a supplement to study, but it wasn't really necessary. VERY fair exams, not easy, just fair given what we cover in class and on the HW. Actually cares about students & our wellbeing!
Great lecturer, kept people engaged. Homeworks and tests were very fair. Always willing to help/

While the course was not too difficult, I found many things very frustrating. She frequently had to repost homeworks and grades (even edit questions during tests) due to mistakes. I found the homeworks time consuming but not unnecessary. The lectures were sometimes disorganized and the notes (posted afterward) were difficult to read

Her lectures are very clear, the material is engaging but not too difficult. The homeworks and exams are very fair. She clearly cares about her students. She sometimes comes to the next lecture with slides prepared to better answer student questions from the lecture before.
Such a great professor who really cares about people learning!

Lectures were very well organized and easy to follow. Covered a wide range of propulsion topics and went appropriately in-depth with most of them. Weekly homeworks that weren't too difficult, were usually engaging and applicable. Office hours were always very helpful.

Great professor--her lectures were pretty clear, and the exams were fair.

Fine

She is a nice, clear, and overall a friendly professor. Her class, however, is very poorly managed by undergrad TAs. Good and clear teacher, but class is terribly managed.

One of the least skilled Prof I had in my college life. A waste of time to take her course. Just check-out a book from the library and read it.

Great to get to know in person.  There's no textbook, just her notes, so it's kinda hard to study and really have a deep understanding of the material. A lot of time spent in office hours, but probably the best class I've taken at Cornell thus far. Actually felt like I learned something.
She is very dependent on her notes.

2600 is awful, just get through it. 4590 though, is AMAZING. I can't recommend it enough for BEEs. Baeumner is at the top of the biosensors field and it's an extremely rewarding class. She's strict and the course is (very) hard but 100% worth the effort.

There are many office hours for this class, which was helpful for completing homework and case studies. Most lectures have nothing to do with hw or tests. hw deals only w mathematical eq. which arent hard, but she doesnt provide any derivations or explanations, rendering the work useless. 1) no textbook: okay job in teaching but mostly feeds you with a whole bunch of differential equations. class time can be better used otherwise and textbook would do this easily. Not the greatest lecturer, but really helpful and pleasant if you catch her out of class.  Her class gives a good overview of BEE, resonable tests, and pretty good overall.  I can see how some people didn't like her class, but I thought she was pretty good.

Not as bad as previous posts say.   She's an expert in her field (just run a literature search on biosensors) but not the best teacher. Terrible professor.  Not only was she poor at explaining things in lecture, but her exams were way too long, there was no textbook so you have to go to class, and the case studies are just terrible.  Totally unreasonable when it comes to grading the case studies as well.

Grading was a huge problem. I would get a lot of points off for certain things my friends would get none off for, but that was really a TA problem. Terrible at explaining things, directions not clear for what to do on case studies.
Wow, she's mean and intimidating and boring.  Is this what the BEE department wants teaching a opening-welcome-to-the-BEE-department intro class? Geez. I've had enough. Auf weidersehn!

Quite a boring and annoying prof! Killed any interest that I may have had in engineering by a rigid, top-down, teaching methodology. Great prof - gives excellent notes and knows the material well.  She can be intimidating, but her class was very interesting... wish I took it in a year when the lab component was also offered.  I learned a lot.

Antje is extremely organized, prints out nice powerpoint slides for notes, covers a wide range of material and you leave the class feeling like you actually learned something. class avg is pretty high, lots of hmwk thats pretty hard, no outside reading. good prof kind of a tightass but in a good way
I wrote a 3 page evaluation for her. Two of my friends w/ over a 3.8 GPA left the major. And her class can be summarized as the worst experience I've had at Cornell.

Her lectures are her reading differential equations off power point.  Midterm was terrible, and her response was to blame us for not going to office hours enough.

wonderful and useful for real world application

Professor Dietrich makes an effort to know your name and care about you as a student. her class is not hard if you put in effort and she is always available for office hours and stuff

Professor Dietrich is awesome! She does go over lectures a bit quick but as long as you pay adequate attention lectures are not too hard to comprehend. She hosts a lot of office hours and is always accessible. Tests are easy as long as you review quizzes, homework, and practice prelim.

Absolutely horrible. Literally the worst professor I had at Cornell ever. Will never take a class with her again.

Brenda is SUPER sweet. She is easy to understand which is insane because she's speaking in a different language. legend

She is clearly very passionate, however not the most interesting professor I've had. Overall I'd say the class and material was more interesting than the lectures.

She is very knowledgeable and eager to help students. Her lecture slides are well-organized, but her lectures themselves often didn't add to the slides that much. Very nice person. Approachable outside of class. Does not grade harshly. Lectures are confusing and not particularly helpful.

Very nice and passionate professor but his lectures were confusing and hard to follow. Attendance is mandatory but I did not learn much within those lectures. I found doing the readings and going to office hours much more useful. Overall, he is a generous grader if you do the necessary work.
Boring lectures, but he's a chill guy and doesn't grade too hard.

All papers. Your grade lives and dies by the TA. This semester, there was a probably a 1.5 gpa spread between the two TAs and nothing was done about it. I kinda disagree with comments for Professor Nagaraja. I first thought he was not good at teaching. However, as I started to listen carefully what he was talking about in class, I learnt a lot. He's a really nice guy, but an AWFUL professor. Lectures are incredibly disorganized. Very little correlation between readings, lectures, and assignments. TAs do all the work and were pretty short staffed. Do not take him if you do not have to.

Nagaraja seems like a good dude who is interested in the subject matter. However, it is clear that he is uninterested in teaching. Sayama Yu Yu is fantastic. She has instilled in our tiny class a genuine love for the Burmese language. The class uses worksheets rather than an expensive textbook and moves at a manageable pace, so long as you dont slack off.

I loved CEE 5420 with Gadikota. The team projects and in-class interactions were amazing. She is very accessible outside class and cared deeply about my progress. Course was well organized and work load was carefully distributed for a four credit class. Expectations are clear and class participation matters.
Dr. Gadikota is very easy to approach out of class and she gave an extension when I needed it. She supported my request for letters of support outside of class and gave me excellent advice.

I liked the course content and appreciated her support. Exams were very fair and I am glad that we wrapped up the course before the Covid outbreak in December. I have an internship where I will be applying this knowledge thanks to Dr. Gadikota.

Soloway is a very caring professor, and readily easily accessible outside of class. He was always willing to help and discuss course content material. Did not stick to how syllabus said grading would go; polleverywhere grade was not accurate as syllabus specified we could miss 4, just took off points;

great

interesting lectures, but exams are very difficult to study for.

Take advantage of section. There are 3 essays and a final, all extremely easy. The final will likely be short answer and multiple choice/true-false.
Great professor. Lectures are always interesting and quite clear. Very friendly guy, though he is a Phillies fan.

very easy class. essays are easy to write and attendance isnt mandatory. however, you might want to go to class because the final relies heavily on class discussion. overall very easy class to get at least a B in
In-class outlines of the arguments from the text are very helpful.  He makes the material very understandable.
Hard material, but he is very willing to go. Above and beyond to help you.

Took in Fall 2020. Best econ class I took at Cornell. Best mix of interesting content, fair hws and tests, and great teaching. Class is more "mathematical/theoretical", but Ted is fantastic at explaining it all. He's also very approachable and caring, and I appreciated that he put in extra effort to deal with the circumstances at the time. GOAT.
Loved this class. Really interesting material and the math/econ basis isn't difficult. Cool concepts and a great lecturer.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. AEM 2020/PSYCH 2940 was so difficult for no reason. Prelims and the final are 100% of your grade and the tests are extremely hard. For a class that does not even count towards your major, it is not worth it.

His lectures are extremely clear and is very willing to engage with students and answer questions. Despite his ability to explain the concepts very thoroughly and make the content look easy, the material itself is pretty challenging. Tests are challenging but not unreasonable. Definitely take a course with prof OD if you get the chance.

By far the best prof I have had at Cornell! Behavioral Economics was amazing, and his lectures were fascinating. I wish more professors were like him. The class is exactly the right amount of work, and Prof Odonoghue is very accessible during office hours.

Despite the difficulty of the course, Professor O'Donoghue makes his slides very clear and concise. He explains everything in plain language and gives constant reminders on previous materials/terms/equations to jog your memory unlike other professors who just put a bunch symbols without clearly explaining. He is the definition of a good professor.

Literally defines what a professor should be like. I'm doing better in this class than other "easier" classes I'm taking, largely due to how thorough and clear his (actually pretty difficult) lectures are.

The best professor I've had at Cornell so faramazing and engaging lecturer, super accommodating and really organized, makes complicated topics seem easy, and literally one of the top academics in the field of behavioral economics. Definitely take one of his classes if you're an Econ major, he's so great :)

Extremely organized and handled the logistics of this 5-professor course. Super clear in explaining concepts and satisfyingly concise slides. I had no prior econ education but still managed to understand everything. Also helpful during office hours: an incredibly intelligent professor!

Professor O'Donoghue is a pretty good lecturer. When speaking about the material he makes it seem so simple. Only thing is, it's not. This class requires a lot of intuition thinking. Nothing like you've probably learned about in your intro econ courses. Problem sets are fairly short but office hours are key to doing well on them.
The course was really interesting, the exams are challenging though and grades are curved such that the median is a B+. The prof was quite engaging, sections are optional

Awesome professor, again, probably the best I have had in all my econ classes. His lectures are exceptionally clear, which is great, but also kinda makes other professors' lectures seem really not-on-par. The materials are definitely not easy, and going to lectures actually help you learn better.
Awesome! Awesome! Awesome!

Probably the best Econ prof. at Cornell. The class is def. not easy, but if you pay attention in class, work hard on the PSets, and go to office hours, you should be fine. Sections were pointless though, and there is no textbook, but his crystal clear lectures are enough to do well. Would def. recommend this for econ majors

Love this class! Lots of interesting subjects covered, and he certainly knows his material. Even though he posts the slides online, it's recommended to go to class because he shows you how to set up problems (which does not end up the powerpoint). He's also a fairly engaging lecturer. Try your best to do the problem sets without help.

Lecture stuff is online, though lecture will help you understand the slides better than just reading them online. He tests hard, but it's possible to do well if you assimilate to his testing style. PSets i dunno, didn't go to section

I thought the class was a bit boring, but others think it's really interesting.  The professor is very clear.  No textbook, his notes are online, and he gives you a number of problem sets that help you learn the material.  Tests are a bit difficult, but he'll scale grades upwards, so no worries there.

Solid professor and a really nice guy but a few points of caution about the course: the class is curved to a fairly low grade making it difficult to exceed an A- for anything but exceptional performance and possible to achieve a B or lower for decent work; the subject matter is inherently interesting but better dealt with in the realm of psychology

crystal clear lecture notes, posted on blackboard but you have to attend class to get his important additions - no textbook, so you have to go. interesting lecturer, not boring at all and the subject is interesting. good class for fulfilling econ major .

Great lecturer. Very clear and willing to help, the subject material is incredibly interesting. There's no textbook for the class, however, and section was optional and not very helpful. Hence, going to every lecture was inherently mandatory and extremely vital to doing well. Just go to the twice-a-week lecture and you'll be fine.
I love this professor. IMO he is the best econ prof. I have had yet. Keep up the good work prof!

No, seriously, he is the best teacher in the econ department. VERY clear lectures. Light reading, hard problem sets that were graded harshly. Tests seemed fair. Overall grading policy is more than fair. EXTREMELY helpful in office hours - use them. Learned a lot. Must take!!
Best Professor in econ department. Very interesting topics, clear teaching, fair in assessing students' learning
Maybe the best instructor of economics at Cornell. Brilliant, helpful and great to talk to.
No Comments
Great professor. Difficult topics in Econ 302.
Pretty good professor. He gave a very clear teaching!!!
No Comments

Most COMM classes give A-range grades if you work hard, at least by far for all the classes I have taken in last 2 years all ended up with solid A's EXCEPT FOR THIS ONE. There's one prelim and a final (60% of the grade), and the class average for the first prelim was a C+, kinda ridiculous for an intro-level COMM concentration class

Such a nice, cool guy. Social influence and persuasion was one of my favorite classes at Cornell. It is so easy to learn in his class because of the way he lectures. Just has a great and interesting way of speaking about the topic. Def recommend
I really enjoyed this class. He's a clear lecturer, and I feel like we had a fair amount of work. He's kind of cute too

Such a great professor. Thought every lecture had interesting parts even if that day's particular topic happened to be a little boring. Works hard to engage the students and brings sense of humor to keep the class fun. Learned a lot. Big group project throughout the semester but he paces it well so it's never overwhelming.

Probably my favorite professor at Cornell so far. He's funny and engaging, and his love of the material is infectious. There are seven pop quizzes throughout the semester, so you need to be sure to stay on top of the readings. This was the first class he taught here, so keep in mind some of the class structure might change.
Such a relaxing class! Best professor ever! Readings are not much and class materials are quite easy yet fun. No finals but does have a research project which could take some time. Great class.

A very lovable professor that is personable, has quirky style, and a straight-forward lecture. Her powerpoints are usually included on blackboard so that is helpful. Review the slides, readings and handouts exclusively to do well.

Professor Bisogni's really nice. A lot of the class readings are papers that she (and Professor Sobal) published so she definitely has a lot of experience in the field and knows what she's talking about. However, I found material covered in NS 2450 to be mostly common knowledge and the project assignments were pretty time consuming.
A really nice lady. Very involved in a newer area of nutrition research. A great person to get to know.
She is an amazing teacher who helped me with my writing skills and really cares about her students. I loved this class.
Great Professor! Laid back and not demanding. Amazing discussion! Good book discussions.

Prof CBD is awesome!  Take classes with her if you're ready to think and be real about it.  Really engaging, she cares deeply about the work which makes the class discussions more dynamic.  The material and style of this class (Black Women Writers: Book to Screen) was great.

Please stay away if at all possible. She makes it pretty clear that she has no interest in teaching or being at all helpful. Would rather cancel class five times in one semester in order to attend conferences, or spend time writing her next book. Most disorganized class I've ever taken with the most frustrating prof I've ever had.
There were no assignments outside of class, the only grade was at the end of the semester and it was a group project. Barely any work, but very boring.
Best professor, best class
Excellent professor who takes the time to clarify concepts and make civil engineering come alive!
Really nice guy.  The class is easy, just plug and chug.  He knows his stuff.

I chose to take this class after attending the first lecture. Professor Legunsen was engaging right from the start. I struggle to focus through lectures but he found the perfect balance of in class activities and asking questions to keep me engaged. Fantastic professor who clearly puts the effort in and cares about his students.

Great Professor. Very interactive lectures and makes sure to explain the reasoning behind every topic. Relates everything very closely to your future experience as a SWE or SWET. Fair homeworks and exams. Very caring. Only downside is lack of an Ed and the existence of pop quizzes.
Super nice professor, class was graded by 3 homeworks and 1 group project that are all covered thoroughly by class lectures.

The course was great, covering all the interesting topics you want to know about environmental economics. Definitely worth the time. The professor and TA are responsive after class. The only problem is too much homework...

The class was pretty good. Lectures were laidback and informative, the professor himself is very knowledgeable, accessible, and nice. The assignments were also not very difficult, one large project w/ presentation that was simple and several problem sets and one paper, also simple. Learned quite a bit.

loved this class. professor was super nice and knowledgeable and the lectures were laidback and interesting. hardly any work and the work itself wasn't that hard. even if you don't like the material you can just not attend the class and probably do fine. I highly recommend taking, learned a good amount considering the low commitment.

Would not recommend this professor at all. Whatever you believe to be a bonus question, is not that. They grade the bonus questions as if they are just regular questions. The TA often doesn't know what she is talking about. The class is very boring and the homeworks, projects, papers are long and stupid.
Excellent class. Prof rocks.
Excellent teacher. Highly recommended.
Very good teacher. Enjoys teaching.

Bad at giving grades, will never tell you how he grades and how much you scored in the final exams. Not at all transparent. Silly exams and doesn't ask questions according to what he has taught in class.

Wireless networks. Turned out to be a useless course. Did not understand a word he says in the class. He himself gets confused while teaching. Do not waste your money by taking any course under him. I strictly advise you to do not go for his course. You will regret it.
Worst class taken.

He makes a lot of mistakes and writes sloppily. Can hardly understand the words he says. HWs take long time and exam is tough unless you're from China. Would not recommend this class as an elective. No help during OH and he doesn't seem to know the material well.

Took both 310 and 566 with him.  I'm a junior in ECE right now and would say he's the best professor I've had in ECE.  Always makes sure to stop if students seem confused, and always reviews the last lecture's material at the beginning of class.  Will have some tough homeworks and tests but he is a fair grader and is always very helpful.

He might be a little disorganized during lectures, but he will always slow down to make sure everyone understands everything. Prof Haas is good at giving "hand-waving" arguments which provided the intuition, unlike some other prof who just dump the math on you.
nice prof. tries his best to have students learn the material, however the classes is not dumbed down.

The funniest class I took. Not because he's funny, but because he managed to cover up for all the mistakes he did during class by affecting a 'i knew that' attitude. His tests were so simple (at least, the first two were...). TA's are extremely helpful to go to. Homeworks were annoying hard at times. Class is overall easy.

Professor Giles may seem clueless, but if you actually get to know him and ask him for help in office hours or one on one settings, you'll find that he really knows what is going on and he knows his stuff.

Make sure you take repro before you take this class, or you're going to be on the bottom of the median. Dr. Giles is extremely nice and happy to explain anything. He is open to many perspectives in his course and is happy to look into new research to change his slides. He is lenient and knows how stressed his students are about vet school.

Professor Giles is the nicest guy that you'll ever meet.  He really cares a lot about his students and is more than willing to give them extra help.  His lectures are somewhat dry and go on forever, but the material is not hard.  If you've taken ANSC 2400 (Repro), you'll be fine for this class. The quizzes are super easy.  Great 1 credit class.
Love Giles. Sometimes a little spacey but generally a good guy that wants his students to do well.
He's clueless but tries.

Giles is sooo sweet. He truly cares about the students and makes an effort to learn everyone's name and something about them-even for a large lecture. Although he appears to be a little absent minded sometimes, if you have a one-on-one conversation with him, he really knows his stuff.

Giles is the nicest guy ever.  He is so sweet and makes an effort to learn everyones name, even in a 100 person lecture hall and 4 teachers taking turns lecturing.  The class is not hard, and Giles is very fair.

Christopherson is an excellent instructor. She's incredibly knowledgeable and engaging, and stimulates very interesting conversations and debates. I went into this class knowing nothing about economic development (and not being all that interested) and left with a thorough understanding of economic development issues and a desire to keep learning.
Has a lot of experience in Econ Development and uses examples from across the world to illustrate her point.

This was a very tough class - definitely take an intro programming course first. The lectures moved super fast and were confusing, but Giles was super helpful in office hours and on Piazza. The problem sets took a long time but weren't too difficult once you understood all the directions. Past knowledge of every math course is expected- be prepared
Super tough material imo but looking back hte lectures were really good. HW and exams were pretty hard. going to lab helps w/ the hw.

He's a very clear and organized lecturer IMO. I think the topics are somewhat math-heavy, which is why a lot of students (including me) struggled. I agree that HW has typos and sometimes isn't clear. But if you check Piazza you'll find the answer you're looking for. He's very helpful during OH as well. Material is also pretty interesting to me.

I completely agree with the review right below - he completely destroyed my interest in the subject area. His lectures are dry, and his assignments are full of mistakes (major ones). He sent out 7 emails for "clarifications" of his mistakes for the last assignment - none of which helped in any way. Also - his lectures literally do not do anything.

Handwriting completely illegible and notation inconsistent, unable to understand when students were confused. Mean on the midterm was in the 50s and he did not seem to care. Would be best if he was kept away from undergraduates. Nearly destroyed my interest in the subject matter.

All the classes he teaches are pretty difficult and have dull material (4030, 4520). The hws take so long! Need to go to office hours to get lots of help. Lectures are also boring and there's often typos (esp in 4030). However, he does care about his students and makes the median an A-.

I took STSCI 4110 in Spring 2018. The class could be insanely difficult if don't have strong R and statistics background. The HW and take-home exam are hard and long. If you have a strong background in statistics, you will love this class as he taught many modern topics in statistics.

4030 is insanely difficult, where the first prelim median was around a 30. However, Giles curves tremendously so that the class median comes out to an A-. I was confused the entire semester, but still walked away with a B+. He's also hilarious in class and a genuinely good professor and person.

Giles is a cool professor and willing to help you if you're struggling to understand the course material. I've never felt intimidated by him when I asked him questions. STSCI 4030/5030, however, was HARD. Both the problem sets and exams were challenging. Make sure you have a solid understanding of Linear Algebra before taking the class...

I get A+ from his class. His lecture is not very well organized and tend to be typos. The lecture is very theoretical. Homework and exam tend to be difficult and hard to understand what's he asking for. However, if you dedicate your time to this class, you will learn a lot. Also, he's very helpful during office hour and active on Piazza.

Contents are not useful but it makes your life the hardest ever. I began to doubt myself because studying does not help me to solve problems at all. He loves trick, deep, theoritical stuff. He assigns homework in a free style, typos appears a lot and he asks questions in a way that no one understands. His class does nothing with homework and exams.

Finest professor at cornell.  Had him for civil pro, evidence and trial tactics.  Went that extra mile for me and concepts from him are still with me after 30 years of practicing law.  He and Clermont were in a league by themselves.
Had him 20 years ago.  Best professor I had in law school. Crystal clear.  Extremely helpful.  A model professor.  If you get him for Civ Pro, thank your lucky stars . . . then take him for Evidence.
marvelous teacher.  always prepared, knows his subject cold.
No Comments
No Comments
rossi is brilliant.  class is engaging and he clearly explains everything.  warning: he only calls on the first few rows of students so be ready.
There was a quiz for every class so that she could know how well we learned. There were three reports but no exams. The course isn't easy and has lots of work to do, but it's worth it! Not that hard!

I'm an ILR major, so to be fair, I suck at math, but this class made me want to pull out my teeth. 

For a 9 am class, she graded iclickers based on accuracy, so you needed to do well during class, as it went on. It was ridiculous, and stressful, and she would make fun of us for getting stressed.
Not good

Worst professor ever, 

Try to switch professors

Kind of neutral on this one -- prof was nice enough but grading/curriculum was really disorganized, and quizzes often had irrelevant questions that we could've been better prepared for. Didn't read the textbook at all and the TAs/sections were a lot more helpful than lectures. However, Karns is clearly a great person who cares about her students!
I will start this review by saying I'm not good at math at all. But nonetheless, not a good professor. Extremely neurotic about cheating and creates a toxic environment with iclickers

She's a horrible human being. She assigned last minute a pretty big essay in replacement to a much easier final assignment just in spite of us. She accused us (a class of somewhere around 400 students) of cheating, even though a lot of people are assigned the same exact data with the same exact prompt, so of course everything is gonna be similar.
Super nice and cares about her students. quizzes are super easy and there are few assignments

This site doesn't let me swear because lol I wrote a scathing review before this. Just know that taking her class is tough man, its really tough. Bad situation to be in. She is a terrible teacher, you won't learn a whole lot of stats I promise you. Peace.
Not cooperative. Doesn't listen to feedback. This class aint it. Unless its a requirement, don't take.

My god they need some better ilr stats teachers. Easy class but she's kind of an awful person, super rude to TAs as well. Explicitly said she's only at cornell to do research so don't expect her to care about intro classes. Soooo many spelling and conceptual errors on her tests and you have to fight for the points back. If not in ILR don't take.

She doesn't know how to communicate, is rude, and expects you to teach yourself. If you want to be stressed out and up late trying to figure out the directions for an assignment even after asking her a multitude of questions about it, then this is the class for you! If not then I would highly suggest taking a course w/a professor who communicates

Worst professor I have ever had. She does not care if you fail. She does not care if you are confused or struggling. She is extremely disinterested and rude. I was excited for statistics and she completely ruined my experience with it. The worst experience I have ever had with a professor. Please, if you can, do not take her class.

This professor does an excellent job at teaching the material and making it easy to understand. That said, she makes constant errors with grading which become frustrating very quickly.  Additionally, she comes off as an extremely rude and uncaring individual, who has absolutely no interest in interacting with her students.
Professor Karns truly cares about all of her students. She wants all of her students to succeed. She teaches in a way that makes statistics easy to understand

Karns is clear and concise when it comes to teaching statistics. However, she is genuinely one of the meanest professors I've met. She doesn't show anyone respect. Not the students, not the TAs. She's passive-aggressive for literally no reason.

Karns has been the MOST frustrating professor. She makes many mistakes with grading and writing questions with appropriate answers, which is fine, but she doesn't take accountability. Fought her on a test question for weeks before she realized she was wrong. All the points I have lost in the class is because of her incompetence.
I could pour days into this class and get nothing out of it.

Karns is a good professor, beware of the participation requirements for section and iclickers. She tries her best to make sure that a huge lecture hall of students is set up for success and does explain things in fairly simple terms. If you miss class, 25% of your grade is participation, more than a single test, so beware of 8:40AM's.

I really like Karns. She's surprisingly accessible for such a large class, more than willing to not count exam problems that stumped a lot of the class, and is really a nice, really bright person. Each of the 3 tests is in-class (including final) and if you do the (very brief) readings, no reason you can't get at least an A-.

Statistics can be difficult, but Professor Karns helps any student is that is willing to work and tries to understand the material. She is a brilliant and has an interesting perspective on statistics. I would highly recommend her class.

Easy stats class. Trust me when I say to read ahead of time and do practice problems BEFORE the lecture. She can go fast but if you read before lecture then the entire class will be a breeze. Her lectures are clear. Seriously read and do practice problems ahead of time and ask questions when you need to and she will give you that A.

Prof. Karns would go over previous lectures if she felt like we, as a class, didn't quite understand the concept. The exams were ALL MULTIPLE CHOICE and quite easy. The best way to get an A in this class is to go to most of the lectures and practice some problems. This has to be the easiest stats class at Cornell! Would I recommend: UM, YES!
I swear nobody understood anything during lecture. She would breeze over concepts that left me feeling more confused about life after each session.

I learned literally nothing from this class. Stats is supposed to be a math class and somehow we were only tested on random irrelevant concepts found in the book. Stats is a pretty important subject, used in most fields so even if another stats is harder, I recommend taking that class instead.

Karn's is one of the nicest professors I've had but she reads off the slides word for word and has no idea how to help you if you come to her outside of class and tell her that you're confused. The class is only easy for non-ILR kids who were too lazy to take a real math class so be prepared to struggle if you're not already great at statistics
Really easy A- course, but can't do much better than that. Only 30 multiple choice questions per exam so misread 2 questions per exam and say good bye to your A.
Solid class. Never needed textbook. Homework problems assigned but not mandatory/necessary. Allowed to bring two pages of cheat sheets to exam. Boring lectures but doable exams.
Why do I need over a 95 for an A...???
Professor Karns genuinely cares about her students. If you study, you will do well. She serves as a role  model to all other professors at Cornell.

Professor Karns is very good at teaching statistics and making it about as easy as possible for everyone to do pretty well. However, her grading criteria is slightly confusing and a 95% (out of 100 with little to no extra credit) is required to receive an A.

Lots of assignments, in class and out. She reads from premade slides of statistics but still manages to do so with a fair bit of enthusiasm. It seems like an easy class and it kind of is, but the grading criteria for the assignments is very fuzzy and it's almost certain you will get points off for some reason or another.

Great class. At times here presentation and exceptions of the course can be a bit unorganized. However, she goes above and beyond to make sure help students learn. She truly cares for her students and is more than fair. I would recommend to any one who is interested/ has to take stats.

I have no idea how she taught this course before this semester, but I can tell that she did a horrible job this spring. She made no sense during lectures, just read the slides out loud. But what makes this course unbearable is that the 3rd prelim turned out to be a nightmare for both the TAs and the students.

She makes NO sense during lecture. I went to lecture every single time and her lectures were hard to follow, especially when she stopped using the powerpoints. She seemed to confuse herself and couldn't even perform some basic math operations. I learned more in section, from the book, and the online problem sets.

Concepts are presented very clearly and assignments are given to increase understanding. Exams are very fair and you can makes notes sheets to bring into the prelims/final. The grading scheme is very clear so you can keep track of how you're doing. You don't do math and its easy to do well. She does not give out out A+ grades though
She is an alright professor who conveys fairly simple concepts. Exams are more than fair. She genuinely wants students to do well and gives lots of chances. Not a difficult class at all.

It's clear that she's a very nice person and cares a lot about her students. I like how she does not emphasize the calculation too much but rather the concepts behind. Grading is tough though - if you miss 7 multiple choice questions on the exam you'll end up with an A- overall. Try to go to class as she gives extra credit assignments.

Karns is awesome. She is down-to-earth and makes learning statistics interesting by focusing on interpreting stats rather than nit-picky calculations. Her exams are MC--very easy if you know what is going on. And if you don't, she is very approachable. She ends class early to answer questions/go over more problems for those who want clarification.
I'll just say, I had to drop the class.
Professor wants to see students succeed.  The tests are multiple choice and pretty straight forward.  She is helpful.  Did not find TAs useful though.
Karns was great. She constantly applied the statistics to real world scenarios to make the class interesting and relevant. She wants you to do well and will meet with you for however long you need.

Karns isn't that smart, but she knows her statistics.  The class really doesn't get very technical at all, but her tests are so easy.  My only gripe is she only gives A+'s to people above 100 in the class.

Professor Karns is so awesome. She presents the information in an interesting way and is extraordinarily helpful. Aside from that she is a fascinating individual. I never thought statistics could be this much fun.

Professor Karns is amazing in this class. Because the class is small, it really allows for discussion, and Karns encourages it. She has great criticism and really wants to help students. More than that, she wants to get to know students. Go to office hours, participate in class, be open, and this class will be one of the best you take at Cornell.
While professor Karns' lectures might lack in clarity or some technical aspects, she is an incredibly kind and helpful individual. Just got to her office hours.
Moisey is a great professor and he makes the course content interesting and engaging. The teaching team is very accommodating. Would definitely recommend to people even if they are non-majors.

Took this as a distribution requirement, and was definitely one of my more interesting ones. Classes at the beginning are definitely a little more boring, but second half was where I felt things got more interesting/relevant. Very easy class, Moisey also made attending lecture interesting even if the content was hit or miss for me. Funny guy

Moisey is such a funny and engaging lecturer. This class opens your eyes in ways few others do. ATTEND LECTURE, ALWAYS. Do the readings (they can be dense/long, but that's where lecture comes in). If you take diligent notes & review them before the exam so that you're familiar with the order of material, you'll do great (open-note exams).

By far the best class I have ever taken at Cornell (and I think the best one I ever will take). He's the most engaging, enthusiastic, and humorous lecturer and he really makes you care about the material. You will leave every class with your mind blown.

Best class I have taken at Cornell. Goes beyond "Visual Studies" and explains everyday life. Moisey is an engaging lecturer and totally hilarious. Really cares about what he teaches. The first few readings are weed out but it gets more interesting after that. Definitely don't do the final paper at the last minute. Easy grading.
Fantastic professor. Fantastic class. You will never be bored in lecture, and you will leave with many things to think about.
Really great class. Do the readings, participate in lecture discussions, attend the out of class events, and put effort into the major paper.

My favorite course I have taken. Highly interdisciplinary-- covers many potentially weighty theoretical and philosophical topics. The majority of the grade is a 15 page research paper, which he insists on being an intervention -- asking and answering a question that begs both. He is hilarious, and he wants you to care about the class. Approachable.
Don't do it!

Dr. Ahmann is incredible. Not only is she a knowledgeable, and passionate anthropologist, but she also is relatable and approachable. She even took the time to speak to me about my interest in switching to anthropology as a major. Her lectures were Ted Talk quality and grading was more than fair. Couldn't recommend taking her classes highly enough!

The class is interesting but Prof. Ahmann often uses language that can be confusing for a person who has not taken an anthro class before. Her slides are helpful so I recommend taking notes. I also think the readings were a little tough but attending discussion helps (Attendance is mandatory for discussion). You can bring notes to exams which helps
Very intelligent professor who gives well put together lectures. Make sure to take notes in class because lecture slides aren't posted.

Organized and enthusiastic professor. Very accessible and we had individual meeting sign ups with her for our papers too which shows she cared. I'm not particularly interested in anthropology but the material for Time Travel was pretty interesting.

Had her for a FWS on time travel. The nature of the class meant it was really reading heavy but they were all interesting and nothing felt like busy work. She took the time to get to know her students and clearly cared about our wellbeing. I would reccomend
Dr. Bauerle was pretty laid back. The classroom wasn't the best I agree but that has nothing to do with the class. We got to actually handle plants and I liked the hands-on approach.

Don't ever take this class agree with the person below.
Each lab session felt like years lost in a fluorescent-lit basement. My love for plants withered in the sterile, chemical-filled atmosphere. The physical dehydration mirrored a profound, academic drought. The experience was akin to solitary confinement, isolating and disheartening.

Not bad but every time I leave Lab I feel I have lost three years of my life, am all of a sudden chronically dehydrated and feel like I have just been released from a month of solitary confinement. If you truly love plants and have a special place in your heart for the florescent lit, espestlce filled basements take this class.
Engaging activities to learn the material and even free plants to take home.
This class was great. The class is mostly based off of activities so you are never sitting still.
I really liked this class. it is laid back enough that you don't have massive anxiety but you also discuss interesting topics and learn a lot about plants. I recommend.

Horrible. Never take any of her classes unless you absolutely have to. Her lectures are partial summaries of textbook chapters. Very disorganized lectures and course content. Very bad sense of humor and does not communicate with students respectfully. However, this was genuinely the easiest class I have taken at Cornell.

She has changed the layout of the course:  papers and multiple quizzes. Perosio was wonderful to see 3 days a week and she genuinely cares about her students. Definitely would recommend this course. Easy to get an A. Quizzes based on textbook and lectures but taken on blackboard and can take with friends. The paper is 1 page. EASY AND FUN.

This professor is the definition of a power trip. She does not care about any single student and will not accept anything late or have the compassion to help you if you have any personal problems. Take this course if you can turn things in on time and the credits but expect the most ambiguous quiz questions that will have no concrete answer.

It's important to pay attention during lecture since all the things that she tests are from her lecture slides. Her tests are EXTREMELY easy; many students get A+. There is a group project. I got randomly assigned to a team and a TA. Luckily my teammates were very cooperative, and my TA was amazing! Prof P will help all of her students to get an A.

Here's how to be successful in this class. Skim the textbook chapter before lecture but don't waste actually reading it. Take notes during lecture!!! and write down examples. All the information in the course can boiled down to a bunch of lists and charts. These lists and charts will in form be on the prelims. Not a hard class but study.

Unfair grading policies: peer evaluations throughout the semester that do not benefit your grade, yet not turning them in on time means a three point deduction from your final grade in the course! Her tests are very difficult and require no insight, only rote memorization, and most guest speakers brought in did not supplement learning.

The class is very poorly organized. She doesn't post any notes and her online Friday's are a total waste of time. It's not an Ivy League level class. She doesn't really care about the class and the students.

She's quite ignorant about her subject as can be seen at how awfully she answers questions. Every piece of material in this class is generic, common sense, or bs jargon. It's a shame that an ivy league's business school has such an ignorant marketing professor. She also made various factually incorrect statements about many international countries.

This is a review for Prof. P, not for AEM 2400. She is an OK lecturer, but can be shrilly and unfocused at times. She is extremely unprofessional- frequently failing to respond to emails, constantly making typos in both her exams and in lecture, and runs the class in a disorganized manner. The TA's were super unhelpful, don't bother with office hrs

This was my first marketing experience and it really shocked me how easy it was. Professor P kept us on track and taught us how to be organized so overall it was an easy and rewarding experience if you paid attention and did your work.v

Too much work for 2 credits even if it ends two weeks early and there's no final. Find a good group and its easy to get a good grade. You don't learn anything but it is good 'teamwork experience' to talk about for interviews.

Material is rather easy- if you go to lectures you will do reasonably well in the class. That being said, she was a very frustrating professor. Some slides and test questions bordered on being incomprehensible due to grammatical errors. She was very little help to me in office hours, and had to rely on her own powerpoint slides to answer questions

despite what some might say, its honestly a very easy class to do well in. must go to lecture and guest lectures as she puts several questions from it on prelims. unless she says otherwise, study all the chapter practice questions she posts as MANY are re-used on prelims. some questions are subjective but she lets you get 3-4 wrong without penalty

2400 & 2410: You need to go to class, she brings in speakers and puts questions on the test that you will NOT get right with just TakeNote. You need to memorize the keywords from all the chapters and know the diagrams from the text for the test. She cant write tests for her life - makes grammer mistakes and repeats choices on MC. DO THE DERBY!!
Class was pretty hard, interesting material and professor but had to work very hard for my B+.

Prof. Perosio bases her class on four tests (three required) that ask detailed questions about book material and any guest speakers she brings in. One must therefore memorize heavily to do well. Prof. Perosio herself is one of the few teachers you'll find that genuinely cares about her students. She does love the athletes a bit too much, though. :|

By far the worst professor I've had at Cornell.  Unprofessional and unfair.  Seems to know all athletes by name and has no concern for other students.  Grading is biased, based on whether you play a sport.  Would not meet with me for help, instead telling me to contact a TA.  Judging by other reviews here, is two-faced.  Absolutely horrible.

This class is easy and gives you the basics for marketing. That said, Professor P conducts the least intellectual class I've attended at Cornell. There is no need to do any thinking in this class, just memorize what she says and you'll get an A
She's a great professor.  Lots of fun and really understanding.

Grades ENTIRELY based on TA and the project you get. If you get a hard TA you're basically screwed. My team's TA was not very helpful and graded very unfairly. Also, he basically allowed another group to steal our ideas. Perosio does nothing in the class except for passing a stupid ball around every class and screams at people.
Had her last semester. Extremely rude. Dont even bother dealing with her if you don't have to do.

This professor is probably the best I've had at Cornell.  She teaches a wonderful class that is easy so long as you do your work, this is Cornell.  She is very helpful and approachable.  She is a Cornell grad and is very understanding of her students.  She gives extra credit opportunities and will drop the lowest exam grade.  Easy to do well.
class should be easy but she is accusatory about written projects, which were annoying and pointless. Tests are easy but if you dont study the right material your screwed. Its a toss up

Course was easy, not difficult to follow if you attend lectures and jot as much notes as you can from the professor's mouth.  Tests are based on what she taught and not necessarily what is in textbook.Grading is ridiculous since it solely depends on TA's moods and arguing for points is nearly impossible and often accustory; an okay class at best.

Lots of energy - keeps your attention during lectures. Very fair grading system - 3 prelims and a final, the lowest one is dropped. Test questions were dumb though, tested memorization rather than understanding - study and do the practice questions and you'll do well.

Very unreasonable and unfair teacher.  Makes students hand in completely useless assignments during class and gives 0's to students who are sick or at home for emailing in the completed assignment.  Easy course but bad professor. Straight textbook/lecture slides memorization needed for A

Her lectures were OK, but the assignments were all useless and stupid. The marketing audits were graded by subjective TAs and they determine how many points to take off depending on their mood of the day. Tests were mostly multiple choice and do not test your understanding of marketing, rather how well you memorized the textbook and her examples.
Great professor who is very enthusiastic about the subject! Lectures are always interesting, and she explains all important concepts. Keep up with the reading and you'll do well.
Her class is not crystal clear or the easiest, but once you understand how she grades, you'll do fine. Also, make sure you write more on tests, it will be more helpful to your grade.
Perosio is extremely bad, useless, and biased professor. There is a reason she teaches marketing instead of applying her knowledge to the real world. (hint: she has no knowledge)

Our grades are based entirely on OPINION.  Prof P is not professional.  I don't know how she teaches at an Ivy League institution...  She belongs @ a Community College.    I'm not even a disgruntled student.. I have an 96 Average. Most work you will ever do for a 1 credit class IN YOUR LIFE! Perosio completely ignored our group presentation at the showcase even though we were second overall in the class.

Professor Perosio is an extemely biased individual and has unprofessional qualities, such as forming personal opinons on students and grading likewise. The TAs grade you, which is awful (I dont know what Prof P does even). Our TA was one of the dumbest students in our major and graded us. This class is terrible and so is she.

Perosio is okay.  She does what she needs to do as a prof.  This major problem is that if you have a problem with the TA. Perosio fine, acceptable, energetic, tried to make the class seem worthwhile.
