Is it fair to be graded by students dumber or more incompetent than youself? This unfortunately required 1 credit class consumes your life

This class proved to be completely fruitless. Teams were assigned, grading was biased and unpredictable, and worst of all, the content was poorly incorporated into the curriculum. It's a required course...unfortunately.
She is awsome! Lots of chances for extra points and she is always there to help you. Do the journal, it does take a lot of time but its worth the A+ in the class.
She makes lecture interesting and never dull.  But she won't give out extensions on papers.

miserable class but awesome prof.  she's great, knows her stuff and always willing to help.  she'll only help if you ask though, don't expect her to come to you.  whenever i asked her for help she gave me everything i needed to get me on the right track.

The class is hard and a lot of work, but she does a good job making it worthwhile, and offers extra credit. Probably gets a bad reputation from the class being a lot fo work, but she's a good professor and the class is worthwhile.

I really hate this woman. She made me want to quit the major, transfer schools, do anything to be away from her snide approach to teaching a 1 credit class that she makes seem like its a 4 credit engineering class.
No Comments

Hard to please. TAs were awful, they treated students with no respect. Prof taught class like we were middle schoolers, but graded class like it was a 400 level 4 credit course. Would not take students' suggestions. Oblivious to fact that class was so frustrated they were on the verge of a coup.
very nice person, terrible choice of ta's, ta's were incompetant and contradictory. Learned nothing, and gained nothing, sad for cornell.
Wonderful, interesting professor- learned a lot!
No Comments
She is a great person.

She rambles A LOT. The entire class consisted of her "lecturing" which wasted the opportunity to discuss in the small class. She was fun and interesting at times, but usually very boring. Worst of all, there were very few grades. I never knew how I was doing in the class. I feel that my grade did not reflect my knowledge of the material accurately.

Debra is great.  Her lectures, although tangential most of the time, are really insightful and interesting.  She is super helpful one on one, so definitely take advantage of that.  Rarely gives back papers, but when she does her comments are attentive and good.  You can tell she has read your paper, but she won't give them back..?  Take her class

Professor Fried is absolutely brilliant! She is also extremely helpful if you approach her during the office hour. With so much credential under her belt, she has an extraordinary patience as a lecturer and often infuses the supposedly boring lecture with rare insights. She might possibly be one of the English professors at Cornell.

Haha oh, Debra... the type of professor who's so off the wall, you take for granted how insightful her lectures are. She's an engaging lecturer in a very bizarre way and unintentionally hilarious. I enjoyed her class, but it sometimes made me want to die. Regardless, she made boring rennaisance literature interesting, which is a tough thing to do.
Brilliant.

the material and assignments were not very difficult, there were very large amounts of reading. i didn't enjoy the class because she never handed anything back and i got very frustrated. my self control was barely up to the challange of not having a giggle fit every time she started foaming at the mouth whilst speaking middle english.

What others have said about assignments being handed back late was true, but on the plus side, several of the assignments were never assigned at all!  I thought the lectures were generally very interesting, and Fried had lots of insight into the trickier bits.  Also, she does respond to emails.
what everyone else said, basically. That class could've been really good, but she never returned anything.

Fried is a really good lecturer, but this semester she slacked off.  The TA did most of the grading and handed papers back really late because he had so much to do.  The midterm was returned THE DAY BEFORE THE FINAL!!!  The class could have been good, but Fried's poor communication limited it.

I signed up for this class extremely interested and intending to take the next course in the sequence (202), but after this semester there is absolutely no way I will take 202 while Fried teaches it.  I still haven't gotten any of my papers back.  Take 201-2 when someone else teaches it.

One of the worst professors I've had.  She knows her stuff and seems very intelligent, but she never gave us our assignments on time or returned any of our papers, even when we were supposed to revise them!
She taught me how to figure out verse in poetry. It wasn't until afterwards that I learned how brilliant and accomplished she is, thinking back on it she had the patience of a saint.
Fried is one of the most erudite and accomplished professors here.

You will get yelled at and might get hit by Nero, but keep asking questions and don't give up. She's definitely there to help you but you need to put in the other half of the work. She'll push you and is not afraid of whacking you on the head to get you to learn.

Not a nice person. I honestly believe she enjoys handing out low grades just because this university doesn't care. If you don't need to take this class but you still enroll, your parents should have sent you to a mental hospital instead of Cornell.

Nero was the worst professor that I have ever had. The genetics course was neither well -organized nor well paced.  The tests were beyond what had been presented in class, and the hw was impossible. This is the only class where 0/100 is a possible exam grade (with studying). Nero curses people during OH and  leaves them feeling confused and stupid.

Debbie isn't the softest of people, but she cares if you do. If you are intimidated by her style, try scheduling a one-on-one meeting with her. She will push you to understand. The only warning I have is that her normal speaking voice outside of her office is approximately lecture-hall enunciation. Don't pick your friends as lab partners, really.

Dr. Nero is the most "unconventional" teacher I've had, to put it mildly. I must admit, her explanations are exceptionally clear, as long as you can filter the genetics from the cursing. Lab is a time-guzzling course, and there's atrocious communication between the TAs and students. It's very unclear what they want. You must go to office hours.

Dr. Nero is extremely intimidating and her last name equates her to the terrors of the same Roman Emperor.  She is extremely abrasive and old-fashioned, which some people like, and others do not.  She wants you to understand the material, and if you show appreciation for her and her subject, she will take a direct interest in you!!
The lab takes up a lot of time and she is hard grader. Other than that she is very helpful and knows her stuff very well.

Cornell is the heart of classic genetics. This is the bread and butter course for the discipline. It shouldn't be easy and it isn't. Nero will help you, but she won't drag you around like a puppy. You have to work for it like an adult, if you do that, she'll show you the way to success. Go to every office hour and lecture you can. Good luck!
She is awful

Dr. Nero is the best. Very helpful and is an incredible professor. Might seem intimidating at first, but if you're lucky enough to get to know her, she is an incredibly sweet lady. She made genetics understandable and fun.

Nero manage to teach with clarity despite teaching a difficult subject. She can be intimidating esp with her loud voice but she's really trying to help you. Don't feel intimidated and ask questions bc she's your best resource.
a lot of screaming involved in the early morning. her problem solving is a must if you want to do well in genetics. lab is hands down the worst class i've taken at cornell
VERY helpful if you just ignore the fact that she's yelling

Intimidating during problem solving sessions but quite approachable during one-on-one interactions. Knows the problems cold and can offer clear and succinct explanations of any problem in the textbook/lab/prelims

You'll either hate or love Nero-- she keeps you awake at 8am. Her PS sessions are gold if you want to do well in the class, and she'll jump through hoops to help you (it's just that her delivery needs work). Labs will suck away your time and are hard, but if you go to office hours every week (yeah, EVERY week) you'll do really well.
Probably the best teacher I've had at Cornell. Made me remember and truly learn the material.
She can be intimidating at first because of the screaming, but once you get past that she's great. Go to her problem solving sessions if you want to do well in genetics.

You will either immediately hate or love Dr. Nero, she has a big personality: her main form of communication is screaming and she cusses like a sailor, all this aside, she is an excellent professor, problem solving is good for understanding concepts but not necessary to do well in the course (that is based on pure luck). This course will be hell!

Her class is like a soccer game: you can't cram study the night before and expect to do well. Practice, book problems and problem solving!! Nero's as sharp as a tack and an understanding of the material that's backwards and forwards. GO TO OFFICE HOURS AND PROBLEM SOLVING. She's exceptionally willing to help!

As a personal rule, I don't respect anyone that doesn't respect me and HATE Dr. Nero. All the worst qualities of professor rolled into one. Students that like her must be masochistic, or unaware of the respect they deserve as human beings.

I don't understand how anyone would want to talk to this lady. She is one of the only few professors at school who represent everything I hate about people.  Terribly useless, she is abrasive for no real reason.  Not how a good teacher behaves.
The Dr. Cox of Genetics.

Her idea of teaching is swearing and screaming. However, if you can get past these characteristics, you will realize she's very well articulated in the class material. Her Problem Sets prepare you for the exams (the PS are much harder). And if you do answer in Problem Solving Session, we ready for screaming. Just take it and keep asking questions.

Scary as hell at 8:30am in problem solving, but very pleasant in office hours. Either way, she helps you understand genetics concepts and problem solving at a much higher level than what's presented in class (quote-"This is deep s*** guys!") Her problem solving packets are challenging but excellent. Wants you to MASTER genetics, not learn it so-so.

She's good at explaining, but she can be intimidating, good at one on one sessions. You don't need to go to her Problem solving sessions to do well in Genetics, but you should do the Problem sets (copies in Bio learning centre). Also, get your hands on previous exams at all costs. Lab should not be a requirement, waste of time.

This woman is sooo freakin funny. Yeah she may seem scary and mean if you say the wrong thing, but really its all very loving and quite hilarious. She corrects people by yelling and making them feel a bit dumb, but boy you'll understand it when shes through. Shes very sweet and helpful if approached 1 on 1. Shes just a teddy bear, dont be scared.
I don't know if she's the one who wrote the exams, but whoever did clearly has a limited understanding of basic probability, ex: P(A given B) is not the same as P(A and B) for Christ's sake!

DEBBIE IS AWSOME.. if i had not heard about how scary she was , i would have approached her 50000 times more than i did ... the times i did approach her ,,, she was excellent ,.. really knows the material well ..if u use her office hrs regualurly ,, u will definitwly do well .. she has an awsome prsonality !
Debbie is amazing!  She will stick it to you and make you hate yourself for trying to answer the question, but then she will drill it into you and you will never get it wrong again.  Kudos!

She may be a bit rough around the edges, but she'll bend over backwards to help you when you really need it. Think of it as tough love. If you put in a little effort, she helps genetics go by much easier.
Excellent at explaining concepts. Sometimes wish she was the main Genetics prof...

nero is crazy.  if you don't know something she'll attack you.  if you do know it, she'll love you forever.  she is one of the best at cornell.  she teaches the problem solving portion of the course.  so if you wanna pass  genetics, go to the problem solving sessions, she's awesome.

she's scary as hell, but a great teacher, and if you go to every one of her review sessions and do all her problem sets, you will do well in Genetics. Also she will totally stand up for you if you have guts enough to talk to her
She's crazy and intimidating but if you know your stuff she'll actually respect you.
Awesome teacher!  Did anyone notice that she wears one long earing and one short earing all the time?
No question: she's crazy. But as a teacher, she's pure gold.
Has a lot of attitude and very pushy. However, other than the fact that her sections are rediculously early in the morning, she is very effective in making you learn.
she acts like she is on speed all the time. she is out of her mind.

I agree, biology students should definately not have to take this lab

Very intimidating. You better know your stuff when approaching her or she will tear you apart. However, very effective lecturer, very energetic, enthusiastic, dirty mind/mouth, and loud. Once you get over the initial shock, she explains things well.

Debra Nero is hilarious.  Even though she is not a tenured proffessor because she would rather teach then do research, she is the best teacher I have ever had at Cornell.  I could skip lecture and just go to her problem solving sessions and do just fine.
nero is awesome!  she really knows how to teach and she's got a great wit.  (love the earring, doll)

Okay, so she is a little eccentric. However, you have to admit that she knows her material well and does a great job of teaching it! And so what if she cusses? It actually makes me remember the material!

c'mon people, get over yourselves.  Don't blame her for a tough course.  She is a little crazy, but a great teacher, and the only one who cares if we understand material or not!  I give her, not professor, credit for most of material i learned!
Terrible CC for a terrible, meaningless course

Being a student at an Ivy League school, I DO NOT appreciate being demeaned, insulted, and mistreated by some bio-crazed woman on a powertrip. Her swearing and unprofessional behavior is unbecoming of such a prestigious department. STAY AWAY FROM HER.

My parents did not pay $34,000 to have some woman yell cuss words in my face at 8 am.It's very unprofessional to act this way, especially since we are an Ivy League school.However, these sessions are essential if you want to pass genetics. Info is clear.

She's pretty scary in her review sessions, but she does a really great job of teaching you the material. She's much nicer outside of that setting. Why does she always wear a post earring in one ear, and a dangly one in the other? I don't get it!

I hate this class, I hate this class, I hate this class.  Takes too many of your hours.  There's no emphasis on learning and thinking.  only on doing stupid busy work and other pointless ****.  I'm starting a letter writing campaign to change this course.

This class kinda stinks...Belina is an amazing person but not that great of a teacher. He simplifies everything FAR too much. The absolute best professor I've had. Look at the recent article in the Engineering magazine about how far out of his way he goes to help students. Shows to ALL labs and sections. He is always in a good mood and ready to help without question. A genuinely passionate professor.
Clear and helpful, what more can you ask for? Definitely one of the best.

This guy is the man. One of the best professors I've ever had. He is friendly, nice and super helpful. His voice is clear and calm, making it easy to understand his lectures. I'm a Belina convert. Here's the guy who made me want to stick to ECE (after I switched from AEP). Best Professor I've encountered so far in Engineering. Lectures are interesting and clear. The best Prof you can get in engineering. Kind and really helpful.
Belina is one of the best profs in engineering.  Willing to help you if you're in his class or just need some advice.  Definitely recommended.
really nice guy...always in high spirits and willing to help
One of the best prof you can get in engineering school. teach the material at an appropriate level, unlike most other engineering profs. Very awesome dude!
solid teacher and very nice fellow, just take good notes in his lectures and ask him questions, he's willing to help
jolly and helpful. lectures not that great. but he is very helpful and friendly.
Belina is an awesome teacher. He is always willing to help anyone, and he's one of the nicest people I've ever met. He's a great professor and I wish he could teach all of my classes.

Go Belina!
Good teacher.  Willing to stay after class or meet seperately to help explaing things better.
Not too bad.  Actually makes the course material interesting sometimes.
Nice guy. Pretty good at teaching.

Johne Belina is very good at clearly describing the course subject matter.  Yes, he does make occasional subtle jokes but most of the time they are pretty funny. In my opinion he has the best interpersonal skills and is the nicest of all the ECE professor
You are blessed by Cornell if you have this teacher.  I've never had a better prof. yet!  His willingness to engage with students and be helpful is unprecidented.  He really enjoys what he does.
Belina teaching has some major flaws. He tries to be helpful but never lets people even finish their questions.  Goes off on tangents.  Tries to be funny but is not in the least.
Great professor. Try's to be funny and makes stupid jokes but you gotta love him anyway.  Good to talk to, very extroverted. Recommended professor.
Great guy; very good friends with him too. he always went the extra mile to help you
The most amazing prof I've ever had. Extremely helpful. A very jolly fellow. If you could learn 10% of what he knows, you would be an expert!

ECE door guardian and most helpful Professor. He is always available to give students advice and very friendly. His love is pizza!
very helpful, very friendly, gives good advice. awesome teacher!!!

Lectures can be a bit dry but he's a good teacher. Answers any questions or concerns you have and is very helpful if you need any help. Problem sets aren't necessarily hard but take a lot of work. Pretty heavy on conceptual knowledge so make sure you actually understand what your equations mean

She's often unclear and contradictory. One minute you do this; the next you do something else. There's also a lot of busy work assigned. She demands you meet 4-5 times a week for class and hands out repetitive assignments almost every day. The grading can be very arbitrary as well.

I really enjoyed my Viet classes at Cornell with co Thuy. Shes an effective teacher who's very generous with her grades.
