Co Thuy is an amazing professor!

Had her as a teacher for almost two years. The courses are challenging, but fun as you bond with your classmates in a casual ambiance. If you keep up with the homework, you'll do great in the class. As a teacher, she wants all her students to succeed and learn the language. However, the student must show the initiative. Overall, great class.
take any other language

This instructor is very inconsistent with regards to her instruction.  She often grades based on her mood at the particular day and time she is looking at your work.  Lacks motivational skills and often pits students against each other for the sack of unhealthy student competition.  Lacks any healthy professionalism.
Does not tolerate half assed students. Will push you into being a better student. Overall a hard ass, but a very good teacher. I learned a lot in her class.

Such a nice Professor, I absolutely loved this class. Such a fun and great FWS. She priorities you above all else and does not punish you for taking mental health days. My favorite class I have taken in Cornell so far. I can imagine someone disliking her, such a great person. Gave us snacks for Halloween and Christmas to celebrate the holidays :)

She is so caring, it almost makes you feel like a human again. She's always checking in and making sure the work load isn't too heavy. She's very poetic when she teaches, and highly relatable (sharing tiktoks she made in her announcement emails). I really felt like I could write papers without worrying about a grade.

I have nothing but nice things to say about her. I've enjoyed working on most of the assignments. The class is low stress, and she is definitely the most caring professor I've ever had. Wish I can take more classes with her in the future.

Briel is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is such an amazing, loving, and caring person. She truly cares about the students and is passionate about her job and writing. If you love all types of writing like poetry, nonfiction, fiction, articles, or story-telling, and many others, this is definitely the class and professor for you.
Prof. Cosgrove is one of my favorite professors at Cornell BME! He is super organized, willing to help, and cares about his students. Highly recommend taking his class.

Prof Cosgrove is probably the best professor I've had at Cornell so far. He truly and completely understands what he is talking about and has a very clear lecture style that makes it easy to learn from him. He cares a lot about the success of his students and wants to see everyone succeed.
I've never seen anyone pour so much effort and passion into teaching a course than this man did. He was loving every minute of it, and so were we.

Great class. Sawyer is an absolute character, but knows everything about the 60's. Reading aren't too bad. Post a response every Friday for section. Take home prelim and final are both 3, 3-page essays. There is also a 10 page research paper. But that's it. Stay on top of those are you are golden.

Professor Sawyer is a unique character, but he is very passionate. He gets really excited during discussion, and he clearly knows his stuff. I found this class to be engaging and I learned a lot. He provides a lot of feedback, and is always open to the opinion of his students, which was refreshing. Take a class with him if you can.

I wasn't sure how I was going to like this class beforehand, but I really really loved it.  Sawyer is enthusiastic and very approachable, and his lectures are interesting and impassioned.  Highly recommend.

Functions more as a literature class than a history class. Course is constructed well; texts are interesting. Sawyer is a bit of a bumbling guy, but he is fascinating and fairly knowledgeable. This class requires a lot of writing; approach your papers like you are writing an English paper. Papers are graded by the TAs.
Class is really interesting. Sawyer is a little strange but very interesting
So he might be a little spaced out, but he gives amazing, thoughtful, extensive feedback on your papers (he obviously spends a lot of time evaluating his students' essays).

No theme during the course, unless you found one yourself.  Seems like a nice guy but really scater-brained.  Paper-grading was unfair and inconsistent.  Texts were interesting, nice supplemental info, but you will work to get anything out of the class.
He is nice enough, but he is kind of boring and I never get what he's talking about. He just goes on and on about... something. The books for the class are really good though.

Prof Sawyer is a really nice guy and the subject matter is really interesting, but he is too disorganized and his lectures are really hard to follow. He is a really random paper grader, and there is a ton of reading and papers in this class.
Awesome class. Very helpful Prof. Kinda cooky, but he is IN the Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test by Wolfe.
Goofy, eccentric prof who truly enjoys teaching.  If you listen, he'll make everything come alive.  Listen and be inspired!  Very approachable (as are most of Cornell's English profs).

Fantastic, passionate teacher with a great deal of real-world experience in death penalty cases.  The socratic method is a little scary, but once you get called on, it won't happen again.  The Death Penalty in America remains the best class I've taken at Cornell.

Unique, engaging lecturer.  Can come off as a bit intimidating because he runs it like a true law class.  Definitely a good primer experience for those interested in law school.  Readings can be a bit heavy and cold-calls will leave you on the edge of your seats.  Definitely gives you a unique experience as an undergrad.
Brilliant, clear, sympathetic. Also an expert on the subject. Take it!
This guy is the man!

Explains why we are doing things such as processes and not just make us do it. He goes above and beyond the understanding of the course which helps me make connections to concept in biology, that I finally get my aha moment.
I am always looking forward to this one class in my week, wish other classes got as interesting as this one. He motivates me to try harder, which I like.
Nirav is an incredible TA and human being. Definitely try to sign up for his lab sections; he truly makes this class worthwhile. He offers really good life advice, too!

I have really enjoyed the class due to his approach of teaching. Not only is he great at teaching the material and organizing labs, he is also very personable and easy to talk to. I am never afraid to ask and he will ensure all of us have understood material before moving on. He shows authority and is most caring instructor on campus.

I like how he used humor and gave random (really random) spiels about life experiences and current events in science. Made three hours worthwhile. Outlines useful information and goes in depth with lecture material that helps!
His enthusiasm for biology and evolution is contagious, I might just consider going to grad school.....

I would not take the class again, but I would gladly take a class offered by Nirav. I am a senior forced to take this class. I would say he is one of the most invested instructors I've had during my time at Cornell so far. He truly cares about students and works hard to ensure we understand everything that is taught. Above all he admires criticism.

I hate the class, the lectures, and even what I have to put up for a 2-credit class. He definitely saves the day by making 3-hr lab the most interesting part of my week. But if this class was not required, I might still take it due to advices that I get about research, life, and studying. Above all love the tangents.. they keep me engaged.
Nirav is very helpful.  He wants you to succeed and is a fair teacher!

Nirav is a fantastic TA.  He loves what he teaches, and if you show interest in the subject, he is more than willing to help you.  Tests are hard, study up, but you really learn the material.  he makes class enjoyable, connects the material to real world events, and loves to joke around.  best TA i've had at cornell
I should studied his exams since finals were so similar, but I loved this class....only because he was teaching it. I have heard terrible stories of other TA's. Hope I get him again this semester.
I loved this class...the best TA I ever had.....so much better than my last semesters TA...he was the best.
guess its that time of the year but despite hard ass ..he defn taught me how to look at biology  in  a new way...would recommend him anyday compared to others that I have had in past

Despite all the effort I put into this class and the resulting crappy grade I received, I have to say that Nirav is a freaking great TA. He's genuinely interested in how his students are doing in the class and really strives to cultivate a passion for biology. Tests are mad hard but he really tries to prepare you for them. Plus, he'll play music!

well I have this guy this semester and so far I think its the best class on my schedule....I can listen to music, seems like he really cares abut his students and above all he knows his stuff!!!! lez see how the semester goes:)
Despite being hard I found that it was to my advantage....sorry gave a bad review since had not seen final then but I understand why he gives the quiz the way he does.
depsite being tough, he rocks....I wonder why I did not have hime before.  Way to go

Well I took upon myself to write here since found that one persons review is not enuf. I had him for the whole year and he will repeat what he said several times so I found that very helpful and I think he loves what he does and that is rare....I think he was the best teacher I have had so far at Cornell.....
No Comments

Majority of class dropped out. The exams were fair but the problem sets were atrocious. Only two questions (out of 4-6) in each PS (which takes 4+ hours to complete) are graded but never mentions which ones. Lectures and textbook are almost never enough to be able to complete PS thoroughly. Avoids answering questions in office hours. Steer clear

Genuinely funny guy, lectures are long, but he makes sure to make it worth your while. There are books required, but I just checked them out from the library instead of buying, they were pretty easy find since they're all classics.

It's obvious he knows what he's talking about, but I sometimes had a hard time staying interested because class is basically him talking at you the whole time. I thought he was pretty good at explaining difficult concepts clearly, though.

Swedberg means well, he's just sort of 'aloof.' And not gonna lie, his lectures bored me to tears. However, if you pay enough attention to get the gist of what is going on in class and write in a clear, organized manner, you will do well.
Very entertaining lectures, clearly knows a great deal about the subject, and enjoys including anecdotes about the authors' lives and about life in Sweden.

I don't think this class was boring at all. it is very easy to relate the material to your life. I think Swedberg is the best sociology professor in the department. He livens classical theory by relating it to art history, for goodness sake!
As long as you go to class you will do well. His lectures can be boring but they're better than doing the readings. I didn't read anything and went to half the lectures and did fine

Swedberg is extremely intelligent and really cares about his students.  Soc 395 is interesting and he really wants to make sure that his students learn. Definitely take a class with him if you are a soc major!

I agree with the other reviews: the professor is good, it's just that the material is shove-pencils-in-your-eye dull. Poor, poor soc majors. What makes it tolerable is that he's a nice, soft-spoken, pleasantly old-school kind of guy with a sly sense of humor. But don't take this class unless you have to.

Professor Swedberg was a good professor. He knew his stuff and seemed really interested in teaching. His accent is entertaining as is his humor. Unfortunately, my dislike for the material made me hate the class with a passion. Incredibly boring and pointless, but easy. Swedberg makes the class bearable.

His style takes a bit of getting used to, once you do you can learn a hell of a lot from this guy. He's a very frank and objective academic which is often hard to find in a field of big egos (Nee, anyone?) . His slightly self-depricating humor combined with the heavy swedish accent sometimes had me laughing out loud. Mandatory attendance is a pain.

Classical Theory (of soc.) is required for Soc majors, and is a large lecture with not a whole lot of interaction available throughout the class.  Swedberg really knew his stuff, and would have been extremely if I was even remotely into the topic.  He attempts to make some jokes. I did really well on the tests but lost pts due to attendance factor.

Prof. Swedberg's apparent enthusiasm for what he teaches really makes you want to listen to him.  He is one of the most ernest I've had at Cornell.  Though the reading can be dry, the class is not hard at all.  Swedberg is, in general, a really likable, inteligent guy.
he is really smart and nice though sometimes the class is boring (but at least it's easy)
He's really nice and obviously really loves what he does, though he hates big classes.  The material is so incredibly boring though.
Easiest class Ive taken.  20% of ur grade is signing in to lectures.  However, you'd better leave after you sign in unless you want a nap.
No Comments

He's a really nice guy. A little wierd when he waits at the end of class for questions. He's a bit hard to understand at first and lectures are a bit boring. You'll get an A if you do the readings and sign into class. It's worth it to take.
while his swedish accent and mild manner are at first a turnoff, prof. swedberg proves to be one of the most clear, organized, intelligent, and knowledgeable profs around.
Had him for classical theory; funny in class and very knowledgeable. It was a privilege being in his class.

Lectures are hasty and it feels like they rush through some parts while wasting time on unhelpful derivations one could find in the textbook. Prelims + final quite straightforward with non-strict rubric, but no practice exams provided which is annoying. Problem sets a bit lengthy, but not too bad. Would want better lectures, but not bad overall

The professor tries hard to help people understand the very complicated material and is a great person. However, the course material remains difficult to absorb, partly because the material itself is very dense. Problem sets take substantial time (go to TA office hours for help) and exams are fairly difficult. Median was a B+.

This professor is an awful lecturer and the classes are extremely monotone and hard to follow. There are no practice exams and they simply say to practice off problem sets and the textbook. Would not take again.

Not a very explicit teacher and the homework and exams didn't always cover and follow what was taught in lectures. The book is terribly structured and difficult to go through, which made learning the material more difficult than it should have been. Quite difficult for someone without previous exposure to game theory or a good fine math background.

Professor Rarytska is a very professional yet approachable professor. Lectures were a bit unclear since her handwriting was small and she didn't really seem to project her voice, but she was excellent in office hours - always willing to go concepts or past exams; however, was reluctant to give any guidance with problem sets at all. Very fair exams.
Easy grader, but but her class is so boring
shes a great teacher, passionate, it was my fws but i always liked her and shes very sympathetic

She gives good lectures generally, but her tests are absolutely ridiculous for an intro class. You pretty much need to know every single detail on the lecture slides. The answer choices are very tricky. You could "defend your answer" but you need to give her a very very detailed explanation. She seems like a sweet and caring professor though.

The test content are all in the slides. She tries somewhat hard and the slides aren't that bad, but she isn't that good at answering questions. 

The most annoying thing is that she tests you on the smallest details on the slides so no matter how hard you study you're bound to get at least a few questions wrong.
Lectures give exactly what you need. Honest about the material - which one is really useful and which one you just need to know to pass the exam.

She's a really nice woman, but she definitely does not belong teaching at Cornell.  Actually, she doesn't deserve to teach anywhere.  Even if you can understand her thick accent, it won't do much good- her lectures are useless and she has no teaching ability.  Avoid her if you can if you want to learn calculus!

The worst teacher by far.  Her thick accent makes it very difficult to understand which may be an advantage. She did not understand the material and most classes were spent correcting her mistakes and trying to help her understand concepts. Clearly she never taught multi-var before and hopefully she won't again.

Good-natured and highly talented in her field (her speciality has to do with knitting advanced geometric shapes), but her thick (Austrian?) accent and ability to forget how to solve problems on the board in the middle of showing the class can make calculus II a living hell. Willing to give extra credit to those who need it!

Very clear course, knew the expectations from the beginning. She prepares a lot for classes & students. Learnt all fundamental concepts in 1 course. She's a very sweet person, & gives great feedback. She is very accommodating, empathetic and passionate about what she teaches, & I respect her tons.

He is a the type of professor who tries hard to be idolized by students. This is not a good thing. Nor should he take philosophical disagreements so personally. When people disagreed with Sturgeon, I got the sense that he disapproved of them in a moral sense---and that he kind of got off on it. Steer clear.

In short, a great professor. To succeed in his class-attend every single lecture, make exhaustive notes, go to his office hours and he'll be ready to help. But be very careful about each claim you make in your essays-back them up with appropriate reasoning and citation. Prof. Sturgeon is extremely considerate and rewards hard work. Fair grading.

I have taken two philosophy classes with Professor Sturgeon at Cornell, and he is by far the best professor I have ever had.  He cares a lot about the subject and also about his students. He is very renowned in his field, so if you are interested in ethics and philosophy definitely take one of his classes!

If you are seriously interested in ethics you will love this class.  If not there is a good chance it is very boring.  Sturgeon is a litimus test for potential  philosophy majors.  As a phil major, I cannot speak more highly of him as a prof and a man.

One of the worst professors I have had. He gives the impression that philosophy has less to do with intellectual curiosity than with scoring petty "points" against whomever he's decided to dislike today.
Super intelligent and devoted professor. Truly a privilege to take one of his classes.

Ethics in philosophy is not the same as ethics in the everyday sense. Sturgeon is a philosophy prof, not a life coach so if you think he’s going to tell you if thing X is right or wrong you are mistaken and will be disappointed. However, if you actually want to learn PHILOSOPHY you will understand that Sturgeon is one of the best profs around.

If you love ethics, you will love professor Sturgeon. He's one of the veterans of the phil department and he's probably the best guy here for ethics. Incredibly intelligent, sweet, and very clear presentation of material in class. Make sure you stay on top of the reading (there's a lot) and a fair bit of writing too -- three 8-pages papers.
Very boring, unclear, and unhelpful. He managed to turn the interesting subjects of ethics into a dull/monotonous (and completely irrelevant) lecture. Stay far away.

repetitive lectures, bad assigments and syllabus, absolutely no application at all... expect to catch an early morning nap.  if you're interested in ethics, take one of the classes about a specific area of ethics (medicine, environment, etc).  very boring and poorly organized class.

Very boring lecturer. Very unhelpful. Material is not organized; a stream of boring lectures with some notes on the board. He took an interesting subject (Ethics) and taught it in a horrible way- I hope he didn't turn too many people away from phil...maybe that was his goal  :(...Stay FAR AWAY.
This class is TERRIBLE!!!! Sturgeon is a nice guy and cares about his students but his class is soooo boring. Repetitious and irrelevant- this class sucks.
If I were to rename this professor, his new name would be Jake****stein XVII.  This class is so boring!
Consider this an honest opinion from someone who received an A in this class - it sucks. Boring as hell and a total waste of time.  I personally now hate philosophy after respecting it beforehand.

The most boring class I've taken.  I heard great things about it, but it honestly isn't good unless you have a knack for Phil.  Even though it is an intro class, there seems to be a standard to already know about Philosophy.  His lectures are boring but thorough and there isn't a clear syllabus.
Fantastic lecturer; very helpful; striking clarity and examples; good with questions.
Definitely one of the best Professors I've had. Very helpful and knows exactly what he's talking about.
Why doesn't this guy have a pepper next to his name?!
Fun to listen to and watch.  He's quite animated.  Repitition is key here.  Grading however is a bit strange, but that is on the count of the TAs.
Not a fan of his class, but I really like the fish.
Great teacher; very clear thinker and material is presented in such a coherent, captivating fashion.
One of my favorite professors ever.
By far the best class I've taken at Cornell.  Nicest professor I have ever had.
This guy is an amazing lecturer, and a very clear thinker. If you can, take a class with him.

Prof. Tebbe is my favorite professor this semester. He makes very difficult topics much more accessible, and he does it in a fun and lighthearted way. He's also very encouraging and is the kindest professor when it comes to cold calling. All in all, 10/10.

Tebbe's class was nuanced & accessible. His discussions are politically neutral & he treated controversial issues objectively & sensitively,, making us comfortable. He posts & reviews problems that mirror test questions & responds to feedback. Leaves some cases for his amendment 1 class. Lots of us want to take it bc this one was great.

Tebbe is cool and charming as a person, but treats his class as an opportunity to pontificate his political point of view. His Con Law class for 1Ls only covered a few topics and left vast swathes of Con Law untouched. I feel unprepared for discussing constitutional law outside of school and annoyed at his closed minded teaching style.

Heavy workload! Doesn't understand meaning of homework and assigns month long assignments. Is extremely delusional in what it means to teach NLP and teach MLE. He thinks his homework assignments are reinforcing course topics yet so much isn't taught. It's so telling when half the class drops after the first homework.

Alert!!!!!workload is super heavy, each homework is like a research project that requires extensive self-learning and dependent on how well your random-assigned teammates perform. Not really much of the HW is covered in the lecture material, you basically need to do all the research by yourself

She writes everything on the board, so if you miss lectures, don't expect any slides to be uploaded on Blackboard. She is very helpful and friendly in office hours. Exams are super hard, but class is curved to a median B+.

She's a great professor. She's definitely very.. opinionated, but it's entertaining and makes an otherwise dull class fun and interesting. She approaches the material very logically and gives you a good idea of what will be on each test well ahead of time, as well as providing problem sets that prepare you well. Take class with her if you can!
Simply the best. Thanks Francesca!

Amazing prof who makes econometrics both interesting and clear. Her blackboard notes are very organized/clear and she always uses fun examples in class to keep you awake. Prelims straightforward, too.
Great professor who loves teaching. Pretty challenging but you'll be happy you went through it.

possibly one of the more rewarding classes I've taken yet. The material is CHALLENGING, but Molinari is extremely helpful and enthusiastic both in the class and in office hours (go to office hours, trust me) and if you put forth some effort, you will be rewarded. Molinari has a very loud italian voice, but she's hilarious.
very helpful, and exams are very similar to problem sets. Difficult material and too many irrelevant proofs in class
Class material is difficult. Majority of class relied entirely on the TA feeding us the solutions to the problem sets. Exams similar to problem sets.

Understands that there's a reason you didn't take 319/320. Only 6 PS, prelims EXACTLY like the practice one. Spends too much time on proofs, but as long as you understand application of material you're good.

She is very pretty and has a great accent, but difficult to understand.  Her problems in class are far too complicated, and her exams are exactly like the practice ones.  All theory based and little practicality.  Don't expect much.
very difficult course and she didnt help make it better.

I'm not a big fan of Mollinari. First of all she's not that hot. Second of all she does overcomplicate things and make simple concepts too technical. The problem sets are difficult but manageable. This class has many math majors and some hard science majors too. If you're not naturally a math person, this class may be a struggle (it was for me).

This is the greatest professor in the econ department: her exams are reasonble if you do your work, her lectures are interesting and engaging, spiced with her great sense of humor.  She's very approachable.  I would take another class with this professor.
Pretty tough class but she's a really good teacher.  Plus, she is hot.  Especially when she wears those boots.
This class isn't that hard. If you do all your homework, review all the class handouts, and notes, then you'll be fine. She rocks!
SHE IS HOT. Aside from that, the class isn't as hard as people say. She moves at a fair pace and is quite amusing during lecture. And yes.. she is HOT.

she is a nice lady who actually cares about you learning but i feel like she makes things more complicated than they need to be. can hilarious at times and my suffer a breakdown at some point. but give her a break she is nice and tries very hard. her tests are copies of the pre-lim and she is someone you can't be mad at.
She deserves a chili next to her name... cause she's definitely HOT!
320 is supposed to be harder, but I was far more miserable in 319 with Molinari.  The DeGroot textbook is AWFUL-- overly technical, few examples, and tedious to read
Good person, but lectures are confusing.  Difficult exams.
she is the best! i am in love with her
Very nice, pleasant, and very dedicated. Exams are fair, and you know what to expect.. I respect her.
No Comments

Nicest professor ever. Very dedicated to her job. (The first prof. in history to substitute for her TA's officer hours.) Really enjoyed taking the course under her. Italian accent cracks me up. Be nice to her. She deserves it.
Do not take his foundations of robotics class...
Cornell made a huge mistake. Our loss, Iowa's gain. She is a wonderful professor.

One of the best professors I've had in ILR. Classes are mainly lecture based, with some group exercises and discussions interspersed. If she still taught at Cornell I would take her classes again in a heartbeat.

Very clear lecturer. Clear expectations. Easy grader. Most of the grade was based on group case-studies and an exam based on the topics covered in the case studies (easy). Super helpful and approachable.

Of all my classes, her class is the only class I actually remember things from. She presents the material in a very clear manner and doesn't purposefully confuse you. She is probably the best and most reasonable prof in ILR (not a high standard, but she really is great).
An extremely easy (to get some form of an A) but horrible professor (teaching-wise). Be prepared to be forced to watch her face for 5-6 hours prior to exams in order to prep for them..

Textbook is useless except or a few writing assignments. Just watch her lectures on videonote, do the work and you will get an A. Also Beth helps keep the class relatively interesting (section in the other hand is useless and intolerable)

easy A. Course work is minamal. Test are multiple choice. There is always 1 or 2 Questions that appear to be unfair but she gives the statistics on how many got right and wrong to prove her case they were. Overall great class, and you actually retain material. Recommended

Great professor and TAs are cool. Just go to section and keep up with posted lecture notes. not necessary to attend class. Very easy if u pay attention and have all lecture notes with detail. shes a southern belle who looks great and is super approachable! Liked her energy and her interest in research.
Good class with a good professor.

With Prof. Livingston, you know exactly what you're getting.  Clear expectations for grades and most assignments, great lectures and straightforward guidelines for class success.  Very easy to get an A – just keep up on work and pay attention in lecture – exams are not difficult. She also makes a great effort to bring in real-world HR practitioners

She's very good at lecturing, good at distilling information in her lectures down to what's important, gives you flexibility in terms of which assignments you decide to complete, and tries her best to be helpful and accommodating despite how large the class is. I enjoyed it.
Beth is amazing. Take her. Just focus on lecture for the exams. EAASSSYYY A+. Im in love.

Beth is amazing. One of the best professors I've had at Cornell. She's really into the material she teaches and the concepts are really easy to grasp. Tests are extremely fair and she let's you know exactly what you need to do to get a certain grade; let's you do 4/6 writing assignments and 6/11 online quizzes as long as you get over a 70% on them.
super easy class, lots of opportunities for extra credit, she is a very good speaker and her lectures are engaging. i didn't really care for HR but i always showed up to her class.
Although she's sweet and very interested in teaching and sharing info about staffing her class is SO MUCH WORK. It should be 6 credits.
Too focused on details.  She'll spend a class focusing on a paragraph and over-analyzing every single minor flaw.  Every single thing she harps on is her own personal preference.  Do not recommend.
Yes, she is detail oriented, but at the same time, she is fair. If you work hard, you will end up with a good grade in her class.

Worthless class-- it's a freshman writing seminar all over again, but now worse.  She worries about margin width and line spacing, and teaches a completely outdated way of giving presentations (completely contrary to COMM 201/301).  This is much more of a technical journalism course-- she has NO clue about engineering, and it shows.  Avoid.

Actually, focusing on the details is important in teaching good communication skills.  Presentations are key in any real-world engineering job.  In this dog-eat-dog world, managers will pass over for promotions any person who seems less capable in any aspe

This woman is incredibly annoying and rediculous. Seems to be more concerned with formatting than written content and deducts for stupid details like underlining, margin width, etc. Totally inflexible as an instructor, takes attendance. Avoid.
Tough Course, but Awesome Professor. Archer really knows his fluids and is kind. I do not like Denn's Book. Let me repeat, I do not Like Denn's Book. I hope this causes Archer to choose another text.

Good professor. However the homeworks were long and hard. Prelims were open-notes and very doable. However, the TAs tend to be not useful in office hours. Better off going straight to Archer for Office hours

Hmm..Hmm more than month after finals and still arguing about fluids. In agree with some of these posts - archer is a great prof. one of the best ones in cheme at cornell. I also think he is fair, cool, and yes hot!
Hands down the best course I have had at Cornell! Archer has very high standards, but is fair. Horrible text, notes helped a lot.

Terrible class, the material is very interesting, but Archer completely ruins it. He's completely disorganized and arrogant, and his tests are very poorly designed, not necessarily hard, just poorly thought out.
Difficult course, awesome professor. Archer is thorough and rigorous. His fluids course demands a butt load of effort, but I can say I've learned alot. He is very helpful and a master of his subject.
Worst class I ever took. Worst teaching style I've ever encountered.

Archer is a great professor. The material is really tough, but he is always willing to help and is really friendly.  If you attend his office hours, he essentially tells you what is going to be covered on the exam.  Exams are fair but problem sets are VERY long.  I'm not the biggest fan of fluids, but if you have to take it, take it with Archer.

No one wrote a fluids review? At least I'M trying to help out my future chemE underclassmen.  Anyways, Archer gives you a crap load of notes throughout the semester and blazes through them at light speed.  However, his tests were FAIR (unlike the Hws) and office hours helpful, good teacher more or less, just too much material..

Professor Archer is an extremely friendly and helpful teacher. Although fluid mechanics was tough, he made it easier to handle and definitely wants his students to do well. He is extremely fair and devotes much of his time to office hours. He is a really great teacher.

Professor Friedland's lectures were great and he is very knowledgeable about the French Revolution, which was the topic of the class.

Throughout the semester, he managed to draw a clear, logical line from the beginning of the Revolution to its end.

I would definitely strongly recommend this course.

French Rev is the coolest class i've taken at Cornell. Prof Friedland makes a dramatic period of time both interesting and fun. Be ready to read a lot. 2 essays, one final essay based. Prof makes sure to make his lectures as interesting as possible and knows so many little facts. Doesn't like Napoleon though.
An exemplary historian who is one of the nicest professors you will meet at Cornell. Class act.

Friedland's French Revolution class is amazing. He knows an insane amount about the subject, and his lectures are soooo interesting, and he's a really funny guy. You don't have to go, but you really won't want to miss any. He doesn't seem to be a tough grader and gives really great essay feedback. Definitely do the readings and participate.

Best professor I've had at Cornell so far. His lectures were always interesting and he added his sense of humor to them in small ways that kept it engaging. Honestly just a great guy and a great prof, take a class with him if you can.
beast mode

A wonderful class with an amazing professor!! The French Revolution course has by far been my favorite class at Cornell. He is incredibly engaging, provides insightful commentary, and his lectures are super fun and always interesting. Discussion is mandatory, but lecture is not (but you'll never want to miss it). The grading can be a more difficult

Professor Friedland's lectures are very clear for those with or without a background in history. Very funny guy who doesn't take himself too seriously, but still effectively communicates his course material. Two essays + an essay-only final. Doesn't post slides online.

BEST LECTURER AT CORNELL. Was able to make incredibly boring material extremely exciting. Very engaging. Weekly readings aren't that bad and the Prelims are straightforward. If there's one professor at Cornell you should absolutely take a class from it's Friedland.
The lectures are great. Prof. Friedland gives clear descriptions about the French Revolution.  You have to work hard and read each week though.
Easily one of the best professors I had at Cornell. I actually looked forward to his lectures.

Engaging lectures and interesting, manageable reading load. Discussions were sometimes difficult because he could be a bit reluctant to let you have your own ideas. Assignment and exam instructions were unclear. On exams, wanted long-winded summaries of readings, not argumentative essays. Overall an interesting but slightly frustrating class.

Friedland is brilliant and super knowledgeable, even about the most random stuff. He's really easy-going, friendly, and engaging, but he keeps the class challenging and thoughtful. Discussion flows well.
He's an awesome lecturer. He's also a really nice person and takes the time to give lots of feedback on papers. Don't miss a chance to take a class with him.
He was a great lecturer but was unclear in his paper assignments and never followed through with personally helping students.  He is new but already notorious for being somewhat of a tough grader.

I loved Professor Friedland. His lectures were always clear and focused, and he would often add little jokes into his lecture slides. I had him for discussion as well, and the section was always really helpful in understanding that week's material and he made sure it was never boring. I'm taking another class from him next semester!

Fantastic, and easily the best professor I've had. Lectures were always very clear and very funny--he really goes the extra mile in everything he does. Extensive and helpful grading feedback. He's not easy, but he's not unduly hard either. Take him!

Professor Friedland is one of the best professors at Cornell. He is so nice and so passionate about what he teaches and will help you whenever you need it. I do recommend that you show up to all the lectures since the majority of info from the course will be given there. Overall, an awesome professor.
He is incredible. Take a class with him! Amazing lectures, super clear and gives great feedback. He really wants everyone to do well.
Awesome lectures. Really nice prof. Entertaining and serious at the same time. I'll  definitely try to take another class with him.
Professor Welker is very nice. Her lectures were very engaging. The readings provoked deep thought about global problems. The discussion sections were also very insightful.

Professor Welker always ensured that material was relevant to current issues and connected with students experiences in the real world. Class discussions always were lively and she allowed time for all students to voice their opinions throughout the class. Although some readings were on confusing topics, Professor Welker always was understanding.
Prof. Welker is such a knowledgeable, aware, and caring professor. She is very involved in her research and genuinely wants her students to learn as well. Talk to her about her time in Indonesia!
great class, bees are cool!
amazing class, professor and person. Vey clear and engaging presentations, slides, and grading criteria. As long as you show up to class, you'll do well on assignments

Professor Caillaud is a great lecturer and I really enjoying learning about the fascinating biology of honeybees. It was always interesting to be in lecture and very often fun. I wish her slide shows were a bit shorter so we can get to everything in class
I swear to god just show up and get your A

Taking this course right now and really loving what I am learning. the course is super intersting and well structured with pre and post lecture quizzes that keep me on my toes and engaged. The in class activities help with that too. Definitely a great course for non majors

TAKE THIS CLASS!! Mrs Calliaud is literally the sweetest little French professor and her energy lights up the room every time she speaks. The content is also super interesting! Best class I've taken at Cornell so far

I love Professor Caillaud!She is funny, passionate, about honey bees and wild bees. I really liked the structure of the classwith the activities during lecture and the weekly online quizzes. It kept me engaged and on top of the  material covered and made prep of exams easier.
Professor Caillaud is a great lecturer; she goes the extra step to ensure her students are engaged and interested in the topics she discusses.

She was the best and a fantastic lecturer, very understanding with regrads to needs of individual student, and very responsive. The active learning material during lecture was useful even though it slowed down the pace of the lectures. Great class! We need to save the bees!

A great class about bees, really interesting, and taught with care and thoughtfully. Weekly homework involves pre-lecture videos and readings, plus an online quiz. The final project is awesome and I had a lot of fun with my partners. Loved this class! And professor Caillaud too!

Without question, the greatest professor I've ever had the pleasure of studying under ever. You guys will learn so much being in her class and the commitments for the week are minimal at most. Would definitely take again, and no, this isn't a paid review. Prof. Caillaud is an 11/10.

She has great knowledge of the subject and she is very enthusiastic which kept me very engaged during lectures. Using polleverywhere also helped me stay motivated during class, the weekly online quizzes were super helpful but she never posted the key

Professor Caillaud is so lovely, kind, and intelligent. Her lectures are engaging, and while there's a ton of information, most of the work is just busywork. Her quizzes are kind of poorly written, but she clearly cares so much about her students. Definitely would take again.

Marina Caillaud was the best professor I had in my four years at Cornell. She is caring, kind, intelligent, and she is absolutely hilarious. I took the course in 2019 and was a TA in 2021 and can honestly say graduating without taking one of her courses is a travesty! She has inspired my passion for public health advocacy and I am so so grateful!
just taking that course rn and loving it.
Super kind prof and passionate about material. Need to study for exams but questions are straight-forward if you know the content
Great professor with really interesting lectures. Professor was very accessible and accommodating when I tested positive for Covid-19. This was by far my favorite class at CU so far (i am a senior)

Lectures by professor caillaud included latest information on the topic at at hand and that was really unexpected given that this class was described as a non major, and I definitely had several friends in the class who were not biology majors yet they enjoyed being treated with latest info
amazing lecturer, and I learned so much from her course
very interesting material taught with enthusiasm and care

If you are interested in learning about diseases and epidemics, this class is great for you. The material is pretty interesting but Professor Caillaud often reads off the slides. The tests aren't so difficult, as long as you know the material, but the sections are a little unnecessary.

Great professor-- cares about your learning. This is one of the few classes where I felt like I learned a LOT but didn't feel like I was until I got to the end of the course and realized I know a lot more about the process of epidemiology. She's super nice and very helpful and accessible during OH and through emails.

The course was really interesting. If u read the articles she sends out (there is no textbook), you should be able to get 100s on the prelims. There were some quizzes, but they were not hard at all. There is no final just a final project. Definitely an easy A. I would take it over again if I could.

Good class. I learned a lot, but we didn't focus on writing skills as much as an FWS maybe should and the class was lecture heavy most times. Still really enjoyed it and Libby is a great philosophy teacher & person.

Larry is great, he does make it obvious that 1585 is meant to lure people into taking more history classes so if you think of it like a baby history class it makes more sense. Lots of reading, but if you do them and show interest in sports history you'll probably get an A

I took Sports & Politics with Glickman -- had some interesting topics but overall grading ruined my experience. Not a terrible lecturer but exam content is minimally focused on big picture ideas and themes taught in lecture but more on specifics (dates, obscure people, listing athlete DOBs first to last). some interesting content, poor class

He is an absolutely amazing professor, I took this course as a distribution but it ended up becoming my favorite course of the semester. The homework was light, the research paper final project was not stressful but extremely interesting to do. Super amazing class!

Great class here at Cornell, Professor Glickman is a passionate teacher who ensures that topics are interesting. Readings are manageable and I felt that tests were reflective of course content. Finally, final research project was allowed to be creative, overall great class, with an interesting topic, and a really caring professor. Would recommend!

Great Professor teaching a very interesting class. He is clearly both passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter which makes listening to him actually interesting. Readings every week but they are really not bad at all if you are interested in sports

Great professor and great class. He's obviously an expert on 20th century American political history and his class taught me so much about the subject and gave me a greater appreciation for the study of history of a whole. He's also super nice and extremely approachable. Overall an amazing class.

Very approachable, kind professor that knows his field extremely well. Hes written pieces for the Washington Post and the Atlantic among others which I thought was cool. My only criticism would be that he lectures too much toward the end of the semester (its a seminar). Great class that I learned a lot from.

Glickman is a nice guy and a good professor. The content of Sports and politics class at Cornell gets REALLY REALLYH BORING. It is a LOT of reading and the TA's are so harsh with grading they leave little to no room for improvement. There is a weekly assignment everyweek due THURS 7 am which isn't hard at all. MY POINT IS THE GRADING IS UNFAIR!!!!!

Prof Glickman is one of the best professors. He is passionate about the subject (which is really interesting), and is just an overall amazing human. He responds to emails quickly. He also cancels sections during exam weeks and before breaks. The research paper is only 5-7 pages and the readings are required, but interesting. 15/10 class

Prof. Glickman is amazing. Gives interesting lectures and responds to emails quickly. A decent amount of reading and a research paper, but the readings are interesting and the paper is only 5-7 pgs. Take this class if you love sports, I would take it again in a heartbeat.

Professor Lakhani is one of the most flexible and easy-to-understand professors in the Hotel school. She is clearly knowledgeable in human resources but always willing to learn and be open-minded. HR has a very light workload and easy/fair exams, making the learning experience enjoyable and stress-free.

Professor Lakhani is one of the best professors in the hotel school. She cares a lot about her students and is accessible outside of class. Classes are largely discussion based with chances to do discussion posts instead of speaking in class. Prelims and group projects are graded fairly.
A legendary genius who cannot talk to anyone below his level of intelligence.

Hopcroft is legendary! He is one of the best in his field, and is still going strong. CS 4810 was a very easy course, especially if you have taken discrete math and/or algorithms, but Hopcroft manages to make it interesting. Beware, he does not fret about technical details, so that may be something to consider depending on your learning style.

Never really used the textbook, almost all material comes from lecture. Hopcroft's been doing this for years, extremely experienced. But lecture goes VERY fast. He is very open open to reviewing past topics or answering questions, but if you miss something, it'll be hard to catch up. Homework and exams aren't hard, but there is quite a time crunch.

Reading the textbook he wrote, I realize just how much he clarifies such difficult-to-understand concepts by just saying things aloud. I guess that's just a genius professor thing. Everything flowed together, and while the topics could get difficult, he was also receptive to feedback.
Smart dude, but can't teach for beans.

He is a genius of a professor. However, because of that he often taught way above the level of the class. People frequently had no idea what he was talking about in lecture, and sometimes his co-professor would even be confused about what he was explaining. I can't recommend his lectures in good faith.

Took CS4850 with him.  Definitely a fantastic lecturer. The content is incredibly interesting, lectures are engaging and Hopcroft makes sure that everyone learnt the material by asking us questions and answering any possible question anyone has. This class was a great class and I would definitely recommend it for anyone into math andor cs.

Lectures can be a little disorganized, but prof is extremely approachable and helpful during office hours. Course gets easier towards end of semester. Reasonable HW sets, easy prelims if you've been paying attention to the HWs.

Terrible professor. Brilliant, but terrible at conveying information. Extremely unorganized and assumes everyone in the room has already seen half of the material. Essentially taught myself the course, but it was not very hard. 2800 is much easier with Hopcroft but he will not teach you anything
Great guy, and brilliant. Not very organized, and the lecture was too large for him to handle, but he really does care about teaching...which is pretty cool considering how distinguished the guy is.

I took Discrete Structures with Hopcroft and found it very unorganized. The textbook barely helped, and the information given was inconsistent (Only a couple lectures had notes online and homework answers stopped being given to us halfway through the semester.) Prelims were easy enough, but course overall was not very good

Absolutely fantastic professor!  The best one you will find in computer science, he is top in the field (wrote the textbook!) but still cares about students and will go out of his way to help them to understand the material.  Take advantage of his office hours--the class is easy if you do all of the work!
Awesome professor

The problem with this course this year was that CS 381 and 481 shared a lecture. As a result, Hopcroft did not spend enough time helping the 481 students. He was not very helpful in his office hours (he would go too fast). His lectures on the other hand are slow and easy to follow. Be prepared for the quizes every class, and go to TA office hours.
A righteous professor teaching a righteous course.  As much as I like his approach, I have a bias towards Richard Feynman's lectures on computation.
Class is definately worth taking. Prof Hopcroft is a very dedicated prof. Goes out of his way to help students grasp the material. You'll really remember the material even after completing his class.

As everyone has said, he is a wonderful professor. The grades seem arbitrary and the lecture isn't terribly inspiring, but he is *extremely* intelligent. This course is certainly one of the easiest in CS.

Extremely patient and helpful to his students, and genuinely wants us to learn. (I mean, how many professors are like that?) In terms of teaching, his explanations make complicated theories easy to understand. So nice I can't believe he's a cs professor.
very willing to explain concepts to you again if you don't understand them the first time; most likely one of the best professors at Cornell i will end up having by the time i graduate
He is without a doubt the best teacher in the CS school.

A great man and one who is genuinely interested in the welfare of students. He is probably the most distinguished prof in the CS dept but you wouldn't know from talking to him...an extremely humble and kind person.
He is the best CS teacher I ever had. Class is soo much fun to be in, even in the morning!

Easily the best professor I've had in three years at Cornell. He knows what he's teaching, and does an excellent job of communicating it to the class. I've never had a professor offer to go back over a topic because he thinks we're not understanding it...

He did indeed win the Turing Award. He's a great guy, a very clear lecturer, and not unwilling to help even outside of office hours. The material in the course isn't that thrilling, but Hopcroft does more with it than anyone else could.
really really good. He tries really hard to explain things in class. is really clear. best of all his exams are made so that everyone can get an A. just go to class and do the work.
he won the turing award, man.
Not well organized in in terms of the lecture, and difficult to get his email reply
Kinda bad honesty. Teacher was all over the place. Very poor organisation
one of the best lecturers at ECE

Overall a nice and knowledgeable lecturer. But he can be very unorganized at some points, which can create distractions (a typical phrase from him: "ok forget about this, let me explain it that way"). The problem is that he tries to teach the whole course from his memory. But somebody needs to tell him it is OK to use some notes while teaching.

Really good professor who makes a difficult subject (digital signal processing) clear and easy to understand. Especially Spring 2020, with coronavirus, he has been extremely understanding and flexible in making the course help accessible and with changing deadlines and such. Wish there were more profs like him who care so much about the students.

Smart prof. Lectures can be a bit dry sometimes, coding assignments were really fun. The grading/psets are done by the TAs who don't know anything, so be ready to argue points back. Overall the first half of the class was a repeat of 2200, and the second half was hard asf stats/ML. Final project was diagnosing lung cancer on CT scans--rly dope

I took Mr. Najemy's 'Machiavelli' course in Fall 2006. He truly inspired his students,  and was clearly passionate about history. He had an unparalleled knowledge of early modern Europe, particularly Florence. He may speak a little softly, but this fits well with his unassuming character.  If you like European history, you must take this seminar.

Extremely knowledgeable.  Very quiet and somewhat neurotic with his notes.  Speaks a little too softly, but is interested in his coursework and his students.  Could be somewhat more exciting, though.  Readings are excellent.  Major complaint is the promise of discussions of texts in class, but we never get to say anything.

Most well-prepared professor I've ever had--borderline OCD. Najemy's not interested in big picture ideas or daring interpretations. He is more interested in what Machiavelli has to say than students' interpretations (he'll argue to the contrary) and frequently cuts off comments. That said, I learned a great deal about Machiavelli. Worthwhile class.
Fantastic professor.  He is charismatic in a quiet way.  If you want to hear a speaker who doesn't use notes, go to a Pentecostal church.

I have taken two seminars with Najemy and loved his classes. He is absolutely brilliant and knows everything about the italian renaissance. He is witty, and interesting. I never had any issues hearing him lecture...I took two seminars with him, and wish I had another semester to take another class with him!
he never looks up from his notes and goes over time every time

It's been 25 YEARS since I had this class and I still remember the prof as one of the best I ever had at Cornell. Yes, he does speak very softly and you have to be on your toes because lectures are absolutely jam-packed with info, delivered rapid-fire. Brilliant man and very dedicated.

Najemy is probably a brilliant historian on 15th c. Italy but he is not engaging at all. They are not intellectually stimulating bc he doesn't present the material in an interesting way. If you want someone to lull you to sleep in class, take Najemy's course. He speaks SO softly. There's a difference b/t being a brilliant expert and a good teacher

the best professor i've ever had. not only are his lectures as interesting as possible when talking about 500 years ago but he's also able to joke about current issues and a wide variety of unrelated topics.  i would definitely recommend this or any of his other classes for anyone

You'll really like Najemy if you're a history major or into romance studies. His lectures are interesting and easy to understand. You do have to go to sections, but not all reading is necessary each week. Overall, a really nice guy who really loves Italy
I have taken two classes with this man and will take more.  His lectures are uber-stellar.  Go to them.  Anyone who doesn't like him has no taste and is dumb, besides.

My advice would be only to take Najemy if (a) you are prepared to attend class weekly; and (b) you are capable of understanding intellectually demanding topics.  If you are one of the few at Cornell who actually meet these criteria, you'll love Najemy.
Najemy is a brilliant academic and a great professor.  I've taken two classes with him and look forward to taking a third.

Dr. Najemy is the single worst lecturer in the hist. dept.  the italian renaissance should be a pretty interesting class, right?  Wrong.  The only things that save this class are the quality reading list and Bob, the TA.
chill professor but tries too hard to be funny. does not provide any practice for exams other than the 4 easy homework we had that did not help on the exams. take the hotel version instead.
Very chill guy. Tests are very similar to HWs and were curved like crazy

My favorite professor on campus hands down. The finance class he teaches is critical for any business student to take as the concepts you learn are invaluable. He is a fantastic lecturer, and keeps things clear for everyone to understand. The material can be tough but curve is huge, he is awesome, and I couldn't recommend a class with him more.

Took finance with him. Lecture slides are very useless. Doesn't provide any practice materials that are useful for his exams. The content we're presented on exams are nothing like what we learned in class.

Great professor, actually made people do some work for once in the major. Lectures are absolutely necessary as tests count for 75 percent of your grade, and there are not many other options to learn the material. Exams are curved very generously

Professor Addoum is one of my favorite professors in Dyson. His class (corporate finance) is, by far, one of the most useful courses I have taken. His lectures are captivating and well structured. He is reasonable and never asks you to do impossible tasks.

Professor Silver's networking class is a must-take for anyone looking to master networking. Her engaging teaching style and guest lecturers provide invaluable insights into building and managing professional connections. I gained timeless skills that will last a lifetime, making it one of the most valuable classes I've taken at Cornell.

Professor Silver did an incredible job teaching us the integral aspects of networking as a part of our careers and daily lives. She brought in incredible industry experts for each class session and taught me skills I will use throughout my entire life! Highly recommend the course!
Gave clear and organized lectures even though the topics are difficult.

Gives very clear lectures that coincide neatly with textbook topics. Orgo is daunting but it is manageable if you take good notes in lecture and from the book. Go to class and you will pass. (I stopped going when Ganem started lecturing and that's when I dropped to a B+). Some overlap with 2510 so that was helpful.
He is an amazing professor. He truly cares about every student. He is very engaging and teaches a very difficult subject in a clear way!
Best lecturer in the chemistry department and super helpful at office hours
Orgo is tuff, but he's great!

A very overrated professor. He clearly was passionate about organic chemistry, but he was never clear on what he wanted you to know on tests. Also, he glossed over many important details and later put questions pertaining to those concepts on the exams. A nice person, but barely a decent professor.
Dichtel was a pretty good prof! Definitely read the text book and keep up with the problem sets. The class is really challenging, but at least he's decent at teaching the material.
dichtel was a great lecturer, occasionally funny, always clear. Nice guy too.

Dichtel is one of the best chemistry professors in Cornell. His lectures are clear and he follows the textbook to a degree in which if you skipped a class, you can catch up by doing the readings. I am horrendous at chemistry but Dichtel makes life easier for you
one of the best chemistry professors that I have had. He is a great lecturer(very organized and clear), and he seriously cares about his students and teaching undergrads.
Extremely nice professor, always happy to help and discuss. Also, he's a really good lecturer.

The class is not easy but the tests are very fair and if you put the time into studying and paying attention in lecture the class isn't that bad. If you ever have a question go to Dichtel's office hours, he is really helpful and really wants his students to succeed. His lectures are good and the information is presented in a order that makes sense.

Dichtel is an amazing professor. He is extremely helpful and wants the absolute best for his students. The material is difficult however he is very helpful i office hours. He's a very intelligent and caring professor. He makes Organic Chemistry fun to learn.

He's a good lecturer, puts material across very clearly and precisely.  Also, the molecules of the day were an interesting way to link material to everyday life (and a free 14 points on each prelim).  Go to lecture and do the practice problems he puts up and you'll do fine in the class.  Expect the tests to be difficult though.

Homonoff's not bad - behavioral econ is an interesting subject and she was pretty straightforward in explaining concepts and gave a lot of interesting policy examples. However, she has a horrible habit of asking questions while the answer is ON THE POWERPOINT SLIDE. One group proj at the end, which wasn't too much work but was kind of annoying.

Would NOT recommend. He treats students like little kids. He should understand students only pay attention in classes because professors talk about interesting things, not because phones and computers are banned. For a class that repeats industry leadership jargons and outdated concepts, 2 cumulative prelims and 1 final are more than excessive.
His classes are fun and insightful
Despite being at 8am, I really enjoyed the lectures. Learned a lot of applicable skills and Prof Newman is a great lecturer. Can get stressful when group project work picks up.
The workload can be a lot, but is doable as he gives plenty of in-class time to work on it. Appreciated the team learning environment. Great lecturer and participation is encouraged.

Having taken other 4 credit STEM courses here, I can say Newman gives an unreasonable amount of work for a 4-credit class. He gives us limited time (e.g. 48 hours) do a decent amount of work over the weekend. He often doesn't even create the content for us to work on until right before the weekends yet tells us not to procrastinate - hypocritical!

Group projects did not provide much learning and too focused on who was considered the best. Too much reliance on participation grade. Feedback received was elementary and hardly focused on descriptive content, rather on length of presentation or minor, irrelevant details. The discussions allowed for critical thinking. Disorganized at times.

Thinks that a 4-credit course is valid for giving hours of work for participation homework. Not even including the other individual homework, team project, team project homework, quizzes, final project, and a final exam we also have to complete for this class alone.
Horrible Professor!  Never had class, graded very hard, no feedback whatsoever

Horrendous professor. Canceled over 50% of classes because she was "sick" and e-mailed unnecessary assignments with arbitrary guidelines to try and make it look like she was doing her job. Learned almost nothing over the entire semester and could have taken the class online. Easy class with very strange paper grading but Bogel should be fired.

Great, great, professor. She clearly loves what she does and wants to share it with you. Easygoing about deadlines and such, very understanding. Definitely a worthwhile class, especially if you have to take a FWS.

Best FWS ever. Very nice lady, has free, fun, and insightful discussions about the interesting films she picks out. Short papers (2-3 pages) about each of the 6~7 movies watched, no long papers. Pretty easy and interesting class.

Amazing professor. I have never met someone with such interest in her field as well as interest in helping students understand her world of film. Didn't require any reading, watched great films, cancelled class a lot, and was very flexible with due dates. Best professor thus far.
good class, cancels class a lot, understanding with deadlines
This FWS rocks!  Despite haveing to go watch the movie once in a while, I don't think I have written a paper over 5 pages!  Also the material is actually interesting... and hey free movies!
Bogel is just cool; she cancels class all the time.  I heard all the other FWS profs sucked, so take Bogel.  She's easy, fun, and CANCELS class often.
Excellent professor. Flexible with deadlines, not too harsh on papers, and very knowledgeable about the subject. A class act.
Very nice and cool teacher who def enjoys cancelling class. Difficult grader but ultimately very fair. Movies are fun and Bogel is both funny and mad chill.
Prepare to get your mind bogeled.
Cancels ALL the time.  But the time spent not in class is made up by the time the movie screenings take up.  The class is great, but she's such a strict grader!!
Canceled half of her classes, wish I had known in advance, great discussion when there actually is class.

Very good discussion in class, but cancels many classes.  Enjoyable at first, but when you start getting poor grades for leaving out material that was never covered (because no classes were held) it gets annoying and unfair.  Fickle on grading.

Intelligent and interested in the material. Stretches meanings in the movies. The semester I had her she cancelled 25% of classes for some unknown reason. She's okay, but the writing seminar was good.
Hitchcock class is great.  Sometimes Prof. Bogel seems a bit unorganized, but she is extremely intelligent and makes the class interesting and fun.
She's very easy going and interested in the material. She is also a pretty fair grader.

She seems to have two personalities...one is the warm, easy going person you experience in class...the other is a very harsh grader that you only experience via email as all the assignments are done this way...

Though I really liked watching all the cool films, I'm not a fan of the course. Writing about movies, or even writing about literature/fiction, seems pointless to me. You often have to find meaning where there is none.Movies/books are meant to be enjoyed.
I took a movies FWS from Lynda. She's an awesome person and a great teacher. I also liked watching movies instead of reading books. :-)

To be fair, I was really excited for this class before I took it. You just talk about paradoxes the entire course. It's great. Just show up to lecture, minimal readings that are basically optional. Very helpful lecture notes distributed in class. Class makes you think. Explains things clearly and thoroughly. Grading was kind of tough though.

Grades hard, provides lecture notes but has no talent in teaching, other than reading off the notes. Awkward silence for 75 minutes is the essence of the class. SO many students opt to not show up even if attendance matters bc of that. His thick accent and obvious rambling in English is often hard to listen to...

Prof. Eklund is a nice guy, and pretty knowledgeable, but the class wasn't that great or interesting.  However, he has a great Swiss (I believe) accent.  And he is very approachable.  I don't recommend the class though.  The grading really depends on the TA.

The course turned out to be easy for me, but I can see where it could cause trouble for some people. Best avoid this one if you aren't comfortable with math and philosophy. Course reading was relatively unimportant, lectures were everything. Tests were pretty easy, I got a 100 on a prelim. Oh, and Eklund is great--smart, nice, and approachable.
He made exams unrealistically hard for what we learned and graded them entirely too harshly.  I think he also assumed that people generally had more knowledge than they actually did.
Semi-boring lecturer, but if you can stay awake, lectures are helpful in understanding homework and lab quizzes.
goes very fast, doesn't really seem to care

I had Professor Crane for CHEM 2070. He is a good teacher but sometimes his teaching style was not the best for the subjects we were learning. However, he does care for his students, and will help you if you go to his office hours. His prelims are formidable and very difficult, but if you put in solid effort you should be fine. I enjoyed Dr. Crane.

Dr. Crane made Chem 2070 a LITTLE better (just a smidge), but overall CRAZY CLASS! You either a) really have to love Chemistry or b) want to be a doctor super badly to get through this class without saying, "I HATE CHEMISTRY!"
The best gen. Chem professor. Willing to work with you if you ask.
Lectures were fairly clear and easy to follow. Does a lot of practice problems in class. Tries to make it interesting by doing a question every class.

Well played, Brian, well played. The lab reports were exhaustingly time-consuming. You could tell he planned his jokes in great detail before he came to class. He unnecessarily switched the chalkboard quite frequently. His voice cracked frequently during the semester and he tried to pass it off as a cold. Overall, fair testing but eh as a professor

The lectures were pretty engaging and he almost always did in class demos relating to what was lectured on. It was cool! The exams were fair, and his lectures were never boring. He always provided examples on the chalkboard which were very helpful. He would often crack a joke which is pretty nice for an early morning class.
Definitely better than Wolzcanski! The first half was clear, but pretty fast. Stay on top of things!
No
Everyday that goes by sitting in Wolczanski's lectures I miss Crane so much more. He's not the best, but with Wolczanski right next to him Crane feels like the best teacher ever.
Awesome professor, hard class
Definitely better than Wolczanski (or however you say his name).

Professor Crane was a pretty clear lecturer, however he was very condescending whenever I had a question or asked for help.  His tests were decent, but his rude attitude generally detracted from the class.

Fantastic professor. He usually goes over problems in class like the ones on the homework so you'll get an idea of how to do it. His lectures are pretty clear and understandable. His test wasn't that hard either, he's also funny and likable.
worship this man while you can
Great lecturer,  clear and methodical in the way he presents the information. Also a really nice guy.

Professor Crane is fairly clear (although his handwriting can be a little small). His lectures are pretty well organized and he gets all the information across. He seems to be a fairly well-natured and an understanding person. The prelim wasn't very difficult, just do what is required from the class (prob sets, study group, lec, discussion).

Brian is cool. He does a demo of a reaction every class so far except for today's lecture. He tries to be funny and create a relaxed atmosphere. He's good at explaining most topics. Very understandable.

The course content is boring, but he tries his best to make it interesting by including demos and interesting examples. He sometimes gets too theoretical, but most of the time explains things well. The tests are really hard, but they are curved. The textbook was really boring, and didn't really line up with the curriculum well.

OK professor. He teaches the material but not much more than that. Lectures are rather boring, but if you listen you'll be fine. Also the Labs don't line up with lecture material which is annoying. Class only has a few graded assignments, so light on work, but that just means each one matters. Some good chances to earn extra credit as well. every lecture has a quiz but super useful and almost exact same as exams

ENGRI 1160 was an easy class and he is a great professor. A little intimidating but I think he was great.

BEST PROF EVER!!! LOTS OF WORK AND DEMANDING

Unique course, great professor.
sweet class. doesn't matter if you are interested in construction planning and operations; you will be by the end.

She runs up and down the stairs and has a funny voice. But she's hilarious and you get to do arts and crafts in class.

Its actually incredible to think that not only is he extremely distinguished, having won more awards than one can count and is one of the top 100 chemists in the world, but he is extremely caring and compassionate torwards his students. Very thorough, engaging lecturer. Concerned with what students think, encourages questions. Extremely approachable during the lecture break, before, after and during OH. Thoughtful and understanding as well. If you need to take genetics, Spring is a good time! Plus, he's a yeast dude, unlike the Fall guy which is a Drosophila dude.

First-rate professor!  Excellent lectures- great explanations with occasional humor injected. Do/understand all book problems, as those are going to comprise the  majority of prelims. Tough class, grades maybe a bit deflated, but you'll learn a lot.
BEST TEACHER AT CORNELL! Lectures are always clear, he is incredibly helpful to meet with and always available- great to talk to about stuff other than genetics too!

Lectures were interesting/engaging most of the time... toward the end of the semester they became somewhat erratic and hard to follow. Overall, a very nice guy, very helpful if you ever see him around. Definitely do the hw problems!
He is way more interesting than the dude who teaches in fall. He's real nice and lively, so you wont be too bored by the tedious material.

Excellent professor!  His lectures are well-planned and organized.  The material is complicated, but he does a good job of explaining things.  It is impressive that he can make this subject interesting!  I would definitely recommend taking genetics with Dr. Fox.  Of course, the class itself is a pain, so better to not take it at all!
amazing professor. incredibly clear. always helpful if have any questions.
Wonderful professor. Definitely wants to communicate to his students well. Looks like Mark Twain a bit, but with a nice compact body (and what a butt).
Fox is an extremely good professor.  In preparation for exams, I suggest doing all problems assigned.
Great professor! His lectures are very enjoyable and easy to follow.  Make sure to take genetics in spring with Professor Fox!
Tom Fox is an excellent professor. His lectures are very clear and interesting, and it is surprisingly easy to stay awake for the two hour lecture. The lab, however, is far from enjoyable.
He's a great lecturer. Lab is the real killer, not the lecture. Take this class in the spring not fall, the fall professor is horrible.

This class is definitely difficult, but interesting and practical. Fox is a good lecturer- a little unorganized but tons better than Macintyre. Lab is a pain, problem solving is helpful. Tests really aren't that bad but you have to put LOTS of time into this course. Don't fall behind!!!!!

Hey Guys, c'mon, FOX is a nice guy. The lectures could be a little bit more structured and follow the test more. But, wow, you really get to appreciate Fox when Macentire came in a did a lecture. Fox was like 500 times better!

Profesor is extremely out of touch with the material on the exam. If you want to do well in the lecture part of the course go to all the Problem Sovling Sessions and do those problems. You should be fine. Lab is a ton of work. If you're interested in the material great class, otherwise stay away.
This class is difficult but interesting if you like biology. Fox is a good lecturer, very clear and helpful. He is an all-around nice guy and kept me awake and interested through a long lecture.
Fly with the hippies

The course subject is difficult, but I think Fox did a good job of teaching it.  He's one of the better lecturers I've had: speaks and writes on the board at just the right pace, so I usually don't have trouble with taking notes.

Yes, it may not be the easiest class, but to be honest I had a LOT more trouble with orgo.  I find the class interesting, and Fox is a great guy-easy to talk to about anything, real down to Earth.  I like his lectures.
The professor looks like a mouse. Actually, he reminds me of the Pinocchio's woodmaker. I like the way he stares into the space after he finishes a thought. Cracks us up and wakes us up.

Lecture had nothing to do with exam content. Lab pushed me to the brink of suicide. Head TA is a psychotic B*TCH who swears too much and treats students like SH*T. This class sucks--stay the hell away!

The class is pointless. all stuff we've learned in other classes, mainly Intro Bio. Lab's the killer. a violation of our constitutional rights in how many hours and days of lab work it requires. doesn't respect the religious sabbath. write a letter!!!

Prof. Grossman is by far one of the best professors I have ever had.  Her courses are challenging and cover a lot of material.  If you want to get an A+ in the class you should read the book and attend lecture.  Very fair grader and notices who participates.  Really enjoyed her classes and wish I could take more.

Although I wasn't very interested in the topic before taking the class, Dale's passion about the material and tendency to keep topics relevant to contemporary issues shaped my views about law and business. I would highly recommend this class to any communication major who's willing to work hard to learn a lot

B+ & never went to class. Only two tests (open book) but you can't bring TakeNote.
