Loved it

Good teacher.  Class is difficult, law material is very hard to understand.  The class time sucks, 8:40am.  If you have a choice, take law somewhere else, unless really ambitious, but if you have to take 320, don't worry, its not that bad.

Dale is a great professor. Always a stickler, dont waste her time, especially at office hours! But come with something to say, or ask, and she is an invaluable resource. The class is not that hard, spend a lot of time on the papers, go to office hours with the TAs before hand! The tests arent bad, just retype and reread the TakeNote, dont read book

She is not a bad prof.   The materials in class really help students to understand the basics of law in the business world.  Her TAs are very helpful.  The only problem is the early class time.  As she often says, it is not "very civilized".
excellent prof, highly recommended

Dale is incredible, with a sly sense of humor and tons of knowledge to give out to anyone who is interested. Her Comm Law class generates a lot of interesting discussion, and this class will defintely prepare you for a future in law.

Prof. Grossman is EXCELLENT. She does come off as a bit unapproachable at first. But do not fear her. She is very enjoyable and very knowledgeable of Law and Business. I highly recommend either taking a course of hers or speaking to her about any Law queries.

I had Dale for three classes and thought she was a brilliant, interesting, and helpful professor.  As luck would have it, she also became my advisor and was one of the most approachable professors I have ever encountered.

Seems intimidating at first but nice after all. Good at making things relevant, fair grader. 428 would be more fitting with a Communications program, not a Communication program like Cornell has (there is a difference). Still a worthwhile course.
Great teacher!  She's very approachable and always willing to help.  Only bad things about the class are that it's at 8:40 and there's a lot of reading.
Never really went to class but still learned a lot.
Dale is hot, hot, hot.  I take her classes just to watch her.
Looks like a certain famous Cornell alum but is very helpful and knows her stuff

she is mean when you ask for help

You have to be a fast note taker b/c tons of information on slides that are fine print. No electronics allowed in class! Be on time to every lecture! Try to ask specific or detailed questions as much as you can b/c vague ones don't get accurate answers. Go to office hours frequently to understand structure of assignments as much as possible.

Better communication skills needed and less words on the lecture slides, so information won't feel overwhelming when trying to take notes in a 50 min class. This class is fairly confusing when it comes to completing assignments. Overall, this class needs better structure and order to provide a more effective learning environment for students.

Dr. Loss really enjoys teaching. He has such a passion for food. From his culinary background to his food science expertise, he is the perfect man for the job. Chris Loss is definitely not the most organized guy, but he is caring and very knowledgable about his subject matter. I took an intro level class with him and had a generally good time. He is not super accessible as a professor, but when you do get in contact with him he is helpful and passionate.

Dr. Loss has is sometimes disorganized but has an incredible breadth of knowledge on what he teaches. I learn a TON with every conversation with him in and outside of class. I recommend being very involved in the classes he teaches. You will get a lot out of it if you let yourself.

Love Dr. Loss! As a food sci major, I loved being able to take this class and it got me excited for my major. Material is pretty easy to understand and as long as you do the work you will pass. Dr. Loss and the TAs give clear instructions with assignments and when to sign up for prototype sessions. The final was open book even before COVID got bad.
Have had Professor Loss for 4 classes at this point, and all of them have been a mess. Very disorganized, and the FDSC department likes to put him in charge of every class for some reason.

Nice guy, but didn't make enough effort to be professional to students in the class. He didn't show up to lab, cancelled plenty of assignments last-minute due to his lack of organization. Couldn't get his act together but still held his students to a ridiculous expectation of perfection when it came to grading and turning in on time.
Lots of work. Very passionate about Gulf. Learned a lot but the readings were very dense. Also not the most approachable.

topic was 'globalization in the persian gulf'. didn't buy any books bc readings were instructor provided! participation (via discussion and weekly canvas reading reflection) IMPORTANT. 3 analytical essays (5-6 pg). not easy, but fair grader. discussions and readings were enlightening and engaging! highly recommend this class! yay Emilio!

I heard from a friend that Professor Odato would be an easy grader, and at Cornell I feel like that is hard to come by. The project has no rubric no matter how much you ask. Then you get a random grade a few peers come up with. Its just a shame there are not other good ML classes available. it forces people to take this class.

very accomplished person but atrocious professor... put out one of the most poorly prepared prelims i have ever seen at cornell and came up with a very unfair and universally hated peer grading scheme that students abused to help themselves in terms of the curve

I find it difficult to believe that Cornell University would include this professor in its team of excellent professors. You can just skip class because the lectures are worthless. Rarely am I compelled to post a review on Rate My Professor but this class was so horrible and utter garbage that I must insist. The class is hard for no reason at the expensive of learning, I can probably find more help from Scooby Doo than the Professor and TA team. There is no transparency in grading. Don't take any of her classes stay far away.

Udell's explanations were so unclear to the point that I had to google everything she said - the Internet did a much better job than her in teaching. She made us do peer grading - this coupled with non-transparent grading incentivized students to sabotage their peers.

Probably one of the worst classes I've taken at Cornell. Udell is a confusing lecturer, and the TAs for the class are very focused on not giving you the answers to problem sets, even if it comes at the expense of a student's understanding. He's a great guy. He was extremely helpful in office hours and his tests/quizzes were very fair. He made it very clear what material would be on the exam. However, his exams are difficult, but if you put in the work, you will succeed.

He's a great professor. I Learned a lot from him. He's also got great stories from his time in research labs and industry.
very kind and caring
i loved sogah he is kind and really cares about his students

one of my worst professors ever. Lectures are absolutely useless and he rambles on and on. Prelims are fair though and come straight from psets, fridays sessions and notes

Awful professor. Does not really care about students or grades. Lectures are pretty useless, very disorganized and prelims can have questions that will throw you for a loop. Do reading and the problem sets and you'll be fine, but forget about actually learning anything from the professor.

Sogah seems like he really cares about his students with his many OH and friday sessions. That being said, I thought that he was a terrible lecturer. He is bad at explaining concepts clearly and moves very fast. I stopped going after 1 week and just looked at the book. Everything he says is straight from the book. Extremely helpful and wants his students to do well (Fri review sessions and lots of OH). Get weekly help, do the PS when they are assigned, stay on top of readings and you will be fine.  People who complain about orgo just don't do the work necessary to do well.  Prelim averages are so low b/c people don't study, not because tests are too hard.
Sogah is the real deal- if you cannot learn chemistry from this man you are simply a joke and i hope you get rejected from medical school

I got a B in 357 and decided that I wanted to do better in 358--so I actually started reading, working, trying--I went to his office hours to clarify things, and sometimes went to the Friday sessions (not vital for the class)and got an A.  Do all the problem sets. Go to lecture to see what he emphasizes. Don't be intimidated by him. Fair prelims.

terrible at teaching; accent difficult to understand; does not explain well

Overall good professor-not as entertaining as Ruttledge, but not as difficult. Passionate about chem, and offers Fri. problemm solving session-VERY helpful for prelims. Sticks mostly to the book. Polymer stuff isn't actually that bad. Work hard and you'll succeed in 358.

MUCH EASIER than last semester. Tests are succinct and straight-forward. Sure, he isn't Tom Ruttledge. Horrible teacher, just wants to screw peoples GPAs over.  Gives impossible tests with means under 50/100. Mumbles into the board. Lectures out of the book. Teaches things to memorize, tests on concepts.

Better than 357. Prelims are pretty fair and actually test what you learned.

Professor Sogah, although is a nice guy, is an awful teacher. He mumbles and most of the class consists of the phrase, "This does that"  I learned very little in lecture. Despite everyone else's comments, I really like Professor Sogah. I especially like his one-on-one office hour sign up sheet he has at each class. Friday problem solving sessions were great for exams. Not as good as the other prof

one of the worst professors ever - doesn't care about students, is just a terrible lecturer

Not a good teacher, explains things very badly, doesn't try to help students.

This class is the laziest A. I never went to class, never read an assignment. This class is not at all and easy A and it is very stupid. Asks about the most random stuff on the tests that you won't even know is important when your at lecture. Dont be fooled
Interesting topic and Professor Monroe is passionate during lectures!

Really easy class if you got to lecture and pay attention. Worth going to office hours just to talk to him.
Incredible professor. Take all of his courses if you get the chance. Favorite at Cornell. Might minor is NES because hes so amazing.

I took this just out of casual curiosity about Egypt and now I'm pursuing a major in Archaeology if that tells you anything about how great this class is. Prof is funny, engaging, gives great lectures that make use of all kinds of media. You will get an expert internal timeline of Ancient Egypt 4000BC-300BC. Take this class!!!!

Maybe this course benefited from the switch to online, but I thought it was super worth it overall -- Professor Monroe was compelling and funny, clearly has a genuine passion for the subject, and the class in general is just pretty chill / interesting.
I took this class just to fulfill the degree requirements but it ended up being one of the best classes I have ever taken at Cornell.

Monroe is clearly very passionate about Egyptology. He is very good at lecturing and I learned a lot about Ancient Egypt from this class. Exams were all multiple choice, matching, and true or false questions. It is extremely easy to do well if you put some effort into it.

This professor has the most monotonous voice I have ever heard, and the content is pretty boring unless you were interested in it prior to this class - you probably won't be interested in it after this class. few good jokes from the professor here and there but if you try and pay attention you will fall asleep. Material sometimes interesting, but prof is boring aside from the rare joke. However, prof is very nice. Papers require a lot of work. Studying  just memorizing all the slides for exams. If you're interested in the topic, it's a great class. The exams were all straight memorization (esp. with the literature excerpts) from lecture powerpoints. Very easy to do well if you can memorize/cram well. Readings were assigned but not necessary to do well or pass.

This class is extremely boring and I learned  nothing. Going to lectures was pointless, I never opened the textbooks, and all I did was cram 24 hours before the test. It is all about memorizing the lecture slides, and there is a crazy amount of info (esp, for final). Would not recommend this. (not an easy A)

Monroe was pretty dry and monotonous overall, despite the occasional funny moment. I was really excited to take the course, but I was thoroughly disappointed by it. Monroe made little effort to make it challenging, and there was no analysis involved whatsoever. If you're looking for an interesting history course, look elsewhere.

Boring unless your into nautical archaeology which is really boring btw.  Sign in sheet every lecture, class  is all powerpoints which he puts online, only midterm/final & attendence grades, no essays, easy A if you cram well for the mid/final, really easy A if you can somehow pay attention in class

Honestly, I could have worked a lot harder in this class. Obviously I only have myself to blame for not getting an A, but I don't recommend taking this class just for an "easy A." You should actually be interested in the material, otherwise, it's surprisingly dry. Monroe does have his funny moments, though. He's a nice guy.

Somehow ended up with an A, but absolutely did not take this class the right way. Should've gone to class more often, and when I actually did, should've paid more attention. He's pretty boring, but can have some funny moments (according to the people who paid attention). Is a very nice and understanding man---gave a 7 point curve on the hard final
This is certainly an okay class and awesome if you get into it, but it's not a piece of cake, like I thought it would be. Be aware of this when you enroll.
Prof. Monroe is awesome. I had Ancient Egyptian Civilization with him last spring. He's always excited about what he's teaching which makes the subject interesting.
Great professor! Made nautical archaeology really interesting. Made me want to go to class. Sometimes the material was repetitive, but I think it was just the content of the course not the professor.
Amazing prof and amzaingly easy yet extremely interesting class. Go for it!

He's such a great professor. He's clearly incredibly excited about his material and his enthusiasm is contagious. He really makes his lectures funny and interesting, while still full of real information. The material isn't hard at all, but attend lectures, please, because they're just so good. It's be a shame to take his class and not go.

Prof. Monroe is robably the best prof. I've ever had.  He is hilarious and makes lectures so interesting, but he is also clearly interested in making his students as enthusiastic as he is about the subject.  Take any class that he teaches!  He is great and incredibly easy.

Prof. Monroe is an incredibly entertaining lecturer! The quizzes are very fair if you pay attention in lecture and do the readings. A full page cheat sheet is allowed for the final. He is always willing to give advice on papers and is easy to talk to. His enthusiasm in the subject matter comes through in his lectures. Great class!
An okay class if you need to fulfill an arkeo requirment. Quizzes given often and essays were graded harshly but professor is one of the nicest people you will ever meet
He doesn't really lecture, lets the students teach the class so you don't learn much, but I got a decent grade and it was easy so I can't complain too much

Monroe deeply cares about his students. He gives extensive feedback on essays, which I found very valuable. The reading list is long, but interesting, and is partially built on student recs. Discussion sometimes felt disorganized, but his passion for literature made the class worthwhile.

I really enjoyed Prof. Monroe's class  COML 2020 Great Books  it's a decent amount of reading material, but they're all "great" picks, which made the class so enjoyable. Monroe's discussions are engaging, and he's just a really great professor overall. He cares about the success of his students, and his delight for his work is infectious.
Great professor

Prof. Monroe was inspiring and spread his firm belief in the humanities to this entirely freshman class. Extremely insightful and great editor. Class discussions were engaging and he made sure everyone had a chance to speak. Well-rounded knowledge and interest in various cultures.

Brilliant, insightful, and knowledgeable. He is an amazing professor who encourages students to really dig deep. No worries if you can't. He's always there to help out and lead you in the right direction. His essay feedbacks are incredibly detailed and honest, and he's always available for office hours to talk about anything you want.

I had Prof Monroe for both ENGL 3910&4960. He's honestly one of the best professors here at Cornell. If you have any interest in the subject matter, take his classes! He is so passionate & knowledgable with all the material & his enthusiasm transfers to his students. I've also produced some of the best writing in his class, and I have him to thank.

Professor Monroe is arguably the most knowledgeable professors I have had at Cornell. He demonstrates a clear passion and knowledge of world poetry. By the end of the semester, you'll have some understanding, too. He's really flexible about papers and gives students a lot of freedom to write about the literature they want to from the course.

Great and motivational instructor. He is very caring about his students and is reasonable. Though his lectures may be dry at times, they are very educational and rich. Definitely one of the better professors in this university!

He's a highly knowledgeable professor, very patient and understanding especially when it comes to deadlines. The classes are mainly focused around the discussions, which in my experience are always engaging without ever turning into lectures. I'd definitely recommend his classes to anyone, one of the best professors you could hope for.

Not always the clearest when he speaks in class and pretty disorganized- there were many books he put on the optional book list that we ended up having to read for class, and the syllabus is vague. Only grades are long papers, two presentations and participation. Not my favorite Comp Lit class.
Shes very kind and engaging and approaches the material in a really unique way. Made me actually not upset to wake up early to go to class. Highly recommend.

Professor Monroe is phenomenal! She presents her material in a very clear and concise manner. She is engaging. She is thoroughly invested in the well-being of her students. She is fair and honest. If you ever have the chance to take a course with her, you must!

Monroe is the sweetest lady ever.. her class was awesome, super enlightening, and she really tried to make it interesting for everyone in the class. The books we used were pretty dense, and long readings, but class discussions made up for them.
Enlightening lectures, workload not too burdensome.

Professor Monroe is absolutely amazing! This was one of my favorite classes. I regularly looked forward to our class discussions. There is a LOT of reading, but make sure to do the bible readings and as much else as you can. The final exam questions were a little unexpected, but my final paper for this class was one of my favorite research papers.

She is one of the best professors I have had a Cornell. This class , thanks to Professor Monroe, was extremely interesting and I learned A LOT. The class is "easy" but you have to put a lot of time into understating the material. I ended up understanding so much more of the course at the end of all her assignments and exams.
Class is certainly worth taking on any level of interest.
Taught material that she was genuinely interested in, and tests allowed students to show what they learned instead of random facts they had forgotten.  Informative and pleasant class.
Professor Monroe is very sweet and helpful, and she is very clear with which topics are most important to know.  She's enthusiastic and interesting.  The testing system is nearly enjoyable.
Prof Monroe is wonderful! The class is discussion based, and it's pretty interesting. I loved it!

I didn't really attend a lot of the lectures (cause they were optional) but I thought I'd nevertheless leave a review for the class. The class content was extremely interesting and insightful. Just download the textbook "Networks, Crowds and Markets" and read through some parts. You'll know whether you wanna take this class.

Difficulty of this class made a 180 compared to last year. Practice problems before the two exams were useless as not even 1/3 of the problems made it onto the exam. If you're looking for easy liberal studies and have a rough workload definitely think again. You have to read the textbook and camp office hours, not what I expected for 3 credits.

i cant believe people thought this course was easy. midterms/finals are so advanced compared to psets and practice exams it was like whiplash. every time i felt like i understood something it got flipped upside down the next chapter or on the exam. i was an office hours warrior and barely passed. genuinely saw someone cry during the final today too

Easley and Kleinberg are the original authors for the textbook and them teaching the class is ABSOLUTELY GOATED. It was extremely eye-opening to hear him share his past experiences and it is obvious that he is extremely intelligent. Also very very kind during office hours. Best class I've ever taken at Cornell -- made me change my way of thinking.
Superb class, extremely applicable, and grading was both fair and unbiased. Anybody saying otherwise has cope levels off the charts, probably because they need to reevaluate their IQ score
AMAZING AND SO CLEAR -- HE MADE THE CLASS CONTENT SO EASY TO UNDERSTAND AND INTERESTING!

Networks gets a bad rap, as I never found it to be that bad. Lectures were clear (sometimes boring), but textbook a great resource if still confused. People got mad at the weekly HWs and they are kinda annoying but I never found them to be too difficult. Easley does his best to make lecture interesting, but the class was a bit forgettable overall

Amazing class and professor! It was a super interesting class, but there is a lot of work. weekly hw assignments that take a few hours to complete, but if you take time and do them well, the tests are easy and straight forward just like the hw.
The lectures are fantastic. The class is not easy but worth taking.

Dr. Easley makes PhD microeconomics clear and easy to understand. He knows the material inside and out and knows how to present it to the class. He is just as helpful outside of class, and is incredibly helpful in office hours. The class wasn't easy, but it was all fair.

Class: Networks. Very organized class. Most people wouldn't show up. It was pretty easy overall. Professor Easley did a great job at getting the content across. The average final grade was an A I think.
He's good at explaining hard to understand concepts in an easy-to-understand manner. Silky, butter-like, rich voice. He would have been a great sports commentator.

Networks is an easy class. Maybe it was made easy by Easley and Kleinberg's ability to teach, but truthfully I don't think teaching this material would be challenging for anyone. I would love to see what Easley could do in an intense economics course. He seems very smart and very personable.
Very good
Great lecturer and taught mostly from the textbook. The textbook is legally free to download digitally; print copies are $40.
Easley is easily one of the best profs I've had. Really nice guy and very happy to discuss material in office hours.
I prefer Kleinberg but Easley comes really close. Both great lecturers.
great + dedicated

Excellent class, highly recommended! Slow and steady coverage of material, easy, especially if you have prior experience in game theory (I did). Very good explanations of material. Better handwriting than Kleinberg. Easy tests and homework. Free electronic textbook is not necessary unless you don't understand the notes or want to go deeper.
Easley lectures to us as if we're two year olds. Networks is  boring but ridiculously easy. Class is optional because he recites what is in the textbook, verbatim.

there is not much work to do. the test is not very hard, but the grading system is kind of harsh. last year this class was a median A class, but this year I DONT THINK SO.i have pretty good GPA and i got the lowest grade on this class. the material is interesting though. if you are taking this class for GPA booster, think about it again

econ 204 / cs 285 Networks - great class, easy , interesting, little work and little reading to do . easley lectures very clearly, almost painstakingly slow over some material --- not hard to get an A.

This prof is pretty cool but his class is deceptive. It might seem easy at first but things just come like a torrent of information. Stay on top of your material you are almost guaranteed an B+/A-. His lectures are pretty interesting.

Easley is a very capable professor and definitely knows what he's talking about. His lectures were good, although I still slept through/missed a lot. But that's just me. Homeworks are doable and graded easily. Prelims are almost exactly like the example ones he gives you from the previous year.

easley is an amazing prof, one of the best at cornell.  he takes a drab subject and makes it approachable and bearable. the problem sets are hard but they are graded easily, and while the exams are tough, easley's teaching makes up for it.  i highly recommend this class.

Easley is an awesome professor. Period. He is fair. He grades without a curve so the smartasses don't hurt your grade. He tells you exactly how hard the class will be from the start. He has realistic expectations. Lecture is mandatory, but never boring. He's good at giving an intuition for econ.

Great lecturer.. you must attend class. Makes material much easier than it has to be. Willing to work with you, but is very busy (understandable with a 150 person class). Don't take Microecon with anyone other than him.

Easley is an excellent professor. His lectures are very clear and organized, and he uses interesting examples to supplement the sometimes dry material. Exams and problem sets are challening (somewhat) but you get used to it. Almost no understanding of calc is needed, he teaches it all.

This was my first econ class, and I can't praise Easley enough! He had great lectures and was always clear, organized, thoughtful, and provided many examples.  His weekly problem sets were very do-able, although it takes a little getting used to.  Same goes for the exams.  One of the best.

Teaches very well. Comes up with creative examples, and makes the dry material a bit better. As much as this is econ for engineers and calculus is expected, you barely need to understand a derivative.
Extremely helpful and clear, engaging, great professor. Very recommended.
Tough but fair, great instructor (for econ!)
Smooth lectures and fair exams.  A rarity for Cornell!!
great teacher.  great course
I admit that the course is well taught, but I suppose I just don't get economics.  Be aware that this course is DESIGNED FOR ENGINEERS!!!!
The class is deceptive. Everyone seemed to get a lower grade than their grades warranted. Only take the class if you have to, because it kinda blows.
Easley is a very good lecturer, using good examples and always making the material as interesting as it possibly can be. This is way better to take than ECON 313.  Plus, the TA's grade pretty easy.
Very dry. Methodical. Robotic, even.
He makes a difficult, boring subject somewhat easier to handle. The examples are well thought out and makes a topic simpler to grasp.
Seems like a nice guy.  The 75 minute lecture is a little long and gets boring towards the end.  However, he manages to come up with interesing/amusing examples to keep our attention.
clear and precise, great lecture.
Great Chest man!
Gotta love that open shirt!

He made the learning outcome thing much better this sem. I liked it a lot personally. His lectures were pretty solid. Kinda rushed at the end a little since content was harder. Course is generally smooth sailing until u hit Fourier Series/PDEs. Just practice PDEs a lot b4 the final and use the inner product shortcut when u can, it makes life easier

The Mastery system was a complete trainwreck last fall, and I was scared when I learned Freund would be implementing it as well. However, his version of the system was far superior to Ritz's and as long as you stay on top of things, it's honestly a nice system. Quizzes were fair, prelims were a little harder. Lectures were not great, not terrible.
Amazing lecturer!!! This class was much easier than I was led to believe

Very nice guy and seems like he is a good professor, but the way he teaches makes no sense. Students have to teach themselves new concepts, and get thrown hard questions about what we taught ourselves the next day in class. Might just be Calc 1 in general, not sure
Great professor with amazing lectures.
Not only the best math teacher I have ever had, but one of the kindest people out there. Lecturing is his second nature; participate in class and you'll get so much out of it.
Good prof. You can tell he's taught before. Not sure if he or delp made the tests this year but they were fairer than most past years.
He does aerial silks and bakes cookies for his class. 10/10 would recommend
Draga was always available for help outside class and was patient with all my questions. I found it a little hard to follow along in class, but her helpfulness made up for that.

The professor teaches the content with enthusiasm, which makes the class more engaging. Getting cheat sheets is a huge plus for exams + finals, and with enough time and effort, all content is understandable, just a bit time-consuming.

He would definitely be better at lecturing to higher-level students, but the actual content is very understandable and it is very easy to succeed in this class. You get to have cheat sheet(s) on every exam and there are a lot of different components that go into your final grade. It can sometimes be time consuming but is pretty straightforward.

Pretty nice and accommodating teacher. Attendance is not mandatory so I didn't really go to lecture but reviewed recordings and crammed before tests. Allows cheatsheets for exams which was helpful. Overall material was digestible

Don't do all the readings. The lectures are adequate enough to understand the material. Dr. Cleland does a great job explaining concepts and is open to questions. Use the practice questions at the end of the textbook to study. Do the assignments and quizzes in regular weekly study groups to make them more fun.

Overall, he was generally accommodating, however this semester after finals he changed the grading percentages, and I went from getting an A+ to an A. This is extremely unfair, and he even implied that he did this to lower peoples grades. No professor of mine has completely changed the grading last minute to screw over their students so beware.

Prof. Cleland is an awesome and kindhearted professor, but he can be nit-picky about the grading. Go to OH and review your homework questions with a TA before you submit; otherwise, you can miss points even if you understood the question. Go to lecture and take detailed notes, then transcribe those onto your exam cheat sheet. You'll get an A.

Tons of homework, esp. if you do the 4-credit option. Thom (as he signs his emails) is an interesting guy teaching a *very* dry subject. Intro stats can be memorized, which makes it pretty boring. I don't go to lecture and I just read the slides so I'm not a great judge of his teaching abilities. Very easy class, however, as he grades v reasonably.

Easy class if you put in the effort to read the textbooks. Prelims are open-note, but you don't really even need the notes: the information isn't that hard. Lectures are kinda a doozy but he's a nice guy with some funny moments.
GOAT. Interesting topic. Class is mainly paper-based with one group final project. Prof. Ellis is great.

Professor Ellis is one of the nicest and most genuine professors I have had at Cornell. The course material on Idea Theft was extremely interesting, and the class was taught in a manner that made it even more so. Couldnt recommend more highly.
Best Professor! Super down to earth and brilliant - learn in a really fun environment. Would recommend taking any class by her, especially for ILR students

Professor Ellis is definitely the best professor I've had while at Cornell. She is so kind and caring, and makes sure to personally get to know each of her students. She is so passionate about her course material, and passes this excitement on to anyone who takes the class. I can't recommend this class or this professor enough, definitely take!!!

Amazing to have as a teacher and mentor!! She is both passionate about and an expert in her field, but still always listens and encourages her students to contribute their own experiences and follow their outside interests. Super interesting/engaging class-- I'd love to take another one soon

Lily is an absolute gem! She makes a great mentor for research I was doing with her and I learned a ton. She is very accessible outside of class to help with anything (personal, academic, professional). If you do your work, you'll do well--she's veryyyy reasonable. She is hilarious, knowledgeable, and a great professor!

Lily was my TA for ILRLR 2040 and ILROB 1220 and the PI for my research lab. She is by far the most dedicated and engaging TA I ever worked with at Cornell. She works with you to make the material clear and assigns interesting and relevant readings. More than that, she is hilarious and genuinely cares about her students.
really interesting research group on IP, psych, and law. she was great and enjoyed every minute of our research together
Lily is AWESOME -- one of the best TAs I've ever had. Very reasonable expectations. Participation and discussion matter the most, and she'll work with you if you're struggling
This guy always go on tangents during lecture so we never know what shows up on the test and what doesn't.

Good professor. Often goes on tangents and ends up missing material, so if you like biology that's a problem. If you're doing it for the requirement you might like that since his stories are often pretty funny. No need to buy the text.

Dr. Loew is my favorite professor so far at Cornell. He is very interested in the topic he's teaching and tells some hilarious stories. Make sure you go to lecture! He goes through the slides very quickly and puts very few words on them. If you aren't in class you will have no idea what it was about. Go to office hours and ask questions.
Pretty easy. Do the readings and pass. They got rid of the curve that was there in the past because they would have had to curve grades down.
Dr. Loew falls asleep when Silva is teaching, which is pretty hilarious. His lectures are interesting and worth attending. Pay attention and don't fall asleep!

Nice guy, but if you are not that interesting in comparative physiology or bio- this is not the class for you. He goes through slides too quickly so it is hard to follow sometimes. you NEED TO SHOW up to class because the book over explains. the tests are hard, but easier than they were in past years. lots of TF & multiple choice. record lectures!!
So funny!  And a great guy.  Tough class though.  Be prepared to study a lot and ask him questions.  A little effort goes a long way.  He cares if you care!

Best class I have taken at Cornell! Dr. Loew is brilliant as both an instructor and a scientist. I love how he infuses his engineering knowledge to make real, concrete sense of physiological processes. Dr. Loew is a great teacher and, more importantly, a great man. He has been a joy to learn from. And he is hysterical.

Great professor and a fantastic academic advisor!  He's an all-around great person to talk to, about class work or anything else.  His lectures are some of best I have attended at Cornell, and his understanding and relating of animal physiology to his students is crystal clear, informative, and thought-provoking.
Funny guy and a good lecturer. Gets off topic sometimes but I still think he was a great teacher.
review sessions are extremely helpful. definitely argue for points after the tests if you think you have a legitimate reason. great guy, wants you to learn. best professor i've had so far

Great professor! Lectures are interesting. Exams are hard, but you can argue for more points afterwards. Go to the review sessions!!! He tells you everything (and I mean everything) you need to know for the exam. Definately take this class if you are interested in physiology.

Incredibly knowledgeable. Really willing to work with students. He wants you to argue for more points- wants to see effort more than the right answer. Lectures are heavy but I guess that's just the material. His review sessions cover EVERYTHING- total lifesavers. Definitely the most encouraging professor in the sciences.

Great class and even better professor.Insanely knowledgeable man, believe every word he says.Physics incorporation is great too.Extremely clear, well presented lectures, and his grading scheme rocks.This man knows how to teach, and loves it!Tests are hard, but talking to Loew helps your grade,and he's always willing to help you.
Good teacher, but all over the place..very scatter-brain. Not very organized. Likes to bring physics into bio, which is decent (he's got a 1st and 2nd degree in engineering)... otherwise, cool guy.
Very nice, always willing to help.  However, is buffoon.  Gave up on lecturing about 1/3rd way through semester.  Tests are on random pieces of knowledge, play Jeopardy to prepare for exams.

Very funny, great attitude in lecture and informative.  Makes things very clear if you have trouble.  His choice in TA's though...not so good so if you have questions, ask him.  Tough exams - hint - he likes beer, give him a nice present and he'll remember.

He's a great professor, he's really entertaining. You probably won't do well on the exams, but don't worry, that has nothing to do with your grade in the course. definitely take it if you're interested in physiology.
argue about your grade and he will give you points even if you are wrong, seriously. he likes it.

Really interesting lectures, easy class.

Tests were made to be difficult and sometimes vague.  The professor was not willing to budge with grading criteria, which she would sometimes refuse to release.  Additionally, she was impossible to talk to and always assumed you were not starting  your work early enough if you became overwhelmed with the project, homework, and exam studying.

Took a very long time to grade. Lectures were not engaging or adaptive and she was a very strict grader on top of that. Gave contradictory advice for writing and tests were not as advertised. Worst prof I have worked with in the department as well. Not sure why Cornell admin assigned her this class as it's her first year and this is a req class.

Worst Professor I have had by far in the CRP department. Grading was unfair, never returned in a timely manner, and harsh. Lectures were profusely dense with the containment of far too much information, as well as extremely fast-paced because she writes down a script of what to say. Exams and papers were difficult, lengthy, and lacked correlation.

Jerrie is an amazing professor and extremely kind and helpful, especially to pre-vet students. She has an enormous wealth of experience and knowledge that she is happy to share, and does so frequently through her courses and while advising students. Definitely take her class, and get to know her!
Dr. Gavalchin is amazing! The best professor at Cornell, insanely helpful to all students, especially pre-vets!

Dr. Gavalchin is amazing! So helpful and always responds to emails quickly. Lectures are straightforward, sometimes she can be a little quiet and not energetic while lecturing but she clearly knows what she's talking about. Exams are very reasonable.

Professor Gavalchin is always willing to help and provide excellent advice.  Definitely a professor that you should have as an advisor if you are pre-vet.  Also, the class was pretty helpful and interesting, it shows you what else is out there.

I had Diane for PE 1100 (beginning swim) and she made learning to swim super easy and not scary at all. I think the entire class ended up passing the swim test by the end of the semester. I really appreciated her feedback and thought she was kind, but also knew exactly how to help students if they were struggling.
Worst professor yet at Cornell. Does not care about students well-being and has horrible TA's that grade very unfairly and erroneously.
Great! Just make sure to sit closely, as he is a soft speaker
Comrade Gross was a chill Professor. The class is one big paper and participation. Be prepared for lots of conversation. The man speaks truth to justice.

no work except 20-30 pg paper. He gives no input or direction until you hand in the draft which was harshly graded by a TA. Grade 50% participation based but you don't really have to do any of the readings to participate. Gross is very biased and espouses tons of communist views. He enjoys when students challenge him but is very biased in grading

As a graduating senior, Gross was one of my favorite profs. He has a strong opinion, but approaches topics by challenging the status quo. Class is meant to be discussion based, so those with opposing beliefs are encouraged to speak out. The class itself is not too challenging, yet hugely rewarding.

Professor Gross is a completely biased individual.  He spends his entire lecture espousing his socialist ideals, urging us comrades to join him in the fight against the evil corporations. He is extremely forgetful and tends to repeat things he has already taught.  Don't ever ask him for advice on papers, he doesn't even look at them, his TA grades.
To be honest I didn't like this class. The way he taught made the class painful and if you disagreed with him he would normally just blow off your argument. He's far too opinionated.
Quiet bias, doesn't really budge on any point so there's not point except to sit there a let him talk at you... sad really. There is the one paper, make sure you write what he wants.

Nice guy, but seriously, the most biased professor you will ever have.  Doesn't just disagree on certain economic philosophies, he derides and often curses about them.  I felt very uncomfortable in this class because of his opinion of the value of my beliefs.  I can deal with liberal professors but Gross treated me like an idiot based on politics.

Great guy. One of the nicest, most helpful, and most well-respected profs in ILR, and he knows a ton about human rights and the workplace. That said, he has strong liberal views which he seems to expect you to support in your papers.  He also really reads papers thoroughly and will pick them apart. CB383 is a great 4-cred class tho, not much work.
Nice person but final grade is completely disconnected from the grades you receive in class. It is based on what he "thinks you contributed to the course." In other words, who he likes the most.

STAY away. One guy's dad died a week before the paper was due and the Prof. would not give an extension. Also, he tears your paper into shreds. Ten papers (in all classes) this semester all A's except this one C-. nice guy hard Prof.
No Comments
Great guy, extremely helpful and understanding, an excellent professor who really cares about his students and is excellent in his field, highly recommended.
the best looking 75 year old man I know
Great Professor.  Classes are straightforward and the assignments are challenging but doable.  I found his material and perspective to be useful in the engineering field.

Nice guy, but rambled a lot and took forever to get to the point and deliver a simple idea. Took off points on homework for really trivial things, like including units in your spreadsheet if his example one didn't have it, or not multiplying by 1. Also had a strange habit of addressing students as Mr./Ms. (last name).
great teacher who puts a lot of effort into class material understandable and applicable
Great course, professor made class very interesting and graded fairly

Professor McKee is a great lecturer and professor. They always try to make the class interesting and applicable to the real world. The work can be a lot but he is always willing to help students when needed! I would absolutely take another class with him!

One of the kindest professors I've encountered. He has great lectures, which are all recorded and posted, and is really good at explaining complex topics. Exams have a group portion at the end to boost your grade, and he is very fair overall with grading. Overall a great professor and human being.
Very accessible and understanding professor. He is willing to help in Econ3030 and is a professor economic majors should get to know.

Loved ECON 3030 with McKee though it was difficult at times to keep up paticularly as someone who took the class freshman fall. There's quite a bit of content in the course so it's important to keep up by going to office hours and to discussion sections. The TAs are really good so do take advantage of their help.

The exams were pretty tough and made sure you did all the homeworks legit and understood them. In person lectures aren't required in the sense you could make them up later. Quizzes were just tedious (but some of the questions showed up on the exams so make sure to do them). His lectures were very useful and him and a student were very active on ED.

Great professor with really great lectures. He is very active on Ed and quickly responds to emails. Very open to adapt to students' needs. Sometimes the homeworks were huge and also not the biggest fan of the PollEv's but you can do them after the class if you miss the lecture. Fair exams.

Exams aren't about how well you know the material, but about how much can he twist the material so that he can get the bell curve. 
Covers a lot of material in one class, make sure to study every week. He's a good prof, but exams just don't fairly reflect what we have studied or done in class/psets.
Best Econ professor for core classes by far. Teaches difficult material in an accessible way, but you will still have to put in the effort.

Bad comments are disappointing. He is an expert in economics education, truly the best Cornell prof. He can cover so many topics on time but also make you comprehend the important parts by giving you intuition without confusing you. GO TO THE LECTURES, they are well planned, you won't need to study much later. Very inspirational if you like econ!
Absolute goat.... this man makes a strong case for fav prof all time
Good guy

The class lacks a lot of substance relating to some very important concepts. Problem sets are nothing like the exams and are often long and repetitive, not really helping you improve much. Exams are pretty easy, but he tends to make them long for little substantive reason. Also, there is a really annoying group project that just super tedious.

Lots of econ majors love McKee. Very caring/accommodating but also fair. Teaches one of the most important core courses in econ and makes it worth your while. His "flipped classroom" technique wasn't my favorite, but it at least keeps people engaged during lecture. Class is even accessible to non-econ majors. He's just goated. Hope he sticks around

McKee is one of my favorite professors. I hadn't taken a math class in years, but he explained things clearly in class and was very accessible in office hours. The problem sets and the practice prelims were EXTREMELY helpful to learn and to study. I literally just did the practice prelims several times to study and got A's. Excellent teacher.
Excellent professor! Long problem sets (I would definitely work with other people on these, which he encourages) but I learned a ton! I'm glad I took this class with professor mckee.

Amazing teacher! Professor McKee genuinely cares about his students & their learning. He's super helpful in office hours, especially for problem set and lecture questions. The textbook isn't necessary (I didn't even use it) but participation is VERY helpful. Also, the previous exams are a great way to study!!
Overall 10/10 great prof!
Incredible and passionate lecturer that truly stands out for his great ability at communicating the material. Would absolutely take any course with Professor McKee again!

One of the more overrated professors in the Econ department. He gives very superficial explanations for the concepts covered in the class and doesn't seem to care if students understand the underlying math and statistics. If you're looking for a class where you'll learn and be challenged, don't take this class.

McKee is a fantastic lecturer and really approachable outside of class. Go to his office hours, he's exceedingly helpful and always does his best to help the student understand. Prelims and final were very fair, problem sets were fine and he drops 1. Plenty of extra credit opportunities to boot. Definitely taking a class with him again if I can.

Prof. McKee is a real nice guy who is ready to help anytime. The positioning of the course was a bit weird as it is supposed to be a somewhat rigorous course but the target audience is a group of econ majors who have no training in higher math at all. The result is "learning" a bunch of formulae you never have to prove (or see the proof).

Nice and approachable, but class was structured badly. Required attendance at 8am lectures, where a lot of the time was spent in silent breakout rooms. Exams were all multiple choice, which is horrible for a math-heavy course!!! Problem sets were laborious, but really helpful to learn material. Overall good prof, bad class.

This man is easily the best professor I've had so far. He is a great lecturer, but more importantly he is super considerate and accommodating especially during a tough semester. Absolute goat, and this is coming from someone who took his 8am class.

Professor McKee is one of the best professors in the Econ department. He manages to make every class entertaining with games and challenges, even when course material is a bit dry. If you're someone who does better with active learning than lecture-style courses, I highly recommend ECON 3030 with McKee!
He's a really funny and interesting lecturer. Examples given in lecture are very good and help students understand the material

It took me time to get used to Professor McKee's interactive style of teaching, but once I did, I really enjoyed the class. Professor McKee truly cares about making sure students are thinking about the material in relation to the world they are living in. Go to office hours, they're really helpful.
Overall good teacher. Interesting lectures, relatively long homework (but nothing too bad), and pretty easy exams.
Prof McKee is amazing. He really cares for his students and rewards effort. Problem sets are quite challenging, prelims are less so. Highly recommend to take 3030 with him.

McKee is a stud- never seen a professor so intentioned in structuring their class. First day of class I was in awe at his grading criteria/expectations. He tries to reward hard work and understanding, not penalize you if you're struggling. He APPLIES the stuff we are learning to the real world. Don't expect an easy class, it's still a lot of work..

McKee is AMAZING. He knows his stuff, cares for students, class is not an easy A, but easy B if you study a lot. He is just a great guy in general, and as a prof he is ok. Online quizzes, HW, project, exams, and group exams. He does everything he can to make sure you get at least a B for 3120, not so sure about 3030. He is passionate about teaching

Really approachable and nice professor. I put off taking this class on purpose because this class is one of the most rigorous classes one takes in the Economics major. I was fortunate enough to have this professor. Although problem sets are long, he is a great lecturer and as long as you pay attention in class he explains the material well.
The most amazing professor I've ever met. Professor McKee is super nice and a really good teacher. His office hours are valuable.

It's unfortunate that this is a required class for the Economics major at Cornell. This is a god awful class with a professor that doesn't teach clearly and gives extremely long and dumb problem sets. Be prepared to learn stata and try to work with people that may not want to work with you. WORST class I've taken so far.

Professor McKee is not only a fantastic teacher, but an awesome person. I had a bad first exam, but McKee was very easy to talk to and make sure my grade was not affected by one bad performance. When I had this meeting, I got to talk to Professor McKee as an equal and a counselor. He has been very successful; talk to him if you get the chance!

Professor Mckee is great! He is clearly passionate about the material and it really shows in his teaching. Its a hard course by its nature, but Doug does a good job of making it understandable. If you put in work, its definitely doable. Would highly recommend the class and the professor!

This professor makes Intermediate microeconomics interesting and exciting! He also really cares about teaching and uses different perspectives to engage the class. Definitely one of my favorite teachers. He made me love the econ major again and have some hope. ECON 3030 was still just as hard as I had heard though.

I had put off taking this course because I was really scared but McKee is very sweet and patient. He actually cares about teaching-even has a whole podcast and blog about it. If you go to lecture and try your best to do the p-sets and actually are able to solve them before exams you can do really well. He's very helpful during office hours too.

WORST class I've taken at Cornell. Hands down. Purposely long and hard problem sets that no one could solve. Just resulted in students writing stuff down they didn't even understand.  Each problem set was painful, even after going to lectures and discussions. This class killed my major and cumulative GPA all on its own.

Great professor who is very accomplished in Graphics. A class is hard with a lot of work and a median grade of B so make sure you have time and are interested in the subject. He is monotone in lecture but very knowledgable and descriptive. Fair and easy to access.

Steve is a really nice guy overall, I guess people could find his lectures boring if theyre not into the topic. Test was hard and projects are okay, like dont get intimidated by the first few projects as they get much better when you get to the later ones. Prac is usually instructed by his phds, but steves willing to help on question on prac too

Projects are too hard, beyond the scope of the lectures. Steve is a nice guy but his lectures are rather elementary and the projects are 99% self-taught material. He claims that the projects will not be big programs, but I ended up writing 1000+ lines of code for the first assignment. There are other more manageable and interesting 4000+ electives.
Great professor. Nice person. Helpful in office hours. 45 work load. Practicom requires lot of time as well. Highly recommended.

Lectures were pretty removed from the assignments, assignments were difficult and impossible to figure out without help from course staff or significant previous background. Tests were similar to assignments.

This dude keeps you in the dark to struggle with the material and let you figure it out on your own.  The exams are graded in a very picky fashion so you have to be super explicit with everything and still complete the exam on time.  He almost never gives direct answers to questions - bothersome.
great teacher. has good notes cause the book was terrible

Does a good job of making an interesting subject very boring, but you will learn if you manage to stay awake.Pretends to care about his students by learning their names but truly lacks concern for his students.(i.e. if you miss an exam for a death in the family, serious injury, etc. he doesn't care)
This guy is weird. "Nap Day"? "Talk like a Pirate Day"? Is this what excessive ORIE does do you? Brilliant guy, no doubt but very bland teaching style.

Very boring teacher. HIS VOICE PUTS YOU TO SLEEP! The lectures are an hour and a half long! I have never missed his lecture, but I also haven't been able to stay awake for an entire class yet. Average professor. He loves the Red Sox. I hate the Red Sox. He likes Arsenal. That's cool. He's a good guy
very easy compared to other profs for this course- avoid renegar

The guy has an adjective for a name...Get it Maria ??

His mellow voice during lectures means lights out.  But he tries to make the class as interesting as possible, and one of the few professors I know who actually responds to student feedback.  Uncanny ability to remember names.  Final is impossible though.
quite possibly the sexiest man alive...no joke

Not a bad class but very boring lecture.  The name says it all.
Interesting class, Velazquez makes class interesting. Class consists of presentations and participation mostly. Take him he is also a DJ on the side, chill professor

Lectures are basically reading over the slides and does not communicate information effectively or in a logical manner. The assigned reading gets very dull and jargony which really makes doing the reading reflections hard. Only stayed in the course for minor requirements, which I think is the reason 90% of the class is there for too.

Overall chill class as long as you keep up with it. Weekly quizzes are open note but it helps to be familiar with readings ahead of time. TAs are super generous graders. Landon is super accomodating, but as others have said he does have a limit. He makes lecture content relevant and interesting

Interesting guy, but the material in SOC 1101 is pretty common sense. His lectures were funny and engaging. The TAs are the ones giving feedback, but they're super lenient graders. The answers for the reading quizzes are word-for-word in the readings, and they're open-note.

The class was easy very straight forward, no exams instead 2 weekly quizzez and memos (1 page papers) were assigned. Grading wasn't hard on memos and quizzes were easy can get away with skimming the readings

Professor Schnabel's lectures were always well organized and detail oriented. He posted the lecture slides with notes on them before lecture so students could really listen during lecture and take their additional notes. Very flexible in terms of grading and due dates but if he begins to feel taken advantage of, privileges will be lost.

You would think that for a class with such intuitive content, this course would be simple but Prof. Sternberg/TA's grading made it excessively difficult. Given his tendency to ramble off & base the quizzes almost completely on his tangentially related stories, my consistent efforts to attend class every day were wasted. Funny though so props there.

We were graded on being able to recall the professor's life experiences instead of actual psychology concepts. I was excited to learn about adolescent psychology but his lectures were so boring. I don't recommend him if you don't want to be tested on random tangents during lectures. The questions you're tested on are random so go to every lecture.

Class is pretty easy (take home, short answer prelims) and he definitely caters to what students want out of their experience. Lectures were tedious and he would ramble on about irrelevant topics, he also came off as very insensitive at times

He is the least empathetic and most ignorant professor that I have ever come across at Cornell. He spoke about triggering topics such as eating disorders and suicide in a highly insensitive way; for example, once said that a female jogger he had seen "was obviously anorexic and had probably been running all day." Also refused to give any TWs.
no leniency with grading or late work and boring lectures, easy class though

Prof. Sternberg was extremely rude after a family death. He indirectly referenced me in a message to the entire class, insinuating that it was my fault that my relative had passed away because I informed him that I turned an assignment late. I felt it was incredibly unprofessional and that he demonstrated a clear lack of empathy.

Dr. Sternberg is adorable! I took this class in Spring semester of 2021, so it was online. I am not sure how the course is in person, but the quizzes were 3 open ended questions concerning the lectures/textbook. It was not very difficult to manage at all. I would take a class with him again!
Not a good professor. Two types of lectures, 1) reading the assigned textbook reading to us or 2) talking about his only kinda related research. Do not recommend

Intermediate Narrative Writing with Professor Viramontes has been on of my favorite classes at Cornell so far. Not only does she have great knowledge in the subject as an accredited novelist and short story writer, but she also takes the time to connect and impart this knowledge on her students. I know have improved as a writer with her guidance.

Took her creative writing course at Scripps College. She builds a great community in the classroom. Might be a little New Agey for some, but I appreciate her approach compared to more cynical profs I've had. Love the "passion presentations" as a way to learn from classmates.

Viramontes is a phenomenal teacher and writer. If you EVER have the chance of taking her class, you must. She really cares about each and every one of her students and is willing to spend quality office hour time with them. The diction she employs even when she speaks will make you have goosebumps! VIRAMONTES IS AMAZING!

Wonderful professor. Genuinely cares about her students and is willing to put in quite the amount of time in office hours. Each time I come out of her class, I just want to go write more. Definitely a professor every English major should encounter.
Lovely woman, great writer and professor
Helena Viramontes is a genius!
Prof. Viramontes is great!--Interested and interesting, and quirky. Take her for creative writing.

Participation was graded based on a few questions during lecture and was 10% of the final grade. Weekly problem sets make up 40%, while exams make up the rest. Professor was nice and lectures were fairly engaging. Sections were a bit boring. You don't need to buy the textbook.

Your ideal FWS teacher - caring, knowledgeable, well-spoken, and engaging. There were times where some lectures could get a tad long-winded, but you won't need to listen to every word in order to succeed in the class.

Kalas is an amazing lecturer, and she really makes an effort to get to know her students. She's very passionate about the material, which makes a world of difference in a class that can get pretty dry at times. If you're worried about your grade, go and talk to her. She will help you and will likely offer extra credit.

Prof. Kalas is a great professor! She taught my FWS (Technologies of Writing). Her expectations are clear and the workload is manageable compared to other FWS's. Our in-class discussions were always productive and enormously helpful in writing papers. She is a caring and passionate professor. Her feedback on essays is enormously valuable.

Brilliant poetic analyst. She is excellent in a small, seminar-type class, not an amazing lecturer. Her critique on papers was always helpful, and she comes up with some fun creative assignments too. If many students are having trouble keeping up with readings, she will listen and adjust the schedule some to help.

Rayna is tough but fair and she grades according to your ability. If you can swallow your pride long enough to watch her eviscerate your papers you can learn more from this one woman than you can imagine. Her comments are illuminating and she really tries to understand what YOU wanted to say and help you say it better.
Eh, alright class.  My positive impressions probably flow more from the interesting subject matter though.

Kalas is a hard grader, and she destroyed any interest I had in medieval lit after taking her class-otherwise a nice woman. She only likes you if you repeat what she says. No matter how much I tried to make office hours and meet with her, she was always late. Her final exam was one of the worst English finals I'd ever taken at Cornell.

I dreaded a class on Milton; but by the time the class was done, I could honestly say it was one of the best at Cornell. Dynamic, passionate professor with a profound knowledge of both Milton and the period in which he wrote. Pretty difficult class. But definitely recommend taking it just for the professor.
If you talk in class, help with the discussions etc, she will give you an A on your paper regardless of whether it was well-written.
Kalas knows her stuff and she's a dynamic lecturer.  really hard topics but they make you think. if you get bored by a challenge then don't take her.

Definitely one of the most challenging classes I have ever taken here.  She has a great style of lecturing, although sometimes they go off too long, but for the most part, if one is as enthused in the subject matter as she, then it's all good.
Passionate about Shakespeare and nice woman, but discussions are boring, paper topics are obscure, and grading is very arbitrary. Definitely one of the hardest writing seminars in terms of work load.
Professor Campanella's lectures are inspirational and amazing. He is always well prepared and passionate about everything urban planning and architecture
Very interesting lectures presented in an energetic way. Extremely knowledgeable about everything urban planning.

very inconsiderate of students reactions and feelings to the stressful events on campus over the last couple of days. he undermined their trauma by saying that he went through 9/11 no compassion or empathy

Campanella is an eccentric but fun professor. His lectures, while not very organized and lacking informative slides, are enjoyable, and the grading for the three essays was very lenient. Attendance determines your participation grade
The struggle to be at a spring class at 8:40 am in the morning is worthwhile. Very inspiring and informative class.

Horrible Lectures. Prof. randomly responsive to emails. Lectures in Milstein where he shows a picture for 5-10 minutes and drones on about mostly American (mostly NYC) history. He doesn't bother to create power point slides or even share the photos, so people are google searching for their own photos and how to spell quoted names all during class.
Not very interested in students' work or career goalsresearch. Unclear grading criteria and project guidelines

Not enough clarity on what the goal of the course is. The total hours required for this class is A LOT and at the end of the day doesn't offer any skills that can help you fetch a job. The group discussions don't compliment the lectures. Not sure if you can learn anything new that you wouldn't by reading a few books on american history.

Not sure if the the course is about 'Urban and Spatial Theory' or American history. Rather than touching on concepts of spatial theory, the class seemed more about American (actually New York City) history. Professor is not very accessible either in person or over emails. Assignments are really vague no clear skills learnt at the end of the class.

Tom is an exceptional professor. As a new addition to the faculty, he brought a breath of fresh air and personality to the program. He is VERY well-versed in his topic. Although he can seem a bit pretentious, just keep look past the MIT degree and listen to his balance of experience and wisdom exude. You will appreciate his class in the end.
KV is awesome! Very chill , nice , caring, smart and responsive guy. Learned a lot on the IARD trip over winter break.

I took IARD 402 & IARD 602 with Professor KV. His teaching was informative (learnt about genetically engineered organisms and how their commercialization improves rural livelihoods in developing countries). Best year long course I took at Cornell. The class included a field trip to India Jan Break. Prof.KV is an awesome prof.
She does not care.
You never know what you're gonna get with Beth, but usually it's awesome. Definitely unlike any other courses I've taken at Cornell. Worth it!
Beth makes class feel informative and interesting and pushes us to do better than we did yesterday. She's brilliant.
Beth is great!

Not your typical playwriting class.  Beth talks a lot about theory and the unconventional in playwriting, but it's balanced with Aoise's practicality in the craft.  Readings aren't bad (though some are pretty weird), but Beth is simply an excellent presence to be around, especially with finding one's playwriting voice.

A great class, though it definitely requires work.  If you think that because it's an acting class it'll be easy, then this class isn't for you.  Prof. Milles is wonderful and I would take any class with her.

Worst class every. Course not curved. Not given a single point to extra points problems, even if you did all of them and received full credits. No response in email and failed to answer students questions during classes. Told you quiz tested on a certain chapters, but actually tested on different chapters.
She is a kind, caring person who is accessible by email. She did not curve the class at all, so many people hate her for that. Many people did not like her teaching but I found it okay.
Terrible instructor. A black box grading process and you lose points for NO explanation!

Absolutely awful. 10 minute quizzes that are worth 5% of your grade each that are hyper specific to the textbook. No drops. Lectures are very slow. Sadistic grading on exams, youll lose 10% for a mistake on a question, does not matter how big or small, minimal partial credit. Horrible communication, gives no information about means/medians.
do not take her class period.
Do not take her class, She give bad grade.

Very disorganized and incomprehensible grading. On multiple occasions, she's randomly deducted points from my exams and when I ask her about it, she can't remember why she took off points and refuses to fix my grade. One of the worst professors I've ever had.
A nice person, but not a great lecturer.

One of my favorite professors I've had at Cornell. Math and Politics is a great class, and she taught it well. Prelims were fair and had an easy final project instead of an exam. Like another commenter said, she is a nice person, but her lectures are quite poor. She'll often ask the class a question, then wait about 5 minutes in silence for someone to figure it out, and when no one does, she just gives the answer. This can happen about 1-3 times per lecture.

She's a nice person but just not good at teaching... Her lecture is not well organized and her notes are very unclear. She seems to be a happy, helpful person and she tries...  I found the lectures not helpful at all and just learned most of material from the textbook. The book is very good and cover all the material fairly clearly.

I think she is a very good lecturer. Her lectures are clear and organized and summarize all the important points in the textbook. Homeworks are not always straightforward, but they are in general a lot of fun! Enjoy this class very much!
Lectures are quite useless
The worst teacher I have had at Cornell. I couldn't understand when she spoke english words let alone calculus jargon. Don't take calc with her!!!
Try to have another professor.

It is true that you do have to go to class every lecture, but that is because attendance is 40% of your grade! Thats awesome! The material is not hard, and is actually interesting.  It is easy to get an A+ if you just do the work.

It was supposed to be an easy class, but every class you miss, you get reamed. I even wrote 3 extra credit papers, forged a dentist appointment, but she is a Nazi for grading. I was smart enough to get an easy A, I got a C+ from missed classes. If you like coming to class and listening to her babble, you are golden. If you like to party... Pass

Go to section, participate every once in a while and do the readings. Very reading intensive course, weekly writing responses that are not graded but are just for participation credit.
Extremely helpful one-on-one. Knows the material inside and out. Skip the TA's office hours and go to his instead.

Uber hard prep sheets (30% of grade and 5 pages each in great detail) each week about an article. High amounts of papers to read that are 5 years old and ancient in the field added on. Only plus is she gives out prelim questions before the exam and you can drop a prelim (out of 3). Lectures are decent and relevant to the week's paper.

I've learned more in this class than any other class at Cornell. If you're at all interested in cell biology, this class provides the context you need. Don't fall behind in lectures, the material is DENSE and plentiful. Put in the time and effort and it will pay off. First time a prof will give you helpful practice/feedback on scientific writing.

Biology like you've NEVER SEEN BEFORE. SO MUCH INFORMATION. WOW. After taking this course I have never seen biology the same way again. Honestly that's how much you learn. Reading papers is so much faster bc. of how much you learn. Great if you are considering going into biology. But it should definitely be 4 credits bc. it's LOADED. Amazing.

People seem to be complaining about the course, but it's really not that bad. The level of detail you're expected to know is reasonable for a high-level cell biology course. Also, Dr. Vogt makes it easier with comprehensive lecture slides. Plus he really seems to care about the material and the students. It's a great cell bio class.
Avoid the class if you can because: this is a 8:40 class; he has extremely detailed lecture slides; he grades papers on how well you can write in English; he is not the most engaging lecturer.

The lecturer is not engaging in anyway while all the material is online, which is aggravated by the mandatory attendance at 8:40am. The assessments rely on you to memorise extremely specific details and punish you for not memorising them thoroughly. The material would otherwise be interesting if it weren't for the labourious memorisation required.

Dr. Allred is very kind and extremely intelligent. She is warm and helpful with any questions. She knows the material so well and her class is enjoyable. The final research paper and story map are hefty and lack clear guidelines, but that was the only downside of this course. The material is interesting. Make sure you ask clear questions.

I feel like Professor Whitmore is about as good a professor as you can get for biz comp. In class he's always willing to help you and his TAs are helpful as well (and hold lots of office hours). Regardless of who you get, the class has a ton of work, so just do it and you should be fine. The excel prelim and final are easy imo, only word was hard.
Practical class. Teacher was professional. Maybe too much coding in the lecture though.
Very useful class for internship and jobs. One of the harder core classes, but worth it at the end.

Now that we got our final grades I am much more satisfied with this class. It was a hard semester back on campus after over a year of remote learning. The situation with the final being postponed until the following semester didn't help either. That was the university, not him though. I did better than I expected and I think the grading was fair.

Pretty good. Was clear about expectations. Tough grader though. Good at explaining stuff in person, but the structure of the class didn't really facilitate much of that. I would suggest to hold more office hours and get to know students more. Other than that I learned a lot from him.
The single worst teacher I have ever had for a lectures. Disrespectful, entitled, arrogant, and self absorbed.

Professor Whitmore was 100% my worst professor this semester. His course is set up terribly so I will give him some credit for that, but he made it even worse. If someone was doing bad in the class, the other two prof. would try to help and give feedback but Whitmore did none. If you had an issue with grading or a question, he left you on your own

Andrew Whitmore is possibly the least caring professor I've ever had. He acts very passive aggressive towards students and is not accommodating towards individuals who ask questions. When students try to ask questions he usually gets angry rather than being helpful and asking a question.

Simply the least understanding instructor at Cornell.

Professor Whitmore is very professional and helpful. He will respond to your emails quickly and is responsive on discussion boards (if you have them). I highly suggest meeting with the TA's because they will be grading most of your assignments. I would definitely take this class again.

Prof Whitmore is very talented and clear in his presentations and Business Computing comes highly recommended to any Cornellian. Though he can come off as arrogant and annoyed, he displays information in an easy to understand and comprehensive manner.

Professor Constable may be a brilliant researcher but he is anything but brilliant as a teacher. Lectures were extremely disorganized, he repeated himself many times during lectures, and our entire grade was based on one paper, for which we received no guidance.

He did not understand that the point of teaching a class is to help the students learn the material. He also did not let us demonstrate any knowledge we learnt from the textbook. Our entire grade was based on one paper which he kept claiming would be graded easily as an excuse to not guide us through writing the paper. This was false!

By far the worst professor I've had at Cornell. Lectures were extremely disorganized.
