I felt that I learned nothing from his class, and relied entirely on the TAs in recitation for my understanding of the material.

Worst CS class I have ever taken at Cornell. Lectures are extremely disorganized and topics is not typical CS at all (to me, I believe for theory ppl it might be more interesting). He is a nice guy, though.

Lectures are boring and disorganized. He frequently goes off on tangents too. The hardest part about this class though is that what we are taught and what we are expected to know are completely different. The TAs teach us using last year's notes. That's the only way that we learn anything.
Hard course taught with a lot of jargon

Professor Cowie is genuinely amazing. He is the most captivating lecturer I've ever seen. He's so smart and witty and he has his his finger on the pulse of what matters and makes his class relevant and enlightening.
Told me he had a very bad year 1314 but overall a very great teacher. Makes the class very interesting and worth taking.

Cowie's lectures are tough to follow because he has no powerpoint or slides to help. He does not have a website so if you miss a lecture, you're on your own. He grades much easier than his TA's; try to get your essay into his pile.

His lectures are really disorganized. I relied a lot on the TA, but that can't replace a quality/organized professor. He is a great guy and can deliver an interesting lecture, but those two things don't help when it comes down to writing papers etc.

WARNING: HE IS VERY DISORGANIZED. You will have to spend a lot of your time  trying to put everything together. He is a really interesting person to listen to, but he expects students to place everything into a "Story" but it's a story that you don't know the beginning, middle or end to because he's is SO DISORGANIZED.

He is a very interesting person to listen to, BUT, he is very disorganized and does not give clear instructions. As a person who loves history he made me hate the subject. The entire class is essay based and very subjective. You can make a great argument with great support, but if you don't say what he feels is important your grade will suffer.

Had Prof. Cowie for Six Pretty Good Books. Great professor, very well-read, excellent grasp of subject matter.  Knows how to engage the class and remains open to new ideas and views.  Likes to incorporate discussion into lectures and connect everything back to history.  I strongly recommend Cowie-he's fun, smart and will leave you thinking.
He is a amazing teacher and the lectures are very interesting... he is also.. very very good to look at. Some of the girls just stare.

He is a very entertaining and engaging lecturer.  If you need clarification about something in class, then he is very helpful.  He is not really available out of class for much discussion.  His TA this semester offered no help and was pretty much useless.
Great prof. Great lectures, makes labor history interesting. Readings are long and necessary but doable. Papers and exams are fair. Highly recommended

Very smart, funny, extremely nice and helpful. Would definitely recommend taking any of his courses. He's a great guy who's hella hot. Makes Labor History remotely interesting, which is a tough thing to do. Grading is slightly tougher then other labor history courses, but definitely worth taking a slight GPA hit. Cannot recommend him enough...
His was the best class I had at Cornell!
He's really good and easy going
tough class. the TA is responsible for a lot of the  grading, which doesn't make it any easier. but, cowie is still the best because he makes it interesting..
His lectures were very interesting, despite the fact that subject is boring. If you go to lectures and do the readings, you will be fine.
Great professor, really cares about the material. In order to do well stay on top of the reading and don't miss class + take lots of lecture notes.

Fun, interesting class. Cowie is great professor (very passionate about the subject matter) and loves to teach. His class covers a lot of material. If you stay on top of the readings, go to class and take notes, and form study groups for the exams, you should be fine.
excellent class...don't pass it up!
Selects really good readings and is a great discussion leader.  Demanding workload.
Amazing Professor! His Recent History Class is Just Great! Highly Recommended
very cocky

Basically, I love this man for what he did for our class this semester and for being so interesting. I thought I would dread the early class, but he really cares about the material and his students. You are very foolish to pass up an opportunity to take his class- I'll be taking another one soon! Just know that it is a lot of reading...
Take his recent history class. It was one of my favorite classes. The man knows how to teach!

I had him for three classes (could not fit them all on here)!  He was one of my favorite professors at the law school.  He was passionate about the subject and really imparted that passion onto his students!

Cowie is THE BEST professor I had at Cornell.  Period.  His lectures are wonderful.  He teaches history the way everyone should learn it.  He assigns fascinating readings and has interesing & complex analyses of historical themes.  Take any of his classes that you can get in!

Great professor, even though I was confused at times.  Rob (the TA) was kind of hard on paper grading at times.

interesting lectures (and guest lecturers), assigned readings are interesting for the most part, TA grades essays fairly hard

He is an amazing professor.  I don't know how anyone can only take 2 pgs of notes.  I take about 5-6 per lecture.  Everything is so interesting in his class.  Excellent use of pop culture in class also.
i like his stories, but can take a while to answer the questions...what's up with never looking at the left side of the room?

I agree that his class is interesting, however he seems to go too slow for me.  i mean he literally takes 20 mins to say one significant point!  look around, half the students fall asleep!!! and notes that we take dont even reach two pages!!
Prof. Cowie is the best the ILR School has to offfer.  He is a great teacher who really cares about his students.  Take any class that he offers.

He is the man.  Amazing lectures

Great professor!  Take him for CB 100 and 101 if you get the choice.  Not bad to look at either!
Great young prof who relates well with his students and the girls love him!
Jeff Cowie is the last great hope of the ILR school, especially now that Nick Salvatore teaches once every two years.
Great guy. Lots of movies in class.
eh, overrated.
His initials are not JC by coincidence. Jefferson Cowie is the man.
dope professor
Sid's a very entertaining lecturer. He explained concepts well and was very helpful outside of class...I'm sad he's leaving Cornell.
Makes the lectures very entertaining, and is skilled at explaining difficult concepts in terms of easier, real-life situation

Sid is hands down one of the best lecturers at Cornell. He is clear, engaging, and truly cares about teaching. It also helps that his slides are clean, simple, and super well-designed, which is something that you don't see very often. I'm not even a CS major and his lectures made me want to stay in the class.

Sid's lectures were clearly organized and engaging. He could do more to project himself clearly, but his passion for the material definitely comes across well.  His overall course organization, however, was incredibly poor and detracted from interaction with the material. While that may have been solely this run, prepare to buckle down regardless.

Did is a great and engaging lecturer. His lectures often combine difficult material, jokes, and class engagement. Between class and online, he is constantly answering questions and looking for feedback. His assignments were often difficult and the class was hard due to organization problems. Hopefully his future classes are more organized.
Class consensus that he's one of the best computer science professors ever. Makes some tough stuff enjoyable to listen to.

His lectures are always very informative, and he's very passionate about the subject matter. He teaches everything very clearly, and he's always available outside of class for more help. The homework is challenging, but interesting, because it forces you to think about problems in a different way. Overall, he's a great professor.

The most responsive professor I've had here. Responds to email super fast and is always on time. His analysis is hard to follow at first but once you get the skeletons everything starts to make so much sense. Will take his class again.
To put it plainly, he is a bad lecturer and is unnecessarily difficult to follow. He makes an easy subject difficult to understand by using unnecessary academic language.
Great guy, great professor.  Every bit as smart as the next, but easily one of the coolest profs at the law school.
One of my favorite 1L professors.  Cares that students walk out of class understanding the material.  Easily accessible whether after class or during office hours.
She is the best. Super knowledgeable and super friendly. A tough grader in writing assignments but she gives you the chance to improve your writing skills and your grade.

Such a sweet professor who really cared about students learning the material. Would like students to participate in class. Offers a helpful study session before the prelim. Exam is very straightforward. Definitely recommend taking any class with her!
Very good and articulate, clearly knows what shes talking about, only graded on tests so you have to go to lectures because notes arent always posted.

Professor Batt has been the best part of ILR so far. Her lectures are brilliant, I came away from this course with such a better understanding of globalization, pensions, private equity, and the financial sector of the economy. She provides really great writing feedback too. Readings were tough but enlightening. TAKE THIS CLASS.

Amazing and inspirational teacher who really knows her stuff. She is super accessible outside of class and gives very good and comprehensive feedback on her papers. She is also flexible with deadlines. She does grade assignments a little tough, but you will gan so much knowledge from the class and come out of it as a more polished writer.

Great and inspirational professor who is always willing to help students, both inside and outside of class. She gives very good feedback and, although she grades a little tough, you will come out of the class with so much knowledge and will improve your writing tons.

Good lecturer, one of the better ones in WLC.  Test is tough, but she makes it clear what she wants you to know, which isn't too difficult

Prof Batt was really helpful to me. The class was split into 4 modules. She taught the 2nd one and I had come in having struggled in the previous module. I talked to her about my problems and she helped me. I ended up being motivated by her to put alot more time into her module and as a result did better. She is also a good lecturer in-class.
He's really helpful. Emphasizes participation in class and staying engaged.

Carolyn is clearly passionate about acting and wants each of her students to succeed. As long as you show up to classes and participate, you'll do well in this class. Most work is done in-class, and there is very little homework/assignments.
super caring instructor. very talented. amazing class.
take this class. meet with him.
If you go to his lecture you will do well. He is a wealth of knowledge. Ask him anything, he knows. Do the work.
Professor Ahl is a GENIUS. Genuinely an old-world gem. Otherworldly intelligence that can be hard to follow, but once you embrace his thought processes you begin to think differently too.
If you love greek stuff you will love his class. He is very devoted.
GREAT

An absolutely amazing professor and person in general. Show up to his class and just listen. Write a few notes but really just absorb the content. Most importantly DO THE READINGS!!!! The most fascinating and engaging lecturer I've had at Cornell, and in my top 2 or three all time (I have a BA elsewhere).  Like another reviewer said, sometimes you just put the pen down and listen. Assigned very creative and effective essay prompts, one of which I now use as a writing teacher. Opinionated for sure. Progressive white British.

Fred Ahl is an all-time great professor. I was his student 43 years ago and he was one of the most impressionable professors I have ever had in my life. Fred has no hubris. The man certainly knows his subject but his pompous attitude and lack of respect for opinions other than his own make class aggravating at times. He was not helpful with grading and just difficult to work with in general. Avoid unless you are a die-hard classics fan.

He has a pet theory for every play he assigns. And he shows very little respect for students. He would mockingly read little bits from students' papers.
If you haven't taken a course with Professor Ahl, you're entire university experience has been a worthless waste of time. He is undoubtedly the best professor at Cornell.

I took a few courses with Ahl almost ten years ago and his remain the best lectures I have ever heard in my life.  I sat through his classes riveted and anticipating whatever it was about antiquity he would say next.  It was amazing and I am grateful I happened into his classes.

He knows more or less everything about Ancient Greece, and never once used notes during a lecture. Also a very nice guy. Lots of reading, most of which is enjoyable, but make sure you keep up, or else you will be sorry when the midterm and final come around!
I'm the curly-haired greek.  Hot!
Lots of dense reading for this course, but great lecturer and interesting material to write about.  Tough midterm and final, but learned alot
Forget ratings; forget grades.  A class with Professor Ahl is a memorable experience not to be missed at Cornell.

I love professor Ahl. He tells histories like he knows the people he's talking about personally and sometimes it turns out he does. If you're good he'll have the class over for dinner and prove his cooking is as incredible as his lectures.

I would sometimes just put down my pencil and listen in awe as he told greek history/myth like a bedtime story. This man is a great talker and I came away feeling like I'd lived in another century for an hour.

As a Latin teacher, Fred Ahl is tough. If you don't work hard, you will be toast. Professor Ahl is THE MAN. That's all I have to say.
Great and challenging professor and an excellent person.
No Comments

Professor Ahl has a great personality; brilliant, knows what, 20 languages?  Very full of grand ideas and schemes.  This makes him a very good lecturer, though he rambles a lot.  The semester I took Tragic Theater he set up and directed a play for our class to participate in.  Afterwards had a nice party in his home with nice wine!
very erratic in his moods, impossible to find in his office, full of grand ideas but not helpful on specific points. Charming personality, but not reliable as a teacher/mentor.
Makes you think in ways you've never thought before.  Extremely interesting and the best professor/teacher I've ever had the pleasure of learning from.
Best professor I ever had
Fred Ahl is the best professor at Cornell. Period.

I took Marxism and Liberalism with him and really enjoyed it. His lectures are super engaging and I loved the way he connected ideas. He graded the essays pretty easily and gave good feedback on what to change. I'd definitely recommend him if you are looking for an FWS to take.

I took the Liberalism and Marxism FWS and thought it was super interesting. Despite this course's complex readings many of the topics that appeared in readings were addressed during class. Many papers required an understanding of the readings and drew from concepts/ideas brought up during the discussion. Grading isn't harsh at all 10/10 would rec.

Great course, I would 100% recommend taking it with Dr. Mozafari as he responds and addresses any concern related to assignments as fast as he possibly can. Just make sure to reach out with any questions with hw submissions as early as possible so he can act as leniently and understandably as he can.
He cares about your mental health, you're learning and wants to include everyone in the class. He grades really nicely because grades aren't his motto but how much you learn.
One of the most enjoyable learning experiences I have ever had.
Made me love the subject and really improved my writing.
Wonderful teacher. I learned a lot from her.

Dr. Kassam is very wise and knowledgeable. Pushes his students to their fullest potential and gives great and specific feedback on the essays, as a grad student. He is a really incredible man and an incredible professor. The weekly essays aren't hard, they just are a weekly thing you have to do. The amount I have learned in this class and adjusted my perspective is incredible. I recommend it, but don't take this class if you don't want to work or aren't willing to have a diverse perspective.
Lies and misinformation  Fake Science  Socialism  Anarchy. That simply describes it. Stay away from this class and Prof Kassam's brainwashing with fake science.

Dr. Kassam is extremely knowledgeable in his field and will bring in other in his department or his grad students if they happen to know more about a topic. His lectures are incredibly engaging. The grading can be tough in this class but he is very willing to provide feedback and he very much wants you to succeed. He truly cares about his students.

Great undergrad course, but had conflict with his grad students; many left his working group. Some projects weren't clear in what was being asked for/evaluated, but that may have been addressed since I took the course. Participation goes a long way.
His one of the demanding professor at Cornell. I am highly recommend him to especially at Sociology, ecology, policy and environmental science majors.

Some good and some bad. Easy class, be prepared to participate in discussion. Dr. Kassam is not a bad lecturer, but many of his conclusions are based on anecdotes and opinion. Overall came off as poetically pretentious, but a lot of students seemed to think that he was wise. Easy A if you show up.
Plain wrong. Prof K dicusses in his class the demise of republicans. He is plain wrong. So are his ideas of environmental policies. Stay away.

Don't miss the opportunity,

Dr. Kassam is one of the best professors you could ever have the honor of taking a class from at Cornell. He is incredibly invested in his students. His class is absolutely amazing! I definitely learned more about Native Americans. I wouldn't recommend this class to students, who don't like to read and write a lot of papers. There were no prelims and finals; instead, there were two 10-page essays and weekly reading and writing assignment.

Confusing class taught by a Canadian professor who is disgruntled with US policies. Reminds me of Ted Cruz: Hey prof, if you are not happy with US policies, go back to Canada.  Follows his own confusing book.
Great professor! And great class. One of my favorite classes at Cornell.

Confusing class.  Canadian professor who seems to teach this class to promote over - regulation of environment policies similar to Canada. May be he desperately needs to work in United States to promote this flawed concept.  He has a good sense of humor - may be good class for entertainment.

Eye-opener Dr. Kassam opened my eyes about indigenous communities all around the world. Easy A if you go to class and ask Qs.

Dr. Kassam has won many teaching awards for good reason!  He is a one-of-a-kind professor whose life mission is to make a difference in his students' lives. This guy is something else. He's one of the few professor's who can be described as wise. His mellifluous words make it impossible to lose your concentration. Take any class of his if you want to become well rounded individual.
Professor Hirschl is disorganized and he presents his theories like they are facts. While he claims to be objective, his lectures and essays are anything but. Easy class though.

Honestly a bit unorganized, but still a solid professor that knows his stuff. You have to be a bit patient because he can sometimes jump around topics, but you'll learn a lot of interesting things. Very easy grader, really just wants you all to understand the primary points (which he'll emphasize and review during lecture).

Great professor, had him for DSOC 1101. Go to lecture once a week when the weekly quizzes are, if no quiz don't bother going to lecture. The class was not bad and I learned a lot!

Actually the worst professor I've had at Cornell -- I don't care if he is a brilliant researcher. He had no investment in the class, terrible lectures and had no care whatsoever what students took away from his class - truly terrible.

Really easy class and the topics are interesting, but he presents it in a way that doesn't really hold your interest. Don't really need to go to class to do well.
Easy class. Sweet professor. No studying necessary.

he twists the students' comments so they'll fit his thoughts, all he ever talks about is how cars are ruining the world, and he is ABSOLUTELY NOT objective... keep that in mind... you don't need to do the reading cuz he'll explain them well in the class and is pretty clear, but his personal thoughts get in the way of teaching
easy but a little boring - not incredibly enthusiatic or personable

Professor Bachminska is an exceptional instructor! I took POLSH 2034: Intermediate Polish II with her and there was never a time when I did not feel supported, heard, or respected. I highly recommend taking any class with her :)

In the Polish class, I liked the best the trip to Cornell museum. I also really enjoyed the movie about Walesa. Ewa even brought Polish sweets for us and we learned how to order food in Polish at a restaurant. I recommend taking her class.

Simply one of the best language courses I have ever taken. Professor Bachminska is very engaging and makes learning Polish a truly wholesome experience of Polish culture, film, art and history. Very poor instructions on assignments followed by grading on criteria that was never stated. English is not her first language and it clearly shows when your paper is read. great guy, easy exams (can easily get 100s), doesn't matter if you show up to class, take him for HR over the other profs, very chill class, one final group project and 2 prelims.

Excellent professor, and hilarious lecturer. Nothing bad to say about this course and how it was run.

Henderson is one of the better stats teachers. While lectures were long, he did his best to make them interesting. The course doesn't have a textbook (one is recommended but not included in CAMP). Can't go wrong with Henderson. Great class and made stats very interesting. Had no background coming into the subject and now feel very confident in the material all thanks to the professor and course staff. Highly recommend taking a class with Henderson if possible, you will not be disappointed.

lectures are great and homework is fun and very easy. The test for 60% of grade was nothing like the homework. Practice test useless for actual test prep.
Great Prof with amazing lectures. Assignments are tough.

Good professor. Lectures are good and he emphasizes applications and understanding. When he's gone, Dr. Huang teaches, and Huang is not as good of a lecturer. Prelim was not hard at all, Psets can be a bit of work but not too bad. R skills are also helpful. Definitely recommended.
Very good professor
Chill professor. Actually makes an attempt to make stats interesting. The new zealand accent doesnt hurt either.

Cases were not what I expected. I did not know AMPL too well coming into this class and all he said during OH was "you should have taken the prereqs." One of the top teachers I have ever had. Great professor

This class is not hard! He is such good professor. And he makes this class interesting. Great work. ORIE 582 is even better.
he is really hard. it looks like he enjoys failing students. does anyone here know how many students he fails each year for orie 580 clas?

This class was amongst the best classes I took during my ORIE major. Sure the tests were hard but I felt like I was actually learning material during the class. The professor hid behind a tough fascade but was very willing to help.
good prof. hard tests. go to lecture!
Yeah, everyone loves this guy.  Easy to see why, just take one of his classes.  You work your ass off, but you get through it and in the end, you realize how good this guy is.

hes from new zealand....

Good professor and lecture but this teacher gives hard tests.

Professor Gleeson is incredibly knowledgable about the topics she presents. She provides many guest lecturers to give real insight on the topics and events she speaks about. Her lectures are pretty helpful, but half the class doesn't pay enough attention, or reads anything at all to realize that. If you do the work, and don't bs you can learn a lot

Professor Gleeson is a wonderful human being and a kind professor.

This class has MANY assignments, but the class is structured extremely well. Take advantage of office hours and go talk to her! All in all, great professor.

Professor Gleeson is awesome! If you don't have a problem with writing, this is the course for you! Easy A if you submit things on time and follow all her directions. Well outlined course and lots of freedom to write about what you want. Just go to class, talk once in a while, and do some good writing and you will pass with flying colors.

Does not post slides, is VERY one sided in her arguments of what she is teaching.  Grading is fair and not too difficult, biggest challenges are the two mentioned already and the mass amount of material.

The first few classes were intimidating.  She's fast-paced during lectures. Talks SO fast and does not post her slides so write EVERYTHING down. She doesn't respond to emails quickly, so email her days in advance. The readings are the most helpful part of the class, but have a lot of irrelevant information, so learn how to decide what is and is not important.

Calc II is pretty standardized so you get the same work/grading regardless of prof, but Sen has to be the worst. Just NEVER take his class if you are not a pro in the material yourself. Even you spend as much time as you can in his class, you end up understanding nothing sound due to his poor organization of the class

Professor Sen is a smart person, but is horrible at explaining concepts. His handwriting is very messy and he often gets lost and confused while lecturing. Honestly, he was pretty terrible but I think that's got to do with him not wanting to teach an intro class. He's confusing, disorganized and boring. Amazing Professor. Very aware of the material. Fair grading and homework.
The greatest math professor ever! I wish all my classes are taught for him!

A true Mathematical Prodigy. He complements his mathematical skill with an excellent capacity to teach. He truly appreciates undergrads, and loves to be asked questions. His advice and understanding has steered many, including myself, into the math major. He is incredibly aware, and almost never messes up either.
Easiest class ever! Shankar Sen really knows how to teach! A hot professor!

Prof. Shankar Sen gives the best math lecture I've ever heard. He is so hot when he's talking about math! I would definitely recommend you to take a math class with him! Never show up to the lectures, but got an easy A+.

Weird seeing how great he is for upper level courses. Not organized, occasionally goes in circles, and usually 2-3 lectures behind the other professor. I ended up teaching myself material from the textbook, but you should still attend lectures because they can be helpful.

This dude is so diorganized, please take the alternate teacher for whoever is teaching linear algebra. Doesnt speak up very well, adn terrible handwriting on the board. Never comes in with notes, my semester he was always a week behind the other class.

His lectures are truly fantastic. He takes a unique approach towards material that you may have already seen before and opens your eyes to a deeper understanding.  Truly different from any other math class you will have.
One of the most passionate professors at Cornell. He always knows how to make lectures interesting and stays on topic. One of Cornell's true treasures.

Her goal is to make hebrew fun and exciting and I would say for the most part she succeeded. Readings could sometimes be challenging but if you know hebrew fairly well you're set. Easy grader.
Very nice and personable, but def. hard to overcome her first impressions of you (and grades). Sometimes unclear about assignment instructions. A lot of busy work but generally easy class.

I found Nava to be very hard to get a long with,. She let her moods and emotions interfere with her teaching greatly lessening the amount I was able to learn.  I came to the class knowing that it would not be easy for me, but she turned me off ever trying Hebrew again. Do not take a class with her.

My vocabulary and speaking skills got less after this class.  Class focuses too much on outdated literature and not enough on vocabulary building, sentance formation, and speaking skills for modern Hebrew.
Nava is a great Hebrew teacher.  She cares so much about the success of her students, and is available to help at any time.  She is an incredible person and an incredible professor.

Easily the most irritating person I've met in my whole life.  Doesn't know how to teach Hebrew systematically, and doesn't have much of a Hebrew vocabulary herself, e.g. I asked her how to say tattoo and she wrongly told me there was no Hebrew word for it

Interesting material in the class, but the professor was extremely boring and the 1:15 lectures were painful. 1-2 page and a half response papers are due every week after a lot of reading, so if you're looking for a class with little work this isn't it. They also grade the papers and exams pretty hard - I studied a lot and got B+s...Not an easy A.

BORING BORING BORING. Crowded lecture + monotone professor= snoozefest. I thought it would be a really great course but he made everything sound so tedious. I'll never take another class from this professor

His lectures are pretty flat. He assigns a lot of articles, some of which are interesting, but mostly they're just time consuming. Grading system is really annoying: every point you lose is 1% of your final grade. Miss a few questions on the midterm and you're already stuck at a B.

This teacher was horrible. I was very interested in the subject but he assigns inordinate amounts of work and grades very harshly. The experience was a negative one and my interest in the subject is now shot.

Sounded like it could be interesting from course description but Lynch is just a really flat lecturer. I couldnt help falling asleep.  Its just power point after power point, and the prelims cant really be studied for...

Great course... very repetitive of 301 tho, but new material is introdued. HW assignment dur every lecture, but counts towards final grade and keeps you up-to-date with reading. Profis really nice, and willing to offer extra help and explainant of anything. Took 30 1 and 407- i loved them both!
the course is very interesting, puts common ideas/concepts into different perspectives, exams are fair, straight forward, i'd recommend
Lynch is a good, friendly prof. His lectures do tend to make you rather sleepy, but his chosen material was interesting. Grading is fair, class wasn't too hard, but lots of reading.
spare me the lecture, i used it to catch up on my sleep....a lot of writing
he's really really nice but lecture is like having your sweet old uncle tell you a bedtime story...  just wanders off and voice drops off...  which is prolly why i just slept thru lecture.
Really smart guy, and kind of funny.

Overall good prof. Lectures are clear- they're sometimes engaging but sometimes boring. However, the class content is mostly a review of basic statistics, and doesn't involve very much MATLAB. Class is also very theoretical at times, which can be annoying. Overall, it's a pretty straightforward class, but isn't the most exciting/interesting.
She is great at teaching writing.

She always goes the extra mile for her students. She always shows them kindness and is so understanding. She is one of the nicest people I've ever met. Her feedback is thorough and enriching. It can be hard to keep up with her in class, but if you can manage to do so you'll find it rewarding. However, the reading she assigns is hard to comprehend

Masha is my favorite professor at Cornell! She is so inclusive and appreciates the diverse perspectives of her students! She knows how to get young students interested in boring old literature! Take her class and you'll see why she's so great!

Behaves like a high school teacher. The pacing was very slow. The professor did not manage time well.  Not enough time was spent discussing the text. Not much reading. Very little writing. Very slow grading. Professor only wants to talk about contemporary gender issues. Very mediocre medievalist, if one can call her that.

Masha is the best! I took two classes with her over my time in college and both were incredibly dynamic and interesting. She is incredibly caring towards her students and passionate about the content of the courses she has taught me. 10/10 recommend taking a class with her at Cornell.

Masha is an amazing professor and such a caring person! She helped me so much as a freshman getting adjusted to Cornell and learning how to navigate the English department. Would recommend her classes to everyone for sure
Not a bad professor.  But her metadiscursive narcissism does get tiring.

Aloof, insincere, & careless. I can see why her style feels abrasive to some, but she's a passionless, daft lecturer who clearly makes little effort to know & accommodate her students. Participation grade criteria are unclear. Text selection had a narrow range of narrative styles, w/ common themes of gender, sexuality and race.

Passionate, honest, & caring. I can see why her style feels abrasive to some, but she's a vibrant, intelligent lecturer who clearly makes an effort to know & accommodate her students. Participation grade can be earned with online discussion posts. Text selection had a good range of narrative styles, w/ common themes of gender, race, and literature

There are some comments here saying that Masha is very caring, passionate, respectful and presents a fascinating selection of readings in class, but it's not true. It was something I was excited about after reading these comments before taking her class, but it turned out to be lies! Masha is the most pompous, whiniest professor I know!

Masha must learn to respect opinions other than her own. She may love to make her students look up the definitions of words in the Oxford Engl Dictionary, but she herself needs to not just look up, but take a very thorough, rigorous course (nothing like the courses she offers) on the word HUMBLE.
People are right, she does talk a lot and insert her own stories between each person's thought, but everything she says is insightful. She is also incredibly helpful, understanding, and sweet.

Connecting with Masha was one of the best opportunities I had as a student at Cornell! She's passionate about the material, happy to help, and truly understands the impact that learning respectfully and self-critiquing has on academia. She always has a wide and fascinating selection of readings for class. I always left seminar feeling focused!

The one thing you need to understand about Masha is that she knows what today's english majors want far, far better than they themselves could ever possibly know. Masha's "How Reading changes your life" syllabus was the most self indulgent thing I've ever seen. She should have her own dept and major. A degree in Masha will surely come in handy...

We were graded by few things and the grading criteria were inconsistent. She found a bunch of things wrong with one paper and gave it an A and another had 1 problem and she gave it a B+. She wouldnt explain how she determined my final grade, which did not add up based on what she told us in class. I also feel that I learned little from the course

Masha was alright but the course was so light on reading and writing that I kept forgetting about it. I had thought masha was supposed to be known as a hard professor, and I was surprised both by how little insight she offered into the texts and by how little she seemed to prepare for class. She mostly wants to talk about gender theory

Masha is so funny and sweet. One thing to note: any course with Masha is mostly about . . .well . . . Masha. Even in Chaucer course, "Masha" eclipses whatever the course is ostensibly "about." Hence, you have to get with her program, and you must show an interest in her personally. Face-time and relationship building are more important than smarts
Masha is a superb professor. However, 10% less "Masha," and 10% more learning content, would hardly have been an unwelcome change. Make that 20.

There are some comments here saying that Masha doesn't accept other viewpoints or is very confrontational when there are disagreements, but it's not true. It was something I was concerned about after reading these comments before taking her class, but it turned out not to be an issue at all! Masha is the most caring professor I know!

PROF Raskolnikov is THE BEST ENGLISH PROFESSOR at the English Department in Cornell. Please do not listen to the other comments saying she is harsh. She is so so so sweet, caring, understanding and funny. She is such a fair grader she will give you 100 comments on your paper but you will still get an A. I want to take all of her classes at Cornell.

This professor can be very confrontational. It is best to agree with what she says, though she will act like she is engaging you. This professor wants an echo chamber. Just smile and act like you like her and you'll get a good grade. It's very creepy.

The course lacked depth and did not stimulate reflection. The professor made unfounded assumptions about medieval culture and offered questionable conclusions about the texts under discussion. The professor was also very arrogant and could not stop bragging about things she didn't and does not do.

Masha is witty, funny, smart, caring, and incredibly inspirational. Lectures are never boring. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I learnt so much in her Body as Text class about what it means to live in a body with a gender, sexuality, etc. Go to office hours and participate in discussions.
Bless this woman Hard to get the work (reading) done, easy to do well

Prof. Raskolnikov's Origins of English Lit class was one of the first classes I took at Cornell, and one of my favorites. Get to know her really well-- go to her office hours, go to the events she announces in class, have lunch with her, etc.-- and you'll get so much out of the class and the professor herself. Wonderful, engaging class.

Professor Raskolnikov is truly inspiring. Be warned, her class is a lot of work and ready. However, it is well worth it and in-class discussions are fascinating. The best was to succeed is simply by showing up and trying to participate. She is a wonderful professor and well worth the effort!

I could not be happier I found Masha in the very diverse sea of cornell english professors. I took 2010 and Chaucer with her and if i could minor in her i would. She's tough, but only because she wants to every student to reach- or exceed- his/her potential. my writing has improved more than i couldve hoped. HIGHLY recommended-seize the opportunity
Excellent lecturer, very fun to listen to. Tough but fair grader, and the class was well worth the time!

Very engaging and helpful professor. Lectures are usually really interesting and sometimes funny. Very passionate about what she studies. Papers and assignments are usually graded by the TA. Overall 2010 was an amazing intro to english literature and I would definitely take a class with Masha again.

Wassup y'all. I took Masha for Pleasure/Danger last semester and I have her this semester for Chaucer - and let me say that she is entirely without rival in the English department. She's a strict but fair grader and will do everything in her power to help you improve as a writer AND her lectures are boss. A teacher of the highest calibre, 5 stars.

Professor Raskolnikov is great. Be warned that she says what's on her mind, though she tries to avoid offending people to a degree. While I didn't really enjoy many of the readings, the in-class discussions were fantastic. Professor Raskolnikov sometimes talks too much be aggressive when you have something to say and sit in her line of sight.
She is one of my favorite professors at Cornell.  She's so intelligent, funny, and passionate.  I love her teaching style and insights.  She is also absolutely gorgeous.  Love this woman!
she is amazzinnggg!!!
What an awesome professor! She's very intelligent and interesting, although she may be tough at times.
Masha is the best professor ever. Smart, funny, caring, and totally hot. Only she could make medieval lit fun!

Masha is one of the most amazing professors I have encountered.  No way to fall asleep in her class, she's constantly cracking intelligent jokes and then laughing at them... but seriously, this woman is so intelligent it almost hurts.  Very opinionated, honest, and a great professor overall.  Loooove her.

this professor thinks she is funny, when really she is not. she doesn't accept any viewpoints other than her own, so you better agree with her. if not, your grade will definitely reflect your 'disagreement.' do not take classes with this woman.

Very helpful and one of the nicest profs!  However, she is not open to viewpoints or methodologies besides her own and is a staunch feminist post-structuralist - if you actually enjoy reading  the texts and not focusing on secondary lit, she may not be for you.
Masha's simply a badass.  Tough, opinionated, honest, brilliant, and hilarious.  And a fabulous dresser.  Teach me more!!!
No Comments
Masha rocks! Super smart, super cool.

I thought this class was very fun and interesting.  She could be blunt at times, but she was very helpful and ultimately a very nice person.  I always looked forward to this class.  She gets the chili pepper because she told us to give her one.
tough class, but lots of fun
offensive, mean spirited, made me bad writer
She was so funny and made fun of all the dumb kids in class, made me want to go just to hear her make fun of them. She also was just plain cool.
wow.. hardest class ever.  really mean and rude.

He has a reputation for not caring about classes since he's near retirement, and can be a bit ethereal and touchy as someone else mentioned. He's really brilliant, but during the pandemic kind of lectured about something off topic. Kind of moody, and maybe even rude at times

Professor Aching is awesome! He is extremely intelligent and knowledgable of the subject he is teaching while simultaneously open to hearing and understanding the opinions of others. He is also really understanding when it comes to extensions, missing class, etc. Grading is a bit tough but you get used to it and there's not that much work.

He is a solid professor overall and likes to answer questions. He does not give rubrics for his few graded assignments. I found that he contradicted himself sometimes ideologically and seemed to respect his own ideas more than students' or just had a hard time relating. He says he is understanding but also puts you off a bit too, so tread lightly.

Professor Corpis is THE professor to whom I compare all my other teachers. He is engaging, enthusiastic, an amazing lecturer, funny, friendly, and an overall wonderful man. His lectures were always filled with interesting tidbits, and he has such a deep knowledge base. I absolutely loved his class.

Prof. Corpis was an excellent professor! His class was so interesting and he is particularly good at guiding discussions and his knowledge of history is vast. Take one of his classes before he leaves!!
Fantastic Professor, easy grader, always answers every question in detail, very nice guy!!
Pretty good teacher, pretty decent person. Lectures well, keeps things interesting, explains issues clearly and well, and knows a lot about the subject even if it's out of his specialty.

Prof. Corpis is the man. Great, interesting, concise lectures. Leads good class discussions. Answers questions clearly and comprehensively. Good readings, fair assignments and grading. Likes to talk about TV shows. Take his courses. He's a smart guy.
Amazing Professor! Excellent lectures, readings, and paper topics. If you have any interest in Early Modern Europe or microhistory, take one of his classes!
awful lectures, it always seemed like he had no idea what he was talking about. Unfair grader, no idea how i got what i did, my assignments just dont add up to my final grade
THis was one of the most interesting classes I have ever had.  This class just cemented my decision to study history.  Everyone should take one of his classes.
This professpr is not good, his lectures are extremely boring. The class was awful. If you are the typ of person who sits in the front row and can be engaged in boring lectures you might enjoy it.
Very approachable and helpful. Definitely go to his office hours to discuss paper topics... he will make everything crystal clear. Great class, great prof!
A really nice professor who wants his students to exceed. I would take again

Prof. Boone is by far one of my favorite professors at SHA. He has an enthusiasm for teaching and energy that makes even boring subjects interesting. What stands out is that he cares about his students and always tries his best to give us flexibility with assignments and grades. I would 100% take another class with him.

Insensitive, decent lecturer but thinks his class is students' only responsibility. Considers students lazy and attempts to overwhelm them with a difficult workload, even during crisis. Severe lack of emotional intelligence unsuccessfully balanced with attempts to be witty. Subject matter is not inherently difficult but lecturer tries to make it so
Explains very clearly and with simple language.

Boone is an amazing guy and is a professor that will always have your back. I recommend going to office hours to work through problems with him. Tests are fair; however, he does like students to have a conceptual understanding of the concepts, and will put questions to trip up students who just memorized formulae and problem solving setups.
We love Boone

Boone was a great professor! He made micro interesting and easy to understand with his examples. He was always willing to go over things again if people were confused. He was also very caring and understanding outside class. Would 100% take him again.

He is the best professor I have ever had. He was a true master of the subject and knew so much about Economics. However, he was also such an amazing human who truly cared, was so sweet, always there if you needed him for anything, and had an amazing sense of humor. Wish I wanted to do economics so I could take another one of his classes.

Zia is one of the best professors I've ever had at Cornell. Her lectures were clear, easy to follow, and helped with the homework and exams. She was helpful outside of class and provided fun and useful extra credit activities. She really wanted to make sure we learned the material and enjoyed joying so.

Single handedly one of the most intelligent, understanding professors in the department. Yes, she's incredibly tough, but she really cares about her students doing well. She can go really fast sometimes in lecture but they're very well organized and all her tests are very fair.

At first, she was bad, going way too fast in lecture, answering questions as dismissively as possible, and clearly planning the course without ever reading the ChemE curriculum and realizing we haven't taken Statics or Thermo. She got progressively better over the course of the semester, but continued to be incredibly condescending all year long.
By far the best professor I have had.  She really cares, and clearly understands the material.  She wants students to enjoy the class and do well, and is great

At first, she was terrible, i.e. she moved too quickly, assumed knowledge we did not have or simply had not used in a long time, and so forth. After receiving criticism, adjusted her style for the class. Willing to meet outside of class for help on homework. Does not post solutions for problem sets, so you're forced to go to office hours for help.
Really stubborn professor. Can't fade!!!!
very unpleasant person
Guest lecturers were great. Sadly though, Neema's rudeness kept getting in the way.
Can't say I learned anything interesting, Neema was useless, and I'm so happy that the course is over and I fulfilled my requirement.

Neema is a great person with an interesting background. She only gives As to people who work very hard, and her readings and assignments are challenging, but if you put in he work, it will be one of the most rewarding, eye-opening classes you will take. Do the readings, show up, put in effort, and you will love it!

Challenging but rewarding. Attendance to sections is mandatory make sure you attend. Long interesting readings. She may not seem like it but is approachable and is very knowledgeable. Prelims weren't hard but grading was confusing. Overall a brilliant course, very interdisciplinary and broad but grounded by group assignment.

Though this class might have a pretty heavy workload, it definitely pays off in the end. Neema isn't about babying students through the course--you're really on your own to interpret what is said in lecture and apply it to the essays and the midterm. Overall, I highly recommend the course to anyone who has the time and energy that it requires.

Yes, this class is tough but you will learn a lot if you put in the effort. I enjoyed the material and Neema's enthusiasm and knowledge of the topics.  I probably wouldn't recommend it as an elective because of the workload though.

No notes on slides so you have to pay attention to every word she says, and she always goes after class is over. It feels like she just regurgitates the readings outloud and you can't skip class because attendence counts. The TAs grade harshly but they're on your side and will try to help, but Neema expects everyone to be studying all the time.
Incomprehensible, lacking substance lectures. The tests aren't bad while the essays are graded by TAs who are instructed to not give many As and Bs.
Decent Prof, but doles out way too much work and takes attendance WAY too seriously.  Cool accent too.

Only take this class if you have to/if it's relevant to what you're studying. It is way too much work--both in terms of reading and essays if you're just looking for an elective. Neema is fine, but lectures can be confusing/scattered, while the TAs act like her loyal minions.
Uninspiring

Neema did not seem to care about improving her teaching methods or organizing herself to levels that don't drive students crazy. Can't recommend her knowing that there are better instructors in the department. CRP 3201 was completely useless despite its potential.
Loves to argue about silly stuff and as a result the class never gets to discuss key planning issues
Decent prof, but you gotta break your back to do well in the class.
Simply a bad teacher, intellectualy confused, and often ignorant of imporant books. But at least she knows how to hide it.

Minus whiney students and HORRIBLE TAs, her classes are wonderful but challenging. You learn so much if you actually do the readings (of which there are A LOT). She is VERY sharp, VERY engaging, and assigns fasinating material. I left CRP after that semester, but to me, she exemplified what a professor should be like- sharp and no nonsense.
Looking back on Neema's course, I realize that it is one of the best that I have taken at Cornell.  Lots of work, but worth it in the end!

i don't understand people who complain about a class being hard. what are you paying all that money for?  neema responds to students who put in the effort, and has little respect for those who don't -- i'd be the same way!

Not good. She explains everything unclearly. Whenever someone asks a question, she doesn't really answer the right thing... and she is very mean... The course itself is very interesting, but the TAs hate her...... The workload is definitely not  3-credit like.

Neema makes this class harder than it needs to be, but nevertheless, she is awesome. Despite the horrible TAs I had and the difficulty of the class, everything else was fine. I feel I learned quite a bit.

I initially struggled in Neema's class, but she helped me all throughout the semester. Do all the work and attend lectures, and you will be fine. As others have said, she is easily available and a very nice professor.

I disagree with the previous comment. Professor Kudva is always willing to help. If you are struggling with your papers, write a rough draft and take it to her. She might be very strict and indeed does not easily give away A's, but she is not unfair. The main problem is that most students expect to get an A in this 100-level class.

Arbitrary paper grading standards that were "beyond articulation", would berate the class at any given point for a number of reasons, generally cranky, took an interesting subject and removed any kind of scientific or academic grounding. Worst class I have taken at cornell.
Excellent professor. Not an easy class, but Neema is very fair. Great class overall.

Phyllis Janowitz, besides being a world-renowned poet, is a gifted professor, able to give the deeper shades of critique and understanding to a fiction writer's work. Highly recommended for serious writers.

i love this professor.  She nurtures every single person who comes in her class, and if you have talent, she works with you amazingly.  Of course, you have to go to her office hours - she is a rare jewel in CU, and you shouldn't miss her classes for the world

I love phyllis janowitz! She at first seems a bit spacey (aren't all writer types?) but her poetry is amazing and her class was definitely worth it. :) I wanted to drop the course the first day because it seemed unorganized but by day three she really grows on you. It's been one of my favorite courses at Cornell. Cute lady.

easiest class at cornell, gave everybody an A because "i'm a professor and i can do what i want"  work was almost optional, lectures were about..whatever.  and that dog she brought to class, i loved it
very little help in regards to constructive feedback. she hides behind the argument of 'who am i to criticize anyone else's work?'
Her lectures go everywhere.  It will be rare that you go really in depth into a piece of poetry brought in, unless you meet with her during office hours, where she was quite helpful.
she is wacky but the class is good if you want 4 credits with almost no work, and you like reading/writing poetry.
Too easy, no learning, no feedback.

Prof. Hammer is an amazing lecturer. His lecture is clear, organized, informative, and engaging. He's also very friendly, approachable, and he actually cares about students. The class itself can be hard tho - especially for someone who doesn't have a solid background in physics, but he's very helpful in office hours and outside of the class.

Class is incredibly interesting. The final project is an open-ended research paper on something to do with Fusion aand has an optional presentation. 8% of the grade is at the Profs discretion and the pres is the easiest way to get it. Lectures can be dry but as long as you read the book you will be fine. Dr. Hammer give good help in OH too.

Lectures from the assumption that students know about/have prior interest in fusion, so he sometimes speaks aimlessly, assuming students know what he's talking about. But, he was very helpful in office hours and provided lots of advice on the major project ("designing" a nuclear reactor). HW was vital to clarifying the actual course expectations.

Hammer is an amazing lecturer, being clear, informative, and engaging. He is approachable, friendly, and very knowledgeable. The material for fusion is difficult, like Physics 2214 on crack.  Fusion weekly HW takes 4-7 hours.  Do well on the final project!   Expect B+/A- median grades for Fusion and a free A for attendance for Energy Seminar.
Amazing teacher! The class is hard - but he's so helpful and always available in his office.
GREAT GUY ! Very very helpful :)

His is an amazing teacher. Class material may seem difficult, and it is one of those classes where either you get it or you don't, but he is very helpful at helping you get it. Go to his office hours if you're confused, and you're sure to understand the material.

Took this class as an elective and don't regret it at all. Professor Hafeez is one of the best people out there. He cares about his students understanding the material well and doesn't assign readings unless it's absolutely necessary. I appreciated his flexibility with deadlines and resources. He also delivers amazing lectures - 100/10 class!!

the BEST professor in ILR!!! He makes sure everyone understands his material, and his lectures are highly engaging. He is very flexible and cares a lot about his students. Doesn't require readings and preps you well for the exams. Attendance is mandatory, but his enthusiasm and stories make me want to attend class every day!

While he has sadly moved on to Tufts, Spurlock was one of the best professors I've ever had for Spanish! He went beyond teaching and really tried to connect with each and everyone of his students. His OH were very helpful and he'd always explain things in an easy to understand way. I have no doubt that you'll learn great things from him.

Professor Spurlock made lectures engaging and interesting. Although the class was horribly structured by the Spanish department, Spurlock kept students interested in the subject and provided us with great feedback in class and in office hours. It is sad to see the corrupted Spanish department push such a dedicated professor away.

Exceptionally kind and caring professor, a real gem in the department! Great at breaking down grammar concepts while making classes interesting with lessons on culture, history, and current events. Extremely accessible, so take advantage of OHs especially to talk about the essays and oral presentations. 10/10 professor!

Extremely caring. Accessible outside of class and is willing to meet and discuss anything, whether it be how to get better at grammar, get better at essay writing, or the oral. You'll never fall asleep in his lectures; literally the most animated lecturer ever and genuinely passionate about his material. Content is a lot but he adapts it.

One of the best Spanish instructors I have ever had. Enthusiastic, caring, prepared. He is so deeply understanding of his students and understands what it's like to be an undergraduate with other responsibilities. There is a lot of homework associated with 2090, but that is not his doing; it is the nature of the course and the coordinator.

enthusiastic, compassionate, patient, knowledgeable. welcoming environment. includes info about dialects, history, current events, culture. cares ab student wellbeing & learning more than grades. 2090 is a lot of work w/ frivolous rules but Spurlock didnt care if we followed them. tests were hard. learned a lot & attribute it to Spurlock, not 2090

I have never had a Spanish teacher/professor who is so accessible and understanding toward his students. Highly, highly recommend--he rekindled my love for Spanish! That being said, 2090 does have a lot of homework involved, but it is assigned by the language department not the professor himself, so there's nothing you can do to get out of that.

Had him for a lab supervisor this year.  He will give you an A if you just run people like you should.  He's famous for being a solid experimental designer in the questionable field of parapsychology.  Doesn't teach regular classes anymore but I highly recommend his lab.
worst professor ever

My absolute favorite professor at Cornell. I think he's retired from teaching now, but if you get a chance to work with him, take it. His lectures were always interesting, eye-opening and full of wisdom about human beings.

Professor Bem was the worst professor I have had at Cornell. He would rather trick his students on exams than actually test what they know. He is a weird guy and I would never take a class with him again.
One of the most wonderful people I've ever met.  A genius too.
His opinion and theories are well addressed, and are fascinating. This class may change the way you see social situations.

This class is the most interesting class I have ever taken at Cornell thanks to Bem! His lectures are so entertaining somebody ought to set up a booth at the door and sell tickets. He will push your comfort zones in terms of the issues in sexuality and personality that he will discuss. Very smart ma
Dominant Teacher. Interesting and engaging!
Daryl Bem is amazing.  Maybe the greatest professor I've ever had.  I'm not going to lie; I'm obsessed with him.
Awesome professor...has a way of keeping you on your toes by bringing up controversial topics and interesting subjects within the realm of personality psych.  Great lecturer, fun class.
hard.

Has no reservations about revealing his sexual preferences, marital strife, and children's upbringing in lecture.  Cracks jokes without even intending to be funny.  I guess they're funny because they're so unexpected from such a straight-edge guy.

This is my second course with him (did a summer in high school) and I'm obsessed with this prof.  He's a fascinating person, and a cool lecturer.  Stayed after today to ask a question, and man does he know his stuff.  He is political, but it's interesting
great teacher--one of the best ever!

I love this class! Prof Bem is such an interesting guy and his lectures actually keep me interested and awake! His tests are somewhat challenging, but he has a really sweet curve. If you do the readings (which aren't that much, you can do really well!
Weird guy. His teaching can be very political at times. Anyone who calls him a bad professor is clueless. Not a good professor either; he doesn't make the material live.

Bem is a very engaging lecturer.  He does talk about himself quite a bit, but his not in an arrogant way.  He often makes fun of himself.  Doing well on his tests requires that you look very closely at the readings and attend all his lectures.

No coherence in his teaching style at all. Very full of himself and contradicts the textbook often. Makes tests as difficult as possible in an attempt to show how complex his field is.  Doesn't like to deal with students, says to go to the TA for help.
No Comments
No Comments

He makes you think critically for the required discussions. His lectures are taught well and it was obvious that he was really passionate about Astronomy. I looked forward to the labs and lectures because they demonstrated interesting things about space. The assignments and quizzes were manageable, and the essay was the only difficult thing I did.
